children.text: pañcatantram
children.translated_text: The <s>Pañcatantra</s>

children.text: kathā-mukham
children.translated_text: Prologue (<s>Kathā-mukha</s>)

children.text: oṃ namaḥ śrī-śāradā-gaṇapati-gurubhyaḥ | mahā-kavibhyo namaḥ |
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutations to the revered <s>Śāradā</s>, <s>Gaṇapati</s>, and the teachers. Salutations to the great poets.

children.text: brahmā rudraḥ kumāro hari-varuṇa-yamā vahnir indraḥ kuberaś
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kubera</s>,

children.text: candrādityau sarasvaty-udadhi-yuga-nagā vāyur urvī-bhujaṅgāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the oceans, the <s>Yuga</s>s (ages), the mountains, <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), the earth, the serpents,

children.text: siddhā nadyo 'śvinau śrīr ditir aditi-sutā mātaraś caṇḍikādyā
children.translated_text: the <s>Siddha</s>s, the rivers, the <s>Aśvin</s>s, <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), <s>Diti</s>, the sons of <s>Aditi</s>, the divine mothers beginning with <s>Caṇḍikā</s>,

children.text: vedās tīrthāni yakṣā gaṇa-vasu-munayaḥ pāntu nityaṃ grahāś ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vedas</s>, the sacred fords, the <s>Yakṣa</s>s, the <s>Gaṇa</s>s, the <s>Vasu</s>s, the sages — may they and the planets always protect [us].

children.text: manave vācaspataye śukrāya parāśarāya sa-sutāya |
children.translated_text: To <s>Manu</s>, to <s>Vācaspati</s>, to <s>Śukra</s>, to <s>Parāśara</s> together with his son,

children.text: cāṇakyāya ca viduṣe namo 'stu naya-śāstra-kartṛbhyaḥ ||Panc_0.1||
children.translated_text: and to the learned <s>Cāṇakya</s> — salutation to the authors of the science of statecraft. [Panc 0.1]

children.text: sakalārtha-śāstra-sāraṃ jagati samālokya viṣṇuśarmedam |
children.translated_text: Having surveyed in the world the essence of all treatises on practical wisdom, <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>

children.text: tantraiḥ pañcabhir etac cakāra sumanoharaṃ śāstram ||Panc_0.2||
children.translated_text: composed this most delightful treatise in five books (<s>tantras</s>). [Panc 0.2]

children.text: tad yathānuśrūyate | asti dakṣiṇātye janapade mahilāropyaṃ nāma nagaram | tatra sakalārthi-sārtha-kalpa-drumaḥ pravara-nṛpa-mukuṭa-maṇim ajarīcayacarcitacaraṇa-yugalaḥ sakala-kalpa-pāraṅgato 'maraśaktir nāma rājā babhūva | tasya trayaḥ putrāḥ parama-durmedhaso vasuśaktir ugraśaktir anekaśaktiś ceti nāmāno babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: The story goes as follows. In the southern country there was a city called <s>Mahilāropya</s>. There lived a king named <s>Amaraśakti</s>, who was a wish-fulfilling tree for all who sought his aid, whose pair of feet were anointed with the crest-jewels of eminent kings, and who was accomplished in all branches of learning. He had three sons of extremely dull intellect, named <s>Vasuśakti</s>, <s>Ugraśakti</s>, and <s>Anekaśakti</s>.

children.text: atha rājā tān śāstra-vimukhān ālokya sacivān āhūya provāca-bhoḥ jñātam etad bhavadbhir yan mamaite trayo 'pi putrāḥ śāstra-vimukhā viveka-hīnāś ca | tad etān paśyato me mahad api rājyaṃ na saukhyam āvahati | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Then the king, observing them averse to learning, summoned his ministers and said: 'Gentlemen, it is known to you that these three sons of mine are averse to learning and devoid of discernment. Seeing them thus, even a great kingdom brings me no happiness. As it is rightly said —'

children.text: ajāta-mṛta-mūrkhebhyo mṛtājātau sutau varam |
children.translated_text: Of the unborn, the dead, and the foolish — the dead and the unborn are preferable as sons;

children.text: yatas tau svalpa-duḥkhāya yāvaj-jīvaṃ jaḍo dahet ||Panc_0.3||
children.translated_text: for those two cause grief only briefly, while the dull-witted one burns [his parents] for as long as he lives. [Panc 0.3]

children.text: varaṃ garbha-sravo varam ṛtuṣu naivābhigamanaṃ
children.translated_text: Better a miscarriage; better no conjugal union at the fertile time;

children.text: varaṃ jātaḥ preto varam api ca kanyaiva janitā |
children.translated_text: better that the child be stillborn; better even that a daughter be born;

children.text: varaṃ bandhyā bhāryā varam api ca garbheṣu vasatir
children.translated_text: better a barren wife; better even to dwell in the womb [forever] —

children.text: na cāvidagdhān rūpa-draviṇa-guṇa-yukto 'pi tanayaḥ ||Panc_0.4||
children.translated_text: than a son who, though endowed with beauty, wealth, and good qualities, is a fool. [Panc 0.4]

children.text: kiṃ tayā kriyate dhenvā yā na sūte na dugdhadā |
children.translated_text: What use is a cow that neither calves nor gives milk?

children.text: ko 'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena yo na vidvān na bhaktimān ||Panc_0.5||
children.translated_text: What use is a son who is neither learned nor devoted? [Panc 0.5]

children.text: tad eteṣāṃ yathā buddhi-prabodhanaṃ bhavati tathā ko 'py upāyo 'nuṣṭhīyatām | atra ca mad-dattāṃ vṛttiṃ bhuñjānānāṃ paṇḍitānāṃ pañcaśatī tiṣṭhati | tato yathā mama manorathāḥ siddhiṃ yānti tathānuṣṭhīyatām iti |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore let some means be devised by which the awakening of their intellects may come about. And here there are five hundred scholars living on the stipend granted by me. Let measures be taken so that my desires may be fulfilled.'

children.text: tatraikaḥ provāca-deva dvādaśabhir varṣair vyākaraṇaṃ śrūyate | tato dharma-śāstrāṇi manv-ādīni artha-śāstrāṇi cāṇakyādīni kāma-śāstrāṇi vātsyāyanādīni | evaṃ ca tato darmārtha-kāma-śāstrāṇi jñāyante | tataḥ pratibodhanaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: One of them said: 'Your Majesty, grammar takes twelve years to learn. After that, the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s> (legal texts) beginning with <s>Manu</s>, the <s>Arthaśāstras</s> (treatises on polity) beginning with <s>Cāṇakya</s>, and the <s>Kāmaśāstras</s> (treatises on desire) beginning with <s>Vātsyāyana</s>. Thus, after knowing the sciences of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s>, the awakening [of intellect] will come about.'

children.text: atha tan-madhyataḥ sumatir nāma sacivaḥ prāha-aśāśvato 'yaṃ jīvitavya-viṣayaḥ | prabhūta-kāla-jñeyāni śabda-śāstrāṇi | tat saṅkṣepa-mātraṃ śāstraṃ kiñcid eteṣāṃ prabodhanārthaṃ cintyatām iti | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then from among them, a minister named <s>Sumati</s> said: 'This span of life is impermanent. The sciences of language take a long time to master. Therefore let some concise treatise be devised for the awakening of these [princes].' And it is said —

children.text: anantapāraṃ kila śabda-śāstraṃ
children.translated_text: The science of language is indeed boundless;

children.text: svalpaṃ tathāyur bahavaś ca vighnāḥ |
children.translated_text: life is short, and obstacles are many.

children.text: sāraṃ tato grāhyam apāsya phalgu
children.translated_text: Therefore one should grasp the essence, discarding the trivial —

children.text: haṃsair yathā kṣīram ivāmbudhyāt ||Panc_0.6||
children.translated_text: as swans [extract] milk from water. [Panc 0.6]

children.text: tad atrāsti viṣṇuśarmā nāma brāhmaṇaḥ sakala-śāstra-pāraṅgamaś chātra-saṃsadi labdha-kīrtiḥ | tasmai samarpayatu etān | sa nūnaṃ drāk prabuddhān kariṣyati iti |
children.translated_text: 'Now here there is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>, accomplished in all branches of learning, who has won fame in the assembly of students. Entrust them to him. He will surely make them wise in no time.'

children.text: sa rājā tad ākarṇya viṣṇuśarmāṇam āhūya provāca-bho bhagavan mad-anugrahārtham etān artha-śāstraṃ prati drāg yathānanya-sadṛśān vidadhāsi tathā kuru | tadāhaṃ tvāṃ śāsana-śatena yojayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: The king, hearing this, summoned <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> and said: 'Reverend sir, for my sake, do instruct these [princes] in the science of statecraft so that they quickly become peerless. Then I shall reward you with a hundred land-grants.'

children.text: atha viṣṇu-śarmā taṃ rājānam āha-deva śrūyatāṃ me tathya-vacanam | nāhaṃ vidyā-vikrayaṃ śāsana-śatenāpi karomi | punar etāṃs tava putrān māsa-ṣaṭkena yadi nīti-śāstrajñān na karomi tataḥ sva-nāma-tyāgaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s> said to the king: 'Your Majesty, hear my truthful words. I do not sell knowledge, not even for a hundred land-grants. But if I do not make these sons of yours knowledgeable in the science of statecraft within six months, then I shall renounce my own name.'

children.text: athāsau rājā tāṃ brāhmaṇasyāsambhāvyāṃ pratijñāṃ śrutvā sa-sacivaḥ prahṛṣṭo vismayānvitas tasmai sādaraṃ tān kumārān samarpya parāṃ nirvṛtim ājagāma | viṣṇuśarmaṇāpi tān ādāya tad-arthaṃ mitra-bheda-mitra-prāpti-kākolūkīya-labdha-praṇāśa-aparīkṣita-kārakāṇi ceti pañca-tantrāṇi racayitvā pāṭhitās te rājaputrāḥ | te'pi tāny adhītya māsa-ṣaṭkena yathoktāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | tataḥ prabhṛty etat pañcatantrakaṃ nāma nīti-śāstraṃ bālāvabodhanārthaṃ bhūtale pravṛttam | kiṃ bahunā-
children.translated_text: Then the king, hearing that incredible vow of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, together with his ministers was delighted and astonished, and reverently entrusted the princes to him, attaining supreme satisfaction. <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>, having taken them, composed five books for that purpose — namely, <s>Mitra-bheda</s> (Loss of Friends), <s>Mitra-prāpti</s> (Winning of Friends), <s>Kākolūkīya</s> (Of Crows and Owls), <s>Labdha-praṇāśa</s> (Loss of Gains), and <s>Aparīkṣita-kāraka</s> (Rash Deeds) — and taught the princes. And they, having studied these, became as described within six months. From that time on, this treatise on statecraft called the <s>Pañcatantra</s> has been current in the world for the instruction of the young. In short —

children.text: adhīte ya idaṃ nityaṃ nīti-śāstraṃ śṛṇoti ca |
children.translated_text: He who constantly studies this science of statecraft and hears it recited —

children.text: na parābhavam āpnoti śakrād api kadācana ||Panc_0.7||
children.translated_text: never meets with defeat, even from <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself. [Panc 0.7]

children.text: iti kathā-mukham |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Prologue.

children.text: mitra-bhedaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mitra-bheda</s> (Loss of Friends)

children.text: vardhamāna-vṛttāntaḥ
children.translated_text: The Story of <s>Vardhamāna</s>

children.text: athātaḥ prārabhyate mitra-bhedo nāma prathamaṃ tantram | yasyāyam ādimaḥ ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now begins the first book called <s>Mitra-bheda</s> (Loss of Friends). Its opening verse is —

children.text: vardhamāno mahān snehaḥ siṃha-go-vṛṣayor vane |
children.translated_text: The great and growing friendship between a lion and a bull in the forest

children.text: piśunenātilubdhena jambukena vināśitaḥ ||Panc_1.1||
children.translated_text: was destroyed by a slanderous and excessively greedy jackal. [Panc 1.1]

children.text: tad yathānuśrūyate | asti dakṣiṇātye janapade mahilāropyaṃ nāma nagaram | tatra dharmopārjita-bhūri-vibhavo vardhamānako nāma vaṇik-putro babhūva | tasya kadācid rātrau śayyārūḍhasya cintā samutpannā | tat prabhūte'pi vitte'rthopāyāś cintanīyāḥ kartavyāś ceti | yata uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The story goes as follows. In the southern country there was a city called <s>Mahilāropya</s>. There lived a merchant's son named <s>Vardhamāna</s>, who had amassed great wealth through righteous means. One night, lying in bed, a thought arose in him: 'Even when wealth is abundant, the means to [increase] wealth should be considered and acted upon.' For it is said —

children.text: nahi tad vidyate kiṃcid yad arthena na siddhyati |
children.translated_text: There is nothing indeed that cannot be accomplished by wealth;

children.text: yatnena matimāṃs tasmād artham ekaṃ prasādhayet ||Panc_1.2||
children.translated_text: therefore a wise person should by all effort secure wealth above all. [Panc 1.2]

children.text: yasyāryas tasya mitrāṇi yasyārthās tasya bāndhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen;

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃ loke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ ||Panc_1.3||
children.translated_text: he who has wealth is a [true] man in this world; he who has wealth is [considered] learned. [Panc 1.3]

children.text: na sā vidyā na tad dānaṃ na tac chilpaṃ na sā kalā |
children.translated_text: There is no learning, no gift, no craft, no art,

children.text: na tat sthairyaṃ hi dhanināṃ yācakair yan na gīyate ||Panc_1.4||
children.translated_text: no steadfastness of the wealthy that is not praised by supplicants. [Panc 1.4]

children.text: iha loke hi dhanināṃ paro 'pi svajanāyate |
children.translated_text: In this world, even a stranger becomes a kinsman of the wealthy;

children.text: svajano 'pi daridrāṇāṃ sarvadā durjanāyate ||Panc_1.5||
children.translated_text: even a kinsman of the poor always becomes an enemy. [Panc 1.5]

children.text: arthebhyo 'pi hi vṛddhebhyaḥ saṃvṛttebhya itas tataḥ |
children.translated_text: From wealth that has grown, accumulated from here and there,

children.text: pravartante kriyāḥ sarvāḥ parvatebhya ivāpagāḥ ||Panc_1.6||
children.translated_text: all activities proceed — like rivers from mountains. [Panc 1.6]

children.text: pūjyate yad apūjyo 'pi yad agamyo 'pi gamyate |
children.translated_text: That even the un-worshippable is worshipped, that even the inaccessible is approached,

children.text: vandyate yad avandyo 'pi sa prabhāvo dhanasya ca ||Panc_1.7||
children.translated_text: that even the un-salutable is saluted — such is the power of wealth. [Panc 1.7]

children.text: aśanād indriyāṇīva syuḥ kāryāṇy akhilāny api |
children.translated_text: Just as all the senses [function] from food,

children.text: etasmāt kāraṇād vittaṃ sarva-sādhanam ucyate ||Panc_1.8||
children.translated_text: so all undertakings [succeed] — therefore wealth is called the means to everything. [Panc 1.8]

children.text: arthārthī jīva-loko 'yaṃ śmaśānam api sevate |
children.translated_text: This world of living beings, seeking wealth, resorts even to the cremation ground;

children.text: tyaktvā janayitāraṃ svaṃ niḥsvaṃ yacchati dūrataḥ ||Panc_1.9||
children.translated_text: abandoning one's own father if he is destitute, [the world] casts him far away. [Panc 1.9]

children.text: gata-vayasām api puṃsāṃ yeṣām arthā bhavanti te taruṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even men who are past their prime, if they have wealth — they are [considered] young;

children.text: arthe tu ye hīnā vṛddhās te yauvane'pi syuḥ ||Panc_1.10||
children.translated_text: but those who lack wealth are old, even in their youth. [Panc 1.10]

children.text: sa cārthaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ ṣaḍbhr upāyair bhavati bhikṣāyā nṛpa-sevayā kṛṣi-karmaṇā vidyopārjanena vyavahāreṇa vaṇik-karmaṇā vā | sarveṣām api teṣāṃ vāṇijyenātiraskṛto 'rtha-lābhaḥ syāt | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And that wealth comes to people by six means: begging, royal service, farming, earning through learning, trade, and merchant-craft. Of all these, the acquisition of wealth through commerce is the most excellent. As it is said —

children.text: kṛtā bhikṣānekair vitarati nṛpo nocitam aho
children.translated_text: Begging has been resorted to by many; a king does not bestow what is proper — alas!

children.text: kṛṣiḥ kliṣṭā vidyā guru-vinaya-vṛttyātiviṣamā |
children.translated_text: Farming is toilsome; learning, with its discipline under a teacher, is extremely arduous;

children.text: kusīdād dāridryaṃ parakaragata-granthi-śamanān
children.translated_text: from money-lending comes poverty through the untying of knots in others' purses —

children.text: na manye vāṇijyāt kim api paramaṃ vartanam iha ||Panc_1.11||
children.translated_text: I think there is no livelihood superior to commerce in this world. [Panc 1.11]

children.text: upāyānāṃ ca sarveṣām upāyaḥ paṇya-saṃgrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of all means, the collecting of wares is the [best] means

children.text: dhanārthaṃ śasyate he ekas tad-anyaḥ saṃśayātmakaḥ ||Panc_1.12||
children.translated_text: recommended for [acquiring] wealth — any other is fraught with uncertainty. [Panc 1.12]

children.text: tac ca vāṇijyaṃ sapta-vidham arthāgamāya syāt | tad yathā gāndhika-vyavahāraḥ, nikṣepa-praveśaḥ, goṣṭhika-karma, paricita-grāhakāgamaḥ, mithyā-kraya-kathanam, kūṭa-tulā-mānam, deśāntarād bhāṇḍānayanaṃ ceti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And that commerce is of seven kinds for the acquisition of wealth, namely: dealing in perfumes and spices, deposit-banking, cattle-rearing, attracting regular customers, misrepresenting prices, fraudulent weights and measures, and importing goods from other countries. As it is said —

children.text: paṇyānāṃ gāndhikaṃ paṇyaṃ kim anyaiḥ kāñcanādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Among wares, the perfumer's ware is the [best] ware — what [use are] other things like gold?

children.text: yatraikena ca yat krītaṃ tac chatena pradīyate ||Panc_1.13||
children.translated_text: For what is bought for one [coin] is sold for a hundred. [Panc 1.13]

children.text: nikṣepe patite harmye śreṣṭhī stauti sva-devatām |
children.translated_text: When a deposit falls [into his hands due to the depositor's death], the merchant praises his own deity:

children.text: nikṣepī mriyate tubhyaṃ pradāsyāmy upayācitam ||Panc_1.14||
children.translated_text: 'The depositor has died — I shall give [the deposit] to you when asked.' [Panc 1.14]

children.text: goṣṭhika-karma-niyuktaḥ śreṣṭhī cintayati cetasā hṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: The merchant engaged in cattle-rearing thinks joyfully in his heart:

children.text: vasudhā vasu-sampūrṇā mayādya labdhā kim anyena ||Panc_1.15||
children.translated_text: 'The earth full of wealth has been obtained by me today — what need of anything else?' [Panc 1.15]

children.text: paricitam āgacchantaṃ grāhakam utkaṇṭhyā vilokayāsau |
children.translated_text: He gazes with longing at the familiar customer approaching;

children.text: hṛṣyati tad-dhana-labdho yadvat putreṇa jātena ||Panc_1.16||
children.translated_text: he rejoices at obtaining that one's money, as at the birth of a son. [Panc 1.16]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: pūrṇāpūrṇe māne paricita-jana-vañcanaṃ tathā nityam |
children.translated_text: Using full and short measures, constant cheating of familiar people,

children.text: mithyā-krayasya kathanaṃ prakṛtir iyaṃ syāt kirātānām ||Panc_1.17||
children.translated_text: and quoting false prices — this is the nature of petty traders. [Panc 1.17]

children.text: dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vittaṃ bhāṇḍa-kraya-vicakṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those skilled in purchasing goods obtain double and triple wealth

children.text: prāpnuvanty udyamāl lokā dūra-deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ ||Panc_1.18||
children.translated_text: through enterprise, having traveled to distant foreign lands. [Panc 1.18]

children.text: ity evaṃ sampradhārya mathurā-gāmīni bhāṇḍāny ādāya śubhāyāṃ tithau guru-janānujñātaḥ surathādhirūḍhaḥ prasthitaḥ | tasya ca maṅgala-vṛṣabha saṃjīvaka-nandaka-nāmānau gṛhotpannau dhūrvoḍhārau sthitau | tayor ekaḥ saṃjīvakābhidhāno yamunā-kaccham avatīrṇaḥ sampaṅka-pūram āsādya kalita-caraṇo yuga-bhaṅgaṃ vidhāya viṣasāda |
children.translated_text: Having deliberated thus, taking goods bound for <s>Mathurā</s>, on an auspicious day, with the permission of his elders, he set out mounted on a fine cart. He had two bulls born in his household, yoked as draft animals, named <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> and <s>Nandaka</s>. One of them, the one called <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, having descended to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, encountered a deep mire, got his legs stuck, broke the yoke, and collapsed.

children.text: atha taṃ tad-avastham ālokya vardhamānaḥ paraṃ viṣādam āgamat | tad arthaṃ ca snehārdra-hṛdayas tri-rātraṃ prayāṇa-bhaṅgam akarot | atha taṃ viṣaṇṇam ālokya sāṛthikair abhihitam- bhoḥ śreṣṭhin ! kim evaṃ vṛṣabhasya kṛte siṃha-vyāghra-samākule bahv-apāye'smin vane samasta-sārthas tvayā sandehe niyojitaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vardhamāna</s>, seeing him in that condition, was overcome with great sorrow. Out of tenderness of heart, he halted his journey for three nights on that account. Then his fellow travelers, seeing him despondent, said: 'O merchant! Why have you, for the sake of a bull, in this forest infested with lions and tigers and full of dangers, put the entire caravan in jeopardy? As it is said —'

children.text: na svalpasya kṛte bhūri nāśayen matimān naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A wise man should not destroy much for the sake of a little;

children.text: etad evātra pāṇḍityaṃ yat svalpād bhūri-rakṣaṇam ||Panc_1.19||
children.translated_text: this indeed is wisdom — protecting the greater from [the loss of] the lesser. [Panc 1.19]

children.text: athāsau tad avadhārya saṃjīvakasya rakṣā-puruṣān nirūpyāśeṣa-sārthaṃ nītvā prasthitaḥ | atha rakṣā-puruṣā api bahv-apāyaṃ tad-vanaṃ viditvā saṃjīvakaṃ parityajya pṛṣṭhato gatvā'nyedyus taṃ sārthavāhaṃ mithyāhuḥ- svāmin, mṛto 'sau saṃjīvakaḥ | asmābhis tu sārthavāhasyābhīṣṭa iti matvā vahninā saṃskṛtaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then he, accepting this [advice], appointed guards for <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, led the entire caravan onward, and departed. But those guards too, knowing that forest to be full of dangers, abandoned <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, followed [the caravan] from behind, and the next day falsely told the caravan-leader: 'Master, that <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> is dead. We cremated him with fire, thinking it to be the wish of the caravan-leader.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sārthavāhaḥ kṛtajñatayā snehārdra-hṛdayas tasyaurdhva-dehika-kriyā vṛṣotsargādikāḥ sarvāś cakāra | saṃjīvako 'py āyuḥ-śeṣatayā yamunā-salila-miśraiḥ śiśirataravātair āpyāyita-śarīraḥ kathaṃcid apy utthāya yamunā-taṭam upapede | tatra marakata-sadṛśāni bāla-tṛṇāgrāṇi bhakṣayan katipayair ahobhir hara-vṛṣabha iva pīnaḥ kakudmān balavāṃś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | pratyahaṃ valmīka-śikharāgrāṇi śṛṅgābhyāṃ vidārayan garjamāna āste | sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the caravan-leader, being grateful and tender-hearted with affection, performed all the post-mortem rites for him, including the releasing of a [memorial] bull. But <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, having some lifespan remaining, his body revived by the cool breezes mixed with the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>, somehow managed to get up and reached the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>. There, eating the tips of tender grass resembling emeralds, within a few days he became fat, hump-backed, and powerful, like the bull of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva). Every day, tearing apart the tops of anthills with his horns, he stood bellowing. And rightly is it said —

children.text: arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati deva-rakṣitaṃ
children.translated_text: That which is unprotected [by man] stands protected by the gods;

children.text: surakṣitaṃ deva-hataṃ vinaśyati |
children.translated_text: that which is well-protected [by man], if struck down by the gods, perishes.

children.text: jīvaty anātho 'pi vane visarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even one without a protector survives, released into the forest —

children.text: kṛta-prayatno 'pi gṛhe vinaśyati ||Panc_1.20||
children.translated_text: even one who has made effort perishes at home. // Panc_1.20 //

children.text: atha kadācit piṅgalako nāma siṃhaḥ sarva-mṛga-parivṛtaḥ pipāsākula udaka-pānārthaṃ yamunā-taṭam avatīrṇaḥ saṃjīvakasya gambhīratara-rāvaṃ dūrād evāśṛṇot | tac chrutvā'tīva vyākula-hṛdayaḥ sasādhvasam ākāraṃ pracchādya baṭa-tale catur-maṇḍalāvasthānenāvasthitaḥ | caturmaṇḍalāvasthānaṃ tv idaṃ- siṃhaḥ siṃhānuyāyinaḥ kākaravāḥ kivṛttā iti |
children.translated_text: Now, once upon a time, a lion named <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, surrounded by all the animals, descended to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> to drink water, being afflicted with thirst. From afar he heard the deep bellowing of <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>. Hearing that, greatly agitated in his heart, concealing his fearful demeanor, he stationed himself at the base of a banyan tree in the four-circle position. The four-circle position is this: the lion, the lion's followers, the <s>kākaravas</s>, and the <s>kivṛttās</s>.

children.text: atha tasya karaṭaka-damanaka-nāmānau dvau śṛgālau mantri-putrau bhraṣṭādhikārau sadānuyāyināv āstām | tau ca parasparaṃ mantrayataḥ | tatra damanako 'bravīt- bhadra karaṭaka, ayaṃ tāvad asmat-svāmī piṅgalaka udaka-grahaṇārthaṃ yamunā-kaccham avatīrya sthitaḥ | sa kiṃ nimittaṃ pipāsākulo 'pi nivṛttya vyūha-racanāṃ vidhāya daurmanasyenābhibhūto 'tra baṭa-tale sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now he had two jackals named <s>Karaṭaka</s> and <s>Damanaka</s>, sons of ministers, who had lost their positions but were always in attendance. They consulted with each other. There, <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Friend <s>Karaṭaka</s>, our master <s>Piṅgalaka</s> descended to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> to take water and stood there. For what reason, even though thirsty, has he turned back, arranged the military formation, and now stands here at the base of this banyan tree, overcome with despondency?'

children.text: karaṭaka āha- bhadra kim āvayor anena vyāpāreṇa uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Friend, what business is this of ours? For it is said:'

children.text: avyāpareṣu vyāpāraṃ yo naraḥ kartum icchati |
children.translated_text: A man who wishes to meddle

children.text: sa eva nidhanaṃ yāti kīlotpāṭīva vānaraḥ ||Panc_1.21||
children.translated_text: in affairs that are not his own — he alone goes to destruction, like the monkey who pulled out the wedge. // Panc_1.21 //

children.text:
kathā 1
kīlotpāṭi-vānara-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 1
The Tale of the Wedge-Pulling Monkey

children.text:
kasmiṃścin nagarābhyāśe kenāpi vaṇik-putreṇa taru-khaṇḍa-madhye devatāyatanaṃ kartum ārabdham | tatra ca ye karmakarāḥ sthāpanādayaḥ | te madhyāhna-belāyām āhārārthaṃ nagara-madhye gacchanti | atha kadācit tatrānuṣaṅgikaṃ vānara-yūtham itaś cetaś ca paribhramad āgatam | tatraikasya kasyacic chilpino 'rdha-sphāṭito 'ñjana-vṛkṣa-dārumayaḥ stambhaḥ khadira-kīlakena madhya-nihitena tiṣṭhati | etasminn antare te vānarās taru-śikhara-prasāda-śṛṅga-dāru-paryanteṣu yathecchayā krīḍitum ārabdhāḥ | ekaś ca teṣāṃ pratyāsanna-mṛtyuś cāpalyāt tasminn ardha-sphoṭita-stambhe upaviśya pāṇibhyāṃ kīlakaṃ saṃgṛhya yāvad utpādayitum ārebhe tāvat tasya stambha-madhya-gata-vṛṣaṇasya sva-sthānāc calita-kīlakena yad vṛttaṃ tat prāg eva niveditam
| ato 'haṃ bravīmi- avyāpāreṣu iti | āvayor bhakṣita-śeṣa āhāro 'sty eva | tat kim anena vyāpāreṇa | damanaka āha tat kiṃ bhavān āhārārthī kevalam eva | tan na yuktam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text:
Near a certain city, a merchant's son had begun building a temple in the midst of a grove of trees. The craftsmen there — masons and the like — would go into the city at midday for their meal. Now one day, a troop of monkeys, wandering here and there by chance, arrived there. There, a certain carpenter had a post made of <s>añjana</s>-tree wood, half-split, standing with a <s>khadira</s>-wood wedge inserted in the middle. Meanwhile, the monkeys began playing as they pleased on the treetops, terraces, pinnacles, and timber-ends. One of them, near death [due to fate], out of restlessness sat upon that half-split post, grasped the wedge with both hands, and just as he began to pull it out — what happened to him whose testicles were caught in the middle of the post when the wedge slipped from its place has already been told.
Therefore I say: 'In affairs that are not his own...' We have food enough from our master's leftovers. So what need is there for this meddling?

children.text: suhṛdām upakāraṇād dviṣatām apy apakāraṇāt |
children.translated_text: By rendering service to friends and by inflicting harm on enemies,

children.text: nṛpa-saṃśraya iṣyate budhair jaṭharaṃ ko na bibharti kevalam ||Panc_1.22||
children.translated_text: the wise seek the shelter of a king — who does not merely fill his belly? // Panc_1.22 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yasmiñ jīvanti jīvanti bahavaḥ so 'tra jīvatu |
children.translated_text: He in whose living many others live — let him live!

children.text: vayāṃsi kiṃ na kurvanti cañcvā svodara-pūraṇam ||Panc_1.23||
children.translated_text: Do not birds fill their bellies with their beaks? // Panc_1.23 //

children.text: tathā ca-
yaj jīvyate kṣaṇam api prathitaṃ manuṣyair
children.translated_text: That life alone which, even if lived but a moment, is renowned among men,

children.text: vijñāna-śaurya-vibhavārya-guṇaiḥ sametam |
children.translated_text: endowed with the noble qualities of knowledge, valor, and prosperity —

children.text: tan nāma jīvitam iha pravadanti taj-jñāḥ
children.translated_text: that alone the wise call 'life' in this world;

children.text: kāko 'pi jīvati cirāya baliṃ ca bhuṅkte ||Panc_1.24||
children.translated_text: even a crow lives long and eats scraps of offerings. // Panc_1.24 //
And also:

children.text: yo nātmanā na ca pareṇa ca bandhu-varge
children.translated_text: He who shows no compassion to himself, to others, or to his kinsmen

children.text: dīne dayāṃ na kurute na ca martya-varge |
children.translated_text: when they are in distress, nor to the human race —

children.text: kiṃ tasya jīvita-phalaṃ hi manuṣya-loke
children.translated_text: what is the fruit of his life in this world of men?

children.text: kāko 'pi jīvati cirāya baliṃ ca bhuṅkte ||Panc_1.25||
children.translated_text: Even a crow lives long and eats scraps of offerings. // Panc_1.25 //

children.text: supūrā syāt kunadikā supūro mūṣikāñjaliḥ |
children.translated_text: A small stream is easily filled; a mouse's cupped hands are easily filled;

children.text: susaṃtuṣṭaḥ kāpuruṣaḥ svalpakenāpi tuṣyati ||Panc_1.26||
children.translated_text: a worthless man is easily contented — he is satisfied with even a trifle. // Panc_1.26 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: kiṃ tena jātu jātena māṭur yauvana-hāriṇā |
children.translated_text: What use is the birth of one who robs his mother's youth

children.text: ārohati na yaḥ svasya vaṃśasyāgre dhvajo yathā ||Panc_1.27||
children.translated_text: but does not rise like a banner at the head of his family line? // Panc_1.27 //

children.text: parivartini saṃsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate |
children.translated_text: In the revolving cycle of existence, who that has died is not born again?

children.text: jātas tu gaṇyate so 'tra yaḥ sphurec ca śriyādhikaḥ ||Panc_1.28||
children.translated_text: But only he is counted in this world who shines forth resplendent with glory. // Panc_1.28 //

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: jātasya nadī-tīre tasyāpi tṛṇasya janma-sāphalyam |
children.translated_text: Even for a blade of grass born on a riverbank, birth is fruitful,

children.text: yat salila-majjanākula-jana-hastālambanaṃ bhavati ||Panc_1.29||
children.translated_text: if it becomes a handhold for people struggling as they drown in the water. // Panc_1.29 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: stimitonnata-sañcārā jana-santāpa-hāriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Moving with calm dignity, dispelling the sorrows of people,

children.text: jāyante viralā loke jaladā iva sajjanāḥ ||Panc_1.30||
children.translated_text: the virtuous arise rarely in the world — like rain-clouds. // Panc_1.30 //

children.text: niratiśayaṃ garimāṇaṃ tena
children.translated_text: The wise recall the unsurpassed weightiness

children.text: jananyāḥ smaranti vidvāṃsaḥ |
children.translated_text: of a mother from this:

children.text: yat kam api vahati garbhaṃ
children.translated_text: she bears in her womb someone unknown,

children.text: mahatām api yo gurur bhavati ||Panc_1.31||
children.translated_text: who becomes the teacher even of the great. // Panc_1.31 //

children.text: aprakaṭīkṛta-śaktiḥ śakto 'pi janas tiraskriyāṃ labhate |
children.translated_text: A person whose power has not been displayed, though capable, receives contempt;

children.text: nivasann antar-dāruṇi laṅghyo vahnir na tu jvalitaḥ ||Panc_1.32||
children.translated_text: fire dwelling within wood may be disregarded, but not when blazing. // Panc_1.32 //

children.text: karaṭaka āha- āvāṃ tāvad apradhānau tat kim āvayor anena vyāpareṇa |
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'We are of no consequence. So what business is this of ours?

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: For it is said:'

children.text: apṛṣṭo 'trāpradhāno yo brūte rājñaḥ puraḥ kudhīḥ |
children.translated_text: A fool of no consequence who speaks unasked before the king

children.text: na kevalam asaṃmānaṃ labhate ca viḍambanam ||Panc_1.33||
children.translated_text: receives not only disrespect but also humiliation. // Panc_1.33 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: vacas tatra prayoktavyaṃ yatroktaṃ labhate phalam |
children.translated_text: Words should be spoken where what is said bears fruit

children.text: sthāyī bhavati cātyantaṃ rāgaḥ śukla-paṭe yathā ||Panc_1.34||
children.translated_text: and where the impression remains permanently — like dye on a white cloth. // Panc_1.34 //

children.text: damaka āha- mā maivaṃ vada |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Don't speak thus!

children.text: apradhānaḥ pradhānaḥ syāt sevate yadi pārthivam |
children.translated_text: One of no consequence becomes consequential if he serves a king;

children.text: pradhāno 'py apradhānaḥ syād yadi sevā-vivarjitaḥ ||Panc_1.35||
children.translated_text: one who is consequential becomes of no consequence if devoid of service. // Panc_1.35 //

children.text: yata uktaṃ ca-
āsannam eva nṛpatir bhajate manuṣyaṃ
children.translated_text: A king favors the person who is near,

children.text: vidyā-vihīnam akulīnam asaṃskṛtaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: even one lacking learning, of no family, or uncultured;

children.text: prāyeṇa bhūmi-patayaḥ pramadā latāś ca
children.translated_text: generally, rulers, women, and creepers

children.text: yat pārśvato bhavati tat pariveṣṭayanti ||Panc_1.36||
children.translated_text: embrace whatever is beside them. // Panc_1.36 //
For it is also said:

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: kopa-prasāda-vastūni ye vicinvanti sevakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Servants who discern the matters that cause [the king's] anger and pleasure

children.text: ārohanti śanaiḥ paścād dhunvantam api pārthivam ||Panc_1.37||
children.translated_text: gradually rise, even if the king dismisses [them]. // Panc_1.37 //

children.text: vidyāvatāṃ mahecchānāṃ śilpa-vikrama-śālinām |
children.translated_text: For the learned, the greatly ambitious, those endowed with skill and valor,

children.text: sevā-vṛtti-vidāṃ caiva nāśrayaḥ pārthivaṃ vinā ||Panc_1.38||
children.translated_text: and those who know the ways of service — there is no refuge without a king. // Panc_1.38 //

children.text: ye jāty-ādi-mahotsāhān narendrān nopayānti ca |
children.translated_text: Those who, despite being born to great enterprise, do not approach kings —

children.text: teṣām āmaraṇaṃ bhikṣā prāyaścittaṃ vinirmitam ||Panc_1.39||
children.translated_text: for them, begging until death has been ordained as their penance. // Panc_1.39 //

children.text: ye ca prāhur durātmāno durārādhyā mahībhujaḥ |
children.translated_text: And those wicked ones who say 'kings are hard to please' —

children.text: pramādālasya-jāḍyāni khyāpitāni nijāni taiḥ ||Panc_1.40||
children.translated_text: they [merely] proclaim their own negligence, laziness, and stupidity. // Panc_1.40 //

children.text: sarpān vyāghrān gajān siṃhān dṛṣṭvopāyair vaśīkṛtān |
children.translated_text: Seeing serpents, tigers, elephants, and lions brought under control by stratagems —

children.text: rājeti kiyatī mātrā dhīmatām apramādinām ||Panc_1.41||
children.translated_text: what is a king in comparison, for the wise and vigilant? // Panc_1.41 //

children.text: rājānam eva saṃśritya vidvān yāti parāṃ gatim |
children.translated_text: Only by taking refuge with a king does a learned man attain the highest goal;

children.text: vinā malayam anyatra candanaṃ na prarohati ||Panc_1.42||
children.translated_text: sandalwood does not grow anywhere except on the <s>Malaya</s> [mountain]. // Panc_1.42 //

children.text: dhavalāny ātapatrāṇi vājinaś ca manoramāḥ |
children.translated_text: White parasols, delightful horses,

children.text: sadā mattāś ca mātaṅgāḥ prasanne sati bhūpatau ||Panc_1.43||
children.translated_text: and ever-intoxicated elephants [come] when the king is pleased. // Panc_1.43 //

children.text: karaṭaka āha- atha bhavān kiṃ kartumanāḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Then what does your honor intend to do?'

children.text: so 'bravīt- adyāsmat-svāmī piṅgalako bhīto bhīta-parivāraś ca vartate | tadainaṃ gatvā bhaya-kāraṇaṃ vijñāya sandhi-vigraha-yāna-āsana-saṃśraya-dvaidhī-bhāvānām ekatamena saṃvidhāsye |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Today our master <s>Piṅgalaka</s> is frightened, and his retinue too is frightened. I shall go to him, learn the cause of his fear, and deal with it by one of the [six expedients]: alliance, war, marching, sitting, seeking shelter, or duplicity.'

children.text: karaṭaka āha- kathaṃ vetti bhavān yad bhayāviṣṭo 'yaṃ svāmī ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'How does your honor know that our master is gripped by fear?'

children.text: so 'bravīt- jñeyaṃ kim atra ? yata uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'What is there to know? For it is said:'

children.text: udīrito 'rthaḥ paśunāpi gṛhate
children.translated_text: Even a beast grasps a meaning when expressed;

children.text: hayāś ca nāgāś ca vahanti coditāḥ |
children.translated_text: horses and elephants carry [burdens] when urged on;

children.text: anuktam apy ūhati paṇḍito janaḥ
children.translated_text: but a wise man infers even what is unexpressed —

children.text: pareṅgita-jñāna-phjalā hi buddhayaḥ ||Panc_1.44||
children.translated_text: for the intellects [of the wise] bear the fruit of knowing others' gestures. // Panc_1.44 //

children.text: tathā ca manuḥ (8.26)-
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Manu</s> [says] (8.26):

children.text: ākārair iṅgitair gatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣaṇena ca |
children.translated_text: By appearances, gestures, gait, actions, and speech,

children.text: netra-vaktra-vikāraiś ca lakṣyate'ntargataṃ manaḥ ||Panc_1.45||
children.translated_text: and by changes of the eyes and face, the inner mind is discerned. // Panc_1.45 //

children.text: tad adyainaṃ bhayākulaṃ prāpya sva-buddhi-prabhāvena nirbhayaṃ kṛtvā vaśīkṛtya ca nijāṃ sācivya-padavīṃ samāsādayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: So today, having approached him while he is agitated with fear, I shall render him fearless by the power of my intellect, bring him under control, and thereby attain the position of minister for myself.'

children.text: karaṭaka āha- anabhijño bhavān sevā-dharmasya | tat katham enaṃ vaśīkariṣyasi ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'You are unfamiliar with the duties of service. How then will you bring him under control?'

children.text: so 'bravīt- katham ahaṃ sevānabhijñaḥ ? mayā hi tātotsaṅge krīḍatābhyāgata-sādhūnāṃ nīti-śāstraṃ paṭhatā yac chrutaṃ sevā-dharmasya sāraṃ tad hṛdi sthāpitam | śrūyatāṃ tac cedam-
children.translated_text: He said: 'How am I unfamiliar with service? For when I was playing in my father's lap, I heard the <s>Nītiśāstra</s> (science of polity) being recited by visiting sages, and I fixed in my heart the essence of the duties of service. Listen to it now:'

children.text: suvarṇa-puṣpitāṃ pṛthvīṃ vicinvanti narās trayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Three kinds of men harvest the earth that blossoms with gold:

children.text: śūraś ca kṛta-vidyaś ca yaś ca jānāti sevitum ||Panc_1.46||
children.translated_text: the hero, the learned, and he who knows how to serve. // Panc_1.46 //

children.text: sā sevā yā prabhu-hitā grāhyā vākya-viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: True service is that which benefits the master; it should be performed with discrimination of words;

children.text: āśrayet pārthivaṃ vidvāṃs tad-dvāreṇaiva nānyathā ||Panc_1.47||
children.translated_text: a wise man should take refuge with a king — through that [service] alone, not otherwise. // Panc_1.47 //

children.text: yo na vetti guṇān yasya na taṃ seveta paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wise man should not serve one whose virtues he does not know;

children.text: na hi tasmāt phalaṃ kiñcit sukṛṣṭād ūṣarād iva ||Panc_1.48||
children.translated_text: for no fruit comes from it — like well-plowed barren soil. // Panc_1.48 //

children.text: dravya-kṛti-hīno 'pi sevyaḥ sevya-guṇānvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even one lacking wealth and possessions, if endowed with the qualities of one worth serving, should be served;

children.text: bhavaty ājīvanaṃ tasmāt phalaṃ kālāntarād api ||Panc_1.49||
children.translated_text: livelihood comes from such [a master], and fruit in due time as well. // Panc_1.49 //

children.text: api sthāṇuvad āsīnaḥ śuṣyan parigataḥ kṣudhā |
children.translated_text: Even sitting motionless like a post, withering and consumed by hunger,

children.text: na tv ajñānātma-sampannād vṛttim īhate paṇḍitaḥ ||Panc_1.50||
children.translated_text: a wise man does not seek livelihood from one possessed of ignorance. // Panc_1.50 //

children.text: sevakaḥ svāminaṃ dveṣṭi kṛpaṇaṃ paruṣākṣaram |
children.translated_text: A servant hates a master who is miserly and harsh of speech;

children.text: ātmānaṃ kiṃ sa na dveṣṭi sevyāsevyaṃ na vetti yaḥ ||Panc_1.51||
children.translated_text: does he not hate himself — he who cannot distinguish between one worth serving and one not? // Panc_1.51 //

children.text: yasyāśritya viśrāmaṃ kṣudhārtā yānti sevakāḥ |
children.translated_text: That king to whose shelter hungry servants come for rest —

children.text: so 'rkavan nṛpatis tyājyaḥ sadā puṣpa-phalo 'pi san ||Panc_1.52||
children.translated_text: if [they find none], he should be abandoned like the sun, even though he always has flowers and fruit. // Panc_1.52 //

children.text: rāja-mātari devyāṃ ca kumāre mukhya-mantriṇi |
children.translated_text: Toward the king's mother, the queen, the prince, the chief minister,

children.text: purohite pratīhāre sadā varteta rājavat ||Panc_1.53||
children.translated_text: the family priest, and the chamberlain, one should always behave as toward the king himself. // Panc_1.53 //

children.text: jīveti prabruvan proktaḥ kṛtyākṛtya-vicakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, being addressed, declares the right and wrong courses [without being asked],

children.text: karoti nirvikalpaṃ yaḥ sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.54||
children.translated_text: and acts without hesitation — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.54 //

children.text: prabhu-prasādajaṃ vittaṃ suprāptaṃ yo nivedayet |
children.translated_text: One who reports wealth obtained by the king's grace as properly received,

children.text: vastrādyaṃ ca dadhāty aṅge sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.55||
children.translated_text: and wears garments and the like [given by the king] on his person — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.55 //

children.text: antaḥ-pura-caraiḥ sārdhaṃ yo na mantraṃ samācaret |
children.translated_text: One who does not plot with those who move within the inner chambers,

children.text: na kalatrair narendrasya sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.56||
children.translated_text: nor with the king's wives — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.56 //

children.text: dyūtaṃ yo yama-dūtābhaṃ hālāṃ hālāhalopamam |
children.translated_text: One who regards gambling as akin to the messenger of death, liquor as akin to poison,

children.text: paśyed dārān vṛthākārān sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.57||
children.translated_text: and other men's wives as vain appearances — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.57 //

children.text: yuddha-kāle'graṇīr yaḥ syāt sadā pṛṣṭhānugaḥ pure |
children.translated_text: One who is in the vanguard in time of battle, and always follows behind in the city,

children.text: prabhor dvārāśrito harmye sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.58||
children.translated_text: and waits at the master's door at the mansion — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.58 //

children.text: sammato 'haṃ vibhor nityam iti matvā vyatikramet |
children.translated_text: One who, thinking 'I am always esteemed by the lord,' never transgresses

children.text: kṛcchreṣv api na maryādāṃ sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.59||
children.translated_text: propriety even in difficulties — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.59 //

children.text: dveṣi-dveṣa-paro nityam iṣṭānām iṣṭa-karma-kṛt |
children.translated_text: One who is always hostile to the lord's enemies and performs pleasing deeds for his favorites —

children.text: yo naro nara-nāthasya sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.60||
children.translated_text: that man of the king of men becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.60 //

children.text: proktaḥ pratyuttaraṃ nāha viruddhaṃ prabhunā na yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, when addressed, does not give a contrary reply to the master,

children.text: na samīpe hasaty uccaiḥ sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.61||
children.translated_text: and does not laugh loudly in his presence — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.61 //

children.text: up raṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ tadvan manyate bhaya-varjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, free from fear, regards the battlefield as a refuge just like [a safe haven],

children.text: pravāsaṃ sva-purāvāsaṃ sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.62||
children.translated_text: and foreign travel as [equal to] dwelling in his own city — he becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.62 //

children.text: na kuryān naranāthasya yoṣidbhiḥ saha saṃgatim |
children.translated_text: One should not associate with the king's women,

children.text: na nindāṃ na vivādaṃ ca sa bhaved rāja-vallabhaḥ ||Panc_1.63||
children.translated_text: nor slander [the king], nor quarrel [with him] — [such a person] becomes a royal favorite. // Panc_1.63 //

children.text: karaṭaka āha- atha bhavāṃs tatra gatvā kiṃ tāvat prathamaṃ vakṣyati tat tāvad ucyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'When you go there, what will you say first? Let that be told.'

children.text: damanaka āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said:

children.text: uttarād uttaraṃ vākyaṃ vadatāṃ samprajāyate |
children.translated_text: From one utterance, ever more utterances arise among those who are speaking —

children.text: suvṛṣṭi-guṇa-sampannād bījād bījam ivāparam ||Panc_1.64||
children.translated_text: like seed from seed born of a well-watered, quality-endowed [field]. // Panc_1.64 //

children.text: apāya-sandarśanajāṃ vipattim
children.translated_text: The ruin born from perceiving dangers,

children.text: upāya-sandarśanajāṃ ca siddhim |
children.translated_text: and the success born from perceiving remedies —

children.text: medhāvino nīti-guṇa-prayuktāṃ
children.translated_text: the wise, employing the virtues of statecraft,

children.text: puraḥ sphurantīm iva varṇayanti ||Panc_1.65||
children.translated_text: describe [these] as if flashing before their eyes. // Panc_1.65 //

children.text: ekeṣāṃ vāci śukavad anyeṣāṃ hṛdi mūkavat |
children.translated_text: For some, fine words are on the tongue like a parrot; for others, in the heart like a mute;

children.text: hṛdi vāci tathānyeṣāṃ valgu valgantiu sūktayaḥ ||Panc_1.66||
children.translated_text: but for yet others, fine words resonate beautifully both in the heart and on the tongue. // Panc_1.66 //

children.text: na ca aham aprāpta-kālaṃ vakṣye | ākarṇitaṃ mayā nīti-sāraṃ pituḥ pūrvam utsaṅgaṃ hi niṣevatā |
children.translated_text: And I will not speak at the wrong time. I have heard the essence of statecraft from my father, while sitting formerly upon his lap.

children.text: aprāpta-kālaṃ vacanaṃ bṛhaspatir api bruvan |
children.translated_text: Even <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, if he speaks words at the wrong time,

children.text: labhate bahv-avajñānam apamānaṃ ca puṣkalam ||Panc_1.67||
children.translated_text: receives much contempt and abundant disrespect. ||Panc_1.67||

children.text: karaṭaka āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said —

children.text: durārādhyā hi rājānaḥ parvatā iva sarvadā |
children.translated_text: Kings are always hard to please, like mountains —

children.text: vyālākīrṇāḥ suviṣamāḥ kaṭhinā duṣṭa-sevitāḥ ||Panc_1.68||
children.translated_text: infested with serpents, very rugged, hard, and frequented by the wicked. ||Panc_1.68||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: bhoginaḥ kañcukāviṣṭāḥ kuṭilāḥ krūra-ceṣṭitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Wealthy ones, enclosed in armor, crooked, of cruel conduct —

children.text: suduṣṭā mantra-sādhyāś ca rājānaḥ pannagā iva ||Panc_1.69||
children.translated_text: very wicked and to be won only by counsel — kings are like serpents. ||Panc_1.69||

children.text: dvi-jihvāḥ krūra-karmāṇo 'niṣṭhāś chidrānusāriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Double-tongued, of cruel deeds, faithless, seeking out weak points —

children.text: dūrato 'pi hi paśyanti rājāno bhujagā iva ||Panc_1.70||
children.translated_text: kings see from afar, like snakes. ||Panc_1.70||

children.text: svalpam apy apakurvanti ye'bhīṣṭā hi mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who do even slight harm to a king's favorites —

children.text: te vahnāv iva dahyante pataṅgāḥ pāpa-cetasaḥ ||Panc_1.71||
children.translated_text: they are burned as moths in fire, those of evil mind. ||Panc_1.71||

children.text: durārohaṃ padaṃ rājñāṃ sarva-loka-namaskṛtam |
children.translated_text: The position of kings, bowed to by all the world, is hard to ascend —

children.text: svalpenāpy apakāreṇa brāhmaṇyam iva duṣyati ||Panc_1.72||
children.translated_text: it is spoiled even by a slight offense, like Brahminhood. ||Panc_1.72||

children.text: durārādhyāḥ śriyo rājñāṃ durāpā duṣparigrahāḥ |
children.translated_text: The fortunes of kings are hard to please, hard to win, hard to maintain —

children.text: tiṣṭhanty āpa ivādhāre ciram ātmani saṃsthitāḥ ||Panc_1.73||
children.translated_text: they remain, like water in a vessel, established in oneself for but a while. ||Panc_1.73||

children.text: damanaka āha- satyam etat param | kintu-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said — That is entirely true. However —

children.text: yasya yasya hi yo bhāvas tena tena samācaret |
children.translated_text: Whatever disposition anyone has, one should behave accordingly —

children.text: anupraviśya medhāvī kṣipram ātma-vaśaṃ nayet ||Panc_1.74||
children.translated_text: the wise one, having entered into [the master's confidence], should quickly bring him under his control. ||Panc_1.74||

children.text: bhartuś cittānuvartitvaṃ suvṛttaṃ cānujīvinām |
children.translated_text: Conformity to the master's mind is good conduct for dependents;

children.text: rākṣasāś cāpi gṛhyante nityaṃ chandānuvartibhiḥ ||Panc_1.75||
children.translated_text: even <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) are captured by those who constantly follow their whims. ||Panc_1.75||

children.text: saruṣi nṛpe stuti-vacanaṃ tad-abhimate prema tad-dviṣi dveṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the king is angry, words of praise; affection for what he likes, hatred for what he hates;

children.text: tad-dānasya ca śaṃsā amantra-tantraṃ vaśīkaraṇam ||Panc_1.76||
children.translated_text: praise of his generosity — this is subjugation without mantras or stratagems. ||Panc_1.76||

children.text: karaṭaka āha- yady evam abhimataṃ tarhi śivās te panthānaḥ santu | yathābhilaṣitam anuṣṭhīyatām | so 'pi praṇamya piṅgalakābhimukhaṃ pratasthe |
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said — If that is your resolve, then may your paths be auspicious! Let it be done as you wish. And he [<s>Damanaka</s>], having bowed, set out toward <s>Piṅgalaka</s>.

children.text: athāgacchantaṃ damanakam ālokya piṅgalako dvāstham abravīt- apasāryatāṃ vetra-latā | ayam asmākaṃ cirantano mantriputro damanako 'vyāhata-praveśaḥ | tat praveśyatāṃ dvitīya-maṇḍala-bhāgī | iti |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Damanaka</s> approaching, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said to the doorkeeper: Let the bamboo-staff barrier be removed! This <s>Damanaka</s> is our long-standing minister's son, with unobstructed access. Let him be admitted as a member of the second circle.

children.text: sa āha- yathāvādīd bhavān iti |
children.translated_text: He said: As Your Lordship commands.

children.text: athopasṛtya damanako nirdiṣṭa āsane piṅgalakaṃ praṇamya prāptānujña upaviṣṭaḥ | sa tu tasya naka-kuliśālaṅkṛtaṃ dakṣiṇa-pāṇim upari dattvā māna-puraḥ-saram uvāca- api śivaṃ bhavataḥ | kasmāc cirād dṛṣṭo 'si ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Damanaka</s>, having approached and been shown to the designated seat, bowed to <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, received permission, and sat down. And [<s>Piṅgalaka</s>], placing upon [<s>Damanaka</s>'s head] his right paw adorned with claw-thunderbolts, spoke with honor first: Is all well with you? Why have you been seen after so long?

children.text: damanaka āha- na kiṃcid deva-pādānām asmābhiḥ prayojanam | paraṃ bhavatāṃ prāpta-kālaṃ vaktavyam yata uttama-madhyamādhamaiḥ sarvair api rājñāṃ prayojanam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: There is nothing that Your Lordship's servants need [for themselves]. But there is something timely to be said to you, since kings have use for all — the highest, middling, and lowest. And it is said —

children.text: dantasya niṣkoṣaṇakena nityaṃ
children.translated_text: By a splinter for cleaning teeth constantly,

children.text: karṇasya kaṇḍūyanakena vāpi |
children.translated_text: or by [a stick] for scratching the ear —

children.text: tṛṇena kāryaṃ bhavatīśvarāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: even by a blade of grass, a task of lords is accomplished;

children.text: kim āṅga vāggha-stavatā nareṇa ||Panc_1.77||
children.translated_text: what then of a man endowed with eloquence? ||Panc_1.77||

children.text: tathā vayaṃ deva-pādānām anvayāgatā bhṛtyā āpatsv api pṛṣṭha-gāmino yadyapi svam adhikāraṃ na labhāmahe tathāpi deva-pādānām etad yuktaṃ na bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Thus we are servants of Your Lordship inherited by lineage, following even in adversity. Even if we do not receive our own post, still it is not proper for Your Lordship [to neglect us]. And it is said —

children.text: sthāneṣv eva niyoktavyā bhṛtyā ābharaṇāni ca |
children.translated_text: Servants and ornaments should be employed in their proper places;

children.text: na hi cūḍāmaṇiḥ pāde prabhavāmīti badhyate ||Panc_1.78||
children.translated_text: a crest-jewel is not tied to the foot [saying] 'I am capable.' ||Panc_1.78||

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For —

children.text: anabhijño guṇānāṃ yo na bhṛtyair anugamyate |
children.translated_text: One who is unaware of [his servants'] merits is not followed by servants,

children.text: dhanāḍhyo 'pi kulīno 'pi kramāYāto 'pi bhūpatiḥ ||Panc_1.79||
children.translated_text: even if he is rich, of noble birth, or a hereditary king. ||Panc_1.79||

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
asamaiḥ samīyamānaḥ samaiś ca
children.translated_text: Being treated equally with unequals, and with equals

children.text: parihīyamāṇa-sat-kāraḥ |
children.translated_text: having his honor diminished,

children.text: dhuri yo na yujyamānas tribhir
children.translated_text: and not being yoked to the foremost position — for these three [reasons]

children.text: artha-patiṃ tyajati bhṛtyaḥ ||Panc_1.80||
children.translated_text: a servant abandons even a wealthy master. ||Panc_1.80||
And it is said —

children.text: yac cāvivekitayā rājñā bhṛtyānuttama-pada-yogyān hīnādhama-sthāne niyojayati, na te tatraiva sa bhūpater doṣo na teṣām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And when a king, through lack of discernment, assigns servants worthy of the highest position to a low and inferior station — that is the king's fault, not theirs. And it is said —

children.text: kanaka-bhūṣaṇa-saṅgrahaṇocito
children.translated_text: A gem worthy of being set in gold ornaments,

children.text: yadi maṇis trapuṇi pratibadhyate |
children.translated_text: if it is fastened in tin —

children.text: na sa virauti na cāpi sa śobhate
children.translated_text: it neither shines nor is beautiful;

children.text: bhavati yojayitur vacanīyatā ||Panc_1.81||
children.translated_text: the blame falls on the one who placed it. ||Panc_1.81||

children.text: yac ca svāmy evaṃ vadati cirād dṛśyate | tad api śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: And as to the master saying 'you are seen after a long time' — let this too be heard —

children.text: savya-dakṣiṇayor yatra viśeṣo nāsti hastayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there is no distinction between the left and right hands,

children.text: kas tatra kṣaṇam apyāryo vidyamāna-gatir bhavet ||Panc_1.82||
children.translated_text: what noble person of established position would remain even for a moment? ||Panc_1.82||

children.text: kāce maṇir maṇau kāco yeṣāṃ buddhir vikalpate |
children.translated_text: Those who confuse glass for a gem and a gem for glass —

children.text: na teṣāṃ sannidhau bhṛtyo nāma-mātro 'pi tiṣṭhati ||Panc_1.83||
children.translated_text: in their presence, a servant does not remain even in name. ||Panc_1.83||

children.text: parīkṣakā yatra na santi deśe
children.translated_text: In a land where there are no discerning judges,

children.text: nārghanti ratnāni samudrajāni |
children.translated_text: ocean-born jewels have no value.

children.text: ābhīra-deśe kila candrakāntaṃ
children.translated_text: In the land of the <s>Ābhīras</s> (cowherds), it is said, a moonstone

children.text: tribhir varāṭair vipaṇanti gopāḥ ||Panc_1.84||
children.translated_text: is sold by herdsmen for three cowrie shells. ||Panc_1.84||

children.text: lohitākhyasya ca maṇeḥ padmarāgasya cāntaram |
children.translated_text: Where there is no [ability to see] the difference between a red stone and a ruby,

children.text: yatra nāsti kathaṃ tatra kriyate ratna-vikrayaḥ ||Panc_1.85||
children.translated_text: how can gem-trading be conducted there? ||Panc_1.85||

children.text: nirviśeṣaṃ yadā svāmī samaṃ bhṛtyeṣu vartate |
children.translated_text: When a master behaves toward his servants without distinction, equally,

children.text: tatrodyama-samarthānām utsāhaḥ parihīyate ||Panc_1.86||
children.translated_text: there the enthusiasm of those capable of exertion diminishes. ||Panc_1.86||

children.text: na vinā pārthivo bhṛtyair na bhṛtyāḥ pārthivaṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: A king cannot [exist] without servants, nor servants without a king;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca vyavahāro 'yaṃ paraspara-nibandhanaḥ ||Panc_1.87||
children.translated_text: their interaction is mutually dependent. ||Panc_1.87||

children.text: bhṛtyair vinā svayaṃ rājā lokānugraha-kāribhiḥ |
children.translated_text: A king himself, without servants who act for the welfare of the people,

children.text: mayūkhair iva dīptāṃśus tejasvy api na śobhate ||Panc_1.88||
children.translated_text: even though radiant, does not shine — like the sun without its rays. ||Panc_1.88||

children.text: araiḥ sandhāryate nābhir nābhau cārāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: The hub is held by the spokes, and the spokes are established on the hub;

children.text: svāmi-sevakayor evaṃ vṛtti-cakraṃ pravartate ||Panc_1.89||
children.translated_text: thus between master and servant, the wheel of livelihood revolves. ||Panc_1.89||

children.text: śirasā vidhṛtā nityaṃ snehena paripālitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Always borne on the head, nurtured with affection —

children.text: keśā api virajyante niḥsnehāḥ kiṃ na sevakāḥ ||Panc_1.90||
children.translated_text: even hairs fall out when without oil; what then of servants? ||Panc_1.90||

children.text: rājā tuṣṭo hi bhṛtyānām artha-mātraṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: A pleased king gives servants only wealth;

children.text: te tu saṃmāna-mātreṇa prāṇair apy upakurvate ||Panc_1.91||
children.translated_text: but they, for mere respect alone, serve even with their lives. ||Panc_1.91||

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā narendreṇa bhṛtyāḥ kāryā vicakṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Knowing this, a king should employ servants [who are] discerning,

children.text: kulīnāḥ śaurya-saṃyuktāḥ śaktā bhaktāḥ kramāgatāḥ ||Panc_1.92||
children.translated_text: of noble birth, endowed with valor, capable, devoted, and hereditary. ||Panc_1.92||

children.text: yaḥ kṛtvā sukṛtaṃ rājño duṣkaraṃ hitam uttamam |
children.translated_text: He who, having accomplished a difficult, beneficial, and excellent deed for the king,

children.text: lajjayā vakti no kiñcit tena rājā sahāyavān ||Panc_1.93||
children.translated_text: out of modesty says nothing — through him the king becomes well-supported. ||Panc_1.93||

children.text: yasmin kṛtyaṃ samāveśya nirviśaṅkena cetasā |
children.translated_text: That servant in whom one can entrust a task and then

children.text: āsyate sevakaḥ sa syāt kalatram iva cāparam ||Panc_1.94||
children.translated_text: rest with an unworried mind — he is like a second wife. ||Panc_1.94||

children.text: yo 'nāhūtaḥ samabhyeti dvāri tiṣṭhati sarvadā |
children.translated_text: He who comes without being summoned, always stands at the door,

children.text: pṛṣṭhaḥ satyaṃ mitaṃ brūte sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.95||
children.translated_text: and when asked, speaks truthfully and briefly — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.95||

children.text: anādiṣṭo 'pi bhūpasya dṛṣṭvā hānikaraṃ ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, even without being commanded, seeing what is harmful to the king,

children.text: yatate tasya nāśāya sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.96||
children.translated_text: strives for its destruction — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.96||

children.text: tāḍito 'pi durukto 'pi daṇḍito 'pi mahībhujā |
children.translated_text: He who, even when beaten, spoken to harshly, or punished by the king,

children.text: yo na cintayate pāpaṃ sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.97||
children.translated_text: does not think evil — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.97||

children.text: na garvaṃ kurute māne nāpamāne ca tapyate |
children.translated_text: He who does not become proud when honored, nor burns when dishonored,

children.text: svākāraṃ rakṣayed yas tu sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.98||
children.translated_text: and guards his own composure — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.98||

children.text: na kṣudhā pīḍyate yas tu nidrayā na kadācana |
children.translated_text: He who is never afflicted by hunger or by sleep,

children.text: na ca śītātapādyaiś ca sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.99||
children.translated_text: nor by cold, heat, and the like — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.99||

children.text: śrutvā sāṃgrāmikīṃ vārtāṃ bhaviṣyāṃ svāminaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: He who, upon hearing news of an impending battle concerning his master,

children.text: prasannāsyo bhaved yas tu sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.100||
children.translated_text: becomes cheerful of face — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.100||

children.text: sīmā vṛddhiṃ samāyāti śukla-pakṣa ivoḍurāṭ |
children.translated_text: The boundary grows, like the moon in the bright fortnight,

children.text: niyoga-saṃsthite yasmin sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||Panc_1.101||
children.translated_text: in whichever [territory] he is posted — that servant is worthy of kings. ||Panc_1.101||

children.text: sīmā saṃkocam āyāti vahnau carma ivāhitam |
children.translated_text: The boundary contracts, like leather placed in fire,

children.text: sthite yasmin sa tu tyājyo bhṛtyo rājyaṃ samīhatā ||Panc_1.102||
children.translated_text: where he is posted — that servant should be dismissed, [for he] covets the kingdom. ||Panc_1.102||

children.text: tathā śṛgālo 'yam iti manyamānena mamopari svāminā yady avajñā kriyate tad apy ayuktam | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And if my master, thinking 'this is only a jackal,' treats me with contempt, even that is improper. And it is said, for —

children.text: kauśeyaṃ kṛmijaṃ suvarṇam upalād durvāpi goromataḥ
children.translated_text: Silk comes from a worm, gold from stone, <s>dūrvā</s> grass is considered [to come] from cow-hair,

children.text: paṅkāt tāmarasaṃ śaśāṅka udadher indīvaraṃ gomayāt |
children.translated_text: the lotus from mud, the moon from the ocean, the blue lotus from cow-dung,

children.text: kāṣṭhād agnir aheḥ phaṇād api maṇir go-pittato rocanā
children.translated_text: fire from wood, a jewel from a snake's hood, <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment) from ox-bile —

children.text: prākāśyaṃ sva-guṇodayena guṇino gacchanti kiṃ janmanā ||Panc_1.103||
children.translated_text: the meritorious attain fame through the arising of their own qualities; what [matters] birth? ||Panc_1.103||

children.text: mūṣikā gṛha-jātāpi hantavyā svāpa-kāriṇī |
children.translated_text: A household mouse, though home-born, should be killed if it causes loss;

children.text: bhakṣya-pradānair jāro hitakṛt prāpyate janaiḥ ||Panc_1.104||
children.translated_text: a stranger who benefits [one] is obtained by people through offerings of food. ||Panc_1.104||

children.text: eraṇḍa-bhiṇḍārka-nalaiḥ prabhūtair api sañcitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Even with <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), <s>bhiṇḍī</s> (okra), <s>arka</s> (milkweed), and reeds accumulated in abundance,

children.text: dāru-kṛtyaṃ yathā nāsti tathaivājñaiḥ prayojanam ||Panc_1.105||
children.translated_text: the purpose of timber is not [served] — so too is the use of the ignorant. ||Panc_1.105||

children.text: kiṃ bhaktenāsamarthena kiṃ śakternāpakāriṇā |
children.translated_text: What use is a devotee who is incapable? What use is a capable one who does harm?

children.text: bhaktaṃ śaktaṃ ca māṃ rājan nāvajñātuṃ tvam arhasi ||Panc_1.106||
children.translated_text: I am both devoted and capable, O king — you should not despise me. ||Panc_1.106||

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- bhavatv evaṃ tāvat | asamarthaḥ samartho vā cirantanas tvam asmākaṃ mantri-putraḥ | tad viśrabdhaṃ brūhi yat kiñcid vaktukāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Very well then. Whether capable or incapable, you are our long-standing minister's son. So speak freely whatever you wish to say.

children.text: damanaka āha- deva jijñāpyaṃ kiñcid asti |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: Lord, there is something to be reported.

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- tan nivedayābhipretam |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Then declare what is on your mind.

children.text: so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text: api svalpataraṃ kāryaṃ yad bhavet pṛthivī-pateḥ |
children.translated_text: Even the slightest matter concerning a king

children.text: tan na vācyaṃ sabhā-madhye provācedaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ ||Panc_1.107||
children.translated_text: should not be spoken in the midst of an assembly — so declared <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. ||Panc_1.107||

children.text: tad aikāntike mad-vijñāpyam ākarṇayantu deva-pādāḥ | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Therefore let Your Lordship hear my submission in private. For —

children.text: ṣaṭ-karṇo bhidyate mantraś catuṣkarṇaḥ sthiro bhavet |
children.translated_text: A counsel [heard by] six ears is broken; [heard by] four ears, it remains firm.

children.text: tasmāt sarva-prayatnena ṣaṭkarṇaṃ varjayet sudhīḥ ||Panc_1.108||
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise one should by all effort avoid a six-eared [counsel]. ||Panc_1.108||

children.text: atha piṅgalakābhiprāyajñā vyāghra-dvīpi-vṛka-puraḥsarā sarve'pi tad-vacaḥ samākarṇya saṃsadi tat-kṣaṇād eva dūrībhūtāḥ | tataś ca damanaka āha- udaka-grahaṇārthaṃ pravṛttasya svāminaḥ kim iha nivṛttyāvasthānam |
children.translated_text: Then all — the tiger, leopard, and wolf at the forefront — knowing <s>Piṅgalaka</s>'s intention, upon hearing his words, immediately withdrew from the assembly. Then <s>Damanaka</s> said: Why does the master, who set out to get water, stop and remain here?

children.text: piṅgalaka āha savilakṣa-smitam- na kiñcid api |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said with an embarrassed smile: It is nothing.

children.text: so 'bravīt- deva yady anākhyeyaṃ tat tiṣṭhatu | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Lord, if it is not to be told, then let it be. And it is said —

children.text: dariṣu kiñcit svajaneṣu kiñcid
children.translated_text: Some [things are] to be concealed in caves, some among one's own people,

children.text: gopyaṃ vayasyeṣu suteṣu kiñcit |
children.translated_text: some among friends, some among children —

children.text: yuktaṃ na vā yuktam idaṃ vicintya
children.translated_text: having considered whether this is proper or improper,

children.text: vaded vipaścin mahato 'nurodhāt ||Panc_1.[*100]
children.translated_text: the wise one should speak, [moved] by regard for a great [person]. ||Panc_1.[*100]

children.text: tac chrutvā piṅgalakaś cintayāmāsa- yogyo 'yaṃ dṛśyate | tat kathayāmy etasyāgre ātmano 'bhiprāyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> thought: This one appears worthy. I shall tell him my own intention. And it is said —

children.text: svāmini guṇāntarajñe guṇavati bhṛtye'nuvartini kalaye |
children.translated_text: When the master discerns inner qualities, when the servant is virtuous and conforming, when the time is right,

children.text: suhṛdi nirantara-citte nivedya duḥkhaṃ sukhī bhavati ||Panc_1.[*101]
children.translated_text: when the friend is of undivided mind — having confided one's sorrow, one becomes happy. ||Panc_1.[*101]

children.text: bho damanaka śṛṇoṣi śabdaṃ dūrān mahāntam |
children.translated_text: O <s>Damanaka</s>, do you hear that great sound from afar?

children.text: so 'bravīt- svāmin śṛṇomi | tat kim |
children.translated_text: He said: Master, I hear it. What of it?

children.text:
piṅgalaka āha- bhadra aham asmād vanād gantum icchāmi |
damanaka āha- kasmāt |
children.translated_text:
<s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Friend, I wish to leave this forest.
<s>Damanaka</s> said: Why?

children.text: piṅgalaka āha - yato 'dyasmad-vane kim apy apūrvaṃ sattvaṃ praviṣṭaṃ yasyāyaṃ mahā-śabdaḥ śrūyate | tasya ca śabdānurūpeṇa parākrameṇa bhavitavyam iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Because today some unprecedented creature has entered our forest, whose great sound is heard. And its prowess must be proportionate to its sound.

children.text: damanaka āha- yac-chabda-mātrād api bhayam upagataḥ svāmī tad apy ayuktam | uktaṃ ca-
ambhasā bhidyate setus tathā mantro 'py arakṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A dam is broken by water; likewise a secret is [broken] when unguarded;

children.text: paiśunyād bhidyate sneho bhidyate vāgbhir āturaḥ ||Panc_1.111||
children.translated_text: affection is broken by slander; a sick person is broken by words. ||Panc_1.111||
<s>Damanaka</s> said: If the master is afraid merely from a sound, that too is improper. And it is said —

children.text: tan na yuktaṃ svāminaḥ pūrvopārjitaṃ vanaṃ tyaktum | yato bherī-veṇu-vīnā-mṛdaṅga-tāla-paṭaha-śaṅkha-kāhalādi-bhedena śabdā aneka-vidhā bhavanti | tan na kevalāc chabda-mātrād api bhetavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not proper for the master to abandon a forest acquired of old. For sounds are of many kinds — distinguished as drums, flutes, <s>vīṇās</s>, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, cymbals, kettledrums, conches, trumpets, and the like. So one should not be afraid merely from a sound. And it is said —

children.text: atyutkaṭe ca raudre ca śatrau prāpte na hīyate |
children.translated_text: He who, when a most fierce and terrible enemy arrives, does not lose

children.text: dhairyaṃ yasya mahīnātho na sa yāti parābhavam ||Panc_1.112||
children.translated_text: courage — that lord of the earth does not come to ruin. ||Panc_1.112||

children.text: darśita-bhaye'pi dhātari dhairya-dhvaṃso bhaven na dhīrāṇām |
children.translated_text: Even when fate shows [cause for] fear, the courageous do not suffer a collapse of fortitude.

children.text: śoṣita-sarasi nidāghe nitarām evoddhataḥ sindhuḥ ||Panc_1.113||
children.translated_text: When the lake is dried up in summer, the ocean is all the more swollen. ||Panc_1.113||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yasya na vipadi viṣādaḥ sampadi harṣo raṇe na bhīrutvam |
children.translated_text: He who has no despair in calamity, no elation in prosperity, and no cowardice in battle —

children.text: taṃ bhuvana-traya-tilakaṃ janayati jananī sutaṃ viralam ||Panc_1.114||
children.translated_text: such a son, the ornament of the three worlds, a mother rarely brings forth. ||Panc_1.114||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: śakti-vaikalya-namrasya niḥsāratvāl laghīyasaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is bowed down by weakness of power, who is light because of being without substance —

children.text: jannimo mānahīnasya tṛṇasya ca samā gatiḥ ||Panc_1.115||
children.translated_text: the fate of such a worthless person is equal to that of a blade of grass. ||Panc_1.115||

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: anya-pratāpam āsādya yo dṛḍhatvaṃ na gacchati |
children.translated_text: He who, encountering another's might, does not attain firmness —

children.text: jatujābharaṇasyeva rūpeṇāpi hi tasya kim ||Panc_1.116||
children.translated_text: what use is even his form, like that of a lac ornament? ||Panc_1.116||

children.text: tad evaṃ jñātvā svāminā dhairyāvaṣṭambhaḥ kāryaḥ | na śabda-mātrād bhetavyam | api ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing this, the master should maintain his composure. One should not be frightened merely by a sound. Moreover —

children.text: pūrvam eva mayā jñātaṃ pūrṇam etad dhi medasā |
children.translated_text: I knew beforehand that this was indeed full of fat;

children.text: anupraviśya vijñātaṃ yāvac carma ca dāru ca ||Panc_1.117||
children.translated_text: having entered, I discovered that it was only leather and wood. ||Panc_1.117||

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- katham etat |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: How is that?

children.text: so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text:
kathā 2
śṛgāla-dundubhi-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 2
The Story of the Jackal and the Drum

children.text: kaścid gomāyur nāma śṛgālaḥ kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭhaḥ itas tataḥ paribhraman vane sainya-dvaya-saṃgrāma-bhūmim apaśyat | tasyāṃ ca dundubheḥ patitasya vāyu-vaśād vallī-śākhāgrair hanyamānasya śabdam aśṛṇot | atha kṣubhita-hṛdayaś cintayāmāsa aho vinaṣṭo 'smi | tad yāvan nāsya proccārita-śabdasya dṛṣṭi-gocare gacchāmi tāvad anyato vrajāmi | athavā naitad yujyate sahasaiva |
children.translated_text: A jackal named <s>Gomāyu</s>, with a throat parched from hunger, wandering here and there in the forest, came upon a battlefield where two armies had fought. There he heard the sound of a drum that had fallen and was being struck by the tips of creeper-branches blown by the wind. Then, his heart agitated, he thought: 'Alas, I am lost! Let me go elsewhere before I come within sight of that which is making this sound.' But then [he thought]: 'No, this is not proper — [to act] so hastily.'

children.text: bhaye vā yadi vā harṣe samprāpte yo vimarśayet |
children.translated_text: He who deliberates when either fear or joy arrives,

children.text: kṛtyaṃ na kurute vegān na sa santāpam āpnuyāt ||Panc_1.118||
children.translated_text: and does not act impulsively — he does not come to grief. ||Panc_1.118||

children.text: tat tāvaj jānāmi kasyāyaṃ śabdaḥ | dhairyam ālambya vimarśayan yāvan mandaṃ mandaṃ gacchati tāvad dundubhim apaśyat | sa ca taṃ parijñāya samīpaṃ gatvā svayam eva kautukād atāḍayat | bhūyaś ca harṣād acintayat- aho cirād etad asmākaṃ mahodbhojanam āpatitam | tan nūnaṃ māṃsa-medo 'sṛgbhiḥ paripūritaṃ bhaviṣyati | tataḥ paruṣa-carmāvaguṇṭhitaṃ tat katham api vidāryaikadeśe chidraṃ kṛtvā saṃhṛṣṭa-manā madhye praviṣṭaḥ | paraṃ carma-vidāraṇato daṃṣṭrābhaṅgaḥ samajani | atha nirāśībhūtas tad-dāru-śeṣam avalokya ślokam enam apaṭhat pūrvam eva mayā jñātam iti | ato na śabda-mātrād bhetavyam |
children.translated_text: So let me first find out whose sound this is. Maintaining his courage and deliberating, as he slowly, slowly went forward, he saw the drum. And having recognized it, going near it, he struck it himself out of curiosity. And again he thought with delight: 'Ah! After a long time, a great feast has come our way! Surely it must be filled with meat, fat, and blood.' Then, having somehow torn open that [drum] wrapped in rough leather, making a hole in one spot, he entered inside with a joyful mind. But from tearing the leather, his fangs broke. Then, having become hopeless, looking at the remaining wood, he recited this verse: 'I knew beforehand...' Therefore one should not be frightened merely by a sound.

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- bhoḥ paśyāyaṃ mama sarvo 'pi parigraho bhaya-vyākulita-manāḥ palāyitum icchati | tat katham ahaṃ dhairyād avaṣṭambhaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Sir, look — all my retinue, with minds agitated by fear, wishes to flee! How then can I maintain my composure?

children.text: so 'bravīt- svāmin naiṣām eṣa doṣaḥ | yataḥ svāmi-sadṛśā evaṃ bhavanti bhṛtyāḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Master, this is not their fault. For servants become like their master. And it is said —

children.text: aśvaḥ śastraṃ śāstraṃ vīṇā vāṇī naraś ca nārī ca |
children.translated_text: A horse, a weapon, a treatise, a lute, speech, a man, and a woman —

children.text: puruṣa-viśeṣaṃ prāptā bhavanty ayogyāś ca yogyāś ca ||Panc_1.119||
children.translated_text: when they come into the possession of different persons, they become either unfit or fit. ||Panc_1.119||

children.text: tat-pauruṣāvaṣṭaṃ kṛtvā tvaṃ tāvad atraiva pratipālaya yāvad aham etac chabda-svarūpaṃ jñātvāgacchāmi | tataḥ paścād yathocitaṃ kāryam iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, taking firm resolve in your manliness, remain here while I go and learn the nature of that sound and return. After that, the appropriate action [shall be taken].

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- kiṃ tatra bhavān gantum utsahate |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: What — does sir dare to go there?

children.text: sa āha- kiṃ svāmy-ādeśāt sad-bhṛtya kṛtyākṛtyam asti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Is there anything doable or undoable for a good servant [when given] the master's command? And it is said —

children.text: svāmy-ādeśāt subhṛtyasya na bhoḥ sañjāyate kvacit |
children.translated_text: For a good servant, at the master's command, there never arises [any hesitation] anywhere —

children.text: praviśen mukham āheyaṃ dustaraṃ vā mahārṇavam ||Panc_1.120||
children.translated_text: he would enter the mouth of a snake or an impassable great ocean. ||Panc_1.120||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: svāmy-ādiṣṭas tu yo bhṛtyaḥ samaṃ viṣamam eva ca |
children.translated_text: A servant who, when commanded by the master, considers the level and the uneven as the same —

children.text: manyate na sa sandhāryo bhūbhujā bhūtim icchatā ||Panc_1.121||
