children.translated_text: should not be retained by a king who desires prosperity. ||Panc_1.121||

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- bhadraṃ, yady evaṃ tad gaccha | śivās te panthānaḥ santu iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Good — if so, then go. May your paths be auspicious!

children.text: damanako 'pi tam praṇamya saṃjīvaka-śabdānuṣarī pratasthe |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s>, having bowed to him, set out following the sound of <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>.

children.text: atha damanake gate bhaya-vyākula-manāḥ piṅgalakaś cintayāmāsa- aho na śobhanaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā | yat tasya viśvāsaṃ gatvātmābhiprāyo niveditaḥ | kadācid damanako 'yam ubhaya-vetano bhūtvā mamopari duṣṭa-buddhiḥ syād bhraṣṭādhikāratvāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Now, when <s>Damanaka</s> had gone, <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, his mind agitated by fear, thought: 'Alas, I have not done well! For having placed trust in him, I have revealed my inner intention. Perhaps this <s>Damanaka</s>, becoming a double-agent, might harbor evil designs against me, since he was removed from his post.' And it is said —

children.text: ye bhavanti mahīpasya sammānita-vimānitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who have been both honored and dishonored by the king —

children.text: yatante tasya nāśāya kulīnā api sarvadā ||Panc_1.122||
children.translated_text: they always strive for his destruction, even if they are of noble birth. ||Panc_1.122||

children.text: tat tāvad asya cikīrṣitaṃ vettum anyat sthānāntaraṃ gatvā pratipālayāmi | kadācid damanakas tam ādāya māṃ vyāpādayitum icchati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So let me go to another place and wait to learn his intentions. Perhaps <s>Damanaka</s> wishes to bring that [creature] and have me killed. And it is said —

children.text: na badhyante hy aviśvastā balibhir durbalā api |
children.translated_text: Those who are distrustful are never bound, even the weak by the strong;

children.text: viśvastās tv eva badhyante balavanto 'pi durbalaiḥ ||Panc_1.123||
children.translated_text: but those who are trustful are bound, even the strong by the weak. ||Panc_1.123||

children.text: bṛhaspater api prājño na viśvāse vrajen naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A man, even if wiser than <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, should never place trust [blindly]

children.text: ya icched ātmano vṛddhim āyuṣyaṃ ca sukhāni ca ||Panc_1.124||
children.translated_text: if he desires his own prosperity, long life, and happiness. ||Panc_1.124||

children.text: śapathaiḥ sandhitasyāpi na viśvāse vrajed ripoḥ |
children.translated_text: Even of an enemy allied by oaths, one should not trust —

children.text: rājya-lābhodyato vṛtraḥ śakreṇa śapathair hataḥ ||Panc_1.125||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtra</s>, striving for kingship, was slain by <s>Indra</s> through oaths. ||Panc_1.125||

children.text: na viśvāsaṃ vinā śatrur devānām api siddhyati |
children.translated_text: Without trust, an enemy does not succeed, even against the gods;

children.text: viśvāsāt tridaśendreṇa diter garbho vidāritaḥ ||Panc_1.126||
children.translated_text: through trust, <s>Diti</s>'s embryo was split by the lord of the gods. ||Panc_1.126||

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya sthānāntaraṃ gatvā damanaka-mārgam avalokayann ekākī tasthau | damanako 'pi sañjīvaka-sakāśaṃ gatvā vṛṣabho 'yam iti parijñāya hṛṣṭa-manā vyacintayat- aho śobhanam āpatitam | anenaitasya sandhi-vigraha-dvāreṇa mama piṅgalako vaśyo bhaviṣyatīti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having deliberated thus, he went to another place and stood alone, watching <s>Damanaka</s>'s path. <s>Damanaka</s> too, having gone to <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>'s presence and recognizing that this was a bull, thought joyfully: 'Ah, something excellent has turned up! By means of this [bull], through the instrument of alliance and war, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> will be under my control.' And it is said —

children.text: na kaulīnyān na sauhārdān nṛpo vākye pravartate |
children.translated_text: A king does not act on [a minister's] word because of family ties or friendship —

children.text: mantriṇāṃ vāvad abhyeti vyasanaṃ śokam eva ca ||Panc_1.127||
children.translated_text: he only trusts ministers up to the point of distress and grief. ||Panc_1.127||

children.text: sadaivāpadgato rājā bhogyo bhavati mantriṇām |
children.translated_text: A king who is always beset by calamity becomes enjoyable [i.e., useful] for ministers;

children.text: ataeva hi vāñchanti mantriṇaḥ sāpadaṃ nṛpam ||Panc_1.128||
children.translated_text: that is exactly why ministers desire a king beset by calamity. ||Panc_1.128||

children.text: yathā necchati nīrogaḥ kadācit sucikitsakam |
children.translated_text: Just as a healthy man never desires a good physician,

children.text: tathāpad rahito rājā sacivaṃ nābhivāñchati ||Panc_1.129||
children.translated_text: so a king free from calamity does not desire a minister. ||Panc_1.129||

children.text: evaṃ vicintayan piṅgalakābhimukhaḥ pratasthe | piṅgalako 'pi tam āyāntaṃ prekṣya svākāraṃ rakṣan yathā-pūrva-sthitaḥ damanako 'pi piṅgalaka-sakāśaṃ gatvā praṇamyopaviṣṭaḥ | piṅgalaka āha - kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavatā tat sattvam ?
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, he set out toward <s>Piṅgalaka</s>. <s>Piṅgalaka</s> too, seeing him coming, guarded his expression and remained as before. <s>Damanaka</s> too, having gone to <s>Piṅgalaka</s>'s presence, bowed and sat down. <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Did you see that creature?

children.text: damanaka āha- dṛṣṭaṃ svāmi-prasādāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: I saw it, by the master's grace.

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- api satyam |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: Is it true?

children.text: damanaka āha- kiṃ svāmi-pādānām agre'satyaṃ vijñāpyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: Is something untrue reported before the master's feet? And it is said —

children.text: api svalpam asatyaṃ yaḥ puro vadati bhūbhujām |
children.translated_text: He who speaks even a little untruth before kings

children.text: devānāṃ ca vinaśyate sa drutaṃ sumahān api ||Panc_1.130||
children.translated_text: and before the gods — even if very great, he quickly perishes. ||Panc_1.130||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: sarva-deva-mayo rājā manunā samprakīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The king has been declared by <s>Manu</s> to be constituted of all the gods;

children.text: tasmāt taṃ devavat paśyen na vyalīkena karhicit ||Panc_1.131||
children.translated_text: therefore one should regard him as a god — never with deceit. ||Panc_1.131||

children.text: sarva-devamayasyāpi viśeṣo nṛpater ayam |
children.translated_text: But this distinction [exists] of the king, though constituted of all the gods:

children.text: śubhāśubha-phalaṃ sadyo nṛpād devād bhavāntare ||Panc_1.132||
children.translated_text: the fruit of good and evil [comes] immediately from a king; from a god, in the next life. ||Panc_1.132||

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- satyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati bhavatā | na dīnipari mahāntaḥ kupyantīti na tvaṃ tena nipātitaḥ | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: It must be true that you have seen it. Great ones do not become angry with the wretched — that is why you were not struck down by it. For —

children.text: tṛṇāni nonmūlayati prabhañjano
children.translated_text: The hurricane does not uproot grasses

children.text: mrḍūni nīcaiḥ praṇatāni sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: that are soft and bowed low on all sides;

children.text: svabhāva evonnata-cetasām ayaṃ
children.translated_text: this is the nature of the lofty-minded —

children.text: mahān mahatsv eva karoti vikramam ||Panc_1.133||
children.translated_text: the great exert their prowess only against the great. ||Panc_1.133||

children.text: api ca-
gaṇḍasthaleṣu mada-vāriṣu baddha-rāga-
children.translated_text: Though struck on the temple-regions by the feet of bees

children.text: matta-bhramad-bhramara-pāda-talāhato 'pi |
children.translated_text: that buzz madly, clinging to the streams of rut-fluid,

children.text: kopaṃ na gacchati nitānta-balo 'pi nāgas
children.translated_text: an elephant of exceeding strength does not become angry;

children.text: tulye bale tu balavān parikopam eti ||Panc_1.134||
children.translated_text: but when faced with an equal in strength, the powerful one becomes furious. ||Panc_1.134||
Moreover —

children.text: damanaka āha- astv evaṃ sa mahātmā | vayaṃ kṛpaṇāḥ | tathāpi svāmī yadi kathayati tato bhṛtyatve niyojayāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: Let it be so — he is a great soul; we are wretched. Still, if the master commands, then I shall employ him in service.

children.text: piṅgalaka āha socchvāsam- kiṃ bhavān śaknoty evaṃ kartum |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said with a sigh: Can you truly do this?

children.text: damanaka āha- kim asādhyaṃ buddher asti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: Is anything impossible for intelligence? And it is said —

children.text: na tac chastrair na nāgendrair na hayair na padātibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is not accomplished by weapons, by lordly elephants, by horses, or by infantry —

children.text: kāryaṃ saṃsiddhim abhyeti yathā buddhyā prasādhitam ||Panc_1.135||
children.translated_text: that task reaches success when accomplished by intelligence. ||Panc_1.135||

children.text: piṅgalaka āha- yady evaṃ tarhy amātya-pade'dhyāropitas tvam | adya-prabhṛti prasāda-nigrahādikaṃ tvayeva kāryam iti niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: If so, then you are elevated to the position of minister. From today onward, matters of favor, punishment, and the like are to be decided by you alone — this is my resolve.

children.text: atha damanakaḥ satvaraṃ gatvā sākṣepaṃ tam idam āha- ehy ehīto duṣṭa-vṛṣabha | svāmī piṅgalakas tvām ākārayati | kiṃ niḥśaṅko bhūtvā muhur muhur nadasi vṛthā iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Damanaka</s>, going swiftly, said to him [<s>Saṃjīvaka</s>] with reproach: 'Come, come here, wicked bull! The master <s>Piṅgalaka</s> summons you. Why do you bellow repeatedly without fear and without purpose?'

children.text: tac chrutvā sañjīvako 'bravīt- bhadra ko 'yaṃ piṅgalakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> said: 'Good sir, who is this <s>Piṅgalaka</s>?'

children.text: damanaka āha- kiṃ svāminaṃ piṅgalakam api na jānāsi ? tat-kṣaṇam pratipālaya | phalenaiva jñāsyasi | nanv ayaṃ sarva-mṛga-parivṛto baṭa-tale svāmī piṅgalaka-nāmā siṃhas tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'What — you do not even know the master <s>Piṅgalaka</s>? Wait just a moment — you will know by the result. For this master, a lion named <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, stands at the base of a banyan tree, surrounded by all the animals.'

children.text: tac chrutvā gatāyuṣam ivātmānam manyamānaḥ sañjīvakaḥ paraṃ viṣādam agamat | āha ca- bhadra bhavān sādhu-samācāro vacana-paṭuś ca dṛśyate | tad yadi mām avaśyaṃ tatra nayasi tad-abhaya-pradānena svāminaḥ sakāśāt prasādaḥ kārayitavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, considering himself as good as dead, fell into extreme despondency. And he said: 'Good sir, you appear to be one of good conduct and skilled in speech. If you must take me there, then you must obtain a guarantee of safety from the master on my behalf.'

children.text: damanaka āha-bhoḥ satyam abhihitaṃ bhavatā | nītir eṣā yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Sir, what you have said is true. This is indeed the proper course, for —'

children.text: paryanto labhyate bhūmeḥ samudrasya girer api |
children.translated_text: An end can be found of the earth, of the ocean, and of the mountain;

children.text: na kathañcin mahīpasya cittāntaḥ kenacit kvacit ||Panc_1.136||
children.translated_text: but no one, nowhere, can ever [find] the end of a king's mind. ||Panc_1.136||

children.text: tattvam atraiva tiṣṭha yāvad ahaṃ taṃ samaye dṛṣṭvā tataḥ paścāt tvām anayāmi iti | tathānuṣṭhite damanakaḥ piṅgalaka-sakāśaṃ gatvedam āha-svāmin na tat prākṛtaṃ sattvam | sa hi bhagavato maheśvarasya vāhana-bhūto vṛṣabha iti | mayā pṛṣṭa idam ūce | maheśvareṇa parituṣṭena kālindī-parisare śaṣpāgrāṇi bhakṣayituṃ samādiṣṭaḥ | kiṃ bahunā mama pradattaṃ bhagavatā krīḍārthaṃ vanam idam |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore remain right here while I go and meet him at the proper time, and afterward I shall bring you.' When this was done, <s>Damanaka</s> went to <s>Piṅgalaka</s>'s presence and said: 'Master, that is no ordinary creature. He is a bull who serves as the vehicle of the blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s>. When I questioned him, he said this: "The pleased <s>Maheśvara</s> has commanded me to eat the tips of grass on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā). In short, the Lord has given me this forest for play."'

children.text: piṅgalaka āha sabhayam-satyaṃ jñātaṃ mayādhunā | na devatā-prasādaṃ vinā śaṣpa-bhojino vyālākīrṇa evaṃvidhe vane niḥśaṅkā nandato bhramanti | tatas tvayā kim abhihitam |
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said with fear: 'Now I truly understand. Without the grace of a deity, grass-eaters do not wander fearlessly and joyfully in such a forest infested with predators.' Then what did you say?

children.text: damanaka āha-svāmin etad abhihitaṃ mayā yad etad-vanaṃ caṇḍikā-vāhana-bhūtasya piṅgalakasya viṣayībhūtam | tad bhavān abhyāgataḥ priyo 'tithiḥ | tat tasya sakāśaṃ gatvā bhrātṛ-snehenaikatra bhakṣaṇa-pāna-viharaṇa-kriyābhir eka-sthānāśrayeṇa kālo neyaḥ iti | tatas tenāpi sarvam etat pratipannam | uktaṃ ca saharṣaṃ svāminaḥ sakāśād abhaya-dakṣiṇā dāpayitavyā iti | tad atra svāmī pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Master, I said this to him: "This forest is the domain of <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, who serves as the vehicle of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> (the fierce goddess). You have arrived as a welcome guest. Therefore, going to his presence, with brotherly affection, through activities of eating, drinking, and sporting together, sharing one dwelling, time should be passed." And he accepted all this. And he said with delight that a guarantee of safety should be obtained from the master.' In this matter, the master is the authority.

children.text: tac chrutvā piṅgalaka āha-sādhu sumate sādhu | mantri śrotriya sādhu | mama hṛdayena saha saṃmantrya bhavaedam abhihitam | tad dattā mayā tasyābhaya-dakṣiṇā | paraṃ so 'pi mad-arthe'bhaya-dakṣiṇāṃ yācayitvā drutataram ānīyatām iti | atha sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, hearing that, said: 'Well done, wise one, well done! Well done, minister and counselor! You have spoken this in consultation with my heart. The guarantee of safety is given by me to him. But let him also obtain a guarantee of safety from me for my sake, and bring him quickly.' And this is well said —

children.text: antaḥ-sārair akuṭilair acchidraiḥ suparīkṣitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: A kingdom is upheld by ministers who are sound within, straightforward, without weakness, and well-tested —

children.text: mantribhir dhāryate rājyaṃ sustambhair iva mandiram ||Panc_1.137||
children.translated_text: just as a mansion [is upheld] by good pillars. ||Panc_1.137||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: mantriṇāṃ bhinna-sandhāne bhiṣajāṃ sānnipātike |
children.translated_text: Of ministers in breaking alliances, and of physicians in combined fevers —

children.text: karmaṇi vyajyate prajñā svasthe ko vā na paṇḍitaḥ ||Panc_1.138||
children.translated_text: Wisdom is revealed in action — when all is well, who is not a scholar? // Panc_1.138 //

children.text: damanako 'pi taṃ praṇamya saṃjīvaka-sakāśa prasthitaḥ saharṣam acintayat- aho prasāda-saṃmukhī naḥ svāmī vacana-vaśagaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | tan nāsti dhanyataro mama | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s>, having bowed to him, set out toward <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> and thought joyfully: 'Ah, our master has become favorably disposed and obedient to my words! There is no one more fortunate than I.' And it is said:

children.text: amṛtaṃ śiśire vahnir amṛtaṃ priya-darśanam |
children.translated_text: Nectar is fire in the cold season; nectar is the sight of a beloved;

children.text: amṛtaṃ rāja-saṃmānam amṛtaṃ kṣīra-bhojanam ||Panc_1.139||
children.translated_text: nectar is the king's esteem; nectar is a meal of milk. // Panc_1.139 //

children.text: atha saṃjīvaka-sakāśam āsādya sa-praśrayam uvāca-bho mitra prārthito 'sau mayā bhavad-arthe svāmy-abhaya-pradānam | tad-viśrabdhaṃ gamyatām iti | paraṃ tvayā rāja-prasādam āsādya mayā saha samaya-dharmeṇa vartitavyam | na garvam āsādya sva-prabhutayā vicaraṇīyam | aham api tava saṅketena sarvā rājya-dhuram amātya-padavīm āśrityoddhariṣyāmi | evaṃ kṛte dvayor apy āvayo rāja-lakṣmī-bhāgyā bhaviṣyati | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, having reached <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, he said respectfully: 'O friend, I have entreated that master on your behalf to grant you safety. So go with confidence. But having obtained the king's favor, you must conduct yourself toward me according to the pact of alliance. You must not become arrogant and act by your own authority alone. I too, by your signal, shall assume the ministerial position and bear the entire burden of the kingdom. If we act thus, the fortune of royalty shall belong to us both. For:'

children.text: ākheṭakasya dharmeṇa vibhavāḥ syur vaśe nṝṇām |
children.translated_text: By the hunter's method, resources come under the control of men —

children.text: nṛ-prajāḥ prerayaty eko hanty anyo 'tra mṛgān iva ||Panc_1.140 ||
children.translated_text: one drives forth [the prey], while another slays the beasts here. // Panc_1.140 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: yo na pūjayate garvād uttamādhama-madhyamān |
children.translated_text: He who out of pride does not honor those near the king — whether superior, inferior, or middling —

children.text: nṛpāsannān sa mānyo 'pi bhraśyate dantilo yathā ||Panc_1.141||
children.translated_text: even though honored [himself], falls from favor, as did <s>Dantila</s>. // Panc_1.141 //

children.text: saṃjīvaka āha-katham etat ? so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> asked: 'How is that?' He said:

children.text:
kathā 3
dantila-gorambha-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 3
The story of <s>Dantila</s> and <s>Gorambha</s>

children.text: asty atra dharātale vardhamānaṃ nāma nagaram | tatra dantilo nāma nānā-bhāṇḍa-patiḥ sakala-pura-nāyakaḥ prativasati sma | tena pura-kāryaṃ nṛpa-kāryaṃ ca kurvatā tuṣṭiṃ nītās tat-pura-vāsino lokā nṛpatiś ca | kiṃ bahunā, na ko 'pi tādṛk kenāpi caturo dṛṣṭo śruto vā | athavā satyam etad uktam-
children.translated_text: There is in this land a city called <s>Vardhamāna</s>. There dwelt a merchant named <s>Dantila</s>, master of various goods and leader of the entire city. While managing both the city's affairs and the king's affairs, he kept the city's inhabitants and the king satisfied. In short, no one so clever had ever been seen or heard of by anyone. Or rather, this is truly said:

children.text: narapati-hita-kartā dveṣyatāṃ yāti loke
children.translated_text: He who serves the king's interest incurs the hatred of the people;

children.text: janapada-hita-kartā tyajyate pārthivendraiḥ |
children.translated_text: he who serves the people's interest is abandoned by the lords of kings.

children.text: iti mahati virodhe vartamāne samāne
children.translated_text: Thus, when great conflict exists between the two,

children.text: nṛpati-jana-padānāṃ durlabhaḥ kārya-kartā ||Panc_1.142||
children.translated_text: rare is the one who can manage the affairs of both king and populace. // Panc_1.142 //

children.text: athaivaṃ gacchati kāle danitlasya kadācid vivāhaḥ sampravṛttaḥ | tatra tena sarve pura-nivāsino rāja-saṃnidhi-lokāś ca sammāna-puraḥsaram āmantrya bhojitā vastrādibhiḥ sat-kṛtāś ca | tato vivāhānantaraṃ rājā sāntaḥpuraḥ sva-gṛham ānīyābhyarcitaḥ | atha tasya nṛpater gṛha-sammārjana-kartā gorambho nāma rāja-sevako gṛhāyāto 'pi tenānucita-sthāna upaviṣṭo 'vajñāyārdha-candraṃ dattvā niḥsāritaḥ | so 'pi tataḥ prabhṛti niśvasann apamānān na rātrāv apy adhiśete | kathaṃ mayā tasya bhāṇḍapate rāja-prasāda-hāniḥ kartavyā iti cintayann āste | athavā kim anena vṛthā śarīra-śoṣaṇena | na kiṃcin mayā tasyāpakartuṃ śakyam iti | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Now, in the course of time, a wedding celebration of <s>Dantila</s> once commenced. There, having respectfully invited all the city's inhabitants and the people of the king's court, he fed them and honored them with garments and the like. Then, after the wedding, he brought the king along with the queen to his own house and worshipped him. Now, <s>Gorambha</s> by name, a royal servant whose duty was sweeping the king's house, though he too had come to the house, sat down in an improper seat. [<s>Dantila</s>] slapped him [with a half-moon blow] with contempt and threw him out. From that day onward, [<s>Gorambha</s>], sighing from the insult, could not sleep even at night. He kept thinking, 'How can I bring about the ruin of that merchant's royal favor?' Or rather, [he thought,] 'Why waste away my body in vain? I am unable to harm him in any way.' Or rather, this is well said:

children.text: yo hy apakartum aśaktaḥ kupyati
children.translated_text: He who, unable to retaliate, becomes angry —

children.text: kim asau naro 'tra nirlajjaḥ |
children.translated_text: what is that shameless man [to do] here?

children.text: utpatito 'pi hi caṇakaḥ śaktaḥ
children.translated_text: Even a chickpea, though it pops up,

children.text: kiṃ bhrāṣṭrakaṃ bhaṅktum ||Panc_1.143||
children.translated_text: can it break the frying pan? // Panc_1.143 //

children.text: atha kadācit pratyūṣe yoga-nidrāṃ gatasya rājñaḥ śayyānte mārjanaṃ kurvann idam āha-aho dantilasya mahad dṛptatvaṃ yad rāja-mahiṣīm āliṅgati |
children.translated_text: Now once, at dawn, while sweeping at the bedside of the king who had fallen into a light sleep, he said this: 'Ah, what great insolence of <s>Dantila</s>, that he embraces the chief queen!'

children.text: tac chrutvā rājā sa-sambhramam utthāya tam uvāca-bho bho gorambha | satyam etat yat tvayā jalpitam | kiṃ dantilena samāliṅgitā iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king rose up in alarm and said to him: 'Ho, ho, <s>Gorambha</s>! Is this true, what you have uttered? Has <s>Dantila</s> embraced [the queen]?'

children.text: gorambhaḥ prāha-deva ! rātri-jāgaraṇena dyūtāsaktasya me balān nidrā samāyātā | tan na vedmi kiṃ mayābhihitam | rājā serṣyaṃ sva-gatam-eṣa tāvad asmad-gṛhe'pratihata-gatis tathā dantilo 'pi | tat kadācid anena devī samāliṅgyamānā dṛṣṭā bhaviṣyati | tenedam abhihitam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Gorambha</s> said: 'Your Majesty! Being awake all night due to my addiction to gambling, sleep overpowered me. So I do not know what I said.' The king thought jealously to himself: 'This [<s>Gorambha</s>] has unrestricted access to my house, and so does <s>Dantila</s>. So perhaps [<s>Gorambha</s>] once saw the queen being embraced by him. That is why he said this.' And it is said:

children.text: yad vāñchati divā martyo vīkṣate vā karoti vā |
children.translated_text: Whatever a mortal desires by day, or sees, or does —

children.text: tat svapne'pi tad-abhyāsād brūte vātha karoti vā ||Panc_1.144||
children.translated_text: that very thing, through habit, he speaks of or does even in his sleep. // Panc_1.144 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: śubhaṃ vā yadi pāpaṃ yan nṝṇāṃ hṛdi saṃsthitam |
children.translated_text: Whether auspicious or sinful, whatever is lodged in men's hearts,

children.text: sugūḍham api taj jñeyaṃ svapna-vākyāt tathā madāt ||Panc_1.145||
children.translated_text: even though well-concealed, it can be known from sleep-talk and from intoxication. // Panc_1.145 //

children.text: athavā strīṇāṃ viṣaye ko 'tra sandehaḥ |
children.translated_text: Or else, regarding women, what doubt is there [about their fidelity]?

children.text: jalpanti sārdham anyena paśyanty anyaṃ sa-vibhramāḥ |
children.translated_text: They converse with one man, glance flirtatiously at another,

children.text: hṛd-gataṃ cintayanty anyaṃ priyaḥ ko nāma yoṣitām ||Panc_1.146||
children.translated_text: and think of yet another in their hearts — who then is truly dear to women? // Panc_1.146 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: ekena smita-pāṭalādhara-ruco jalpanty analpākṣaraṃ vīkṣante'nyam itaḥ sphuṭat-kumudinī-phullollasal-locanāḥ |
children.translated_text: With one, their lips rosy with smiles, they exchange many a word; at another they gaze from the side with eyes blooming wide like night-lotuses in full flower; yet another they contemplate in thought, whose character and splendor are manifest from afar — in whom, then, does the love of these fair-browed ones truly abide? // Panc_1.147 //

children.text: dūrodāra-caritra-citra-vibhavaṃ dhyāyanti cānyaṃ dhiyā kenetthaṃ paramārthato 'rthavad iva premāsti vāma-bhruvām ||Panc_1.147||
tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: nāgnis tṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Fire is not sated with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers,

children.text: nāntakaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāma-locanā ||Panc_1.148||
children.translated_text: nor Death with all beings, nor the fair-eyed ones with men. // Panc_1.148 //

children.text: raho nāsti kṣaṇo nāsti nāsti prārthayitā naraḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no privacy, no [opportune] moment, no man who solicits —

children.text: tena nārada nārīṇāṃ satītvam upajāyate ||Panc_1.149||
children.translated_text: for that reason alone, O <s>Nārada</s>, does chastity arise among women. // Panc_1.149 //

children.text: yo mohān manyate mūḍho rakteyaṃ mama kāminī |
children.translated_text: He who, in his delusion, foolishly thinks 'this amorous woman loves me' —

children.text: sa tasyā vaśago nityaṃ bhavet krīḍā-śakuntavat ||Panc_1.150||
children.translated_text: he remains forever under her control, like a pet bird. // Panc_1.150 //

children.text: tāsāṃ vākyāni kṛtyāni svalpāni sugurūṇy api |
children.translated_text: Their words and deeds, though seemingly small, are truly weighty;

children.text: karoti saḥ kṛtair loke laghutvaṃ yāti sarvataḥ ||Panc_1.151||
children.translated_text: he who performs them comes to be regarded as lowly everywhere in the world. // Panc_1.151 //

children.text: striyaṃ ca yaḥ prārthayate sannikarṣaṃ ca gacchati |
children.translated_text: That man whom a woman desires, and who comes near,

children.text: īṣac ca kurute sevāṃ tam evecchanti yoṣitaḥ ||Panc_1.152||
children.translated_text: and who renders even slight service — him alone do women seek. // Panc_1.152 //

children.text: anarthitvān manuṣyāṇāṃ bhayāt parijanasya ca |
children.translated_text: Because men are not [always] desirous, and from fear of their household [members],

children.text: maryādāyām amaryādāḥ striyas tiṣṭhanti sarvadā ||Panc_1.153||
children.translated_text: women who [know] no bounds [always] remain within bounds. // Panc_1.153 //

children.text: nāsāṃ kaścid agamyo 'sti nāsāṃ ca vayasi sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: No man is inaccessible to them, nor do they remain fixed at any [one] age;

children.text: virūpaṃ rūpavantaṃ vā pumān ity eva bhujyate ||Panc_1.154||
children.translated_text: whether ugly or handsome — it is enjoyed simply because it is a man. // Panc_1.154 //

children.text: rakto hi jāyate bhogyo nārīṇāṃ śāṭikā yathā |
children.translated_text: A man infatuated indeed becomes the plaything of women, like a sari —

children.text: ghṛṣyante yo daśālambī nitambe viniveśitaḥ ||Panc_1.155||
children.translated_text: which is worn clinging to ten [fingers], rubbed, and placed upon the hips. // Panc_1.155 //

children.text: alaktiko yathā rakto niṣpīḍya puruṣas tathā |
children.translated_text: Just as lac-dye, being pressed, becomes red, so is a man

children.text: abalābhir balād raktaḥ pāda-mūle nipātyate ||Panc_1.156||
children.translated_text: forcibly reddened [with passion] by weak women and cast at [their] feet. // Panc_1.156 //

children.text: evaṃ sa rājā bahuvidhaṃ vilapya tat-prabhṛti dantilasya prasāda-parāṅmukhaḥ saṃjātaḥ | kiṃ bahunā rāja-dvāra-praveśo 'pi tasya nivāritaḥ | dantilo 'py akasmād eva prasāda-parāṅmukham avanipatim avalokya cintayāmāsa-aho sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Thus the king, having lamented in many ways, became from that day onward averse to showing favor to <s>Dantila</s>. In short, even entry to the palace gate was barred to him. <s>Dantila</s> too, seeing the king unexpectedly turned away from favor, pondered: 'Ah, well is this said:'

children.text: ko 'rthān prāpya na garvito viṣayiṇaḥ kasyāpado 'staṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Who, having obtained wealth, is not puffed up? Whose misfortunes have reached their end?

children.text: strībhiḥ kasya na khaṇḍitaṃ bhuvi manaḥ ko nāmā rājñāṃ priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whose mind has not been shattered by women on this earth? Who indeed is dear to kings?

children.text: kaḥ kālasya na gocarāntara-gataḥ ko 'rthī gato gauravaṃ
children.translated_text: Who has not fallen within the range of Time? What supplicant has attained dignity?

children.text: ko vā durjana-vāgurāsu patitaḥ kṣemeṇa yātaḥ pumān ||Panc_1.157||
children.translated_text: What man, fallen into the snares of the wicked, has emerged safely? // Panc_1.157 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: kāke śaucaṃ dyūta-kāreṣu satyaṃ sarpe kṣāntiḥ strīṣu kāmopaśāntiḥ |
children.translated_text: Cleanliness in a crow, truth in gamblers, patience in a serpent, quenching of desire in women,

children.text: klībe dhairyaṃ madyape tattva-cintā rājā mitraṃ kena dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā ||Panc_1.158||
children.translated_text: courage in a eunuch, philosophical reflection in a drunkard, a king as a friend — who has ever seen or heard of [such things]? // Panc_1.158 //

children.text: aparaṃ mayāsya bhūpater athavānyasyāpi kasyacid rāja-sambandhinaḥ svapne'pi nāniṣṭaṃ kṛtam | tat kim etat-parāṅmukho māṃ prati bhūpatiḥ iti |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, I have not done anything displeasing to this king — or for that matter to any other person connected with the king — even in a dream. Then why is the king turned away from me?'

children.text: evaṃ taṃ dantilaṃ kadācid rāja-dvāre viṣkambhitaṃ vilokya saṃmārjana-kartā gorambho vihasya dvārapālān idam ūce-bho bho dvārapālāḥ ! rāja-prasādādhiṣṭhito 'yaṃ dantilaḥ svayaṃ nigrahānugraha-kartā ca | tad anena nivāritena yathāhaṃ tathā yūyam apy ardha-candra-bhājino bhaviṣyatha | tac chrutvā dantilaś cintayāmāsa-nūnam idam asya gorambhasya ceṣṭitam | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
akulīno 'pi mūrkho 'pi bhūpālaṃ yo 'tra sevate |
children.translated_text: Even one of low birth, even a fool, if he serves the king —

children.text: api saṃmānahīno 'pi sa sarvatra prapūjyate ||Panc_1.159||
children.translated_text: even though bereft of honors, he is revered everywhere. // Panc_1.159 //

Thus, one day, seeing <s>Dantila</s> blocked at the palace gate, the sweeper <s>Gorambha</s> laughed and said to the gatekeepers: 'Ho, gatekeepers! This <s>Dantila</s>, established in the king's favor and himself the dispenser of punishment and reward — now that he has been barred, just as I [was treated], so too shall you become recipients of the half-moon [slap]!' Hearing that, <s>Dantila</s> thought: 'Surely this is the doing of that <s>Gorambha</s>. Or rather, well is this said:'

children.text: api kāpuruṣo bhīruḥ syāc cen nṛpati-sevakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a coward and weakling, if he be a servant of the king —

children.text: tathāpi na parābhūtiṃ janād āpnoti mānavaḥ ||Panc_1.160||
children.translated_text: even so, that man does not suffer humiliation from the people. // Panc_1.160 //

children.text: evaṃ sa bahu-vidhaṃ vilapya vilakṣa-manāḥ sodvego gata-prabhāvaḥ sva-gṛhaṃ niśāmukhe gorambham āhūya vastra-yugalena saṃmānyedam uvāca-bhadra ! mayā na tadā tvaṃ rāga-vaśān niḥsāritaḥ | yatas tvaṃ brāhmaṇānām agrato 'nucita-sthāne samupaviṣṭo dṛṣṭa ity apamānitaḥ | tat kṣamyatām |
children.translated_text: Thus, having lamented in many ways, disheartened and anxious, his power gone, [<s>Dantila</s>] summoned <s>Gorambha</s> to his house at nightfall, honored him with a pair of garments, and said: 'Good man! It was not out of malice that I threw you out that day. Since you were seen sitting in an improper seat in front of the Brahmins, you were slighted. Forgive me for that.'

children.text: so 'pi svarga-rājyopamaṃ tad-vastra-yugalam āsādya paraṃ paritoṣaṃ gatvā tam uvāca-bhoḥ śreṣṭhin ! kṣāntaṃ mayā te tat | tad asya saṃmānasya kṛte paśya me buddhi-prabhāvaṃ rāja-prasādaṃ ca | evam uktvā saparitoṣaṃ niṣkrāntaḥ | sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: [<s>Gorambha</s>], having obtained that pair of garments — as [precious to him] as the kingdom of heaven — and having attained supreme satisfaction, said to him: 'O merchant! I have forgiven you for that. Now, in return for this honor, behold my power of intellect and [watch me restore] the king's favor.' Having said this, he departed with satisfaction. And well is this said:

children.text: stokenonnatim āyāti stokenāyāty adho-gatim |
children.translated_text: With a trifle one is raised up, with a trifle one is brought low —

children.text: aho sasadṛśo ceṣṭā tulāyaṣṭeḥ khalasya ca ||Panc_1.161||
children.translated_text: ah, how similar are the actions of a balance-beam and of a rogue! // Panc_1.161 //

children.text: tataś cānye-dyuḥ sa gorambho rāja-kule gatvā yoga-nidrāṃ gatasya bhūpateḥ saṃmārjana-kriyāṃ kurvann idam āha-aho aviveko 'smad-bhūpateḥ | yat purīṣotsargam ācaraṃś carbhaṭī-bhakṣaṇaṃ karoti |
children.translated_text: Then, the next day, <s>Gorambha</s>, having gone to the palace, while sweeping as the king lay in light sleep, said this: 'Ah, what lack of discernment in our king! He eats cucumbers while evacuating his bowels!'

children.text: tac chrutvā rājā sa-vismayaṃ tam uvāca-re re gorambha ! kim aprastutaṃ lapasi | gṛha-karmakaraṃ matvā tvāṃ na vyāpādayāmi | kiṃ tvayā kadācid aham evaṃvidhaṃ karma samācaran dṛṣṭaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king said to him in astonishment: 'You there, <s>Gorambha</s>! What irrelevant nonsense are you babbling? Considering you a household servant, I do not have you killed. Have you ever seen me performing such an act?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-dyūtāsaktasya rātri-jāgaraṇena saṃmārjanaṃ kurvāṇasya mama balān nidrā samāyātā | tayādhiṣṭhitena mayā kiṃcij jalpitam | tan na vedmi | tat prasādaṃ karotu svāmī nidrā-paravaśasya iti |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Being awake all night due to my addiction to gambling, sleep overpowered me while I was sweeping. Under its sway, I uttered something — I do not know what. May the master pardon one overcome by sleep.'

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā rājā cintitavān-yan mayā janmāntare purīṣotsargaṃ kurvatā kadāpi cirbhaṭikā na bhakṣitā | tad yathāyaṃ vyatikaro 'sambhāvyo mamānena mūḍhena vyāhṛtaḥ | tathā dantilasyāpīti niścayaḥ | tan mayā na yuktaṃ kṛtaṃ yat sa varākaḥ saṃmānena viyojitaḥ | na tādṛk-puruṣāṇām evaṃvidhaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ sambhāvyate | tad-abhāvena rāja-kṛtyāni paura-kṛtyāni na sarvāṇi śithilatāṃ vrajanti |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the king reflected: 'In no previous birth have I ever eaten a cucumber while evacuating. Just as this impossible occurrence was uttered about me by this fool, so too [the statement] about <s>Dantila</s> must be [equally baseless]. I was wrong to have that poor man deprived of his honors. Such conduct is not to be expected of a man like him. Without him, all the royal and civic affairs are falling into disarray.'

children.text: evam anekadhā vimṛśya dantilaṃ samāhūya nijāṅga-vastrābharaṇādibhiḥ saṃyojya svādhikāre niyojayāmāsa | ato 'haṃ bravīmi yo na pūjayate garvāt iti |
children.translated_text: Having deliberated thus in many ways, he summoned <s>Dantila</s>, presented him with garments and ornaments from his own person, and appointed him to his [former] office. Therefore I say: 'He who out of pride does not honor [those near the king]...' [and so on].

children.text: saṃjīvaka āha-bhadra evam evaitat | yad bhavatābhihitaṃ tad eva mayā kartavyam iti | evam abhihite damanakas tam ādāya piṅgalaka-sakāśam agamat | āha ca-deva eṣa mayānītaḥ sa saṃjīvakaḥ | adhunā devaḥ pramāṇam | saṃjīvako 'pi taṃ sādaraṃ praṇamyāgrataḥ sa-vinayaṃ sthitaḥ | piṅgalako 'pi tasya pīnāyata-kakudmato nakha-kuliśālaṃkṛtaṃ dakṣiṇa-pāṇim upari dattvā māna-puraḥsaram uvāca-api śivaṃ bhavataḥ | kutas tvam asmin vane vijane samāyāto 'si ?
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> said: 'Good man, it is exactly so. What you have said — that is what I shall do.' When this had been said, <s>Damanaka</s> took him and went to the presence of <s>Piṅgalaka</s>. And he said: 'Sire, this <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> has been brought by me. Now Your Majesty is the authority.' <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> too, having bowed to him respectfully, stood before him humbly. <s>Piṅgalaka</s> too, placing his right paw — adorned with claws [hard as] thunderbolts — upon [the head of] that one with his stout, tall hump, said with honor: 'Is all well with you? Whence have you come to this desolate forest?'

children.text: tenāpy ātmaka-vṛttāntaḥ kathitaḥ | yathā vardhamānena saha viyogaḥ saṃjātas tathā sarvaṃ niveditam | tac chrutvā piṅgalakaḥ sādarataraṃ tam uvāca-vayasya na bhetavyam | mad-bhuja-pañjara-parirakṣitena yathecchaṃ tvayādhunā vartitavyam | anyac ca nityaṃ mat-samīpa-vartinā bhāvyam | yataḥ kāraṇād bahv-apāyaṃ raudra-sattva-niṣevitaṃ vanaṃ gurūṇām api sattvānām asevyam | kutaḥ śaṣpa-bhojinām |
children.translated_text: He too told his own story. He reported everything — how his separation from <s>Vardhamāna</s> had come about. Hearing that, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said to him with great affection: 'Friend, do not be afraid! Protected within the cage of my arms, you should now live as you please. And furthermore, you should always remain near me. For the forest, being fraught with many dangers and inhabited by fierce creatures, is unfit even for great beings — let alone grass-eaters!'

children.text: evam uktvā sakala-mṛga-parivṛto yamunā-kaccham avatīryodaka-grahaṇaṃ kṛtvā svecchayā tad eva vanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tataś ca karakaṭa-damanaka-nikṣipta-rājya-bhāraḥ saṃjīvikena saha subhāṣita-goṣṭhīm anubhavann āste | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having said this, surrounded by all the animals, he descended to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, took water, and entered that very forest as he pleased. Then, having entrusted the burden of the kingdom to <s>Karaṭaka</s> and <s>Damanaka</s>, he spent his time enjoying conversations of fine sayings with <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>. Indeed, this is well said:

children.text: yadṛcchayāpy upanataṃ sakṛt sajjana-saṅgatam |
children.translated_text: A single encounter with the virtuous, even if it comes by chance,

children.text: bhavaty ajaram atyantaṃ nābhyāsa-kramam īkṣate ||Panc_1.162||
children.translated_text: becomes imperishable and everlasting — it does not depend on a process of repeated practice. // Panc_1.162 //

children.text: saṃjīvakenāpy aneka-śāstrāvagāhanād utpanna-buddhi-prāgalbhyena stokair evāhobhir mūḍha-matiḥ piṅgalako dhīmāṃs tathā kṛto yathāraṇya-dharmād viyojya grāmya-dharmeṣu niyojitaḥ | kiṃ bahunā pratyahaṃ piṅgalaka-saṃjīvakāv eva kevalaṃ rahasi mantrayataḥ | śeṣaḥ sarvo 'pi mṛga-jano dūrībhūtas tiṣṭhati | karaṭaka-damanakāv api praveśaṃ na labhete | anyac ca siṃha-parākramābhāvāt sarvo 'pi mṛga-janas tau ca śṛgālau kṣudhā-vyādhi-bādhitā ekāṃ diśam āśritya sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: And <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, whose intellectual boldness had arisen from deep study of many <s>śāstras</s>, within just a few days made the dull-witted <s>Piṅgalaka</s> wise — to the point that he was weaned from the ways of the forest and directed toward civilized conduct. In short: every day <s>Piṅgalaka</s> and <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> alone conferred in private; all the rest of the animal-folk stood at a distance. Even <s>Karaṭaka</s> and <s>Damanaka</s> could not gain admission. Moreover, because the lion's prowess was absent, all the animal-folk, and those two jackals as well, afflicted by the malady of hunger, stayed in a corner.

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: phala-hīnaṃ nṛpaṃ bhṛtyāḥ kulīnam api connatam |
children.translated_text: Servants abandon a king who is fruitless — even if noble and exalted —

children.text: santy ajyāny atra gacchanti śuṣkaṃ vṛkṣam ivāṇḍajāḥ ||Panc_1.163||
children.translated_text: and go elsewhere, like birds [abandoning] a dry tree. // Panc_1.163 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: api saṃmāna-saṃyuktāḥ kulīnā bhakti-tat-parāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even servants who are honored, noble, and devoted to service

children.text: vṛtti-bhaṅgān mahīpālaṃ tyajanty eva hi sevakāḥ ||Panc_1.164||
children.translated_text: abandon a king when their livelihood is disrupted. // Panc_1.164 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: kālātikramaṇaṃ vṛtteryo na kurvīta bhūpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: That king who does not let the livelihood [of his servants] lapse —

children.text: kadācit taṃ na muñcanti bhartsitā api sevakāḥ ||Panc_1.165||
children.translated_text: servants never abandon him, even when rebuked. // Panc_1.165 //

children.text: tathā ca kevalaṃ sevakā itthambhūtā yāvat samastam apy etaj jagat parasparaṃ bhakṣaṇārthaṃ sāmādibhir upāyais tiṣṭhati | tad yathā-
children.translated_text: And not only servants are like this — indeed this entire world subsists on one another for the purpose of consumption, through stratagems such as conciliation and the like. Namely:

children.text: deśānām upari kṣmābhṛd āturāṇāṃ cikitsakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Kings [subsist] on territories; physicians on the sick;

children.text: vaṇijo grāhakāṇāṃ ca mūrkhāṇām api paṇḍitāḥ ||Panc_1.166||
children.translated_text: merchants on customers; and scholars on fools. // Panc_1.166 //

children.text: pramādināṃ tathā caurā bhikṣukā gṛha-medhinām |
children.translated_text: Thieves on the careless; mendicants on householders;

children.text: gaṇikāḥ kāmināṃ caiva sarva-lokasya śilpinaḥ ||Panc_1.167||
children.translated_text: courtesans on the lustful; and craftsmen on everyone. // Panc_1.167 //

children.text: sāmādi-sajjitaiḥ pāśaiḥ pratīkṣante divā-niśam |
children.translated_text: With snares fashioned from conciliation and the like, they watch day and night,

children.text: upajīvanti śaktyā hi jalajā jaladān iva ||Panc_1.168||
children.translated_text: subsisting by their power — like aquatic creatures on rain-clouds. // Panc_1.168 //

children.text: athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Indeed, this is well said:

children.text: sarpāṇāṃ ca khalānāṃ ca para-dravyāpahāriṇām |
children.translated_text: The schemes of serpents, of the wicked, and of thieves of others' property

children.text: abhiprāyā na sidhyanti tenedaṃ vartate jagat ||Panc_1.169||
children.translated_text: do not always succeed — that is why this world survives. // Panc_1.169 //

children.text: attuṃ vāñchati śāmbhavo gaṇapater ākhuṃ kṣudhārtaḥ phaṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>'s [serpent] wishes to devour <s>Gaṇapati</s>'s mouse; the serpent, tormented by hunger, [wishes to devour] the peacock of the enemy of <s>Krauñca</s>;

children.text: taṃ ca krauñca-ripoḥ śikhī giri-sutā-siṃho 'pi nāgāśanam |
children.translated_text: and the lion of the Mountain's Daughter [wishes to devour] the elephant that is the serpent's food;

children.text: itthaṃ yatra parigrahasya ghaṭanā śambhor api syād gṛhe
children.translated_text: thus, where such conflict of household [members] would occur even in <s>Śambhu</s>'s home,

children.text: tatrāpy asya kathaṃ na bhāvi jagato yasmāt svarūpaṃ hi tat ||Panc_1.170||
children.translated_text: how could it not occur in this [ordinary] world? — for that is its very nature. // Panc_1.170 //

children.text: tataḥ svāmi-prasāda-rahitau kṣut-kṣāma-kaṇṭhau parasparaṃ karaṭaka-damanakau mantrayete | tatra damanako brūte-ārya karaṭaka | āvāṃ tāvad apradhānatāṃ gatau | eṣa piṅgalakaḥ saṃjīvakānuraktaḥ sva-vyāpāra-parāṅmukhaḥ saṃjātaḥ | sarvo 'pi parijano gataḥ | tat kiṃ kriyate |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Karaṭaka</s> and <s>Damanaka</s>, deprived of the master's favor and with throats emaciated by hunger, consulted with each other. There <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Noble <s>Karaṭaka</s>, we have become of no consequence. This <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, attached to <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, has turned away from his own duties. The entire retinue has departed. What is to be done?'

children.text: karaṭaka āha-yadyapi tvadīya-vacanaṃ na karoti tathāpi svāmī sva-doṣa-nāśāya vācyaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Even if he does not heed your words, the master should still be counseled for the removal of his own faults. And it is said:'

children.text: aśṛnvann api boddhavyo mantribhiḥ pṛthivī-patiḥ |
children.translated_text: A king should be counseled by ministers even when he does not listen —

children.text: yathā sva-doṣa-nāśāya vidureṇāmbikāsutaḥ ||Panc_1.171||
children.translated_text: for the removal of his own faults — as <s>Vidura</s> [counseled] the son of <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>). // Panc_1.171 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: madonmattasya bhūpasya kuñjarasya ca gacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: When a king intoxicated with power or an elephant in rut

children.text: unmārgaṃ vācyatāṃ yānti mahāmātrāḥ samīpagāḥ ||Panc_1.172||
children.translated_text: takes a wrong path, the great ministers who are near him become liable to be censured. // Panc_1.172 //

children.text: tat tvayaiṣa śaṣpa-bhojī svāminaḥ sakāśam ānītaḥ | tat svahastenāṅgārāḥ karṣitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'It was you who brought this grass-eater to the master's presence. You have drawn burning coals with your own hand.'

children.text: damanaka āha-satyam etat | mamāyaṃ doṣaḥ | na svāminaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Truly so. This fault is mine, not the master's. And it is said:'

children.text: jambūko huḍu-yuddhena vayaṃ cāṣāḍha-bhūtinā |
children.translated_text: The jackal by the ram-fight, we by <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>,

children.text: dūtikā para-kāryeṇa trayo doṣāḥ svayaṃ kṛtāḥ ||Panc_1.173||
children.translated_text: the female messenger by another's affair — these three faults were self-inflicted. // Panc_1.173 //

children.text: karaṭaka āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 4
devaśarma-parivrājaka-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 4
The Tale of <s>Devaśarman</s> and the Mendicant

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vivikta-pradeśe maṭhāyatanam | tatra deva-śarmā nāma parivrājakaḥ partivasati sma | tasyāneka-sādhu-jana-datta-sūkṣma-vastra-vikraya-vaśāt kālena mahatī vitta-mātrā sañjātā | tataḥ sa na kasyacid viśvasiti | naktaṃ dinaṃ kakṣāntarāt tāṃ mātrāṃ na muñcati | athavā sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: In a certain secluded place there was a monastery. There a wandering ascetic named <s>Devaśarman</s> used to live. In time, from selling the fine garments given by many virtuous people, a great sum of money accumulated. Because of it, he trusted no one. Day and night he would not release that sum from under his arm. Indeed, this is well said:

children.text: arthānām arjane duḥkham arjitānāṃ ca rakṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: There is pain in acquiring wealth, and in protecting what has been acquired;

children.text: nāśe duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhaṃ dhig arthāḥ kaṣṭa-saṃśrayāḥ ||Panc_1.174||
children.translated_text: pain in its loss, pain in its spending — alas for wealth, the abode of misery! // Panc_1.174 //

children.text: athāṣāḍha-bhūtir nāma para-vittāpahārī dhūrtas tām artha-mātrāṃ tasya kakṣāntara-gatāṃ lakṣayitvā vyacintayat-kathaṃ mayāsyeyam artha-mātrā hartavyā iti |
children.translated_text: Now a rogue named <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>, a thief of others' property, having noticed that sum of money concealed under his arm, thought: 'How shall I steal this sum from him?'

children.text: tad atra maṭhe tāvad dṛḍha-śilā-sañcaya-vaśād bhitti-bhedo na bhavati | uccaistaratvāc ca dvāre praveśo na syāt | tad enaṃ māyā-vacanair viśvāsyāhaṃ chātratāṃ vrajāmi yena sa viśvastaḥ kadācid viśvāsam eti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Now, in this monastery, because of its strong stone construction, breaking through the wall is not possible. And because of its great height, entry through the door is not feasible. So I shall gain his trust through deceitful words and become his disciple, so that, trusting [me], he may someday let his guard down.' And it is said:

children.text: nispṛho nādhikārī syān nākāmī maṇḍana-priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is desireless would not hold office; one without desire [for beauty] would not love adornment;

children.text: nāvidagdhaḥ priyaṃ brūyāt sphuṭa-vaktā na vañcakaḥ ||Panc_1.175||
children.translated_text: one who is not shrewd would not speak pleasantly; one who speaks plainly is not a deceiver. // Panc_1.175 //

children.text: evaṃ niścitya tasyāntikam upagamya-oṃ namaḥ śivāya-iti proccārya sāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇamya ca sa-praśrayam uvāca-bhagavan asāraḥ saṃsāro 'yam | giri-nadī-vegopamaṃ yauvanam | tṛṇāgni-samaṃ jīvitam | śarad-abhra-cchāyā-sadṛśā bhogāḥ svapna-sadṛśo mitra-putra-kalatra-bhṛtya-varga-sambandhaḥ | evaṃ mayā samyak parijñātam | tat kiṃ kurvato me saṃsāra-samudrottaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, he approached him, uttered 'Oṃ namaḥ Śivāya,' prostrated fully, and said with humility: 'Lord, this worldly existence is without substance. Youth is like the rush of a mountain torrent. Life is like a fire in straw. Pleasures are like the shadow of autumn clouds. The connection with friends, sons, wives, and servants is like a dream. Having thus fully understood, what should I do so that I may cross the ocean of worldly existence?'

children.text: tac chrutvā deva-śarmā sādaram āha-vatsa ! dhanyo 'si yat prathame vayasy evaṃ viraktī-bhāvaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Devaśarman</s> said with great respect: 'Child, you are blessed that at such a young age you have such detachment! And it is said:'

children.text: pūrvaṃ vayasi yaḥ śāntaḥ sa śānta iti me matiḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is tranquil in the first stage of life — he is truly tranquil, in my view;

children.text: dhātuṣu kṣīyamāṇeṣu śamaḥ kasya na jāyate ||Panc_1.176||
children.translated_text: when the bodily constituents are wasting away, whose tranquility does not arise? // Panc_1.176 //

children.text: ādau citte tataḥ kāye satāṃ saṃjāyate jarā |
children.translated_text: For the virtuous, old age first arises in the mind, then in the body;

children.text: asatāṃ ca punaḥ kāye naiva citte kadācana ||Panc_1.177||
children.translated_text: for the wicked, however, [it arises only] in the body — never in the mind. // Panc_1.177 //

children.text: yac ca māṃ saṃsāra-sāgarottaraṇopāyaṃ pṛcchasi | tac chrūyatām-
children.translated_text: 'And as for what you ask me about the means of crossing the ocean of worldly existence — hear this:'

children.text: śūdro vā yadi vānyo 'pi caṇḍālo 'pi jaṭādharaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether a <s>Śūdra</s> or anyone else, even a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, if he bears matted locks

children.text: dīkṣitaḥ śiva-mantreṇa sa bhasmāṅgī śivo bhavet ||Panc_1.178||
children.translated_text: and is initiated with a <s>Śiva</s>-mantra, smeared with ashes, he becomes <s>Śiva</s>. // Panc_1.178 //

children.text: ṣaḍ-akṣareṇa mantreṇa puṣpam ekam api svayam |
children.translated_text: He who, with a six-syllable mantra, himself places even a single flower

children.text: liṅgasya mūrdhni yo dadyān na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate ||Panc_1.179||
children.translated_text: upon the head of the <s>liṅga</s> — he is not born again. // Panc_1.179 //

children.text: tac chrutvāṣāḍha-bhūtis tat-pādau gṛhītvā sa-praśrayam idam āha-bhagavan, tarhi dīkṣayā me'nugrahaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s> grasped his feet and said with humility: 'Lord, then grant me your grace through initiation.'

children.text: devaśarmā āha-vatsa anugrahaṃ te kariṣyāmi | parantu rātrau tvayā maṭha-madhye na praveṣṭavyam | yat-kāraṇaṃ niḥsaṅgatā yatīnāṃ praśasyate tava ca mamāpi ca | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Devaśarman</s> said: 'Child, I will bestow grace upon you. But at night you must not enter the monastery. For non-attachment is praised for ascetics — both for you and for me.' And it is said:

children.text: durmantrān nṛpatir vinaśyati yatiḥ saṅgāt suto lālasād
children.translated_text: A king perishes by bad counsel; an ascetic by attachment; a son by indulgence;

children.text: vipro 'nadhyayanāt kulaṃ kutanayāc chīlaṃ khalopāsanāt |
children.translated_text: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by not studying; a family by a bad son; character by association with the wicked;

children.text: maitrī cāpraṇayāt samṛddhir anayāt snehaḥ pravāsāśrayāt
children.translated_text: friendship by lack of affection; prosperity by misconduct; love by staying abroad;

children.text: strī garvād anavekṣaṇād api kṛṣis tyāgāt pramādād dhanam ||Panc_1.180||
children.translated_text: a woman by arrogance; agriculture by neglect; and wealth by carelessness. // Panc_1.180 //

children.text: tat tvayā vrata-grahaṇānantaraṃ maṭha-dvāre tṛṇa-kuṭīrake śayitavyam iti |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, after taking the vow, you should sleep in a grass hut at the monastery door.'

children.text: sa āha-bhagavan ! bhavad-ādeśaḥ pramāṇam | paratra hi tena me prayojanam |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Lord, your command is my authority. For I have no concern with worldly matters.'

children.text: atha kṛta-śayana-samayaṃ devaśarma-nigrahaṃ kṛtvā śāstrokta-vidhinā śiṣyatām anayat | so 'pi hasta-pādāvamardanādi-paricaryayā taṃ paritoṣam anayat | punas tathāpi muniḥ kakṣāntarān mātrāṃ na muñcati | athaivaṃ gacchati kāle āṣāḍha-bhūtiś cintayāmāsa-aho, na kathañcid eṣa me viśvāsam āgacchati | tat kiṃ divāpi śastreṇa mārayāmi, kiṃ vā viṣaṃ prayacchāmi ? kiṃ vā paśu-dharmeṇa vyāpādayāmi ? iti |
children.translated_text: Then, at bedtime, having initiated <s>Devaśarman</s> [i.e., having been initiated by <s>Devaśarman</s>], he became his disciple according to the procedure prescribed in the scriptures. He too, by attending upon him with massaging of hands and feet and such services, brought him to satisfaction. But nevertheless, the ascetic would not release the sum from under his arm. As time went on, <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s> thought: 'Alas, he will not trust me in any way. Shall I kill him by day with a weapon? Or shall I give him poison? Or shall I destroy him by brute force?'

children.text: evaṃ cintayatas tasya devaśarmaṇo 'pi śiṣya-putraḥ kaścid grāmād āmantraṇārthaṃ samāyātaḥ | prāha ca-bhagavan, pavitrāropaṇa-kṛte mama gṛham āgamyatām iti |
children.translated_text: While he was thus thinking, a certain pupil's son of <s>Devaśarman</s> arrived from a village to deliver an invitation. He said: 'Lord, please come to my house for the sacred thread ceremony.'

children.text: tac chrutvā devaśarmāṣāḍhabhūtinā saha prahṛṣṭa-manāḥ prasthitaḥ | athaivaṃ tasya gacchato 'gre kācin nadī samāyātā | tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mātrāṃ kakṣāntarād avatārya kanthā-madhye suguptāṃ nidhāya snātvā devārcanaṃ vidhāya tad-anantaram āṣāḍhabhūtim idam āha-bho āṣāḍhabhūte ! yāvad ahaṃ purīṣotsargaṃ kṛtvā samāgacchāmi, tāvad eṣā kanthā yogeśvarasya svāvadhānatayā rakṣaṇīyā | ity uktvā gataḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Devaśarman</s>, with a joyful heart, set out together with <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>. As they were going, a certain river lay ahead. Seeing it, he took the sum from under his arm, placed it well-hidden within his tattered blanket, and having bathed and worshipped the gods, he then said to <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>: 'O <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>! While I go to relieve myself and return, this blanket must be guarded by Your Reverence with careful attention.' Having said this, he went.

children.text: āṣāḍhabhūtir api tasminn adarśanī-bhūte mātrām ādāya satvaraṃ prasthitaḥ | devaśarmāpi chātra-guṇānurañjita-manāḥ suviśvasto yāvad upaviṣṭas tiṣṭhati tāvat suvarṇa-roma-deha-yūtha-madhye huḍu-yuddham apaśyat | atha roṣa-vaśād dhuḍu-yugalasya dūram apasaraṇaṃ kṛtvā bhūyo 'pi samupetya lālaṭa-paṭṭābhyāṃ praharato bhūri rudhiraṃ patati | tac ca jambūko jihvā-laulyena raṅga-bhūmiṃ prāveśyāsvādayati | devaśarmāpi tad ālokya vyacintayat-aho manda-matir ayaṃ jambūkaḥ | yadi katham apy anayoḥ saṅghaṭṭe patiṣyati tan nūnaṃ mṛtyum avāpsyatīti vitarkayāmi |
children.translated_text: And <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>, when [<s>Devaśarman</s>] had gone out of sight, seized the sum and hastily departed. <s>Devaśarman</s> too, his mind charmed by the student's qualities, was sitting in full trust, when he saw a ram-fight in the midst of a flock of golden-fleeced [rams]. Out of rage, the pair of rams would retreat far apart, then rush together again, striking with their foreheads, and copious blood would flow. A jackal, out of greed for licking, entered the arena and tasted [the blood]. <s>Devaśarman</s> too, observing this, thought: 'Ah, this jackal is dull-witted. If somehow he falls between the two as they clash, he will surely meet his death — so I surmise.'

children.text: kṣaṇāntare ca tathaiva raktāsvādana-laulyān madhye praviśaṃs tayoḥ śiraḥ-sampāte patiot mṛtaś ca śṛgālaḥ | devaśarmāpi taṃ śocamāno mātrām uddiśya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ prasthito yāvad āṣāḍhabhūtiṃ na paśyati tataś cautsukyena śaucaṃ vidhāya yāvat kanthām ālokayati tāvan mātrāṃ na paśyati | tataś ca-hā hā muṣito 'smi iti jalpan pṛthivī-tale mūrcchayā nipapāta | tataḥ kṣaṇāc cetanāṃ labdhvā bhūyo 'pi samutthāya phūtkartum ārabdhaḥ-bho āṣāḍhabhūte ! kva māṃ vañcayitvā gato 'si ? tad dehi me prativacanam |
children.translated_text: And in the next moment, that very [jackal], out of greed for tasting blood, entering between them just as their heads crashed together, fell and died. <s>Devaśarman</s> too, mourning for him, slowly set out toward the sum — but did not see <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>. Then, anxiously performing his ablutions, he looked at the blanket — but did not see the sum. Then, crying 'Alas, alas, I have been robbed!' he fell to the ground in a faint. Then, after a moment, regaining consciousness, he rose again and began to exclaim: 'O <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>! Where have you gone, having deceived me? Give me an answer!'

children.text: evaṃ bahu vilapya tasya pada-paddhatim anveṣayan śanaiḥ śanaiḥ prasthitaḥ | athaiva gacchan sāyantana-samaye kañcid grāmam āsasāda | atha tasmād grāmāt kaścit kaulikaḥ sabhārhyo madya-pāna-kṛte samīpa-vartini nagare prasthitaḥ | devaśarmāpi tam ālokya provāca-bho bhadra vayaṃ sūryoḍhā atithayas tavāntikaṃ prāptāḥ | na kam apy atra grāme jānīmaḥ | tad gṛhyatām atithi-dharmaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having lamented thus at length, he set out slowly, following in the footprints [of his lost companion]. As he walked on, at eventide he reached a certain village. From that village, a certain weaver (<s>kaulika</s>), a respectable man, had set out for a nearby town for the purpose of drinking wine. <s>Devaśarman</s> too, seeing him, said: 'Good sir, we have arrived at your doorstep as guests brought by the setting sun. We do not know anyone in this village. Therefore accept the duty of hospitality. As it is said —'

children.text: samprāpto yo 'tithiḥ sāyaṃ sūryoḍhe gṛha-medhinām |
children.translated_text: The guest who arrives at evening, brought by the setting sun,

children.text: pūjayā tasya devatvaṃ prayānti gṛha-medhinaḥ ||Panc_1.181||
children.translated_text: by worshipping him the householders attain divinity. [Panc 1.181]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: tṛṇāni bhūmir udakaṃ vāk-caturthī ca sūnṛtā |
children.translated_text: Grass, ground, water, and fourthly a kind word —

children.text: satām etāni harmyeṣu nocchidyante kadācana ||Panc_1.182||
children.translated_text: these in the houses of the good are never denied. [Panc 1.182]

children.text: svāgatenāgnayas tṛptā āsanena śatakratuḥ |
children.translated_text: By a welcome, the fires are satisfied; by a seat, <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra);

children.text: pāda-śaucena pitaraḥ arghāc chambhus tathātitheḥ ||Panc_1.183||
children.translated_text: by foot-washing, the ancestors; by the respectful offering (<s>arghya</s>), <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) — thus the guest. [Panc 1.183]

children.text: kauliko 'pi tac chrutvā bhāryām āha-priye, gaccha tv atithim ādāya gṛhaṃ prati pāda-śauca-bhojana-śayanādibhiḥ satkṛtya tvaṃ tatraiva tiṣṭha | ahaṃ tava kṛte prabhūta-madyam āneṣyāmi | evam uktvā prasthitaḥ | sāpi bhāryā puṃścalī tam ādāya prahasita-vadanā devadattaṃ manasi dhyāyantī gṛhaṃ prati pratasthe | athavā sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: The weaver too, hearing this, said to his wife: 'Dear, go and take the guest home; honor him with foot-washing, food, a bed, and the like, and you stay there. I shall bring plenty of wine for you.' Having said this, he departed. And his wife — a woman of loose morals — taking [the guest] along, her face beaming with a smile, thinking of <s>Devadatta</s> in her mind, set out toward home. Or rather, rightly is it said —

children.text: durdivase ghana-timire duḥsañcārāsu nagara-vīthīṣu |
children.translated_text: On a stormy day, in dense darkness, when the city streets are hard to traverse,

children.text: patyur videśa-gamane parama-sukhaṃ jaghana-capalāyāḥ ||Panc_1.184||
children.translated_text: and when the husband has gone abroad — supreme is the happiness of a woman fickle in her hips. [Panc 1.184]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: paryaṅkeṣv āstaraṇaṃ patim anukūlaṃ manoharaṃ śayanam |
children.translated_text: Couches, bedding, a compliant husband, a charming bed —

children.text: tṛṇam iva laghu manyante kāminyaś caurya-rata-lubdhāḥ ||Panc_1.185||
children.translated_text: amorous women lusting for stolen pleasures regard these as light as straw. [Panc 1.185]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: keliṃ pradahati lajjā śṛṅgāro 'sthīni cāṭavaḥ kaṭavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Modesty burns their play; love-making [burns] their bones; sweet talk, harsh talk —

children.text: vandha-trayāḥ paritoṣo na kiṃcid iṣṭaṃ bhavet patyau ||Panc_1.186||
children.translated_text: the three bonds; contentment — nothing is pleasing in a husband. [Panc 1.186]

children.text: kula-patanaṃ jana-garhāṃ bandhanam api jīvitavya-sandeham |
children.translated_text: The fall of the family, the censure of people, even imprisonment, even doubt about [one's] life —

children.text: aṅgīkaroti kulaṭā satataṃ para-puruṣa-saṃsaktā ||Panc_1.187||
children.translated_text: all this a wanton woman accepts, constantly attached to another man. [Panc 1.187]

children.text: atha kaulika-bhāryā gṛhaṃ gatvā deva-śarmaṇe gatāstaraṇaṃ bhagnāṃ ca khaṭvāṃ samarpyedam āha-bho bhagavan ! yāvad ahaṃ sva-sakhīṃ grāmād abhyāgatāṃ sambhāvya drutam āgacchāmi tāvat tvayā mad-gṛhe'pramattena bhāvyam |
children.translated_text: Then the weaver's wife, having gone home, gave <s>Devaśarman</s> a worn-out mat and a broken cot, and said: 'Reverend sir, while I quickly go to welcome a friend who has come from the village and return, you must remain alert in my house.'

children.text: evam abhidhāya śṛṅgāra-vidhiṃ vidhāya yāvad-devadattam uddiśya vrajati tāvat tad-bhartā saṃmukho mada-vihvalāṅgo mukta-keśaḥ pade pade praskhalan gṛhīta-madya-bhāṇḍaḥ samabhyeti | taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sā drutataraṃ vyāghuṭya sva-gṛhaṃ praviśya nukta-śṛṅgāra-veśā yathā-pūrvam abhavat | kauliko 'pi tāṃ palāyamānāṃ kṛtādbhuta-śṛṅgārāṃ vilokya prāg eva karṇa-paramparayā tasyāḥ śrutāvapavāda-kṣubhita-hṛdayaḥ svākāraṃ nigūhamānaḥ sadaivāste | tataś ca tathāvidhaṃ ceṣṭitam avalokya dṛṣṭa-pratyayaḥ krodha-vaśago gṛhaṃ praviśya tām uvāca-āḥ pāpe puṃścali ! kva prasthitāsi ?
children.translated_text: Having said this, she adorned herself for love-making, and was heading toward <s>Devadatta</s> when her husband came face to face with her — his body staggering with intoxication, hair disheveled, stumbling at every step, carrying a vessel of wine. Seeing him, she very quickly turned back, entered her house, and undoing her amorous attire, became as before. The weaver too, seeing her fleeing and elaborately adorned, his heart already agitated by the gossip he had heard through hearsay, concealed his own [feelings] and stayed as usual. Then, having observed such conduct and gained direct evidence, overcome with anger, he entered the house and said to her: 'Oh, wicked adulteress! Where were you going?'

children.text: sā provāca-ahaṃ tvat-sakāśād āgatā na kutracid api nirgatā | tat kathaṃ madya-pāna-vaśād aprastutaṃ vadasi ? athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: She said: 'I came from your presence; I have not gone out anywhere. So why do you, under the influence of drink, speak irrelevantly? Or rather, rightly is it said —'

children.text: vaikalyaṃ dharaṇī-pātam ayathocita-jalpanam |
children.translated_text: Disability, falling to the ground, speaking incoherently —

children.text: saṃnipātasya cihnāni madyaṃ sarvāṇi darśayet ||Panc_1.188||
children.translated_text: wine displays all the symptoms of delirium. [Panc 1.188]

children.text: kara-spando 'mbara-tyāgas tejo-hāniḥ sarāgatā |
children.translated_text: Trembling of the hands, casting off of garments, loss of vigor that has come upon one —

children.text: vāruṇī-saṅgajāvasthā bhānunāpy anubhūyate ||Panc_1.189||
children.translated_text: the condition caused by the company of liquor is experienced even by the Sun. [Panc 1.189]

children.text: so 'pi tac chrutvā pratikūla-vacanaṃ veśa-viparyayaṃ cāvalokya tam āha-puṃścali ! cira-kālaṃ śruto mayā tavāpavādaḥ | tad adya svayaṃ sañjāta-pratyayas tava yathocitaṃ nigrahaṃ karomi | ity abhidhāya laguḍa-prahārais tāṃ jarjarita-dehāṃ vidhāya sthūṇayā saha dṛḍha-bandhanena baddhvā so 'pi mada-vihvalo vijñāya tāṃ gatvedam āha-sakhi ! sa devadattas tasmin sthāne tvāṃ pratīkṣate | tac chīghram āgamyatām iti |
children.translated_text: He too, hearing her contrary words and observing the change in her attire, said to her: 'Adulteress! I have heard gossip about you for a long time. Today, having obtained direct proof myself, I shall punish you as you deserve.' Having said this, he beat her with a cudgel until her body was battered, tied her firmly to a pillar, and he too, dazed with drink, fell asleep. Then a [female] barber, his wife's friend, knowing [the situation], came and said: 'Friend, that <s>Devadatta</s> is waiting for you at that place. So come quickly.'

children.text: sā cāha-paśya mamāvasthām | tat kathaṃ gacchāmi ? tad gatvā brūhi taṃ kāminaṃ yad asyāṃ rātrau na tvayā saha samāgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Look at my condition! How can I go? Go and tell that lover that tonight there will be no meeting with you.'

children.text: nāpitī prāha-sakhi, mā maivaṃ vada | nāyaṃ kulaṭā-dharmaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The barber's wife said: 'Friend, don't say that! This is not the way of an adulteress. As it is said —'

children.text: viṣama-stha-svādu-phala-grahaṇa-vyavasāya-niścayo yeṣām |
children.translated_text: Those whose determination is set on grasping the sweet fruit growing on a precipice —

children.text: uṣṭrāṇām iva teṣāṃ manye'haṃ śaṃsitaṃ janma ||Panc_1.190||
children.translated_text: like camels, their birth I consider praiseworthy. [Panc 1.190]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: sandigdhe para-loke janāpavāde ca jagati bahu-citre |
children.translated_text: When the next world is doubtful, when there is censure from people in this wondrous world,

children.text: svādhīne para-ramaṇe dhanyās tāruṇya-phala-bhājaḥ ||Panc_1.191||
children.translated_text: blessed are those who enjoy the fruits of youth, with a lover of their own choosing. [Panc 1.191]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yadi bhavati deva-yogāt pumān virūpo 'pi bandhako rahasi |
children.translated_text: If by divine fate a man — even an ugly one — becomes a lover in secret,

children.text: na tu kṛcchrād api bhadraṃ nija-kāntaṃ sā bhajaty eva ||Panc_1.192||
children.translated_text: she does not, even with difficulty, forsake him — she serves her own beloved. [Panc 1.192]

children.text: sābravīt-yady evaṃ tarhi kathaya kathaṃ dṛḍha-bandhana-baddhā satī tatra gacchāmi | sannihitaś cāyaṃ pāpātmā mat-patiḥ |
children.translated_text: She said: 'If that is so, then tell me — how can I, being firmly bound, go there? And this wicked husband of mine is right here.'

children.text: nāpity āha-sakhi, mada-vihvalo 'yaṃ sūrya-kara-spṛṣṭaḥ prabodhaṃ yāsyati | tad ahaṃ tvam unmocayāmi | mām ātma-sthāne baddhvā drutataraṃ deva-dattaṃ sambhāvyāgaccha |
children.translated_text: The barber's wife said: 'Friend, this one, dazed with drink, will wake up when touched by the sun's rays. I shall free you. Tie me in your place, go quickly to honor <s>Devadatta</s>, and come back.'

children.text: sābravīt-evam astu iti |
children.translated_text: She said: 'So be it.'

children.text: tad anu sā nāpitī tāṃ sva-sakhīṃ bandhanād vimocya tasyāḥ sthāne yathā-pūrvam ātmānaṃ baddhvā tāṃ devadatta-sakāśe saṅketa-sthānaṃ preṣitavatī | tathānuṣṭhite kaulikaḥ kasmiṃścit kṣaṇe samutthāya kiṃcid gata-kopo vimadas tām āha-he paruṣa-vādini ! yad adya-prabhṛti gṛhān niṣkramaṇaṃ na karoṣi, na ca paruṣaṃ vadasi, tatas tvām unmocayāmi |
children.translated_text: Thereupon the barber's wife freed her friend from the bonds, tied herself in her place as before, and sent her to the appointed meeting-place with <s>Devadatta</s>. When this had been done, the weaver, waking up after some time, his anger somewhat abated and his intoxication gone, said to her: 'O harsh-tongued woman! If from today onward you do not leave the house, and if you do not speak harshly, then I shall free you.'

children.text: nāpity api svara-bheda-bhayād yāvan na kiṃcid ūce, tāvat so 'pi bhūyo bhūyas tāṃ tad evāha | atha sā yāvat pratyuttaraṃ kim api na dadau, tāvat sa prakupitas tīkṣṇa-śastram ādāya nāsikām acchinat | āha ca-re puṃścali ! tiṣṭhedānīm | tvāṃ bhūyas toṣayiṣyāmi | iti jalpan punar api nidrā-vaśam agāt |
children.translated_text: The barber's wife too, fearing detection by difference in voice, said nothing for a while, and he repeated the same words again and again. When she still gave no reply, he became furious, took a sharp blade, and cut off her nose. And he said: 'You adulteress! Stay now. I shall reward you further.' Muttering thus, he fell asleep again.

children.text: devaśarmāpi vitta-nāśāt kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭho naṣṭa-nidras tat sarvaṃ strī-caritram apaśyat | sāpi kaulika-bhāryā yathecchayā devadattena saha surata-sukham anubhūya kasmiṃścit kṣaṇe sva-gṛham āgataya tāṃ nāpitīm idam āha-ayi ! śivaṃ bhavatyāḥ | nāyaṃ pāpātmā mama gatāyā utthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Devaśarman</s> too, his throat parched with hunger from the loss of his wealth, sleepless, watched all this drama of women. The weaver's wife, having enjoyed the pleasures of love with <s>Devadatta</s> as she pleased, came home after a while and said to the barber's wife: 'Ah! Is all well with you? This wicked one did not wake up while I was gone?'

children.text: nāpity āha-śivaṃ nāsikayā vinā śeṣasya śarīrasya | tad drutaṃ tāṃ mocaya bandhanād yāvan nāyaṃ māṃ paśyati, yena sva-gṛhaṃ gacchāmi |
children.translated_text: The barber's wife said: 'All is well — except for the nose; the rest of the body is fine. So quickly free me from these bonds before he sees me, so that I can go home.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite bhūyo 'pi kaulika utthāya tām āha-puṃścali ! kim adyāpi na vadasi ? kiṃ bhūyo 'py ato duṣṭataraṃ nigrahaṃ karṇa-cchedena karomi ?
children.translated_text: When this had been done, the weaver woke up again and said: 'Adulteress! Will you still not speak? Shall I inflict an even harsher punishment — cutting off your ears?'

children.text: atha sā sa-kopaṃ sādhikṣepam idam āha-dhiṅ mahā-mūḍha ! ko māṃ mahā-satīṃ dharṣayituṃ vyaṅgayituṃ vā samarthaḥ ? tac chṛṇvantu sarve'pi loka-pālāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then she spoke angrily, with contemptuous words: 'Shame on you, great fool! Who is able to violate or mutilate me, a supremely chaste woman? Let all the guardians of the world hear this!'

children.text: āditya-candra-hari-śaṃkara-vāsavādyāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), and others —

children.text: śaktā na jetum atiduḥkha-karāṇi yāni |
children.translated_text: are unable to conquer the senses, which cause extreme suffering.

children.text: tānīndriyāṇi balavanti sudurjayāni
children.translated_text: Those powerful and supremely unconquerable senses —

children.text: ye nirjayanti bhuvane balinas ta eke ||Panc_1.193||
children.translated_text: those who conquer them in this world are the only truly strong ones. [Panc 1.193]

children.text: tad yadi mama satītvam asti, manasāpi para-puruṣo nābhilaṣitaḥ, tato devā bhūyo 'pi me nāsikāṃ tādṛg-rūpākṣatāṃ kurvantu | athavā yadi mama citte para-puruṣasya bhrāntir api bhavati, māṃ bhasmasān nayantu | evam uktvā bhūyo 'pi tam āha-bho durātman ! paśya me satītva-prabhāveṇa tādṛśy eva nāsikā saṃvṛttā |
children.translated_text: 'If my chastity is real, if I have not desired another man even in thought, then let the gods make my nose whole and unblemished again. Or if even a passing thought of another man has entered my mind, let them reduce me to ashes.' Having spoken thus, she said to him again: 'You wretch! See — by the power of my chastity, my nose has become just as it was.'

children.text: athāsāv ulmukam ādāya yāvat paśyati, tāvat tad-rūpāṃ nāsikāṃ ca bhūtale rakta-pravāhaṃ ca mahāntam apaśyat | atha sa vismita-manās tāṃ bandhanād vimucya śayyāyām āropya ca cāṭu-śataiḥ paryatoṣayat | devaśarmāpi taṃ sarva-vṛttāntam ālokya vismita-manā idam āha-
children.translated_text: Then he, taking a firebrand to look, saw her nose in its original form — and a great stream of blood on the ground. Then, his mind astonished, he freed her from the bonds, placed her on the bed, and appeased her with a hundred endearments. And <s>Devaśarman</s> too, having observed this entire episode, astonished in mind, said —

children.text: śambarasya ca yā māyā yā māyā namucer api |
children.translated_text: The magic of <s>Śambara</s>, and the magic of <s>Namuci</s>,

children.text: baleḥ kumbhīnasaś caiva sarvās tā yoṣito viduḥ ||Panc_1.194||
children.translated_text: and of <s>Bali</s> and <s>Kumbhīnasa</s> — all these women know. [Panc 1.194]

children.text: hasantaṃ prahasanty etā rudantaṃ prarudanty api |
children.translated_text: They laugh when [someone] laughs; they weep when [someone] weeps;

children.text: apriyaṃ priya-vākyaiś ca gṛhṇanti kāla-yogataḥ ||Panc_1.195||
children.translated_text: and with sweet words they capture [one's] heart at the opportune time. [Panc 1.195]

children.text: uśanā veda yac chāstraṃ yac ca veda bṛhaspatiḥ |
children.translated_text: The treatise that <s>Uśanas</s> (Śukra) knows, and that which <s>Bṛhaspati</s> knows —

children.text: strī-buddhyā na viśiṣyete tāḥ sma rakṣyāḥ kathaṃ naraiḥ ||Panc_1.196||
children.translated_text: these do not surpass women's wit; how then can they be guarded by men? [Panc 1.196]

children.text: anṛtaṃ satyam ity āhuḥ satyaṃ cāpi tathānṛtam |
children.translated_text: They call falsehood truth, and truth too falsehood —

children.text: iti yās tāḥ kathaṃ vīra saṃrakṣyāḥ puruṣair iha ||Panc_1.197||
children.translated_text: such women as these, O hero, how can men guard them here? [Panc 1.197]

children.text: anyatrāpy uktam-
nātiprasaṅgaḥ pramadāsu kāryo
children.translated_text: One should not become overly attached to young women,

children.text: necched balaṃ strīṣu vivardhamānam |
children.translated_text: nor should one wish their power to grow;

children.text: atiprasaktaiḥ puruṣair yatas tāḥ
children.translated_text: for women, when men are overly attached,

children.text: krīḍanti kākair iva lūna-pakṣaiḥ ||Panc_1.198||
children.translated_text: play with them as with wing-clipped crows. [Panc 1.198]
Elsewhere too it is said —

children.text: sumukhena vadanti vagunā praharanty eva śitena cetasā |
children.translated_text: With a smiling face they speak; with a sharp, cutting mind they strike;

children.text: madhu tiṣṭhati vāci yoṣitāṃ hṛdaye hālāhalaṃ mahad-viṣam ||Panc_1.199||
children.translated_text: honey sits on the lips of women; in their hearts, <s>hālāhala</s> — the great poison. [Panc 1.199]

children.text: ata eva nipīyate'dharo hṛdayaṃ muṣṭibhir eva tāḍyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore the lip is sipped, but the heart is struck with fists —

children.text: puruṣaiḥ sukha-leśa-vañcitair madhu-lubdhaiḥ kamalaṃ yathālibhiḥ ||Panc_1.200||
children.translated_text: by men deceived by a morsel of pleasure, honey-seekers, like bees [attracted] to a lotus. [Panc 1.200]

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: āvartaḥ saṃśayānām avinaya-bhavanaṃ pattanaṃ sāhasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ saṃnidhānaṃ kapaṭa-śata-mayaṃ kṣetram apratyayānām |
children.translated_text: A whirlpool of doubts, a mansion of impropriety, a harbor of rash acts, a treasury of faults, a field of distrust made of a hundred deceptions,

children.text: svarga-dvārasya vighnaṃ naraka-pura-mukhaṃ sarva-māyā-karaṇḍaṃ strī-yantraṃ kena sṛṣṭaṃ viṣam amṛta-mayaṃ prāṇi-lokasya pāśaḥ ||Panc_1.201||
children.translated_text: an obstacle to heaven's gate, the entrance to the city of hell, a casket of all illusions — by whom was the mechanism of woman created? Poison made of nectar, the snare of all living beings. [Panc 1.201]

children.text: kārkaśyaṃ stanayor dṛśos taralatālīkaṃ mukhe ślāghyate kauṭilyaṃ kaca-saṃcaye ca vacane māndyaṃ trike sthūlatā |
children.translated_text: Hardness in their breasts, fickleness in their eyes — 'fine'; crookedness in the mass of their hair, and in their speech — 'gentleness'; fullness in their waist —

children.text: bhīrutvaṃ hṛdaye sadaiva kathitaṃ māyā-prayogaḥ priye yāsāṃ doṣa-gaṇo guṇo mṛga-dṛśāṃ tāḥ syur narāṇāṃ priyāḥ ||Panc_1.202||
children.translated_text: timidity always said to be in their hearts, [but actually] the practice of illusion, O beloved — those whose catalogue of faults is [considered] a virtue, [those] doe-eyed ones — they would be dear to men! [Panc 1.202]

children.text: etā hasanti ca rudanti ca kārya-hetor
children.translated_text: They laugh and cry for a purpose;

children.text: viśvāsayanti ca paraṃ na ca viśvasanti |
children.translated_text: they inspire trust in others but do not trust [anyone] themselves.

children.text: tasmān nareṇa kula-śīla-samanvitena nāryaḥ śmaśāna-ghaṭikā iva varjanīyāḥ ||Panc_1.203||
children.translated_text: Therefore a man of good family and character should shun women as one [shuns] cremation-ground pots. [Panc 1.203]

children.text: tasmān nareṇa kulaśīlavatā sadaiva
children.translated_text: Therefore a man of good family and virtue should always
