children.text: nāryaḥ śmaśāna-vaṭikā iva varjanīyāḥ |
children.translated_text: shun women as one [shuns] cremation-ground plots.

children.text: vyakīrṇa-kesara-karāla-mukhā mṛgendrā
children.translated_text: Lions with their manes streaming and terrifying faces,

children.text: nāgāś ca bhūri-mada-rāja-virājamānāḥ ||Panc_1.204||
children.translated_text: and elephants resplendent with abundant flowing rut — [Panc 1.204]

children.text: kurvanti tāvat prathamaṃ priyāṇi
children.translated_text: They first show affection

children.text: yāvan na jānanti naraṃ prasaktam |
children.translated_text: as long as they do not perceive the man to be infatuated;

children.text: jñātvā ca taṃ manmatha-pāśa-baddhaṃ
children.translated_text: but once they know him bound by the noose of passion,

children.text: grastāmiṣaṃ mīnam ivoddharanti ||Panc_1.205||
children.translated_text: they pull him out like a fish that has swallowed the bait. [Panc 1.205]

children.text: samudra-vīcīva cala-svabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Fickle by nature like ocean waves,

children.text: sandhyābhra-rekheva muhūrta-rāgāḥ |
children.translated_text: coloring for but a moment like streaks of evening clouds —

children.text: striyaḥ kṛtārthāḥ puruṣaṃ nirarthaṃ
children.translated_text: women, having gotten what they wanted, discard the worthless man

children.text: niṣpīḍotālaktakavat tyajanti ||Panc_1.206||
children.translated_text: like a squeezed-out ball of lac. [Panc 1.206]

children.text: anṛtaṃ sāhasaṃ māyā mūrkhatvam atilubdhatā |
children.translated_text: Falsehood, violence, deceit, foolishness, excessive greed,

children.text: aśaucaṃ nirdayatvaṃ ca strīṇāṃ doṣāḥ svabhāvajāḥ ||Panc_1.207||
children.translated_text: impurity, and cruelty — these are the natural faults of women. ||Panc_1.207||

children.text: sammohayantimadayanti viḍambayanti
children.translated_text: They bewitch, intoxicate, mock,

children.text: nirbharstayanti ramayanti viṣādayanti |
children.translated_text: scold, delight, and distress —

children.text: etāḥ praviśya saralaṃ hṛdayaṃ narāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: having entered the guileless hearts of men,

children.text: kiṃ vā na vāma-nayanā na samācaranti ||Panc_1.208||
children.translated_text: what do those doe-eyed ones not do? ||Panc_1.208||

children.text: antar-viṣa-mayā hy etā bahiś caiva manoramāḥ |
children.translated_text: Inwardly full of poison, yet outwardly charming —

children.text: guñjā-phala-samākārā yoṣitaḥ kena nirmitāḥ ||Panc_1.209||
children.translated_text: resembling <s>guñjā</s> berries in appearance — by whom were women made? ||Panc_1.209||

children.text: evaṃ cintayatas tasya parivrājakasya sā niśā mahatā kṛcchreṇāticakrāma | sā ca dūtikā chinna-nāsikā sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā cintayāmāsa-kim idānīṃ kartavyam ? katham etan mahac-chidraṃ sthagayitavyam ?
children.translated_text: Thus for the wandering ascetic, lost in thought, that night passed with great difficulty. And the go-between, her nose cut off, went to her own house and thought: What is to be done now? How can this great wound be concealed?

children.text: atha tasyā evaṃ vicintayantyā bhartā kārya-vaśād rāja-kule paryuṣitaḥ pratyūṣe ca sva-gṛham abhyupetya dvāra-deśa-stho vividha-paura-kṛtyotsukatayā tām āha-bhadre śīghram ānīyatāṃ kṣura-bhāṇḍaṃ yena kṣaura-karma-karaṇāya gacchāmi |
children.translated_text: Now, while she was thus deliberating, her husband, who had stayed overnight at the royal court on account of business, returned home at dawn. Standing at the doorway and eager [to attend to] various civic duties, he said to her: Good woman, quickly bring the razor-case so that I may go to do my barbering work.

children.text: sāpi chinnanāsikā gṛha-madhya-sthitaiva kārya-karaṇāpekṣayā kṣura-bhāṇḍāt kṣuram ekaṃ samākṛṣya tasyābhimukhaṃ preṣayāmāsa | nāpito 'py utsukatayā tam ekaṃ kṣuram avalokya kopāviṣṭaḥ san tad-abhimukham eva taṃ kṣuraṃ prāhiṇot | etasminn antare sā duṣṭordhva-bāhū vidhāya phutakartu-manā gṛhān niścakrāma | aho paśyata pāpenānena mama sad-ācāra-vartinyāḥ nāsikā-cchedo vihitaḥ | tat-paritrāyatāṃ paritrāyatām |
children.translated_text: She, with her nose cut off, remaining inside the house, drew out a single razor from the razor-case — on the pretext of [attending to] the task — and sent it toward him. The barber too, in his eagerness, seeing just that one razor, became filled with anger and threw that very razor back toward her. At this moment, she — the wicked woman — raising her arms upward and wishing to create a commotion, rushed out of the house [crying]: Look! By this villain my nose has been cut off — me, a woman of virtuous conduct! Save me, save me!

children.text: atrāntare rāja-puruṣāḥ samabhyetya taṃ nāpitaṃ laguḍa-prahārair jarjarīkṛtya dṛḍha-bandhanair baddhvā tayā chinnanāsikayā saha dharmādhikaraṇa-sthānaṃ nītvā sabhyān ūcuḥ-śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ sabhāsadaḥ | anena nāpitenāparādhaṃ vinā strī-ratnam etad vyaṅgitam | tad asya yad yujyate tat kriyatām |
children.translated_text: Then the king's men arrived, beat that barber with cudgel-blows until he was bruised, bound him with tight bonds, and took him along with the nose-cut woman to the court of justice. They told the judges: Hear, honored members of the court! This barber, without [her having committed any] offense, has mutilated this jewel of a woman. Therefore let whatever is appropriate be done to him.

children.text: ity abhihite sabhyā ūcuḥ-re nāpita ! kim-arthaṃ tvayā bhāryā vyaṅgitā | kim anayā para-puruṣo 'bhilaṣitaḥ | unta svit prāṇa-drohaḥ kṛtaḥ, kiṃ vā caurya-karmācaritam | tat kathyatām asyā aparādhaḥ ?
children.translated_text: When this was stated, the judges said: You, barber! For what reason have you mutilated [your] wife? Has she desired another man? Or has she committed an attempt on [your] life? Or has she committed theft? State her offense!

children.text: nāpito 'pi prahāra-pīḍita-tanur vaktuṃ na śaśāka | atha taṃ tūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā punar ūcuḥ-aho, satyam etad rāja-puruṣāṇāṃ vacaḥ | pāpātmāyam | aneneyaṃ nirdoṣā varākī dūṣitā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The barber too, his body afflicted by the blows, was unable to speak. Then, seeing him silent, they said again: Ah, truly what the king's men say is correct. This man is a sinner. By him this innocent, wretched woman has been defaced. And it is said —

children.text: bhinna-svara-mukha-varṇaḥ śaṅkita-dṛṣṭiḥ samutpatita-tejāḥ |
children.translated_text: His voice broken, face discolored, gaze suspicious, brilliance fled —

children.text: bhavati hi pāpaṃ kṛtvā sva-karma-santrāsitaḥ puruṣaḥ ||Panc_1.210||
children.translated_text: a man who has committed sin is terrified by his own deed. ||Panc_1.210||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: āyāti skhalitaiḥ pādair mukha-vaivarṇya-saṃyutaḥ |
children.translated_text: He comes with stumbling feet, accompanied by discoloration of face,

children.text: lalāṭa-sveda-bhāg bhūri-gadgadaṃ bhāṣate vacaḥ ||Panc_1.211||
children.translated_text: sweat on his forehead, speaking words with much stammering. ||Panc_1.211||

children.text: adho-dṛṣṭir vadet kṛtvā pāpaṃ prāptaḥ sabhāṃ naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A man who has committed sin and come to the court speaks with downcast eyes;

children.text: tasmād yatnāt parijñeyāś cihnair etair vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||Panc_1.212||
children.translated_text: therefore, by these signs, the discerning should carefully ascertain [the truth]. ||Panc_1.212||

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: prasanna-vadano dṛṣṭaḥ spaṣṭa-vākyaḥ saroṣa-dṛk |
children.translated_text: One who is seen with a serene face, speaks clearly, with an indignant look,

children.text: sabhāyāṃ vakti sāmarṣaṃ sāvaṣṭambho naraḥ śuciḥ ||Panc_1.213||
children.translated_text: speaks boldly in the assembly with confidence — such a man is innocent. ||Panc_1.213||

children.text: tad eṣa duṣṭa-caritra-lakṣaṇo dṛśyate | strī-dharsaṇād vadhya iti | tac chūlīyām āropyatām iti |
children.translated_text: This one displays the marks of wicked conduct. For assaulting a woman he deserves death. Therefore let him be impaled on the stake!

children.text: atha vadhya-sthāne nīyamānaṃ tam avalokya deva-śarmā tān dharmādhikṛtān gatvā provāca-bho bhoḥ, anyānyenaiṣa varāko vadhyate nāpitaḥ | sādhu-samācāra eṣaḥ | tac chrūyatāṃ me vākyam-jambūko huḍu-yuddhena iti |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him being led to the execution ground, <s>Devaśarman</s> went to those officers of justice and said: Sirs! This wretched barber is being killed for another's crime. He is of virtuous conduct. So hear my words — [as the tale goes:] 'The jackal by the drum-battle.'

children.text: atha te sabhyā ūcuḥ-bho bhagavan ! katham etat ?
children.translated_text: Then those judges said: Reverend sir! How is that?

children.text: tato devaśarmā teṣāṃ trayāṇām api vṛttāntaṃ vistareṇākathayat | tad ākarṇya suvismita-manasas te nāpitaṃ vimocya mithaḥ procuḥ-aho !
children.translated_text: Then <s>Devaśarman</s> narrated in detail the circumstances of all three. Hearing that, greatly astonished in mind, they released the barber and said to one another: Ah!

children.text: avadhyā brāhmaṇā gāvo striyo bālāś ca jñātayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Not to be killed are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cows, women, children, and kinsmen,

children.text: yeṣāṃ cānnāni bhuñjīta ye ca syuḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ ||Panc_1.214||
children.translated_text: and those whose food one has eaten, and those who have taken refuge. ||Panc_1.214||

children.text: tad asyā nāsikā-cchedaḥ sva-karmaṇā hi saṃvṛttaḥ | tato rāja-nigrahas tu karṇa-cchedaḥ kāryaḥ | tathānuṣṭhite devaśarmāpi vitta-nāśa-samudbhūta-śoka-rahitaḥ punar api svakīyaṃ maṭhāyatanaṃ jagāma | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-jambūko huḍu-yuddhena (1.174) iti |
children.translated_text: Her nose-cutting has occurred by her own deed. Therefore the royal punishment should be ear-cutting. When this was carried out, <s>Devaśarman</s> too, free from grief born of loss of wealth, went once again to his own monastery. Therefore I say: 'The jackal by the drum-battle' (1.174).

children.text: karaṭaka āha-evaṃ-vidhe vyatikare kiṃ kartavyam āvayoḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: In a situation of this kind, what is to be done by us two?

children.text: damanako 'bravīt-evaṃ-vidhe'pi samaye mama buddhi-sphuraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, yena sañjīvakaṃ prabhor viśleṣayiṣyāmi | uktaṃ ca, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: Even in such a situation, my intelligence will flash forth, by which I shall separate <s>Sañjīvaka</s> from the master. And it is said, for —

children.text: ekaṃ hanyān na vā hanyād iṣuḥ kṣipto dhanuṣmatā |
children.translated_text: An arrow shot by a bowman may kill one or may not kill;

children.text: prājñena tu matiḥ kṣiptā hanyād garbha-gatān api ||Panc_1.215||
children.translated_text: but a plan launched by a wise man can kill even those [still] in the womb. ||Panc_1.215||

children.text: tad ahaṃ māyā-prapañcena guptam āśritya taṃ sphoṭayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: So I, having taken refuge in a secret stratagem of deception, shall expose him.

children.text: karaṭaka āha-bhadra, yadi katham api tava māyā-praveśaṃ piṅgalako jñāsyati, sañjīvako vā tadā nūnaṃ vighāta eva |
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: Friend, if somehow <s>Piṅgalaka</s> discovers your resort to deception, or <s>Sañjīvaka</s> [does], then surely there will be calamity.

children.text: so 'bravīt-tāta, maivaṃ vada | gūḍha-buddhibhir āpat-kāle vidhure'pi daive buddhiḥ prayoktavyā | nodyamas tyājyaḥ | kadācid ghuṇākṣara-nyāyena buddheḥ sāmrājyaṃ bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Dear one, do not say so! Those of hidden intelligence must exercise their wits even in times of adversity, when fate is cruel. Effort must not be abandoned. Sometimes, by the principle of the worm-letters [i.e., accidental success], intelligence attains sovereignty. And it is said —

children.text: tyājyaṃ na dhairyaṃ vidhure'pi daive
children.translated_text: Courage should not be abandoned even when fate is cruel;

children.text: dhairyāt kadācit sthitm āpnuyāt saḥ |
children.translated_text: through courage one may sometimes attain stability.

children.text: yāte samudre'pi hi pota-bhaṅge
children.translated_text: Even when the ship has broken in mid-ocean,

children.text: sāṃyātriko vāñchati karma eva ||Panc_1.216||
children.translated_text: the voyager desires action alone. ||Panc_1.216||

children.text: tathā ca-
udyoginaṃ satatam atra sameti lakṣmīr
children.translated_text: Fortune always comes to the industrious;

children.text: daivaṃ hi daivam iti kāpuruṣā vadanti |
children.translated_text: cowards say 'it is fate, it is fate.'

children.text: daivaṃ nihatya kuru pauruṣam ātma-śaktyā yatne kṛte yadi na sidhyati ko 'tra doṣaḥ ||Panc_1.217||
children.translated_text: Cast aside fate and exert manly effort by your own power; if [success] is not achieved despite effort, what fault is there? ||Panc_1.217||
And likewise —

children.text: tad evaṃ jñātvā sugūḍha-buddhi-prabhāveṇa yathā tau dvāv api na jñāsyataḥ, tathā mitho viyojayiṣyāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So knowing this, by the power of deeply hidden intelligence, I shall separate those two in such a way that neither will discover it. And it is said —

children.text: suprayuktasya dambhasya brahmāpy antaṃ na gacchati |
children.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s> cannot reach the end of deceit well-employed;

children.text: kauliko viṣṇu-rūpeṇa rāja-kanyāṃ niṣevate ||Panc_1.218||
children.translated_text: a weaver in the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s> enjoys a king's daughter. ||Panc_1.218||

children.text: karaṭaka āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 5
kaulika-rathakāra-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said —
Tale 5
The Story of the Weaver and the Chariot-maker

children.text:
kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne kaulika-rathakārau mitre prativasataḥ sma | tatra ca bālyāt-prabhṛti sahacāriṇau parasparam atīva sneha-parau sadaika-sthāna-vihāriṇau kālaṃ nayataḥ | atha kadācit tatrādhiṣṭhāne kasmiṃścid devāyatane yātrā-mahotsavaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | tatra ca naṭa-nartaka-cāraṇa-saṅkule nānā-deśāgata-janāvṛte tau sahacarau bhramantau kāñcid rāja-kanyāṃ kareṇukārūḍhāṃ sarva-lakṣaṇa-sanāthāṃ kañcuki-varṣa-dhara-parivāritāṃ devatā-darśanārthaṃ samāyātāṃ dṛṣṭavantau | athāsau kaulikas tāṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣārdita iva duṣṭa-graha-gṛhīta iiva kāma-śarair hanyamānaḥ sahasā bhūtale nipapāta | atha taṃ tad-avastham avalokya rathakāras tad-duḥkha-duḥkhita āpta-puruṣais taṃ samutkṣipya sva-gṛham ānāyayat | tatra
ca vividhaiḥ śītopacāraiś cikitsakopadiṣṭair mantra-vādibhir upacaryamāṇaiś cirāt kathaṃcit sa-cetano babhūva |
children.translated_text: In a certain town, a weaver and a chariot-maker were living as friends. Having been companions since childhood, exceedingly fond of each other, always spending time in the same place, they passed their days. Now once, in that town, at a certain temple, a festival with a great procession occurred. There, amidst crowds of actors, dancers, and bards, thronged with people come from various lands, the two companions wandering about saw a certain princess riding an elephant, endowed with all auspicious marks, surrounded by eunuchs and umbrella-bearers, who had come for the purpose of seeing the deity. Then that weaver, upon seeing her — as if poisoned, as if seized by an evil spirit, struck by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (the love-god) — suddenly fell to the ground. Then the chariot-maker, seeing him in that state, grieved by his friend's grief, had him lifted up by trusted men and brought to his own house. There, treated with various cooling remedies prescribed by physicians and attended by mantra-chanters, after a long time he somehow regained consciousness.

children.text: tato rathakāreṇa pṛṣṭaḥ-bho mitra ! kim evaṃ tvam akasmād vicetanaḥ sañjātaḥ ? tat kathyatām ātma-svarūpam ?
children.translated_text: Then, questioned by the chariot-maker: Friend! Why have you suddenly become unconscious like this? Tell [me] your true condition!

children.text: sa āha-vayasya ! yady evaṃ tac chṛṇu me rahasyaṃ yena sarvām ātma-vedanāṃ te vadāmi | yadi tvaṃ māṃ suhṛdaṃ manyase tataḥ kāṣṭha-pradānena prasādaḥ kriyatām | kṣamyatāṃ yad vā kiñcit praṇay>atirekād ayuktaṃ tava mayānuṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: He said: Comrade! If so, then hear my secret, by which I shall tell you all my inner pain. If you consider me a friend, then grant me a favor by [providing] wood. And forgive whatever improper [thing] I may have done to you out of excessive affection.

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇya bāṣpa-pihita-nayanaḥ sa-gadgadam uvāca-vayasya, yat kiñcid duḥkha-kāraṇaṃ tad vada yena pratīkāraḥ kriyate, yadi śakyate kartum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He too, hearing that, his eyes veiled with tears, said with a choked voice: Comrade, state whatever is the cause of your suffering, so that a remedy may be devised — if it can be done. And it is said —

children.text: auṣadhārtha-sumantrāṇāṃ buddheś caiva mahātmanām |
children.translated_text: Of medicines, good counsel,

children.text: asādhyaṃ nāsti loke'tra yad brahmāṇḍasya madhyagam ||Panc_1.219||
children.translated_text: and the intelligence of great souls — there is nothing incurable in this world that lies within the cosmic egg. ||Panc_1.219||

children.text: tad eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ yadi sādhyaṃ bhaviṣyati tadāhaṃ sādhayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: If it is achievable by these four [means], then I shall accomplish it.

children.text: kaulika āha-vayasya, eteṣām anyeṣām api sahasrāṇām upāyānām asādhyaṃ tan me duḥkham | tasmān mama maraṇe mā kāla-kṣepaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: Comrade, my suffering is unachievable even by thousands of other means. Therefore do not waste time on my death.

children.text: rathakāra āha-bho mitra ! yadyapy asādhyaṃ tathāpi nivedaya yenāham api tad asādhyaṃ matvā tvayā samaṃ vahnau praviśāmi | na kṣaṇam api tvad-viyogaṃ sahiṣye | eṣa me niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The chariot-maker said: Friend! Even if it is unachievable, still tell me, so that I too, considering it unachievable, may enter the fire together with you. I will not endure separation from you even for a moment. This is my resolve.

children.text: kaulika āha-vayasya, yāsau rāja-kanyā kareṇum ārūḍhā tatrotsave dṛṣṭā, tasyā darśanānantaraṃ makara-dhvajena mameyam avasthā vihitā | tan na śaknomi tad-vedanāṃ soḍhum | tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: The weaver said: Comrade, that princess who was seen at the festival, mounted on an elephant — immediately after seeing her, this condition was inflicted on me by the Banner-bearer [<s>Kāma</s>, the love-god]. I cannot endure that pain. And thus it is said —

children.text: mattebha-kumbha-pariṇāhini kuṅkumārdre
children.translated_text: When shall I, wearied by love's exertion, placing my chest

children.text: tasyāḥ payodhara-yuge rati-kheda-khinnaḥ |
children.translated_text: upon her pair of breasts — round as the frontal globes of a rutting elephant, moist with saffron —

children.text: vakṣo nidhāya bhuja-pañjara-madhya-vartī
children.translated_text: resting within the cage of [her] arms,

children.text: svapsye kadā kṣaṇam avāpya tadīya-saṅgam ||Panc_1.220||
children.translated_text: sleep for a moment, having attained union with her? ||Panc_1.220||

children.text: tathā ca-
rāgī bimbādharo 'sau stana-kalaśa-yugaṃ yauvanārūḍha-garvaṃ
children.translated_text: Her passionate lip [red as] a <s>bimba</s> fruit, her pair of breast-pitchers swelling with the pride of youth,

children.text: nīcā nābhiḥ prakṛtyā kuṭilakam alakaṃ svalpakaṃ cāpi madhyam |
children.translated_text: her navel naturally deep, her hair naturally curly, and her waist so slender —

children.text: kurvatv etāni nāma prasabham iha manaś cintitāny āśu khedaṃ
children.translated_text: let these indeed, forcibly contemplated by my mind, quickly cause distress;

children.text: yan māṃ tasyāḥ kapolau dahata iti muhuḥ svacchakau tan na yuktam ||Panc_1.221||
children.translated_text: but that her two cheeks, which are perfectly clear, burn me again and again — that is not fair! ||Panc_1.221||
And likewise —

children.text: rathakāro 'py evaṃ sa-kāmaṃ tad-vacanam ākarṇya sa-smitam idam āha-vayasya ! yady evaṃ tarhi diṣṭyā siddhaṃ naḥ prayojanam | tad adyaiva tayā saha samāgamaḥ kriyatām iti |
children.translated_text: The chariot-maker too, hearing those words full of desire, said with a smile: Comrade! If so, then fortunately our purpose is accomplished! Let a union with her be arranged this very day!

children.text: kaulika āha-vayasya, yatra kanyāntaḥpure vāyuṃ muktvā nānyasya praveśo 'sti tatra rakṣā-puruṣādhiṣṭhite kathaṃ mama tasyā saha samāgamaḥ ? tat kiṃ mām asatya-vacanena viḍambayasi ?
children.translated_text: The weaver said: Comrade, where in the inner apartments of the princess no one besides the wind has entry — there, guarded by watchmen — how can I have a meeting with her? Why do you mock me with false words?

children.text: rathakāra āha-mitra, paśya me buddhi-balam |
children.translated_text: The chariot-maker said: Friend, behold the power of my intelligence!

children.text: evam abhidhāya tat-kṣaṇāt kīla-sañcāriṇaṃ vainateyaṃ bāhu-yugalaṃ vāyuja-vṛkṣa-dāruṇā śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padmānvitaṃ sa-kirīṭa-kaustubham aghaṭayan | tatas tasmin kaulikaṃ samāropya viṣṇu-cihnitaṃ kṛtvā kīla-sañcaraṇa-vijñānaṃ ca darśayitvā provāca-vayasya, anena viṣṇu-rūpeṇa gatvā kanyāntaḥpure niśīthe tāṃ rājakanyām ekākinīṃ sapta-bhūmika-prāsāda-prānta-gatāṃ mugdha-svabhāvāṃ tvāṃ vāsudevaṃ manyamānāṃ svakīya-mithyā-vakroktibhī rañjayitvā vātsyāyanokta-vidhinā bhaja |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he immediately fashioned, from the wood of a <s>vāyuja</s> tree, a mechanical <s>Garuḍa</s> (eagle-mount) with movable pegs, a pair of arms bearing conch, discus, mace, and lotus, together with crown and <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem]. Then, mounting the weaver upon it, making him bear the marks of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and showing him the science of peg-operation, he said: Comrade, in this form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, go to the princess's inner apartments at midnight. She — alone on the terrace of the seven-storied palace, innocent by nature, thinking you to be <s>Vāsudeva</s> (Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>) — delight her with your own crafty, false words and enjoy her according to the method prescribed by <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: kauliko 'pi tad ākarṇya tathā-rūpas tatra gatvā tām āha-rāja-putri, suptā kiṃ vā jāgarṣi ? ahaṃ tava kṛte samudrāt sānurāgo lakṣmīṃ vihāyaivāgataḥ | tat kriyatāṃ mayā saha samāgamaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: The weaver too, hearing that, went there in that form and said to her: Princess, are you asleep or awake? I, out of love for you, have come leaving <s>Lakṣmī</s> [behind] in the ocean. So let a union with me be made.

children.text: sāpi garuḍārūḍhaṃ caturbhujaṃ sāyudhaṃ kaustubhopetam avalokya sa-vismayā śayanād utthāya provāca-bhagavan ! ahaṃ mānuṣī kīṭikāśuciḥ | bhagavāṃs trailokya-pāvano vandanīyaś ca | tat katham etad yujyate |
children.translated_text: And she, seeing the four-armed one mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, armed and adorned with the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem], rose from her bed in astonishment and said: 'Lord! I am a human woman, impure as an insect. The Lord is the purifier of the three worlds and worthy of worship. How then is this appropriate?'

children.text: kaulika āha-subhage, satyam abhihitaṃ bhavatyā | paraṃ kiṃ tu rādhā nāma me bhāryā gopa-kula-prasūtā prathama āsīt | sā tvam atrāvatīrṇā | tenāham atrāyātaḥ |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'Fair one, what you say is true. But I had a wife named <s>Rādhā</s>, born in a cowherd clan, in a former [life]. You are she, descended here. Therefore I have come here.'

children.text: ity uktā sā prāha-bhagavan, yady evaṃ tan me tātaṃ prārthaya | so 'py avikalpaṃ māṃ tubhyaṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, she said: 'Lord, if it is so, then ask my father. He will give me to you without hesitation.'

children.text: kaulika āha-subhage, nāhaṃ darśana-pathaṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ gacchāmi | kiṃ punar ālāpa-karaṇam | tvaṃ gāndharveṇa vivhāneātmānaṃ prayaccha | no cec chāpaṃ dattvā sānvayaṃ te pitaraṃ bhasmasāt kariṣyāmi iti | evam abhidhāya garuḍād avatīrya savye pāṇau gṛhītvā tāṃ sabhayāṃ salajjāṃ vepamānāṃ śayyāyām ānayat | tataś ca rātri-śeṣaṃ yāvad vātsyāyanokta-vidhinā niṣevya pratyūṣe sva-gṛham alakṣito jagāma |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'Fair one, I do not come within the sight of humans. Much less do I converse [with them]. Give yourself [to me] by the <s>Gāndharva</s> form of marriage. If not, I shall give a curse and reduce your father along with his lineage to ashes.' Having spoken thus, he descended from <s>Garuḍa</s>, took her by the left hand — her fearful, bashful, and trembling — and brought her to the bed. Then, for the remainder of the night, having enjoyed her according to the method prescribed by <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, he went unnoticed to his own home at dawn.

children.text: evaṃ tasya tāṃ nityaṃ sevamānasya kālo yāti | atha kadācit kañcukinas tasyā adharoṣṭha-pravāla-khaṇḍanaṃ dṛṣṭvā mithaḥ procuḥ-aho ! paśyatāsyā rāja-kanyāyāḥ puruṣopabhuktāyā iva śarīrāvayavā vibhāvyante | tat katham ayaṃ surakṣite'py asmin gṛha evaṃvidho vyavahāraḥ | tad rājñe nivedayāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, as he visited her daily, time passed. Then one day, the chamberlains, seeing the biting of her lower lip's tender [flesh], said to one another: 'Look! The limbs of this princess appear as if enjoyed by a man. How is such conduct [possible] in this well-guarded residence? Let us inform the king.'

children.text: evaṃ niścitya sarve sametya rājānaṃ procuḥ-deva ! vayaṃ na vidmaḥ | paraṃ surakṣite'pi kanyāntaḥ-pure kaścit praviśati | tad devaḥ pramāṇam iti | tac chrutvā rājātīva vyākulita-citto vyacintayat-
children.translated_text: Having so resolved, all of them together addressed the king: 'Majesty! We do not know [how], but even in the well-guarded princess's inner quarters, someone enters. The king is the authority [on what to do].' Hearing that, the king, his mind greatly agitated, thought:

children.text: putrīti jātā mahatīha cintā
children.translated_text: 'A daughter is born — and with her, great anxiety;

children.text: kasmai pradeyeti mahān vitarkaḥ |
children.translated_text: to whom shall she be given — that is the great deliberation;

children.text: dattvā sukhaṃ prāpsyati vā na veti
children.translated_text: having given her, will she attain happiness or not? —

children.text: kanyā-pitṛtvaṃ khalu nāma kaṣṭam ||Panc_1.222||
children.translated_text: being a daughter's father is truly a hardship.' ||Panc_1.222||

children.text: nadyaś ca nāryaś ca sadṛk-prabhāvās
children.translated_text: Rivers and women are of equal power;

children.text: tulyāni kūlāni kulāni tāsām |
children.translated_text: their banks and their families are alike;

children.text: toyaiś ca doṣaiś ca nipātayanti
children.translated_text: by their waters and their faults they cause ruin —

children.text: nadyo hi kūlāni kulāni nāryaḥ ||Panc_1.223||
children.translated_text: rivers [ruin] banks, and women [ruin] families. ||Panc_1.223||

children.text: jananī-mano harati jātavatī
children.translated_text: She steals her mother's heart when born;

children.text: parivardhate saha śucā suhṛdām |
children.translated_text: she grows up along with the anxiety of her loved ones;

children.text: para-sātkṛtāpi kurute malinaṃ
children.translated_text: even when given to another, she causes disgrace —

children.text: durita-kramā duhitaro vipadaḥ ||Panc_1.224||
children.translated_text: daughters are calamities whose course is sinful. ||Panc_1.224||

children.text: evaṃ bahu-vidhaṃ vicintya devīṃ rahaḥ-sthāṃ provāca-devi, jñāyatāṃ kim ete kañcukino vadanti ? tasya kṛtāntaḥ kupito yenaitad evaṃ kriyate |
children.translated_text: Having thought in many such ways, he addressed the queen in private: 'Queen, find out what these chamberlains are saying. Death is angry with whoever is doing this.'

children.text: devy api tad ākarṇya vyākulī-bhūtā satvaraṃ kanyāntaḥpure gatvā tāṃ khaṇḍitādharāṃ nakha-vilikhita-śarīrāvayavāṃ duhitaram apaśyat | āha ca-āḥ pāpe ! kula-kalaṅka-kāriṇi ! kim eva śīla-khaṇḍanaṃ kṛtam | ko 'yaṃ kṛtāntāvalokitas tvat-sakāśam abhyeti | tat kathyatāṃ mamāgre satyam |
children.translated_text: And the queen, hearing that, became distressed; going quickly to the princess's inner quarters, she saw her daughter with bitten lower lip and body-parts marked by nail-scratches. And she said: 'Oh wicked one! Disgrace of the family! What violation of virtue have you committed? Who is this death-courting one who comes to you? Tell me the truth!'

children.text: iti kopāṭopa-visaṅkaṭaṃ vadatyāṃ mātari rāja-putrī bhaya-lajjānatānanaṃ provāca-amba, sākṣān nārāyaṇaḥ pratyahaṃ garuḍārūḍho niśi samāyāti | ced asatyaṃ mama vākyam, tat sva-cakṣuṣā vilokayatu niguḍhatarā niśīthe bhagavantaṃ ramā-kāntam |
children.translated_text: When the mother spoke thus, terrible with the fury of anger, the princess, her face bowed with fear and shame, said: 'Mother, it is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself who comes every night, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>. If my words are false, then let her look with her own eyes upon the Lord, the beloved of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), in deepest secrecy at midnight.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sāpi prahasita-vadanā pulakāṅkita-sarvāṅgī satvaraṃ rājānam ūce-deva, diṣṭyā vardhase | nityam eva niśīthe bhagavān nārāyaṇaḥ kanyakā-pārśve'bhyeti | tena gāndharva-vivāhena sā vivāhitā | tad adya tvayā mayā ca rātrau vātāyana-gatābhyāṃ niśīthe draṣṭavyaḥ | yato na sa mānuṣaiḥ sahālāpaṃ karoti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, she too, with a smiling face and her whole body covered in goosebumps, quickly told the king: 'Majesty, may you prosper! Every night at midnight, the blessed Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> comes to the princess's side. She has been married to him by the <s>Gāndharva</s> form of marriage. Today, you and I, stationed at the window at night, should see [him] at midnight. For he does not converse with humans.'

children.text: tac chrutvā harṣitasya rājñas tad dinaṃ varṣa-śata-prāyam iva kathañcij jagāma | tatas tu rātrau nibhṛto bhūtvā rājñī-sahito rājā vātāyanas-stho gaganāsakta-dṛṣṭir yāvat tiṣṭhati, tāvat tasmin samaye garuḍārūḍhaṃ taṃ śaṅka-cakra-gadā-padma-hastaṃ yathokta-cihnāṅkitaṃ vyomno 'vatarantaṃ nārāyaṇam apaśyat | tataḥ sudhā-pūra-plāvitam ivātmānaṃ manyamānas tām uvāca-priye ! nāsty anyo dhanyataro loke mattas tvattaś ca | tat prasūtiṃ nārāyaṇo bhajate | tat-siddhāḥ sarve'smākaṃ manorathāḥ | adhunā jāmātṛ-prabhāveṇa sakalām api vasumatīṃ vaśyāṃ kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the delighted king's day passed as if it were a hundred years. Then at night, having become still, the king, accompanied by the queen, stood at the window with his gaze fixed on the sky. At that moment, he saw <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, holding conch, discus, mace, and lotus in his hands, marked with the described signs, descending from the sky. Then, feeling as if drenched in a flood of nectar, he said to her: 'Beloved! There is no one more blessed in the world than I and you. For <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is taking our daughter. All our desires are fulfilled. Now, by the power of [this] son-in-law, I shall bring the entire earth under my sway.'

children.text: evaṃ niścitya sarvaiḥ sīmādhipaiḥ saha maryādā-vyatikramam akarot | te ca taṃ maryādā-vyatikrameṇa vartamānam ālokya sarve sametya tena saha vigrahaṃ cakruḥ |
children.translated_text: Having so resolved, he violated the boundaries with all the neighboring kings. And they, seeing him acting in violation of boundaries, all assembled and waged war against him.

children.text: atrāntare sa rājā devī-mukhena tāṃ duhitaram uvāca-putri, tvayi duhitari vartamānāyāṃ nārāyaṇe bhagavati jāmātari sthite tat kim evaṃ yujyate yat sarve pārthivā mayā saha vigrahaṃ kurvanti | tat sambodhyo 'dya tvayā nija-bhartā, yathā mama śatrūn vyāpādayati |
children.translated_text: In the meantime, the king, through the queen, said to his daughter: 'Daughter, while you — our daughter — are present, and the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is [our] son-in-law, how is it fitting that all the kings wage war against me? Therefore, today you should admonish your own husband, that he should destroy my enemies.'

children.text: tatas tayā sa kauliko rātrau sa-vinayam abhihitaḥ-bhagavan, tvayi jāmātari sthite mama tāto yac chatrubhiḥ paribhūyate tan na yuktam | tat prasādaṃ kṛtvā sarvāṃs tān śatrūn vyāpādaya |
children.translated_text: Then she respectfully told the weaver at night: 'Lord, while you are [our] son-in-law, that my father is overwhelmed by enemies is not fitting. Therefore, please show grace and destroy all those enemies.'

children.text: kaulika āha-subhage ! kiyan-mātrās tv ete tava pituḥ śatravaḥ | tad-viśvastā bhava | kṣaṇenāpi sudarśana-cakreṇa sarvāṃs tilaśaḥ khaṇḍayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'Fair one! How insignificant are these enemies of your father? Be confident — in a moment, with the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus, I shall cut them all to pieces.'

children.text: atha gacchatā kālena sarva-deśaṃ śatrubhir udvāsya sa rājā prākāra-śeṣaḥ kṛtaḥ | tathāpi vāsudeva-rūpa-dharaṃ kaulikam ajānan rāja nityam eva viśeṣataḥ karpūrāguru-kastūrikādi-parimala-viśeṣān nānā-prakāra-vastra-puṣpa-bhakṣya-peyāṃś ca preṣayan duhitṛ-mukhena tam ūce-bhagavan, prabhāte nūnaṃ sthāna-bhaṅgo bhaviṣyati | yato yavasendhana-kṣayaḥ sañjātas tathā sarvo 'pi janaḥ prahārair jarjarita-dehaḥ saṃvṛtto yoddhum akṣamaḥ pracuro mṛtaś ca | tad evaṃ jñātvātra kāle yad ucitaṃ bhavati tad vidheyam iti |
children.translated_text: Then, as time passed, having been driven from every territory by the enemies, the king was reduced to [possessing only] the ramparts. Even so, the king, not knowing the weaver who wore the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, kept sending to his daughter's [quarters] especially fine camphor, aloe, musk and other perfumes, and various types of garments, flowers, foods and drinks, and through his daughter said to him: 'Lord, surely in the morning there will be a fall of our position. For the supply of grain and fuel has been exhausted; moreover, all the people, with bodies battered by blows, have become unable to fight, and many have died. Therefore, knowing this, at this time whatever is proper should be done.'

children.text: tac chrutvā kauliko 'py acintayat-sthāna-bhaṅge jāte mamānayā saha viyogo bhaviṣyati æ tasmād garuḍam āruhya sāyudham ātmānam ākāśe darśayāmi | kadācin māṃ vāsudevaṃ manyamānās te sāśaṅkā rājño yoddhṛbhir hanyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the weaver thought: 'When the position falls, I shall be separated from her. Therefore I shall mount <s>Garuḍa</s> and display myself armed in the sky. Perhaps, thinking me to be <s>Vāsudeva</s>, they will become fearful and the king's warriors will slay them.' And it is said —

children.text: nirviṣeṇāpi sarpeṇa kartavyā mahatī phaṇā |
children.translated_text: Even a non-venomous snake should spread its hood wide;

children.text: viṣaṃ bhavatu vā mābhūt phaṇāṭopo bhayaṅkaraḥ ||Panc_1.225||
children.translated_text: whether there is venom or not, the display of the hood is terrifying. ||Panc_1.225||

children.text: atha yadi mama sthānārtham udyatasya mṛtyur bhaviṣyati tad api sundarataram | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'But if death should come to me while striving for [this] position, that too is most beautiful.' And it is said —

children.text: gavām arthe brāhmaṇārthe svāmy-arthe svīkṛte'thavā |
children.translated_text: For the sake of cows, for the sake of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, for the sake of a master, or for one who has taken refuge —

children.text: sthānārthe yas tyajet prāṇāṃs tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ ||Panc_1.226||
children.translated_text: for the sake of one's position, he who gives up his life — his worlds are eternal. ||Panc_1.226||

children.text: candre maṇḍala-saṃsthe vigṛhyate rāhuṇā dinādhīśaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the moon is in its full orb, it is seized by <s>Rāhu</s>, the lord of the day;

children.text: śaraṇāgatena sārdhaṃ vipad api tejasvinā ślāghyā ||Panc_1.227||
children.translated_text: for the heroic one, even calamity together with a refugee is glorious. ||Panc_1.227||

children.text: evaṃ niścitya pratyūṣe danta-dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā tāṃ provāca-subhage ! samastaiḥ śatrubhir hatair annaṃ pānaṃ cāsvādayiṣyāmi | kiṃ bahunā, tvayāpi saha saṅgamaṃ tataḥ kariṣyāmi | paraṃ vācyas tvayātma-pitā yat prabhāte prabhūtena sainyena saha nagarān niṣkramya yoddhavyam | ahaṃ cākāśa-sthita eva sarvāṃs tān nistejasaḥ kariṣyāmi | paścāt sukhena bhavatā hantavyāḥ yadi punar ahaṃ tān svayam eva sūdayāmi tat teṣāṃ pāpātmanāṃ vaikuṇṭhīyā gatiḥ syāt | tasmāt te tathā kartavyā yathā palāyanto hanyamānāḥ svargaṃ na gacchanti |
children.translated_text: Having so resolved, at dawn, having cleaned his teeth, he said to her: 'Fair one! After all the enemies have been slain, I shall taste food and drink. In short, I shall have union with you as well only after that. But you should tell your father that in the morning he should come out of the city with a large army and fight. I, stationed in the sky, shall render them all powerless. Afterwards, they can be slain at ease. But if I myself kill them, then those evil souls would attain the abode of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>. Therefore they should be dealt with in such a way that, while fleeing and being slain, they do not go to heaven.'

children.text: sāpi tad ākarṇya pituḥ samīpaṃ gatvā sarvaṃ vṛttāntaṃ nyavedayat | rājāpi tasyā vākyaṃ śraddadhānaḥ pratyūṣe samutthāya samunnaddha-sainyo yuddhārthaṃ niścakrāma | kauliko 'pi maraṇe kṛta-niścayaś cāpa-pāṇir gagana-gatir garuḍārūḍho yuddhāya prasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: She too, hearing that, went to her father's presence and reported the entire matter. And the king, believing her words, rose at dawn, and with his army arrayed in full force, marched out for battle. The weaver too, having resolved on death, with bow in hand, moving through the sky, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, set out for battle.

children.text: atrāntare bhagavatā nārāyaṇenātītānāgata-vartamāna-vedinā, smṛta-mātro vainateyaḥ samprāpto vihasya proktaḥ-bho garutman ! jānāsi tvaṃ yan mama rūpeṇa kauliko dāru-maya-garuḍe samārūḍho rāja-kanyāṃ kāmayate |
children.translated_text: In the meantime, the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who knows the past, future, and present, [summoned] <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) — who arrived merely by being thought of — and said with a smile: 'O <s>Garutman</s>! Do you know that a weaver, mounted on a wooden <s>Garuḍa</s>, is desiring a princess in my form?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva, sarvaṃ jñāyate tac ceṣṭitam | tat kiṃ kurmaḥ sāmpratam ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'Lord, all his doings are known. What shall we do now?'

children.text: śrī-bhagavān āha-adya kauliko maraṇe kṛta-niścayo vihita-niyamo yuddhārthe vinirgataḥ sa nūnaṃ pradhāna-kṣatriyair militvā vāsudevo garuḍaś ca nipātitaḥ | tataḥ paraṃ loko 'yam āvayoḥ pūjāṃ na kariṣyati | tatas tvaṃ drutataraṃ tatra dāru-maya-garuḍe saṅkramaṇaṃ kuru | aham api kaulika-śarīre praveśaṃ kariṣyāmi | yena sa śatrūn vyāpādayati | tataś ca śatru-vadhād āvayor māhātmya-vṛddhiḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: The blessed Lord said: 'Today the weaver, having resolved on death and observed his vows, has gone out for battle. He will surely be struck down by the chief <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, [thinking] "<s>Vāsudeva</s> and <s>Garuḍa</s> have been brought down!" Thereafter, this world will not worship the two of us. Therefore, go quickly there and transfer yourself to that wooden <s>Garuḍa</s>. I too shall enter the weaver's body — so that he destroys the enemies. And from the destruction of the enemies, the greatness of us both will increase.'

children.text: atha garuḍe tatheti pratipanne śrī-bhagavan-nārāyaṇas tac-charīre saṅkramaṇam akarot | tato bhagavan-māhātmyena gagana-sthaḥ sa kaulikaḥ śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-cāpa-cihnitaḥ kṣaṇād eva līlayaiva samastān api pradhāna-kṣatriyān nistejasaś cakārar | tatas tena rājñā sva-sainya-parivṛtena saṅgrāme jitā nihatāś ca te sarve'pi śatravaḥ | jātaś ca loka-madhye pravādo, yathā-anena viṣṇu-jāmātṛ-prabhāveṇa sarve śatravo nihatā iti |
children.translated_text: When <s>Garuḍa</s> agreed, the blessed Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> transferred himself into that [weaver's] body. Then, by the Lord's power, that weaver, stationed in the sky, marked with conch, discus, mace, and bow, in a moment, effortlessly, rendered all the chief <s>Kṣatriyas</s> powerless. Then that king, surrounded by his own army, conquered in battle and slew all those enemies. And a saying spread among the people: 'By the power of this son-in-law of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, all the enemies were slain.'

children.text: kauliko 'pi tān hatān dṛṣṭvā pramudita-manā gaganād avatīrṇaḥ san, yāvad rājāmātya-paura-lokās taṃ nagara-vāstavyaṃ kaulikaṃ paśyanti tataḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kim etad iti | tataḥ so 'pi mūlād ārabhya sarvaṃ prāg-vṛttāntaṃ nyavedayat | tataś ca kaulika-sāhasānurañjita-manasā śatru-vadhād avāpta-tejasā rājñā sā rāja-kanyā sakala-jana-pratyakṣaṃ vivāha-vidhinā tasmai samarpitā deśaś ca pradattaḥ | kauliko 'pi tayā sārdhaṃ pañca-prakāraṃ jīva-loka-sāraṃ viṣaya-sukham anubhavan kālaṃ nināya | atas tūcyate suprayuktasya dambhasya (218) iti |
children.translated_text: And the weaver, seeing them slain, descended from the sky with a joyful mind. When the king, ministers, citizens, and common people saw that he was a weaver dwelling in the city, they asked: 'What is this?' Then he too, beginning from the root, reported the entire previous account. Then the king, his mind delighted by the weaver's daring, having gained glory from the destruction of enemies, gave that princess to him in marriage according to proper rites in the sight of all the people, and also gave him a territory. And the weaver, together with her, enjoying the five kinds of sensual pleasure — the essence of mortal life — passed his time. Therefore it is said: 'Of well-employed audacity' (verse 218).

children.text: tac chrutvā karaṭaka āha-bhadra, asty evam | paraṃ tathāpi mahan me bhayam | yato buddhimān sañjīvako raudraś ca siṃhaḥ | yadyapi te buddhi-prāgalbhyaṃ tathāpi tvaṃ piṅgalakāt taṃ viyojayitum asamartha eva |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Friend, this is so. But still I have great fear. For <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> is intelligent and the lion is fierce. Even though you have boldness of intellect, still you are incapable of separating him from <s>Piṅgalaka</s>.'

children.text: damanaka āha-bhrātaḥ ! asamartho 'pi samartha eva | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Brother! Even the incapable is indeed capable. And it is said —'

children.text: upāyena hi yac chakyaṃ na tac chakyaṃ parākramaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What can be accomplished by stratagem cannot be accomplished by valor;

children.text: kākī kanaka-sūtreṇa kṛṣṇa-sarpam aghātayat ||Panc_1.228||
children.translated_text: a female crow, by means of a golden chain, had a black serpent killed. ||Panc_1.228||

children.text: karaṭaka āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 6
vāyasa-dampati-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 6
The story of the crow couple

children.text: asti kasmiṃścit pradeśe mahān nyagrodha-pādapaḥ | tatra vāyasa-dampatī prativasataḥ sma | atha tayoḥ prasava-kāle vṛkṣa-vivarān niṣkramya kṛṣṇa-sarpaḥ sadaiva tad-apatyāni bhakṣayati | tatas tau nirvedād anya-vṛkṣa-mūla-nivāsinaṃ priya-suhṛdaṃ śṛgālaṃ gatvocatuḥ-bhadra ! kim evaṃvidhe sañjāta āvayoḥ kartavyaṃ bhavati | evaṃ tāvad duṣṭātmā kṛṣṇa-sarpo vṛkṣa-vivarān nirgatyāvayor bālakān bhakṣayati | tat kathyatāṃ tad-rakṣārthaṃ kaścid upāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain place there was a great banyan tree. There a crow couple lived. Now, at their breeding season, a black serpent would crawl out from a hollow of the tree and always devour their offspring. Then those two, overcome with despair, went to a dear friend — a jackal living at the base of another tree — and said: 'Good friend! What should we do when such a situation has befallen us? This wicked black serpent keeps coming out of the tree-hollow and devouring our young. So tell us some stratagem for protecting them.'

children.text: yasya kṣetraṃ nadī-tīre bhāryā ca para-saṅgatā |
children.translated_text: He whose field is on a riverbank, whose wife consorts with another,

children.text: sa-sarpe ca gṛhe vāsaḥ kathaṃ syāt tasya nirvṛtiḥ ||Panc_1.229||
children.translated_text: and who dwells in a house with a serpent — how can there be happiness for him? // Panc_1.229 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: sarpa-yukte gṛhe vāso mṛtyur eva na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Dwelling in a house with a serpent is death itself — there is no doubt;

children.text: yad grāmānte vaset sarpas tasya syāt prāṇa-saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_1.230||
children.translated_text: even if the serpent lives at the village's edge, there would be danger to one's life. // Panc_1.230 //

children.text: asmākam api tatra-sthitānāṃ pratidinaṃ prāṇa-saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: For us too, dwelling there, there is daily danger to life.

children.text: sa āha-nātra viṣaye svalpo 'pi viṣādaḥ kāryaḥ | nūnaṃ sa lubdho nopāyam antareṇa vadhyaḥ syāt |
upāyena jayo yādṛg ripos tādṛṅ na hetibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Such victory as is won by stratagem over an enemy — that cannot [be won] by weapons;

children.text: upāya-jño 'lpa-kāyo 'pi na śūraiḥ paribhūyate ||Panc_1.231||
children.translated_text: one skilled in stratagems, even if small-bodied, is not overpowered by the mighty. // Panc_1.231 //
He said: 'In this matter, not even the slightest despondency should be entertained. Surely that greedy one cannot be killed without a stratagem.'

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And so:

children.text: bhakṣayitvā bahūn matsyān uttamādhama-madhyamān |
children.translated_text: Having devoured many fish — great, middling, and small —

children.text: atilaulyād bakaḥ kaścin mṛtaḥ karkaṭaka-grahāt ||Panc_1.232||
children.translated_text: a certain crane, out of excessive greed, died from the grip of a crab. // Panc_1.232 //

children.text: tāv ūcatuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The two said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 7
baka-kulīraka-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 7
The story of the crane and the crab

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vana-pradeśe nānā-jala-cara-sanāthaṃ mahat saraḥ | tatra ca kṛtāśrayo baka eko vṛddha-bhāvam upāgato matsyān vyāpādayitum asamarthaḥ | tataś ca kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭhaḥ saras-tīre upaviṣṭo muktā-phala-prakara-sadṛśair aśru-pravāhair dharā-talam abhiṣiñcan ruroda | ekaḥ kulīrako nānā-jala-cara-sametaḥ sametya tasya duḥkhena duḥkhitaḥ sādaram idam ūce-māma ! kim adya tvayā nāhāra-vṛttir anuṣṭhīyate ? kevalam aśru-pūrṇa-netrābhyāṃ sa-niḥśvāsena sthīyate |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there was a great lake, home to various aquatic creatures. There, a crane who had made it his refuge had grown old and was unable to catch fish. Then, with throat emaciated from hunger, he sat at the lake's shore, watering the ground with streams of tears resembling clusters of pearls, and wept. A certain crab, accompanied by various aquatic creatures, approached him, and distressed by his distress, said respectfully: 'Uncle! Why are you not going about your feeding today? You simply sit here with eyes brimming with tears and sighing.'

children.text: sa āha-vatsa ! satyam upalakṣitaṃ bhavatā | mayā hi matsyādanaṃ prati parama-vairāgyatayā sāmprataṃ prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtam | tenāhaṃ samīpāgatān api matsyān na bhakṣayāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Child! What you have observed is true. For, having attained supreme dispassion toward eating fish, I have now undertaken a fast unto death. Therefore I do not eat fish even when they come near me.'

children.text: kulīrakas tac chrutvā prāha-māma, kiṃ tad vairāgya-kāraṇam ?
children.translated_text: The crab, hearing that, said: 'Uncle, what is the cause of this dispassion?'

children.text: sa prāha-vatsa, aham asmin sarasi jāto vṛddhiṃ gataś ca | tan mayaitac chrutaṃ yad dvādaśa-varṣikyānāvṛṣṭiḥ sampadyate lagnā |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Child, I was born in this lake and grew up in it. Now I have heard that a twelve-year drought is about to occur.'

children.text: kulīraka āha-kasmāt tac chrutam ?
children.translated_text: The crab asked: 'From whom was that heard?'

children.text: baka āha-daivajña-mukhād eṣa śanaiścaro hi rohiṇī-śakaṭaṃ bhittvā bhaumaṃ śakraṃ ca prayāsyati | uktaṃ ca varāha-mihireṇa-
children.translated_text: The crane said: 'From the mouth of an astrologer. This <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) will pierce the wagon of <s>Rohiṇī</s> and will enter [the house of] <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars) and <s>Śakra</s> (Jupiter). And <s>Varāhamihira</s> has said:'

children.text: yadi bhinte sūrya-suto rohiṇyāḥ śakaṭam iha loke |
children.translated_text: If <s>Sūryasuta</s> (Saturn) pierces the wagon of <s>Rohiṇī</s> in this world,

children.text: dvādaśa varṣāṇi tadā nahi varṣati vāsavau bhūmau ||Panc_1.233||
children.translated_text: then for twelve years <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) does not rain upon the earth. // Panc_1.233 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: prājāpatye śakaṭe bhinne kṛtvaiva pātakaṃ vasudhā |
children.translated_text: When the wagon of <s>Prajāpati</s> is pierced, the earth, having committed a sin,

children.text: bhasmāsthi-śakalākīrṇā kāpālikam iva vrataṃ dhatte ||Panc_1.234||
children.translated_text: strewn with ashes and bone-fragments, assumes a vow like that of a <s>Kāpālika</s>. // Panc_1.234 //

children.text: tathā ca-
rohiṇī-śakaṭam arka-nandanaś ced
children.translated_text: If the son of the Sun [Saturn],

children.text: bhinnatti rudhiro 'thavā śaśī |
children.translated_text: or the blood-red Moon, pierces the wagon of <s>Rohiṇī</s> —

children.text: kiṃ vadāmi tad-aniṣṭa-sāgare
children.translated_text: what can I say? In that ocean of calamity,

children.text: sarva-lokam upayāti saṅkṣayaḥ ||Panc_1.235||
children.translated_text: all the world goes to destruction. // Panc_1.235 //
And also:

children.text: rohiṇī-śakaṭa-madhya-saṃsthite
children.translated_text: When [Saturn] is situated in the middle of the wagon of <s>Rohiṇī</s>,

children.text: candram asya śaraṇī-kṛtā janāḥ |
children.translated_text: people who have made the Moon their shelter,

children.text: kvāpi yānti śiśupācitāśanāḥ
children.translated_text: wander everywhere, eating food cooked by children,

children.text: sūrya-tapta-bhidurāmbu-pāyinaḥ ||Panc_1.236||
children.translated_text: drinking water cracked by the sun's heat. // Panc_1.236 //

children.text: tad etat saraḥ svalpa-toyaṃ vartate | śīghraṃ śoṣaṃ yāsyati | asmin śuṣke yaiḥ sahāhaṃ vṛddhiṃ gataḥ, sadaiva krīḍitaś ca, te sarve toyābhāvān nāśaṃ yāsyanti | tat teṣāṃ viyogaṃ draṣṭum aham asamarthaḥ | tenaitat prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtam | sāmprataṃ sarveṣāṃ svalpa-jalāśayānāṃ jalacarā guru-jalāśayeṣu sva-svajanair nīyante | kecic ca makara-godhā-śiśumāra-jalahasti-prabhṛtayaḥ svayam eva gacchanti | atra punaḥ sarasi ye jalacarās te niścintāḥ santi, tenāhaṃ viśeṣād rodimi yad bīja-śesa-mātram apy atra noddhariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'Now this lake has little water. It will soon dry up. When it dries up, all those with whom I grew up and always played — they will all perish from lack of water. I am unable to witness their separation [from life]. That is why I have undertaken this fast unto death. At present, the aquatic creatures of all small water-bodies are being carried by their own kin to larger water-bodies. And some — crocodiles, monitor lizards, dolphins, water-elephants, and the like — go by themselves. But the aquatic creatures in this lake are unconcerned, and therefore I weep especially — that not even a seed's worth [of life] will be preserved here.'

children.text: tataḥ sa tad ākarṇyānyeṣām api jalacarāṇāṃ tat tasya vacanaṃ nivedayāmāsa | atha te sarve bhaya-trasta-manaso matsya-kacchapa-prabhṛtayas tam abhyupetya papracchuḥ-māma ! asti kaścid upāyo yenāsmākaṃ rakṣā bhavati ?
children.translated_text: Then he, hearing this, informed the other aquatic creatures of those words of his. Thereupon all of them — fish, turtles, and others — their minds stricken with fear, approached him and asked: 'Uncle! Is there some means by which we may be saved?'

children.text: baka āha-asty asya jalāśayasya nātidūre prabhūta-jala-sanāthaṃ saraḥ padminī-khaṇḍa-maṇḍitaṃ yac caturviṃśaty api varṣāṇām avṛṣṭyā na śoṣam eṣyati | tad yadi mama pṛṣṭhaṃ kaścid ārohati, tad ahaṃ taṃ tatra nayāmi |
children.translated_text: The crane said: 'Not far from this lake there is a lake abundantly filled with water, adorned with clusters of lotuses, which even in twenty-four years of drought will not dry up. If anyone climbs on my back, I shall carry him there.'

children.text: atha te tatra viśvāsam āpannāḥ, tāta mātula bhrātaḥ iti bruvāṇāḥ ahaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ pūrvam iti samantāt paritasthuḥ | so 'pi duṣṭāśayaḥ krameṇa tān pṛṣṭha āropya jalāśayasya nātidūre śilāṃ samāsādya tasyām ākṣipya svecchayā bhakṣayitvā bhūyo 'pi jalāśayaṃ samāsādya jalacarṇāṇāṃ mithyā-vārtā-sandeśakair manāṃsi rañjayan nityam evāhāra-vṛttim akarot |
children.translated_text: Then they, having placed their trust in him, calling out 'Father!' 'Uncle!' 'Brother!' — stood all around saying 'Me first! Me first!' And he, with evil intent, carried them on his back one by one, reached a flat rock not far from the lake, dashed them upon it, ate them at his leisure, and returned again to the lake — gladdening the hearts of the aquatic creatures with false reports of news — and thus carried on his daily sustenance forever.

children.text: anyasmin dine ca kulīrakeṇoktaḥ-māma ! mayā saha te prathamaḥ sneha-sambhāṣaḥ sañjātaḥ | tat kiṃ māṃ parityajyānyān nayasi ? tasmād adya me prāṇa-trāṇaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: On another day, the crab said to him: 'Uncle! My friendship with you began first. Why do you carry others while neglecting me? Therefore save my life today.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya so 'pi duṣṭāśayaś cintitavān-nirviṇṇo 'haṃ matsya-māṃsādanena tad adyainaṃ kulīrakaṃ vyañjana-sthāne karomi | iti vicintya taṃ pṛṣṭe samāropya tāṃ vadhya-śilām uddiśya prasthitaḥ | kulīrako 'pi dūrād evāsthi-parvataṃ śilāśrayam avalokya mastyāsthīni parijñāya tam apṛcchat-māma, kiyad dūre sa jalāśayaḥ ? madīya-bhāreṇātiśrāntas tvam | tat kathaya |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the evil-minded one thought: 'I am weary of eating fish-flesh. So today I shall make this crab a side-dish.' Having thought thus, he mounted him on his back and set out toward that slaughter-rock. The crab too, seeing from afar the pile of bones at the rock's base and recognizing them as fish-bones, asked him: 'Uncle, how far is that lake? You are exhausted from my weight. Tell me.'

children.text: so 'pi manda-dhīr jalacaro 'yam iti matvā sthale na prabhavatīti sa-smitam idam āha-kulīraka, kuto 'nyo jalāśayaḥ ? mama prāṇa-yātreyam | tasmāt smaryatām ātmano 'bhīṣṭa-devatā | tvām apy anyāṃ śilāyāṃ nikṣipya bhakṣayiṣyāmi | ity uktavati tasmin sva-vadana-daṃśa-dvayena mṛṇāla-nāla-dhavalāyāṃ mṛdu-grīvāyāṃ gṛhīto mṛtaś ca |
children.translated_text: And he, being dim-witted, thinking 'This is a water-creature — he cannot prevail on dry land,' said with a smile: 'Crab, what other lake is there? This is my livelihood. Therefore remember your chosen deity. I shall dash you too upon a rock and eat you.' When he had said this, [the crab] seized his soft, lotus-stalk-white neck with both his pincers — and he died.

children.text: atha sa tāṃ baka-grīvāṃ samādāya śanaiḥ śanais taj jalāśayam āsasāda | tataḥ sarvair eva jalacaraiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ-bhoḥ kulīraka ! kiṃ nivṛttas tvam ? sa mātulo 'pi nāyātaḥ | tat kiṃ cirayati ? vayaṃ sarve sotksukāḥ kṛta-kṣaṇās tiṣṭhāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then [the crab], taking that crane's neck, slowly made his way back to the lake. Thereupon all the aquatic creatures asked him: 'Ho, crab! Why have you returned? That uncle of ours has not come either. Why does he delay? We are all waiting eagerly, ready [to go].'

children.text: evaṃ tair abhihite kulīrako 'pi vihasyovāca-mūrkhāḥ ! sarve jalacarās tena mithyā-vādinā vañcayitvā nātidūre śilā-tale prakṣipya bhakṣitāḥ | tan mamāyuḥ-śeṣatayā tasya viśvāsa-ghātakasyābhiprāyaṃ jñātvā grīveyam ānītā | tad alaṃ sambhrameṇa | adhunā sarva-jala-carāṇāṃ kṣemaṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: When they had spoken thus, the crab laughed and said: 'Fools! All the aquatic creatures were deceived by that liar — he carried them to a rock-slab not far away, dashed them down, and ate them. But by the good fortune of my remaining lifespan, having discovered the intention of that betrayer of trust, I have brought back this neck [of his]. So enough with your panic! Now all the aquatic creatures shall be safe.'

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bhakṣayitvā bahūn matsyān iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Having devoured many fish...' [and so on].

children.text: vāyasa āha-bhadra ! tat kathaya kathaṃ sa duṣṭa-sarpo vadham upaiṣyati |
children.translated_text: The crow said: 'Good friend! Then tell me — how can that wicked serpent be killed?'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-gacchatu bhavān kañcin nagaraṃ rājādhiṣṭhānam | tatra kasyāpi dhanino rājāmātyādeḥ pramādinaḥ kanaka-sūtraṃ hāraṃ vā gṛhītvā tat-koṭare prakṣipa, yena sarpas tad-grahaṇena vadhyate |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Go to some city — a royal capital. There, from some wealthy person — a royal minister or the like — who is careless, take a gold chain or a necklace and drop it into that hollow, so that the serpent will be killed in the seizure of it.'

children.text: tat-kṣaṇāt kākaḥ kākī ca tad ākarṇyātmecchayotpatitau | tataś ca kākī kiñcit saraḥ prāpya yāvat paśyati, tāvat tan-madhye kasyacid rājño 'ntaḥpuraṃ jalāsannaṃ nyasta-kanaka-sūtraṃ mukta-muktāhāra-vastrābharaṇaṃ jala-krīḍāṃ kurute | atha sā vāyasī kanaka-sūtram ekam ādāya sva-gṛhābhimukhaṃ pratasthe | tataś ca kañcukino varṣa-varāś ca tan-nīyamānam upalakṣya gṛhīta-laguḍāḥ satvaram anuyayuḥ | kāky api sarpa-koṭare tat-kanaka-sūtraṃ prakṣipya sudūram avasthitā |
children.translated_text: Instantly the crow and his mate, hearing this, flew off as they pleased. The female crow, reaching a certain lake, looked and saw that in its midst the harem of some king, situated near the water, had set down its gold chains, removed its pearl necklaces and garments and ornaments, and was sporting in the water. Then that female crow took one gold chain and set off toward her home. Thereupon the guards and excellent soldiers, noticing it being carried away, seized their staffs and followed quickly. The female crow dropped that gold chain into the serpent's hollow and stationed herself far away.

children.text: atha yāvad rāja-puruṣās taṃ vṛkṣam āruhya tat-koṭaram avalokayanti, tāvat kṛṣṇa-sarpaḥ prasārita-bhogas tiṣṭhati | tatas taṃ laguḍa-prahāreṇa hatvā kanaka-sūtram ādāya yathābhilaṣitaṃ sthānaṃ gatāḥ | vāyasa-dampatī api tataḥ paraṃ sukhena vasataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-upāyena hi yat kuryāt iti |
children.translated_text: Then, when the king's men climbed that tree and looked into the hollow, the black serpent was sitting there with its hood spread wide. Then, having killed it with a blow of a staff, they took the gold chain and went to their desired destination. And the crow couple from then on lived in happiness. Therefore I say: 'By stratagem indeed one should accomplish [what is to be done].'

children.text: tan na kiṃcid iha buddhimatām asādhyam asti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: For nothing here is unachievable for those who possess intelligence. And it is said:

children.text: yasya buddhir balaṃ tasya nirbuddhes tu kuto balam |
children.translated_text: He whose [resource] is intelligence — his is strength; but whence comes strength to the witless?

children.text: vane siṃho madonmattaḥ śaśakena nipātitaḥ ||Panc_1.237||
children.translated_text: In the forest, a lion intoxicated with pride was felled by a hare. // Panc_1.237 //

children.text: karaṭaka āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: sa āha-
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text:
kathā 8
bhāsurakākhya-siṃha-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 8
The story of the lion named <s>Bhāsuraka</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścid vane bhāsurako nāma siṃhaḥ prativasati sma | athāsau vīryātirekān nityam evānekān mṛga-śaśakādīn vyāpādayan nopararāma | athānyedyus tad-vanajāḥ sarve sāraṅga-varāha-mahiṣa-śaśakādayo militvā tam abhyupetya procuḥ-svāmin ! kim anena sakala-mṛga-vadhena nityam eva, yatas tavaikenāpi mṛgeṇa tṛptir bhavati tat kriyatām asmābhiḥ saha samaya-dharmaḥ | adya-prabhṛti tavātropaviṣṭasya jāti-krameṇa pratidinam eko mṛgo bhakṣaṇārthaṃ sameṣyati | evaṃ kṛte tava tāvat prāṇa-yātrā kleśaṃ vināpi bhaviṣyati | asmākaṃ ca punaḥ sarvocchedanaṃ na syāt | tad eṣa rāja-dharmo 'nuṣṭhīyatām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: In a certain forest there lived a lion named <s>Bhāsuraka</s>. Now, out of excess of valor, he never ceased daily killing many deer, hares, and other [animals]. One day, all the forest-born creatures — deer, boars, buffaloes, hares, and others — assembled, approached him, and said: 'Lord! What is the purpose of this constant slaughter of all the animals, since you are satisfied by even one animal? Therefore let a pact be made between us. From today onward, while you sit here, one animal shall come to you daily for eating, in order of species. If it is done thus, your sustenance will continue without effort. And for us, there will be no total annihilation. Therefore let this duty of a king be observed. And it is said:'

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiś ca yo rājyam upabhuṅkte yathā-balam |
children.translated_text: He who gradually enjoys his kingdom according to his strength,

children.text: rasāyanam iva prājñaḥ sa puṣṭiṃ paramāṃ vrajet ||Panc_1.238||
children.translated_text: wisely, like a tonic — he attains supreme nourishment. // Panc_1.238 //

children.text: vidhinā mantra-yuktena rūkṣāpi mathitāpi ca |
children.translated_text: Even the earth, though barren and churned, when [tilled] with method and sacred formula,

children.text: prayacchati phalaṃ bhūmir araṇīva hutāśanam ||Panc_1.239||
children.translated_text: yields fruit — like the fire-drill [yields] fire. // Panc_1.239 //

children.text: prajānāṃ pālanaṃ śasyaṃ svarga-kośasya vardhanam |
children.translated_text: Protection of subjects is praiseworthy — it increases the treasury of heaven;

children.text: pīḍanaṃ dharma-nāśāya pāpāyāyaśase sthitam ||Panc_1.240||
children.translated_text: oppression leads to the destruction of <s>dharma</s>, to sin, and to infamy. // Panc_1.240 //

children.text: gopālena prajādhenor vitta-dugdhaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: From the cow of subjects, the cowherd-[king] should milk the wealth-milk gradually,

children.text: pālanāt poṣaṇād grāhyaṃ nyāyyāṃ vṛttiṃ samācaret ||Panc_1.241||
children.translated_text: through protection and nourishment — he should follow a just course of conduct. // Panc_1.241 //

children.text: ajām iva prajāṃ mohād yo hanyāt pṛthivī-patim |
children.translated_text: A king who, out of delusion, slaughters his subjects like a goat —

children.text: tasyaikā jāyate tṛptir na dvitīyā kathañcana ||Panc_1.242||
children.translated_text: for him there arises one satisfaction [only], never a second. // Panc_1.242 //

children.text: phalārthī nṛpatir lokān pālayed yatnam āsthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king desiring fruit should protect his people with effort,

children.text: dāna-mānādi-toyena mālākāro 'ṅkurān iva ||Panc_1.243||
children.translated_text: like a gardener [tending] his seedlings with the water of gifts, honors, and the like. // Panc_1.243 //

children.text: nṛpa-dīpo dhana-snehaṃ prajābhyaḥ saṃharann api |
children.translated_text: The lamp of a king, though it draws the oil of wealth from its subjects,

children.text: āntara-sthair guṇaiḥ śubhrair lakṣyate naiva kenacit ||Panc_1.244||
children.translated_text: is not perceived by anyone [because it shines] with the inner radiance of bright qualities. // Panc_1.244 //

children.text: yathā gaur duhyate kāle pālyate ca tathā prajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as a cow is milked at the proper time and tended,

children.text: sicyate cīyate caiva latā puṣpa-phala-pradā ||Panc_1.245||
children.translated_text: so are the subjects [to be treated]; and a creeper bearing flowers and fruit is watered and harvested. // Panc_1.245 //

children.text: yathā bījāṅkuraḥ sūkṣmaḥ prayatnenābhirakṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as a tiny seed-sprout, protected with care,

children.text: phala-prado bhavet kāle tadval lokaḥ surakṣitaḥ ||Panc_1.246||
children.translated_text: becomes a fruit-bearer in time — so too the people when well-protected. // Panc_1.246 //

children.text: hiraṇya-dhānya-ratnāni yānāni vividhāni ca |
children.translated_text: Gold, grain, jewels, and various conveyances,

children.text: tathānyad api yat kiñcit prajābhyaḥ syān mahīpateḥ ||Panc_1.247||
children.translated_text: and whatever else there may be — [all] comes to the king from his subjects. // Panc_1.247 //

children.text: lokānugraha-kartāraḥ pravardhante nareśvarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Kings who bestow favor upon the people prosper;

children.text: lokānāṃ saṅkṣayāc caiva kṣayaṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_1.248||
children.translated_text: and from the ruin of the people, they too come to ruin — there is no doubt. // Panc_1.248 //

children.text: atha teṣāṃ tad-vacanam ākarṇya bhāsuraka āha-aho satyam abhihitaṃ bhavadbhiḥ | paraṃ yadi mamopaviṣṭasyātra nityam eva naikaḥ śvāpadaḥ samāgamiṣyati | tan nūnaṃ sarvān api bhakṣayiṣyāmi | atha te tathaiva pratijñāya nirvṛti-bhājas tatraiva vane nirbhayāḥ paryaṭanti | ekaś ca pratidinaṃ krameṇa yāti | vṛddho vā, vairāgya-yukto vā, śoka-grasto vā, putra-kalatra-nāśa-bhīto vā, teṣāṃ madhyāt tasya bhojanārthaṃ madhyāhna-samaya upatiṣṭhate |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing their words, <s>Bhāsuraka</s> said: 'Ah, truly spoken by your honors! But if I sit here, not a single beast of prey will come to me daily. So I shall surely devour them all.' Thereupon they, having made that very agreement, went about freely and fearlessly in that forest. And one by one, in turn, each day [an animal] would go [to the lion] — whether old, or detached, or grief-stricken, or one fearing the loss of sons and wife — from among them, [one] would present himself at midday for his meal.

children.text: atha kadācij jāti-kramāc chaśakasyāvasaraḥ samāyātaḥ | sa samasta-mṛgaiḥ prerito 'nicchann api mandaṃ mandaṃ gatvā tasya vadhopāyaṃ cintayan velātikramaṃ kṛtvāvyākulita-hṛdayo yāvad gacchati tāvan-mārge gacchatā kūpaḥ sandṛṣṭaḥ | yāvat kūpopari pāti tāvat kūpa-madhya ātmanaḥ pratibimbaṃ dadarśa | dṛṣṭvā ca tena hṛdaye cintitam-yad bhāvya upāyo 'sti | ahaṃ bhāsurakaṃ prakopya sva-buddhyāsmin kūpe pātayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Now one day, by the sequence of species, the turn of the hare arrived. He, sent forth by all the animals, though unwilling, went very slowly, thinking of a stratagem for [the lion's] killing, deliberately arriving late. As he went along with an untroubled heart, on the way he spotted a well. As he leaned over the top of the well, he saw his own reflection in the middle of the well. Seeing it, he thought in his heart: 'Now there is a stratagem!' 'I shall provoke <s>Bhāsuraka</s> and by my own wit cause him to fall into this well.'

children.text: athāsau dina-śeṣe bhāsuraka-samīpaṃ prāptaḥ | siṃho 'pi velātikrameṇa kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭhaḥ kopāviṣṭaḥ sṛkkaṇī parilelihad vyacintayat-aho ! pratār-āhārāya niḥsattvaṃ vanaṃ mayā kartavyam | evaṃ cintayatas tasya śaśako mandaṃ mandaṃ gatvā praṇamya tasyāgre sthitaḥ | atha taṃ prajvalitātmā bhāsurako bhartsayann āha-re śaśakādhama ekas tāvat tvaṃ laghuḥ prāpto 'parato velātikrameṇa | tad asmād aparādhāt tvāṃ nipātya prātaḥ sakalāny api mṛga-kulāny ucchedayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of the day, he arrived in the presence of <s>Bhāsuraka</s>. The lion, his throat emaciated with hunger from the lateness, was seized with rage, licking his chops, and thought: 'Ah! Tomorrow I shall make the forest devoid of life for my breakfast.' While he was thinking thus, the hare came very slowly, bowed, and stood before him. Then <s>Bhāsuraka</s>, his soul ablaze, rebuked him: 'You, lowest of hares! First, you are small, and on top of that, you have arrived late. So, punishing you for this offense, tomorrow I shall exterminate all the animal clans!'

children.text: atha śaśakaḥ sa-vinayaṃ provāca-svāmin ! nāparādho mama | na ca sattvānām | tac chyrūtāṃ kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: Then the hare said respectfully: 'Master, it is not my fault, nor the animals' fault. Please hear the reason.'

children.text: siṃha āha-satvaraṃ nivedaya yāvan mama daṃṣṭrāntargato na bhavān bhaviṣyati iti |
children.translated_text: The lion said: 'Tell me quickly, before you end up between my fangs!'

children.text: śaśaka āha-svāmin, samasta-mṛgair adya jāti-krameṇa mama laghutarasya prastāvaṃ vijñāya tato 'haṃ pañca-śaśakaiḥ samaṃ preṣitaḥ | tataś cāham āgacchenn antarāle mahatā kenacid apareṇa siṃhena vivarān nirgatyābhihitaḥ-abhīṣṭa-devatāṃ smarata |
children.translated_text: The hare said: 'Master, all the animals, knowing that today by the order of species it is the turn of someone as small as me, sent me along with five [other] hares. Then, as I was coming, on the way, some other great lion emerged from a cave and said: "Remember your chosen deity!"'

children.text: tato mayābhihitam-vayaṃ svāminon bhāsuraka-siṃhasya sakāśam āhārārthaṃ samaya-dharmeṇa gacchāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Then I said: "We are going to our master, the lion <s>Bhāsuraka</s>, for his meal, in accordance with our agreement."'

children.text: tatas tenābhihitam-yady evaṃ tarhi madīyam etad-vanam | mayā saha samaya-dharmeṇa samastair api śvāpadair vartitavyam | cora-rūpī sa bhāsurakaḥ | atha yadi so 'tra rājā | viśvāsa-sthāne caturaḥ śaśakān atra dhṛtvā tam āhūya drutataram āgaccha | yena yaḥ kaścid āvayor madhyāt parākrameṇa rājā bhaviṣyati sa sarvān etān bhakṣayiṣyati iti |
children.translated_text: 'Then he said: "If so, then this forest is mine. All the beasts must live in accordance with an agreement with me. That <s>Bhāsuraka</s> is a thief in disguise. If he is the king here, then hold four hares in trust, and quickly come back, summoning him — so that whichever of the two of us proves himself king by prowess shall devour all of them."'

children.text: tato 'haṃ tenādiṣṭaḥ svāmi-sakāśam abhyāgataḥ | etad velā vyatikrama-kāraṇam | tad atra svāmī pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: 'Then, directed by him, I have come to my master's presence. This is the reason for the lateness. In this matter, the master is the authority.'

children.text: tac chrutvā bhāsuraka āha-bhadra, yady evaṃ tat satvaraṃ darśaya me taṃ caura-siṃhaḥ yenāhaṃ mṛga-kopaṃ tasyopari kṣiptvā svastho bhavāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Bhāsuraka</s> said: 'Friend, if so, then quickly show me that thief-lion, so that I may hurl my rage at the animals upon him and be at peace.' And it is said:

children.text: bhūmir mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca vigrahasya phala-trayam |
children.translated_text: Territory, allies, and gold — these are the three fruits of war;

children.text: nāsty ekam api yady eṣāṃ na taṃ kuryāt kathañcana ||Panc_1.249||
children.translated_text: if not even one of these is [obtainable], one should by no means wage it. // Panc_1.249 //

children.text: yatra na syāt phalaṃ bhūri yatra casyāt parābhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there would be no abundant fruit, and where there would be humiliation —

children.text: na tatra matimān yuddhaṃ samutpādya samācaret ||Panc_1.250||
children.translated_text: there a wise man should not instigate and wage war. // Panc_1.250 //

children.text: śaśāka āha-svāmin ! satyam idam | sva-bhūmi-hetoḥ paribhavāc ca yudhyante kṣatriyāḥ | paraṃ sa durgāśrayaḥ durgān niṣkramya vayaṃ tena viṣkambhitāḥ | tato durgastho duḥsadhyo bhavati ripuḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The hare said: 'Master, this is true. Warriors fight for their own land and to avenge insults. But he is sheltered in a fortress — he emerged from his fortress and confronted us. An enemy in a fortress is hard to overcome.' And it is said:

children.text: na gajānāṃ sahasreṇa na ca lakṣeṇa vājinām | yat kṛtyaṃ sidhyati rājñāṃ durgeṇaikena vigrahe ||Panc_1.251|| śatam eko 'pi saṃdhatte prākārastho dhanurdharaḥ | tasmād durgaṃ praśaṃsanti nītiśāstravicakṣaṇāḥ ||Panc_1.252|| purā guroḥ samādeśādd hiraṇyakaśipor bhayāt | śakreṇa vihitaṃ durgaṃ prabhāvād viśvakarmaṇaḥ ||Panc_1.253|| tenāpi ca varo datto yasya durgaṃ sa bhūpatiḥ | vijayī syāt tato bhūmau durgāṇi syuḥ sahasraśaḥ ||Panc_1.254|| daṃṣṭrāvirahito nāgo madahīno yathā gajaḥ | sarveṣāṃ jāyate vaśyo durgahīnas tathā nṛpaḥ ||Panc_1.255||
children.translated_text: What cannot be accomplished by a thousand elephants or a hundred thousand horses — that a king accomplishes in war with a single fortress. // Panc_1.251 // Even a single archer stationed on a rampart can hold off a hundred; therefore those skilled in the <s>Nītiśāstra</s> praise the fortress. // Panc_1.252 // Of old, by the guru's command, out of fear of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, <s>Indra</s> had a fortress built by the power of <s>Viśvakarman</s>. // Panc_1.253 // And by him (<s>Viśvakarman</s>) a boon was given: 'He who has a fortress shall be the victorious king.' Therefore there are thousands of fortresses on earth. // Panc_1.254 // A serpent without fangs, an elephant without rut — just as these come under everyone's power, so too a king without a fortress. // Panc_1.255 //

children.text: tac chrutvā bhāsuraka āha | bhadra durgastham api darśaya taṃ caura-siṃhaṃ yena vyāpādayāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Bhāsuraka</s> said: 'Friend, show me that thief-lion even in his fortress, so that I may destroy him.' And it is said:

children.text: jāta-mātraṃ na yaḥ śatruṃ rogaṃ ca praśamaṃ nayet | mahābalo 'pi tenaiva vṛddhiṃ prāpya sa hanyate ||Panc_1.256||
children.translated_text: One who does not suppress an enemy or a disease at its very inception — even if very powerful, is killed by that [enemy or disease] when it has grown. // Panc_1.256 //

children.text:
tathā ca-
uttiṣṭhamānas tu paro nopekṣyaḥ pathyam icchatā | samau hi śiṣṭair āmnātau vartsyantāv āmayaḥ sa ca ||Panc_1.257||
children.translated_text:
And also:
A rising adversary should not be ignored by one who desires wellbeing; for the learned have declared that a disease and an adversary are alike when both are growing. // Panc_1.257 //

children.text:
api ca-
upekṣitaḥ kṣīṇa-balo 'pi śatruḥ pramāda-doṣāt puruṣair madāndhaiḥ | sādhyo 'pi bhūtvā prathamaṃ tato 'sāv
asādhyatāṃ vyādhir iva prayāti ||Panc_1.258||
children.translated_text: passes into incurability — like a disease. // Panc_1.258 //

Moreover:
An enemy, even when weakened, if neglected by men blinded with arrogance through the fault of carelessness, though at first curable, thereafter

children.text:
tathā ca-
ātmanaḥ śaktim udvīkṣya manotsāhaṃ ca yo vrajet | bahūn hanti sa eko 'pi kṣatriyān bhārgavo yathā ||Panc_1.259||
children.translated_text:
And also:
One who, having assessed his own strength and mental resolve, goes [to battle] — he, even alone, slays many warriors, like <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>). // Panc_1.259 //

children.text:
śaśaka āha-asty etat | tathāpi balavān sa mayā dṛṣṭaḥ | tan na yujyate svāminas tasya tasya sāmarthyam aviditvā gantum | uktaṃ ca-
aviditvātmanaḥ śaktiṃ parasya ca samutsukaḥ | gacchann abhimukho vahnau nāśaṃ yāti pataṅgavat ||Panc_1.260|| yo balāt pronnataṃ yāti nihantuṃ sabalo 'py arim | vimadaḥ sa nivarteta śīrṇa-danto gajo yathā ||Panc_1.261||
children.translated_text:
The hare said: 'This is true. Nevertheless, I have seen him and he is powerful. So it is not proper for the master to go without knowing his strength.' And it is said:
One who, without knowing his own strength and the other's, eagerly advances head-on toward fire — he is destroyed, like a moth. // Panc_1.260 // One who, by force and with his army, advances to strike down a mighty enemy, returns dispirited — like an elephant with broken tusks. // Panc_1.261 //

children.text: bhāsuraka āha-bhoḥ kiṃ tavānena vyāpāreṇa | darśaya me taṃ durgastham api |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāsuraka</s> said: 'Bah! What is this fuss of yours! Show me that [lion], even if he is in his fortress.'

children.text: atha śaśaka āha-yady evaṃ tarhy āgacchatu svāmī | evam uktvāgre vyavasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the hare said: 'If so, then let the master come.' Having said this, he stood in front.

children.text: tataś ca tenāgacchatā yaḥ kūpo dṛṣṭo 'bhūt tam eva kūpam āsādya bhāsurakam āha-svāmin kas te pratāpaṃ soḍhuṃ samarthaḥ ? tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā dūrato 'pi caura-siṃhaḥ praviṣṭaḥ svaṃ durgam | tad āgaccha yathā darśayāmīti | bhāsuraka āha-darśaya me durgam | tad anu darśitas tena kūpaḥ | tataḥ so 'pi mūrkhaḥ siṃhaḥ kūpa-madhya ātma-pratibimbaṃ jala-madhya-gataṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃha-nādaṃ mumoca | tataḥ pratiśabdena kūpa-madhyād dvi-guṇataro nādaḥ samutthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, as [<s>Bhāsuraka</s>] came along, [the hare led him to] the very well he had seen, and arriving at that well, said to <s>Bhāsuraka</s>: 'Master, who is able to withstand your might? Having seen you even from afar, the thief-lion has entered his fortress. So come — I shall show him.' <s>Bhāsuraka</s> said: 'Show me his fortress.' Then the hare showed him the well. And that foolish lion, seeing his own reflection in the water in the middle of the well, let out a lion's roar. Then from the echo, a roar twice as loud arose from the middle of the well.

children.text: atha tena taṃ śatruṃ matvātmānaṃ tasyopari prakṣipya prāṇāḥ parityaktāḥ | śaśako 'pi hṛṣṭa-manāḥ sarva-mṛgān ānandya taiḥ saha praśasyamāno yathā-sukhaṃ tatra vane nivasati sma | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-yasya buddhir balaṃ tasya iti |
children.translated_text: Then, thinking it to be his enemy, he hurled himself upon it and gave up his life. The hare too, joyful in heart, delighted all the animals, and praised by them, lived happily in that forest. Therefore I say: 'he whose strength is wit...'

children.text: tad yadi bhavān kathayati tat tatraiva gatvā tayoḥ sva-buddhi-prabhāveṇa maitrī-bhedaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: 'So if you agree, I shall go there and by the power of my own wit create a breach in their friendship.'

children.text: karaṭaka āha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tarhi gaccha | śivās te panthānaḥ santu | yathābhipretam anuṣṭhīyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Friend, if so, then go. May your paths be auspicious! Let your plan be carried out.'

children.text: atha damanakaḥ sañjīvaka-viyuktaṃ piṅgalakam avalokya tatrāntare praṇamyāgre samupaviṣṭaḥ | piṅgalako 'pi tam āha-bhadra, kiṃ cirād dṛṣṭaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Damanaka</s>, seeing <s>Piṅgalaka</s> separated from <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, bowed and sat before him in the interval. <s>Piṅgalaka</s> too said to him: 'Friend, why have you been seen after so long?'
