children.text: damanaka āha-na kañcid deva-pādānām asmābhiḥ prayojanam | tenāhaṃ nāgacchāmi | tathāpi rāja-prayojana-vināśam avalokya sandahyamāna-hṛdayo vyākulatayā svayam evābhyāgato vaktum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Your Lordship's servants have no need [of anything from you]. That is why I have not been coming. But nonetheless, seeing the ruin of the king's interests, with a burning heart and in agitation, I have come of my own accord to speak.' And it is said:

children.text: priyaṃ vā yadi vā dveṣyaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham |
children.translated_text: Whether pleasing or displeasing, whether auspicious or inauspicious,

children.text: apṛṣṭo 'pi hitaṃ vakṣyed yasya necchet parābhavam ||Panc_1.262||
children.translated_text: one who does not wish another's downfall should speak what is beneficial, even unasked. // Panc_1.262 //

children.text: atha tasya sābhiprāyaṃ vacanam ākarṇya piṅgalaka āha-kiṃ vaktu-manā bhavān ? tat kathyatāṃ yat kathanīyam asti |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his purposeful words, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: 'What do you intend to say? Let what is worth telling be told.'

children.text: sa prāha-deva sañjīvako yuṣmat-pādānām upari droha-buddhir iti | viśvāsa-gatasya mama vijane idam āha-bho damanaka ! dṛṣṭā mayāsya piṅgalakasya sārāsāratā | tad aham enaṃ hatvā sakala-mṛgādhipatyaṃ tvat-sācivya-padavī-samanvitaṃ kariṣyāmi | piṅgalako 'pi tad-vajra-sāra-prahāra-sadṛśaṃ dāruṇaṃ vacaḥ samākarṇya moham upagato na kiñcid apy uktavān | damanako 'pi tasya tam ākāram ālokya cintitavān-ayaṃ tāvat sañjīvaka-nibaddha-rāgaḥ | tan nūnam anena mantriṇā rājā vināśam avāpsyati iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Lord, <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> harbors treacherous intent against Your Lordship. To me, in whom he has placed his trust, he said in private: "O <s>Damanaka</s>! I have seen the substance and insubstantiality of this <s>Piṅgalaka</s>. So I shall kill him and, with you in the position of minister, make myself lord of all the animals."' <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, hearing those words as cruel as a thunderbolt's blow, fell into a swoon and said nothing at all. <s>Damanaka</s> too, observing his demeanor, thought: 'He is bound by attachment to <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>. Surely, through this minister, the king will come to ruin.' And it is said:

children.text: ekaṃ bhūmi-patiḥ karoti sacivaṃ rājye pramāṇaṃ yadā taṃ mohāc chrayate madaḥ sa ca madād dāsyena nirvidyate |
children.translated_text: When a king makes one man his minister, the sole authority in his kingdom, that man becomes intoxicated with arrogance, and from that arrogance he becomes contemptuous of servitude;

children.text: nirviṇṇasya padaṃ karoti hṛdaye tasya svatantra-spṛhā- svātantrya-spṛhayā tataḥ sa nṛpateḥ prāṇān abhidruhyati ||Panc_1.263||
children.translated_text: of the one grown contemptuous, the desire for independence takes root in his heart — and from the desire for independence, he then plots against the king's very life. // Panc_1.263 //

children.text: tat kim atra yuktam iti | piṅgalako 'pi cetanāṃ samāsādya katham api tam āha-sañjīvakas tāvat prāṇa-samo bhṛtyaḥ | sa kathaṃ mamopari droha-buddhiṃ karoti |
children.translated_text: 'So what is proper here?' And <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, regaining consciousness, said with difficulty: '<s>Saṃjīvaka</s> is a servant as dear as life to me. How could he harbor treacherous intent toward me?'

children.text: damanaka āha-deva, bhṛtyo 'bhṛtya ity anekāntikam etat | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Lord, whether someone is a servant or not — that is uncertain. And it is said:'

children.text: na so 'sti puruṣo rājñāṃ yo na kāmayate śriyam |
children.translated_text: There is no man who does not desire the royal fortune;

children.text: aśaktā eva sarvatra narendraṃ paryupāsate ||Panc_1.264||
children.translated_text: it is only the incapable who everywhere attend upon the king [without ambition]. // Panc_1.264 //

children.text: piṅgalaka āha-bhadra, tathāpi mama tasyopari citta-vṛttir na vikṛtiṃ yāti | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: 'Friend, even so, my heart's disposition toward him does not change.' Indeed, this is well said:

children.text: aneka-doṣa-duṣṭasya kāyaḥ kasya na vallabhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whose own body is not dear, even though afflicted with many faults?

children.text: kurvann api vyalīkāni yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ ||Panc_1.265||
children.translated_text: He who is beloved remains beloved, even when doing wrong. // Panc_1.265 //

children.text: damanaka āha-ata evāyaṃ doṣaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'That is precisely the fault! And it is said:'

children.text: yasminn evādhikaṃ cakṣur āropayati pārthivaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whichever man the king showers with his gaze excessively —

children.text: akulīnaḥ kulīno vā sa śriyā bhājanaṃ naraḥ ||Panc_1.266||
children.translated_text: whether of low birth or noble birth, that man becomes the vessel of [royal] fortune. // Panc_1.266 //

children.text: aparaṃ kena gaṇa-viśeṣeṇa svāmī sañjīvakaṃ nirguṇakam api nikaṭe dhārayati | atha deva, yady evaṃ cintayasi mahā-kāyo 'yam | anena ripūn vyāpādayiṣyāmi | tad asmān na sidhyati, yato 'yaṃ śaṣpa-bhojī | deva-pādānāṃ punaḥ śatravo māṃsāśinaḥ | tad-ripu-sādhanam asya sāhāyyena na bhavati | tasmād enaṃ dūṣayitvā hanyatām iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, by what special virtue does the master keep <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> near him, though he is without merit? Now, Your Majesty, if you think 'He is large-bodied; with his help I shall destroy enemies' — that will not work for us, because he is a grass-eater. Your Majesty's enemies, on the other hand, are meat-eaters. Defeating enemies cannot be accomplished with his help. Therefore, having discredited him, he should be killed.

children.text: piṅgalaka āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said —

children.text: ukto bhavati yaḥ pūrvaṃ guṇavān iti saṃsadi |
children.translated_text: He who was previously declared virtuous in the assembly —

children.text: tasya doṣo na vaktavyaḥ pratijñā-bhaṅga-bhīruṇā ||Panc_1.267||
children.translated_text: his faults should not be spoken of by one who fears breaking his word. [Panc 1.267]

children.text: anyac ca | mayāsya tava vacanenābhaya-pradānaṃ dattam | tat kathaṃ svayam eva vyāpādayāmi | sarvathā sañjīvako 'yaṃ suhṛd asmākam | na taṃ prati kaścin manyur iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover, I granted him a pledge of safety on your recommendation. So how can I myself kill him? In every way, this <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> is our friend. I bear no ill will toward him. As it is said —

children.text: itaḥ sa daityaḥ prāpta-śrīr neta evārhati kṣayam |
children.translated_text: This demon who has attained prosperity should not be destroyed from this very place;

children.text: viṣa-vṛkṣo 'pi saṃvardhya svayaṃ chettum asāmpratam ||Panc_1.268||
children.translated_text: even a poison-tree, once nurtured, is improper to cut down oneself. [Panc 1.268]

children.text: ādau na vā praṇayināṃ praṇayo vidheyo
children.translated_text: Either one should not bestow affection on dependents at first,

children.text: datto 'thavā pratidinaṃ paripoṣaṇīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: or, having given it, one should nurture [them] daily.

children.text: utkṣipya yat kṣipati tat prakaroti lajjāṃ
children.translated_text: To raise up and then cast down brings shame —

children.text: bhūmau sthitasya patanād bhayam eva nāsti ||Panc_1.269||
children.translated_text: one who is already on the ground has nothing to fear from falling. [Panc 1.269]

children.text: upakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sādhutve tasya ko guṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is good to benefactors — what virtue is there in his goodness?

children.text: apakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sa sādhuḥ sadbhir ucyate ||Panc_1.270||
children.translated_text: He who is good even to those who harm him — he is called truly good by the virtuous. [Panc 1.270]

children.text: tad-droha-buddher api mayāsya na viruddham ācaraṇīyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though he has treacherous intentions, I should not act against him.

children.text: damanaka āha-svāmin ! naiṣa rāja-dharmo yad droha-buddhir api kṣamyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: Master! This is not the way of kings — that even one with treacherous intentions should be forgiven. As it is said —

children.text: tulyārthaṃ tulya-sāmarthyaṃ marmajñaṃ vyavasāyinam |
children.translated_text: A servant of equal purpose, equal capability, who knows the vital points, who is resolute,

children.text: ardha-rājya-haraṃ bhṛtyaṃ yo na hanyāt sa hanyate ||Panc_1.271||
children.translated_text: and who seeks half the kingdom — he who does not kill such a one is himself killed. [Panc 1.271]

children.text: aparaṃ tvayāsya sakhitvāt sarvo 'pi rāja-dharmaḥ parityaktaḥ rāja-dharmābhāvāt sarvo 'pi parijano viraktiṃ gataḥ | yaḥ sañjīvakaḥ śaṣpa-bhojī | bhavān māṃsādaḥ | tava prakṛtayaś ca yat tavāvadhyavyasāya-bāhyaṃ kutas tāsāṃ māṃsāśanam | yad-rahitās tvāṃ tyaktvā yāsyanti | tato 'pi tvaṃ vinaṣṭa eva | asya saṅgatyā punas te na kadācid ākheṭake matir bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
yādṛśaiḥ sevyate bhṛtyair yādṛśāṃś copasevate |
children.translated_text: By the kind of servants one employs, and the kind of people one serves,

children.text: kadācin nātra sandehas tādṛg bhavati pūruṣaḥ ||Panc_1.272||
children.translated_text: a person inevitably becomes of that kind — there is never any doubt about this. [Panc 1.272]

Moreover, because of your friendship with him, you have abandoned all the duties of a king. Because of the absence of kingly duties, your entire retinue has become disaffected. <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> eats grass; you eat meat. Your subjects too — since they are excluded from the provisions of your hunting, where will they get their meat? Deprived of this, they will abandon you and leave. From that too, you will be ruined. Because of your association with him, your mind will never again turn to hunting. As it is said —

children.text: tathā ca-
santaptāyasi saṃsthitasya payaso nāmāpi na jñāyate
children.translated_text: When water rests on heated iron, even its name is not known;

children.text: mukta-kāratayā tad eva nalinī-patra-sthitaṃ rājate |
children.translated_text: the same [water], freed [and rolling], shines on a lotus leaf;

children.text: svātau sāgara-śukti-kukṣi-patitaṃ taj jāyate mauktikaṃ
children.translated_text: and falling into an oyster-shell in the ocean during the <s>Svāti</s> [constellation], it becomes a pearl —

children.text: prāyeṇādhama-madhyamottama-guṇaḥ saṃvāsato jāyate ||Panc_1.273||
children.translated_text: generally, the qualities of low, middling, and high are born from one's associations. [Panc 1.273]
And also —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: asatāṃ saṅga-doṣeṇa satī yāti matir bhramam |
children.translated_text: By the fault of association with the wicked, even a virtuous mind goes astray;

children.text: eka-rātri-pravāsena kāṣṭhaṃ muñje pralambitam ||Panc_1.274||
children.translated_text: [just as] a piece of wood, by staying one night, becomes entangled in <s>muñja</s> grass. [Panc 1.274]

children.text: ata eva santo nīca-saṅgaṃ varjayanti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the virtuous avoid the company of the low. As it is said —

children.text: na hy avijñāta-śīlasya pradātavyaḥ pratiśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not give shelter to one whose character is unknown;

children.text: mat-kuṇasya ca doṣeṇa hatā manda-visarpiṇī ||Panc_1.275||
children.translated_text: because of the fault of the bedbug, the slow-crawling louse was killed. [Panc 1.275]

children.text: piṅgalaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 9
manda-visarpiṇī-nāma-yūkā-kathā
children.translated_text:
He told —
Story 9
The Tale of the Louse Named <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s> (Slow-Crawler)

children.text:
asti kasyacin mahīpater manoramaṃ śayana-sthānam | tatra śvetatara-paṭa-yugala-madhya-saṃsthitā manda-visarpiṇī yūkā prativasati sma | sā ca tasya mahīpate raktam āsvādayantī sukhena kālaṃ nayamānā tiṣṭhati | anye-dyuś ca tatra śayane kvacid bhrāmyann agnimukho nāma matkuṇaḥ samāyātaḥ | atha taṃ dṛṣṭvā sā viṣaṇṇa-vadanā provāca | bho 'gnimukha kutas tvam atrānucita-sthāne samāyātaḥ | tad yāvan na kaścid vetti tāvac chīghraṃ gamyatām iti |
sa āha-bhagavati gṛhāgatasyāsādhor api naitad yujyate vaktum | uktaṃ ca-
ehy āgaccha samāviśāsanam idaṃ kasmāc cirād dṛśyase kā vārteti sudurbalo 'si kuśalaṃ prīto 'smi te darśanāt |
children.translated_text: 'Come, come in! Here is a seat. Why has it been so long since you were seen? What news? You look weak. Are you well? I am pleased to see you' —

children.text: evaṃ ye samupāgatān praṇayinaḥ pratyālapanty ādarāt teṣāṃ yuktam aśaṅkitena manasā harmyāṇi gantuṃ sadā ||Panc_1.276||
children.translated_text: those who address arriving friends with such welcoming words — to their homes one should always go with an untroubled mind. [Panc 1.276]

In a certain king's beautiful bedchamber, dwelling between a pair of pure white sheets, there lived a louse named <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s> (Slow-Crawler). She would suck the blood of that king and happily pass her time. One day, a bedbug named <s>Agnimukha</s> (Fire-Face), wandering about, arrived at that bed. Seeing him, she said with a dismayed face: 'O <s>Agnimukha</s>, from where have you come to this unsuitable place? Go away quickly before anyone notices you.'
He said: 'Madam, it is not proper to speak thus even to a wicked person who has come as a guest. As it is said —'

children.text:
aparaṃ mayāneka-mānuṣāṇām aneka-vidhāni rudhirāṇy āsvāditāny āhāra-doṣāt kaṭu-tikta-kaṣāyāmla-rasāsvādāni na ca kadācin madhura-raktaṃ samāsvāditam | tad yadi tvaṃ prasādaṃ karoṣi tad asya nṛpater vividha-vyañjanānna-pāna-coṣya-lehya-svādv-āhāra-vaśād asya śarīre yan miṣṭaṃ raktaṃ saṃjātaṃ tad-āsvādanena saukhyaṃ sampādayāmi jihvāyā iti | uktaṃ ca-
raṅkasya nṛpater vāpi jihvā-saukhyaṃ samaṃ smṛtam | tan-mātraṃ ca smṛtaṃ sāraṃ tad-arthaṃ yatate janaḥ ||Panc_1.277||
children.translated_text:
Moreover, I have tasted the blood of many humans, of many kinds — sour, bitter, astringent, and acidic on account of dietary faults — but I have never tasted sweet blood. If you show me kindness, then because of this king's diet of food and drink rich in varied seasonings, chewable and lickable delicacies, the sweet blood that has been produced in his body — by tasting that I shall achieve the happiness of the tongue. As it is said —
'Whether a pauper or a king, the happiness of the tongue is said to be the same. That alone is considered the essence [of life], and for that people strive. [Panc 1.277]'

children.text: yady eva na bhavel loke karma jihvā-pratuṣṭidam | tan na bhṛtyo bhavet kaścit kasyacid vaśago 'tha vā ||Panc_1.278|| yad asatyaṃ vaden martyo yad vāsevyaṃ ca sevate | yad gacchati videśaṃ ca tat sarvam udarārthataḥ ||Panc_1.279||
children.translated_text: 'If there were no deed in this world that gratifies the tongue, then no one would be a servant or subject to anyone. [Panc 1.278] Whatever falsehood a mortal speaks, whatever unworthy person he serves, wherever he goes abroad — all that is for the sake of the belly. [Panc 1.279]'

children.text: tan mayā gṛhāgatena bubhukṣayā pīḍyamānenāpi tvat-sakāśād bhojanam arthanīyam | tan na tvayaikākinyāsya bhūpate rakta-bhojanaṃ kartuṃ yujyate |
children.translated_text: So I, a guest who has arrived at your home, tormented by hunger, should receive food from you. It is not proper for you alone to feast on this king's blood.

children.text: tac chrutvā mandavisarpiṇy āha-bho matkuṇa ! asya nṛpater nidrā-vaśaṃ gatasya raktam āsvādayāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s> said: 'O bedbug, I suck this king's blood [only] when he has fallen asleep.'

children.text:
punas tvam agnimukhaś capalaś ca-tad yadi mayā saha rakta-pānaṃ karoṣi tat tiṣṭha | abhīṣṭatara-raktam āsvādaya |
so 'bravīt-bhagavaty evaṃ kariṣyāmi | yāvat tvaṃ nāsvādayasi prathamaṃ nṛpa-raktaṃ tāvan mama deva-guru-kṛtaḥ śapathaḥ syād yadi tad āsvādayāmi |
 evaṃ tayoḥ parasparaṃ vadatoḥ sa rājā tac-chayanam āsādya prasuptaḥ | athāsau matkuṇo jihvā-laulyotkṛṣṭautsukyāj jāgratam api taṃ mahī-patim adaśat | atha vā sādhv idam ucyate |
svabhāvo nopadeśena śakyate kartum anyathā | sutaptam api pānīyaṃ punar gacchati śītatām ||Panc_1.280|| yadi syāc chītalo vahniḥ śītāṃśur dahanātmakaḥ | na svabhāvo 'tra martyānāṃ śakyate kartum anyathā ||Panc_1.281||
children.translated_text:
'But you, <s>Agnimukha</s>, are impulsive — so if you wish to drink blood with me, then stay. Taste the most delicious blood.'
He said: 'Madam, I shall do so. May my oath, sworn by teacher and gods, be [broken] if I taste the king's blood before you do.'
Thus, while the two were conversing, the king came to that bed and fell asleep. Then that bedbug, dragged by the eagerness of tongue-greed, bit the king even while he was awake. Or rather, rightly is it said —
'One's nature cannot be changed by instruction; even thoroughly heated water returns to coldness. [Panc 1.280] If fire were cold and the moon of fiery nature — [even then] the nature of mortals cannot be made otherwise. [Panc 1.281]'

children.text: athāsau mahīpatiḥ sūcy-agra-viddha iva tac-chayanaṃ tyaktvā tat-kṣaṇād evotthitaḥ | aho jñāyatām atra pracchādana-paṭe matkuṇo yūkā vā nūnaṃ tiṣṭhati yenāhaṃ daṣṭa iti | atha ye kañcukinas tatra sthitās te satvaraṃ pracchādana-paṭaṃ gṛhītvā sūkṣma-dṛṣṭyā vīkṣāṃ cakruḥ | atrāntare sa matkuṇaś cāpalyāt khaṭvāntaṃ praviṣṭaḥ sā mandavisarpiṇy api vastra-sandhy-antar-gatā tair dṛṣṭā vyāpāditā ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-na hy avijñāta-śīlasya iti |
children.translated_text: Then that king, stung as if by a needle-point, instantly rose from the bed and left it. 'Look here! In the bed-sheet there must be a bedbug or a louse by which I have been bitten.' Then the attendants stationed there quickly took the bed-sheet and examined it with keen eyes. In the meantime, that bedbug, because of his swiftness, had entered the crack of the bedframe, while <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s>, stuck in the fold of the cloth, was seen by them and killed. Therefore I say: 'One should not give shelter to one whose character is unknown.'

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā tvayiṣa vadhyaḥ | no cet tvāṃ vyāpādayiṣyatīti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Knowing this, he should be killed by you. Otherwise, he will kill you. As it is said —

children.text: tyaktāś cābhyantarā yena bāhyāś cābhyantarīkṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: He by whom insiders are abandoned and outsiders are made insiders —

children.text: sa eva mṛtyum āpnoti yathā rājā kakud-drumaḥ ||Panc_1.282||
children.translated_text: he himself meets with death, like king <s>Kakuddruma</s>. [Panc 1.282]

children.text: piṅgalaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 10
caṇḍarava-nāma-śṛgāla-kathā
children.translated_text:
He told —
Story 10
The Tale of the Jackal Named <s>Caṇḍarava</s>

children.text:
asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe caṇḍaravo nāma śṛgālaḥ prativasati sma | sa kadācit kṣudhāviṣṭo jihvā-laulyān nagara-madhye praviṣṭaḥ | atha taṃ nagara-vāsinaḥ sārameyā avalokya sarvataḥ śabdāyamānāḥ paridhāvya tīkṣṇa-daṃṣṭṛāgrair bhakṣitum ārabdhāḥ | so 'pi tair bhakṣyamāṇaḥ prāṇa-bhayāt pratyāsanna-rajaka-gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tatra nīlī-rasa-paripūrṇaṃ mahā-bhāṇḍam sajjīkṛtam āsīt | tatra sārameyair ākrānto bhāṇḍa-madhye patitaḥ | atha yāvan niṣkrāntas tāvan nīlī-varṇaḥ sañjātaḥ | tatrāpare sārameyās taṃ śṛgālam ajānanto yathābhīṣṭa-diśaṃ jagmuḥ | caṇḍaravo 'pi dūrataraṃ pradeśam āsādya kānanābhimukhaṃ pratasthe | na ca nīla-varṇena kadācin nija-raṅgas tyajyate | uktaṃ
ca-
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there lived a jackal named <s>Caṇḍarava</s> (Fierce-Howler). Once, driven by hunger and tongue-greed, he entered the middle of a town. Then the town dogs, seeing him, barking from all sides, chased him and began to devour him with their sharp fangs. Being eaten by them, out of fear for his life, he entered the house of a washerman that was nearby. There stood a large vat filled with indigo dye. Attacked by the dogs, he fell into the vat. When he emerged, he had turned indigo-colored. Then the other dogs, not recognizing him as a jackal, went off in whichever direction they pleased. <s>Caṇḍarava</s> too, reaching a more remote area, headed toward the forest. And the indigo color would not leave his own hue. As it is said —

children.text: vajra-lepasya mūrkhasya nārīṇāṃ karkaṭasya ca | eko grahas tu mīnānāṃ nīlīmadyapayor yathā ||Panc_1.283||
children.translated_text: 'Of diamond-paste, of a fool, of women, and of a crab — the grip is one [i.e., unrelenting]; likewise of fish, and of indigo and wine. [Panc 1.283]'

children.text: atha taṃ hara-gala-garala-tamāla-sama-prabham apūrvaṃ sattvam avalokya sarve siṃha-vyāghra-dvīpi-vṛka-prabhṛtayo 'raṇya-nivāsino bhaya-vyākulita-cittāḥ samantāt palāyana-kriyāṃ kurvanti | kathayanti ca-na jñāyate'sya kīdṛg viceṣṭitaṃ pauruṣaṃ ca | tad dūrataraṃ gacchāmaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, seeing this unprecedented creature, of a color resembling the <s>tamāla</s> tree and the blue poison on <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) throat, all the forest-dwellers — lions, tigers, leopards, wolves, and the rest — their minds agitated with fear, fled in all directions. And they said: 'We do not know what its behavior or prowess is. Let us go far away.' As it is said —

children.text: na yasya ceṣṭitaṃ vidyān na kulaṃ na parākramam |
children.translated_text: One whose conduct is not known, nor family, nor valor —

children.text: na tasya viśvaset prājño yadīcchec chriyam ātmanaḥ ||Panc_1.284||
children.translated_text: in such a one the wise person should not place trust, if he desires his own prosperity. [Panc 1.284]

children.text: caṇḍaravo 'pi bhaya-vyākulitān vijñāyedam āha-bho bhoḥ śvāpadāḥ ! kiṃ yūyaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvaiva saṃtrastā vrajatha | tan na bhetavyam | ahaṃ brahmaṇādya svayam eva sṛṣṭvābhihitaḥ-yac chvāpadānāṃ kaścid rājā nāsti, tat tvaṃ mayādya sarva-śvāpada-prabhutve'bhiṣiktaḥ kakud-drumābhidhaḥ | tato gatvā kṣiti-tale tān sarvān paripālayeti | tato 'ham atrāgataḥ | tan mama cchatra-cchāyāyāṃ sarvair api śvāpadair vartitavyam | ahaṃ kakuddrumo nāma rājā trailokye'pi sañjātaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍarava</s> too, perceiving them stricken with fear, said: 'Ho, wild animals! Why do you flee in terror just from seeing me? Do not be afraid. Today <s>Brahmā</s> himself created me and declared: "Since the wild animals have no king, I have today anointed you as lord over all wild animals, with the name <s>Kakuddruma</s>." Therefore go and protect all [the animals] on earth.' So saying, he said: 'I have come here. Let all the wild animals dwell under the shelter of my umbrella. I am the king named <s>Kakuddruma</s>, recognized even in the three worlds.'

children.text: tac chrutvā siṃha-vyāghra-puraḥ-sarāḥ śvāpadāḥ svāmin prabho samādiśeti vadantas taṃ parivavruḥ | atha tena siṃhasyāmātya-padavī pradattā | vyāghrasya śayyā-pālakatvam | dvīpinas tāmbūlādhikāraḥ | vṛkasya dvāra-pālakatvam | ye cātmīyāḥ śṛgālās taiḥ sahālāpa-mātram api na karoti | śṛgālāḥ sarve'py adharma-candraṃ dattvā niḥsāritāḥ | evaṃ tasya rājya-kriyayāṃ vartamānasya te siṃhādayo mṛgān vyāpādya tat-purataḥ prakṣipanti | so 'pi prabhu-dharmeṇa sarveṣāṃ tān pravibhajya prayacchati |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the wild animals — with lions and tigers at the forefront — saying 'Master! Lord! Command us!' — surrounded him. Then he gave the lion the office of minister; the tiger was made guardian of the bedchamber; the leopard was given charge of the betel; the wolf was made doorkeeper. But with the jackals — his own kind — he would not even converse. All the jackals were given a dishonorable dismissal and expelled. Thus, while he was conducting his kingly affairs, the lions and others would kill deer and throw them before him. And he, in the manner of a lord, would divide and distribute them to all.

children.text: evaṃ gacchati kāle kadācit tena samāgatena dūra-deśe śabdāyamānasya śṛgāla-vṛndasya kolāhalo 'śrāvi | taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā pulakita-tanur ānandāśru-pūrṇa-nayana utthāya tāra-svareṇa virotum ārabdhavān | atha te siṃhādayas taṃ tāra-svaram ākarṇya śṛgālo 'yam iti matvā lajjāyādho-mukhāḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā procuḥ-bhoḥ ! vāhitā vayam anena kṣudra-śṛgālena | tad vadhyatām iti |
children.translated_text: As time passed, once, when a pack of jackals howling in the distance was heard, hearing that sound, his body bristling with excitement, his eyes filled with tears of joy, he stood up and began to howl in a loud voice. Then the lions and others, hearing that loud howl and realizing 'This is a jackal,' stood for a moment with their faces downcast in shame, and then said: 'We have been tricked by this wretched jackal! Let him be killed!'

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇya palāyitum icchaṃs tatra sthāna eva siṃhādibhiḥ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛto mṛtaś ca |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing this, wishing to flee, was right there torn to pieces by the lions and others, and died.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-tyaktāś cābhyantarā yena iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'He by whom insiders are abandoned [and outsiders made insiders]...'

children.text: tad ākarṇya piṅgalaka āha-bho damanaka ! kaḥ pratyayo 'tra viṣaye yat sa mamopari duṣṭa-buddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Piṅgalaka</s> said: 'O <s>Damanaka</s>! What proof is there in this matter that he is evil-minded toward me?'

children.text: sa āha-yad adya mamāgre tena niścayaḥ kṛto yat prabhāte piṅgalakaṃ vadhiṣyāmi | tad atraiva pratyayaḥ | prabhāte'vasara-velāyām ārakta-mukha-nayanaḥ sphuritādharo diśo 'valokayann anucita-sthānopaviṣṭas tvāṃ krūra-dṛṣṭyā vilokayiṣyati | evaṃ jñātvā yad ucitaṃ tat kartavyam | iti kathayitvā sañjīvaka-sakāśaṃ gatas taṃ praṇamyopaviṣṭaḥ | sañjīvako 'pi sodvegākāraṃ manda-gatyā samāyāntaṃ tam udvīkṣya sādarataram uvāca-bho mitra ! svāgatam | cirād dṛṣṭo 'si | api śivaṃ bhavataḥ | tat kathaya yenādeyam api tubhyaṃ gṛhāgatāya prayacchāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Today, in my presence, he made a firm resolve: "Tomorrow at dawn I shall kill <s>Piṅgalaka</s>." That itself is the proof. At dawn, at the opportune moment, with reddened face and eyes, lips quivering, glancing in all directions, seated in an unusual place, he will look at you with a cruel gaze. Knowing this, you should do what is appropriate.' Having said this, he went to <s>Sañjīvaka</s>'s presence and sat down after bowing to him. <s>Sañjīvaka</s> too, seeing him approach slowly with an agitated demeanor, said most respectfully: 'O friend! Welcome! It has been long since I saw you. Is all well with you? Tell me, so that I may give you even what is not to be given, since you have come to my home.' And it is said —

children.text: te dhanyās te viveka-jñās te sabhyā iha bhūtale |
children.translated_text: Blessed are they, wise in discrimination, noble on this earth,

children.text: āgacchanti gṛhe yeṣāṃ kāryārthaṃ suhṛdo janāḥ ||Panc_1.285||
children.translated_text: to whose homes friends come seeking some purpose. [Panc 1.285]

children.text: damanaka āha-bhoḥ ! kathaṃ śivaṃ sevaka-janasya |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Friend! How can there be well-being for a servant?'

children.text: sampattayaḥ parāyattāḥ sadā cittam anirvṛtam |
children.translated_text: Fortunes are dependent on others, the mind is ever restless,

children.text: sva-jīvite'py aviśvāsas teṣāṃ ye rāja-sevakāḥ ||Panc_1.286||
children.translated_text: there is no trust even in one's own life — such are those who are servants of kings. [Panc 1.286]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: sevayā dhanam icchadbhiḥ sevakaiḥ paśya yat kṛtam |
children.translated_text: See what is done by servants who seek wealth through service:

children.text: svātantryaṃ yac charīrasya mūḍhais tad api hāritam ||Panc_1.287||
children.translated_text: even the freedom of their own body, fools that they are, they have surrendered. [Panc 1.287]

children.text: tāvaj janmāti-duḥkhāya tato durgatatā sadā |
children.translated_text: Birth is for great suffering, then comes perpetual misfortune;

children.text: tatrāpi sevayā vṛttir aho duḥkha-paramparā ||Panc_1.288||
children.translated_text: and in that too, living by service — ah, what a chain of sorrows! [Panc 1.288]

children.text: jīvanto 'pi mṛtāḥ pañca śrūyante kila bhārate |
children.translated_text: Five are said to be dead while living, as declared in the <s>Bhārata</s>:

children.text: daridro vyādhito mūrkhaḥ pravāsī nitya-sevakaḥ ||Panc_1.289||
children.translated_text: the poor, the diseased, the fool, the exile, and the perpetual servant. [Panc 1.289]

children.text: nāśnāti svacchayotsukyād vinidro na prabudhyate |
children.translated_text: He does not eat freely out of eagerness, sleepless he does not awaken [at will],

children.text: na niḥśaṅkaṃ vaco brūte sevako 'py atra jīvati ||Panc_1.290||
children.translated_text: nor does he speak words without fear — does a servant truly live? [Panc 1.290]

children.text: sevā śva-vṛttir ākhyātā yais tair mithyā prajalpitam |
children.translated_text: Those who have declared service to be a dog's life spoke falsely —

children.text: svacchandaṃ carati svātra sevakaḥ para-śāsanāt ||Panc_1.291||
children.translated_text: a dog roams freely on its own, while a servant acts by another's command. [Panc 1.291]

children.text: bhū-śayyā brahmacaryaṃ ca kṛśatvaṃ laghu-bhojanam |
children.translated_text: Sleeping on the ground, celibacy, emaciation, meager food —

children.text: sevakasya yater yadvad viśeṣaḥ pāpa-dharmajaḥ ||Panc_1.292||
children.translated_text: the servant's lot is like an ascetic's, except that it arises from sinful duty. [Panc 1.292]

children.text: śītātapādi-kaṣṭāni sahate yāni sevakaḥ |
children.translated_text: The hardships of cold, heat, and such that a servant endures

children.text: dhanāya tāni cālpāni yadi dharmān na mucyate ||Panc_1.293||
children.translated_text: for [mere] wealth — and that too little — if [endured] for <s>dharma</s>, he would be liberated. [Panc 1.293]

children.text: mṛdunāpi suvṛttena suśliṣṭenāpi hāriṇā |
children.translated_text: Even if soft, well-rounded, well-fitting, and attractive —

children.text: modakenāpi kiṃ tena niṣpattir yasya sevayā ||Panc_1.294||
children.translated_text: what use is that <s>modaka</s> (sweet-ball) whose production depends on service? [Panc 1.294]

children.text: sañjīvaka āha-atha bhavān kiṃ vaktu-manāḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjīvaka</s> said: 'Then what do you intend to say?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-mitra, sacivānāṃ mantra-bhedaṃ na yujyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Friend, it is not proper for a minister to betray the king's counsel. And it is said —

children.text: yo mantraṃ svāmino bhidyāt sācivye san-niyojitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, appointed to the position of minister, would betray the counsel of his lord —

children.text: sa hatvā nṛpa-kāryaṃ tat svayaṃ ca narakaṃ vrajet ||Panc_1.295||
children.translated_text: he, having destroyed the king's purpose, himself goes to hell. [Panc 1.295]

children.text: yena yasya kṛto bhedaḥ sacivena mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: By whichever minister the king's [counsel] has been broken,

children.text: tenāśastra-vadhas tasya kṛta ity āha nāradaḥ ||Panc_1.296||
children.translated_text: by him a weaponless murder of that [king] has been committed — so says <s>Nārada</s>. [Panc 1.296]

children.text: tathāpi mayā tava sneha-pāśa-baddhena mantra-bhedaḥ kṛtaḥ | yatas tvaṃ mama vacanenātra rāja-kule viśvastaḥ praviṣṭaś ca | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, bound as I am by the bonds of affection for you, I have broken the counsel. Because you entered this royal court trusting in my word. And it is said —

children.text: viśrambhād yasya yo mṛtyum avāpnoti kathañcana |
children.translated_text: If anyone meets death somehow through trusting another,

children.text: tasya hatyā tad-utthā sā prāhedaṃ vacanaṃ manuḥ ||Panc_1.297||
children.translated_text: the sin of that killing falls on that [person] — this is the statement of <s>Manu</s>. [Panc 1.297]

children.text: tat tavopari piṅgalako 'yaṃ duṣṭa-buddhiḥ kathitaṃ cādyānena mat-purataś catuṣkarṇatayā-yat prabhāte sañjīvakaṃ hatvā samasta-mṛga-parivāraṃ cirāt tṛptiṃ neṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: So this <s>Piṅgalaka</s> is evil-minded toward you, and today he declared before me in a private conversation: "Tomorrow at dawn, having killed <s>Sañjīvaka</s>, I shall satisfy the entire company of beasts for a long time."'

children.text: tataḥ sa mayoktaḥ-svāmin ! na yuktam idaṃ yan mitra-droheṇa jīvanaṃ kriyate | uktaṃ ca-
api brahma-vadhaṃ kṛtvā prāyaścittena śudhyati |
children.translated_text: Even one who has committed the sin of killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is purified through penance,

children.text: tad-arthena vicīrṇena na kathañcit suhṛd-druhaḥ ||Panc_1.298||
children.translated_text: but never one who betrays a friend, by any atonement whatsoever. [Panc 1.298]
Then I said to him: 'Lord! This is not proper — that one should sustain life through betrayal of a friend. And it is said —

children.text: tatas tenāhaṃ samarṣeṇoktaḥ-bho duṣṭa-buddhe, sañjīvakas tāvac chaṣpa-bhojī, vayaṃ māṃsāśinaḥ | tad asmākaṃ svābhāvikaṃ vairam iti kathaṃ ripur upekṣyate ? tasmāt sāmādibhir upāyair hanyate | na ca hate tasmin doṣaḥ syāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then he, angered, said to me: "You evil-minded one! <s>Sañjīvaka</s> is merely a grass-eater, while we are meat-eaters. Thus our enmity is natural — how then can an enemy be ignored? Therefore, he should be killed by means of the strategies beginning with conciliation. And there would be no fault in killing him." And it is said —

children.text: dattvāpi kanyakāṃ vairī nihantavyo vipaścitā |
children.translated_text: Even after giving [his] daughter [in marriage], an enemy should be killed by a wise man;

children.text: anyopāyair aśakyo yo hate doṣo na vidyate ||Panc_1.299||
children.translated_text: one who cannot be overcome by other means — there is no fault in killing him. [Panc 1.299]

children.text: kṛtyākṛtyaṃ na manyeta kṣatriyo yudhi saṅgataḥ |
children.translated_text: A warrior engaged in battle should not consider what is proper and improper;

children.text: prasupto droṇa-putreṇa dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ purā hataḥ ||Panc_1.300||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> was formerly killed by <s>Droṇa</s>'s son while asleep. [Panc 1.300]

children.text: tad ahaṃ tasya niścayaṃ jñātvā tvat-sakāśam ihāgataḥ | sāmprataṃ me nāsti viśvāsa-ghātaka-doṣaḥ | mayā sugupta-mantras tava niveditaḥ | atha yat te pratibhāti tat kuruṣva iti | atha sañjīvakas tasya tadvajra-pāta-dāruṇaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā moham upagataḥ | atha cetanāṃ labdhvā sa-vairāgyam idam āha-bho sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: So, having learned his resolve, I have come here to you. Now I bear no guilt of betraying trust. I have reported to you the well-guarded counsel. Now do as you see fit.' Then <s>Sañjīvaka</s>, hearing his words harsh as a thunderbolt, fell into a swoon. Then, recovering consciousness, he said with detachment —

children.text: durjana-gamyā nāryaḥ prāyeṇāsnehavān bhavati rājā |
children.translated_text: Women are accessible to wicked men; a king is generally devoid of affection;

children.text: kṛpaṇānusāri ca dhanaṃ megho giri-durga-varṣī ca ||Panc_1.301||
children.translated_text: wealth follows the miser; and clouds rain upon mountain-fortresses. [Panc 1.301]

children.text: ahaṃ hi saṃmato rājño ya evaṃ manyate kudhīḥ |
children.translated_text: I, who am esteemed by the king — that this fool thinks thus [ill of me] —

children.text: balīvardaḥ sa vijñeyo viṣāṇa-parivarjitaḥ ||Panc_1.302||
children.translated_text: he should be known as a bull deprived of horns. [Panc 1.302]

children.text: varaṃ vanaṃ varaṃ bhaikṣaṃ varaṃ bhāropajīvanam |
children.translated_text: Better the forest, better begging alms, better living by carrying burdens,

children.text: varaṃ vyādhir manuṣyāṇāṃ nādhikāreṇa sampadaḥ ||Panc_1.303||
children.translated_text: better disease for men — than prosperity through [unwanted] authority. [Panc 1.303]

children.text: tad yuktaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ tad anena saha maitrī vihitā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So it was fitting what I did — that I formed friendship with him. And it is said —

children.text: yayor eva samaṃ vittaṃ yayor eva samaṃ kulam |
children.translated_text: Only between those equal in wealth, and those equal in lineage,

children.text: tayor maitrī vivāhaś ca na tu puṣṭa-vipuṣṭayoḥ ||Panc_1.304||
children.translated_text: does friendship and marriage [take place] — not between the prosperous and the destitute. [Panc 1.304]

children.text: tathā ca-
mṛgā mṛgaiḥ saṅgam anuvrajanti
children.translated_text: Deer associate with deer,

children.text: gāvaś ca gobhis turagās turagaiḥ |
children.translated_text: cows with cows, horses with horses,

children.text: mūrkhāś ca mūrkhaiḥ sudhiyaḥ
children.translated_text: fools with fools, the wise

children.text: sudhībhiḥ samāna-śīla-vyasanena sakhyam ||Panc_1.305||
children.translated_text: with the wise — friendship is based on similarity of character and inclination. [Panc 1.305]
And also —

children.text: tad yadi gatvā taṃ prasādayāmi, tathāpi na prasādaṃ yāsyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So even if I go and try to appease him, he will not be appeased. And it is said —

children.text: nimittam uddiśya hi yaḥ prakupyati
children.translated_text: He who becomes angry for a [specific] reason

children.text: dhruvaṃ sa tasyāpagame praśāmyati |
children.translated_text: will certainly be calmed when that [reason] is removed;

children.text: akāraṇa-dveṣa-paro hi yo bhavet
children.translated_text: but he who is inclined to causeless hatred —

children.text: kathaṃ naras taṃ paritoṣayati ||Panc_1.306||
children.translated_text: how can a man appease him? [Panc 1.306]

children.text: aho sādhu cedam ucyate-
bhaktānām upakāriṇāṃ para-hita-vyāpāra-yuktātmanāṃ
children.translated_text: For the devoted, the beneficent, those engaged in working for others' welfare,

children.text: sevā-saṃvyavahāra-tattva-viduṣāṃ droha-cyutānām api |
children.translated_text: those skilled in the principles of service and conduct, even those free from treachery —

children.text: vyāpattiḥ skhalitāntareṣu niyatā siddhir bhaved vā na vā
children.translated_text: calamity is certain when [fortunes] stumble, and success may or may not come;

children.text: tasmād ambupater ivāvani-pateḥ sevā sadā śaṅkinī ||Panc_1.307||
children.translated_text: therefore, like [service to] the lord of waters, service to a king is ever fraught with danger. [Panc 1.307]
Ah, and this is well said —

children.text: tathā ca-
bhāva-snigdhair upakṛtam api dveṣyatāṃ yāti loke
children.translated_text: Even favors done with heartfelt affection turn to hatred in this world,

children.text: sākṣād anyair apakṛtam api prītaye copayāti |
children.translated_text: while manifest harm done by others may lead to love;

children.text: durgrāhyatvān nṛpati-manasāṃ naika-bhāvāśrayāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: because the minds of kings, which shelter many dispositions, are hard to grasp —

children.text: sevā-dharmaḥ parama-gahano yoginām apy agamyaḥ ||Panc_1.308||
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> of service is supremely unfathomable, inaccessible even to yogis. [Panc 1.308]
And also —

children.text: tat parijñātaṃ mayā mat-prasādam asahamānaiḥ samīpavartibhir eṣa piṅgalakaḥ prakopitaḥ | tenāyaṃ mamādoṣasyāpy evaṃ vadati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So I have understood: those near him, unable to bear my [receiving his] favor, have incited this <s>Piṅgalaka</s> against me. Therefore he speaks thus of me though I am faultless. And it is said —

children.text: prabhoḥ prasādam anyasya na sahantīha sevakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Servants cannot tolerate another's receiving the master's favor;

children.text: sapatnya iva saṅkruddhāḥ sapatnyāḥ sukṛtair api ||Panc_1.309||
children.translated_text: like co-wives enraged, they are angered even by a co-wife's good deeds. [Panc 1.309]

children.text: bhavati caivaṃ yad guṇavatsu samīpa-vartiṣu guṇa-hīnānāṃ na prasādo bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is indeed so: when those near [the king] are endowed with virtues, there is no favor for those lacking virtues. And it is said —

children.text: guṇavattara-pātreṇa chādyante guṇināṃ guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: The virtues of the virtuous are eclipsed by one of even greater virtue,

children.text: rātrau dīpa-śikhā-kāntir na bhānāv udite sati ||Panc_1.310||
children.translated_text: as the beauty of a lamp's flame [is eclipsed] when the sun has risen. [Panc 1.310]

children.text: damanaka āha-bho mitra ! yady evaṃ tan nāsti te bhayam | prakopito 'pi sa durjanais tava vacana-racanayā prasādaṃ yāsyati |
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'O friend! If that is so, then you have nothing to fear. Even though incited by wicked ones, he will be appeased by your eloquent speech.'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ ! na yuktam uktaṃ bhavatā | laghūnām api durjanānāṃ madhye vastuṃ na śakyate | upāyāntaraṃ vidhāya te nūnaṃ ghnanti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Friend! What you say is not correct. It is not possible to dwell among wicked men, even insignificant ones. They devise other means and surely kill. And it is said —

children.text: bahavaḥ paṇḍitāḥ kṣudrāḥ sarve māyopajīvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Many learned [but] base men, all living by deception,

children.text: kuryuḥ kṛtyam akṛtyaṃ vā uṣṭre kākādayo yathā ||Panc_1.311||
children.translated_text: would do the proper or the improper — like crows [attacking] a camel. [Panc 1.311]

children.text: damaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 11
madotkaṭa-siṃha-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said: '
Story 11
The Story of the Lion <s>Madotkaṭa</s>'

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe madotkaṭo nāma siṃhaḥ prativasa ti sma | tasya cānucarā anye dvīpi-vāyasa-gomāyavaḥ santi | atha kadācit tair itas tato bhramadbhiḥ sārthād bhraṣṭaḥ krathanako nāmoṣtro dṛṣṭaḥ | atha siṃha āha-aho apūrvam idaṃ sattvam | taj jñāyatāṃ kim etad āraṇyakaṃ grāmyaṃ veti |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there lived a lion named <s>Madotkaṭa</s> (Furious with Rut). His attendants were a leopard, a crow, and a jackal. Now one day, while they were roaming here and there, they spotted a camel named <s>Krathanaka</s>, separated from his caravan. Then the lion said: 'Ah! This is an unusual creature. Let it be found out whether this is a wild or domestic animal.'

children.text:
tac chrutvā vāyasa āha-bhoḥ svāmin ! grāmyo 'yam uṣṭra-nāmā jīva-viśeṣas tava bhojyaḥ | tad vyāpādyatām |
 siṃha āha-nāhaṃ gṛham āgataṃ hanmi | uktaṃ ca-
gṛhaṃ śatrum api prāptaṃ viśvastam akutobhayam | yo hanyāt tasya pāpaṃ syāc chatabrāhmaṇaghātajam ||Panc_1.312||
children.translated_text:
Hearing this, the crow said: 'O lord! This is a domestic creature called a camel — it is your food. So let him be killed.'
The lion said: 'I do not kill one who has come to my home. And it is said —
He who would kill an enemy that has come to his home, trusting and without fear from any quarter — upon him falls the sin equal to that of killing a hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. [Panc 1.312]'

children.text: tad abhaya-pradānaṃ dattvā mat-sakāśam ānīyatāṃ yenāsyāgama-kāraṇaṃ pṛcchāmi |
children.translated_text: 'So, giving him a pledge of safety, let him be brought to me, so that I may ask the reason for his coming.'

children.text: athāsau sarvair api viśvāsyābhaya-pradānaṃ dattvā madotkaṭa-sakāśam ānītaḥ praṇamyopaviṣṭaś ca | tatas tasya pṛcchatas tenātma-vṛttāntaḥ sārtha-bhraṃśa-samudbhavo niveditaḥ | tataḥ siṃhenoktam-bhoḥ krathanaka ! mā tvaṃ grāmaṃ gatvā bhūyo 'pi bhārodvahana-kaṣṭa-bhāgī bhūyāḥ | tad atraivāraṇye nirviśaṅko marakata-sadṛśāni śaṣpāgrāṇi bhakṣayan mayā saha sadaiva vasa | so 'pi tathety uktvā teṣāṃ madhye vicaran na kuto 'pi bhayam iti sukhenāste |
children.translated_text: Then, having been assured by all and given a pledge of safety, he was brought to <s>Madotkaṭa</s>'s presence and sat down after bowing. Then, when asked by him, he related his own story — how he had become separated from the caravan. Then the lion said: 'O <s>Krathanaka</s>! Do not go back to the village and again become a bearer of burdens and hardship. Instead, live here in this forest without fear, eating the tips of grass green as emeralds, and stay with me always.' He too said 'So be it' and, living among them, fearing nothing from anywhere, dwelt in happiness.

children.text:
tathānyedyur madotkaṭasya mahā-gajenāraṇya-cāriṇā saha yuddham abhavat | tatas tasya danta-musala-prahārair vyathā sañjātā | vyathitaḥ katham api prāṇair na viyuktaḥ | atha śarīrāsāmarthyān na kutracit padam api calituṃ śaknoti | te sarve kākādayo 'py aprabhutvena kṣudhāviṣṭāḥ paraṃ duḥkhaṃ bhejuḥ |
atha tān siṃhaḥ prāha-bhoḥ ! anviṣyatāṃ kutracit kiṃcit sattvaṃ yenāham etām api daśāṃ prāptas tad dhatvā yuṣmad-bhojanaṃ sampādayāmi |
children.translated_text:
Then on another day, <s>Madotkaṭa</s> had a fight with a great wild elephant. From the blows of its tusk-clubs, he suffered great pain. Wounded, he somehow did not lose his life. But due to bodily weakness, he could not move even a single step anywhere. All those — the crow and the others — afflicted by hunger due to their master's incapacity, experienced extreme distress.
Then the lion said to them: 'Friends! Search somewhere for some creature, so that even in this condition I may kill it and provide food for you.'

children.text:
atha te catvāro 'pi bhramitum ārabdhā yāvan na kiṃcit sattvaṃ paśyanti tāvad vāyasa-śṛgālau parasparaṃ mantrayataḥ | śṛgāla āha-bho vāyasa ! kiṃ prabhūta-bhrāntena | ayam asmākaṃ prabhoḥ krathanako viśvastas tiṣṭhati | tad enaṃ hatvā prāṇa-yātrāṃ kurmaḥ |
vāyasa āha-yuktam uktaṃ bhavatā | paraṃ svāminā tasyābhaya-pradānaṃ dattam āste na vadhyo 'yam iti |
children.translated_text:
Then all four began to roam about, but when they could not find any creature, the crow and the jackal consulted each other. The jackal said: 'O crow! What use is all this wandering? Here is <s>Krathanaka</s>, standing trustingly before our master. Let us kill him and sustain our lives.'
The crow said: 'What you say is reasonable. But our master has given him a pledge of safety — he cannot be killed.'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-bho vāyasa ! ahaṃ svāminaṃ vijñāpya tathā kariṣye yathā svāmī vadhaṃ kariṣyati | tat tiṣṭhantu bhavanto 'traiva, yāvad ahaṃ gṛhaṃ gatvā prabhor ājñāṃ gṛhītvā cāgacchāmi |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'O crow! I shall petition the master and arrange things so that the master himself will order the killing. So you all stay here while I go home and, obtaining the master's command, return.'

children.text: evam abhidhāya satvaraṃ siṃham uddiśya prasthitaḥ | atha siṃham āsādyedam āha-svāmin ! samastaṃ vanaṃ bhrāntvā vayam āgatāḥ | na kiṃcit sattvam āsāditam | tat kiṃ kurmo vayam | samprati vayaṃ bubhukṣayā padam ekam api pracalituṃ na śaknumaḥ | devo 'pi pathyāśī vartate | tad yadi devādeśo bhavati tat krathanaka-piśitenādya pathya-kriyā kriyate |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he set out quickly toward the lion. Then, having reached the lion, he said this: 'Master! We have wandered through the entire forest and returned. No creature was found. So what shall we do? Now we are unable to move even a single step due to hunger. Your Majesty too is on a regulated diet. Therefore, if it be Your Majesty's command, then today let the curative regimen be performed with the flesh of <s>Krathanaka</s>.'

children.text: atha siṃhas tasya tad dāruṇaṃ vacanam ākarṇya sa-kopam idam āha-dhik pāpādhama ! yady evaṃ bhūyo 'pi vadasi | tatas tvāṃ tat-kṣaṇam eva vadhiṣyāmi | tato mayā tasyābhayaṃ pradattam | tat kathaṃ vyāpādayāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then the lion, hearing those cruel words of his, angrily spoke thus: 'Shame on you, vilest of sinners! If you speak like this again, I shall kill you that very instant! For I have given him a promise of safety. How then can I destroy him?' And it is said —

children.text:
na go-pradānaṃ na mahī-pradānaṃ
na cānna-dānaṃ hi tathā pradhānam | yathā vadantīha budhāḥ pradhānaṃ
sarva-pradāneṣv abhaya-pradānam ||Panc_1.313||
children.translated_text: as the gift of fearlessness among all gifts — so the wise declare. [Panc 1.313]
Neither the gift of cows, nor the gift of land, nor even the gift of food is considered as important

children.text:
tac chrutvā śṛgāla āha-svāmin yady abhayapradānaṃ dattvā vadhaḥ kriyate tad eṣa doṣo bhavati | punar yadi devapādānāṃ bhaktyā sātmano jīvitavyaṃ prayacchati tan na doṣaḥ |
tato yadi sa svayam evātmānaṃ vadhāya niyojayati tad vadhyo 'nyathāsmākaṃ madhyād ekatamo vadhya iti yato devapādāḥ pathyāśinaḥ kṣunnirodhād antyāṃ daśāṃ yāsyanti |
tat kim etaiḥ prāṇair asmākaṃ ye svāmyarthe na yāsyanti | aparaṃ paścād apy asmābhir vahni-praveśaḥ kāryo yadi svāmi-pādānāṃ kiṃcid aniṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
 yasmin kule yaḥ puruṣaḥ pradhānaḥ
sa sarva-yatnaiḥ parirakṣaṇīyaḥ | tasmin vinaṣṭe sva-kulaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ
na nābhi-bhaṅge hy arakā vahanti ||Panc_1.314||
children.translated_text: for when the hub is broken, the spokes cannot carry.' [Panc 1.314]

Hearing that, the jackal said: 'Master, if one kills after having given the promise of fearlessness, then that is indeed a fault. But if, out of devotion to Your Majesty's feet, he of his own accord offers up his life, then there is no fault. Therefore, if he himself willingly devotes himself to death, then he is the one to be slain; otherwise one among us must be the sacrifice — since Your Majesty, being on a restricted diet, will reach a final state from suppression of hunger. What use are these lives of ours if they will not be given for our master's sake? Moreover, afterward we too must enter fire if any misfortune befalls our lord's feet.' And it is said — 'In whatever family, whatever man is chief, he must be protected by all efforts. When he is destroyed, the family is destroyed —

children.text: tad ākarṇya madotkaṭa āha-yady evaṃ tat kuruṣva yad rocate |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Madotkaṭa</s> said: 'If so, then do what pleases you.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sa satvaraṃ gatvā tān āha-bhoḥ ! svāmino mahaty avasthā vartate | tat kiṃ paryaṭitena ? tena vinā ko 'trāsmān rakṣayiṣyati ? tad gatvā tasya kṣud-rogāt para-lokaṃ prasthitasyātma-śarīra-dānaṃ kurmo yena svāmi-prasādasya anṛṇatāṃ gacchāmaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
āpadaṃ prāpnuyāt svāmī yasya bhṛtyasya paśyataḥ |
children.translated_text: The servant in whose sight his master meets with calamity,

children.text: prāṇeṣu vidyamāneṣu sa bhṛtyo narakaṃ vrajet ||Panc_1.315||
children.translated_text: while his own life-breaths still remain — that servant goes to hell. [Panc 1.315]

Hearing that, he quickly went and told them: 'Friends! Our master is in a grave condition. What is the use of wandering about? Without him, who here will protect us? So let us go and offer our own bodies to him who is about to depart to the other world from the disease of hunger, so that we may discharge our debt to our master's grace.' And it is said —

children.text:
tad-anantaraṃ te sarve bāṣpa-pūrita-dṛśo madotkaṭaṃ praṇamyopaviṣṭāḥ | tān dṛṣṭvā madotkaṭa āha-bhoḥ ! prāptaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā kiṃcit sattvam |
atha teṣāṃ madhyāt kākaḥ provāca-svāmin ! vayaṃ tāvat sarvatra paryaṭitāḥ paraṃ na kiṃcit sattvam āsāditaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā | tad adya māṃ bhakṣayitvā prāṇān dhārayatu svāmī, yena devasyāśvāsanaṃ bhavati mama punaḥ svarga-prāptir iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Thereupon, all of them, with eyes filled with tears, bowed to <s>Madotkaṭa</s> and sat down. Seeing them, <s>Madotkaṭa</s> said: 'Well! Has any creature been found or seen?' Then from among them, the crow spoke: 'Master! We have indeed wandered everywhere, but no creature was found or seen. Therefore, let the master preserve his life today by eating me, so that His Majesty may have relief, and I shall attain heaven.' And it is said —

children.text: svāmy-arthe yas tyajet prāṇān bhṛtyo bhakti-samanvitaḥ | sa paraṃ padam āpnoti jarā-maraṇa-varjitam ||Panc_1.316||
children.translated_text: The servant who, full of devotion, gives up his life for his master's sake — he attains the supreme state, free from old age and death. [Panc 1.316]

children.text: tac chrutvā śṛgāla āha-bhoḥ ! svalpa-kāyo bhavān | tava bhakṣaṇāt svāminas tāvat prāṇa-yātrā na bhavati | aparo doṣaś ca tāvat samutpadyate | uktaṃ ca-
kāka-māṃsaṃ tathocchiṣṭaṃ stokaṃ tad api durbalam |
children.translated_text: Crow's flesh is impure and meager, and also weak;

children.text: bhakṣitenāpi kiṃ tena yena tṛptir na jāyate ||Panc_1.317||
children.translated_text: what use is eating that which does not produce satisfaction? [Panc 1.317]
Hearing that, the jackal said: 'Friend! You are small-bodied. By eating you, the master's sustenance cannot be maintained. And another fault also arises.' It is said —

children.text: tad darṣitā svāmi-bhaktir bhavatā gataṃ ca ānṛṇyaṃ bhartṛ-piṇḍasya prāptaś cobhaya-loke sādhu-vādaḥ | tad apasarāgrataḥ | ahaṃ svāminaṃ vijñāpayāmi | tathānuṣṭhite śṛgālaḥ sādaraṃ praṇamyopaviṣṭaḥ prāha-svāmin ! māṃ bhakṣayitvādya prāṇa-yātrāṃ vidhāya mamobhaya-loka-prāptiṃ kuru | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: But your devotion to the master has been demonstrated, and you have discharged your debt to the master's provision, and you have obtained the praise of the good in both worlds. So step aside. I shall inform the master.' When this had been done, the jackal bowed respectfully, sat down, and said: 'Master! Eat me today, maintain your life-breath, and grant me the attainment of both worlds.' And it is said —

children.text: svāmy-āyattāḥ sadā prāṇā bhṛtyānām arjitā dhanaiḥ | yatas tato na doṣo 'sti teṣāṃ grahaṇa-sambhavaḥ ||Panc_1.318||
children.translated_text: The lives of servants are always dependent on the master, earned through wealth. Therefore there is no fault in taking them. [Panc 1.318]

children.text:
atha tac chrutvā dvīpy āha-bhoḥ sādhūktaṃ bhavatā punar bhavān api svalpa-kāyaḥ sva-jātiś ca nakhāyudhatvād abhakṣya eva | uktaṃ ca-
nābhakṣyaṃ bhakṣayet prājñaḥ prāṇaiḥ kaṇṭha-gatair api | viśeṣāt tad api stokaṃ loka-dvaya-vināśakam ||Panc_1.319||
children.translated_text: Then hearing that, the leopard said: 'Friend! Well spoken by you. But you too are small-bodied, and being of the claw-weapon species, you are inedible.' And it is said — 'A wise man should not eat what is forbidden even when his life-breath reaches his throat. Especially that which is scanty and destructive of both worlds.' [Panc 1.319]

children.text:
tad darśitaṃ tvayātmanaḥ kaulīnyam | atha vā sādhu cedam ucyate-
  etad-arthaṃ kulīnānāṃ nṛpāḥ kurvanti saṅgraham | ādi-madhyāvasāneṣu na te gacchanti vikriyām ||Panc_1.320||
children.translated_text: But your noble lineage has been demonstrated. Or rather, this is well said — 'For this very reason kings gather men of good family: at the beginning, middle, and end, they never undergo change.' [Panc 1.320]

children.text:
tad apasarāgrataḥ, yenāhaṃ svāminaṃ vijñāpayāmi | tathānuṣṭhite dvīpī praṇamya madotkaṭam āha-svāmin ! kriyatām adya mama prāṇaiḥ prāṇa-yātrā | dīyatām akṣayo vāsaḥ svarge | mama vistāryatāṃ kṣiti-tale prabhūtaṃ yaśaḥ | tan nātra vismayaḥ kāryaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
mṛtānāṃ svāminaḥ kārye bhṛtyānām anuvartinām | bhavet svarge akṣayo vāsaḥ kīrtiś ca dharaṇī-tale ||Panc_1.321||
children.translated_text: So step aside, that I may inform the master.' When this had been done, the leopard bowed to <s>Madotkaṭa</s> and said: 'Master! Let my life-journey be sustained today by my life-breaths. Grant me imperishable residence in heaven. Let my abundant fame be spread upon the surface of the earth. No wonder is to be made of this.' And it is said — 'For servants who follow their master's cause unto death, there shall be imperishable residence in heaven and fame upon the earth.' [Panc 1.321]

children.text:
tac chrutvā krathanakaś cintayāmāsa-etais tāvat sarvair api śobhā-vākyāny uktāni na caiko 'pi svāminā vināśitaḥ | tad aham api prāpta-kālaṃ vakṣyāmi citrakaṃ yena mad-vacanam ete trayo 'pi samarthayanti | iti niścitya provāca-bhoḥ satyam uktaṃ bhavatā paraṃ bhavān api nakhāyudhaḥ | tat kathaṃ bhavantaṃ svāmī bhakṣayati | uktaṃ ca-
manasāpi svajātyānāṃ yo 'niṣṭāni pracintayet | bhavanti tasya tāny eva iha loke paratra ca ||Panc_1.322||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Krathanaka</s> thought to himself: 'All of these have spoken fine words, yet not a single one has been killed by the master. So I too shall speak what is fitting, so that <s>Citraka</s> — all three will endorse my words.' Having resolved thus, he said: 'Friend! What you say is true, but you too are a claw-weapon animal. How then will the master eat you?' And it is said — 'He who even in thought contemplates harm to those of his own kind — those very evils befall him in this world and the next.' [Panc 1.322]

children.text: tad apasarāgrataḥ, yenāhaṃ svāminaṃ vijñāpayāmi | tathānuṣṭhite krathanako 'gre sthitvā praṇamyovāca-svāmin ! ete'bhakṣyās tava tan mama prāṇaiḥ prāṇa-yātrā vidhīyatāṃ yena mamobhaya-loka-prāptir bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So step aside, that I may inform the master.' When this had been done, <s>Krathanaka</s> stood before him, bowed, and said: 'Master! These are inedible for you; therefore let my life-breaths sustain your life-journey, so that I may attain both worlds.' And it is said —

children.text: na yajvāno 'pi gacchanti tāṃ gatiṃ naiva yoginaḥ | yāṃ yānti projjhita-prāṇāḥ svāmy-arthe sevakottamāḥ ||Panc_1.323||
children.translated_text: Not even sacrificers attain that state, nor even <s>yogins</s>, which the best of servants attain who cast off their lives for their master's sake. [Panc 1.323]

children.text: evam abhihite tābhyāṃ śṛgāla-citrakābhyāṃ vidāritobhaya-kukṣiḥ krathanakaḥ prāṇān atyākṣīt | tataś ca taiḥ kṣudra-paṇḍitaiḥ sarvair bhakṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus, those two — the jackal and <s>Citraka</s> — tore open both his flanks, and <s>Krathanaka</s> gave up his life. And then he was eaten by all those petty intellectuals.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bahavaḥ paṇḍitāḥ kṣudrāḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Many scholars are base' — and so on.

children.text: tad bhadra, kṣudra-parivāro 'yaṃ te rājā mayā samyag jātaḥ | satām asevyaṃ ca | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So, my good friend, this king of yours surrounded by base attendants has been properly assessed by me. He is not to be served by the virtuous. And it is said —

children.text: aśuddha-prakṛtau rājñi janatā nānurajyate |
children.translated_text: The people do not become attached to a king whose counselors are impure,

children.text: yathā gṛdhra-samāsannaḥ kalahaṃsaḥ samācaret ||Panc_1.324||
children.translated_text: just as a swan would not frequent the vicinity of a vulture. [Panc 1.324]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: gṛdhrākāro 'pi sevyaḥ syād dhaṃsākāraiḥ sabhāsadaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Even one who looks like a vulture should be served, if he has swan-like courtiers;

children.text: haṃsākāro 'pi santyājyo gṛdhrākāraiḥ sa tair nṛpaḥ ||Panc_1.325||
children.translated_text: but even a swan-like king should be abandoned if he has vulture-like courtiers. [Panc 1.325]

children.text: tan nūnaṃ mamopari kenacid durjanenāyaṃ prakopitaḥ, tenaivaṃ vadati | athavā bhavaty etat | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Surely some wicked person has incited him against me, and that is why he speaks thus. Or perhaps it is inevitable. And it is said —

children.text: mṛdunā salilena khanyamā
children.translated_text: By soft water being excavated,

children.text: nānyavad dhṛṣyanti girer api sthalāni |
children.translated_text: even the surfaces of mountains are eroded like anything else;

children.text: upajāpavidāṃ ca karṇa-jāpaiḥ
children.translated_text: and by the ear-whispers of those skilled in sedition,

children.text: kim u cetāṃsi mṛdūni mānavānām ||Panc_1.326||
children.translated_text: how much more so the soft minds of men! [Panc 1.326]

children.text: karṇa-viṣeṇa ca bhagnaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na karoti bāliśo lokaḥ |
children.translated_text: And what does the foolish world, broken by ear-poison, not do?

children.text: kṣapaṇakatām api dhatte pibati surāṃ naraka-pālena ||Panc_1.327||
children.translated_text: It even adopts asceticism; it drinks liquor as if guarding hell. [Panc 1.327]

children.text: athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: pādāhato 'pi dṛḍha-daṇḍa-samāhato 'pi
children.translated_text: Struck by the foot, or struck by a strong staff —

children.text: yaṃ daṃṣṭrayā spṛśati taṃ kila hanti sarpaḥ |
children.translated_text: the serpent kills only the one it touches with its fang;

children.text: ko 'py eṣa eva piśunogra-manuṣya-dharmaḥ
children.translated_text: but such indeed is the nature of the vile, fierce, wicked man —

children.text: karṇe paraṃ spṛśati hanti paraṃ samūlam ||Panc_1.328||
children.translated_text: he touches one's ear, and destroys another utterly. [Panc 1.328]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: aho khala-bhujaṅgasya viparīto vadha-kramaḥ |
children.translated_text: Ah, how reversed is the manner of killing of the wicked serpent!

children.text: karṇe lagati cānyasya prāṇair anyo viyujyate ||Panc_1.329||
children.translated_text: It enters the ear of one, and another is deprived of life. [Panc 1.329]

children.text: tad evaṃ gate'pi kiṃ kartavyam ity ahaṃ tvāṃ suhṛd-bhāvāt pṛcchāmi |
children.translated_text: So, even though things are thus, what is to be done — this I ask you out of friendship.

children.text: damanaka āha-tad-deśāntara-gamanaṃ yujyate | naivaṃ-vidhasya kusvāminaḥ sevāṃ vidhātum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Then going to another country is appropriate. One should not serve such a bad master.' And it is said —

children.text: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a preceptor who is arrogant, who does not know what should and should not be done,

children.text: utpatha-pratipannasya parityāgo vidhīyate ||Panc_1.330||
children.translated_text: who has taken to a wrong path — his abandonment is prescribed. [Panc 1.330]

children.text: sañjīvaka āha-asmākam upari svāmini kupite gantuṃ na śakyate, na cānyatra gatānām api nirvṛtir bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjīvaka</s> said: 'When the master is angry with us, it is not possible to go, nor do those who have gone elsewhere find peace.' And it is said —

children.text: mahatāṃ yo 'parādhyena dūrastho 'smīti nāśvaset |
children.translated_text: He who offends the great should not feel secure thinking 'I am far away';

children.text: dīrghau buddhimato bāhū tābhyāṃ hiṃsati hiṃsakam ||Panc_1.331||
children.translated_text: long are the arms of the intelligent — with those he strikes the aggressor. [Panc 1.331]

children.text: tad yuddhaṃ muktvā me nānyad asit śreyaskaram | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore, except for battle, there is no other course that would be beneficial for me. And it is said —

children.text: na tān hi tīrthais tapasā ca lokān
children.translated_text: Not by pilgrimages, not by austerities, not by those worlds

children.text: svargaiṣiṇo dāna-śataiḥ suvṛttaiḥ |
children.translated_text: which the heaven-seekers [attain] through hundreds of gifts and good conduct;

children.text: kṣaṇena yān yānti raṇeṣu dhīrāḥ
children.translated_text: in an instant those [worlds] are attained in battle by the brave

children.text: prāṇān samujjhanti hi ye suśīlāḥ ||Panc_1.332||
children.translated_text: who cast off their lives — those who are of noble character. [Panc 1.332]

children.text: mṛtaiḥ samprāpyate svargo jīvadbhiḥ kīrtir uttamā |
children.translated_text: By dying one attains heaven; by living, the highest fame;

children.text: tad ubhāv api śūrāṇāṃ guṇāv etau sudurlabhau ||Panc_1.333||
children.translated_text: thus both these virtues of heroes are extremely hard to obtain. [Panc 1.333]

children.text: lalāṭa-deśe rudhiraṃ sravat tu
children.translated_text: The blood flowing on the forehead

children.text: śūrasya yasya praviśec ca vaktre |
children.translated_text: of a hero that enters his mouth —

children.text: tat somapānena samaṃ bhavec ca
children.translated_text: that is equal to the drinking of <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: saṅgrāma-yajñe vidhivat pradiṣṭam ||Panc_1.334||
children.translated_text: properly prescribed in the sacrifice of battle. [Panc 1.334]

children.text: tathā ca-
homārthair vidhivat pradāna-vidhinā sad-vipra-vṛndārcanair
children.translated_text: The fruit that is attained through oblations performed according to rule, through proper ritual gifts, through worship of assemblies of true <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: yajñair bhūri-sudakṣiṇaiḥ suvihitaiḥ samprāpyate yat phalam |
children.translated_text: through well-conducted sacrifices with abundant fees,

children.text: sat-tīrthāśrama-vāsa-homa-niyamaiś cāndrāyaṇādyaiḥ kṛtaiḥ
children.translated_text: through dwelling in holy places and hermitages, through observances of <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> and other [vows] —

children.text: pumbhis tat-phalam āhave vinihitaiḥ samprāpyate tat-kṣaṇāt ||Panc_1.335||
children.translated_text: that very fruit is attained in an instant by men who lay down [their lives] in battle. [Panc 1.335]
And likewise —

children.text: tad ākarṇya damanakaś cintayāmāsa-yuddhāya kṛta-niścayo 'yaṃ dṛśyate durātmā | tad yadi kadācit tīkṣṇa-śṛgālābhyāṃ svāminaṃ prahariṣyati tan mahān anarthaḥ sampatsyate | tad enaṃ bhūyo 'pi sva-buddhyā prabodhya tathā karomi, yathā deśāntara-gamanaṃ karoti | āha ca-bho mitra ! samyag abhihitaṃ bhavatā | paraṃ kaḥ svāmi-bhṛtyayoḥ saṅgrāmaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
balavantaṃ ripuṃ dṛṣṭvā kilātmānaṃ pragopayet |
children.translated_text: Seeing a powerful enemy, one should certainly conceal oneself;

children.text: balavadbhiś ca kartavyā śarac-candra-prakāśatā ||Panc_1.336||
children.translated_text: and against the powerful, one should maintain the transparency of the autumn moon. [Panc 1.336]

Hearing that, <s>Damanaka</s> thought to himself: 'This wicked one appears determined to fight. If perchance he strikes the master with his sharp horns, then great calamity will ensue. Therefore, I shall once more counsel him with my wit and arrange things so that he goes to another country.' And he said: 'O friend! Well spoken by you. But what kind of battle is there between master and servant?' And it is said —

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: śatror vikramam ajñātvā vairam ārabhate hi yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who begins a war without knowing the enemy's prowess

children.text: sa parābhavam āpnoti samudraṣ ṭiṭṭibhād yathā ||Panc_1.337||
children.translated_text: meets with defeat, as did the ocean from the <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> (lapwing). [Panc 1.337]

children.text: sañjīvaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjīvaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 12
ṭiṭṭibha-dampatī-kathā
children.translated_text: He narrated — Story 12: The tale of the <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> couple.

children.text: kasmiṃścit samudraika-deśe ṭiṭṭibha-dampatī vasataḥ | tato gacchati kāla ṛtu-samayam āsādya ṭiṭṭibhī garbham ādhatta | āsanna-prasavā satī sā ṭiṭṭibham ūce-bhoḥ kānta ! mama prasava-samayo vartate | tad vicintyatāṃ kim api nirupadravaṃ sthānaṃ yena tatrāham aṇḍaka-mokṣaṇaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: In a certain part of the ocean shore, a <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> (lapwing) couple dwelt. Then, as time passed, having reached the breeding season, the female <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> conceived. When she was near delivery, she said to the male <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s>: 'Dear husband! My time of delivery is at hand. Therefore, find some safe place where I may lay my eggs.'

children.text: ṭiṭṭibhaḥ prāha-bhadre ramyo 'yaṃ samudra-pradeśaḥ | tad atraiva prasavaḥ kāryaḥ |
children.translated_text: The male <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: 'Dear wife, this ocean shore is delightful. So let the delivery take place right here.'

children.text: sā prāha-atra pūrṇimā-dine samudra-velā carati | sā matta-gajendrān api samākarṣati | tad dūram anyatra kiṃcit sthānam anviṣyatām |
children.translated_text: She said: Here, on the full-moon day, the ocean-tide rises. It drags away even intoxicated great elephants. Therefore let some other place far away be sought.

children.text: tac chrutvā vihasya ṭiṭṭibha āha-bhadre na yuktam uktaṃ bhavatyā | kā mātrā samudrasya yā mama dūṣayiṣyati prasūtim | kiṃ na śrutaṃ bhavatyā-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> (lapwing) laughed and said: Good wife, what you have said is not proper. What is the measure of the ocean that it would destroy my offspring? Have you not heard —

children.text: baddhvāmbara-cara-mārgaṃ vyapagata-dhūmaṃ sadā mahad bhayadam |
children.translated_text: Having blocked the path of those who move in the sky, smokeless, always greatly fearsome —

children.text: manda-matiḥ kaḥ praviśati hutāśanaṃ svecchayā manujaḥ ||Panc_1.338||
children.translated_text: what foolish man enters fire of his own will? ||Panc_1.338||

children.text: mattebha-kumbha-vidalana-kṛta-śramaṃ suptam antaka-pratimam |
children.translated_text: Wearied from splitting the frontal globes of intoxicated elephants, sleeping, resembling Death himself —

children.text: yama-loka-darśanecchuḥ siṃhaḥ bodhayati ko nāma ||Panc_1.339||
children.translated_text: who indeed, desiring to see the abode of <s>Yama</s>, awakens a lion? ||Panc_1.339||

children.text: ko gatvā yama-sadanaṃ svayam antakam ādiśaty ajāta-bhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Who, going to the abode of <s>Yama</s>, would himself challenge Death without any fear [saying:]

children.text: prāṇān apahara matto yadi śaktiḥ kācid asti tava ||Panc_1.340||
children.translated_text: 'Snatch away my life-breaths if you have any power!' ||Panc_1.340||

children.text: prāleya-leśa-miśre maruti prābhātike ca vāti jaḍe |
children.translated_text: When the early morning wind blows, chilling, mixed with traces of frost —

children.text: guṇa-doṣa-jñaḥ puruṣo jalena kaḥ śītam apanayati ||Panc_1.341||
children.translated_text: what man who knows merits and faults would dispel cold with water? ||Panc_1.341||

children.text: tasmād viśrabdhātraiva garbhaṃ muñca | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore, being at ease, lay your eggs right here. And it is said —

children.text: yaḥ parābhava-santrastaḥ sva-sthānaṃ santyajen naraḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, terrified of defeat, would abandon his own place —

children.text: tena cet putriṇī mātā tad vandhyā kena kathyate ||Panc_1.342||
children.translated_text: if his mother bore children through him, by what [right] is she called barren? ||Panc_1.342||

children.text: tac chrutvā samudraś cintayām āsa-aho garvaḥ pakṣi-kīṭasyāsya | atha vā sādhv idam ucyate-
utkṣipya ṭiṭṭibhaḥ pādāv āste bha gabhayād divaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> raises its feet upward and stays, from fear of the sky [falling] —

children.text: sva-citta-kalpito garvaḥ kasya nātrāpi vidyate ||Panc_1.343||
children.translated_text: pride imagined by one's own mind — in whom does it not exist here? ||Panc_1.343||
Hearing that, the ocean thought: Ah, what pride this bird-insect has! But then, this is well said —

children.text: tan mayāsya pramāṇaṃ kutūhalād api draṣṭavyam | kiṃ mamaiṣo 'ṇḍāpahāre kṛte kariṣyati | iti cintayitvā sthitaḥ | atha prasavānantaraṃ prāṇayātrārthaṃ gatāyāṣ ṭiṭṭibhyāḥ samudro velāvyājenāṇḍāny apajahāra | athāyātā sā ṭiṭṭibhī prasavasthānaṃ śūnyam avalokya pralapantī ṭiṭṭibham ūce-bho mūrkha ! kathitam āsīn mayā te yat samudravelayā aṇḍānāṃ vināśo bhaviṣyati tad dūrataraṃ vrajāvaḥ paraṃ mūḍhatayāhaṃkāram āśritya mama vacanaṃ na karoṣi | athavā sādhv idam ucyate |
children.translated_text: So I must see his measure, even out of curiosity. What will he do to me when I have stolen his eggs? Having thought thus, he remained [waiting]. Then, after she had laid her eggs and gone away for the purpose of obtaining food, the ocean, under the pretext of the tide, stole away the eggs. Then the <s>Ṭiṭṭibhī</s> (female lapwing), having returned and seeing the nesting place empty, lamenting, said to the <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s>: O fool! I had told you that the eggs would be destroyed by the ocean-tide, that we should go far away. But in your stupidity, clinging to pride, you did not heed my words. But then, this is well said:

children.text: suhṛdāṃ hitakāmānāṃ na karotīha yo vacaḥ | sa kūrma iva durbuddhiḥ kāṣṭhād bhraṣṭo vinaśyati ||Panc_1.344||
children.translated_text: He who does not heed the words of well-wishing friends — that turtle of evil understanding, having fallen from the stick, perishes. ||Panc_1.344||

children.text:
ṭiṭṭibha āha-katham etat ?
sābravīt-
children.translated_text:
The <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: How is that?
She said —

children.text:
kathā 13
kambugrīvākhya-kūrma-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 13
The Story of the Turtle Named <s>Kambugrīva</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścij jalāśaye kambu-grīvo nāma kacchapaḥ | tasya ca saṅkaṭa-vikaṭa-nāmnī mitre haṃsa-jātīye parama-sneha-koṭim āśrite nityam eva saras-tīram āsādya tena sahāneka-devarṣi-maharṣīṇāṃ kathāḥ kṛtvāsta-maya-velāyāṃ sva-nīḍā-saṃśrayaṃ kurutaḥ | atha gacchatā kālenāvṛṣṭi-vaśāt saraḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ śoṣam agamat | tatas tad-duḥkha-duḥkhitau tāv ūcatuḥ-bho mitra ! jambāla-śeṣam etat-saraḥ sañjātam | tat kathaṃ bhavān bhaviṣyatīti vyākulatvaṃ no hṛdi vartate |
children.translated_text: In a certain lake there lived a turtle named <s>Kambugrīva</s> (conch-necked). And he had two friends of the swan species named <s>Saṅkaṭa</s> and <s>Vikaṭa</s>, who had reached the highest limit of affection. They would always come to the shore of the lake and, having discussed the tales of many divine sages and great sages together with him, at the time of sunset they would go to their own nests. Then, as time passed, due to drought the lake gradually dried up. Thereupon those two, grieved by his grief, said: Dear friend! This lake has been reduced to mere mud. So how you will survive — this anxiety dwells in our hearts.

children.text: tac chrutvā kambugrīva āha-bhoḥ, sāmprataṃ nāsty asmākaṃ jīvitavyaṃ jalābhāvāt | tathāpy upāyaś cintyatām iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kambugrīva</s> said: Friends, now there is no means of living for us due to the absence of water. Nevertheless, let a plan be devised. And it is said —

children.text: tyājyaṃ na dhairyaṃ vidhure'pi kāle
children.translated_text: Courage should not be abandoned even in times of adversity;

children.text: dhairyāt kadācid gatim āpnuyāt saḥ |
children.translated_text: through courage one may sometimes find a way.

children.text: yathā samudre'pi ca pota-bhaṅge
children.translated_text: Just as even when the ship has broken in mid-ocean,

children.text: sāṃyātriko vāñchati tartum eva ||Panc_1.345||
children.translated_text: the voyager desires only to cross. ||Panc_1.345||

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: mitrārthe bāndhavārthe ca buddhimān yatate sadā |
children.translated_text: For the sake of friends and kinsmen, the wise one always strives;

children.text: jātāsv āpatsu yatnena jagādedaṃ vaco manuḥ ||Panc_1.346||
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> declared this word: that one should make effort when calamities arise. ||Panc_1.346||

children.text: tad ānīyatāṃ kācid dṛḍha-rajjur laghu-kāṣṭhaṃ vā | anviṣyatāṃ ca prabhūta-jala-sanāthaṃ saraḥ, yena mayā madhya-pradeśe dantair gṛhīte sati yuvāṃ koṭi-bhāgayos tat-kāṣṭhaṃ mayā sahitaṃ saṅgṛhya tat-saro nayathaḥ |
children.translated_text: So let some strong rope or a light stick be brought. And let a lake endowed with abundant water be sought, so that when I hold the middle portion with my teeth, you two, grasping that stick at its two ends together with me, may carry me to that lake.

children.text: tāv ūcatuḥ-bho mitra ! evaṃ kariṣyāvaḥ | paraṃ bhavatā mauna-vratena sthātavyam | no cet tava kāṣṭhāt pāto bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Those two said: Dear friend! We shall do so. But you must maintain a vow of silence. Otherwise you will fall from the stick.

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite gacchatā kambugrīveṇādhobhāga-vyavasthitaṃ kiṃcit puram ālokitam | tatra ye paurās te tathā nīyamānaṃ vilokya savismayam idam ūcuḥ-aho cakrākāraṃ kim api pakṣibhyāṃ nīyate | paśyata paśyata |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, as <s>Kambugrīva</s> was being carried, he observed a certain town situated below. There, the townspeople, seeing him being carried thus, said with wonder: Oh! Something wheel-shaped is being carried by two birds. Look, look!

children.text: atha teṣāṃ kolāhalam ākarṇya kambugrīva āha-bhoḥ ! kim eṣa kolāhalaḥ ? iti vaktu-manā ardhokte patitaḥ pauraiḥ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-suhṛdāṃ hita-kāmānām iti | tathā ca-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing their commotion, <s>Kambugrīva</s> said: 'Friends! What is this commotion?' — wishing to say [this], at the half-utterance he fell, and was cut to pieces by the townspeople. Therefore I say: 'He who does not heed the words of well-wishing friends...' And further —

children.text: anāgata-vidhātā ca pratyutpanna-matis tathā |
children.translated_text: The one who provides against the future and the one of ready wit —

children.text: dvāv etau sukham edhete yad-bhaviṣyo vinaśyati ||Panc_1.347||
children.translated_text: these two prosper happily; the one [who says] 'whatever will be' perishes. ||Panc_1.347||

children.text: ṭiṭṭibha āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
sābravīt-
kathā 14
anāgata-vidhātādi-matsya-traya-kathā
children.translated_text:
She said —
Tale 14
The Story of the Three Fish: Provider-against-the-future and Others

children.text: kasmiṃścij jalāśaye'nāgata-vidhātā pratyutpanna-matir yad-bhaviṣyaś ceti trayo matsyāḥ santi | atha kadācit taṃ jalāśayaṃ dṛṣṭvā gacchadbhir matsya-jīvibhir uktam-yad aho bahu-matsyo 'yaṃ hradaḥ | kadācid api nāsmābhir anveṣitaḥ | tad adya tāvad āhāra-vṛttiḥ sañjātā | sandhyā-samayaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | tataḥ prabhāte'trāgantavyam iti niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain lake there were three fish named <s>Anāgata-vidhātā</s> (provider-against-the-future), <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s> (of ready wit), and <s>Yad-bhaviṣya</s> (whatever-will-be). Now once, fishermen passing by and seeing that lake said: Ah, this lake has many fish! We have never explored it. So today at least a livelihood has been found. And evening has arrived. Therefore let us resolve to come here at dawn.

children.text: atas teṣāṃ tat-kuliśa-pātopamaṃ vacaḥ samākarṇyānāgata-vidhātā sarvān matsyān āhūyedam ūce-aho, śrutaṃ bhavadbhir yan matsya-jīvibhir abhihitam | tad rātrāv api gamyatāṃ kiñcin nikaṭaṃ saraḥ | uktaṃ ca-
