children.translated_text: Then, hearing their words like a thunderbolt-fall, <s>Anāgata-vidhātā</s> summoned all the fish and said: Ah, you have heard what the fishermen said. So let us go even at night to some nearby lake. And it is said —

children.text: aśaktair balinaḥ śatroḥ kartavyaṃ prapalāyanam |
children.translated_text: Those unable [to fight] should flee from a powerful enemy;

children.text: saṃśritavyo 'thavā durgo nānyā teṣāṃ gatir bhavet ||Panc_1.348||
children.translated_text: or they should take refuge in a fortress — there is no other course for them. ||Panc_1.348||

children.text: tan nūnaṃ prabhāta-samaye matsya-jīvino 'tra samāgamya matsya-saṅkṣayaṃ kariṣyanti | etan mama manasi vartate | tan na yuktaṃ sāmprataṃ kṣaṇam apy atrāvasthātum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Surely at dawn the fishermen will come here and cause the destruction of the fish. This is what is in my mind. So it is not proper to remain here even for a moment now. And it is said —

children.text: vidyamānā gatir yeṣām anyatrāpi sukhāvahā |
children.translated_text: Those who have a path available elsewhere that brings happiness —

children.text: te na paśyanti vidvāṃso deha-bhaṅgaṃ kula-kṣayam ||Panc_1.349||
children.translated_text: those wise ones do not witness the destruction of the body and the ruin of the family. ||Panc_1.349||

children.text: tad ākarṇya pratyutpanna-matiḥ prāha-aho satyam abhihitaṃ bhavatā | mamāpy abhīṣṭam etat | tad anyatra gamyatām iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s> said: Ah, what you have said is true. This is my wish too. So let us go elsewhere. And it is said —

children.text: para-deśa-bhayāt bhītā bahu-māyā napuṃsakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Afraid of foreign lands, full of deceit, cowardly —

children.text: sva-deśe nidhanaṃ yānti kākāḥ kāpuruṣā mṛgāḥ ||Panc_1.350||
children.translated_text: crows, cowards, and deer meet their death in their own land. ||Panc_1.350||

children.text: yasyāsti sarvatra gatiḥ sa kasmāt
children.translated_text: He who has passage everywhere — why should he

children.text: sva-deśa-rāgeṇa hi yāti nāśam |
children.translated_text: go to destruction through attachment to his own land?

children.text: tātasya kūpo 'yam iti bruvāṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Saying 'this is our father's well,'

children.text: kṣāra-jalaṃ kāpuruṣāḥ pibanti ||Panc_1.351||
children.translated_text: cowards drink brackish water. ||Panc_1.351||

children.text: atha tat samākarṇya proccair vihasya yad-bhaviṣyaḥ provāca-aho, na bhavadbhyāṃ mantritaṃ samyag etad iti, yataḥ kiṃ vāṅ-mātreṇāpi teṣāṃ pitṛ-paitāmahikam etat saras tyaktuṃ yujyate | yady āyuḥ-kṣayo 'sti tad anyatra gatānām api mṛtyur bhaviṣyaty eva | uktaṃ ca-
arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati daiva-rakṣitaṃ
children.translated_text: That which is unprotected stands protected by fate;

children.text: surakṣitaṃ daiva-hataṃ vinaśyati |
children.translated_text: that which is well-protected, struck by fate, perishes.

children.text: jīvaty anātho 'pi vane visarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even an orphan abandoned in the forest lives;

children.text: kṛta-prayatno 'pi gṛhe na jīvati ||Panc_1.352||
children.translated_text: even one with every effort made does not live at home. ||Panc_1.352||

Then, hearing that, <s>Yad-bhaviṣya</s> laughed aloud and said: Ah, what you two have counseled is not right, because — is it proper to abandon this ancestral lake by mere words alone? If one's lifespan is exhausted, death will come even to those who have gone elsewhere. And it is said —

children.text: tad ahaṃ na yāsyāmi bhavadbhyāṃ ca yat pratibhāti tat kartavyam |
children.translated_text: So I shall not go. And you two may do whatever seems right to you.

children.text: atha tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvānāgata-vidhātā pratyutpanna-matiś ca niṣkrānau saha parijanena | atha prabhāte tair matsya-jīvibhir jālais taj jalāśayam āloḍya yad-bhaviṣyeṇa saha tat-saro nirmatsyatāṃ nītam | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-anāgata-vidhātā ceti |
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his resolve, <s>Anāgata-vidhātā</s> and <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s> departed together with their attendants. Then at dawn, those fishermen, having churned that lake with nets, brought it to a fishless state along with <s>Yad-bhaviṣya</s>. Therefore I say: 'The one who provides against the future...'

children.text: tac chrutvā ṭiṭṭibha āha-bhadre, kiṃ māṃ yadbhaviṣya-sadṛśaṃ sambhāvayasi | tat paśya me buddhi-prabhāvaṃ yāvad enaṃ duṣṭa-samudraṃ sva-cañcvā śoṣayāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: Good wife, do you consider me like <s>Yad-bhaviṣya</s>? Then behold the power of my intelligence — I shall dry up this wicked ocean with my own beak!

children.text: ṭiṭṭibhy āha-aho kas te samudreṇa saha vigrahaḥ | tan na yuktam asyopari kopaṃ kartum | uktaṃ ca-
puṃsām asamarthānām upadravāyātmano bhavet kopaḥ |
children.translated_text: For incapable men, anger becomes a source of harm to themselves;

children.text: piṭharaṃ jvalad-atimātraṃ nija-pārśvān eva dahatitarām ||Panc_1.353||
children.translated_text: a pot burning excessively scorches its own sides all the more. ||Panc_1.353||
The <s>Ṭiṭṭibhī</s> said: O dear husband! What quarrel do you have with the ocean? So it is not proper to be angry at it. And it is said —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: aviditvātmanaḥ śaktiṃ parasya na samutsukaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without knowing one's own strength, one should not be eager against another;

children.text: gacchann abhimukho vahnau nāśaṃ yāti pataṅgavat ||Panc_1.354||
children.translated_text: going face-to-face with fire, one perishes like a moth. ||Panc_1.354||

children.text: ṭiṭṭibha āha-priye, mā maivaṃ vada | yeṣām utsāha-śaktir bhavati te svalpā api gurūn vikramante | uktaṃ ca-
viśeṣāt paripūrṇasya yāti śatror amarṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Against an enemy who is especially full, the wrathful one

children.text: ābhimukhyaṃ śaśāṅkasya yathādyāpi vidhuntudaḥ ||Panc_1.355||
children.translated_text: advances face-to-face — just as <s>Rāhu</s> [does] against the moon even today. ||Panc_1.355||
The <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: Beloved, do not speak thus! Those who have the power of determination — even if small — overpower the great. And it is said —

children.text:
tathā ca-
pramāṇād adhikasyāpi gaṇḍa-śyāma-mada-cyuteḥ | padaṃ mūrdhni samādhatte kesarī matta-dantinaḥ ||Panc_1.356||
children.translated_text:
And likewise —
Even of a rutting elephant, dark ichor flowing from its temples, beyond [normal] measure — the lion places its foot upon its head. ||Panc_1.356||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: bālasyāpi raveḥ pādāḥ patanty upari bhūbhṛtām |
children.translated_text: Even of the young sun, the rays fall upon the tops of mountains;

children.text: tejasā saha jātānāṃ vayaḥ kutropayujyate ||Panc_1.357||
children.translated_text: for those born with splendor, of what use is age? ||Panc_1.357||

children.text: hastau sthūlataraḥ sa cāṅkuśa-vaśaḥ kiṃ hasti-mātro 'ṅkuśo
children.translated_text: The elephant is massive, yet it is under the power of the goad — is the goad as large as an elephant?

children.text: dīpe prajvalite praṇaśyati tamaḥ kiṃ dīpa-mātraṃ tamaḥ |
children.translated_text: When a lamp is lit, darkness perishes — is the darkness as large as a lamp?

children.text: vajreṇāpi hatāḥ patanti girayaḥ kiṃ vajra-mātro giris
children.translated_text: Even mountains fall when struck by the thunderbolt — is the mountain as large as the thunderbolt?

children.text: tejo yasya virājate sa balavān sthūleṣu kaḥ pratyayaḥ ||Panc_1.358||
children.translated_text: He in whom splendor shines is powerful — what reliance is there on bulk? ||Panc_1.358||

children.text: tad anayā cañcvāsya sakalaṃ toyaṃ śuṣka-sthalatāṃ nayāmi |
children.translated_text: So with this beak I shall reduce all its water to dry land!

children.text: ṭiṭṭibhy āha-bhoḥ kānta ! yatra jāhnavī nava-nadī-śatāni gṛhītvā nityam eva praviśati, tathā sindhuś ca | tat kathaṃ tvam aṣṭādaśa-nadī-śataiḥ pūryamāṇaṃ taṃ vipruṣa-vāhinyā cañcvā śoṣayiṣyasi ? tat kim aśraddho yenoktena |
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṭiṭṭibhī</s> said: O dear husband! Where the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges), taking nine hundred rivers with her, enters constantly, and likewise the <s>Sindhu</s> — how then will you, with your beak carrying mere drops, dry up [the ocean] that is being filled by eighteen hundred rivers? So why are you not persuaded by what has been said?

children.text: ṭiṭṭibha āha-priye !
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: Beloved!

children.text: anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlaṃ cañcur me loha-sannibhā |
children.translated_text: Perseverance is the root of prosperity; my beak is like iron;

children.text: aho-rātrāṇi dīrghāṇi samudraḥ kiṃ na śuṣyati ||Panc_1.359||
children.translated_text: the days and nights are long — will the ocean not dry up? ||Panc_1.359||

children.text: duradhigamaḥ para-bhāgo yāvat puruṣeṇa pauruṣaṃ na kṛtam |
children.translated_text: The portion belonging to another is hard to obtain so long as a man has not exerted his manliness;

children.text: jayati tulām adhirūḍho bhāsvān api jalada-paṭalāni ||Panc_1.360||
children.translated_text: the sun, having ascended the scale, conquers even masses of clouds. ||Panc_1.360||

children.text: ṭiṭṭibhy āha-yadi tvayāvaśyaṃ samudreṇa saha vigrahānuṣṭhānaṃ kāryam | tad anyān api vihaṅgamān āhūya suhṛj-jana-sahita evaṃ samācara | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṭiṭṭibhī</s> said: If you must necessarily undertake a conflict with the ocean, then summon other birds too and, accompanied by friendly folk, act thus. And it is said —

children.text: bahūnām apy asārāṇāṃ samvāyo hi durjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even of many worthless things, the combination is hard to overcome;

children.text: tṛṇair āveṣṭyate rajjur yathā nāgo 'pi baddhyate ||Panc_1.361||
children.translated_text: a rope is wound from grass-blades, and by it even an elephant is bound. ||Panc_1.361||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: caṭakākāṣṭha-kūṭena makṣikā-dardurais tathā |
children.translated_text: By a sparrow, a woodpecker, flies, and frogs —

children.text: mahājana-virodhena kuñjaraḥ pralayaṃ gataḥ ||Panc_1.362||
children.translated_text: through conflict with a multitude, an elephant met its destruction. ||Panc_1.362||

children.text: ṭiṭṭibha āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṭiṭṭibha</s> said: How is that?

children.text: sā prāha-
children.translated_text: She said —

children.text:
kathā 15
kuñjara-caṭaka-dampatī-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 15
The Story of the Elephant and the Sparrow Couple

children.text: kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe caṭaka-dampatī tamāla-taru-kṛta-nilayau prativasataḥ sma | atha tayor gacchatā kālena santatir abhavat | anyasminn ahani pramatto vana-gajaḥ kaścit taṃ tamāla-vṛkṣaṃ gharmārtaś chāyārthī samāśritaḥ | tato madotkaṛṣāt tāṃ tasya śākhāṃ caṭakāśritāṃ puṣkarāgreṇākṛṣya babhañja | tasyā bhaṅgena caṭakāṇḍāni sarvāṇi viśīrṇāni | āyuḥ-śeṣatayā ca caṭakau katham api prāṇair na viyuktau |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest tract, a pair of sparrows had made their nest in a <s>tamāla</s> tree and lived there. Then, as time passed, they produced offspring. On another day, a reckless forest elephant, tormented by heat and seeking shade, took shelter under that <s>tamāla</s> tree. Then, from the excess of his rut, he seized with the tip of his trunk the branch on which the sparrows had [nested] and broke it. By its breaking, all the sparrow's eggs were shattered. But by the residue of their lifespan, the sparrow couple somehow did not lose their lives.

children.text: atha caṭakā sāṇḍa-bhaṅgābhibhūtā pralāpān kurvāṇā na kiñcit sukham āsasāda | atrāntare tasyās tān pralāpān śrutvā kāṣṭha-kūṭo nāma pakṣī tasyāḥ parama-suhṛt-tad-duḥkha-duḥkhito 'bhyetya tām uvāca-bhagavati ! kiṃ vṛthā pralāpena | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then the female sparrow, overwhelmed by the destruction of her eggs, lamenting, found no comfort whatsoever. In the meantime, a bird named <s>Kāṣṭhakūṭa</s> (Woodpecker), her closest friend, having heard her lamentations, afflicted by her sorrow, approached and said to her: 'Good lady! What is the use of vain lamentation? And it is said:'

children.text: naṣṭaṃ mṛtam atikrāntaṃ nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise do not grieve over what is lost, what is dead, or what is past;

children.text: paṇḍitānāṃ ca mūrkhāṇāṃ viśeṣo 'yaṃ yataḥ smṛtaḥ ||Panc_1.363||
children.translated_text: this is considered the distinction between the wise and the foolish. ||Panc_1.363||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: aśocyānīha bhūtāni yo mūḍhas tāni śocati |
children.translated_text: The fool who grieves over beings that are not to be grieved for in this world,

children.text: tad-duḥkhāl labhate duḥkhaṃ dvāv anarthau niṣevate ||Panc_1.364||
children.translated_text: from that sorrow he gains [further] sorrow — he cultivates two misfortunes. ||Panc_1.364||

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover:

children.text: śleṣmāśru bāndhavair muktaṃ preto bhuṅkte yato 'vaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Since the departed one helplessly consumes the tears and mucus shed by relatives,

children.text: tasmān na roditavyaṃ hi kriyāḥ kāryāś ca śaktitaḥ ||Panc_1.365||
children.translated_text: therefore one should not weep; rather, the [funeral] rites should be performed according to one's ability. ||Panc_1.365||

children.text: caṭakā prāha-astv etat | paraṃ duṣṭa-gajena madān mama santāna-kṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ | tad yadi mama tvaṃ suhṛt-satyas tad asya gajāpasadasya ko 'pi vadhopāyaś cintyatām | yasyānuṣṭhānena me santati-nāśa-duḥkham apasarati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The female sparrow said: 'Let that be so. But the wicked elephant, out of rut, has caused the destruction of my progeny. So if you are a true friend to me, then let some means of killing this vile elephant be devised — by the performance of which my grief at the loss of offspring will depart.' And it is said:

children.text: āpadi yenopakṛtaṃ yena ca hasitaṃ daśāsu viṣamāsu |
children.translated_text: He who helps in adversity, and he who laughs [with one] in difficult situations —

children.text: upakṛtya tayor ubhayoḥ punar api jātaṃ naraṃ manye ||Panc_1.366||
children.translated_text: having done good to both of them, I consider [one] truly born among men. ||Panc_1.366||

children.text: kāṣṭha-kūṭa āha-bhagavati, satyam abhihitaṃ bhavatyā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṣṭhakūṭa</s> (Woodpecker) said: 'Good lady, what you have said is true.' And it is said:

children.text: sa suhṛd-vyasane yaḥ syād anya-jāty-udbhavo 'pi san |
children.translated_text: He is a [true] friend who is present in calamity, even though born of another species;

children.text: vṛddhau sarvo 'pi mitraṃ syāt sarveṣām eva dehinām ||Panc_1.367||
children.translated_text: in prosperity, everyone becomes a friend — of all embodied beings. ||Panc_1.367||

children.text: sa suhṛd-vyasane yaḥ syāt sa putro yas tu bhaktimān |
children.translated_text: He is a [true] friend who is present in calamity; he is a [true] son who is devoted;

children.text: sa bhṛtyo yo vidheyajñaḥ sā bhāryā yatra nirvṛtiḥ ||Panc_1.368||
children.translated_text: he is a [true] servant who knows obedience; she is a [true] wife in whom there is contentment. ||Panc_1.368||

children.text: tat paśya me buddhi-prabhāvam | paraṃ mamāpi suhṛd-bhūtā vīṇāravā nāma makṣikāsti | tat tām āhūyāgacchāmi, yena sa durātmā duṣṭa-gajo badhyate |
children.translated_text: Then see the power of my intellect. Moreover, I have a dear friend, a fly named <s>Vīṇāravā</s>. Let me summon her and come [back], so that that evil, wicked elephant may be slain.'

children.text: athāsau caṭakayā saha makṣikām āsādya provāca-bhadre, mameṣṭeyaṃ caṭakā kenacid duṣṭa-gajena parābhūtāṇḍa-sphoṭanena | tat tasya vadhopāyam anutiṣṭhato me sāhāyyaṃ kartum arhasi |
children.translated_text: Then he [the Woodpecker], together with the female sparrow, went to the fly and said: 'Dear friend, this beloved female sparrow of mine has been humiliated by a certain wicked elephant who shattered her eggs. So please help me in carrying out the means for his destruction.'

children.text: makṣikāpy āha-bhadra ! kim ucyate'tra viṣaye | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The fly too said: 'Dear friend! What is there to say in this matter?' And it is said:

children.text: punaḥ pratyupakārāya mitrāṇāṃ kriyate priyam |
children.translated_text: For the sake of reciprocal benefit, one does something pleasing for friends;

children.text: yat punar mitra-mitrasya kāryaṃ mitrair na kiṃ kṛtam ||Panc_1.369||
children.translated_text: and what, moreover, would friends not do for a friend's friend? ||Panc_1.369||

children.text: satyam etat | paraṃ mamāpi bheko meghanādo nāma mitraṃ tiṣṭhati | tam apy āhūya yathocitaṃ kurmaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'This is true. But I too have a friend, a frog named <s>Meghanāda</s>. Let us summon him also and do what is fitting.' And it is said:

children.text: hitaiḥ sādhu-samācāraiḥ śāstrajñair mati-śālibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Strategies devised by the learned — those who know the <s>śāstras</s>, are wise, of good conduct, and helpful —

children.text: kathañcin na vikalpante vidvadbhiś cintitā nayāḥ ||Panc_1.370||
children.translated_text: are never in any way frustrated. ||Panc_1.370||

children.text: atha te trayo 'pi gatvā meghanādasyāgre samastaṃ vṛttāntaṃ nivedya tasthuḥ | atha sa provāca-kiyan mātro 'sau varāko gajo mahājanasya kupitasyāgre | tan madīyo mantraḥ kartavyaḥ | makṣike, tvaṃ gatvā madhyāhna-samaye tasya madoddhatasya gajasya karṇe vīṇā-rava-sadṛśaṃ śabdaṃ kuru | yena śravaṇa-sukha-lālaso nimīlita-nayano bhavati | tataś ca kāṣṭha-kūṭa-cañcvā sphoṭita-nayano 'ndhībhūtas tṛṣārto mama garta-taṭāśritasya saparikarasya śabdaṃ śrutvā jalāśayaṃ matvā samabhyeti | tato gartam āsādya patiṣyati pañcatvaṃ yāsyati ceti | evaṃ samavāyaḥ kartavyo yathā vaira-sādhanaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: Then those three, having gone to <s>Meghanāda</s>'s presence, reported the entire matter and stood [waiting]. And he said: 'How insignificant is that wretched elephant before the assembled might [of us all]! Then let my plan be followed: <s>Makṣikā</s> (Fly), you go and at midday make a sound resembling that of a <s>vīṇā</s> in the ear of that rut-maddened elephant. Then, lulled by the pleasure of hearing, he will close his eyes. Thereupon, blinded by the Woodpecker's beak having pecked out his eyes, and parched with thirst, hearing the sound of me — stationed with my retinue at the edge of a pit — and thinking it a water-body, he will approach. Then, reaching the pit, he will fall in and perish.' Thus the coalition should be formed so that the means of vengeance is accomplished.

children.text: atha tathānuṣṭhite sa matta-gajo makṣikā-geya-sukhān nimīlita-netraḥ kāṣṭha-kūṭa-hṛta-cakṣur madhyāhna-samaye bhrāmyan maṇḍūka-śabdānusārī gacchan mahatīṃ gartam āsādya patito mṛtaś ca | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-caṭakā kāṣṭha-kūṭena iti |
children.translated_text: Then, when this was carried out, that rut-maddened elephant, his eyes closed from the pleasure of the fly's singing, his sight destroyed by the Woodpecker, wandering at midday, following the sound of the frog, went [forward] and, reaching a great pit, fell in and died. Therefore I say: 'The female sparrow, with the Woodpecker...' [and so on].

children.text: ṭiṭṭibha āha-bhadre, evaṃ bhavatu | suhṛd-varga-samudāyena saha samudraṃ śoṣayiṣyāmi | iti niścitya baka-sārasa-mayūrādīn samāhūya provāca-bhoḥ parābhūto 'haṃ samudreṇāṇḍakāpahareṇa | tac cintyatām asya śoṣaṇopāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The sandpiper said: 'Dear one, let it be so. Together with the assembly of friends, I shall dry up the ocean.' Having so resolved, he summoned the heron, crane, peacock, and others, and said: 'Sirs! I have been humiliated by the ocean, which stole my eggs. Therefore let a means of drying it up be devised.'

children.text: te sammantrya procuḥ-aśaktā vayaṃ samudra-śoṣaṇe | tat kiṃ vṛthā prayāsena | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: They, having consulted, said: 'We are incapable of drying up the ocean. So what is the use of vain effort?' And it is said:

children.text: abalaḥ pronnataṃ śatruṃ yo yāti mada-mohitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A weak one who, deluded by pride, goes to attack a mighty enemy,

children.text: yuddhārthaṃ sa nivarteta śīrṇa-danto yathā gajaḥ ||Panc_1.371||
children.translated_text: would return [defeated] from battle, like an elephant with broken tusks. ||Panc_1.371||

children.text: tad asmākaṃ svāmī vainateyo 'sti | tasmai sarvam etat-paribhava-sthānaṃ nivedyatām, yena svajāti-paribhava-kupito vairānṛṇyaṃ gacchati | athavātrāvalepaṃ kariṣyati tathāpi nāsti vo duḥkham | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'But our master is <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>). Let this entire cause of humiliation be reported to him, so that, angered at the humiliation of his own kind, he repays the enmity. Or, if he acts with arrogance in this matter, even then there is no sorrow for you.' And it is said:

children.text: suhṛdi nirantara-racite guṇavati bhṛtye'nuvartini kalatre |
children.translated_text: When a friend is constant and close, a servant is virtuous and obedient, a wife is devoted,

children.text: svāmini śakti-samete nivedya duḥkhaṃ sukhī bhavati ||Panc_1.372||
children.translated_text: and a master is endowed with power — having reported one's sorrow [to them], one becomes happy. ||Panc_1.372||

children.text: tad yāmo vinateya-sakāśaṃ yato 'sāv asmākaṃ svāmī |
children.translated_text: 'So let us go to <s>Vainateya</s>'s presence, since he is our lord.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite sarve te pakṣiṇo viṣaṇṇa-vadanā bāṣpa-pūrita-dṛśo vainateya-sakāśam āsādya karuṇa-svareṇa phūtkartum ārabdhāḥ-aho ! abrahmaṇyam abrahmaṇyam ! adhunā sadācārasya ṭiṭṭibhasya bhavati nāthe sati samudreṇāṇḍāny apahṛtāni tat-pranaṣṭam adhunā pakṣi-kulam | anye'pi svecchayā samudreṇa vyāpādiṣyante | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: When this was done, all those birds, with dejected faces and tear-filled eyes, reached <s>Vainateya</s>'s (<s>Garuḍa</s>'s) presence and began to cry out in piteous voices: 'Alas! Injustice! Injustice! Now, while the sandpiper of virtuous conduct has you as his protector, the ocean has stolen his eggs — and now the bird-race is lost! Others too will be destroyed by the ocean at will.' And it is said:

children.text: kva kasya karma saṃvīkṣya karoty anyo 'pi garhitam |
children.translated_text: Seeing the deeds of whom does another also commit reprehensible [acts]?

children.text: gatānugatiko loko na lokaḥ pāramārthikaḥ ||Panc_1.373||
children.translated_text: The world is a follower of followers — the world is not [guided by] ultimate truth. ||Panc_1.373||

children.text: cāṭu-taskara-durvṛttais tathā sāhasikādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Subjects tormented by flatterers, thieves, the wicked, the violent, and the like,

children.text: pīḍyamānāḥ prajā rakṣyāḥ kaṭūcchadmādibhis tathā ||Panc_1.374||
children.translated_text: as well as by the disguised and the harsh, must be protected [by the king]. ||Panc_1.374||

children.text: prajānāṃ dharma-ṣaḍ-bhāgo rājño bhavati rakṣituḥ |
children.translated_text: A sixth portion of the <s>dharma</s> of [his] subjects accrues to the king who protects [them];

children.text: adharmād api ṣaḍ-bhāgo jāyate yo na rakṣati ||Panc_1.375||
children.translated_text: a sixth portion of their sin is born to him who does not protect [them]. ||Panc_1.375||

children.text: prajā-pīḍana-santāpāt samudbhūto hutāśanaḥ |
children.translated_text: The fire that arises from the torment of oppressing subjects

children.text: rājñaḥ śriyaṃ kulaṃ prāṇān nādagdhvā vinivartate ||Panc_1.376||
children.translated_text: does not turn back without burning the king's prosperity, lineage, and life. ||Panc_1.376||

children.text: rājā bandhur abandhūnāṃ rājā cakṣur acakṣuṣām |
children.translated_text: The king is a kinsman to the kinless; the king is an eye to the eyeless;

children.text: rājā pitā ca mātā ca sarveṣāṃ nyāya-vartinām ||Panc_1.377||
children.translated_text: the king is both father and mother to all who follow righteousness. ||Panc_1.377||

children.text: phalārthī pārthivo lokān pālayed yatnam āsthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A king desiring fruit should protect his people with effort,

children.text: dāna-mānādi-toyena mālākāro 'ṅkurān iva ||Panc_1.378||
children.translated_text: as a gardener [tends] seedlings — with the water of gifts, honors, and the like. ||Panc_1.378||

children.text: yathā bījāṅkuraḥ sūkṣmaḥ pratnenābhirakṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as a tiny seed-sprout, carefully nurtured,

children.text: phala-prado bhavet kāle tadval lokaḥ surakṣitaḥ ||Panc_1.379||
children.translated_text: in time becomes fruit-bearing — so too a well-protected people. ||Panc_1.379||

children.text: hiraṇya-dhānya-ratnāni yānāni vividhāni ca |
children.translated_text: Gold, grain, jewels, various vehicles,

children.text: tathānyad api yat kiñcit prajābhyaḥ syān nṛpasya tat ||Panc_1.380||
children.translated_text: and whatever else there may be — all that comes to a king from [his] subjects. ||Panc_1.380||

children.text: athaivaṃ garuḍaḥ samākarṇya tad-duḥkha-duḥkhitaḥ kopāviṣṭaś ca vyacintayat-aho ! satyam uktam etaiḥ pakṣibhiḥ | tad adya gatvā taṃ samudraṃ śoṣayāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Garuḍa</s>, hearing this, afflicted by their sorrow and filled with anger, thought: 'Ah! What these birds have said is true. Then today let us go and dry up that ocean.'

children.text: evaṃ cintayatas tasya viṣṇu-dūtaḥ samāgatyāha-bho garutman ! bhagavatā nārāyaṇenāhaṃ tava pārśve preṣitaḥ | deva-kāryāya bhagavān amarāvatyāṃ yāsyatīti | tat satvaram āgamyatām |
children.translated_text: While he was thus thinking, a messenger of <s>Viṣṇu</s> arrived and said: 'O <s>Garutman</s>! I have been sent to your side by the blessed Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. The Lord will go to <s>Amarāvatī</s> for a task of the gods. So come quickly.'

children.text: tac chrutvā garuḍaḥ sābhimānaṃ prāha-bho dūta ! kiṃ mayā kubhṛtyena bhagavān kariṣyati | tad gatvā taṃ vada yad anyo bhṛtyo vāhanāysamat-sthāne kriyatām | madīyo namaskāro vācyo bhagavataḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Garuḍa</s> said with pride: 'O messenger! What will the Lord do with me — a bad servant? Go and tell him that another servant should be appointed in my place as vehicle. My salutations should be conveyed to the Lord.' And it is said:

children.text: yo na vetti guṇān yasya na taṃ seveta paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wise man should not serve one who does not know his merits;

children.text: na hi tasmāt phalaṃ kiñcit sukṛṣṭād ūṣarād iva ||Panc_1.381||
children.translated_text: for there is no fruit from that — like [none from] well-ploughed barren land. ||Panc_1.381||

children.text: dūta āha-bho vainateya ! kadācid api bhagavantaṃ prati tvayā naitad abhihitam īdṛk | tat kathaya, kiṃ te bhagavatāpamāna-sthānaṃ kṛtam ?
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'O <s>Vainateya</s>! Never before have you spoken thus to the Lord. So tell me, what offense has the Lord committed against you?'

children.text: garuḍa āha-bhagavad-āśraya-bhūtena samudreṇāsmaṭ ṭiṭṭibhāṇḍāny apahṛtāni | tad yadi nigrahaṃ na karoti tad ahaṃ bhagavato na bhṛtya ity eṣa niścayas tvayā vācyaḥ | tad drutataraṃ gatvā bhavatā bhagavataḥ samīpe vaktavyam |
children.translated_text: <s>Garuḍa</s> said: 'Our sandpiper's eggs have been stolen by the ocean, which is sheltered by the Lord. If he does not punish [the ocean], then I am not the Lord's servant — this is the resolution you should convey.' So go quickly and speak [this] in the Lord's presence.'

children.text: atha dūta-mukhena praṇaya-kupitaṃ vainateyaṃ vijñāya sammāna-puraḥsaraṃ tam ānayāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, learning through the messenger's mouth that <s>Vainateya</s> was angry with affection, [the Lord said]: 'Preceded by honor, I shall bring him [here].' And it is said:

children.text: bhaktaṃ śaktaṃ kulīnaṃ ca na bhṛtyam avamānayet |
children.translated_text: One should not disrespect a servant who is devoted, capable, and of good family;

children.text: putraval lālayen nityaṃ ya icchec chriyam ātmanaḥ ||Panc_1.382||
children.translated_text: one who desires one's own prosperity should always cherish him like a son. ||Panc_1.382||

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: rājā tuṣṭo 'pi bhṛtyānām artha-mātraṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: A king, even when pleased, gives servants only wealth;

children.text: te tu sammānitās tasya prāṇair apy upakurvate ||Panc_1.383||
children.translated_text: but they, when honored, serve him even with their lives. ||Panc_1.383||

children.text: ity evaṃ sampradhārya rukma-pure vainateya-sakāśaṃ satvaram agamat | vainateyo 'pi gṛhāgataṃ bhagavantam avalokya trapādhomukhaḥ praṇamyovāca-bhagavan ! tvad-āśrayonmattena samudreṇa mama bhṛtyāsyāṇḍāny apahṛtya mamāpamāno vihitaḥ | paraṃ bhagaval-lajjayā mayā vilambitam | no ced enam ahaṃ sthalāntaram adyaiva nayāmi | yataḥ svāmi-bhayāc chravaṇo 'pi prahāro na dīyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, [the Lord] went quickly to <s>Vainateya</s>'s presence in <s>Rukmapura</s> (the golden city). <s>Vainateya</s> too, seeing the Lord who had come to his home, bowing with face downcast in shame, said: 'Lord! The ocean, emboldened by your shelter, has stolen my servant-sandpiper's eggs and thereby shown me disrespect. But out of shame before the Lord, I had held back. Otherwise I would today itself have reduced him to dry land. For out of fear of the master, one does not strike even [one who deserves] a blow on the ear.' And it is said:

children.text: yena syāl laghutā vātha pīḍā citte prabhoḥ kvacit |
children.translated_text: That act by which the master would suffer any slight or pain in his mind —

children.text: prāṇa-tyāge'pi tat karma na kuryāt kula-sevakaḥ ||Panc_1.384||
children.translated_text: even at the cost of life, a hereditary servant should not do it. ||Panc_1.384||

children.text: tac chrutvā bhagavān āha-bho vainateya ! satyam abhihitaṃ bhavatā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the Lord said: 'O <s>Vainateya</s>! What you have said is true.' And it is said:

children.text: bhṛtyāparādhajo daṇḍaḥ svāmino jāyate yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Since punishment born of a servant's offense falls upon the master,

children.text: tena lajjāpi tasyotthā na bhṛtyasya tathā punaḥ ||Panc_1.385||
children.translated_text: therefore the shame arising from it is also his — not so much the servant's. ||Panc_1.385||

children.text: tad āgaccha yenāṇḍāni samudrād ādāya ṭiṭṭibhaṃ sambhāvayāvaḥ | amarāvatīṃ ca gacchāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'So come, let us take the eggs from the ocean, honor the sandpiper, and go to <s>Amarāvatī</s>.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite samudro bhagavatā nirbharsyāgneyaṃ śaraṃ sandhyāyābhihitaḥ-bho durātman ! dīyantāṃ ṭiṭṭibhāṇḍāni | no cet sthalatāṃ tvāṃ nayāmi |
children.translated_text: When this was done, the Lord, having rebuked the ocean, fitting the fiery arrow to [his bow], said: 'O wicked one! Return the sandpiper's eggs! Otherwise I shall reduce you to dry land.'

children.text: tataḥ samudreṇa sa-bhayena ṭiṭṭibhāṇḍāni tāni pradattāni | ṭiṭṭibhenāpi bhāryāyai samarpitāni | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-śatror balam avijñāya iti | tasmāt puruṣeṇodyamo na tyājyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thereupon the ocean, fearful, returned those sandpiper's eggs. And the sandpiper presented them to his wife. Therefore I say: 'Without knowing the enemy's strength...' [and so on]. Therefore a man should not abandon effort.

children.text: tad ākarṇya sañjīvakas tam eva bhūyo 'pi papraccha-bho mitra ! kathaṃ jñeyo mayāsau duṣṭa-buddhir iti | iyantaṃ kālaṃ yāvad uttarottara-snehena prasādena cāhaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ | na kadācit tad-vikṛtir dṛṣṭā | tat kathyatāṃ yenāham ātma-rakṣārthaṃ tad-vadhāyodyamaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, having heard that, asked him [<s>Damanaka</s>] yet again: 'O friend! How shall I recognize that he is of wicked intent? For so long a time, I have been treated with ever-increasing affection and grace. Never have I seen any change in him. So tell me, that I may make an effort to protect myself or to destroy him.'

children.text: damanaka āha-bhadra, kim atra jñeyam ? eṣa te pratyayaḥ | yadi rakta-netras triśikhāṃ bhrūkuṭiṃ dadhānaḥ sṛkkaṇī parilelihan tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavati, tad duṣṭa-buddhiḥ | anyathā suprasādaś ceti | tad ājñāpaya mām | svāśrayaṃ prati gacchāmi | tvayā ca yathāyaṃ mantra-bhedo na bhavati tathā kāryam | yadi niśāmukhaṃ prāpya gantuṃ śaknoṣi tad-deśa-tyāgaḥ kāryaḥ | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'Friend, what is there to know? This is the sign for you: if, with reddened eyes and a triple furrow on his brow, he licks his jaws upon seeing you — then his mind is hostile. Otherwise, he is well-disposed.' So command me — I shall return to my own place. And you must act so that this secret counsel is not breached. If, when night falls, you are able to leave, then you must abandon this territory. For:

children.text: tyajed ekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet |
children.translated_text: One should abandon one [person] for the sake of the family; a family for the sake of a village;

children.text: grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe svātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet ||Panc_1.386||
children.translated_text: a village for the sake of a country; and the whole earth for the sake of one's own self. // Panc_1.386 //

children.text: āpad-arthe dhanaṃ rakṣed dārān rakṣed dhanair api |
children.translated_text: One should protect one's wealth against calamity, and one's wife even at the cost of wealth;

children.text: ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣed dārair api dhanair api ||Panc_1.387||
children.translated_text: one should always protect oneself — even at the cost of wife and wealth. // Panc_1.387 //

children.text: balavatābhibhūtasya videśa-gamanaṃ tad-anupraveśo vā nītiḥ | tad-deśa-tyāgaḥ kāryaḥ | athavātmā sāmādibhir upāyair ābharakṣaṇīyaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: When overpowered by a stronger [foe], going to another country or entering [the enemy's service] is the policy. You must abandon this territory. Or else, one must protect oneself by means such as conciliation (<s>sāma</s>) and the like. And it is said:

children.text: api putra-kalatrair vā prāṇān rakṣeta paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wise man should protect his life even [at the cost of] his sons and wife;

children.text: vidyamānair yatas taiḥ syāt sarvaṃ bhūyo 'pi dehinām ||Panc_1.388||
children.translated_text: for when he is alive, all those can be obtained again by embodied beings. // Panc_1.388 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: yena kenāpy upāyena śubhenāpy aśubhena vā |
children.translated_text: By whatever means — whether auspicious or inauspicious —

children.text: uddhared dīnam ātmānaṃ samartho dharmam ācaret ||Panc_1.389||
children.translated_text: one should rescue one's wretched self; [only] when capable should one practice <s>dharma</s>. // Panc_1.389 //

children.text: yo māyāṃ kurute mūḍhaḥ prāṇa-tyāge dhanādiṣu |
children.translated_text: The fool who makes a pretense [of indifference] regarding the sacrifice of life, wealth, and the like —

children.text: tasya prāṇāḥ praṇaśyanti tair naṣṭair naṣṭam eva tat ||Panc_1.390||
children.translated_text: his very life-breaths perish; and when those are lost, all that [wealth etc.] is lost too. // Panc_1.390 //

children.text: evam abhidhāya damanakaḥ karaṭaka-sakāśam agamat | karaṭako 'pi tam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā provāca-bhadra ! kiṃ kṛtaṃ tatrabhavatā ?
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Damanaka</s> went to <s>Karaṭaka</s>. <s>Karaṭaka</s> too, seeing him approaching, said: 'Friend! What have you accomplished there?'

children.text: damanaka āha-mayā tāvan nīti-bīja-nirvāpaṇaṃ kṛtam | parato daiva-vihitāyattam | uktaṃ ca-
parāṅmukhe'pi daive'tra kṛtyaṃ kāryaṃ vipaścitā |
children.translated_text: Even when fate is turned away, a wise man should do what must be done —

children.text: ātma-doṣa-vināśāya sva-citta-stambhanāya ca ||Panc_1.391||
children.translated_text: for the destruction of his own faults and for the strengthening of his own resolve. // Panc_1.391 //
<s>Damanaka</s> said: 'I have sown the seed of statecraft. Hereafter, it depends on what fate ordains. And it is said:'

children.text: tathā ca-
udyoginaṃ puruṣa-siṃham upaiti lakṣmīr
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) approaches the lion among men who is industrious;

children.text: daivena deyam iti kāpuruṣā vadanti |
children.translated_text: 'What is to be given is by fate' — so say cowards.

children.text: daivaṃ nihatya kuru pauruṣam ātma-śaktyā yatne kṛte yadi na sidhyati ko 'tra doṣaḥ ||Panc_1.392||
children.translated_text: Strike down fate and exert your manhood by your own power! If, despite effort, success does not come — what fault is there in that? // Panc_1.392 //
And also:

children.text: karaṭaka āha-tat kathaya kīdṛk tvayā nīti-bījaṃ nirvāpitam |
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Then tell me — in what manner have you sown that seed of statecraft?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-mayānyonyaṃ tābhyāṃ mithyā-prajalpena bhedas tathā vihito yathā bhūyo 'pi mantrayantāv eka-sthāna-sthitau na drakṣyasi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'By means of false allegations spoken to each of them separately, I have created such a breach between those two that you shall never again see them conferring together in one place.'

children.text: karaṭaka āha-aho, na yuktaṃ bhavatā vihitaṃ yat parasparaṃ tau snehārdra-hṛdayau sukhāśrayau kopa-sāgare prakṣiptau | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'Alas! What you have done is not right — that those two, whose hearts are moist with mutual affection and who are each other's refuge of happiness, have been cast into an ocean of anger. And it is said:'

children.text: aviruddhaṃ sukha-sthaṃ yo duḥkha-mārge niyojayet |
children.translated_text: He who sets one who is at peace and unharmed upon the path of suffering —

children.text: janma-janmāntare duḥkhī sa naraḥ syād asaṃśayam ||Panc_1.393||
children.translated_text: that man shall be miserable through birth after birth, without a doubt. // Panc_1.393 //

children.text: aparaṃ tvaṃ yad bheda-mātreṇāpi hṛṣṭas tad apy ayuktam, yataḥ sarvato 'pi jano virūpa-karaṇe samartho bhavati nopakartum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, that you are pleased by mere division is also improper. For anyone at all is capable of causing harm, but not of conferring benefit. And it is said:'

children.text: ghātayitum eva nīcaḥ para-kāryaṃ vetti na prasādayitum |
children.translated_text: A base person knows how to destroy another's work, not how to please;

children.text: pātayitum asti śaktir vāyor vṛkṣaṃ na connamitum ||Panc_1.394||
children.translated_text: the wind has the power to topple a tree, but not to raise it up. // Panc_1.394 //

children.text: damanaka āha-anabhijño bhavān nīti-śāstrasya, tenaitad bravīṣi | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'You are ignorant of the science of statecraft — that is why you speak thus. For it is said:'

children.text: jāta-mātraṃ na yaḥ śatruṃ vyādhiṃ ca praśamaṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: He who does not quell an enemy or a disease at its very birth —

children.text: mahā-balo 'pi tenaiva vṛddhiṃ prāpya sa hanyate ||Panc_1.395||
children.translated_text: even though very powerful, is destroyed by that very [foe], which grows [unchecked]. // Panc_1.395 //

children.text: tac-chatru-bhūto 'yam asmākaṃ mantri-padāharaṇāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, this one is our enemy, because of his usurping the position of minister. And it is said:'

children.text: pitṛ-paitāmahaṃ sthānaṃ yo yasyātra jigīṣate |
children.translated_text: He who seeks to seize another's ancestral position —

children.text: sa tasya sahajaḥ śatrur ucchedyo 'pi priye sthitaḥ ||Panc_1.396||
children.translated_text: he is that one's natural enemy, to be destroyed even when established in favor. // Panc_1.396 //

children.text: tan mayā sa udāsīnatayā samānīto 'bhaya-pradānena yāvat tāvad aham api tena sācivyāt pracyāvitaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'By me he was brought here in good faith with a guarantee of safety, yet as soon as [he came] I was displaced from the ministership by him. Or rather, well is this said:'

children.text: dadyāt sādhur yadi nija-pade durjanāya praveśaṃ
children.translated_text: If a good man gives a villain entry into his own position,

children.text: tan-nāśāya prabhavati tato vāñchamānaḥ svayaṃ saḥ |
children.translated_text: that [villain] then works toward his [benefactor's] destruction, desiring [the position] for himself.

children.text: tasmād deyo vipula-matibhir nāvakāśo 'dhamānāṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise should give no opportunity to the base;

children.text: jārāpi syād gṛha-patir iti śrūyate vākyato 'tra ||Panc_1.397||
children.translated_text: for it is heard in the saying: 'even a paramour becomes the householder.' // Panc_1.397 //

children.text: tena mayā tasyopari vadhopāya eva viracyate | deśa-tyāgāya vā bhaviṣyati | tac ca tvāṃ muktvānyo na jñāsyati | tad uktam etat te svārthāyānuṣṭhitam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore a plan for his killing is being devised by me. Or else he will [be forced to] abandon the territory. And no one other than you shall know this. What I have done has been done for your benefit as well. And it is said:'

children.text: nistriṃśaṃ hṛdayaṃ kṛtvā vāṇīm ikṣu-rasopāmām |
children.translated_text: Making the heart a sword and one's speech sweet as sugarcane-juice,

children.text: vikalpo 'tra na kartavyo hanyāt tatrāpakāriṇam ||Panc_1.398||
children.translated_text: one should not hesitate here — one should slay the one who does harm. // Panc_1.398 //

children.text: aparaṃ mṛto 'py asmākaṃ bhojyo bhaviṣyati | tad ekaṃ tāvad vara-sādhanam | aparaṃ sācivyaṃ ca bhaviṣyati tṛptiś ceti | tad-guṇa-traye'sminn upasthite kasmān māṃ dūṣayasi tvaṃ jāḍya-bhāvāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, even dead, he will be food for us. So that is one excellent gain. The second is that the ministership will be ours, and the third is satisfaction. When these three advantages are at hand, why do you blame me out of dullness? And it is said:'

children.text: parasya pīḍanaṃ kurvan svārtha-siddhiṃ ca paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wise man who inflicts harm on another while achieving his own purpose —

children.text: mūḍha-buddhir na bhakṣeta vane caturako yathā ||Panc_1.399||
children.translated_text: the fool should not [dare to] consume [such a person], just as in the forest [the story of] <s>Caturaka</s> [illustrates]. // Panc_1.399 //

children.text: karaṭaka āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṭaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 16
vajra-daṃṣṭra-nāma-siṃha-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 16
The story of the lion named <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe vajra-daṃṣṭro nāma siṃhaḥ | tasya caturaka-kravyamukha-nāmānau śṛgāla-vṛkau bhṛtya-bhūtau sadaivānugatau tatraiva vane prativasataḥ | athānya-dine siṃhena kadācid āsanna-prasavā prasava-vedanayā sva-yūthād bhraṣṭoṣṭry upaviṣṭā kasmiṃścid vana-gahane samāsāditā | atha tāṃ vyāpādya yāvad udaraṃ sphoṭayati, tāvaj jīvan laghu-dāseraka-śiśur niṣkrāntaḥ | siṃho 'pi dāserakyāḥ piśitena saparivāraḥ parāṃ tṛptim upāgataḥ | paraṃ snehād bāla-dāsekaṃ tyaktaṃ gṛham ānīyedam uvāca-bhadra, na te'sti mṛtyor bhayaṃ matto nānyasmād api | tataḥ svecchayātra vane bhrāmyatām iti | yatas te śaṅku-sadṛśau karṇau | tataḥ śaṅkukarṇo nāma bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there was a lion named <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>. Two servants of his — a jackal named <s>Caturaka</s> and a wolf named <s>Kravyamukha</s> — always followed him and lived in that very forest. One day, the lion chanced upon a she-camel, about to give birth, who had strayed from her herd due to labor pains, sitting in a forest thicket. Having killed her, when he tore open the belly, a living baby camel emerged. The lion, together with his retinue, attained full satisfaction with the she-camel's flesh. But out of affection, he spared the baby camel, brought it home, and said: 'Good one, you have no fear of death from me or from anyone else. So roam about in this forest freely.' [He said:] 'Since your ears are pointed like pegs (<s>śaṅku</s>), your name shall be <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>.'

children.text: evam anuṣṭhite catvāro 'pi na eka-sthāne vihāriṇaḥ parasparam aneka-prakāra-goṣṭhī-sukham anubhavantas tiṣṭhanti | śaṅkukarṇo 'pi yauvana-padavīm ārūḍhaḥ kṣaṇam api na taṃ siṃhaṃ muñcati |
children.translated_text: When this arrangement was made, all four lived together in one place, enjoying the pleasures of varied companionship. <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> too, having reached the stage of youth, did not leave the lion's side even for a moment.

children.text: atha kadācid vajra-daṃṣṭrasya kenacid vanyena matta-gajena saha yuddham abhavat | tena mada-vīryāt sa danta-prahārais tathā kṣata-śarīro vihito yathā pracalituṃ na śaknoti | tadā kṣut-kṣāma-kaṇṭhas tān provāca-bhoḥ ! anviṣyatāṃ kiñcit sattvaṃ yenāham evaṃ sthito 'pi taṃ vyāpādyātmano yuṣmākaṃ ca kṣut-praṇāśaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: Now one day, <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s> fought a battle with a certain wild elephant in rut. That [elephant], by the force of its fury, inflicted such wounds upon his body with its tusks that he could not move. Then, with throat parched by hunger, he said to them: 'Ho! Seek out some creature, so that I, even in this state, may kill it and relieve the hunger of myself and of you.'

children.text: tac chrutvā te trayo 'pi vane sandhyā-kālaṃ yāvad bhrāntāḥ, paraṃ na kiñcit sattvam āsāditam | atha caturakaś cintayāmāsa-yadi śaṅkukarṇo 'yaṃ vyāpādyeta tataḥ sarveṣāṃ katicid dināni tṛptir bhavati | paraṃ nainaṃ svāmī mitratvād āśraya-samāśritatvāc ca vināśayiṣyati | athavā buddhi-prabhāveṇa svāminaṃ pratibodhya tathā kariṣye yathā vyāpādayiṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, those three roamed the forest until twilight, but found no creature. Then <s>Caturaka</s> thought: 'If this <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> were killed, it would satisfy everyone for several days. But the master will not destroy him because of friendship and because he has taken refuge [with him]. However, by the power of my intellect, I shall so enlighten the master that he will kill him.' And it is said:

children.text: avadhyaṃ vāthavāgamyam akṛtyaṃ nāsti kiṃcana |
children.translated_text: There is nothing that cannot be slain, nor any [place] that cannot be reached, nor any deed that cannot be done,

children.text: loke buddhimatām atra tasmāt tāṃ yojayāmy aham ||Panc_1.400||
children.translated_text: in this world, for those possessed of intelligence — therefore I shall employ it. // Panc_1.400 //

children.text: evaṃ vicintya śaṅkukarṇam idam āha-bhoḥ śaṅkukarṇa ! svāmī tāvat pathyaṃ vinā kṣudhayā paripīḍyate | svāmya-bhāvād asmākam api dhruvaṃ vināśa eva | tato vākyaṃ kiñcit svāmy-arthe vadiṣyāmi | tac chrūyatām |
children.translated_text: Having thought thus, he said to <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>: 'Ho, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>! The master is tormented by hunger without wholesome food. Since the master perishes, our destruction too is certain. So I shall speak a word for the master's sake. Listen to it.'

children.text: śaṅkukarṇa āha-bhoḥ śīghraṃ nivedyatāṃ, yena te vacanaṃ śīghraṃ nirvikalpaṃ karomi | aparaṃ svāminohite kṛte mayā sukṛta-śataṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> said: 'Ho! Speak quickly, so that I may carry out your word without hesitation. Moreover, in serving the master's interest, I shall have performed a hundred meritorious deeds.'

children.text: atha caturaka āha-bho bhadra ! ātma-śarīraṃ dviguṇa-lābhena svāmine prayaccha, yena te dviguṇaṃ śarīraṃ bhavati | svāminaḥ punaḥ prāṇa-yātrā bhavati |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Caturaka</s> said: 'O good one! Offer your own body to the master with the [promise of] a double reward, whereby your body will become twofold [in the next life], and the master's sustenance will continue.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya śaṅkukarṇaḥ prāha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tan madīya-prayojanam etad ucyatām | svāmy-arthaḥ kriyatām iti | param atra dharmaḥ pratibhūḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> said: 'Friend! If so, then let this purpose of mine be declared! Let the master's interest be served! But here <s>dharma</s> must be the guarantor.'

children.text: te vicintya sarve siṃha-sakāśam ājagmuḥ | tataś caturaka āha-deva ! na kiñcit sattvaṃ prāptam | bhagavān ādityo 'py astaṃ gataḥ | tad yadi svāmī dviguṇaṃ śarīraṃ prayacchati | tataḥ śaṅkukarṇo 'yaṃ dviguṇa-vṛddhyā sva-śarīraṃ prayacchati dharma-pratibhuvā |
children.translated_text: Having deliberated, they all went to the lion. Then <s>Caturaka</s> said: 'Sire! No creature has been found. The blessed sun too has set. Therefore, if the master grants a twofold body [in return], then this <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> offers his own body with [the growth of] double increase, with <s>dharma</s> as guarantor.'

children.text: siṃha āha-bhoḥ, yady evaṃ tat sundarataram | vyavahārasyāsya dharmaḥ pratibhūḥ kriyatām iti |
children.translated_text: The lion said: 'Ho! If so, that is most excellent. Let <s>dharma</s> be made the guarantor of this transaction.'

children.text: atha siṃha-vacanānantaraṃ vṛka-śṛgālābhyāṃ vidāritobhaya-kukṣiḥ śaṅkukarṇaḥ pañcatvam upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, immediately upon the lion's word, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> — his flanks torn open by the wolf and the jackal — met his death.

children.text: atha vajra-daṃṣṭraś caturakam āha-bhoś caturaka ! yāvad ahaṃ nadīṃ gatvā snānaṃ devatārcana-vidhiṃ kṛtvāgacchāmi, tāvat tvayātrāpamattena bhāvyam ity uktvā nadyāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s> said to <s>Caturaka</s>: 'Ho, <s>Caturaka</s>! While I go to the river, perform my ablutions and the worship of the gods, and return — you must remain watchful here.' Having said this, he went to the river.

children.text: atha tasmin gate caturakaś cintayāmāsa-kathaṃ mamaikākino bhojyo 'yam uṣṭro bhaviṣyati iti vicintya kravyamukham āha-bhoḥ kravyamukha ! kṣudhālur bhavān | tad yāvad asau svāmī nāgacchati, tāvat tvam asyoṣṭrasya māṃsaṃ bhakṣaya | ahaṃ tvāṃ svāmino nirdoṣaṃ pratipādayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Then, when he had gone, <s>Caturaka</s> thought: 'How shall this camel become food for me alone?' Having thought thus, he said to <s>Kravyamukha</s>: 'Ho, <s>Kravyamukha</s>! You are hungry. While the master has not yet returned, eat some of this camel's flesh. I shall prove you guiltless before the master.'

children.text: so 'pi tac chrutvā yāvat kiñcin māṃsam āsvādayati tāvac caturakeṇoktam-bhoḥ kravyamukha ! samāgacchati svāmī | tat tyaktvainaṃ dūre tiṣṭha, yenāsya bhakṣaṇaṃ na vikalpayati |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing that, had just begun tasting some flesh when <s>Caturaka</s> said: 'Ho, <s>Kravyamukha</s>! The master is coming! Leave it and stand far away, so that he does not suspect the eating.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite siṃhaḥ samāyāto yāvad uṣṭraṃ paśyati tāvad riktīkṛta-hṛdayo dāserakaḥ | tato bhṛkuṭiṃ kṛtvā paruṣataram āha-aho kenaiṣa uṣṭra ucchiṣṭatāṃ nīto, yena tam api vyāpādayāmi |
children.translated_text: When this had been done, the lion arrived. When he looked at the camel, [he saw that] the wretched creature's chest had been emptied. Then, furrowing his brow, he spoke most harshly: 'Ah! Who has made this camel into leavings? I shall slay him too!'

children.text: evam abhihite kravyamukhaś caturaka-mukham avalokayati | atha caturako vihasyovāca-bhoḥ ! mām anādṛtya piśitaṃ bhakṣayitvādhunā man-mukham avalokayasi | tad-āsvādayāsya durṇaya-taroḥ phalam iti |
children.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Kravyamukha</s> looked at <s>Caturaka</s>'s face. Then <s>Caturaka</s> laughed and said: 'Ho! Having disregarded me and eaten the flesh, now you look at my face? Then taste the fruit of this tree of evil conduct!'

children.text: tad ākarṇya kravyamukho jīva-nāśa-bhayād dūra-deśaṃ gataḥ | etasminn antare tena mārgeṇa dāseraka-sārtho bhārākrāntaḥ samāyātaḥ | tasyāgresaroṣṭrasya kaṇṭhe mahatī ghaṇṭā baddhā | tasyāḥ śabdaṃ durato 'py ākarṇya siṃho jambukam āha-bhadra, jñāyatāṃ kim eṣa raudraḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate'śruta-pūrvaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kravyamukha</s>, fearing for his life, fled to a distant land. In the meanwhile, a camel caravan laden with goods came along that road. A great bell was tied to the neck of the lead camel. Hearing its sound even from afar, the lion said to the jackal: 'Friend, find out what this terrifying sound is that one hears — never heard before.'

children.text: tac chrutvā, caturakaḥ kiñcid vanāntaraṃ gatvā satvaram abhyupetya provāca-svāmin ! gamyatāṃ gamyatāṃ yadi śaknoṣi gantum |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Caturaka</s>, having gone a short way into the forest, quickly returned and said: 'Master! Go, go — if you are able to go!'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-bhadra, kim evaṃ māṃ vyākulayasi | tat kathaya kim etat ?
iti caturaka āha-svāmin, eṣa dharmarājas tavopari kupitaḥ | yad anenākāle dāserako 'yaṃ madīyo vyāpāditaḥ | tat sahasra-guṇam uṣṭram asya sakāśād grahīṣyāmi | iti niścitya bṛhan-mānam ādāyāgresarasyoṣṭrasya grīvāyāṃ ghaṇṭāṃ baddhvā badhya-dāseraka-saktān api pitṛ-pitāmahān ādāya vaira-niryātanārtham āyāta eva |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Good sir, why do you agitate me so? Tell me — what is this?' Then <s>Caturaka</s> said: 'Master, this <s>Dharmarāja</s> (Yama) is angry with you. Because this servant of mine was killed by him untimely. Therefore I shall seize from him a camel of thousandfold value.' Having thus resolved, taking a great measure, tying a bell on the neck of the camel that went before, and bringing along the ancestors and forefathers connected with the executed servant, he has come for the purpose of avenging the enmity.

children.text: siṃho 'pi tac chrutvā sarvato dūrād evāvalokya mṛtam uṣṭraṃ parityajya prāṇa-bhayāt praṇaṣṭaḥ | caturako 'pi śanaiḥ śanais tasyoṣṭrasya māṃsaṃ bhakṣayāmāsa | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-parasaya pīḍanaṃ kurvan (399) iti |
children.translated_text: The lion too, hearing that, seeing from a great distance, abandoned the dead camel and fled in fear for his life. And <s>Caturaka</s> slowly ate the flesh of that camel. Therefore I say: 'He who inflicts injury upon another...' (verse 399) and so on.

children.text: atha damanake gate sañjīvakaś cintayāmāsa-aho kim etan mayā kṛtam ? yac chaṣpādo 'pi māṃsāśitas tasyānugaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
agamyāni pumān yāti yo 'sevyāṃś ca niṣevate |
children.translated_text: He who goes to places that should not be visited, and who serves those who should not be served —

children.text: sa mṛtyum upagṛhṇāti garbham aśvatarī yathā ||Panc_1.401||
children.translated_text: he embraces death, just as the she-mule [dies from] the embryo. [Panc 1.401]
Now, when <s>Damanaka</s> had gone, <s>Sañjīvaka</s> pondered: 'Alas! What have I done? Even though I am a grass-eater, I have become a follower of that flesh-eater.' Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: tat kiṃ karomi ? kva gacchāmi ? kathaṃ me śāntir bhaviṣyati ? athavā tam eva piṅgalakaṃ gacchāmi | kadācin māṃ śaraṇāgataṃ rakṣati | prāṇair na viyojayati | yata uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So what shall I do? Where shall I go? How will there be peace for me? Or rather, I shall go to that very <s>Piṅgalaka</s>. Perhaps he will protect me who have come for refuge. He will not separate me from life. For it is said —

children.text: dharmārthaṃ yatatām apīha vipado devād yadi syuḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Even for those who strive for <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>artha</s> (wealth), if by fate calamities arise somewhere,

children.text: tat tāsām upaśāntaye sumatibhiḥ kāryo viśeṣān nayaḥ |
children.translated_text: then for the alleviation of those, wise men should employ especially prudent counsel;

children.text: loke khyātim upāgatātra sakale lokoktir eṣā yato
children.translated_text: this common saying has become well-known in the entire world:

children.text: dagdhānāṃ kila vahninā hita-karaḥ seko 'pi tasyodbhavaḥ ||Panc_1.402||
children.translated_text: 'For those burnt by fire, the remedy is a sprinkling from that very source [water].' [Panc 1.402]

children.text: tathā ca-
loke'thavā tanu-bhṛtāṃ nija-karma-pākaṃ
children.translated_text: In this world, for embodied beings who constantly take refuge in righteous deeds,

children.text: nityaṃ samāśritavatāṃ suhita-kriyāṇām |
children.translated_text: who always perform beneficial actions —

children.text: bhāvārjitaṃ śubham athāpy aśubhaṃ nikāmaṃ
children.translated_text: whether the ripening of their own <s>karma</s> (actions) brings good or evil abundantly,

children.text: yad bhāvi tad bhavati nātra vicāra-hetuḥ ||Panc_1.403||
children.translated_text: what is destined to be, will be — there is no cause for deliberation here. [Panc 1.403]
And likewise —

children.text: aparaṃ cānyatra gatasyāpi me kasyacid duṣṭa-sattvasya māṃsāśinaḥ sakāśān mṛtyur bhaviṣyati | tad varaṃ siṃhāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover, even if I go elsewhere, death will come to me from some wicked, flesh-eating creature. Better then from the lion. And it is said —

children.text: mahadbhiḥ spardhamānasya vipad eva garīyasī |
children.translated_text: For one who contends with the great, calamity itself is glorious;

children.text: danta-bhaṅge'pi nāgānāṃ ślāghyo giri-vidāraṇe ||Panc_1.404||
children.translated_text: even in the breaking of their tusks, elephants are praiseworthy when splitting mountains. [Panc 1.404]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: mahato 'pi kṣayaṃ labdhvā ślāghyaṃ nīco 'pi gacchati |
children.translated_text: Even a lowly one achieves glory by obtaining destruction from a great one,

children.text: dānārthī madhupo yadvad gaja-karṇa-samāhataḥ ||Panc_1.405||
children.translated_text: just as the honey-bee seeking nectar is struck by the ear of an elephant. [Panc 1.405]

children.text: evaṃ niścitya sa sthalita-gatiṃ mandaṃ gatvā siṃhāśrayaṃ paśyann apaṭhat-aho, sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, walking with faltering gait slowly, seeing the lion's abode, he recited: 'Ah, well is this said —

children.text: antar-līna-bhujaṅgamaṃ gṛham ivāntaḥsthogra-siṃhaṃ vanaṃ
children.translated_text: Like a house with a serpent lurking within, the forest with a fierce lion hidden inside,

children.text: grāhākīrṇam ivābhirāma-kamala-cchāyā-sanāthaṃ saraḥ |
children.translated_text: like a lake sheltered by the shade of lovely lotuses yet teeming with crocodiles,

children.text: kālenārya-janāpavāda-piśunaiḥ kṣudrair anāryaiḥ śritaṃ
children.translated_text: in time, infested by vile, ignoble men who slander the noble —

children.text: duḥkhena pravigāhyate sa-cakitaṃ rājñāṃ manaḥ sāmayam ||Panc_1.406||
children.translated_text: the minds of kings, placated only with difficulty, are entered fearfully.' [Panc 1.406]

children.text: evaṃ paṭhan damanakoktākāraṃ piṅgalakaṃ dṛṣṭvā pracakitaḥ saṃvṛta-śarīro dūrataraṃ praṇāma-kṛtiṃ vināpy upaviṣṭaḥ | piṅgalako 'pi tathāvidhaṃ taṃ vilokya damanaka-vākyaṃ śraddadhānaḥ kopāt tasyopari papāta |
children.translated_text: Thus reciting, seeing <s>Piṅgalaka</s> in the very form described by <s>Damanaka</s>, he was startled, his body contracted, and sat down at a great distance without even making obeisance. <s>Piṅgalaka</s> too, seeing him in such a state, believing <s>Damanaka</s>'s words, fell upon him in anger.

children.text: atha sañjīvakaḥ khara-nakha-vikartita-pṛṣṭhaḥ śṛṅgābhyāṃ tad-udaram ullikhya katham api tasmād apetaḥ śṛṅgābhyāṃ hantum icchan yuddhāyāvasthitaḥ | atha dvāv api tau puṣpita-palāśa-pratimau paraspara-vadha-kāṅkṣiṇau dṛṣṭvā karaṭako damanakam āha-bho mūḍha-mate ! anayor virodhaṃ vitanvatā tvayā sādhu na kṛtam | na ca tvaṃ nīti-tattvaṃ vetsi | nītividbhir uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sañjīvaka</s>, his back torn by sharp claws, somehow escaped from him by gashing his belly with both horns, and stood ready for battle, wishing to kill with his horns. Then, seeing those two — resembling <s>Palāśa</s> trees in bloom [red with blood] — both desiring each other's death, <s>Karaṭaka</s> said to <s>Damanaka</s>: 'O fool! You have done wrong by creating this enmity between these two. Nor do you know the essence of statecraft.' Those skilled in policy have said —

children.text: kāryāṇy uttama-daṇḍa-sāhasa-phalāny āyāsa-sādhyāni ye prītyā saṃśamayanti nīti-kuśalāḥ sāmnaiva te mantriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those ministers skilled in policy who, with affection, pacify through conciliation alone matters that would produce the fruit of severe punishment and great violence and are achievable only with effort —

children.text: niḥsārālpa-phalāni ye tv avidhinā vāñchanti daṇḍodyamais
children.translated_text: but those who desire worthless, small gains through the effort of force contrary to proper procedure —

children.text: teṣāṃ durnaya-ceṣṭitair narapater āropyate śrīs tulām ||Panc_1.407||
children.translated_text: by their misguided actions, the king's fortune is placed in the balance. [Panc 1.407]

children.text: tad yadi svāmy-abhighāto bhaviṣyati tat kiṃ tavdīya-mantra-buddhyā kriyate | atha sañjīvako na badhyate tathāpy abhavyam | yataḥ prāṇa-sandehāt tasya ca vadhaḥ | tan mūḍha ! kathaṃ tvaṃ mantri-padam abhilaṣasi | sāma-siddhiṃ na vetsi | tad vṛthā manoratho 'yaṃ te daṇḍaruceḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So if harm befalls the master, then what is accomplished by your counselor's wisdom? And if <s>Sañjīvaka</s> is not killed, that too is inauspicious — for due to the danger to life, there will be his death. So, fool! How do you aspire to the minister's position? You do not know the success of conciliation. Vain is this fantasy of yours who delights in force. And it is said —

children.text: sāmādi-daṇḍa-paryanto nayaḥ proktaḥ svayambhuvā |
children.translated_text: Policy is declared by the Self-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>) to begin with <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and end with <s>daṇḍa</s> (force);

children.text: teṣāṃ daṇḍas tu pāpīyāṃs taṃ paścād viniyojayet ||Panc_1.408||
children.translated_text: among those, force is the worst — it should be employed last. [Panc 1.408]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: sāmnaiva yatra siddhir na tatra daṇḍo budhena viniyojyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where success is possible through conciliation alone, force should not be employed by the wise;

children.text: pittaṃ yadi śarkarayā śāmyati ko 'rthaḥ paṭolena ||Panc_1.409||
children.translated_text: if bile is pacified by sugar, what need is there for bitter gourd? [Panc 1.409]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: ādau sāma prayoktavyaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā |
children.translated_text: Conciliation should be employed first by a man of discernment;

children.text: sāma-sādhyāni kāryāṇi vikriyāṃ yānti na kvacit ||Panc_1.410||
children.translated_text: affairs that are accomplishable by conciliation never go to ruin. [Panc 1.410]

children.text: na candreṇa na cāuṣadhyā na sūryeṇa na vahninā |
children.translated_text: Neither the moon, nor herbs, nor the sun, nor fire —

children.text: sāmnaiva vilayaṃ yāti vidveṣa-prabhavaṃ tamaḥ ||Panc_1.411||
children.translated_text: only conciliation dissolves the darkness born of enmity. [Panc 1.411]

children.text: tathā yat tvaṃ mantritvam abhilaṣasi, tad apy ayuktam | yatas tvaṃ mantri-gatiṃ na vetsi | yataḥ pañca-vidho mantraḥ | sa ca karmaṇām ārambhopāyaḥ, puruṣa-dravya-sampat, deśa-kāla-vibhāgaḥ, vinipāta-pratīkāraḥ, kārya-siddhiś ceti | so 'yaṃ svāmy-amātyayor ekatamasya kiṃ vā dvayor api vinipātaḥ samutpadyate lagnaḥ | tad yadi kācic chaktir asti tad vicintyatāṃ vinipāta-pratīkāraḥ | bhinna-sandhāne hi mantriṇāṃ buddhi-parīkṣā | tan mūrkha ! tat kartum asamarthatvaṃ yato viparīta-buddhir asi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Likewise, your aspiring to the role of minister is improper, for you do not understand the ways of a minister. For counsel is of five kinds: the means for undertaking actions, the resources of men and materials, the division of place and time, the remedy for reversal, and the accomplishment of the objective. Now this reversal has arisen for either the master or the minister, or perhaps both. So if you have any ability, then consider the remedy for reversal. For the intelligence of ministers is tested in reconciling what is broken. So fool! You are incapable of doing that, since your intellect is perverted. And it is said —

children.text: mantriṇāṃ bhinna-sandhāne bhiṣajāṃ sāṃnipātike |
children.translated_text: The wisdom of ministers is revealed in reuniting the broken; of physicians, in a crisis of humors —

children.text: karmaṇi vyajyate prajñā susthe ko vā na paṇḍitaḥ ||Panc_1.412||
children.translated_text: who is not a scholar when all is well? [Panc 1.412]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: ghātayitum eva nīcaḥ para-kāryaṃ vetti na prasādhayitum |
children.translated_text: A base person knows only how to destroy another's work, not how to accomplish it;

children.text: pātayitum eva śaktir nākhoruddhartum anna-piṭakam ||Panc_1.413||
children.translated_text: the claw has the power only to knock down, not to lift up the food-basket. [Panc 1.413]

children.text: athavā na te doṣo 'yam | svāmino doṣaḥ | yas te vākyaṃ śraddadhāti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Or rather, it is not your fault — it is the master's fault, for he believes your words. And it is said —

children.text: narādhipā nīca-janānuvartino
children.translated_text: Kings who follow base men

children.text: budhopadiṣṭena pathā na yānti ye |
children.translated_text: and do not go by the path indicated by the wise —

children.text: viśanty ato durgama-mārga-nirgamaṃ
children.translated_text: they enter into a cage of calamity

children.text: samasta-sambādham anartha-pañjaram ||Panc_1.414||
children.translated_text: with impassable entrance and exit, full of obstruction everywhere. [Panc 1.414]

children.text: tad yadi tvam asya mantrī bhaviṣyasi tadānyo 'pi kaścin nāsya samīpe sādhu-janaḥ sameṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And if you become his minister, then no other virtuous person will come near him. And it is said —

children.text: guṇālayo 'py asan mantrī nṛpatir nādhigamyate |
children.translated_text: Even though a king may be an abode of virtues, he is not approached [by the good] if his minister is unworthy —

children.text: prasanna-svādu-salilo duṣṭa-grāhyo yathā hradaḥ ||Panc_1.415||
children.translated_text: just as a lake with clear, sweet water is [avoided] if it harbors wicked crocodiles. [Panc 1.415]

children.text: tathā ca śiṣṭa-jana-rahitasya svāmino 'pi nāśo bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise, the master bereft of virtuous men will also perish. And it is said —

children.text: citrāsvāda-kathair bhṛtyair anāyāsita-kārmukaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Kings who take pleasure in servants who entertain with marvelous tales but whose bows are never exerted —

children.text: ye ramante nṛpās teṣāṃ ramante ripavaḥ śriyā ||Panc_1.416||
children.translated_text: their enemies rejoice in their fortune. [Panc 1.416]

children.text: tat kiṃ mūrkhopadeśena | kevalaṃ doṣo na guṇaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So what use is instructing a fool? It produces only fault, not virtue. And it is said —

children.text: nānāmyaṃ namate dāru nāśmani syāt kṣura-kriyā |
children.translated_text: What cannot be bent does not bow like timber; the razor's work cannot be done on stone;

children.text: sūcī-mukhaṃ vijānīhi nāśiṣyāyopaśyate ||Panc_1.417||
children.translated_text: know the needle-mouth (<s>Sūcīmukha</s>) — instruction is not given to the unteachable. [Panc 1.417]

children.text: damanaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 17
vānara-yūtha-kathā
children.translated_text: He narrated — Story 17: The tale of the monkey troop.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścit parvataika-deśe vānara-yūtham | tac ca kadācid dhemanta-samaye'tikaṭhora-vāta-saṃsparśa-vepamāna-kalevaraṃ tuṣāra-varṣoddhata-pravarṣa-ghana-dhārā-nipāta-samāhataṃ na kathañcic chāntim agamat | atha kecid vānarā vahni-kaṇa-sadṛśāni guñjā-phalāny avacitya vahni-vāñchayā phūtkurvantaḥ samantāt tasthuḥ |
children.translated_text: There was, in a certain region of a mountain, a troop of monkeys. Once, in the winter season, their bodies trembling from the touch of extremely harsh winds, struck by the fall of dense torrents of rain intensified by snow, they could find no peace whatsoever. Then some monkeys, having gathered <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea) fruits resembling sparks of fire, stood all around blowing upon them, desiring fire.

children.text: atha sucīmukho nāma pakṣī teṣāṃ taṃ vṛthāyāsamavalokya provāca-bhoḥ, sarve mūrkhā yūyam | naite vahni-kaṇāḥ guñjā-phalāni etāni | tat kiṃ vṛthā śrameṇa | naitasmāc chīta-rakṣā bhaviṣyati | tad anviṣyatāṃ kaścin nirvāto vana-pradeśo guhā giri-kandaraṃ vā | adyāpi sa-ṭopā medhā dṛśyante |
children.translated_text: Then a bird named <s>Sūcīmukha</s> (Needle-beak), observing their futile effort, said: 'Hey! You are all fools. These are not sparks of fire — they are <s>guñjā</s> fruits. So what is the use of pointless effort? No protection from cold will come from this. Therefore, seek some wind-free spot in the forest, a cave, or a mountain cavern. Even now, rain clouds with thunder are visible.'

children.text: atha teṣām ekatamo vṛddha-vānaras tam uvāca-bho mūrkha ! kiṃ tāvad anena vyāpāreṇa | tad gamyatām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then one old monkey among them said to him: 'O fool! What business is this of yours? Be off!' And it is said —

children.text: muhur vighnita-karmāṇaṃ dyūta-kāraṃ parājitam |
children.translated_text: One who knows discrimination should not address a person whose endeavors are constantly thwarted, or a gambler who has lost,

children.text: nālāpayed viveka-jño yadīcchet siddhim ātmanaḥ ||Panc_1.418||
children.translated_text: if he desires his own success. [Panc 1.418]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: ākheṭakaṃ vṛthākleśaṃ mūrkhaṃ vyasanasaṃsthitam |
children.translated_text: A hunter laboring fruitlessly, a fool immersed in vice —

children.text: samālāpena yo yuṅkte sa gacchati parābhavam ||Panc_1.419||
children.translated_text: he who engages with them in conversation meets with humiliation. [Panc 1.419]

children.text: so 'pi tam anādṛtya bhūyo 'pi vānarān anavaratam āha-bhoḥ ! kiṃ vṛthā kleśena ? atha yāvad asau na kathañcit pralapan viramati tāvad ekena vānareṇa vyartha-śramatvāt kupitena pakṣābhyāṃ gṛhītvā śilāyām āsphālita uparataś ca |
children.translated_text: But he, disregarding him, continued to address the monkeys incessantly: 'Friends! What use is pointless exertion?' While he thus continued to prattle without stopping, one monkey, angered by his futile effort [to instruct them], seized him by the wings and dashed him against a rock, and he perished.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-nānamyaṃ namate dāru ity ādi | tathā ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'What cannot be bent does not bow like timber...' and so on. And likewise —

children.text: upadeśo hi mūrkhāṇāṃ prakopāya na śāntaye |
children.translated_text: Instruction to fools leads only to anger, not to peace;

children.text: payaḥ-pānaṃ bhujaṅgānāṃ kevalaṃ viṣa-vardhanam ||Panc_1.420||
children.translated_text: the feeding of milk to serpents only increases their poison. [Panc 1.420]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: upadeśo na dātavyo yādṛśe tādṛśe nare |
children.translated_text: Instruction should not be given to just any person;

children.text: paśya vānaramūrkheṇa sugṛhī nirgṛhīkṛtā ||Panc_1.421||
children.translated_text: see — by the foolish monkey, the bird <s>Sūcīmukha</s> (well-housed) was made homeless. [Panc 1.421]

children.text: damanaka āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 18
children.translated_text: He narrated — Story 18.

children.text:
kasmiṃścid vane śamī-vṛkṣa-śākhālambita-vasathaṃ kṛtvāraṇya-caṭaka-dampatī prativasataḥ sma | atha kadācit tayoḥ sukha-saṃsthayor hemanta-megho mandaṃ mandaṃ varṣitum ārabdhaḥ | atrāntare kaścic chākhā-mṛgo vātāsāra-samāhataḥ proddhūṣita-śarīro dantavīṇāṃ vādayan vepamānas tasyāḥ śamyā mūlam āsādyopaviṣṭaḥ | atha taṃ tādṛṣam avalokya caṭakā prāha-bho bhadra !
hasta-pāda-samopeto dṛśyase puruṣākṛtiḥ | śītena bhidyase mūḍha kathaṃ na kuruṣe gṛham ||Panc_1.422||
children.translated_text: In a certain forest, a pair of jungle sparrows had made their dwelling suspended from the branch of a <s>Śamī</s> (acacia) tree and dwelt there. Then once, when they were comfortably settled, a winter cloud began to rain gently. In the meantime, a certain monkey, battered by the wind and rain, his body shivering, playing a 'tooth-lute' [chattering his teeth], arrived at the base of that <s>Śamī</s> tree and sat down. Then, seeing him in such a state, the female sparrow said: 'O good sir! You are seen to have hands and feet, and a human form. Why, fool, shattered by cold, do you not make yourself a house?' [Panc 1.422]

children.text: etac chrutvā tāṃ vānaraḥ sakopam āha-adhame kasmān na tvaṃ mauna-vratā bhavasi ? aho dhārṣṭyam asyāḥ | adya mām upahasati-
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the monkey angrily said to her: 'You wicked one! Why are you not silent? Oh, the impudence of this one! Today she mocks me —

children.text: sūcī-mukhi durācārā raṇḍā paṇḍita-vādinī |
children.translated_text: O Needle-beak, ill-behaved, wanton, speaking like a scholar!

children.text: nāśaṅkate prajalpantī tat kim enāṃ na hanmy aham ||Panc_1.423||
children.translated_text: She prattles on without fear — why do I not strike her?' [Panc 1.423]

children.text: evaṃ pralapya tām āha-mugdhe ! kiṃ mama cintayā tava prayojanam ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having thus ranted, he said to her: 'Foolish one! What use is your concern for me?' And it is said —

children.text: vācyaṃ śraddhā-sametasya pṛcchateś ca viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: One should speak to one who has faith, and especially to one who asks;

children.text: proktaṃ śraddhā-vihīnasya araṇya-ruditopamam ||Panc_1.424||
children.translated_text: speech delivered to one devoid of faith is like weeping in the wilderness. [Panc 1.424]

children.text: tat kiṃ bahunā tāvat | kulāya-sthitayā tayā punar apy abhihitaḥ | sa tāvat tāṃ śamīm āruhya tasyāḥ kulāyaṃ śatadhā khaṇḍaśo 'karot | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-upadeśo na dātavyaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: But enough of this — even though she remained in her nest, she addressed him again. Thereupon he climbed that <s>Śamī</s> tree and tore her nest into a hundred pieces. Therefore I say: 'Instruction should not be given...' and so on.

children.text: tan mūrkha ! śikṣāpito 'pi na śikṣitas tvam | athavā na te doṣo 'sti, yataḥ sādhoḥ śikṣā guṇāya sampadyate, nāsādhoḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So, fool! Even though taught, you have not learned. Or rather, the fault is not yours, since for the virtuous, instruction leads to improvement, not for the unvirtuous. And it is said —

children.text: kiṃ karoty eva pāṇḍityam asthāne viniyojitam |
children.translated_text: What indeed does learning accomplish when applied in the wrong place?

children.text: andhakāra-praticchanne ghaṭe dīpa ivāhitaḥ ||Panc_1.425||
children.translated_text: It is like a lamp placed in a pot covered with darkness. [Panc 1.425]

children.text: tad-vyartha-pāṇḍityam āśritya mama vacanam aśṛṇvann ātmanaḥ śāntim api vetsi | tan nūnam apajātas tvam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Relying on that useless learning and not heeding my words, do you even know your own peace? Surely you are a degenerate. And it is said —

children.text: jātaḥ putro 'nujātaś ca atijātas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: A son born [equal to mother] is 'born,' one following [the father] is 'after-born,'

children.text: apajātaś ca loke'smin mantavyāḥ śāstra-vedibhiḥ ||Panc_1.426||
children.translated_text: one surpassing [both] is 'super-born,' and one degenerate — these should be recognized by those who know the scriptures. [Panc 1.426]

children.text: mātṛ-tulya-guṇo jātas tv anujātaḥ pituḥ samaḥ |
children.translated_text: One equal in qualities to the mother is 'born,' one equal to the father is 'after-born,'

children.text: atijāto 'dhikas tasmād apajāto 'dhamādhamaḥ ||Panc_1.427||
children.translated_text: one surpassing them is 'super-born,' and the degenerate is the lowest of the low. [Panc 1.427]

children.text: apy ātmano vināśaṃ gaṇayati na khalaḥ para-vyasana-hṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: A wicked person, delighted by others' misfortunes, does not even consider his own destruction;

children.text: prāyo mastaka-nāśe samara-mukhe nṛtyati kabandhaḥ ||Panc_1.428||
children.translated_text: just as a headless trunk often dances on the battlefield after the head is severed. [Panc 1.428]

children.text: aho, sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Ah, and this is well said —

children.text: dharma-buddhiḥ kubuddhiś ca dvāv etau viditau mama |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> (Righteous-mind) and <s>Kubuddhi</s> (Wicked-mind) — these two are known to me:

children.text: putreṇa vyartha-pāṇḍityāt pitā dhūmena ghātitaḥ ||Panc_1.429||
children.translated_text: through the son's useless learning, the father was killed by smoke. [Panc 1.429]

children.text: damanaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 20
kṛṣṇa-sarpa-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 20
The Story of the Black Serpent

children.text: kasmiṃścid deśe dharmabuddhiḥ pāpabuddhiś ca dve mitre prativasataḥ | atha kadācit pāpabuddhinā cintitaṃ yad-ahaṃ tāvan mūrkho dāridryopetaś ca | tad enaṃ dharmabuddhim ādāya deśāntaraṃ gatvā asyāśrayeṇārthopārjanāṃ kṛtvainam api vañcayitvā sukhībhavāmi |
children.translated_text: In a certain country, two friends named <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> (Righteous-mind) and <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> (Evil-mind) lived. Once, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> thought: 'I am a fool beset by poverty. So, taking this <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> along, I shall go to another country, earn wealth by his help, deceive him too, and become happy.'

children.text: athānyasminn ahani pāpabuddhir dharmabuddhiṃ prāha-bho mitra ! vārdhaka-bhāve kiṃ tv ātma-viceṣṭitaṃ smarasi | deśāntaram adṛṣṭvā kāṃ śiṣṭa-janasya vārttāṃ kathayiṣyasi ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then on another day, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> said to <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>: 'O friend! In old age, what of your own exploits will you remember? Without having seen foreign lands, what tale will you tell to cultivated people?' And it is said —
