children.text: deśāntareṣu bahu-vidha-bhāṣā-veṣādi yena na jñātam |
children.translated_text: He who has not learned the diverse languages, customs, and the like of foreign lands

children.text: bhramatā dharaṇī-pīṭhe tasya phalaṃ janmano vyartham ||Panc_1.430||
children.translated_text: while wandering upon the surface of the earth — for him the fruit of birth is wasted. [Panc 1.430]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: vidyāṃ vittaṃ śilpaṃ tāvan nāpnoti mānavaḥ samyak |
children.translated_text: A man does not properly acquire learning, wealth, or skill

children.text: yāvad vrajati na bhūmau deśād deśāntaraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ ||Panc_1.431||
children.translated_text: so long as he does not joyfully travel from one land to another. [Panc 1.431]

children.text: atha tasya tad-vacanam ākarṇya prahṛṣṭa-manās tenaiva saha guru-janānujñātaḥ śubhe'hani deśāntaraṃ prasthitaḥ | tatra ca dharmabuddhi-prabhāveṇa bhramatā pāpabuddhinā prabhūtataraṃ vittam āsāditam | tataś ca tau dvāv api prabhūtopārjita-dravyau prahṛṣṭau sva-gṛhaṃ praty autsukyena prasthitau | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his words and delighted at heart, he set out with him on an auspicious day with the permission of their elders to a foreign land. There, by the influence of <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>, while roaming about, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> acquired abundant wealth. Then both, having earned much property, set out happily and eagerly toward their home. And it is said —

children.text: prāpta-vidyārtha-śilpānāṃ deśāntara-nivāsinām |
children.translated_text: For those who have acquired learning, wealth, and skill and live in a foreign land,

children.text: krośa-mātro 'pi bhū-bhāgaḥ śata-yojanavad bhavet ||Panc_1.432||
children.translated_text: even a mere <s>krośa</s> (two miles) of ground seems like a hundred <s>yojanas</s>. [Panc 1.432]

children.text: atha sva-sthāna-samīpa-vartinā pāpabuddhinā dharmabuddhir abhihitaḥ-bhadra ! na sarvam etad dhanaṃ gṛhaṃ prati netuṃ yujyate | yataḥ kuṭumbino bāndhavāś ca prārthayiṣyante | tad atraiva vana-gahane kvāpi bhūmau nikṣipya kiñcin mātram ādāya gṛhaṃ praviśāvaḥ | bhūyo 'pi prayojane sañjāte tan-mātraṃ sametyāsmāt sthānān neṣyāvaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, when they were near their own town, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> said to <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>: 'Good friend! It is not proper to bring all this wealth home, because family members and relatives will demand it. So let us bury it somewhere in the depths of this forest, take only a small amount, and enter our homes. Later, when the need arises, we shall come to this place and take just as much as needed.' And it is said —

children.text: na vittaṃ darśayet prājñaḥ kasyacit svalpam apy aho |
children.translated_text: A wise man should not show his wealth to anyone, even a little —

children.text: muner api yatas tasya darśanāc calate manaḥ ||Panc_1.433||
children.translated_text: for even a sage's mind wavers upon seeing it. [Panc 1.433]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yathāmiṣaṃ jale matsyair bhakṣyate śvāpadair bhuvi |
children.translated_text: Just as meat in water is devoured by fish, on land by wild animals,

children.text: ākāśe pakṣibhiś caiva tathā sarvatra vittavān ||Panc_1.434||
children.translated_text: and in the sky by birds — so too is a wealthy man [preyed upon] everywhere. [Panc 1.434]

children.text: tad ākarṇya dharmabuddhir āha-bhadra evaṃ kriyatām | tathānuṣṭhite dvāv api tau sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā sukhena saṃsthitavantau | athānyasminn ahani pāpabuddhir niśīthe'ṭavyāṃ gatvā tat sarvaṃ vittaṃ samādāya gartaṃ pūrayitvā sva-bhavanaṃ jagāma |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> said: 'Good friend, let it be done so.' When this was carried out, both went to their homes and lived happily. Then on another day, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>, going to the forest at night, took all the wealth, filled up the pit [to hide his theft], and returned to his own house.

children.text: athānyedyur dharmabuddhiṃ sametya provāca-sakhe bahu-kuṭumbā vayaṃ vittābhāvāt sīdāmaḥ | tad gatvā tatra sthāne kiṃcin mātraṃ dhanam ānayāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then on another day, he approached <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> and said: 'Friend, we have many dependents and are suffering for lack of money. Let us go to that place and bring some amount of wealth.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-bhadra, evaṃ kriyatām |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Good friend, let it be done so.'

children.text: atha dvāv api gatvā tat sthānaṃ yāvat khanatas tāvad riktaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ dṛṣṭavantau | atrāntare pāpabuddhiḥ śiras tāḍayan provāca-bho dharmabuddhe ! tvayā hṛtam etad dhanaṃ, nānyena | yato bhūyo 'pi gartāpūraṇaṃ kṛtam | tat prayaccha me tasyārdham | anyathāhaṃ rāja-kule nivedayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Then both went to that place, and as they dug, they found the vessel empty. Thereupon, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>, striking his head, said: 'O <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>! This wealth was taken by you and no one else! Because the pit has been filled up again. So give me half of it. Otherwise I shall report this to the royal court.'

children.text: sa āha-bho durātman ! mā maivaṃ vada | dharmabuddhiḥ khalv aham | naitac caura-karma karomi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'O wicked one! Do not speak thus. I am <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> (Righteous-mind) indeed! I do not commit such thieving acts. And it is said —

children.text: mātṛvat para-dārāṇi para-dravyāṇi loṣṭavat |
children.translated_text: Others' wives are as [one's] mother, others' property as a clod of earth,

children.text: ātmavat sarva-bhūtāni vīkṣante dharma-buddhayaḥ ||Panc_1.435||
children.translated_text: and all beings as oneself — thus do righteous-minded ones see. [Panc 1.435]

children.text:
evaṃ dvāv api vivadamānau dharmādhikāriṇaṃ gatau ? procatuś ca parasparaṃ dūṣayantau | atha dharmādhikaraṇādhiṣṭhita-puruṣair divyārthaṃ yāvan niyojitau tāvat pāpabuddhir āha-
aho na samyag-dṛṣṭo nyāyaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text:
Thus both, disputing, went to the court of justice and accused each other. When the officers of the court appointed them to undergo an ordeal, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> said:
'Ah, the procedure of justice is not being properly observed.' And it is said —

children.text: vivāde anviṣyate patraṃ tad-abhāve'pi sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a dispute, written evidence is sought; in its absence, witnesses;

children.text: sākṣy abhāvāt tato divyaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ ||Panc_1.436||
children.translated_text: in the absence of witnesses, the wise prescribe an ordeal. [Panc 1.436]

children.text: tad atra viṣaye mama vṛkṣa-devatāḥ sākṣi-bhūtās tiṣṭhanti | tā apy āvayor ekataraṃ cauraṃ sādhuṃ vā kariṣyanti | atha taiḥ sarvair abhihitam-bho yuktam uktaṃ bhavatā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'In this matter, the tree-deities stand as my witnesses. They too will declare one of us to be the thief or the honest one.' Then all of them said: 'What you say is proper.' And it is said —

children.text: antyajo 'pi yadā sākṣī vivāde samprajāyate |
children.translated_text: Even when an outcaste becomes a witness in a dispute,

children.text: na tatra yujyate divyaṃ kiṃ punar vana-devatāḥ ||Panc_1.437||
children.translated_text: an ordeal is not proper there — how much less so when forest deities [testify]? [Panc 1.437]

children.text: tad asmākam apy atra viṣaye mahat kautūhalam vartate | pratyūṣa-samaye yuvābhyām apy asmābhiḥ saha tatra vanoddeśe gantavyam iti | etasminn antare pāpabuddhiḥ sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā sva-janakam uvāca-tāta, prabhūto 'yaṃ mayārtho dharmabuddheś coritaḥ | sa ca tava vacanena pariṇatiṃ gacchati | anyathāsmākaṃ prāṇaiḥ saha yāsyati |
children.translated_text: 'We too have great curiosity in this matter. At dawn, you both must come with us to that forest place.' In the meantime, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> went home and said to his father: 'Father, I have stolen this great wealth from <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>. Its outcome depends on your word. Otherwise it will be lost along with our lives.'

children.text: sa āha-vatsa, drutaṃ vada yena procya tad dravyaṃ sthiratāṃ nayāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Son, tell me quickly so that I may secure that property by speaking [on your behalf].'

children.text: pāpabuddhir āha-tāta, asti tat-pradeśe mahā-śamī | tasyāṃ mahat koṭaram asti | tatra tvaṃ sāṃpratam eva praviśa | tataḥ prabhāte yadāhaṃ satya-śrāvaṇaṃ karomi, tadā tvayā vācyaṃ yad dharmabuddhiś caura iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> said: 'Father, in that place there is a great <s>śamī</s> tree. It has a large hollow. Enter it now. Then at dawn, when I perform the truth-hearing, you must say that <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> is the thief.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite pratyūṣe snātvā pāpabuddhiḥ dharmabuddhi-puraḥ-saro dharmādhikaraṇakaiḥ saha tāṃ śamīm abhyetya tāra-svareṇa provāca |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, at dawn, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>, having bathed, with <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> in front and accompanied by the court officers, approached that <s>śamī</s> tree and spoke in a loud voice:

children.text:
ādityacandrāv anilo 'nalaś ca
dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaś ca | ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca sandhye
dharmo hi jānāti narasya vṛttam ||Panc_1.438||
children.translated_text: and day and night and both twilights — <s>Dharma</s> indeed knows a man's conduct. [Panc 1.438]

<s>Āditya</s> (Sun) and <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Anila</s> (Wind) and <s>Anala</s> (Fire),
heaven, earth, the waters, the heart, and <s>Yama</s> (Death),

children.text: bhagavati vana-devate ! āvayor madhye yaś caura tat kathayata |
children.translated_text: 'O blessed forest deity! Between us two, declare who is the thief.'

children.text: atha pāpabuddhi-pitā śamī-koṭara-sthaḥ provāca-bho, dharmabuddhinā hṛtam etad dhanam |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>'s father, standing in the hollow of the <s>śamī</s> tree, spoke: 'Listen — this wealth was taken by <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya sarve te rāja-puruṣā vismayotphulla-locanā yāvad dharmabuddher vitta-haraṇocitaṃ nigrahaṃ śāstra-dṛṣṭyāvalokayanti tāvad dharmabuddhinā tac chamī-koṭaraṃ vahni-bhojya-dravyaiḥ pariveṣṭya vahninā sandīpitam | atha jvalati tasmin śamī-koṭare'rdha-dagdha-śarīraḥ sphuṭitekṣaṇaḥ karuṇaṃ paridevayan pāpabuddhi-pitā niścakrāma | tataś ca taiḥ sarvaiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ-bho kim idam ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, all those royal officers, their eyes wide with amazement, were about to examine in the legal texts what punishment was appropriate for <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>'s theft of wealth, when <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> surrounded that <s>śamī</s>-tree hollow with combustible materials and set it on fire. Then, as the hollow of the <s>śamī</s> tree burned, <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>'s father emerged — his body half-burnt, his eyes burst open, wailing piteously. Then all of them asked him: 'What is this?'

children.text:
ity ukte idaṃ sarvaṃ kukṛtyaṃ pāpabuddheḥ kāraṇāj jātam ity uktvā mṛtaḥ | tatas te rāja-puruṣāḥ pāpabuddhiṃ śamī-śākhāyāṃ pratilambya dharmabuddhiṃ praśaṃsyedam ūcuḥ-
aho sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text:
When thus asked, he said: 'All this evil deed was caused by <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>' — and died. Then those royal officers hanged <s>Pāpabuddhi</s> on a branch of the <s>śamī</s> tree, praised <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>, and said:
'Ah, this is well said —'

children.text: upāyaṃ cintayet prājñas tathāpāyam api cintayet |
children.translated_text: A wise man should think of the means, and also think of the consequences;

children.text: paśyato baka-mūrkhasya nakulair bhakṣitāḥ sutāḥ ||Panc_1.439||
children.translated_text: while the foolish crane watched, the mongoose devoured his young. [Panc 1.439]

children.text: dharma-buddhiḥ prāha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
te procuḥ-
kathā 21
jīrṇadhana-nāma-vaṇik-putra-kathā
children.translated_text:
They said:
Story 21
The Story of the Merchant's Son Named <s>Jīrṇadhana</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe bahu-baka-sanātho vaṭa-pādapaḥ | tasya koṭare kṛṣṇa-sarpaḥ prativasati sma | sa ca baka-bālakān ajāta-pakṣān api sadaiva bhakṣayan kālaṃ nayati | athaiko bakas tena bhakṣitāny apatyāni dṛṣṭvā śiśu-vairāgyāt saras-tīram āsādya bāṣpa-pūraita-nayano 'dho-mukhas tiṣṭhati | taṃ ca tādṛk-ceṣṭitam avalokya kulīrakaḥ provāca-māma kim evaṃ rudyate bhavatādya ?
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there was a banyan tree inhabited by many cranes. In its hollow lived a black serpent. He passed his time by always devouring the young cranes, even those whose wings had not yet grown. Then one crane, seeing its offspring eaten by him, overcome with grief for its young, reached the shore of a lake and stood with downcast face, eyes brimming with tears. A crab, seeing it in such a state, said: 'Uncle, why are you weeping today?'

children.text:
sa āha-bhadra kiṃ karomi ? mama manda-bhāgyasya bālakāḥ koṭara-nivāsinā sarpeṇa bhakṣitāḥ | tad-duḥkha-duḥkhito 'haṃ rodimi | tat kathaya me yady asti kaścid upāyas tad-vināśāya |
tad ākarṇya kulīrakaś cintayāmāsa-ayaṃ tāvad asmat-sahaja-vairī | tathopadeśaṃ prayacchāmi satyānṛtaṃ yathānye'pi bakāḥ sarve saṅkṣayam āyānti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text:
He said: 'Good friend, what can I do? My young ones, ill-fated as I am, have been devoured by a serpent dwelling in the hollow. Grieving that grief, I weep. So tell me — is there any means for his destruction?'
Hearing that, the crab thought: 'He is our natural enemy. I shall give such advice, both true and false, that all the other cranes too will come to ruin.' And it is said —

children.text: navanīta-samāṃ vāṇīṃ kṛtvā cittaṃ tu nirdayam |
children.translated_text: Making one's speech as soft as butter, but one's heart merciless,

children.text: tathā prabodhyate śatruḥ sānvayo mriyate yathā ||Panc_1.440||
children.translated_text: thus one incites an enemy so that he dies along with his family. [Panc 1.440]

children.text: āha ca-māma, yady evaṃ tan matsya-māṃsa-khaṇḍāni nakulasya bila-dvārāt sarpa-koṭaraṃ yāvat prakṣipa yathā nakulas tan-mārgeṇa gatvā taṃ duṣṭa-sarpaṃ vināśayati |
children.translated_text: And he said: 'Uncle, if it is so, then scatter pieces of fish-meat from the mongoose's burrow-entrance all the way to the serpent's hollow, so that the mongoose, following that trail, will go and destroy that wicked serpent.'

children.text: atha tathānuṣṭhite matsya-māṃsānusāriṇā nakulena taṃ kṛṣṇa-sarpaṃ nihatya te'pi tad-vṛkṣāśrayāḥ sarve bakāś ca śanaiḥ śanair bhakṣitāḥ | ato vayaṃ brūmaḥ-upāyaṃ cintayed iti |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, the mongoose, following the trail of fish-meat, killed that black serpent, and then also gradually devoured all the cranes sheltering in that tree. Therefore we say: 'A wise man should think of the means...'

children.text: evaṃ mūḍha ! tvayāpy apāyaś cintito nopāyaḥ pāpa-buddhivat | tan na bhavasi tvaṃ sajjanaḥ | kevalaṃ pāpa-buddhir asi | jñāto mayā svāminaḥ prāṇa-sandehānayanāt | prakaṭīkṛtaṃ tvayā svayam evātmano duṣṭatvaṃ kauṭilyaṃ ca | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'Thus, you fool! You too have thought only of the danger and not of the remedy, like <s>Pāpabuddhi</s>. So you are not a good person — you are nothing but evil-minded. I have known this from your bringing doubt upon the master's life. You yourself have revealed your own wickedness and crookedness. Or rather, this is well said —'

children.text: yatnād api kaḥ paśyec chikhinām āhāra-niḥsaraṇa-mārgam |
children.translated_text: Who could observe with effort the path of food's exit in peacocks?

children.text: yadi jalada-dhvani-muditās ta eva mūḍhā na nṛtyeyuḥ ||Panc_1.441||
children.translated_text: If, delighted by the sound of clouds, those very fools did not dance! [Panc 1.441]

children.text: yadi tvaṃ svāminam enāṃ daśāṃ nayasi tad asmad-vidhasya kā gaṇanā ? tasmān mamāsannena bhavatā na bhāvyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'If you bring the master to such a state, then what account is there of one like me? Therefore you should not remain in my proximity.' And it is said —

children.text: tulāṃ loha-sahasrasya yatra khādanti mūṣakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where rats devour a balance weighing a thousand [units] of iron,

children.text: rājaṃs tatra harec chyeno bālakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_1.442||
children.translated_text: O king, there a hawk would carry off a child — there is no doubt in this. [Panc 1.442]

children.text:
damanaka āha--katham etat ?
so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text:
<s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How is that?'
He said —

children.text:
kathā 22
jīrṇadhana-nāma-vaṇik-putra-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 22
The Story of the Merchant's Son Named <s>Jīrṇadhana</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne jīrṇadhano nāma vaṇik-putraḥ | sa ca dravya-kṣayād deśāntara-gamana-manā vyacintayat-
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a merchant's son named <s>Jīrṇadhana</s> (Worn-out Wealth). He, due to the loss of his property, was thinking of going to another country and reflected —

children.text: yatra deśe atha vā sthāne bhogān bhuktvā svavīryataḥ |
children.translated_text: In whatever country or place one has enjoyed pleasures by one's own prowess,

children.text: tasmin vibhavahīno yo vaset sa puruṣādhamaḥ ||Panc_1.443||
children.translated_text: he who dwells there bereft of prosperity is the lowest of men. [Panc 1.443]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yenāhaṃkārayuktena ciraṃ vilasitaṃ purā |
children.translated_text: He who formerly reveled long with pride,

children.text: dīnaṃ vadati tatraiva yaḥ pareṣāṃ sa ninditaḥ ||Panc_1.444||
children.translated_text: and [now] speaks humbly in that very place before others — he is despised. [Panc 1.444]

children.text: tasya ca gṛhe sahasra-loha-bhāra-ghaṭitā pūrva-puruṣopārjitā tulāsīt | tāṃ ca kasyacid chreṣṭino gṛhe nikṣepa-bhūtāṃ kṛtvā deśāntaraṃ prasthitaḥ | tataḥ suciraṃ kālaṃ deśāntaraṃ yathecchayā bhrāntvā punaḥ sva-puram āgatya taṃ śreṣṭhinam uvāca-bhoḥ śreṣṭhin ! dīyatāṃ me sā nikṣepa-tulā |
children.translated_text: In his house there was an iron balance weighing a thousand <s>bhāras</s>, acquired by his ancestors. Having deposited it as a trust in the house of a certain merchant, he set out for another country. Then, having wandered in foreign lands as he pleased for a very long time, he returned to his own city and said to that merchant: 'O merchant! Give me back that balance which I deposited with you.'

children.text: sa āha-bho ! nāsti sā tvadīyā tulā | mūṣikair bhakṣitā |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Ah! That balance of yours does not exist. It was eaten by mice.'

children.text: jīrṇadhana āha-bhoḥ śreṣṭhin ! nāsti doṣas te yadi mūṣikair bhakṣiteti | īdṛg evāyaṃ saṃsāraḥ | na kiṃcid atra śāśvatam asti | param ahaṃ nadyāṃ snānārthaṃ gamiṣyāmi | tat tvam ātmīyaṃ śiśum enaṃ dhanadeva-nāmānaṃ mayā saha snānopakaraṇa-hastaṃ preṣayeti |
children.translated_text: <s>Jīrṇadhana</s> said: 'O merchant! There is no fault of yours if it was eaten by mice. Such indeed is this world — nothing here is permanent. But I shall go to the river for bathing. So send your own child, this boy named <s>Dhanadeva</s>, with me, carrying the bathing implements.'

children.text: so 'pi caurya-bhayāt tasya śaṅkitaḥ sva-putram uvāca-vatsa, pitṛvyo 'yaṃ tava snānārthaṃ nadyāṃ yāsyati | tad gamyatām anena sārdhaṃ snānopakaraṇam ādāyeti | aho sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: And he, fearing the theft [might be discovered], anxiously said to his own son: 'Child, this is your uncle who will go to the river for bathing. So go with him, taking the bathing implements.' Ah, well is this said —

children.text: na bhaktyā kasyacit ko 'pi priyaṃ prakurute naraḥ |
children.translated_text: No man does a kindness to another out of devotion,

children.text: muktvā bhayaṃ pralobhaṃ vā kārya-kāraṇam eva vā ||Panc_1.445||
children.translated_text: but only from fear, greed, or some purpose and motive. // Panc_1.445 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: atyādaro bhaved yatra kārya-kāraṇa-varjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there is excessive solicitude without any purpose or cause,

children.text: tatra śaṅkā prakartavyā pariṇāme'sukhāvahā ||Panc_1.446||
children.translated_text: there one should harbor suspicion — [for] the outcome brings unhappiness. // Panc_1.446 //

children.text: athāsau vaṇik-śiśuḥ snānopakaraṇam ādāya prahṛṣṭa-manās tenābhyāgatena saha prasthitaḥ | tathānuṣṭhite vaṇik snātvā taṃ śiśuṃ nadī-guhāyāṃ prakṣipya tad-dvāraṃ bṛhac-chilayācchādya satvaraṃ gṛham āgataḥ | pṛṣṭaś ca tena vaṇijā-bho 'bhyāgata tat kathyatāṃ kutra me śiśur yas tvayā saha nadīṃ gataḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then that merchant's boy, taking the bathing implements, set out with a joyful heart together with that visitor. When this was done, the merchant, having bathed, threw the boy into a river-cave, covered its entrance with a large stone, and hastily returned home. And when he was asked by that merchant: 'O visitor, tell me — where is my boy who went to the river with you?'

children.text: sa āha-nadī-taṭāt sa śyenena hṛta iti |
children.translated_text: He said: 'He was carried off by a hawk from the riverbank.'

children.text: śreṣṭhy āha-mithyā-vādin ! kiṃ kvacic chyeno bālaṃ hartuṃ śaknoti ? tat samarpaya me sutam, anyathā rāja-kule nivedayiṣyāmīti |
children.translated_text: The merchant said: 'Liar! Can a hawk ever carry off a boy? Hand over my son, or else I shall report this to the royal court!'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ satyavādin ! yathā śyeno bālaṃ na nayati tathā mūṣikā api loha-bhāra-ghaṭitāṃ tulāṃ na bhakṣayanti | tad arpaya me tulāṃ yadi dārakeṇa prayojanam | evaṃ vivadamānau dvāv api rāja-kulaṃ gatau |
children.translated_text: He said: 'O truth-speaker! Just as a hawk does not carry off a boy, so too mice do not eat a balance made of a thousand [measures of] iron. So return my balance if you want the child.' Thus quarreling, both of them went to the royal court.

children.text: tatra śreṣṭhī tāra-svareṇa provāca-bho 'brahmaṇyam abrahmaṇyam | mama śiśur anena caureṇāpahṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: There, the merchant cried out in a loud voice: 'O injustice, injustice! My child has been stolen by this thief!'

children.text: atha dharmādhikāriṇas tam ūcuḥ-bhoḥ samarpyatāṃ śreṣṭhi-sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the judges of justice said to him: 'Sir, hand over the merchant's son.'

children.text: sa āha-kiṃ karomi ? paśyato me nadī-taṭāc chyenenāpahṛtaḥ śiśuḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'What can I do? Before my very eyes, the child was carried off by a hawk from the riverbank.'

children.text: tac chrutvā te procuḥ-bho na satyam abhihitaṃ bhavatā | kiṃ śyenaḥ śiśuṃ hartuṃ samartho bhavati ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, they said: 'Sir, what you have said is not true. Can a hawk be capable of carrying off a child?'

children.text: sa āha-bho bhoḥ śrūyatāṃ mad-vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Sirs, sirs! Hear my words:,

children.text: tulāṃ loha-sahasrasya yatra khādanti mūṣikāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where mice eat a balance made of a thousand [measures of] iron,

children.text: rājaṃs tatra harec chyeno bālakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_1.447||
children.translated_text: O kings, there a hawk may carry off a boy — there is no doubt in this. // Panc_1.447 //

children.text: te procuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: They said: 'How is this?'

children.text: tataḥ śreṣṭhī sabhyānām agre sarvaṃ vṛttāntaṃ nivedayāmāsa | tatas tair vihasya dvāv api tau parasparaṃ sambodhya tulā-śiśu-pradānena santoṣitau |
children.translated_text: Then the merchant reported the entire account before the judges. Thereupon, laughing, they reconciled the two with each other by having them return the balance and the child respectively.

children.text:
ato 'haṃ bravīmi-tulāṃ loha-sahasrasya iti |
tan mūrkha ! sañjīvaka-prasādam asahamānena tvayaitat kṛtam | aho sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text:
Therefore I say: 'Where mice eat a balance of a thousand [measures of iron]...'
You fool! Unable to tolerate the favor shown to <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, you have done this! Ah, well is this said —

children.text: prāyeṇātra kulānvitaṃ kukulajāḥ śrī-vallabhaṃ durbhagā
children.translated_text: Generally, the low-born [envy] the high-born; the unfortunate, the favorites of <s>Śrī</s>;

children.text: dātāraṃ kṛpaṇā ṛjūn anṛjavo vitte sthitaṃ nirdhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: the miserly, the generous; the crooked, the upright; the destitute, those established in wealth;

children.text: vairūpyopahṛtāś ca kānta-vapuṣaṃ dharmāśrayaṃ pāpino
children.translated_text: those disfigured, the handsome; sinners, those devoted to <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: nānā-śāstra-vicakṣaṇaṃ ca puruṣaṃ nindanti mūrkhāḥ sadā ||Panc_1.448||
children.translated_text: and fools always disparage the man learned in many <s>śāstras</s>. // Panc_1.448 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: mūrkhāṇāṃ paṇḍitā dveṣyā nirdhanānāṃ mahādhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: To fools, the learned are hateful; to the destitute, the very wealthy;

children.text: vratinaḥ pāpa-śīlānām asatīnāṃ kula-striyaḥ ||Panc_1.449||
children.translated_text: to the sinful, the observers of vows; to unchaste women, women of good family. // Panc_1.449 //

children.text: tan mūrkha tvayā hitam apy ahitaṃ kṛtam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So, fool, by you what was beneficial has been made harmful. And it is said —

children.text: paṇḍito 'pi varaṃ śatrur na mūrkho hita-kārakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Better a wise enemy than a foolish well-wisher;

children.text: vānareṇa hato rājā viprāś cīreṇa rakṣitāḥ ||Panc_1.450||
children.translated_text: a monkey killed the king, while <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were saved by a thief. // Panc_1.450 //

children.text: damanaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Damanaka</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 23
children.translated_text:
He said:
Tale 23

children.text: kasyacid rājño nityaṃ vānaro 'tibhakti-paro 'ṅga-sevako 'ntaḥ-pure apy apratiṣiddha-prasaro 'tiviśvāsa-sthānam abhūt | ekadā rājño nidrāṃ gatasya vānare vyajanaṃ nītvā vāyuṃ vidadhati rājño vakṣaḥ-sthalopari makṣikopaviṣṭā | vyajanena muhur muhur niṣidhyamānāpi punaḥ punas tatra evopaviśati | tatas tena svabhāva-capalena mūrkheṇa vānareṇa kruddhena satā tīkṣṇaṃ khaḍgam ādāya tasyā upari prahāro vihitaḥ | tato makṣikoḍḍīya gatā, paraṃ tena śita-dhāreṇāsinā rājño vakṣo dvidhā jātaṃ rājā mṛtaś ca | tasmāc cirāyur icchatā nṛpeṇa mūrkho 'nucaro na rakṣaṇīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: A certain king had a monkey who was extremely devoted in his personal attendance, admitted even into the inner palace without restriction, and a place of great trust. One day, when the king had fallen asleep and the monkey was fanning him with a fan, a fly settled on the king's chest. Though driven away again and again with the fan, it kept settling there once more. Then that fickle-natured foolish monkey, enraged, seized a sharp sword and struck at it. The fly flew off and escaped, but with that keen-edged sword the king's chest was split in two and the king died. Therefore, a king who desires long life should not keep a foolish attendant.

children.text: aparam ekasmin nagare ko 'pi vipro mahā-vidvān paraṃ pūrva-janma-yogena cauro vartate | tasmin pure'nya-deśād āgatāṃś caturo viprān bahūni vastūni vikrīṇato dṛṣṭvā cintitavān-aho kenopāyenaiṣāṃ dhanaṃ labhe | iti vicintya teṣāṃ puro 'nekāni śāstroktāni subhāṣitāni cātipriyāṇi madhurāṇi vacanāni jalpatā teṣāṃ manasi viśvāsam utpādya sevā kartum ārabdhā | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in a certain city there was a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a great scholar, but by the karma of his former birth he was a thief. In that city, seeing four <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had come from another country selling many goods, he thought: 'Ah, by what stratagem may I obtain their wealth?' Having thus reflected, by speaking before them many auspicious and sweet words cited from the <s>śāstras</s> and most pleasing, he generated trust in their hearts and began to serve them. Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: asatī bhavati salajjā kṣāraṃ nīraṃ ca śītalaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: An unchaste woman becomes modest; brackish water becomes cool;

children.text: dambhī bhavati vivekī priyavaktā bhavati dhūrtajanaḥ ||Panc_1.451||
children.translated_text: a hypocrite becomes discerning; a rogue becomes a sweet speaker. // Panc_1.451 //

children.text:
atha tasmin sevāṃ kurvati tair vipraiḥ sarva-vastūni vikrīya bahu-mūlyāni ratnāni krītāni | tatas tāni jaṅghā-madhye tat-samakṣaṃ prakṣipya sva-deśaṃ prati gantum udyamo vihitaḥ | tataḥ sa dhūrta-vipras tān viprān gantum udyatān prekṣya cintā-vyākulita-manāḥ saṃjātaḥ-
aho dhanam etan na kiṃcin mama caṭitam | athaibhiḥ saha yāmi | pathi kvāpi viṣaṃ dattvaitān nihatya sarva-ratnāni gṛhṇāmi | iti vicintya teṣām agre sa-karuṇaṃ vilapyedam āha-bho mitrāṇi ! yūyaṃ mām ekākinaṃ muktvā gantum udyatāḥ | tan me mano bhavadbhiḥ saha sneha-pāśena baddhaṃ bhavad-viraha-nāmnaivākulaṃ sañjātaṃ yathā dhṛtiṃ kvāpi na dhatte | yūyam anugrahaṃ vidhāya sahāya-bhūtaṃ mām api sahaiva nayata |
children.translated_text:
Now, while he was serving them, those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having sold all their goods, purchased precious gems of great value. Then, placing those [gems] inside their calves before his very eyes, they prepared to depart for their own country. Then that rogue <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, seeing them ready to go, became anxious in mind:
'Alas, none of this wealth has come within my grasp! So I shall go along with them. Somewhere on the road I shall give them poison, kill them, and take all the gems.' Having thus resolved, he lamented pitifully before them and said: 'O friends! You are all preparing to go, leaving me alone. My heart, bound by the rope of affection for you, has become so agitated at the mere thought of separation from you that it finds composure nowhere. Please show your grace and, as companions, take me along with you.'

children.text: tad-vacaḥ śrutvā te karuṇārdra-cittās tena samam eva sva-deśaṃ prati prasthitāḥ | athādhvani teṣāṃ pañcānām api pallī-pura-madhye vrajatāṃ dhvāṅkṣāḥ kathayitum ārabdhāḥ-re re kirātāḥ ! dhāvata dhāvata | sa-pāda-lakṣa-dhanino yānti | etān nihatya dhanaṃ nayata |
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, they, their hearts melted with compassion, set out together with him toward their own country. Now on the road, as all five of them were passing through a tribal village, crows began to cry out: 'Ho, ho, tribals! Run, run! Men carrying wealth worth one and a quarter <s>lakṣas</s> are passing! Kill them and take the money!'

children.text: tataḥ kirātair dhvāṅkṣa-vacanam ākarṇya satvaraṃ gatvā te viprā laguḍa-prahārair jarjarī-kṛtya vastrāṇi mocayitvā vilokitāḥ, paraṃ dhanaṃ kiṃcin na labdham | tadā taiḥ kirātair abhihitam-bhoḥ pānthāḥ ! purā kadāpi dhvāṅkṣa-vacanam anṛtaṃ nāsīt | tato bhavatāṃ saṃnidhau kvāpi dhanaṃ vidyate tad arpayata | anyathā sarveṣām api vadhaṃ vidhāya carma vidārya pratyaṅgaṃ prekṣya dhanaṃ neṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the tribals, hearing the words of the crows, quickly went and, having battered those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with club-blows and stripped them of their garments, searched them — but found no money at all. Then those tribals said: 'O travelers! Never before have the words of crows been untrue. So somewhere upon your persons there must be money — hand it over. Otherwise, we shall kill you all, cut open your skin, and inspect each limb to take the money.'

children.text: tadā teṣām īdṛśaṃ vacanam ākarṇya caura-vipreṇa manasi cintitam-yadaiṣāṃ viprāṇāṃ vadhaṃ vidhāyāṅgaṃ vilokya ratnāni neṣyanti, tadāpi māṃ vadhiṣyanti tato 'haṃ pūrvam evātmānam aratnaṃ samarpyaitān muñcāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing those words, the thief-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> thought in his mind: 'When they kill these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and inspect their limbs and take the gems, they will kill me too. So I shall first offer myself as gem-free and [thereby] save them.' And it is said —

children.text: mṛtyor bibheṣi kiṃ bāla na sa bhītaṃ vimuñcati |
children.translated_text: Why do you fear death, child? It does not release the one who fears it;

children.text: adya vābda-śatānte vā mṛtyur vai prāṇināṃ dhruvaḥ ||Panc_1.452||
children.translated_text: whether today or at the end of a hundred years, death is certain for living beings. // Panc_1.452 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: gavārthe brāhmaṇārthe ca prāṇa-tyāgaṃ karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who gives up his life for the sake of cattle or for the sake of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>

children.text: sūryasya maṇḍalaṃ bhittvā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||Panc_1.453||
children.translated_text: pierces through the orb of the sun and goes to the highest abode. // Panc_1.453 //

children.text: iti niścityābhihitaṃ-bhoḥ kirātāḥ ! yady evaṃ tato māṃ pūrvaṃ nihatya vilokayata | tatas tais tathānuṣṭhite taṃ dhana-rahitam avalokyāpare catvāro 'pi muktāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, he said: 'O tribals! If so, then kill me first and examine me.' Then, when they did so and found him devoid of wealth, the other four were also released.

children.text:
ato 'haṃ bravīmi-paṇḍito 'pi varaṃ śatruḥ iti |
athaivaṃ saṃvadatoḥ sañjīvakaḥ kṣaṇam ekaṃ pīṅgalakena saha yuddhaṃ kṛtvā tasya khara-nakhara-prahārābhihito gatāsur vasundharā-pīṭhe nipapāta | atha taṃ gatāsum avalokya piṅgalakas tad-guṇa-smaraṇārdra-hṛdayaḥ provāca-bhoḥ, ayuktaṃ mayā pāpena kṛtaṃ sañjīvakaṃ vyāpādayatā | yato viśvāsa-ghātād anyan nāsti pāpataraṃ karma | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text:
Therefore I say: 'Better a wise enemy than a foolish [friend]...'
Then, while they were thus conversing, <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, having fought with <s>Piṅgalaka</s> for a moment, struck by his sharp claws, gave up his life and fell upon the surface of the earth. Then, seeing him dead, <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, his heart moistened with the remembrance of his virtues, said: 'Alas, what I, a sinner, have done in killing <s>Saṃjīvaka</s> was wrong. For there is no sin more grievous than the betrayal of trust.' And it is said —

children.text: mitra-drohī kṛtaghnaś ca yaś ca viśvāsa-ghātakaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who betrays a friend, he who is ungrateful, and he who kills one who trusts him —

children.text: te narā narakaṃ yānti yāvac candra-divākarau ||Panc_1.454||
children.translated_text: those men go to hell for as long as the moon and sun endure. // Panc_1.454 //

children.text: bhūmi-kṣaye rāja-vināśa eva
children.translated_text: When land is lost, it is simply the ruin of the king;

children.text: bhṛtyasya vā buddhimato vināśe |
children.translated_text: but when a wise servant is lost —

children.text: no yuktam uktaṃ hy anayoḥ samatvaṃ
children.translated_text: equality between the two has never been declared fitting;

children.text: naṣṭāpi bhūmiḥ sulabhā na bhṛtyāḥ ||Panc_1.455||
children.translated_text: for even lost land is easily recovered, but not servants. // Panc_1.455 //

children.text: tathā mayā sabhā-madhye sa sadaiva praśaṃsitaḥ | tat kiṃ kathayiṣyāmi teṣām agrataḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, I always praised him in the midst of the assembly. So what shall I say before them now?' And it is said —

children.text: ukto bhavati yaḥ pūrvaṃ guṇavān iti saṃsadi |
children.translated_text: He who has previously been declared virtuous in the assembly —

children.text: na tasya doṣo vaktavyaḥ pratijñā-bhaṅga-bhīruṇā ||Panc_1.456||
children.translated_text: his faults should not be spoken of by one who fears the breaking of his own word. // Panc_1.456 //

children.text: evaṃ-vidhaṃ pralapantaṃ damanakaḥ sametya saharṣam idam āha-deva, kātaratamas tavaiṣa nyāyo yad droha-kāriṇaṃ śaṣpa-bhujaṃ hatvetthaṃ śocasi | tan naitad upapannaṃ bhūbhujām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: While he was thus lamenting, <s>Damanaka</s> approached and said with delight: 'Your Majesty, this reasoning of yours is the height of cowardice — that you grieve thus after killing a treacherous grass-eater! This is not becoming of kings.' And it is said —

children.text: pitā vā yadi vā bhrātā putro bhāryāthavā suhṛt |
children.translated_text: Whether a father, or a brother, a son, a wife, or a friend —

children.text: prāṇa-drohaṃ yadā gacched dhantavyo nāsti pātakam ||Panc_1.457||
children.translated_text: when one turns to plotting against one's life, he should be killed — there is no sin in it. // Panc_1.457 //

children.text: tathā ca-
rājā ghṛṇī brāhmaṇaḥ sarva-bhakṣī
children.translated_text: A king who is compassionate [when he should not be], a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who eats everything,

children.text: strī cātrapā duṣṭamatiḥ sahāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: a woman without shame, a companion of evil counsel,

children.text: preṣyaḥ pratīpo 'dhikṛtaḥ prasādī
children.translated_text: a servant who is hostile, an official who is [overly] gracious —

children.text: tyājyā amī yaś ca kṛtaṃ na vetti ||Panc_1.458||
children.translated_text: these are to be abandoned, as well as one who does not acknowledge what has been done for him. // Panc_1.458 //
And likewise —

children.text: api ca-
satyānṛtā ca paruṣā priya-vādinī ca
children.translated_text: Truthful and false, harsh and sweet-speaking,

children.text: hiṃsrā dayālur api cārtha-parā vadānyā |
children.translated_text: violent and compassionate, wealth-seeking and generous,

children.text: bhūri-vyathā pracura-vitta-samāgamā ca
children.translated_text: causing much pain yet bringing great gain —

children.text: veśyāṅganeva nṛpa-nītir aneka-rūpā ||Panc_1.459||
children.translated_text: royal policy, like a courtesan, takes many forms. // Panc_1.459 //
Moreover —

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: akṛtopadravaḥ kaścin mahān api na pūjyate |
children.translated_text: One who has caused no harm, even if great, is not worshipped;

children.text: pūjayanti narā nāgān na tārkṣyaṃ nāga-ghātinam ||Panc_1.460||
children.translated_text: men worship serpents, not <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), the slayer of serpents. // Panc_1.460 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñā-vādāṃś ca bhāṣase |
children.translated_text: 'You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom;

children.text: gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||Panc_1.461||
children.translated_text: the wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.' // Panc_1.461 //

children.text: evaṃ tena sambodhitaḥ piṅgalakaḥ sañjīvaka-śokaṃ tyaktvā damanaka-sācivyena rājyam akarot |
children.translated_text: Thus counseled by him, <s>Piṅgalaka</s>, abandoning his grief for <s>Saṃjīvaka</s>, ruled his kingdom with <s>Damanaka</s> as his minister.

children.text:
iti śrī-viṣṇu-śarma-viracite pañcatantre
mitra-bhedo nāma
prathamaṃ tantram
||1||
children.translated_text:
Thus ends, in the <s>Pañcatantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>,
the first <s>tantra</s> named <s>Mitrabheda</s> (The Breach of Friendship).
||1||

children.text: atha mitra-samprāptiḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins <s>Mitrasaṃprāpti</s> (The Gaining of Friends).

children.text: athedam ārabhyate mitra-samprāptir nāma dvitīyaṃ tantram | yasyāyam ādyaḥ ślokaḥ-
asādhanā api prājñā buddhimanot bahu-śrutāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even those without resources, if wise, intelligent, and well-learned —

children.text: sādhayanty āśu kāryāṇi kākākhu-mṛga-kūrmavat ||Panc_2.1||
children.translated_text: accomplish their tasks swiftly, like the crow, the mouse, the deer, and the turtle. ||Panc_2.1||
Here begins the second <s>tantra</s> named <s>Mitrasaṃprāpti</s>. Of which this is the opening verse —

children.text: tad yathānuśrūyate-
children.translated_text: That is heard as follows —

children.text:
prastāvanā-kathā
laghupatanaka-citragrīva-vṛttāntaḥ
children.translated_text:
Introductory Tale
The Story of <s>Laghupatanaka</s> and <s>Citragrīva</s>

children.text: asti dākṣiṇātye janapade mahilāropyaṃ nāma nagaram | tasya nātidūrastho mahocchrāyavān nānā-vihaṅgopabhukta-phalaḥ kīṭair āvṛta-koṭaraś chāyāśvāsita-pathika-jana-samūho nyagrodha-pādapo mahān | athavā yuktam-
children.translated_text: In the southern country there is a city named <s>Mahilāropya</s>. Not far from it stood a great banyan tree, of towering height, its fruits enjoyed by various birds, its hollows covered with insects, its shade giving relief to groups of weary travelers. Or rather, this is fitting —

children.text: chāyā-supta-mṛgaḥ śakunta-nivahair viṣvag-vilupta-cchadaḥ
children.translated_text: Deer sleeping in its shade, flocks of birds stripping its leaves all around,

children.text: kīṭair āvṛta-koṭaraḥ kapi-kulaiḥ skandhe kṛta-praśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: insects covering its hollows, troops of monkeys taking shelter on its branches,

children.text: viśrabdhaṃ madhupair nipīta-kusumaḥ ślāghyaḥ sa eva drumaḥ
children.translated_text: bees confidently drinking from its blossoms — that tree alone is praiseworthy,

children.text: sarvāṅgair bahu-sattva-saṅga-sukhado bhū-bhāra-bhūto 'paraḥ ||Panc_2.2||
children.translated_text: giving happiness through the company of many creatures with all its limbs; another is merely a burden on the earth. ||Panc_2.2||

children.text: tatra ca laghupatanako nāma vāyasaḥ prativasati sma | sa kadācit prāṇa-yātrārthaṃ puram uddiśya pracalito yāvat paśyati, tāvaj jāla-hasto 'tikṛṣṇa-tanuḥ sphuṭita-caraṇa ūrdhva-keśo yama-kiṅkarākāro naraḥ saṃmukho babhūva | atha taṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkita-manā vyacintayat-yad ayaṃ durātmādya mamāśraya-vaṭa-pādapa-sammukho 'bhyeti | tan na jñāyate kim adya vaṭa-vāsināṃ vihaṅgamānāṃ saṅkṣayo bhaviṣyati na vā |
children.translated_text: There dwelt a crow named <s>Laghupatanaka</s> (light-wing). Once, having set out toward the city for the purpose of obtaining food, he saw approaching him a man with a net in hand, of extremely dark body, with cracked feet, hair standing upward, resembling a servant of <s>Yama</s> (Death). Then, seeing him, alarmed in mind, he thought: This evil-souled one today approaches facing my sheltering banyan tree. So it is not known whether today there will be destruction of the birds dwelling in the banyan or not.

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vicintya tat-kṣaṇān nivṛtya tam eva baṭa-pādapaṃ gatvā sarvān vihaṅgamān provāca-bhoḥ ! ayaṃ durātmā lubdhako jāla-taṇḍula-hastaḥ samabhyeti | tat sarvathā tasya na viśvasanīyam | eṣa jālaṃ prasārya taṇḍulān prakṣepsyati | te taṇḍulā bhavadbhiḥ sarvair api kālakūṭa-sadṛśā draṣṭavyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having deliberated thus in many ways, he immediately turned back, went to that very banyan tree, and said to all the birds: Friends! This evil-souled fowler approaches with net and rice-grains in hand. So he is not to be trusted in any way. He will spread his net and scatter rice-grains. Those rice-grains should be regarded by all of you as equal to <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison).

children.text: evaṃ vadatas tasya sa lubdhakas tatra baṭa-tala āgatya jālaṃ prasārya sindu-vāra-sadṛśāṃs taṇḍulān prakṣipya nātidūraṃ gatvā nibhṛtaḥ sthitaḥ | atha ye pakṣiṇas tatra sthitās te laghu-patanaka-vākyārgalayā nivāritās tāṃs taṇḍulān hālāhālāṅkurān iva vīkṣamāṇā nibhṛtās tasthuḥ |
children.translated_text: While he was speaking thus, that fowler came to the base of the banyan, spread his net, scattered rice-grains resembling <s>sinduvāra</s> (vitex) seeds, went not far away, and remained hidden. Now the birds that were there, restrained by the bolt of <s>Laghupatanaka</s>'s words, looking upon those rice-grains as sprouts of <s>hālāhāla</s> (poison), remained still.

children.text: atrāntare citragrīvo nāma kapotarājaḥ sahasra-parivāraḥ prāṇa-yātrārtha-paribhramaṃs tāṃs taṇḍulān dūrato 'pi paśyan laghupatanakena nivāryamāṇo 'pi jihvā-laulyād bhakṣaṇārtham apatat | sa-parivāro nibaddhaś ca | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, a pigeon-king named <s>Citragrīva</s> (speckled-neck), with a retinue of a thousand, wandering about for the purpose of obtaining food, seeing those rice-grains even from afar, though being warned by <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, swooped down to eat them out of the greed of the tongue. He was caught together with his retinue. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: jihvā-laulya-prasaktānāṃ jala-madhya-nivāsinām |
children.translated_text: For those addicted to the greed of the tongue, dwelling in the midst of water,

children.text: acintito vadho 'jñānāṃ mīnānām iva jāyate ||Panc_2.3||
children.translated_text: death comes unforeseen to the ignorant, as to fish. ||Panc_2.3||

children.text: athavā daiva-pratipatikūlatayā bhavaty evam | na tasya doṣo 'sti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Or rather, it happens thus due to the adversity of fate. It is not his fault. And it is said —

children.text: paulastyaḥ katham anya-dāra-haraṇe doṣaṃ na vijñātavān
children.translated_text: How did the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>] not perceive the fault in stealing another's wife?

children.text: rāmeṇāpi kathaṃ na hema-hariṇasyāsambhavo lakṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: How did even <s>Rāma</s> not notice the impossibility of the golden deer?

children.text: akṣaiś cāpi yudhiṣṭhireṇa sahasā prāpto hy anarthaḥ kathaṃ
children.translated_text: How did <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> suddenly obtain calamity through dice?

children.text: pratyāsanna-vipatti-mūḍha-manasāṃ prāyo matiḥ kṣīyate ||Panc_2.4||
children.translated_text: The intellect of those whose minds are deluded by approaching calamity generally diminishes. ||Panc_2.4||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: kṛtānta-pāśa-baddhānāṃ daivopahata-cetasām |
children.translated_text: Of those bound by the noose of Death, whose minds are afflicted by fate,

children.text: buddhayaḥ kubja-gāminyo bhavanti mahatām api ||Panc_2.5||
children.translated_text: the intellects go crookedly, even of great ones. ||Panc_2.5||

children.text: atrāntare lubdhakas tān baddhān vijñāya prahṛṣṭa-manāḥ prodyata-yaṣṭis tad-vadhārthaṃ pradhāvitaḥ | citragrīvo 'py ātmānaṃ sa-parivāraṃ baddhaṃ matvā lubdhakam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā tān kapotān ūce-aho, na bhetavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, the fowler, knowing them to be caught, with a delighted mind, raised his staff and rushed forward to kill them. <s>Citragrīva</s> too, knowing himself and his retinue to be bound, seeing the fowler approaching, said to those pigeons: Ah, there is nothing to fear! And it is said —

children.text: vyasaneṣv eva sarveṣu yasya buddhir na hīyate |
children.translated_text: He whose intelligence is not diminished in all adversities —

children.text: sa teṣāṃ pāram abhyeti tat-prabhāvād asaṃśayam ||Panc_2.6||
children.translated_text: he reaches the far shore of those [adversities] by its power, without doubt. ||Panc_2.6||

children.text: sampattau ca vipattau ca mahatām eka-rūpatā |
children.translated_text: In prosperity and in adversity, great ones have the same form;

children.text: udaye savitā rakto raktaś cāsta-maye tathā ||Panc_2.7||
children.translated_text: the sun is red at rising and red likewise at setting. ||Panc_2.7||

children.text: tat sarve vayaṃ helayoḍḍīya sa-pāśa-jālā asyādarśanaṃ gatvā muktiṃ prāpnumaḥ | no ced bhaya-viklavāḥ santo helayā samutpātaṃ na kariṣyatha | tato mṛtyum avāpsyatha | uktaṃ ca-
tantavo 'py āyatā nityaṃ tantavo bahulāḥ samāḥ |
children.translated_text: Threads too, always long, threads [that are] many and equal —

children.text: bahūn bahutvād āyāsān sahantīty upamā satām ||Panc_2.8||
children.translated_text: many [threads] endure many toils by virtue of their multiplicity — this is the simile for the virtuous. ||Panc_2.8||

So let all of us, flying up effortlessly together with the net and snares, go out of his sight and attain liberation. Otherwise, being terrified by fear, you will not make an effortless ascent, and then you will meet death. And it is said —

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite lubdhako jālam ādāyākāśe gacchatāṃ teṣāṃ pṛṣṭhato bhūmistho 'pi paryadhāvat | tata ūrdhvānanḥ ślokam enam apaṭhat |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, the fowler, [seeing them] going through the sky carrying the net, pursued them on the ground from behind. Then, looking upward, he recited this verse:

children.text: jālam ādāya gacchanti saṃhatāḥ pakṣiṇo 'py amī |
children.translated_text: These birds, united, go carrying the net;

children.text: yāvac ca vivadiṣyante patiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_2.9||
children.translated_text: but as soon as they quarrel, they will fall — no doubt. ||Panc_2.9||

children.text: laghupatanako 'pi prāṇa-yātrā-kriyāṃ tyaktvā kim atra bhaviṣyantīti kutūhalāt tat-pṛṣṭhato 'nusarati | atha dṛṣṭer agocaratāṃ gatān vijñāya lubdhako nirāśaḥ ślokam apaṭhan nivṛttaś ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Laghupatanaka</s> too, abandoning his food-seeking activity, followed behind them out of curiosity [thinking:] What will happen here? Then, knowing them to have gone beyond the range of [the fowler's] sight, the fowler, despairing, recited a verse and turned back:

children.text: nahi bhavati yan na bhāvyaṃ bhavati ca bhāvyaṃ vināpi yatnena |
children.translated_text: What is not fated does not come to be; what is fated comes to be even without effort;

children.text: karatala-gatam api naśyati yasya hi bhavitavyatā nāsti ||Panc_2.10||
children.translated_text: even that which is in the palm of the hand perishes for one whose destiny is not [favorable]. ||Panc_2.10||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: parāṅmukhe vidhau cet syāt kathañcid draviṇodayaḥ |
children.translated_text: If when fate is adverse there should somehow be a rise of wealth,

children.text: tat so 'nyad api saṅgṛhya yāti śaṅkha-nidhir yathā ||Panc_2.11||
children.translated_text: then that, having gathered up other [wealth] too, departs — like the <s>Śaṅkha</s> treasure. ||Panc_2.11||

children.text: tad āstāṃ tāvad vihaṅgāmiṣa-lobho yāvat kuṭumba-vartanopāya-bhūtaṃ jālam api me naṣṭam | citragrīvo 'pi lubdhakam adarśanībhūtaṃ jñātvā tān uvāca-bhoḥ ! nivṛttaḥ sa durātmā lubdhakaḥ | tat sarvair api svasthair gamyatāṃ mahilāropyasya prāg-uttara-dig-bhāge | tatra mama suhṛd dhiraṇyako nāma mūṣakaḥ sarveṣāṃ pāśa-cchedaṃ kariṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So let this greed for bird-flesh be set aside — for even the net, which was the means of my family's livelihood, has been lost! <s>Citragrīva</s> too, knowing the fowler to have disappeared from sight, said to them: Friends! That evil-souled fowler has turned back. So let all of you, being at ease, go to the northeast of <s>Mahilāropya</s>. There my friend, a mouse named <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, will cut the bonds of all. And it is said —

children.text: sarveṣām eva martyānāṃ vyasane samupasthite |
children.translated_text: For all mortals, when adversity has arrived,

children.text: vāṅ-mātreṇāpi sāhāyyaṃ mitrād anyo na sandadhe ||Panc_2.12||
children.translated_text: no one other than a friend provides assistance, even by words alone. ||Panc_2.12||

children.text: evaṃ te kapotāś citragrīveṇa sambodhitā mahilāropye nagare hiraṇyaka-bila-durgaṃ prāpuḥ | hiraṇyako 'pi sahasra-mukha-bila-durgaṃ praviṣṭaḥ sann akutobhayaḥ sukhenāsta | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Thus those pigeons, encouraged by <s>Citragrīva</s>, reached the fortress-burrow of <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> in the city of <s>Mahilāropya</s>. <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> too, having entered his fortress-burrow with a thousand openings, dwelt free from all fear and at ease. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: daṃṣṭrā-virahitaḥ sarpo mada-hīno yathā gajaḥ |
children.translated_text: A serpent deprived of its fangs, an elephant deprived of its rut —

children.text: sarveṣāṃ jāyate vaśyo durga-hīnas tathā nṛpaḥ ||Panc_2.13||
children.translated_text: a king deprived of his fortress likewise becomes subject to all. ||Panc_2.13||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: na gajānāṃ sahasreṇa na ca lakṣeṇa vājinām |
children.translated_text: Not by a thousand elephants, nor by a hundred thousand horses,

children.text: tat karma sidhyate rājñāṃ dureṇaikena yad raṇe ||Panc_2.14||
children.translated_text: is that deed of kings accomplished which [is accomplished] by a single fortress in battle. ||Panc_2.14||

children.text: śatam eko 'pi sandhatte prākārastho dhanurdharaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a single bowman stationed on a rampart can hold off a hundred;

children.text: tasmād durgaṃ praśaṃsanti nīti-śāstra-vido janāḥ ||Panc_2.15||
children.translated_text: therefore those versed in the science of statecraft praise a fortress. ||Panc_2.15||

children.text: atha citragrīvo bilam āsādya tāra-svareṇa provāca-bho bho mitra hiraṇyaka ! satvaram āgaccha | mahatī me vyasanāvasthā vartate |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Citragrīva</s>, having reached the burrow, called out in a loud voice: O friend <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>! Come quickly! A great calamity has befallen me!

children.text: tac chrutvā hiraṇyako 'pi bila-durgāntargataḥ san provāca-bhoḥ ! ko bhavān ? kim artham āyātaḥ ? kiṃ kāraṇam ? kīdṛk te vyasanāvasthānām ? tat kathyatām iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, being inside the fortress-burrow, said: Ho! Who are you? Why have you come? What is the reason? What is the nature of your calamity? Tell me!

children.text:
tac chrutvā citragrīva āha-bhoḥ ! citragrīvo nāma kapota-rājo 'haṃ te suhṛt | tat satvaram āgaccha | gurutaraṃ prayojanam asti |
tad ākarṇya pulakita-tanuḥ prahṛṣṭātmā sthira-manās tvaramāṇo niṣkrāntaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
suhṛdaḥ sneha-sampannā locanānanda-dāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Friends, full of affection, giving delight to the eyes,

children.text: gṛhe gṛhavatāṃ nityaṃ nāgacchanti mahātmanām ||Panc_2.16||
children.translated_text: do not always come to the homes of great-souled householders. ||Panc_2.16||

Hearing that, <s>Citragrīva</s> said: Friend! I am <s>Citragrīva</s>, the pigeon-king, your friend. So come quickly! There is an urgent purpose.
Hearing that, his body thrilling with joy, his spirit delighted, his mind steady, he came out hastily. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: ādityasyodayaṃ tāta tāmbūlaṃ bhāratī kathā |
children.translated_text: The rising of the sun, <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), the speech of <s>Bhāratī</s> (Sarasvatī), a story,

children.text: iṣṭā bhāryā sumitraṃ ca apūrvāṇi dine dine ||Panc_2.17||
children.translated_text: a beloved wife, a good friend — [these are] ever fresh, day after day. ||Panc_2.17||

children.text: suhṛdo bhavane yasya samāgacchanti nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: He in whose home friends constantly gather —

children.text: citte ca tasya saukhyasya na kiñcit pratimaṃ sukham ||Panc_2.18||
children.translated_text: there is no happiness comparable to the joy in his heart. ||Panc_2.18||

children.text: atha citraṃ grīvaṃ saparivāraṃ pāśa-baddham ālokya hiraṇyakaḥ sa-viṣādam idam āha-bhoḥ, kim etat ?
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Citragrīva</s> together with his retinue bound in snares, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said with sorrow: Friend, what is this?

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ, jānann api kiṃ pṛcchasi ? uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: He said: Friend, why do you ask when you already know? And it is said, for —

children.text: yasmāc ca yena ca yadā ca yathā ca yac ca
children.translated_text: From whatever, by whatever, whenever, however, whatever,

children.text: yāvac ca yatra ca śubhāśubham ātma-karma |
children.translated_text: to whatever extent, and wherever — good and evil, [the fruit of] one's own actions,

children.text: tasmāc ca tena ca tadā ca tathā ca tac ca
children.translated_text: from that, by that, then, thus, that,

children.text: tāvac ca tatra ca kṛtānta-vaśād upaiti ||Panc_2.19||
children.translated_text: to that extent, and there — comes by the power of destiny. ||Panc_2.19||

children.text: tat prāptaṃ mayaitad bandhanaṃ jihvā-laulyāt | sāmprāptaṃ tvaṃ satvaraṃ pāśa-vimokṣaṃ kuru | tad ākarṇya hiraṇyakaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: So this bondage has been obtained by me through the greed of the tongue. Now quickly perform the cutting of my bonds. Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said —

children.text: ardhārdhād yojana-śatād āmiṣaṃ vīkṣate khagaḥ |
children.translated_text: A bird sees meat from a distance of half a <s>yojana</s> or a hundred <s>yojanas</s>;

children.text: so 'pi pārśva-sthitaṃ daivād bandhanaṃ na ca paśyati ||Panc_2.20||
children.translated_text: yet it does not see, by fate, a snare placed at its side. ||Panc_2.20||

children.text: tathā ca-
ravi-niśākarayor graha-pīḍanaṃ
children.translated_text: The affliction of the sun and moon by planets,

children.text: gaja-bhujaṅga-vihaṅgama-bandhanam |
children.translated_text: the binding of elephants, serpents, and birds,

children.text: matimatāṃ ca nirīkṣya daridratā
children.translated_text: and seeing the poverty of the wise —

children.text: vidhir aho balavān iti me matiḥ ||Panc_2.21||
children.translated_text: 'Ah, fate is indeed powerful!' — such is my thought. ||Panc_2.21||
And likewise —

children.text: tathā ca-
vyomaikānta-vicāriṇo 'pi vihagāḥ samprāpnuvanty āpadaṃ
children.translated_text: Even birds that roam exclusively in the sky meet with calamity;

children.text: badhyante nipuṇair agādha-salilān mīnāḥ samudrād api |
children.translated_text: even fish are caught by the skillful from the ocean of unfathomable waters.

children.text: durnītaṃ kim ihāsti kiṃ ca sukṛtaṃ kaḥ sthāna-lābhe guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: What misconduct exists here, and what merit? What good is gaining a [safe] place?

children.text: kālaḥ sarva-janān prasārita-karo gṛhṇāti dūrād api ||Panc_2.22||
children.translated_text: Time, with outstretched hand, seizes all people even from afar. ||Panc_2.22||
And likewise —

children.text: evam uktvā citragrīvasya pāśaṃ chettum udyataṃ sa tam āha-bhadra, mā maivaṃ kuru | prathamaṃ mama bhṛtyānāṃ pāśa-cchedaṃ kuru | tad anu mamāpi ca |
children.translated_text: Having said this, as he set about cutting <s>Citragrīva</s>'s bonds, [<s>Citragrīva</s>] said to him: Good friend, do not do so! First cut the bonds of my servants. Then mine as well.

children.text: tac chrutvā kupito hiraṇyakaḥ prāha-bhoḥ ! na yuktam uktaṃ bhavatā | yataḥ svāmino 'nantaraṃ bhṛtyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said angrily: Friend! What you have said is not proper. For servants [come] after the master.

children.text: sa āha-bhadra, mā maivaṃ vada | mad-āśrayāḥ sarva ete varākāḥ | aparaṃ sva-kuṭumbaṃ parityajya samāgatāḥ | tat katham etāvan-mātram api saṃmānaṃ na karomi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Good friend, do not speak thus! All these poor ones depend on me. Moreover, they have come abandoning their own families. So how can I not show them even this much honor? And it is said —

children.text: yaḥ saṃmānaṃ sadā dhatte bhṛtyānāṃ kṣitipo 'dhikam |
children.translated_text: That king who always bestows abundant honor upon his servants —

children.text: vittābhāve'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā te tyajanti na karhicit ||Panc_2.23||
children.translated_text: even in the absence of wealth, seeing him, they never abandon [him]. ||Panc_2.23||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: viśvāsaḥ sampadāṃ mūlaṃ tena yūthapatir gajaḥ |
children.translated_text: Trust is the root of prosperity; therefore the elephant is the herd-leader;

children.text: siṃho mṛgādhipatye'pi na mṛgaiḥ parivāryate ||Panc_2.24||
children.translated_text: the lion, even though lord of beasts, is not surrounded by deer. ||Panc_2.24||

children.text: aparaṃ mama kadācit pāśa-cchede kurvatas te danta-bhaṅgo bhavati | athavā durātmā lubdhakaḥ sambhyeti | tan nūnaṃ naraka-pāta eva | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover, while cutting my bonds, your teeth might sometimes break. Or perhaps the evil-souled fowler returns. Then surely there would be a fall into hell [for me]. And it is said —

children.text: sadācāreṣu bhṛtyeṣu saṃsīdatsu ca yaḥ prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: That lord who is happy while his well-conducted servants are suffering

children.text: sukhī syān narakaṃ yāti paratreha ca sīdati ||Panc_2.25||
children.translated_text: goes to hell, and suffers both here and in the next world. ||Panc_2.25||

children.text: tac chrutvā prahṛṣṭo hiraṇyakaḥ prāha-bhoḥ, vedmy ahaṃ rāja-dharmam | paraṃ mayā tava parīkṣā kṛtā | tat sarveṣāṃ pūrvaṃ pāśa-cchedaṃ kariṣyāmi | bhavān apy anena bahu-kapota-parivāreṇa bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said with delight: Friend, I know the duty of kings. But I was testing you. So I shall first cut the bonds of all. And you too will have this large retinue of pigeons. And it is said —

children.text: kāruṇyaṃ saṃvibhāgaś ca yathā bhṛtyeṣu lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: The compassion and generosity that are seen [in you] toward your servants —

children.text: cittenānena te śaṅkyā trailokyasyāpi nāthatā ||Panc_2.26||
children.translated_text: with that disposition, sovereignty over the three worlds too may be suspected of you. ||Panc_2.26||

children.text: evam uktvā sarveṣāṃ pāśa-cchedaṃ kṛtvā hiraṇyakaś citragrīvam āha-mitra, gamyatām adhunā svāśrayaṃ prati | bhūyo 'pi vyasane prāpte samāgantavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Having said this, having cut the bonds of all, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said to <s>Citragrīva</s>: Friend, go now to your own abode. And when adversity strikes again, you must come [to me].

children.text: tān sampreṣya punar api durgaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | citragrīvo 'pi saparivāraḥ svāśrayam agamat | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having sent them off, he entered his fortress again. <s>Citragrīva</s> too, together with his retinue, went to his own abode. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: mitravān sādhayaty arthān duḥsādhyān api vai yataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who has friends accomplishes tasks, even those hard to accomplish, because —

children.text: tasmān mitrāṇi kurvīta samānāny eva cātmanaḥ ||Panc_2.27||
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should make friends only with those who are equal to oneself. [Panc 2.27]

children.text: laghupatanako 'pi vāyasaḥ sarvaṃ taṃ citragrīva-bandhu-mokṣam avalokya vismitamanā vyacintayat-aho buddhir asya hiraṇyakasya śaktiś ca durga-sāmagrī ca | tad īdṛg eva vidhi-vihaṅgānāṃ bandhana-mokṣātmakaḥ | ahaṃ ca na kasyacid viśvasimi cala-prakṛtiś ca | tadāpy enaṃ mitraṃ karomi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The crow <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, having observed the entire liberation of <s>Citragrīva</s>'s companions from their bonds, thought to himself with wonder — "Ah, what intelligence this <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> has, and what power, and what an excellent fortress! Such indeed is the fate of birds — consisting of bondage and liberation. And I do not trust anyone, being fickle by nature. Nevertheless, I shall make him my friend." And it is said —

children.text: api sampūrṇatā-yuktaiḥ kartavyāḥ suhṛdo budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Even with those who are already complete, the wise should cultivate friendship;

children.text: nadīśaḥ paripūrṇo 'pi candrodayam apekṣate ||Panc_2.28||
children.translated_text: the lord of rivers, though already full, still awaits the rising of the moon. [Panc 2.28]

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya pādapād avatīrya bila-dvāram āśritya citragrīvavac chabdena hiraṇyakaṃ samāhūtavān-ehy ehi bho hiraṇyaka, ehi |
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, he descended from the tree and, stationing himself at the entrance of the burrow, called out to <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> in the same manner as <s>Citragrīva</s> — "Come, come, O <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, come!"

children.text: tac chabdaṃ śrutvā hiraṇyako vyacintayat-kim anyo 'pi kaścit kapoto bandhana-śeṣas tiṣṭhati yena māṃ vyāharati | āha ca-bhoḥ ! ko bhavān ?
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, hearing that voice, thought — "Is there yet another pigeon remaining from the captive group, who is calling me?" And he said — "Sir! Who are you?"

children.text: sa āha-ahaṃ laghupatanako nāma vāyasaḥ |
children.translated_text: He replied — "I am a crow named <s>Laghupatanaka</s>."

children.text: tac chrutvā viśeṣād antarlīno hiraṇyaka āha-bhoḥ ! drutaṃ gamyatām asmāt sthānāt |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> withdrew even deeper inside and said — "Sir! Leave this place at once!"

children.text: vāyasa āha-ahaṃ tava pārśve guru-kāryeṇa samāgataḥ | tat kiṃ na kriyate mayā saha darśanam ?
children.translated_text: The crow said — "I have come to your side on a matter of great importance. Why then will you not grant me an audience?"

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-na me'sti tvayā saha saṅgamena prayojanam iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "I have no purpose to be served by association with you."

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ ! citragrīvasya mayā tava sakāśāt pāśa-mokṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam | tena mama mahatī prītiḥ sañjātā | tat kadācin mamāpi bandhane jāte tava pārśvān muktair bhaviṣyati | tat kriyatāṃ mayā saha maitrī |
children.translated_text: He said — "Sir! I witnessed the liberation of <s>Citragrīva</s> from his bonds through your help. From that, a great affection has arisen in me. If at some time I too should be caught in a trap, I would be freed through your assistance. Therefore, let there be friendship between us."

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-aho tvaṃ bhoktā | ahaṃ te bhojya-bhūtaḥ | tat kā tvayā saha mama maitrī ? tad gamyatām | maitrī virodha-bhāvāt katham ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "Alas! You are the eater, and I am your food. So what friendship can there be between you and me? Be on your way! How can there be friendship where there is natural enmity? And it is said —

children.text: yayor eva samaṃ vittaṃ yayor eva samaṃ kulam |
children.translated_text: Only between those whose wealth is equal, only between those whose lineage is equal,

children.text: tayor maitrī vivāhaś ca na tu puṣṭa-vipuṣṭayoḥ ||Panc_2.29||
children.translated_text: can there be friendship and marriage — never between the well-nourished and the ill-nourished. [Panc 2.29]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: yo mitraṃ kurute mūḍha ātmano 'sadṛśaṃ kudhīḥ |
children.translated_text: The fool of poor judgment who makes a friend unlike himself,

children.text: hīnaṃ vāpy adhikaṃ vāpi hāsyatāṃ yāty asau janaḥ ||Panc_2.30||
children.translated_text: whether inferior or superior, that person becomes an object of ridicule. [Panc 2.30]

children.text: tad gamyatām iti |
children.translated_text: So be on your way."

children.text: vāyasa āha-bho hiraṇyaka ! eṣo 'haṃ tava durga-dvāra upaviṣṭaḥ | yadi tvaṃ maitrī na karoṣi tato 'haṃ prāṇa-mokṣaṇaṃ tavāgre kariṣyāmi | athavā prāyopaveśanaṃ me syāt iti |
children.translated_text: The crow said — "O <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>! Here I am, seated at the entrance of your fortress. If you will not make friendship with me, then I shall give up my life before you. Or else I shall undertake a fast unto death."

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhoḥ ! tvayā vairiṇā saha kathaṃ maitrīṃ karomi ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "Sir! How can I make friendship with you, an enemy? It is said —

children.text: vairiṇā na hi sandadhyāt suśliṣṭenāpi sandhinā |
children.translated_text: One should not make a pact with an enemy, even with a well-joined alliance;

children.text: sutaptam api pānīyaṃ śamayaty eva pāvakam ||Panc_2.31||
children.translated_text: even well-heated water still extinguishes fire. [Panc 2.31]

children.text: vāyasa āha-bhoḥ ! tvayā saha darśanam api nāsti | kuto vairam ? tat kim anucitaṃ vadasi ?
children.translated_text: The crow said — "Sir! There has not even been a meeting between you and me. Whence then this enmity? Why do you speak what is unfitting?"

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-dvividhaṃ vairaṃ bhavati | sahajaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca | tat sahaja-vairī tvam asmākam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "Enmity is of two kinds — innate and acquired. You are our innate enemy. And it is said —

children.text: kṛtrimaṃ nāśam abhyeti vairaṃ drāk kṛtrimair guṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Acquired enmity quickly comes to an end through acquired virtues;

children.text: prāṇa-dānaṃ vinā vairaṃ sahajaṃ yāti na kṣayam ||Panc_2.32||
children.translated_text: but innate enmity does not perish without the sacrifice of life. [Panc 2.32]

children.text: vāyasa āha-bhoḥ ! dvividhasya vairasya lakṣaṇaṃ śrotum icchāmi | tat kathyatām |
children.translated_text: The crow said — "Sir! I wish to hear the characteristics of these two kinds of enmity. Pray tell me."

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhoḥ ! kāraṇena nirvṛtaṃ kṛtrimam | tat-tad-arhopakāra-karaṇād gacchati | svābhāvikaṃ punaḥ katham api na gacchati | tad yathā nakula-sarpāṇāṃ, śaṣpabhuṅ-nakhāyudhānāṃ, jala-vahnyoḥ, deva-daityānāṃ, sārameya-mārjarāṇāṃ, īśvara-daridrāṇāṃ, sapatnīnāṃ, siṃha-gajānāṃ, lubdhaka-hariṇānāṃ, śrotriya-bhraṣṭa-kriyāṇāṃ, mūrka-paṇḍitānāṃ, pativratā-kulaṭānāṃ, sajjana-durjanānām | na kaścit kenāpi vyāpāditaḥ, tathāpi prāṇān santāpayanti |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "Sir! That which arises from a cause is acquired enmity. It passes away through the rendering of appropriate services. But innate enmity never passes away. Such as that between mongooses and serpents, between herbivores and clawed predators, between water and fire, between gods and demons, between dogs and cats, between the rich and the poor, between co-wives, between lions and elephants, between hunters and deer, between the learned and the lapsed in observance, between the foolish and the wise, between faithful wives and wanton women, between the virtuous and the wicked. No one has been harmed by anyone in particular, yet they torment each other's lives."

children.text: vāyasa āha-bhoḥ ! akāraṇam etat | śrūyatāṃ me vacanam-
children.translated_text: The crow said — "Sir! This is without cause. Hear my words —

children.text: kāraṇān mitratām eti kāraṇād yāti śatrutām |
children.translated_text: Through cause one becomes a friend, and through cause one becomes an enemy;

children.text: tasmān mitratvam evātra yojyaṃ vairaṃ na dhīmatā ||Panc_2.33||
children.translated_text: therefore, a wise person should apply friendship here, not enmity. [Panc 2.33]

children.text: tasmāt kuru mayā saha samāgamaṃ mitra-dharmārtham |
children.translated_text: Therefore, make association with me for the sake of the duty of friendship."

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhoḥ, śrūyatāṃ nīti-sarvasvam-
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "Sir, hear the essence of all statecraft —

children.text: sakṛd duṣṭam apīṣṭaṃ yaḥ punaḥ sandhātum icchati |
children.translated_text: He who wishes to reconcile with one who has once proved hostile, even if that one appears friendly,

children.text: sa mṛtyum upagṛhṇāti garbham aśvatarī yathā ||Panc_2.34||
children.translated_text: embraces death, as a she-mule does her foetus. [Panc 2.34]

children.text: athavā guṇavān ahaṃ, na me kaścid vaira-yātanāṃ kariṣyati | etad api na sambhāvyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Or perhaps, since I am virtuous, no one will inflict the torments of enmity upon me — but even this cannot be relied upon. And it is said —

children.text: siṃho vyākaraṇasya kartur aharat prāṇān piryān pāṇiner
children.translated_text: A lion took the life of dear <s>Pāṇini</s>, the author of grammar;

children.text: mīmāṃsā-kṛtam unmamātha sahasā hastī muniṃ jaiminim |
children.translated_text: an elephant suddenly crushed the sage <s>Jaimini</s>, the author of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>;

children.text: chando-jñāna-nidhiṃ jaghāna makaro velā-taṭe piṅgalam
children.translated_text: a crocodile slew <s>Piṅgala</s>, that treasury of the knowledge of metre, on the seashore —

children.text: ajñānāvṛta-cetasām atiruṣā ko 'rthas tiraścāṃ guṇaiḥ ||Panc_2.35||
children.translated_text: what use are virtues to animals whose minds are clouded by ignorance and excessive rage? [Panc 2.35]

children.text: vāyasa āha-asty etat | yathāpi śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: The crow said — "That is so. But hear this as well —

children.text: upakārāc ca lokānāṃ nimittān mṛga-pakṣiṇām |
children.translated_text: Among people, friendship arises from mutual benefit; among animals and birds, from circumstance;

children.text: bhayāl lobhāc ca mūrkhāṇāṃ maitrī syād darśanāt satām ||Panc_2.36||
children.translated_text: among fools, from fear and greed; and among the virtuous, from mere sight. [Panc 2.36]

children.text: mṛd-ghaṭa iva sukha-bhedyo duḥsandhānaś ca durjano bhavati |
children.translated_text: A wicked person is like a clay pot — easily broken and hard to mend;

children.text: sujanas tu kanaka-ghaṭa iva durbhedaḥ sukara-sandhiś ca ||Panc_2.37||
children.translated_text: but a good person is like a golden pot — hard to break and easy to repair. [Panc 2.37]

children.text: ikṣor agrāt kramaśaḥ parvaṇi parvaṇi yathā rasa-viśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as sugarcane yields progressively richer juice from the tip downward, joint by joint,

children.text: tadvat sajjana-maitrī-viparītānāṃ tu viparītā ||Panc_2.38||
children.translated_text: so too is the friendship of the virtuous — and for the opposite sort, it is the reverse. [Panc 2.38]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: ārambha-gurvī kṣayiṇī krameṇa laghvī purā vṛddhimatī ca paścāt |
children.translated_text: Heavy at the start and diminishing by degrees; light at first and growing greater afterward —

children.text: dinasya pūrvārdha-parārdha-bhinnā chāyeva maitrī khala-sajjanānām ||Panc_2.39||
children.translated_text: like a shadow in the first and latter halves of the day, so is the friendship of the wicked and the virtuous. [Panc 2.39]

children.text: tat sādhur aham | aparaṃ tvāṃ śapathādibhir nirbhayaṃ kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: I am indeed virtuous. Moreover, I shall reassure you with oaths and the like."

children.text: sa āha-na me'sti te śapathaiḥ pratyayaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said — "I have no confidence in your oaths. And it is said —

children.text: śapathaiḥ sandhitasyāpi na viśvāsaṃ vrajed ripoḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not trust an enemy even when bound by oaths, however well-joined the alliance may be;

children.text: śrūyate śapathaṃ kṛtvā vṛtraḥ śakreṇa sūditaḥ ||Panc_2.40||
children.translated_text: it is told that <s>Vṛtra</s>, though bound by oath, was slain by <s>Śakra</s>. [Panc 2.40]

children.text: na viśvāsaṃ vinā śatrur devānām api sidhyati |
children.translated_text: Without trust, even an enemy of the gods does not succeed;

children.text: viśvāsāt tridaśendreṇa diter garbho vidāritaḥ ||Panc_2.41||
children.translated_text: through trust, <s>Diti</s>'s embryo was split asunder by the lord of the gods. [Panc 2.41]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: bṛhaspater api prājñas tasmān naivātra viśvaset |
children.translated_text: Even one wiser than <s>Bṛhaspati</s> should never place trust in this matter —

children.text: ya icched ātmano buddhim āyuṣyaṃ ca sukhāni ca ||Panc_2.42||
children.translated_text: he who desires his own wisdom, long life, and happiness. [Panc 2.42]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: susūkṣmeṇāpi randhreṇa praviśyābhyantaraṃ ripuḥ |
children.translated_text: Through even the tiniest opening, an enemy enters within,

children.text: nāśayec ca śanaiḥ paścāt plavaṃ salila-pūravat ||Panc_2.43||
children.translated_text: and then destroys gradually, like a flood of water sinking a raft. [Panc 2.43]

children.text: na viśvased aviśvaste viśvaste'pi na viśvaset |
children.translated_text: One should not trust the untrustworthy, nor should one trust even the trustworthy;

children.text: viśvāsād bhayam utpannaṃ mūlāny api nikṛntati ||Panc_2.44||
children.translated_text: for danger born of trust cuts away even the roots. [Panc 2.44]

children.text: na badhyate hy aviśvasto durbalo 'pi balotkaṭaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The distrustful, even if weak, is not overcome by the exceedingly strong;

children.text: viśvastāś cāśu badhyante balavanto 'pi durbalaiḥ ||Panc_2.45||
children.translated_text: while the trusting, even if powerful, are quickly overcome by the weak. [Panc 2.45]

children.text: sukṛtyaṃ viṣṇu-guptasya mitrāptir bhārgavasya ca |
children.translated_text: The good deed of <s>Viṣṇugupta</s>, the winning of allies by <s>Bhārgava</s>,

children.text: bṛhaspater aviśvāso nītir-sandhis tridhā sthitaḥ ||Panc_2.46||
children.translated_text: and the distrust of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> — statecraft stands as a threefold alliance. [Panc 2.46]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: mahatāpy artha-sāreṇa yo viśvasiti śatruṣu |
children.translated_text: He who trusts his enemies, however great the advantage may be,

children.text: bhāryāsu suviraktāsu tad-antaṃ tasya jīvitam ||Panc_2.47||
children.translated_text: or his wives who are deeply estranged — his life comes to an end thereby. [Panc 2.47]

children.text: tac chrutvā laghupatanako 'pi niruttaraś cintayāmāsa-aho, buddhi-prāgalbhyam asya nīti-viṣaye | athavā sa evāsyopari maitrī-pakṣapātaḥ | sa āha-bho hiraṇyaka !
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> too was rendered speechless and thought — "Ah, what boldness of intellect he has in matters of statecraft! Yet that very quality is itself a reason to favor friendship with him." He said — "O <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>!

children.text: satāṃ sāptapadaṃ maitram ity āhur vibudhā janāḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise declare that friendship among the virtuous is established in seven steps;

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ mitratāṃ prāpto vacanaṃ mama tac chṛṇu ||Panc_2.48||
children.translated_text: therefore you have attained the status of a friend — now hear my words. [Panc 2.48]

children.text: durgasthenāpi tvayā mayā saha nityam evālāpo guṇa-doṣa-subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-kathāḥ sarvadā kartavyāḥ, yady evaṃ na viśvasiṣi |
children.translated_text: Even while remaining within your fortress, you should always engage in conversation with me — discussions of merits and faults, exchanges of wise sayings and stories — if you will not trust me otherwise."

children.text: tac chrutvā hiraṇyako 'pi vyacintayat-vidagdha-vacano 'yaṃ dṛśyate laghupatanakaḥ satya-vākyaś ca tad yuktam anena maitrī-karaṇam | paraṃ kadācin mama durge caraṇa-pāto 'pi na kāryaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> too thought — "This <s>Laghupatanaka</s> appears to be eloquent and truthful in his words. It is fitting, then, to establish friendship with him. However, he must never set foot in my fortress." And it is said —

children.text: bhīta-bhītaiḥ purā śatrur mandaṃ mandaṃ visarpati |
children.translated_text: At first, the enemy creeps slowly, timidly, step by step;

children.text: bhūmau prahelayā paścāj jāra-hasto 'ṅganāsv iva ||Panc_2.49||
children.translated_text: but afterward, over the ground with boldness — like the hand of a lover upon women. [Panc 2.49]
