children.text: tac chrutvā vāyasa āha-bhadra, evaṃ bhavatu | tataḥ-prabhṛti tau dvāv api subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-sukham anubhavantau tiṣṭhataḥ | parasparaṃ kṛtopakārau kālaṃ nayataḥ | laghupatanako 'pi māṃsa-śakalāni medhyāni baliśeṣāṇy anyāni vātsalyāhṛtāni pakvānna-viśeṣāṇi hiraṇyakārtham ānayati | hiraṇyako 'pi taṇḍulān anyāṃś ca bhakṣya-viśeṣāl laghupatanakārthaṃ rātrāv āhṛtya tat-kālāyātasyārpayati | athavā yujyate dvayor apy etat | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the crow said — "Dear friend, let it be so." From that time onward, the two of them remained, enjoying the pleasure of sharing wise sayings. They passed the time rendering services to one another. <s>Laghupatanaka</s> would bring for <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> clean pieces of meat, remnants of offerings, and various cooked delicacies gathered with affection. <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, in turn, would gather rice and other choice edibles at night for <s>Laghupatanaka</s> and present them to him when he came at the appointed time. Indeed, this was fitting for both of them. And it is said —

children.text: dadāti pratigṛhṇāti guhyam ākhyāti pṛcchati |
children.translated_text: Giving and receiving, telling secrets and asking them,

children.text: bhuṅkte bhojāyate caiva ṣaḍ-vidhaṃ prīti-lakṣaṇam ||Panc_2.50||
children.translated_text: eating together and feeding another — these are the six marks of affection. [Panc 2.50]

children.text: nopakāraṃ vinā prītiḥ kathañcit kasyacid bhavet |
children.translated_text: Without mutual service, affection cannot arise in anyone by any means;

children.text: upayācita-dānena yato devā abhīṣṭadāḥ ||Panc_2.51||
children.translated_text: since even the gods grant wishes only in response to offerings made with prayer. [Panc 2.51]

children.text: tāvat prītir bhavel loke yāvad dānaṃ pradīyate |
children.translated_text: Affection in this world lasts only as long as gifts are given;

children.text: vatsaḥ kṣīra-kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā parityajati mātaram ||Panc_2.52||
children.translated_text: a calf, seeing the milk exhausted, abandons its own mother. [Panc 2.52]

children.text: paśya dānasya māhātmyaṃ sadyaḥ pratyaya-kārakam |
children.translated_text: Behold the greatness of giving, which instantly produces trust;

children.text: yat-prabhāvād api dveṣo mitratāṃ yāti tat-kṣaṇāt ||Panc_2.53||
children.translated_text: by its power, even enmity turns to friendship in that very moment. [Panc 2.53]

children.text: putrād api priyataraṃ khalu tena dānaṃ
children.translated_text: Giving is dearer even than a son — so I believe —

children.text: manye paśor api viveka-vivarjitasya |
children.translated_text: even to an animal devoid of discrimination;

children.text: datte khale tu nikhilaṃ khalu yena dugdhaṃ
children.translated_text: for when the wicked one takes all the milk that has been given,

children.text: nityaṃ dadāti mahiṣī sasutāpi paśya ||Panc_2.54||
children.translated_text: the buffalo still gives daily, even with her calf beside her — behold! [Panc 2.54]

children.text: kiṃ bahunā-
children.translated_text: In short —

children.text: prītiṃ nirantarāṃ kṛtvā durbhedyāṃ nakha-māṃsavat |
children.translated_text: Having formed an unbroken affection, inseparable as nail and flesh,

children.text: mūṣako vāyasaś caiva gatau kṛtrima-mitratām ||Panc_2.55||
children.translated_text: the mouse and the crow attained an acquired friendship. [Panc 2.55]

children.text: evaṃ sa mūṣakas tad-upakāra-rañjitas tathā viśvasto yathā tasya pakṣa-madhye praviṣṭas tena saha sarvadaiva goṣṭhīṃ karoti | athānyasminn ahani vāyaso 'śru-pūrṇa-nayanaḥ samabhyetya sagadgadaṃ tam uvāca-bhadra hiraṇyaka, viraktiḥ sañjātā me sāmprataṃ deśasyāsyopari tad anyatra yāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: Thus the mouse, won over by his services, trusted him so completely that he would enter between his wings and always converse with him. Then one day, the crow came with eyes full of tears and spoke to him in a choked voice — "Dear <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, a disenchantment has come over me now with this land. I shall go elsewhere."

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhadra kiṃ virakteḥ kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "Dear friend, what is the cause of your disenchantment?"

children.text: sa āha-bhadra, śrūyatāṃ | atra deśe mahatyānāvṛṣṭyā durbhikṣaṃ sañjātam | durbhikṣatvāj jano bubhukṣā-pīḍitaḥ ko 'pi bali-mātram api na prayacchati | aparaṃ gṛhe gṛhe bubhukṣita-janair vihaṅgānāṃ bandhanāya pāśāḥ praguṇīkṛtāḥ santi | aham apy āyuḥ-śeṣatayā pāśena baddha uddharito 'smi | etad virakteḥ kāraṇam æ| tenāhaṃ videśaṃ calita iti bāṣpa-mokṣaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: He said — "Dear friend, listen. In this land, a great famine has arisen due to a severe drought. Because of the famine, the people, afflicted by hunger, do not give even so much as the remnants of an offering. Moreover, in every house, the starving folk have set out snares for trapping birds. I too, by the remaining merit of my life, was caught in a snare but managed to escape. This is the cause of my disenchantment. Therefore I am departing for another land, shedding tears as I go."

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-atha bhavān kva prasthitaḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said — "And where does your honor intend to go?"

children.text: sa āha-asti dakṣiṇā-pathe vana-gahana-madhye mahāsaraḥ | tatra tvatto 'dhikaḥ parama-suhṛt kūrmo mantharako nāma | sa ca me matsya-māṃsa-khaṇḍāni dāsyati | tad-bhakṣaṇāt tena saha subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-sukham anubhavan sukhena kālaṃ neṣyāmi | nāham atra vihaṅgānāṃ pāśa-bandhanena kṣayaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi | uktaṃ ca-
anāvṛṣṭi-hate deśe sasye ca pralayaṃ gate |
children.translated_text: When a land is ravaged by drought and the crops have perished,

children.text: dhanyās tāta na paśyanti deśa-bhaṅgaṃ kula-kṣayam ||Panc_2.56||
children.translated_text: blessed are those, dear one, who do not witness the ruin of their land and the destruction of their family. [Panc 2.56]

He said — "On the southern road, in the midst of a dense forest, there is a great lake. There dwells a tortoise named <s>Manthara</s>, a dearer friend than even you. He will give me pieces of fish and meat. Eating those and enjoying the pleasure of sharing wise sayings with him, I shall pass the time happily. I do not wish to remain here and witness the destruction of birds through the snares. And it is said —

children.text: ko 'tibhāraḥ samarthānāṃ kiṃ dūraṃ vyavasāyinām |
children.translated_text: What burden is too heavy for the capable? What is too far for the industrious?

children.text: ko videśaḥ savidyānāṃ kaḥ paraḥ priya-vādinām ||Panc_2.57||
children.translated_text: What land is foreign for the learned? Who is a stranger to those who speak kindly? ||Panc_2.57||

children.text: vidvattvaṃ ca nṛpatvaṃ ca naiva tulyaṃ kadācana |
children.translated_text: Scholarship and kingship are never equal;

children.text: sva-deśe pūjyate rājā vidvān sarvatra pūjyate ||Panc_2.58||
children.translated_text: a king is honored in his own country, but a scholar is honored everywhere. ||Panc_2.58||

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-yady evaṃ tad aham api tvayā saha gamiṣyāmi | mamāpi mahad duḥkhaṃ vartate |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'If so, then I too shall go with you. I also have great sorrow.'

children.text: vāyasa āha-bhoḥ ! tava kiṃ duḥkham ? tat kathaya |
children.translated_text: The crow said: 'Friend! What is your sorrow? Tell me.'

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhoḥ ! bahu vaktavyam asty atra viṣaye | tatraiva gatvā sarvaṃ savistaraṃ kathayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'Friend! There is much to be said on this matter. Having gone there, I shall relate everything in detail.'

children.text: vāyasa āha-ahaṃ tāvad ākāśa-gatiḥ | tat kathaṃ bhavato mayā saha gamanam ?
children.translated_text: The crow said: 'I travel through the sky. So how can you travel with me?'

children.text: sa āha-yadi me prāṇān rakṣasi tadā sva-pṛṣṭham āropya māṃ tatra prāpayiṣyasi | nānyathā mama gatir asti |
children.translated_text: He said: 'If you protect my life, then mounting me on your back, you will convey me there. Otherwise I have no means of going.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sānandaṃ vāyasa āha-yady evaṃ tad dhanyo 'haṃ yad bhavatāpi saha tatra kālaṃ nayāmi | ahaṃ sampātādikān aṣāv uḍḍīna-gati-viśeṣān vedmi | tat samāroha mama pṛṣṭhaṃ, yena sukhena tvāṃ tat-saraḥ prāpayāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crow said joyfully: 'If so, then I am fortunate that I shall pass time there with you as well. I know these eight special modes of bird-flight beginning with <s>sampāta</s> (swooping). So mount my back, and I shall convey you to that lake with ease.'

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-uḍḍīnānāṃ nāmāni śrotum icchāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: 'I wish to hear the names of the flights.'

children.text: sa āha-
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text: sampātaṃ vipra-pātaṃ ca mahā-pātaṃ nipātanam |
children.translated_text: Swooping, plunging, soaring, diving,

children.text: vakraṃ tiryak tathā cordhvam aṣṭamaṃ laghu-saṃjñakam ||Panc_2.59||
children.translated_text: oblique, sideways, and upward — the eighth is called 'light.' ||Panc_2.59||

children.text: tac chrutvā hiraṇyakas tat-kṣaṇād eva tad upari samārūḍhaḥ | so 'pi śanaiḥ śanais tam ādāya sampātoḍḍīna-prasthitaḥ krameṇa tat-saraḥ prāptaḥ | tato laghupatanakaṃ mūṣakādhiṣṭhitaṃ vilokya dūrato 'pi deśa-kāla-vida-sāmānya-kāko 'yam iti jñātvā satvaraṃ mantharako jale praviṣṭaḥ | laghupatanako 'pi tīrastha-taru-koṭare hiraṇyakaṃ muktvā śākhāgram āruhya tāra-svareṇa provāca-bho mantharaka ! āgacchāgaccha | tava mitram ahaṃ laghupatanako nāma vāyasaś cirāt sotkaṇṭhaḥ samāyātaḥ | tad āgatyāliṅgaya mām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> at that very instant climbed upon his back. And he [the crow], taking him slowly, slowly, setting out with a swooping flight, gradually reached that lake. Then <s>Mantharaka</s> (the turtle), seeing <s>Laghupatanaka</s> (the crow) from afar with a mouse mounted [on him], recognizing — as one who knows place and time — that this was an ordinary crow, quickly entered the water. <s>Laghupatanaka</s> too, having left <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> in a tree-hollow on the bank, climbed to a branch-top and called out in a loud voice: 'O <s>Mantharaka</s>! Come, come! I am your friend, the crow named <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, arrived after a long time with longing. So come and embrace me!' And it is said:

children.text: kiṃ candanaiḥ sa-karpūrais tuhinaiḥ kiṃ ca śītalaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What use is sandalwood, or camphor, or cool snow?

children.text: sarve te mitra-gātrasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||Panc_2.60||
children.translated_text: All these are not worth a sixteenth part of a friend's body. ||Panc_2.60||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: kenāmṛtam idaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mitram ity akṣara-dvayam |
children.translated_text: By whom was this nectar created — the two syllables '<s>mitra</s>' (friend)?

children.text: āpadāṃ ca paritrāṇaṃ śoka-santāpa-bheṣajam ||Panc_2.61||
children.translated_text: A deliverance from adversities, a medicine for grief and anguish. ||Panc_2.61||

children.text: tac chrutvā nipuṇataraṃ parijñāya satvaraṃ salilān niṣkramya pulakita-tanur ānandāśru-pūrita-nayano mantharakaḥ provāca-ehy ehi mitra, āliṅgaya mām | cira-kālān mayā tvaṃ na samyak parijñātaḥ | tenāhaṃ salilāntaḥ-praviṣṭaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, having recognized him more closely, <s>Mantharaka</s> quickly emerged from the water, his body covered in goosebumps and his eyes filled with tears of joy, and said: 'Come, come, friend, embrace me! For a long time I did not properly recognize you. That is why I entered the water.' And it is said:

children.text: yasya na jñāyate vīryaṃ na kulaṃ na viceṣṭitam |
children.translated_text: One whose valor, family, and conduct are not known —

children.text: na tena saṅgatiṃ kuryād ity uvāca bṛhaspatiḥ ||Panc_2.62||
children.translated_text: one should not associate with him — so said <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. ||Panc_2.62||

children.text: evam ukte laghupatanako vṛkṣād avatīrya tam āliṅgitavān | athavā sādhv idam uktam-
amṛtasya pravāhaiḥ kiṃ kāya-kṣālana-sambhavaiḥ |
children.translated_text: What use are streams of nectar that merely cleanse the body?

children.text: cirān mitra-pariṣvaṅgo yo 'sau mūlya-vivarjitaḥ ||Panc_2.63||
children.translated_text: The embrace of a friend after a long time — that is priceless. ||Panc_2.63||
When this was said, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> descended from the tree and embraced him. Or rather, this is well said:

children.text: evaṃ dvāv api tau vihitāliṅgitau parasparaṃ pulakita-śarīrī vṛkṣād adhaḥ samupaviṣṭau procatur ātma-caritra-vṛttāntam | hiraṇyako 'pi mantharakasya praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā vāyasābhyāśe samupaviṣṭaḥ | atha taṃ samālokya mantharako laghupatanakam āha-bhoḥ hiraṇyako nāma mūṣako 'yam | mama suhṛd-dvitīyam iva jīvitam | tat kiṃ bahunā-
children.translated_text: Thus the two of them, having embraced each other, their bodies thrilling, descended from the tree, sat down below, and related to each other the accounts of their lives. <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> too, having bowed to <s>Mantharaka</s>, sat down near the crow. Then, looking at him, <s>Mantharaka</s> said to <s>Laghupatanaka</s>: 'Friend! This is the mouse named <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> — like a second life to my dear friend. In short:'

children.text: parjanyasya yathā dhārā yathā ca divi tārakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the streams of a rain-cloud, just as the stars in the sky,

children.text: sikatā-reṇavo yadvat saṅkhyayā parivarjitā ||Panc_2.64||
children.translated_text: just as grains of sand — are beyond counting, ||Panc_2.64||

children.text: guṇāḥ saṅkhyā-parityaktās tadvad asya mahātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: so are the virtues of this great soul — beyond enumeration.

children.text: paraṃ nirvedam āpannaḥ samprāpto 'yaṃ tavāntikam ||Panc_2.65||
children.translated_text: But having reached a state of disenchantment, he has come to your vicinity. ||Panc_2.65||

children.text: mantharaka āha-kim asya vairāgya-kāraṇam ?
children.translated_text: <s>Mantharaka</s> said: 'What is the cause of his disenchantment?'

children.text: vāyasa āha-pṛṣṭo mayā, param anenābhihitaṃ, yad bahu vaktavyam iti | tat tatraiva gataḥ kathayiṣyāmi | mamāpi na niveditam | tad bhadra hiraṇyaka ! idānīṃ nivedyatām ubhayor apy āvayos tad ātmano vairāgya-kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: The crow said: 'I asked him, but he said that there is much to tell. He said he would relate [it] once we arrived there. He has not told even me. So, dear <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>! Now tell both of us the cause of your disenchantment.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text:
kathā 1
hiraṇyaka-tāmracūḍa-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 1
The story of <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> and <s>Tāmracūḍa</s>

children.text:
asti dakṣiṇātye janapade mahilāropyaṃ nāma nagaram | tasya nātidūre maṭhāyatanaṃ bhagavataḥ śrī-mahādevasya | tatra ca tāmracūḍo nāma parivrājakaḥ prativasati sma | sa ca nagare bhikṣāṭanaṃ kṛtvā prāṇa-yātrāṃ samācarati | bhikṣā-śeṣaṃ ca tatraiva bhikṣā-pātre nidhāya tad-bhikṣā-pātraṃ nāgadante'valambya paścād rātrau svapiti | pratyūṣe ca tad-annaṃ karmakarāṇāṃ dattvā samyak tatraiva devatāyatane saṃmārjanopalepana-maṇḍanādikaṃ samājñāpayati | anyasminn ahani mama bāndhavair niveditam-svāmin, maṭhāyatane siddham annaṃ mūṣaka-bhayāt tatraiva bhikṣā-pātre nihitaṃ nāgadante'valambitaṃ tiṣṭhati sadaiva | tad vayaṃ bhakṣayituṃ na śaknumaḥ | svāminaḥ punar āgamya kim api nāsti | tat kiṃ vṛthāṭanenānyatra | adya
tatra gatvā yathecchaṃ bhuñjāmahe tava prasādāt |
children.translated_text: In the southern country there is a city called <s>Mahilāropya</s>. Not far from it is a monastery of the blessed Lord <s>Śrī Mahādeva</s>. And there a mendicant named <s>Tāmracūḍa</s> used to dwell. He would go begging in the city and thereby sustain his livelihood. The remainder of his alms he would keep in his begging-bowl right there, hanging the bowl on a wall-peg, and then sleep at night. At dawn, he would give that food to workers and properly order the sweeping, plastering, and decoration of that very temple. One day, my kinsmen reported to me: 'Sir, the prepared food in the monastery is always kept in the begging-bowl, hung on a wall-peg, out of fear of mice. So we are unable to eat it. Moreover, when the master returns, there is nothing [left for him either]. So what is the use of vainly going elsewhere? Today, having gone there, let us eat as we please, by your grace.'

children.text: tad ākarṇyāhaṃ sakala-yūtha-parivṛtas tat-kṣaṇād eva tatra gataḥ | utpatya ca tasmin bhikṣā-pātre samārūḍhaḥ | tatra bhakṣya-viśeṣāṇi sevakebhyo dattvā paścāt svayam eva bhakṣayāmi | sarveṣāṃ tṛptau jātāyāṃ bhūyaḥ sva-gṛhaṃ gacchāmi | evaṃ nityam eva tad annaṃ bhakṣayāmi | parivrājako 'pi yathā-śakti rakṣati | paraṃ yadaiva nidrāntarito bhavati, tadāhaṃ tatrāruhyātma-kṛtyaṃ karomi | atha kadācit tena mama rakṣaṇārthaṃ mahān yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ | jarjara-vaṃśaḥ samānītaḥ | tena supto 'pi mama bhayād bhikṣā-pātraṃ tāḍayati | aham apy abhikṣite'py anne prahāra-bhayād apasarpāmi | evaṃ tena saha sakalāṃ rātriṃ vigraha-parasya kālo vrajati |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, I — surrounded by my entire troop — went there that very instant. Having leaped up, I mounted that begging-bowl. There, having given special delicacies to my followers, afterwards I ate myself. When all were satisfied, I returned to my own home. Thus I ate that food daily. The mendicant too guarded [it] as best he could. But whenever he became overtaken by sleep, then I would climb up there and do my work. Then once, he made a great effort for my protection: he brought a worn bamboo staff. With that, even while sleeping, he would strike the begging-bowl out of fear of me. And I, even when there was no food to be had, would retreat out of fear of blows. Thus, battling with him through the entire night, time passed.

children.text: athānyasminn ahani tasya maṭhe bṛhatsphiṅ-nāmā parivrājakas tasya suhṛt tīrtha-yātrā-prasaṅgena pānthaḥ prāghuṇikaḥ samāyātaḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyutthāna-vidhinā sambhāvya pratipatti-pūrvakam abhyāgata-kriyayā niyojitaḥ | tataś ca rātrāv ekatra kuśa-saṃstare dvāv api prasuptau dharma-kathāṃ kathayitum ārabdhau |
children.translated_text: Then, on another day, a mendicant named <s>Bṛhatsphij</s>, a friend of his, arrived at his monastery as a guest, traveling on pilgrimage. Seeing him, [<s>Tāmracūḍa</s>] received him with the protocol of rising, honored him with due hospitality, and attended to him as a guest. Then at night, the two lay down together on a mat of <s>kuśa</s> grass and began to tell stories of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: atha bṛhasphik-kathā-goṣṭhīṣu sa tāmracūḍo mūṣaka-trāsārthaṃ vyākṣipta-manā jarjara-vaṃśena bhikṣā-pātraṃ tāḍayaṃs tasya śūnyaṃ prativacanaṃ prayacchati | tan-mayo na kiñcid udāharati | athāsāv abhyāgataḥ paraṃ kopam upāgatas tam uvāca-bhos tāmracūḍa ! parijñātaḥ na tvaṃ samyak suhṛt | tena mayā saha sāhlādaṃ na jalpasi | tad-rātrāv api tvadīyaṃ maṭhaṃ tyaktvānyatra mañhe yāsyāmi | uktaṃ ca-
ehy āgaccha samāviśāsanam idaṃ kasmāc cirād dṛśyase kā vārteti sudurbalo 'si kuśalaṃ prīto 'smi te darśanāt |
children.translated_text: 'Come, come in, sit down — why are you seen after so long? What news? You look weak — are you well? I am delighted to see you!'

children.text: evaṃ ye samupāgatān praṇayinaḥ pratyālapanty ādarāt teṣāṃ yuktam aśaṅkitena manasā harmyāṇi gantuṃ sadā ||Panc_2.66||
children.translated_text: Those who thus address newcomers with affection and respect — one should always go to their mansions with an untroubled mind. ||Panc_2.66||

Now, during <s>Bṛhatsphij</s>'s storytelling sessions, that <s>Tāmracūḍa</s>, with his mind distracted by fear of the mouse, would strike the begging-bowl with the worn bamboo staff and give him [only] empty replies — absorbed [in the mouse], he would say nothing [of substance]. Then the guest, becoming greatly angered, said to him: 'Ho, <s>Tāmracūḍa</s>! It is clear you are not a true friend. That is why you do not converse gladly with me. Then tonight too, abandoning your monastery, I shall go to another monastery.' And it is said:

children.text: gṛhī yatrāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā diśo vīkṣeta vāpy adhaḥ |
children.translated_text: A householder who, upon seeing a guest arrive, looks to the directions or downward —

children.text: tatra ye sadane yānti te śṛṅga-rahitā vṛṣāḥ ||Panc_2.67||
children.translated_text: those who go to such a house are like bulls without horns [i.e., without pride]. ||Panc_2.67||

children.text: sābhyutthāna-kriyā yatra nālāpā madhurākṣarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there is no rising in welcome, no sweet-worded conversation,

children.text: guṇa-doṣa-kathā naiva tatra harmyaṃ na gamyate ||Panc_2.68||
children.translated_text: no talk of merits and faults — one should not go to such a mansion. ||Panc_2.68||

children.text: tad eka-maṭha-prāptyāpi tvaṃ garvitaḥ | tyaktaḥ suhṛt-snehaḥ | naitad vetsi yat tvayā maṭhāśraya-vyājena narakopārjanaṃ kṛtam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So, having obtained even a single monastery, you are puffed up! You have abandoned the affection of friendship! You do not know that by the pretext of sheltering in a monastery, you have earned [a place in] hell.' And it is said:

children.text: narakāya matis te cet paurohityaṃ samācāra |
children.translated_text: 'If your mind is set on hell, take up the office of a family priest;

children.text: varṣaṃ yāvat kim anyena maṭha-cintāṃ dina-trayam ||Panc_2.69||
children.translated_text: why anything else for a year? — the worry of a monastery for three days [is enough].' ||Panc_2.69||

children.text: tan-mukhaṃ, śocitavyas tvaṃ garvaṃ gataḥ | tad ahaṃ tvadīyaṃ maṭhaṃ parityajya yāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: 'That [is the truth]; you are to be pitied, having become proud. So I shall abandon your monastery and go.'

children.text: atha tac chrutvā bhaya-trasta-manās tāmracūḍas tam uvāca-bho bhagavan ! maivaṃ vada | na tvat-samo 'nyo mama suhṛt kaścid asti | paraṃ tac chrūyatāṃ goṣṭhī-śaithilya-kāraṇam | eṣa durātmā mūṣakaḥ pronnata-sthāne dhṛtam api bhikṣā-pātram utplutyārohati, bhikṣā-śeṣaṃca tatrasthaṃ bhakṣayati | tad-abhāvād eva maṭhe mārjana-kriyāpi na bhavati | tan mūṣaka
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that, <s>Tāmracūḍa</s>, his mind frightened and alarmed, said to him: 'O venerable one! Do not speak thus! There is no other friend like you to me. But hear the reason for the slackness in conversation. This wicked mouse leaps up and climbs onto the begging-bowl even when it is placed in an elevated spot, and eats the leftover alms kept there. Because of its [eating everything], even the cleaning work in the monastery does not happen. That is why I strike

children.text: muhur muhus tāḍayāmi | nānyat kāraṇam iti | aparam etat kutūhalaṃ paśyāsya durtātmano yan mārjāra-markaṭādayo 'pi tiraskṛtā asyotpatanena |
children.translated_text: again and again — there is no other reason.' 'Moreover, observe this marvel of the wicked one — that even cats and monkeys are put to shame by his leaping.'

children.text: bṛhatsphig āha-atha jñāyate tasya bilaṃ kasmiṃścit pradeśe |
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhatsphij</s> said: 'Is the location of his hole known in some place?'

children.text: tāmracūḍa āha-bhagavan na vedmi samyak |
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmracūḍa</s> said: 'Venerable one, I do not know exactly.'

children.text: sa āha-nūnaṃ nidhānasyopari tasya bilam | nidhānoṣmaṇā prakūrdate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Surely his hole is above a [buried] treasure. By the heat of the treasure he is energized.' And it is said:

children.text: ūṣmāpi vittajo vṛddhiṃ tejo nayati dehinām |
children.translated_text: Even the mere warmth from wealth brings growth of vigor to embodied beings;

children.text: kiṃ punas tasya sambhogas tyāga-dharma-samanvitaḥ ||Panc_2.70||
children.translated_text: how much more so its enjoyment, accompanied by the virtue of generosity! ||Panc_2.70||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: nākasmāc chāṇḍilī mātar vikrīṇāti tilais tilān |
children.translated_text: 'Not without cause, Mother <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>, does she sell sesame for sesame;

children.text: luñcitān itarair yena hetur atra bhaviṣyati ||Panc_2.71||
children.translated_text: the ones [she sells] are shelled by others — there must be a reason here.' ||Panc_2.71||

children.text: tāmracūḍa āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmracūḍa</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: sa āha-
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text:
kathā 2
tilacūrṇa-vikraya-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 2
The story of selling sesame powder

children.text: yadāhaṃ kasmiṃścit sthāne prāvṛṭ-kāle vrata-grahaṇa-nimittaṃ kañcid brāhmaṇaṃ vāsārthaṃ prārthitavān | tataś ca tad-vacanāt tenāpi śuśrūṣitaḥ sukhena devārcana-paras tiṣṭhāmi | athānyasminn ahani pratyūṣe prabuddho 'haṃ brāhmaṇa-brāhmaṇī-saṃvāde dattāvadhānaḥ śṛṇomi | tatra brāhmaṇa āha-brāhmaṇi, prabhāte dakṣiṇāyana-saṅkrāntir ananta-dāna-phaladā bhaviṣyati | tad ahaṃ pratigrahārthaṃ grāmāntaraṃ yāsyāmi | tvayā brāhmaṇasyaikasya bhagavataḥ sūryasyoddeśena kiñcid bhojanaṃ dātavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Once, when I was in a certain place during the rainy season, I had asked a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for shelter for the purpose of observing a vow. Then, by his word, being attended by him, I lived comfortably, devoted to the worship of the deity. On another day, having awakened at dawn, I gave attention and listened to a conversation between the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and his wife. There the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'Wife, tomorrow at dawn there will be the <s>dakṣiṇāyana-saṅkrānti</s> (winter solstice), which yields infinite fruit for gifts. So I shall go to another village for the purpose of receiving gifts. You should give some food to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for the sake of the blessed Sun.'

children.text: atha tac chrutvā brāhmaṇī paruṣatara-vacanais taṃ bhartsayamānā prāha-kutas te dāridryopahatasya bhojana-prāptiḥ | tat kiṃ lajjasa evaṃ bruvāṇaḥ | api ca na mayā tava hasta-lagnayā kvacid api labdhaṃ sukham | na miṣṭhānnasyāsvādanam | na ca hasta-pāda-kaṇṭhādi-bhūṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the wife, berating him with very harsh words, said: 'Whence will you, afflicted by poverty, obtain food? Are you not ashamed to say such things? Moreover, I — clinging to your hand [in marriage] — have never anywhere obtained happiness. No tasting of fine food! Nor any ornament for hands, feet, or neck!'

children.text: tac chrutvā bhaya-trasto 'pi vipro mandaṃ mandaṃ prāha-brāhmaṇi ! naitad yujyate vaktum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, though frightened, said softly: 'Wife! It is not proper to say this.' And it is said:

children.text: grāsād api tad ardhaṃ ca kasmān no dīyate'rthiṣu |
children.translated_text: From [even] a morsel, why should not half of it be given to supplicants?

children.text: icchānurūpo vibhavaḥ kadā kasya bhaviṣyati ||Panc_2.72||
children.translated_text: When will wealth proportionate to [one's] desire ever come to anyone? ||Panc_2.72||

children.text: īśvarā bhūri-dānena yal labhante phalaṃ kila |
children.translated_text: Lords, by lavish giving, whatever fruit they obtain —

children.text: daridras tac ca kākiṇyā prāpnuyād iti na śrutiḥ ||Panc_2.73||
children.translated_text: and that a poor man would obtain it for a cowrie-shell — there is no such scripture. // Panc_2.73 //

children.text: dātā laghur api sevyo bhavati na kṛpaṇo mahān api samṛddhyā |
children.translated_text: A giver, however small, deserves to be served; not a miser, however great in prosperity.

children.text: kūpo 'ntaḥ-svādu-jalaḥ prītyai lokasya na samudraḥ ||Panc_2.74||
children.translated_text: A well with sweet water inside gives delight to the people — not the ocean. // Panc_2.74 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: akṛta-tyāga-mahimnāṃ mithyā kiṃ rāja-rāja-śabdena |
children.translated_text: For those who have not attained the glory of generosity, what use is the empty title 'king of kings'?

children.text: goptāraṃ na nidhīnāṃ mahayanti maheśvaraṃ vibudhāḥ ||Panc_2.75||
children.translated_text: The gods do not honor <s>Maheśvara</s> (Śiva) as [merely] the guardian of treasures. // Panc_2.75 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: sadā dāna-parikṣīṇaḥ śasta eva karīśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord of elephants, ever diminished by giving, is always praised;

children.text: adānaḥ pīna-gātro 'pi nindya eva hi gardabhaḥ ||Panc_2.76||
children.translated_text: the donkey, though fat-limbed and giving nothing, is always despised. // Panc_2.76 //

children.text: suśīlo 'pi suvṛtto 'pi yāty adānād adho ghaṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though well-mannered and well-behaved, a pot sinks downward because it gives nothing;

children.text: punaḥ kubjāpi kāṇāpi dānād upari karkaṭī ||Panc_2.77||
children.translated_text: but a cucumber, even though hunchbacked and one-eyed, rises upward because it gives. // Panc_2.77 //

children.text: yacchan jalam api jalado vallabhatām eti sakala-lokasya |
children.translated_text: The rain-cloud, giving water, wins the love of all people;

children.text: nityaṃ prasārita-karo mitro 'pi na vīkṣituṃ śakyaḥ ||Panc_2.78||
children.translated_text: the sun (<s>Mitra</s>), though always with outstretched hand, cannot even be looked at. // Panc_2.78 //

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā daridryābhibhūtair api svalpāt svalpataraṃ kāle pātre ca deyam | uktaṃ ca-
sat-pātraṃ mahatī śraddhā deśe kāle yathocite |
children.translated_text: What is given by the discerning to a worthy recipient, with great faith, in the appropriate place and time —

children.text: yad dīyate viveka-jñais tad anantāya kalpate ||Panc_2.79||
children.translated_text: that [gift] becomes infinite [in merit]. // Panc_2.79 //
Knowing this, even those overwhelmed by poverty should give something however small, at the proper time and to the proper recipient. And it is said:

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: atitṛṣṇā na kartavyā tṛṣṇāṃ naiva parityajet |
children.translated_text: One should not have excessive greed, nor should one abandon desire entirely;

children.text: atitṛṣṇābhibhūtasya śikhā bhavati mastake ||Panc_2.80||
children.translated_text: for one overcome by excessive greed, there will be a topknot [of flame] upon his head. // Panc_2.80 //

children.text: brāhmaṇy āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The Brahmin woman asked: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 3
śavara-śūkara-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 3
The story of the hunter and the boar

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe kaścit pulindaḥ | sa ca pāparddhiṃ kartuṃ vanaṃ prati prasthitaḥ | atha tena prasarpatā mahān añjana-parvata-śikharākāraḥ kroḍaḥ samāsāditaḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇāntākṛṣṭa-niśita-sāyakena samāhataḥ | tenāpi kopāviṣṭena cetasā bālendu-dyutinā daṃṣṭrāgreṇa pāṭitodaraḥ pulindo gatāsur bhūtale'patat |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there was a certain <s>Pulinda</s> (tribal hunter). He set out for the forest to do his sinful work. While he was prowling, he encountered a huge boar, resembling the peak of the collyrium-mountain (<s>Añjana</s>). Seeing it, he struck it with a sharp arrow drawn to the ear. That [boar] too, its mind filled with rage, tore open the hunter's belly with the tip of its tusk — gleaming like the young moon — and the hunter fell dead upon the ground.

children.text: atha lubdhakaṃ vyāpādya śūkaro 'pi śara-prahāra-vedanayā pañcatvaṃ gataḥ | etasminn antare kaścid āsanna-mṛtyuḥ śṛgāla itas tato nirāhāratayā pīḍitaḥ paribhramaṃs taṃ pradeśam ājagāma | yāvad varāha-pulindau dvāv api paśyati tāvat prahṛṣṭo vyacintayat-bhoḥ ! sānukūlo me vidhiḥ | tenaitad apy acintitaṃ bhojanam upasthitam | athavā sādhv idam uktam-
children.translated_text: Having killed the hunter, the boar too died from the pain of the arrow-wound. In the meanwhile, a certain jackal at the point of death, tormented by hunger from not eating, wandering here and there, came to that spot. When he saw both the boar and the hunter, he was overjoyed and thought: 'Ah! Fate is favorable to me — for this unforeseen food has presented itself.' Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: akṛte'py udyame puṃsām anya-janma-kṛtaṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: Even without effort by men, the fruit of deeds done in another birth —

children.text: śubhāśubhaṃ samabhyeti vidhinā saṃniyojitam ||Panc_2.81||
children.translated_text: whether auspicious or inauspicious — comes [to them], ordained by fate. // Panc_2.81 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: yasmin deśe ca kāle ca vayasā yādṛśena ca |
children.translated_text: In whatever place, and at whatever time, and at whatever age,

children.text: kṛtaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ karma tat tathā tena bhujyate ||Panc_2.82||
children.translated_text: good or bad <s>karma</s> was performed — that is enjoyed accordingly by that [person]. // Panc_2.82 //

children.text: tad ahaṃ tathā bhakṣayāmi yathā bahūny ahāni me prāṇa-yātrā bhavati | tat tāvad enaṃ snāyu-pāśaṃ dhanuṣkoṭi-gataṃ bhakṣayāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So I shall eat in such a way that my sustenance will last for many days. First, let me eat this sinew-cord attached to the tip of the bow.' And it is said:

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiś ca bhoktavyaṃ svayaṃ vittam upārjitam |
children.translated_text: Wealth acquired by oneself should be consumed gradually,

children.text: rasāyanam iva prājñair helayā na kadācana ||Panc_2.83||
children.translated_text: like a tonic by the wise — never carelessly. // Panc_2.83 //

children.text: ity evaṃ manasā niścitya cāpa-ghaṭita-koṭiṃ mukha-madhye prakṣipya snāyuṃ bhakṣituṃ pravṛttaḥ | tataś ca truṭite pāśe tālu-deśaṃ vidārya cāpa-koṭirmastaka-madhyena niṣkrāntā | so 'pi tadvad enayā tat-kṣaṇāntan mṛtaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-atitṛṣṇā na kartavyā iti |
children.translated_text: Having resolved thus in his mind, he put the bow-tip fitted [with the cord] into his mouth and began eating the sinew. When the cord snapped, the bow-tip pierced his palate and emerged through the middle of his skull. He too died instantly from that. Therefore I say: 'One should not have excessive greed' [and so on].

children.text: sa punar apy āha-brāhmaṇi, na śrutaṃ bhavatyā |
children.translated_text: He spoke yet again: 'O Brahmin lady, have you not heard?'

children.text: āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Lifespan, <s>karma</s>, wealth, learning, and the time of death —

children.text: pañcaitāni hi sṛjyante garbhasthasyaiva dehinaḥ ||Panc_2.84||
children.translated_text: these five are determined for the embodied being while still in the womb. // Panc_2.84 //

children.text: athaivaṃ sā tena prabodhitā brāhmaṇy āha-yady evaṃ tad asti me gṛhe stokas tila-rāśiḥ | tatas tilān luñcitvā tila-cūrṇena brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayiṣyāmi iti |
children.translated_text: Thus enlightened by him, the Brahmin woman said: 'If so, then I have at home a small heap of sesame seeds. I shall husk the sesame and feed the Brahmin with sesame-flour.'

children.text: tatas tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇo grāmaṃ gataḥ | sāpi tilānuṣṇodakena sammardya kuṭitvā sūryātape dattavatī | atrāntare tasyā grha-karma-vyagrāyās tilānāṃ madhye kaścit sārameyo mūtrotsargaṃ cakāra | taṃ dṛṣṭvā sā cintitavatī-aho naipuṇyaṃ paśya parāṅmukhībhūtasya vidheḥ | yad ete tilā abhojyāḥ kṛtāḥ | tad aham etān samādāya kasyacit gṛhaṃ gatvā luñcitair aluñcitān ānayāmi | sarvo 'pi jano 'nena vidhinā pradāsyati iti |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing her words, the Brahmin went to the village. She too, having soaked the sesame in hot water, pounded them, and placed them in the sunshine. In the meanwhile, while she was busy with housework, a dog urinated in the midst of the sesame. Seeing that, she thought: 'Ah, behold the cunning of adverse fate! These sesame seeds have been made unfit for eating. So I shall take these and go to someone's house and exchange husked [seeds] for unhusked ones. Everyone will give by this arrangement.'

children.text: atha yasmin gṛhe'haṃ bhikṣārthaṃ praviṣṭas tatra gṛhe sāpi tilān ādāya praviṣṭā vikrayaṃ kartum | āha ca-gṛhṇātu kaścid aluñcitair luñcitāṃs tilān |
children.translated_text: Now, in the very house where I had entered seeking alms, she too entered carrying the sesame to make an exchange. And she said: 'Let someone take husked sesame in exchange for unhusked.'

children.text: atha tad-gṛha-gṛhiṇī-gṛhaṃ praviṣṭā yāvad aluñcitair luñcitān gṛhṇāti tāvad asyāḥ putreṇa kāmandakī-śāstraṃ dṛṣṭvā vyāhṛtam-mātaḥ ! agrāhyāḥ khalv ime tilāḥ | nāsyā aluñcitair luñcitā grāhyāḥ | kāraṇaṃ kiñcid bhaviṣyati | tenaiṣāluñcitair luñcitān prayacchati |
children.translated_text: Then, having entered the house of the mistress of that household, just as [the mistress] was about to take the husked for unhusked, her son, having seen the <s>Kāmaṇḍakī</s> (a treatise on polity), spoke: 'Mother! These sesame seeds should certainly not be accepted. One should not accept her husked ones in exchange for unhusked. There must be some reason [for this exchange] — that is why she offers husked for unhusked.'

children.text: tac chrutvā ayā parityaktās te tilāḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-nākasmāc chāṇḍilī-mātaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, those sesame seeds were refused by her. Therefore I say: 'Not without cause, O mother of <s>Śāṇḍilī</s>...' [and so on].

children.text: etad uktvā sa bhūyo 'pi prāha-atha jñāyate tasya kramaṇa-mārgaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he spoke yet again: 'Now, is his path of approach known?'

children.text: tāmracūḍa āha-bhagavan, jñāyate | yata ekākī na samāgacchati, kintv asaṅkhya-yūtha-parivṛtaḥ paśyato me paribhramann itas tataḥ sarva-janena sahāgacchati yāti ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmracūḍa</s> (Red-Crest) said: 'Sir, it is known. He does not come alone, but comes and goes surrounded by an innumerable herd, wandering here and there in my sight, along with everyone.'

children.text: abhyāgata āha-asti kiñcit khanitrakam |
children.translated_text: The guest said: 'Is there any digging tool?'

children.text: sa āha-bāḍham asti | eṣā sarva-loha-mayī sva-hastikā |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Indeed there is — this iron spade in my hand.'

children.text: abhyāgata āha-tarhi pratyūṣe tvayā mayā saha sthātavyam | yena dvāv api jana-caraṇa-malināyāṃ bhūmau tat-padānusāreṇa gacchāvaḥ | mayāpi tad-vacanam ākarṇya cintitam-aho vinaṣṭo 'smi, yato 'sya sābhiprāya-vacāṃsi śrūyante | nūnaṃ, yathā nidhānaṃ jñātaṃ tathā durgam apy asmākaṃ jñāsyati | etad abhiprāyād eva jñāyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The guest said: 'Then, at dawn you must stand with me, so that we two may follow his footprints on the ground soiled by people's feet.' Having heard his words, I too thought: 'Ah, I am ruined! For his words are full of purpose. Surely, just as he has discovered the treasure, he will discover our fortress too. This is understood from his very intention.' And it is said:

children.text: sakṛd api dṛṣṭvā puruṣaṃ vibudhā jānanti sāratāṃ tasya |
children.translated_text: Having seen a man even once, the wise know his essence;

children.text: hasta-tulayāpi nipuṇāḥ pala-pramāṇā vijānanti ||Panc_2.85||
children.translated_text: experts skilled with a hand-balance know the measure of a <s>pala</s> weight. // Panc_2.85 //

children.text: vāñchaiva sūcayati pūrvataraṃ bhaviṣyaṃ
children.translated_text: Desire itself reveals beforehand the future —

children.text: puṃsāṃ yad anya-tanujaṃ tv aśubhaṃ śubhaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: whether inauspicious or auspicious — born in another body, for men.

children.text: vijñāyate śiśur ajāta-kalāpa-cihnaḥ
children.translated_text: A young peacock, whose tail-fan markings have not yet appeared,

children.text: pratyudgatair apasaran saralaḥ kalāpī ||Panc_2.86||
children.translated_text: is recognized as a straightforward peacock by those who come forward to meet [it]. // Panc_2.86 //

children.text: tato 'haṃ bhaya-trasta-manāḥ saparivāro durga-mārgaṃ parityajyānya-mārgeṇa gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ | saparijano yāvad agrato gacchāmi tāvat sammukho bṛhatkāyo mārjāraḥ samāyāti | sa ca mūṣaka-vṛndam avalokya tan-madhye sahasotpapāta | atha te mūṣakā māṃ kumārga-gāminam avalokya garhayanto hata-śeṣā rudhira-plāvita-vasundharās tam eva durgaṃ praviṣṭāḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Then I, my mind terrified with fear, along with my retinue, abandoning the path to the fortress, set out on another path. While I, with my followers, was going forward, a huge cat came directly toward us. He, seeing the troop of mice, suddenly leapt into their midst. Then those mice, seeing me going on a wrong path, reviling me, the survivors — on ground drenched with blood — entered that very fortress. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: chittvā pāśam apāsya kūṭa-racanāṃ bhaṅktvā balād vāgurāṃ
children.translated_text: Having cut the snare, pushed aside the trap, broken by force the net,

children.text: paryantāgni-śikhā-kalāpa-jaṭilān nirgatya dūraṃ vanāt |
children.translated_text: having emerged far from the forest with its borders blazing with tongues of fire,

children.text: vyādhānāṃ śara-gocarād api javenotpatya dhāvan mṛgaḥ
children.translated_text: having leapt with speed even beyond the arrow-range of hunters and run —

children.text: kūpāntaḥ-patitaḥ karotu vidhure kiṃ vā vidhau pauruṣam ||Panc_2.87||
children.translated_text: the deer has fallen into a well! What can manly effort do against adverse fate? // Panc_2.87 //

children.text: athāham eko 'nyatra gataḥ | śeṣā mūḍhatayā tatraiva durge praviṣṭāḥ | atrāntare sa duṣṭa-parivrājako rudhira-bindu-carcitāṃ bhūmim avalokya tenaiva durga-mārgeṇāgatyopasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then I alone went elsewhere. The rest, in their foolishness, entered that very fortress. In the meanwhile, that wicked mendicant, seeing the ground spotted with drops of blood, came along that very fortress-path and arrived.

children.text: yad utsāhī sadā martyaḥ parābhavati yaj janān |
children.translated_text: That a mortal is always enterprising, that he overcomes people,

children.text: yad uddhataṃ vaded vākyaṃ tat sarvaṃ vittajaṃ balam ||Panc_2.88||
children.translated_text: that he speaks bold words — all that strength is born of wealth. // Panc_2.88 //

children.text: athāhaṃ tac chrutvā kopāviṣṭo bhikṣā-pātram uddiśya viśeṣād utkūrdito 'prāpta eva bhūmau nipatitaḥ | tac chrūtvāsau me śatrur vihasya tāmracūḍam uvāca-bhoḥ ! paśya paśya kautūhalam | āha ca-
children.translated_text: Then I, hearing that, filled with rage, leapt up with special effort toward the begging bowl — but without reaching it, fell to the ground. Hearing that, my enemy laughed and said to <s>Tāmracūḍa</s>: 'Ho! Look, look at the spectacle!' And he said:

children.text: arthena balavān sarvo 'py artha-yuktaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Everyone is strong through wealth; one endowed with wealth is the [true] wise man.

children.text: paśyainaṃ mūṣakaṃ vyarthaṃ sajāteḥ samatāṃ matam ||Panc_2.89||
children.translated_text: Behold this mouse, now useless — considered equal to his own kind. // Panc_2.89 //

children.text: tat svapihi tvaṃ gata-śaṅkaḥ | yad asyotpatana-kāraṇaṃ tad āvayor hasta-gataṃ jātam | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'So sleep without worry. The cause of his leaping has now come into our hands.' Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: daṃṣṭrā-virahitaḥ sarpo mada-hīno yathā gajaḥ |
children.translated_text: A snake without fangs, like an elephant without rut —

children.text: tathārthena vihīno 'tra puruṣo nāma-dhārakaḥ ||Panc_2.90||
children.translated_text: so too a man bereft of wealth is merely a name-bearer in this world. // Panc_2.90 //

children.text: tac chrutvāhaṃ manasā vicintitavān-yato 'ṅguli-mātram api kūrdana-śaktir nāsti, tad dhig artha-hīnasya puruṣasya jīvitam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, I thought to myself: 'Since I cannot leap even a finger's breadth, then shame on the life of a man without wealth!' And it is said:

children.text: arthena ca vihīnasya puruṣasyālpa-medhasaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a man bereft of wealth and of feeble intellect,

children.text: vyucchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā ||Panc_2.91||
children.translated_text: all activities are cut off — like a small river in summer. // Panc_2.91 //

children.text: yathā kāka-yavāḥ proktā yathāraṇya-bhavās tilāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as crow-barley are so called [but are not real barley], just as forest-sesame [are not real sesame],

children.text: nāma-mātrā na siddhau hi dhana-hīnās tathā narāḥ ||Panc_2.92||
children.translated_text: so men without wealth are [men] in name only — not in accomplishment. // Panc_2.92 //

children.text: santo 'pi na hi rājante daridrasyetare guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: The other virtues of a poor man, though they exist, do not shine;

children.text: āditya iva bhūtānāṃ śrīr guṇānāṃ prakāśinī ||Panc_2.93||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) reveals the virtues of beings, like the sun. // Panc_2.93 //

children.text: na tathā bādhyate loke prakṛtyā nirdhano janaḥ |
children.translated_text: A person naturally poor is not so tormented in the world

children.text: yathā dravyāṇi samprāpya tair vihīno 'sukhe sthitaḥ ||Panc_2.94||
children.translated_text: as one who, having obtained wealth, is deprived of it and placed in misery. // Panc_2.94 //

children.text: śuṣkasya kīṭa-khātasya vahni-dagdhasya sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Of a tree that is dried up, eaten by insects, burnt by fire on all sides,

children.text: taror apy ūṣarasthasya varaṃ janma na cārthinaḥ ||Panc_2.95||
children.translated_text: and standing in barren soil — even its birth is better than that of a supplicant. // Panc_2.95 //

children.text: śaṅkanīyā hi sarvatra niṣpratāpā daridratā |
children.translated_text: Poverty without power is to be suspected everywhere;

children.text: upakartum api hi prāptaṃ niḥsvaṃ santyajya gacchati ||Panc_2.96||
children.translated_text: even one who has come to help abandons the destitute and departs. // Panc_2.96 //

children.text: unnamyonnamya tatraiva daridrāṇāṃ manorathāḥ |
children.translated_text: The aspirations of the poor rise up again and again, only to fall

children.text: patanti hṛdaye vyarthā vidhavāstrīstanā iva ||Panc_2.97||
children.translated_text: uselessly upon their hearts — like the breasts of a widow. // Panc_2.97 //

children.text: vyakte'pi vāsare nityaṃ daurgatya-tamasāvṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even in broad daylight, ever shrouded in the darkness of misfortune,

children.text: agrato 'pi sthito yatnān na kenāpīha dṛśyate ||Panc_2.98||
children.translated_text: even though standing right in front, with effort [still] he is seen by no one here. // Panc_2.98 //

children.text: evaṃ vilapyāhaṃ bhagnotsāhas tan-nidhānaṃ gaṇḍopadhānīkṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā svaṃ durgaṃ prabhāte gataḥ | tataś ca mad-bhṛtyāḥ prabhāte gacchanto mitho jalpanti-aho, asamartho 'yam udara-pūraṇe'smākam | kevalam asya pṛṣṭha-lagnānāṃ viḍālādi-vipattayaḥ tat kim anenārādhitena ? uktaṃ ca-
yat-sakāśān na lābhāḥ syāt kevalāḥ syur vipattayaḥ |
children.translated_text: A master from whom there are no gains but only calamities —

children.text: sa svāmī dūratas tyājyo viśeṣād anujīvibhiḥ ||Panc_2.99||
children.translated_text: he should be abandoned from afar, especially by dependents. // Panc_2.99 //

Having lamented thus, I, with broken spirit, seeing that treasure used as a cheek-pillow [by the mendicant], went to my own fortress in the morning. Then my servants, departing in the morning, muttered among themselves: 'Ah, this one is incapable of filling our bellies. For those clinging to his back, there are only calamities from cats and the like. So what use is serving him?' And it is said:

children.text: evaṃ teṣāṃ vacāṃsi śrutvā sva-durgaṃ praviṣṭo 'ham | yāvan na kaścin mama saṃmukhe'bhyeti tāvan mayā cintitam-dhig iyaṃ daridratā | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
mṛto daridraḥ puruṣo mṛtaṃ maithunam aprajam |
children.translated_text: A poor man is [as good as] dead; sexual union without offspring is dead;

children.text: mṛtam aśrotriyaṃ śrāddhaṃ mṛto yajñas tv adakṣiṇam ||Panc_2.100||
children.translated_text: a <s>śrāddha</s> without a learned Brahmin is dead; a sacrifice without <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee) is dead. // Panc_2.100 //
Having heard their words, I entered my own fortress. When no one came before me, I thought: 'Shame on this poverty!' Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: vyathayanti paraṃ ceto manoratha-śatair janāḥ |
children.translated_text: People torment another's mind with hundreds of aspirations,

children.text: nānuṣṭhānair dhanair hīnāḥ kulajāḥ vidhavā iva ||Panc_2.101||
children.translated_text: yet being without means and wealth — [they are] like well-born widows, [unable to act]. // Panc_2.101 //

children.text: daurgatyaṃ dehināṃ duḥkham apamāna-karaṃ param |
children.translated_text: Poverty of embodied beings is a suffering that brings the utmost dishonor,

children.text: yena svair api manyante jīvanto 'pi mṛtā iva ||Panc_2.102||
children.translated_text: by which even one's own people regard the living as if dead. // Panc_2.102 //

children.text: dainyasya pātratām eti parābhṛteḥ paraṃ padam |
children.translated_text: He becomes a vessel of wretchedness, attains the supreme state of dependence on others,

children.text: vipadām āśrayaḥ śaśvad daurgatya-kaluṣī-kṛtaḥ ||Panc_2.103||
children.translated_text: becomes the perpetual refuge of misfortunes — tainted by poverty. // Panc_2.103 //

children.text: lajjante bāndhavās tena sambandhaṃ gopayanti ca |
children.translated_text: Kinsmen are ashamed of him and conceal the connection;

children.text: mitrāṇy amitratāṃ yānti yasya na syuḥ kapardakāḥ ||Panc_2.104||
children.translated_text: friends turn to enmity for one who has not even a cowrie-shell. [Panc 2.104]

children.text: mūrtaṃ lāghavam evaitad apāyānām idaṃ gṛham |
children.translated_text: This is the embodiment of disgrace, this is the abode of calamities,

children.text: paryāyo maraṇasyāyaṃ nirdhanatvaṃ śarīriṇām ||Panc_2.105||
children.translated_text: this is a synonym for death — the poverty of embodied beings. [Panc 2.105]

children.text: ajā-dhūlir iva trastair mārjanī-reṇuvaj janaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Like dust raised by goats, like sweeping-dust by frightened people,

children.text: dīpa-khaṭvottha-cchāyeva tyajyate nirdhano janaḥ ||Panc_2.106||
children.translated_text: like a shadow cast by a lamp on a cot — a poor man is abandoned. [Panc 2.106]

children.text: śaucāvaśiṣṭayāpy asti kiñcit kāryaṃ kvacin mṛdā |
children.translated_text: Even clay left over from cleaning has some use somewhere,

children.text: nirdhanena janenaiva na tu kiñcit prayojanam ||Panc_2.107||
children.translated_text: but a poor man has no purpose whatsoever. [Panc 2.107]

children.text: adhano dātu-kāmo 'pi samprāpto dhanināṃ gṛham |
children.translated_text: A poor man, even if he comes wishing to give, arriving at a rich man's house,

children.text: manyate yācako 'yaṃ dhig dāridryaṃ khalu dehinām ||Panc_2.108||
children.translated_text: is thought to be a beggar — alas, poverty is indeed [the curse] of embodied beings! [Panc 2.108]

children.text: sva-vitta-haraṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā yo hi rakṣaty asūn naraḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, seeing his wealth being seized, [merely] preserves his life —

children.text: pitaro 'pi na gṛhṇanti tad-dattaṃ saliāñjalim ||Panc_2.109||
children.translated_text: even his ancestors do not accept the water-offering given by him. [Panc 2.109]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: gavārthe brāhmaṇārthe ca strī-vitta-haraṇe tathā |
children.translated_text: For the sake of a cow, for the sake of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and for the protection of a woman's wealth —

children.text: prāṇāṃs tyajati yo yuddhe tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ ||Panc_2.110||
children.translated_text: he who gives up his life in battle, for him are the eternal worlds. [Panc 2.110]

children.text: evaṃ niścitya rātrau tatra gatvā nidrāvaśam upāgatasya peṭāyāṃ mayā chidraṃ kṛtaṃ yāvat, tāvat prabuddho duṣṭa-tāpasaḥ | tataś ca jarjara-vaṃśa-prahāreṇa śirasi tāḍitaḥ kathañcid āyuḥ-śeṣatayā nirgato 'ham, na mṛtaś ca | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, going there at night, I made a hole in the box while he was overcome by sleep, when the wicked ascetic awoke. Then, struck on the head with a blow from a worn bamboo-staff, I somehow escaped alive by the remainder of my lifespan, but did not die. And it is said —

children.text: prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣyo
children.translated_text: A man obtains what is destined to be obtained —

children.text: devo 'pi taṃ laṅghayituṃ na śaktaḥ |
children.translated_text: even a god is unable to prevent it.

children.text: tasmān na śocāmi na vismayo me
children.translated_text: Therefore I do not grieve, nor am I surprised —

children.text: yad asmadīyaṃ na hi tat pareṣām ||Panc_2.111||
children.translated_text: what is ours does not belong to others. [Panc 2.111]

children.text: kāka-kūrmau pṛcchataḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crow and the tortoise asked: 'How is that?'

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said:

children.text:
kathā 4
sāgaradatta-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 4
The Story of <s>Sāgaradatta</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścin nagare sāgaradatto nāma vaṇik | tat-sūnunā rūpaka-śatena vikrīyamāṇaṃ pustakaṃ gṛhītam | tasmiṃś ca likhitam asti-
children.translated_text: In a certain city there was a merchant named <s>Sāgaradatta</s>. His son purchased a book being sold for a hundred <s>rūpakas</s> (silver coins). In it was written:

children.text: prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣyo
children.translated_text: A man obtains what is destined to be obtained —

children.text: devo 'pi taṃ laṅghayituṃ na śaktaḥ |
children.translated_text: even a god is unable to prevent it.

children.text: tasmān na śocāmi na vismayo me
children.translated_text: Therefore I do not grieve, nor am I surprised —

children.text: yad asmadīyaṃ na hi tat pareṣām ||Panc_2.111||
children.translated_text: what is ours does not belong to others. [Panc 2.111]

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā sāgaradattena tanujaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ-putra, kiyatā mūlyenaitat pustakaṃ gṛhītam ?
children.translated_text: Seeing that, <s>Sāgaradatta</s> asked his son: 'Son, for how much was this book purchased?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-rūpaka-śatena |
children.translated_text: He said: 'For a hundred <s>rūpakas</s>.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sāgaradatto 'bravīt-dhiṅ mūrkha ! tvaṃ likhitaika-ślokaṃ rūpaka-śatena yad gṛhṇāsi, etayā buddhyā kathaṃ dravyopārjanaṃ kariṣyasi | tad adya-prabhṛti tvayā me gṛhe na praveṣṭavyam |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Sāgaradatta</s> said: 'Shame on you, fool! You who purchase a book containing only one verse for a hundred <s>rūpakas</s> — with such intelligence, how will you earn wealth? Therefore, from today onward, you shall not enter my house.'

children.text: evaṃ nirbhartsya gṛhān niḥsāritaḥ | sa ca tena nirvedena viprakṛṣṭaṃ deśāntaraṃ gatvā kim api nagaram āsādyāvasthitaḥ | atha katipaya-divasais tan-nagara-nivāsinā kenacid asau pṛṣṭaḥ-kuto bhavān āgataḥ ? kiṃ nāma-dheyo vā ? iti |
children.translated_text: Having thus rebuked him, he expelled him from the house. And he, with that disgust, went far away to another country and, reaching some city, settled there. Then after some days, a certain resident of that city asked him: 'Where have you come from? What is your name?'

children.text: asāv abravīt-prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣya iti | athānyenāpi pṛṣṭenānena tathaivottaraṃ dattam | evaṃ ca tasya nagarasya madhye prāptavyamartha iti tasya prasiddha-nāma jātam |
children.translated_text: He said: 'A man obtains what is destined to be obtained.' And when asked by others too, he gave the same answer. Thus in that city, '<s>Prāptavyamartha</s>' (Destined-Wealth) became his well-known name.

children.text: atha rāja-kanyā candravatī nāmābhinava-rūpa-yauvana-sampannā sakhī-dvitīyaikasmin mahotsava-divase nagaraṃ nirīkṣamāṇāsti | tatraiva ca kaścid rāja-putro 'tīva-rūpa-sampanno manoramaś ca katham api tasyā dṛṣṭi-gocare gataḥ | tad-darśana-sama-kālam eva kusuma-bāṇāhatayā tayā nija-sakhy-abhihitā-sakhi ! yathā kilānena saha samāgamo bhavati tathādya tvayā yatitavyam |
children.translated_text: Now a princess named <s>Candravatī</s>, endowed with fresh beauty and youth, accompanied by a friend, was one day observing the city during a great festival. There, a certain prince, exceedingly handsome and charming, somehow came within her sight. The very moment she saw him, struck by <s>Kāma</s>'s (Love's) flower-arrows, she said to her friend: 'Friend! You must arrange today that a meeting takes place between him and me.'

children.text: evaṃ ca śrutvā sā sakhī tat-sakāśaṃ gatvā śīghram abravīt-yad ahaṃ candravatyā tavāntikaṃ preṣitā | bhaṇitaṃ ca tvāṃ prati tayā yan mama tvad-darśanān manobhavena paścimāvasthā kṛtā | tad yadi śīghram eva mad-antike na sameṣmasi tadā me maraṇaṃ śaraṇam |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, that friend quickly went to him and said: 'I have been sent to you by <s>Candravatī</s>. She has said to you: "By seeing you, <s>Manobhava</s> (Love) has brought me to my final state. If you do not come to me quickly, death will be my refuge."'

children.text: iti śrutvā tenābhihitaṃ-yady avaśyaṃ mayā tatrāgantavyaṃ, tat kathaya kenopāyena praveṣṭavyam ?
children.translated_text: Hearing this, he said: 'If I must necessarily go there, then tell me — by what means should I enter?'

children.text: atha sakhyābhihitam-rātrau saudhāvalambitayā dṛḍha-varatrayā tvayā tatrāroḍhavyam |
children.translated_text: Then the friend said: 'At night, by a strong rope hung from the white palace, you must climb up.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-yady evaṃ niścayo bhavatyās tad aham evaṃ kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'If that is the lady's resolve, then I shall do so.'

children.text: iti niścitya sakhī candravatī-sakāśaṃ gatā | athāgatāyāṃ rajanyāṃ sa rāja-putraḥ sva-cetasā vyacintayat-aho mahad akṛtyam etat | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having decided thus, the friend went back to <s>Candravatī</s>. Then, when night came, that prince reflected in his mind: 'Ah, this is a great wrong deed.' And it is said —

children.text: guroḥ sutāṃ mitra-bhāryāṃ svāmi-sevaka-gehinīm |
children.translated_text: He who goes to the teacher's daughter, a friend's wife, or the wife of one's master's servant —

children.text: yo gacchati pumāṃl loke tam āhur brahma-ghātinam ||Panc_2.112||
children.translated_text: him they call a slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in this world. [Panc 2.112]

children.text: aparaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: ayaśaḥ prāpyate yena yena cādho-gatir bhavet |
children.translated_text: That action by which one gains infamy, by which one falls downward,

children.text: svārthāc ca bhraśyate yena tat karma na samācaret ||Panc_2.113||
children.translated_text: and by which one loses one's own purpose — that action one should not perform. [Panc 2.113]

children.text: iti samyag vicārya tat-sakāśaṃ na jagāma | atha prāptavyamarthaḥ paryaṭan dhavala-gṛha-pārśve rātrāv avalambita-varatrāṃ dṛṣṭvā kautukāviṣṭa-hṛdayas tām ālambyādhirūḍhaḥ | tayā ca rāja-putryā sa evāyam ity āśvasta-cittayā snāna-khādana-pānācchādanādinā sammānya tena saha śayana-talam āśritayā tad-aṅga-saṃsparśa-sañjāta-harṣa-romāñcita-gātrayoktaṃ-yuṣmad-darśana-mātrānuraktayā mayātmā pradatto 'yam | tvad-varjam anyo bhartā manasy api me na bhaviṣyati iti | tat kasmān amyā saha na bravīṣi ?
children.translated_text: Having properly reflected thus, he did not go to her. Then <s>Prāptavyamartha</s>, wandering about, saw the rope hanging from the white palace at night. With his heart seized by curiosity, he climbed it. And the princess, confident that this was indeed he [the prince], honored him with bathing, food, drink, garments, and the like, and lying on the bed with him, her body thrilled with joy-born goosebumps from the touch of his limbs, she said: 'Captivated by merely seeing you, I have given myself. Other than you, no other husband shall ever be in my mind. So why do you not speak freely with me?'

children.text: so 'bravīt- prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'A man obtains what is destined to be obtained.'

children.text: ity ukte tayānyo 'yam iti matvā dhavala-gṛhād uttārya muktaḥ | sa tu khaṇḍa-pāśakaḥ prāptaḥ | tāvad asau khaṇḍa-deva-kule gatvā suptaḥ | atha tatra kayācit svairiṇyā datta-saṅketako yāvad daṇḍa-pāśakaḥ prāptaḥ, tāvad asau pūrva-suptas tena dṛṣṭo rahasya-saṃrakṣaṇārtham abhihitaś ca-ko bhavān ?
children.translated_text: When he said this, she thought 'this is someone else' and had him lowered from the palace and released him. He then arrived at a <s>Khaṇḍa</s>-district. He went to a local temple and fell asleep. Now a certain wanton woman had made an assignation there, and when the watchman arrived, he saw this man already sleeping there. For the sake of guarding his secret, he said: 'Who are you?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'A man obtains what is destined to be obtained.'

children.text: iti śrutvā daṇḍa-pāśakenābhihitam-yac chūnyaṃ deva-gṛham idam | tad atra madīya-sthāne gatvā svapihi |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the watchman said: 'Since this temple is empty, go and sleep in my place.'

children.text: tathā pratipadya sa matir viparyāsād anya-śayane suptaḥ | atha tasya rakṣakasya kanyā vinayavatī nāma rūpa-yauvana-sampannā kasyāpi puruṣasyānuraktā saṅketaṃ dattvā tatra śayane suptāsīt | atha sā tam āyātaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa evāyam asmad-vallabha iti rātrau ghanatarāndhakāra-vyāmohitotthāya bhojanācchādanādi-kriyāṃ kārayitvā gāndharva-vivāhenātmānaṃ vivāhayitvā tena samaṃ śayane sthitā vikasita-vadana-kamalā tam āha-kim adyāpi mayā saha viśrabdhaṃ bhavān na bravīti |
children.translated_text: Agreeing to this, he, by a twist of fate, slept on another's bed. Now the watchman's daughter, named <s>Vinayavatī</s>, endowed with beauty and youth, enamored of a certain man, having given him a signal, was sleeping on that bed. Seeing him arrive [as she thought], thinking 'This is indeed my beloved,' in the dense darkness of the night she arose, confused, had him fed and clothed, married herself to him by <s>gāndharva</s> rite (love-marriage), and lying on the bed with him, her lotus-face blooming, she said: 'Why do you still not speak freely with me?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'A man obtains what is destined to be obtained.'

children.text: iti śrutvā tayā cintitam-yat kāryam asamīkṣitaṃ kriyate tasyedṛk-phala-vipāko bhavati iti | evaṃ vimṛśya sa-viṣādayā tayā niḥsārito 'sau | sa ca yāvad-vīthī-mārgeṇa gacchati tāvad anya-viṣaya-vāsī vara-kīrtir nāma varo mahatā vādya-śabdenāgacchati | prāptavyamartho 'pi taiḥ samaṃ gantum ārabdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, she thought: 'The deed that is done without deliberation — such is its fruit.' Reflecting thus, she, filled with dismay, expelled him. As he walked along the main road, a bridegroom named <s>Varakīrti</s>, coming from another province, was approaching with a great sound of music. <s>Prāptavyamartha</s> too began walking along with them.

children.text: atha yāvat pratyāsanne lagna-samaye rāja-mārgāsanna-śreṣṭhi-gṛha-dvāre racita-maṇḍapa-vedikāyāṃ kṛta-kautuka-maṅgala-veśā vaṇik-sutāsti, tāvan mada-matto hasty-ārohakaṃ hatvā praṇaśyaj-jana-kolāhalena lokam ākulayaṃs tam evoddeśaṃ prāptaḥ | taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sarve varānuyāyino vareṇa saha praṇaśya diśo jagmuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, just as the auspicious time [for marriage] was near, at a pavilion-platform constructed at the gate of a wealthy merchant's house near the royal road, the merchant's daughter stood adorned in her wedding finery. Just then, a maddened elephant, having killed its rider, arrived at that very spot, throwing people into panic with fleeing crowds. Seeing it, all the bridegroom's attendants, along with the bridegroom, fled in all directions.

children.text: athāsminn avasare bhaya-tarala-locanām ekākinīṃ kanyām avalokya-mā bhaiṣīḥ | ahaṃ paritrāteti sudhīraṃ sthirīkṛtya dakṣiṇa-pāṇau saṅgṛhya mahā-sāhasikatayā prāptavyamarthaḥ puruṣa-vākyair hastinaṃ nirbhartsitavān | tataḥ katham api daiva-yogād apāye hastini sa-suhṛd-bāndhavenātikrānta-lagna-samaye vara-kīrtir nāgatya tāvat tāṃ kanyām anya-hasta-gatāṃ dṛṣṭvābhihitam-bhoḥ śvaśura, viruddham idaṃ tvayānuṣṭhitaṃ yan mahyaṃ pradāya kanyānyasmai pradattā iti |
children.translated_text: At that moment, seeing the girl alone with fear-trembling eyes, [<s>Prāptavyamartha</s> said:] 'Do not fear! I am your protector.' Having thus firmly reassured her, grasping her right hand, with great daring, <s>Prāptavyamartha</s> drove off the elephant with manly words. Then, somehow by the working of fate, when the elephant retreated, <s>Varakīrti</s>, arriving with his friends and relatives after the auspicious time had passed, saw that girl in another's hand and said: 'O father-in-law, this is improper — you have done wrong by giving the girl promised to me to another!'

children.text: so 'bravīt-bhoḥ ! aham api hasti-bhaya-palāyitobhavadbhiḥ sahāyāto na jāne kim idaṃ vṛtam ity abhidhāya duhitaraṃ praṣṭum ārabdhaḥ-vatse, na tvayā sundaraṃ kṛtam | tat kathyatāṃ ko 'yaṃ vṛttāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Sir! I too fled in fear of the elephant along with you all. I do not know what has happened.' Saying this, he began to ask his daughter: 'Child, this was not well done by you. Tell me — what is this matter?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-yad aham anena prāṇa-saṃśayād rakṣitā, tad enaṃ muktvā mama jīvantyā nānyaḥ pāṇiṃ grahīṣyati iti |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Since I was saved from mortal danger by this man, I shall not — while living — allow any other than him to take my hand.'

children.text: anena vārtā-vyatikareṇa rajanī vyuṣṭā | atha prātas tatra sañjāte mahā-jana-samavāye vārtā-vyatikaraṃ śrutvā rāja-duhitā tam uddeśam āgatā | karṇa-paramparayā śrutvā daṇḍapāśaka-sutāpi tatraivāgatā | atha taṃ mahājana-amavāyaṃ śrutvā rājāpi tatra evājagāma |
children.translated_text: While this exchange was going on, the night passed. Then in the morning, when a great assembly of people gathered there and heard the exchange, the king's daughter came to that place. The watchman's daughter too, having heard through word-of-mouth, came there as well. Then, hearing of the great assembly, the king himself also arrived there.

children.text:
prāptavyamarthaṃ prāha-bhoḥ viśrabdhaṃ kathaya | kīdṛśo 'sau vṛttāntaḥ ?
atha so 'bravīt-prāptavyamarthaṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ iti |
children.translated_text:
<s>Prāptavyamartha</s> was asked: 'Sir, speak freely. What manner of story is this?'
Then he said: 'A man obtains what is destined to be obtained.'

children.text: rāja-kanyā smṛtvā prāha-devo 'pi taṃ laṅghayituṃ na śakta iti |
children.translated_text: The king's daughter, remembering, said: 'Even a god is unable to prevent it.'

children.text: tato daṇḍapāśaka-sutābravīt-tasmān na śocāmi na vismayo me iti |
children.translated_text: Then the watchman's daughter said: 'Therefore I do not grieve, nor am I surprised.'

children.text: tam akhilaloka-vṛttāntam ākarṇya vaṇik-sutābravīt-yad asmadīyaṃ na hi tat pareṣām iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing the entire account, the merchant's daughter said: 'What is ours does not belong to others.'

children.text: tato 'bhaya-dānaṃ dattvā rājā pṛthak pṛthag vṛttāntān jñātvāvagata-tattvas tasmai prāptavyam arthāya sva-duhitaraṃ sa-bahu-mānaṃ grāma-sahasreṇa samaṃ sarvālaṅkāra-parivāra-yutāṃ dattvā tvaṃ me putro 'sīti nagara-viditaṃ taṃ yauvarājye'bhiṣiktavān | daṇḍa-pāsakenāpi sva-duhitā sva-śaktyā vastra-dānādinā sambhāvya prāptavyamarthāya pradattā |
children.translated_text: Then the king, having granted assurance of safety and learning the separate accounts, understanding the truth, gave his own daughter with great honor to <s>Prāptavyamartha</s>, together with a thousand villages and all ornaments and retinue, saying 'You are my son,' and installed him as crown-prince, making it known throughout the city. The watchman too gave his daughter to <s>Prāptavyamartha</s>, honoring him according to his means with gifts of cloth and the like.

children.text: atha prāptavyamarthenāpi svīya-pitṛ-mātarau samasta-kuṭumbāvṛtau tasmin nagare sammāna-puraḥsaraṃ samānītau | atha so 'pi sva-gotreṇa saha vividha-bhogānupabhuñjānaḥ sukhenāvasthitaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-prāptavyam arthaṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prāptavyamartha</s> also had his own father and mother, surrounded by the entire family, brought to that city with honors. And he, with his kinfolk, enjoying various pleasures, lived happily. Therefore I say: 'A man obtains what is destined to be obtained.' [Panc 2.111]

children.text: tad etat sakalaṃ sukha-duḥkham anubhūya paraṃ viṣādam upāgato 'nena mitreṇa tvat-sakāśam ānītaḥ | tad etan me vairāgya-kāraṇam | mantharaka āha-bhadra, bhavati suhṛd ayam asandigdhaṃ yaḥ kṣut-kṣāmo 'pi śatru-bhūtaṃ tvāṃ bhakṣya-sthāne sthitam evaṃ pṛṣṭham āropyānayati na mārge'pi bhakṣayati | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: So, having experienced all this happiness and suffering and having fallen into extreme despondency, I was brought to you by this friend [the crow]. That is the reason for my dispassion.' <s>Mantharaka</s> (the tortoise) said: 'Friend, this one is undoubtedly a true friend — who, though starving with hunger, carries you, an enemy by nature, [a mouse] being a fit morsel, upon his back and brings you here without eating you even along the way.' And it is said —

children.text: vikāraṃ yāti no cittaṃ vitte yasya kadācana |
children.translated_text: He whose mind never wavers regarding one's wealth —

children.text: mitraṃ syāt sarva-kāle ca kārayen mitram uttamam ||Panc_2.114||
children.translated_text: he would be a friend at all times; one should make such a one the best of friends. [Panc 2.114]

children.text: vidvadbhiḥ suhṛdām atra cihnair etair asaṃśayam |
children.translated_text: By these signs, the wise have declared without doubt

children.text: parīkṣā-karaṇaṃ proktaṃ homāgner iva paṇḍitaiḥ ||Panc_2.115||
children.translated_text: that friends should be tested — as [one tests] the fire of a <s>homa</s> (sacrificial offering). [Panc 2.115]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: āpat-kāle tu samprāpte yan mitraṃ mitram eva tat |
children.translated_text: A friend in the time of calamity is a friend indeed;

children.text: vṛddhi-kāle tu samprāpte durjano 'pi suhṛd bhavet ||Panc_2.116||
children.translated_text: but in times of prosperity, even a wicked person becomes a friend. [Panc 2.116]

children.text: tan mamāpy adyāsya viṣaye viśvāsaḥ samutpanno yato nīti-viruddheyaṃ maitrī māṃsāśibhir vāyasaiḥ saha jalacarāṇām | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: So today, trust has arisen in me toward him in this regard, even though this friendship of water-creatures with flesh-eating crows is contrary to policy. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: mitraṃ ko 'pi na kasyāpi nitāntaṃ na ca vaira-kṛt |
children.translated_text: No one is anyone's absolute friend, nor is anyone an absolute enemy;

children.text: dṛśyate mitra-vidhvastāt kāryād vairī parīkṣitaḥ ||Panc_2.117||
children.translated_text: an enemy tested through the affair of a friend's destruction is seen [to be a friend or foe]. [Panc 2.117]

children.text: tat svāgataṃ bhavataḥ | sva-gṛha-vadāsyatām atra saras-tīre | yac ca vitt-nāśo videśa-vāsaś ca te sañjātas tatra viṣaye santāpo na kartavyaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So welcome to you! Please sit here on the bank of this lake as if in your own home. And as for the loss of wealth and dwelling in a foreign land that has befallen you — one should not grieve over that. And it is said —

children.text: abhrac-chāyā khala-prītiḥ samudrānte ca medinī |
children.translated_text: The shadow of a cloud, the affection of the wicked, and land at the ocean's edge,

children.text: alpenaiva vinaśyanti yauvanāni dhanāni ca ||Panc_2.118||
children.translated_text: youth and wealth — all perish in but a little while. [Panc 2.118]

children.text: ata eva vivekino jitātmāno dhana-spṛhāṃ na kurvanti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the discriminating and self-controlled do not cultivate desire for wealth. And it is said —

children.text: susañcitair jīvanavat surakṣitair
children.translated_text: Well-accumulated, well-guarded as if it were one's own life,

children.text: nije'pi dehe na viyojitaiḥ kvacit |
children.translated_text: never separated even from one's own body,

children.text: puṃso yamāntaṃ vrajato 'pi niṣṭhurair
children.translated_text: yet when a man journeys to the realm of <s>Yama</s> (Death),

children.text: etair dhanaiḥ pañcapadī na dīyate ||Panc_2.119||
children.translated_text: these harsh riches do not grant even five steps. [Panc 2.119]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: yathāmiṣaṃ jale matsyair bhakṣyate śvāpadair bhuvi |
children.translated_text: Just as flesh in water is eaten by fish, on land by beasts,

children.text: ākāśe pakṣibhiś caiva tathā sarvatra vittavān ||Panc_2.120||
children.translated_text: and in the sky by birds — so is the wealthy man [devoured] everywhere. [Panc 2.120]

children.text: nirdoṣam api vittāḍhya doṣair yojayate nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a faultless wealthy man is charged with faults by the king;

children.text: nidhanaḥ prāpta-doṣo 'pi sarvatra nirupadravaḥ ||Panc_2.121||
children.translated_text: but one without wealth, even if guilty, is everywhere free from trouble. [Panc 2.121]

children.text: arthānām arjanaṃ kāryaṃ vardhanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: One should earn wealth, increase it, and protect it;

children.text: bhakṣyamāṇo nirādāyaḥ sumerurapi hīyate ||Panc_2.122||
children.translated_text: even <s>Sumeru</s> itself diminishes when consumed without income. [Panc 2.122]

children.text: arthārthī yāni kaṣṭāni mūḍho 'yaṃ sahate janaḥ |
children.translated_text: The hardships that this foolish world endures for the sake of wealth —

children.text: śatāṃśenāpi mokṣārthī tāni cen mokṣam āpnuyāt ||Panc_2.123||
children.translated_text: if one seeking liberation were to endure even a hundredth part, one would attain liberation. [Panc 2.123]

children.text: ko dhīrasya manasvinaḥ sva-viṣayaḥ ko vā videśaḥ smṛto
children.translated_text: For the steadfast and spirited man, what is his own land, and what is considered a foreign land?

children.text: yaṃ deśaṃ śrayate tam eva kurute bāhu-pratāpārjitam |
children.translated_text: Whatever land he resorts to, he makes it his own, won by the prowess of his arms.

children.text: yad daṃṣṭrānakhalāṅgula-praharaṇaiḥ siṃho vanaṃ gāhate
children.translated_text: When a lion enters a forest with fangs, claws, and digits as his weapons,

children.text: tasmin eva hata-dvipendra-rudhirais tṛṣṇāṃ chinatty ātmanaḥ ||Panc_2.124||
children.translated_text: in that very forest he quenches his thirst with the blood of slain elephant-lords. [Panc 2.124]

children.text: artha-hīnaḥ pare deśe gato 'pi yaḥ prajñāvān bhavati sa kathañcid api na sīdati | uktaṃ ca-
ko 'tibhāraḥ samarthānāṃ kiṃ dūraṃ vyavasāyinām |
children.translated_text: What burden is too heavy for the capable? What is too far for the industrious?

children.text: ko videśaḥ suvdyānāṃ kaḥ paraḥ priya-vādinām ||Panc_2.125||
children.translated_text: What land is foreign to the learned? Who is a stranger to those who speak kindly? [Panc 2.125]
Even one who has gone abroad bereft of wealth, if he is wise, does not somehow perish. And it is said —

children.text: tat prajñā-nidhir bhavān na prākṛta-puruṣa-tulyaḥ | athavā-
children.translated_text: You, sir, are a treasury of wisdom, not like ordinary men. Or rather —

children.text: utsāha-sampannam adīrgha-sūtraṃ kriyā-vidhijñaṃ vyasaneṣv asaktam |
children.translated_text: One endowed with enterprise, not given to procrastination, knowing the rules of action, unattached to vices,

children.text: śūraṃ kṛtajñaṃ dṛḍha-sauhṛdaṃ ca- lakṣmīḥ svayaṃ vāñchati vāsa-hetoḥ ||Panc_2.126||
children.translated_text: brave, grateful, and firm in friendship — <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) herself desires to dwell with him. [Panc 2.126]

children.text: aparaṃ prāpto 'py arthaḥ karma-prāptyā naśyati | tad etāvanti dināni tvadīyam āsīt | muhūrtam apy anātmīyaṃ bhoktuṃ na labhyate | svayam āgatam api vidhināpahriyate |
children.translated_text: Moreover, even wealth that has been obtained perishes through the working of <s>karma</s>. So for all these days it was yours. One cannot enjoy even for a moment what is not one's own. Even what has come by itself is taken away by fate.

children.text: arthasyopārjanaṃ kṛtvā naivābhāgyaḥ samaśnute |
children.translated_text: Having earned wealth, the unfortunate one does not enjoy it;

children.text: araṇyaṃ mahadāsādya mūḍhaḥ somilako yathā ||Panc_2.127||
children.translated_text: like the foolish <s>Somilaka</s>, who having reached a great forest [lost everything]. [Panc 2.127]

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> asked: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 5
somilaka-kathā
children.translated_text: He said — Story 5: The tale of <s>Somilaka</s>.

children.text:
asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne somilako nāma kauliko vasati sma | so 'neka-vidha-paṭṭa-racanārañjitāni pārthivocitāni sadaiva vastrāṇy utpādayati | paraṃ tasya cāneka-vidha-paṭṭa-racana-nipuṇasyāpi na bhojanācchādanābhyadhikaṃ katham apy artha-mātraṃ sampadyate | athānye tatra sāmānya-kaulikāḥ sthūla-vastra-sampādana-vijñānino mahardhi-sampannāḥ | tān avalokya sa sva-bhāryām āha-priye ! paśyaitān sthūla-paṭṭa-kārakān dhana-kanaka-samṛddhān | tad adhāraṇakaṃ mamaitat sthānam | tad anyatropārjanāya gacchāmi |
sā prāha-bhoḥ priyatama ! mithyā pralapitam etad yad anyatra-gatānāṃ dhanaṃ bhavati, sva-sthāne na bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
utpatanti yad ākāśe nipatanti mahītale |
children.translated_text: They fly up into the sky, they fall upon the ground;

children.text: pakṣiṇāṃ tad api prāptyā nādattam upatiṣṭhati ||Panc_2.128||
children.translated_text: yet even for birds, what is not destined does not come to hand. [Panc 2.128]

In a certain town there lived a weaver named <s>Somilaka</s>. He always produced garments worthy of kings, adorned with various patterns of silk weaving. Yet, even though he was skilled in various silk patterns, he could not obtain even the slightest wealth beyond food and clothing. Meanwhile other ordinary weavers there, possessing knowledge only of coarse cloth production, were endowed with great prosperity. Seeing them, he said to his own wife: 'Dear one! See these makers of coarse cloth, rich in wealth and gold. This place is unprofitable for me. So I shall go elsewhere to earn.' She said: 'O dearest! What you say is false — that those who go elsewhere have wealth, while those at home do not.' And it is said —

children.text: tathā ca-
