na hi bhavati yan na bhāvyaṃ
children.translated_text: What is not destined to be does not come to be;

children.text: bhavati ca bhāvyaṃ vināpi yatnena |
children.translated_text: and what is destined comes to be even without effort.

children.text: kara-tala-gatam api naśyati
children.translated_text: Even what is already in the palm of the hand perishes

children.text: yasya tu bhavitavyatā nāsti ||Panc_2.129||
children.translated_text: for one for whom it was not meant to be. [Panc 2.129]
And likewise —

children.text: yathā dhenu-sahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaraṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as among a thousand cows, a calf finds its mother,

children.text: tathā pūrva-kṛtaṃ karma kartāram anugacchati ||Panc_2.130||
children.translated_text: so does previously performed <s>karma</s> follow the doer. [Panc 2.130]

children.text: śete saha śayānena gacchantam anugacchati |
children.translated_text: It sleeps with the one who sleeps and follows the one who walks;

children.text: narāṇāṃ prāktanaṃ karma tiṣṭhati tu sahātmanā ||Panc_2.131||
children.translated_text: a man's past <s>karma</s> remains always with him. [Panc 2.131]

children.text: yathā chāyā-tapau nityaṃ susambaddhau parasparaṃ |
children.translated_text: Just as shadow and sunlight are always mutually connected,

children.text: evaṃ karma ca kartā ca saṃśliṣṭāv itaretaram ||Panc_2.132||
children.translated_text: so the deed and the doer are bound to one another. [Panc 2.132]

children.text: kaulika āha-priye ! na samyag abhihitaṃ bhavatyā | vyavasāyaṃ vinā na karma phalati | uktaṃ ca-
yathaikena na hastena tālikā saṃprapadyate |
children.translated_text: Just as a clap cannot be produced by one hand alone,

children.text: tathodyama-parityaktaṃ na phalaṃ karmaṇaḥ smṛtam ||Panc_2.133||
children.translated_text: so the fruit of <s>karma</s> abandoned by enterprise is said not to come. [Panc 2.133]
The weaver said: 'Dear one! What you say is not right. Without enterprise, <s>karma</s> does not bear fruit.' And it is said —

children.text: paśya karma-vaśāt prāptaṃ bhojyakāle'pi bhojanam |
children.translated_text: See — even food that comes by <s>karma</s> at the time of eating

children.text: hastodyamaṃ vinā vaktre praviśen na kathañcana ||Panc_2.134||
children.translated_text: would never enter the mouth without the effort of the hand. [Panc 2.134]

children.text: tathā ca-
udyoginaṃ puruṣa-siṃham upaiti lakṣmīr
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) approaches the industrious lion among men;

children.text: daivena deyam iti kāpuruṣā vadanti |
children.translated_text: 'It is to be given by fate' — thus speak cowards.

children.text: daivaṃ nihatya kuru pauruṣam ātma-śaktyā yatne kṛte yadi na sidhyati ko 'tra doṣaḥ ||Panc_2.135||
children.translated_text: Cast aside fate and exert your own manly effort by your own power; if after effort it does not succeed, what fault is there? [Panc 2.135]
And likewise —

children.text:
tathā ca-
udyamena hi sidhyanti kāryāṇi na manorathaiḥ |
na hi suptasya siṃhasya viśanti vadane mṛgāḥ ||Panc_2.136|| udyamena vinā rājan na sidhyanti manorathāḥ |
kātarā iti jalpanti yad bhāvyaṃ tad bhaviṣyati ||Panc_2.137||
children.translated_text: the timid prattle: 'What is destined to be, will be.' [Panc 2.137]
And likewise — affairs are accomplished by effort, not by wishful thinking; prey does not enter the mouth of a sleeping lion. [Panc 2.136] Without effort, O king, desires are not fulfilled;

children.text: sva-śaktyā kurvataḥ karma na cet siddhiṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> does not grant success to one who acts by his own power,

children.text: nopālabhyaḥ pumāṃs tatra daivāntarita-pauruṣaḥ ||Panc_2.138||
children.translated_text: that man should not be blamed — his manliness is overridden by fate. [Panc 2.138]

children.text: tan mayāvaśyaṃ deśāntaraṃ gantavyam |
children.translated_text: So I must certainly go to another country.

children.text: iti niścitya vardhamāna-puraṃ gatvā tatra varṣa-trayaṃ sthitvā suvarṇa-śata-trayopārjanaṃ kṛtvā bhūyaḥ sva-gṛhaṃ prasthitaḥ | athārdha-pathe gacchatas tasya kadācid aṭavyāṃ paryaṭato bhagavān ravir astam upāgataḥ | tatra ca vyāla-bhayāt sthūlatara-vaṭa-skandha ārūhya prasupto yāvat tiṣṭhati tāvan niśīthe dvau puruṣau raudrākārau parasparaṃ jalpantāv aśṛṇot |
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, he went to the city of <s>Vardhamāna</s>, stayed there for three years, earned three hundred gold pieces, and then set out again for his home. While traveling on the halfway path, wandering in a forest one day, the blessed sun set. There, fearing wild beasts, he climbed the stout trunk of a banyan tree and fell asleep; but while resting, at midnight he heard two men of terrible form conversing with each other.

children.text: tatraika āha-bhoḥ kartaḥ tvaṃ kiṃ samyaṅ na vetsi yad asya somilakasya bhojanācchādanād ṛte'dhikā samṛddhir nāsti | tat kiṃ tvayāsya suvarṇa-śata-trayaṃ dattam |
children.translated_text: One of them said: 'O <s>Kartṛ</s> (Doer)! Do you not rightly know that for this <s>Somilaka</s>, there is no prosperity beyond food and clothing? So why have you given him three hundred gold pieces?'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ karman mayāvaśyaṃ dātavyaṃ vyavasāyināṃ tatra ca tasya pariṇatis tvad āyatteti | atha yāvad asau kaulikaḥ prabuddhaḥ suvarṇa-granthim avalokayati tāvad riktaṃ paśyati |
children.translated_text: He replied: 'O <s>Karman</s> (Destiny)! I must necessarily give to the industrious. But the outcome thereof depends on you.' Then when the weaver awoke and looked at his bundle of gold, he found it empty.

children.text:
tataḥ sākṣepaṃ cintayāmāsa | aho kim etat ? mahatā kaṣṭenopārjitaṃ vittaṃ helayā kvāpi gatam | yad vyartha-śramo 'kiñcanaḥ kathaṃ sva-patnyā mitrāṇāṃ ca mukhaṃ darśayiṣyāmi | iti niścitya tad eva pattanaṃ gataḥ | tatra ca varṣa-mātreṇāpi suvarṇa-śata-pañcakam upārjya bhūyo 'pi sva-sthānaṃ prati prasthitaḥ | yāvad ardha-pathe bhūyo 'ṭavī-gatasya bhagavān bhānur astaṃjagāmātha suvarṇa-nāśa-bhayāt suśrānto 'pi na viśrāmyati kevalaṃ kṛta-gṛhotkaṇṭhaḥ satvaraṃ vrajati |
atrāntare dvau puruṣau tādṛṣau dṛṣṭi-deśe samāgacchantau jalpantau ca śṛṇoti | tatraikaḥ prāha-bhoḥ kartaḥ ! kiṃ tvayaitasya suvarṇa-śata-pañcakaṃ dattam ? tat kiṃ na vetsi yad bhojanācchādanābhyadhikam asya kiṃcin nāsti |
children.translated_text: Then he thought bitterly: 'Ah, what is this? Wealth earned with great hardship has gone somewhere carelessly. Now I, having labored in vain and become destitute — how shall I show my face to my wife and friends?' Having thus resolved, he went to that very city again. And there, in just a year, having earned five hundred gold pieces, he set out once more for home. While on the halfway path, again having entered the forest, the blessed sun set. Due to fear of losing his gold, though exhausted, he did not rest but, yearning eagerly for home, hurried onward. In the meantime, he saw those two men of the same appearance approaching within sight and conversing. One of them said: 'O <s>Kartṛ</s>! Why have you given this man five hundred gold pieces? Don't you know that he has nothing beyond food and clothing?'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ karman ! mayāvaśyaṃ deyaṃ vyavasāyinām | tasya pariṇāmas tvad-āyattaḥ | tat kiṃ mām upālambhayasi ?
children.translated_text: He replied: 'O <s>Karman</s>! I must necessarily give to the industrious. The outcome depends on you. So why do you reproach me?'

children.text: tac chrutvā somilako yāvad granthim avalokayati tāvat suvarṇaṃ nāsti | tataḥ paraṃ duḥkham āpanno vyacintayat-aho kiṃ mama dhana-rahitasya jīvitena ? tad atra vaṭa-vṛkṣa ātmānam udbadhya prāṇāṃs tyajāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, when <s>Somilaka</s> looked at his bundle, the gold was gone. Then, plunged into extreme grief, he thought: 'Alas, what use is life for me without wealth? So here, on this banyan tree, I shall hang myself and give up my life.'

children.text: evaṃ niścitya darbha-mayīṃ rajjuṃ vidhāya sva-kaṇṭhe pāśaṃ niyojya śākhāyām ātmānaṃ nibadhya yāvat prakṣipati tāvad ekaḥ pumān ākāśa-stha evedam āha-bho bhoḥ somilaka ! maivaṃ sāhasaṃ kuru | ahaṃ te vittāpahārako na te bhojanācchādanābhyadhikaṃ varāṭikām api sahāmi | tad gaccha sva-gṛhaṃ prati | anyac ca bhavadīya-sāhasenāhaṃ tuṣṭaḥ | tathā me na syād vyarthaṃ darśanam | tat prārthyatām abhīṣṭo varaḥ kaścit |
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, making a rope of <s>darbha</s> grass, fastening a noose around his own neck, binding himself to a branch, just as he was about to throw himself down, a certain being standing in the sky spoke thus: 'Ho! Ho! <s>Somilaka</s>! Do not commit such a rash act! I am the one who took away your wealth. I do not allow you even a single cowrie beyond food and clothing. So go home. Moreover, I am pleased by your daring. Therefore my appearance should not be in vain. So ask for whatever boon you desire.'

children.text: somilaka āha-yady evaṃ tad dehi me prabhūtaṃ dhanam |
children.translated_text: <s>Somilaka</s> said: 'If so, then give me abundant wealth.'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ ! kiṃ kariṣyasi bhoga-rahitena dhanena yatas tava bhojanācchādanābhyadhikā prāptir api nāsti ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He replied: 'Sir, what will you do with wealth devoid of enjoyment, since there is no attainment for you beyond food and clothing?' And it is said —

children.text: kiṃ tayā kriyate lakṣmyā yā vadhūr iva kevalā |
children.translated_text: What use is that <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth) which is like a wife kept secluded?

children.text: yā na veśyeva sāmānyā pathikair upabhujyate ||Panc_2.139||
children.translated_text: Not like a courtesan enjoyed in common by travelers. [Panc 2.139]

children.text: somilaka āha-yady api bhogo nāsti tathāpi bhavatu me dhanam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Somilaka</s> said: 'Even if there is no enjoyment, still let me have wealth.' And it is said —

children.text: kṛpaṇo 'py akulīno 'pi sadā saṃśrita-mānuṣaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a miser, even one of ignoble birth, is always

children.text: sevyate sa naro loke yasya syād vitta-sañcayaḥ ||Panc_2.140||
children.translated_text: served by people who depend on him — that man in this world who has an accumulation of wealth. [Panc 2.140]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: śithilau ca subaddhau ca patataḥ patato na vā |
children.translated_text: Whether loosely or tightly bound, whether they fall or do not fall —

children.text: nirīkṣitau mayā bhadre daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca ||Panc_2.141||
children.translated_text: I have observed them, O good sir, for fifteen years. [Panc 2.141]

children.text: puruṣa āha-kim etat ?
children.translated_text: The being said: 'What is this?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text:
kathā 6
tīkṣṇa-viṣāṇa-śṛgāla-kathā
children.translated_text: Story 6: The tale of <s>Tīkṣṇaviṣāṇa</s> and the jackal.

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne tīkṣṇaviṣāṇo nāma mahā-vṛṣabho vasati | sa ca madātirekāt parityakta-nija-yūṭhaḥ śṛṅgābhyāṃ nadī-taṭāni vidārayan svecchayā marakata-sadṛśāni śaṣpāṇi bhakṣayann araṇya-caro babhūva | atha tatraiva vane pralobhako nāma śṛgālaḥ prativasati sma | sa kadācit sva-bhāryayā saha nadī-tīre sukhopaviṣṭas tiṣṭhati | atrāntare sa tīkṣṇaviṣāṇo jalārthaṃ tad eva pulinam avatīrṇaḥ | tataś ca tasya lambamānau vṛṣaṇāv ālokya śṛgālyā śṛgālo 'bhihitaḥ-svāmin ! paśyāsya vṛṣabhasya māṃsa-piṇḍau lambamānau yathā sthitau | tataḥ kṣaṇena prahareṇa vā patiṣyataḥ | evaṃ jñātvā bhavatā pṛṣṭha-yāyinā bhāvyaṃ |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a great bull named <s>Tīkṣṇaviṣāṇa</s> (Sharp-horns). Due to excess of rut, having abandoned his own herd, tearing up riverbanks with his horns, eating emerald-like grass at will, he became a forest-wanderer. Now in that very forest there lived a jackal named <s>Pralobhaka</s> (the Greedy). Once, he was sitting comfortably with his wife on the bank of a river. In the meantime, that <s>Tīkṣṇaviṣāṇa</s> descended to that very sandbank for water. Then, seeing his two testicles hanging, the she-jackal said to the jackal: 'Husband! Look at these two lumps of flesh hanging from this bull. They will fall off at any moment or at a blow. Knowing this, you should follow behind him.'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-priye ! na jñāyate kadācid etayoḥ patanaṃ bhaviṣyati vā na vā | tat kiṃ vṛthā śramāya māṃ niyojayasi ? atra-sthas tāvaj jalārtham āgatān mūṣakān bhakṣayiṣyāmi samaṃ tvayā | mārgo 'yaṃ yatas teṣām | atha yadā tvāṃ muktvāsya tīkṣṇaviṣāṇasya vṛṣabhasya pṛṣṭhe gamiṣyāmi tadāgatyānyaḥ kaścid etat sthānaṃ samāśrayiṣyati | naitad yujyate kartum | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Dear wife! It is not known whether these two will ever fall or not. So why do you set me to labor in vain? Staying here, I shall eat the mice that come for water, together with you. This is their path. Now, if I were to leave you and follow the back of this sharp-horned bull, someone else would come and take over this spot. That would not be right to do.' And it is said —

children.text: yo dhruvāṇi parityajyādhruvāṇi niṣevate |
children.translated_text: He who abandons what is certain and pursues what is uncertain —

children.text: dhruvāṇi tasya naśyanti adhruvaṃ naṣṭam eva ca ||Panc_2.142||
children.translated_text: what is certain perishes for him, and what is uncertain is already lost. // Panc_2.142 //

children.text: śṛgāly āha-bhoḥ kāpuruṣas tvaṃ yat kiṃcit prāptaṃ tenāpi santoṣaṃ karoṣi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The she-jackal said: 'Bah! You are a coward, content with whatever little you have obtained!' And it is said —

children.text: supūrā syāt kunadikā supūro mūṣikāñjaliḥ |
children.translated_text: A small stream is easily filled; a mouse's cupped hands are easily filled;

children.text: susantuṣṭaḥ kāpuruṣaḥ svalpakenāpi tuṣyati ||Panc_2.143||
children.translated_text: a coward is easily satisfied — he is content with even a trifle. // Panc_2.143 //

children.text: tasmāt puruṣeṇa sadaivotsāhavatā bhāvyam | uktaṃ ca-
yatrotsāha-samārambho yatrālasya-vinigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there is the commencement of enterprise, where there is the restraint of laziness,

children.text: naya-vikrama-saṃyogas tatra śrīr acalā dhruvaṃ ||Panc_2.144||
children.translated_text: where there is the conjunction of policy and valor — there <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) is surely unwavering. // Panc_2.144 //
'Therefore a man should always be full of enterprise.' And it is said —

children.text: tad daivam iti sañcintya tyajen nodyogam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not abandon one's own effort, thinking 'it is fate';

children.text: anuyogaṃ vinā tailaṃ tilānāṃ nopajāyate ||Panc_2.145||
children.translated_text: without pressing, oil does not arise from sesame seeds. // Panc_2.145 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: yaḥ stokenāpi santoṣaṃ kurute mandadhīr janaḥ |
children.translated_text: The dull-witted man who is content with even a little —

children.text: tasya bhāgya-vihīnasya dattā śrīr api mārjyate ||Panc_2.146||
children.translated_text: for that one bereft of fortune, even wealth that has been given is wiped away. // Panc_2.146 //

children.text: yac ca tvaṃ vadasi | etau patiṣyato na veti | tad apy ayuktam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'And as for what you say — whether these two will fall or not — that too is wrong.' And it is said —

children.text: kṛta-niścayino vandyās tuṅgimā nopabhujyate |
children.translated_text: Those of firm resolve are to be praised; loftiness is not enjoyed [by the timid];

children.text: cātakaḥ ko varāko 'yaṃ yasyendro vārivāhakaḥ ||Panc_2.147||
children.translated_text: how pitiable is the <s>cātaka</s> bird — yet <s>Indra</s> himself is its water-bearer! // Panc_2.147 //

children.text: aparaṃ mūṣaka-māṃsasya nirviṇṇāham | etau ca māṃsa-piṇḍau patana-prāyau dṛśyete | tat sarvathā nānyathā kartavyam iti | athāsau tad ākarṇya mūṣaka-prāpti-sthānaṃ parityajya tīkṣṇaviṣāṇasya pṛṣṭham anvagacchat | atha vā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, I am sick of mouse-flesh! And these two lumps of meat look as though they are about to fall. So by all means, it must not be otherwise.' Then he, hearing that, abandoned the spot where mice could be obtained and followed the back of the sharp-horned [bull]. Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: tāvat syāt sarva-kṛtyeṣu puruṣo 'tra svayaṃ prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: A man remains his own master in all matters

children.text: strī-vākyāṅkuśa-vikṣuṇṇo yāvan no dhriyate balāt ||Panc_2.148||
children.translated_text: only so long as he is not forcibly restrained by the goad of a woman's words. // Panc_2.148 //

children.text: akṛtyaṃ manyate kṛtyaṃ agamyaṃ manyate sugam |
children.translated_text: A man goaded by a woman's words considers what should not be done as fit to be done,

children.text: abhakṣyaṃ manyate bhakṣyaṃ strī-vākya-prerito naraḥ ||Panc_2.149||
children.translated_text: what is impassable as easy, and what should not be eaten as fit to eat. // Panc_2.149 //

children.text: evaṃ sa tasya pṛṣṭhataḥ sa-bhāryaḥ paribhramaṃś cira-kālam anayat | na ca tayoḥ patanam abhūt | tataś ca nirvedāt pañcadaśe varṣe śṛgālaḥ svabhāryām āha-śithilau ca subaddhau ca (141) ityādi |
children.translated_text: Thus, following behind it together with his wife, he wandered for a very long time. But neither of the two fell. Then, out of disgust, in the fifteenth year, the jackal said to his wife: 'Loose and well-tied...' (verse 141) and so on.

children.text: tayos tat-paścād api pāto na bhaviṣyati | tat tad eva sva-sthānaṃ gacchāvaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-śithilau ca subaddhau ca (141) iti |
children.translated_text: 'Even after this, no fall of theirs will happen. So let us go back to our own place.' Therefore I say: 'Loose and well-tied...' (verse 141).

children.text: puruṣa āha-yady evaṃ tad gaccha bhūyo 'pi vardhamāna-puram | tatra dvau vaṇik-putrau vasataḥ | eko gupta-dhanaḥ | dvitīya upabhukta-dhanaḥ | tatas tayoḥ svarūpaṃ buddhvaikasya varaḥ prārthanīyaḥ | yadi te dhanena prayojanam abhakṣitena tatas tvām api gupta-dhanaṃ karomi | athavā datta-bhogyena dhanena te prayojanaṃ tad upabhukta-dhanaṃ karomīti | evam uktvādarśanaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: The man [<s>Lakṣmī</s>'s agent] said: 'If so, then go once again to the city of <s>Vardhamāna</s>. Two merchant's sons live there. One hoards his wealth; the second spends his wealth. Then, having observed the nature of both, the boon should be sought from one of them. If your need is for wealth that is not consumed, then I shall make you too a hoarder of wealth. Or if your need is for wealth that is given and enjoyed, then I shall make you a spender of wealth.' Having said this, he vanished.

children.text: somilako 'pi vismita-manā bhūyo 'pi vardhamāna-puraṃ gataḥ | atha sandhyā-samaye śrāntaḥ katham api tat-puraṃ prāpto guptadhana-gṛhaṃ pṛcchan kṛcchrāl labdhvāstamita-sūrye praviṣṭaḥ | athāsau bhāryā-putra-sametena guptadhanena nirbhartsyamāno haṭhād gṛhaṃ praviśyopaviṣṭaḥ | tataś ca bhojana-velāyāṃ tasyāpi bhakti-varjitaṃ kiṃcid aśanaṃ dattam | tataś ca bhuktvā tatraiva yāvat supto niśīthe paśyati tāvat tāv api dvau puruṣau parasparaṃ mantrayataḥ | tatraika āha-bhoḥ kartaḥ ! kiṃ tvayāsya guptadhanasyānyo 'dhiko vyayo nirmito yat somilakasyānena bhojanaṃ dattam | tad ayuktaṃ tvayā kṛtam |
children.translated_text: <s>Somilaka</s> too, his mind amazed, went once again to the city of <s>Vardhamāna</s>. Then, exhausted at twilight, having somehow reached that city and having asked [the way] with difficulty, he entered the house of <s>Guptadhana</s> (the hoarder) after sunset. There, scolded by <s>Guptadhana</s> together with his wife and children, he forcibly entered the house and sat down. Then, at mealtime, some food devoid of devotion was given to him too. Then, having eaten, he slept right there. At midnight he saw those same two men conferring with each other. One of them said: 'O <s>Kartā</s> (Destiny)! Why have you created an expenditure beyond the allotment for this <s>Guptadhana</s>, in that food was given to <s>Somilaka</s>? What you have done is improper.'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ karman ! na mamātra doṣaḥ | mayā puruṣasya lābha-prāptir dātavyā | tat-pariṇatiḥ punas tvad-āyatteti | athāsau yāvad uttiṣṭhati tāvad guptadhano visūcikayā khidyamāno rujābhibhūtaḥ kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭhati | tato dvitīye'hni tad-doṣeṇa kṛtopavāsaḥ sañjātaḥ |
children.translated_text: The other said: 'O <s>Karma</s>! The fault is not mine. I must grant the acquisition of gain to a man. Its outcome, however, depends on you.' Then, as he rose, <s>Guptadhana</s>, afflicted by cholera and overcome with pain, lay suffering for a while. Then, on the second day, due to his illness, a fast was imposed [on the household].

children.text: somilako 'pi prabhāte tad-gṛhān niṣkramya upabhuktadhana-gṛhaṃ gataḥ | tenāpi cābhyutthādinā sat-kṛto vihita-bhojanācchādana-saṃmānas tasyaiva gṛhe bhavya-śayyām āruhya suṣvāpa | tataś ca niśīthe yāvat paśyati tāvat tāv eva dvau puruṣau mitho mantrayataḥ | atra tayor eka āha-bhoḥ kartaḥ ! anena somilakasyopakāraṃ kurvatā prabhūto vyayaḥ kṛtaḥ | tat kathaya katham asyoddhāraka-vidhir bhaviṣyati | anena sarvam etad vyavahāraka-gṛhāt samānītam |
children.translated_text: <s>Somilaka</s> too, in the morning, left that house and went to the house of <s>Upabhuktadhana</s> (the spender). By him too, with a rising welcome, he was honored with food and clothing provided with respect, and sleeping on a fine bed in that very house, he slept well. Then at midnight, he saw those same two men conferring with each other. There, one of them said: 'O <s>Kartā</s>! By doing a favor to this <s>Somilaka</s>, [<s>Upabhuktadhana</s>] has incurred great expenditure. So tell me, how will the means of his recovery come about? He has obtained all this from the house of the tradesman.'

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ karman ! mama kṛtyam etat | pariṇatis tvad-āyatteti | atha prabhāta-samaye rāja-puruṣo rāja-prasādajaṃ vittam ādāya samāyāta upabhukta-dhanāya samarpayām āsa |
children.translated_text: The other said: 'O <s>Karma</s>! This is my task. The outcome depends on you.' Then, at daybreak, a king's officer arrived bringing wealth as a royal favor and delivered it to <s>Upabhuktadhana</s>.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā somilakaś cintayāmāsa | sañcaya-rahito 'pi varam eṣa upabhuktadhano nāsau kadaryo guptadhanaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Seeing that, <s>Somilaka</s> reflected: 'Even without savings, this <s>Upabhuktadhana</s> is better than that miser <s>Guptadhana</s>.' And it is said —

children.text: agnihotra-phalā vedāḥ śīla-vṛtta-phalaṃ śrutam |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> have the <s>Agnihotra</s> as their fruit; learning has good character and conduct as its fruit;

children.text: rati-putra-phalā dārā datta-bhukta-phalaṃ dhanam ||Panc_2.150||
children.translated_text: a wife has love and sons as her fruit; wealth has giving and enjoying as its fruit. // Panc_2.150 //

children.text: tad vidhātā māṃ datta-bhukta-dhanaṃ karotu | na kāryaṃ me guptadhanena | tataḥ somilako dattabhuktadhanaḥ saṃjātaḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-arthasyopārjanaṃ kṛtvā iti |
children.translated_text: 'So let the Creator make me one who gives and enjoys wealth. I have no use for hoarded wealth.' Then <s>Somilaka</s> became one who gives and enjoys wealth. Therefore I say: 'Having earned wealth...'

children.text: gṛha-madhya-nikhātena dhanena dhanino yadi |
children.translated_text: If by wealth buried in the midst of the house we become wealthy,

children.text: bhavāmaḥ kiṃ na tenaiva dhanena dhanino vayaṃ ||Panc_2.151||
children.translated_text: then are we not wealthy by that very [buried] wealth? // Panc_2.151 //

children.text: tad bhadra ! hiraṇyakaivaṃ jñātvā dhana-viṣaye santāpo na kāryaḥ | atha vidyamānam api dhanaṃ bhojya-bandhyatayā tad-avidyamānaṃ mantavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So, good friend <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>! Knowing this, one should not grieve over wealth. Moreover, even wealth that exists, if it is barren of enjoyment, should be regarded as non-existent.' And it is said —

children.text: upārjitānām arthānāṃ tyāga eva hi rakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Of wealth that has been earned, giving alone is the [true] protection;

children.text: taḍāgodara-saṃsthānāṃ parīvāha ivāmbhasām ||Panc_2.152||
children.translated_text: like an overflow-channel for the waters stored within a reservoir. // Panc_2.152 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: upārjitānām arthānāṃ tyāga eva hi rakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Of wealth that has been earned, giving alone is the [true] protection;

children.text: taḍāgodara-saṃsthānāṃ parivāha ivāmbhasām ||Panc_2.153||
children.translated_text: like an overflow-channel for the waters stored within a reservoir. // Panc_2.153 //

children.text:
anyac ca-
dānaṃ bhogo nāśas tisro gatayo bhavanti vittasya | yo na dadāti na bhuṅkte tasya tṛtīyā gatir bhavati ||Panc_2.154||
children.translated_text:
And further —
Giving, enjoying, and perishing — these are the three destinations of wealth; he who neither gives nor enjoys — for him the third destination comes about. // Panc_2.154 //

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā vivekinā na sthity-arthaṃ vittopārjanaṃ kartavyaṃ yato duḥkhāya tat | uktaṃ ca-
dhanādikeṣu vidyante ye'tra mūrkhāḥ sukhāśayāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those fools who, expecting happiness, [pursue] wealth and the like —

children.text: tapta-grīṣmeṇa sevante śaityārthaṃ te hutāśanam ||Panc_2.155||
children.translated_text: they, scorched by summer's heat, seek out fire for the sake of coolness. // Panc_2.155 //
Knowing this, a discerning person should not earn wealth merely for the purpose of accumulation, for that leads to suffering. And it is said —

children.text: sarpāḥ pibanti pavanaṃ na ca durbalās te
children.translated_text: Serpents drink the wind, yet they are not weak;

children.text: śuṣkais tṛṇair vana-gajā balino bhavanti |
children.translated_text: forest elephants grow mighty on dry grass;

children.text: kandaiḥ phalair muni-varā gamayanti kālaṃ
children.translated_text: great sages pass the time on roots and fruits —

children.text: santoṣa eva puruṣasya paraṃ nidhānam ||Panc_2.156||
children.translated_text: contentment alone is the supreme treasure of a man. // Panc_2.156 //

children.text: santoṣāmṛta-tṛptānāṃ yat sukhaṃ śānta-cetasām |
children.translated_text: The happiness of those with tranquil minds, sated with the nectar of contentment —

children.text: kutas tad-dhana-lubdhānām itaś cetaś ca dhāvatām ||Panc_2.157||
children.translated_text: whence would that come to the wealth-greedy, running hither and thither? // Panc_2.157 //

children.text: pīyūṣam iva saṃtoṣaṃ pibatāṃ nirvṛtiḥ parā |
children.translated_text: For those who drink contentment as if it were ambrosia, there is supreme bliss;

children.text: duḥkhaṃ nirantaraṃ puṃsām asaṃtoṣavatāṃ punaḥ ||Panc_2.158||
children.translated_text: but for men who are discontented, there is unceasing suffering. // Panc_2.158 //

children.text: nirodhāc cetaso 'kṣāṇi niruddhāny akhilāny api |
children.translated_text: By the restraint of the mind, all the senses too are restrained —

children.text: ācchādite ravau meghaiḥ sañchannāḥ syur gabhastayaḥ ||Panc_2.159||
children.translated_text: [just as] when the sun is covered by clouds, its rays are hidden. // Panc_2.159 //

children.text:
vāñchā-vicchedanaṃ prāhuḥ svāsthyaṃ śāntā maha-rṣayaḥ |
vāñchā nivartate nārthaiḥ pipāsevāgni-sevanaiḥ ||Panc_2.160|| anindyam api nindanti stuvanty astutyam uccakaiḥ |
svāpateya-kṛte martyāḥ kiṃ kiṃ nāma na kurvate ||Panc_2.161||
children.translated_text: for the sake of their own property, what indeed do mortals not do? // Panc_2.161 //

The severing of desire, the tranquil great sages declare, is well-being;
desire is not quenched by objects of desire, just as thirst is not [quenched] by attending upon fire. // Panc_2.160 // Men revile even the blameless and praise even the unpraiseworthy loudly;

children.text: dharmārthaṃ yasya vittehā tasyāpi na śubhāvahā |
children.translated_text: Even the desire for wealth for the sake of <s>dharma</s> does not bring good fortune;

children.text: prakṣālanādd hi paṅkasya dūrād asparśanaṃ varam ||Panc_2.162||
children.translated_text: for better than washing mud is simply not touching it from afar. // Panc_2.162 //

children.text: dānena tulyo nidhir asti nānyo
children.translated_text: There is no treasure equal to giving,

children.text: lobhāc ca nānyo 'sti paraḥ pṛthivyām |
children.translated_text: and no enemy on earth greater than greed;

children.text: vibhūṣaṇaṃ śīla-samaṃ na cānyat
children.translated_text: there is no ornament equal to good character,

children.text: santoṣa-tulyaṃ dhanam asti nānyat ||Panc_2.163||
children.translated_text: and no wealth equal to contentment. // Panc_2.163 //

children.text: dāridryasya parā mūrtir yan māna-draviṇālpatā |
children.translated_text: The supreme form of poverty is a paucity of honor and wealth;

children.text: jarad-gava-dhanaḥ śarvas tathāpi parameśvaraḥ ||Panc_2.164||
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose wealth is an old bull, is yet the Supreme Lord. // Panc_2.164 //

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā bhadra tvayā santoṣaḥ kārya iti | mantharakavacanam ākarṇya vāyasa āha-bhadra mantharako yad evaṃ vadati tat tvayā citte kartavyam | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'Knowing this, good friend, you should practice contentment.' Hearing <s>Mantharaka</s>'s words, the crow said: 'Good friend, what <s>Mantharaka</s> says thus — you should take it to heart.' Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājan satataṃ priya-vādinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Easy to find, O king, are men who always speak pleasantly;

children.text: apriyasya ca pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||Panc_2.166||
children.translated_text: but rare is one who speaks, and one who hears, what is disagreeable yet salutary. // Panc_2.166 //

children.text: apriyāṇy api pathyāni ye vadanti nṛṇām iha |
children.translated_text: Those who speak to men what is disagreeable yet beneficial —

children.text: ta eva suhṛdaḥ proktā anye syur nāma-dhārakāḥ ||Panc_2.167||
children.translated_text: they alone are declared to be true friends; the rest are merely name-bearers. // Panc_2.167 //

children.text: athaivaṃ jalpatāṃ teṣāṃ citrāṅgo nāma hariṇo lubdhaka-trāsitas tasminn eva sarasi praviṣṭaḥ | athāyāntaṃ sa-sambhramam avalokya laghupatanako vṛkṣam ārūḍhaḥ | hiraṇyakaḥ śarastambaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | mantharakaḥ salilāśayam āsthitaḥ | atha laghupatanako mṛgaṃ samyak parijñāya mantharakam uvāca-ehy ehi sakhe mantharaka ! mṛgo 'yaṃ tṛṣārto 'tra samāyātaḥ sarasi praviṣṭaḥ | tasya śabdo 'yaṃ na mānuṣa-sambhava iti |
children.translated_text: While they were thus conversing, a deer named <s>Citrāṅga</s>, frightened by a hunter, entered that very lake. Then, seeing him approach in alarm, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> (the crow) climbed up a tree; <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> (the mouse) entered a clump of reeds; and <s>Mantharaka</s> (the tortoise) took to the water. Then <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, having properly recognized the deer, said to <s>Mantharaka</s>: 'Come, come, friend <s>Mantharaka</s>! This deer, tormented by thirst, has come here and entered the lake. His sound is not of human origin.'

children.text: tac chrutvā mantharako deśa-kālocitam āha-bho laghupatanaka ! yathāyaṃ mṛgo dṛśyate prabhūtam ucchvāsam udvahann udbhrānta-dṛṣṭyā pṛṣṭhato 'valokayati tan na tṛṣārta eṣa nūnaṃ lubdhaka-trāsitaḥ | taj jñāyatām asya pṛṣṭhe lubdhakā āgacchanti na veti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Mantharaka</s> spoke words suited to the time and place: 'O <s>Laghupatanaka</s>! As this deer appears — drawing deep breaths, looking about with startled eyes, glancing behind him — he is certainly not merely thirsty but frightened by a hunter. So let it be ascertained whether hunters are coming behind him or not.' And it is said —

children.text: bhaya-trasto naraḥ śvāsaṃ prabhūtaṃ kurute muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: A man stricken with fear repeatedly draws heavy breaths,

children.text: diśo 'valokayaty eva na svāsthyaṃ vrajati kvacit ||Panc_2.168||
children.translated_text: looks in every direction, and nowhere attains composure. // Panc_2.168 //

children.text: tac chrutvā citrāṅga āha-bho mantharaka ! jñātaṃ tvayā samyaṅ me trāsa-kāraṇam | ahaṃ lubdhaka-śara-prahārād uddhāritaḥ kṛcchreṇātra samāyātaḥ | mama yūthaṃ tair lubdhakair vyāpāditaṃ bhaviṣyati | tac charaṇāgatasya me darśaya kiṃcid agamyaṃ sthānaṃ lubdhakānām |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Citrāṅga</s> said: 'O <s>Mantharaka</s>! You have correctly understood the cause of my fear. I, barely rescued from the blow of a hunter's arrow, have come here with difficulty. My herd must have been slain by those hunters. So, to me who has come seeking refuge, show some place inaccessible to the hunters.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya mantharaka āha-bhoś citrāṅga ! śrūyatāṃ nīti-śāstram |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Mantharaka</s> said: 'O <s>Citrāṅga</s>! Hear the teaching of the <s>Nītiśāstra</s>:'

children.text: dvāv upāyāv iha proktau vimuktau śatru-darśane |
children.translated_text: Two means are prescribed here for one freed from the sight of enemies:

children.text: hastayoś cālanād eko dvitīyaḥ pāda-vega-jaḥ ||Panc_2.169||
children.translated_text: one is the waving of the hands [for speed], and the second arises from the swiftness of the feet. // Panc_2.169 //

children.text: tad gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ ghanaṃ vanaṃ yāvad adyāpi nāgacchanti te durātmāno lubdhakāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'So go quickly to the dense forest, as long as those evil-souled hunters have not yet come even today.'

children.text:
atrāntare laghupatanakaḥ satvaram abhyupetyovāca-bho mantharaka ! gatās te lubdhakāḥ sva-gṛhonmukhāḥ pracura-māṃsa-piṇḍa-dhāriṇaḥ | tac citrāṅga ! tvaṃ viśrabdho jalād bahir bhava |
tatas te catvāro 'pi mitra-bhāvam āśritās tasmin sarasi madhyāhna-samaye vṛkṣa-cchāyādhastāt subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-sukham anubhavantaḥ sukhena kālaṃ nayanti | athavā yuktam etad ucyate-
subhāṣita-rasāsvāda-baddha-romāñca-kañcukaṃ |
children.translated_text: The happiness of poets grows — their bodies covered with goosebumps from savoring wise sayings —

children.text: vināpi saṃgamaṃ strīṇāṃ kavīnāṃ sukham edhate ||Panc_2.170||
children.translated_text: even without the company of women. ||Panc_2.170||

Meanwhile, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> quickly approached and said: O <s>Mantharaka</s>! Those hunters have gone homeward carrying abundant pieces of flesh. So, <s>Citrāṅga</s>, come out of the water with confidence!
Then those four, having assumed the bond of friendship, passed their time happily at that lake, beneath the shade of a tree at midday, enjoying the pleasure of conversation about wise sayings. Or rather, this is rightly said —

children.text: subhāṣita-maya-dravya-saṅgrahaṃ na karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who does not accumulate a treasury of substance made of wise sayings —

children.text: sa tu prastāva-yajñeṣu kāṃ pradāsyati dakṣiṇām ||Panc_2.171||
children.translated_text: what fee will he offer at the sacrifices of discourse? ||Panc_2.171||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: sakṛd uktaṃ na gṛhṇāti svayaṃ vā na karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who does not grasp [a thing] told once, or does not do [it] himself,

children.text: yasya saṃpuṭikā nāsti kutas tasya subhāṣitam ||Panc_2.172||
children.translated_text: he who has no casket [of learning] — whence will he have wise sayings? ||Panc_2.172||

children.text: athaikasminn ahani goṣṭhī-samaye mṛgo nāyātaḥ | atha te vyākulībhūtāḥ parasparaṃ jalpitum ārabdhāḥ | aho kim adya suhṛn na samāyātaḥ | kiṃ siṃhādibhiḥ kvacid vyāpādita uta lubdhakair atha vānale prapatito gartā-viṣame vā nava-tṛṇa-laulyād iti | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
sva-gṛhodyāna-gate'pi snigdhaiḥ pāpaṃ viśaṅkyate mohāt |
children.translated_text: Even when a loved one has merely gone to one's own garden, affectionate ones, from delusion, suspect evil;

children.text: kim u dṛṣṭa-bahv-apāya-pratibhaya-kāntāra-madhya-sthe ||Panc_2.173||
children.translated_text: what then when he is in the midst of a forest, terrifying with its many visible dangers? ||Panc_2.173||

Now one day, at the time of their gathering, the deer did not come. Then they became anxious and began to talk among themselves: Ah, why has our friend not come today? Has he been killed somewhere by lions and such, or by hunters, or has he fallen into fire or into a pit or rough [terrain] through the greed for fresh grass? Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: atha mantharako vāyasam āha-bho laghupatanakāhaṃ hiraṇyakaś ca tāvad dvāv apy aśaktau tasyānveṣaṇaṃ kartuṃ mandagatitvāt | tad gatvā tvam araṇyaṃ śodhaya yadi kutracit taṃ jīvantaṃ paśyasīti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mantharaka</s> said to the crow: O <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, I and <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> — we two are unable to search for him, because of our slow movement. So go and search the forest; [see] if you find him alive somewhere.

children.text: tad ākarṇya laghupatanako nātidūre yāvad gacchati tāvat palvala-tīre citrāṅgaḥ kūṭa-pāśa-niyantritas tiṣṭhati | taṃ dṛṣṭvā śoka-vyākulita-manās tam avocat | bhadra kim idam ? citrāṅgo 'pi vāyasam avalokya viśeṣeṇa duḥkhita-manā babhūva | athavā yuktam etat-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> went not far and found <s>Citrāṅga</s> standing at the edge of a pool, restrained by a snare-trap. Seeing him, his mind agitated with grief, he said: Dear one, what is this? <s>Citrāṅga</s> too, seeing the crow, became especially sorrowful in mind. Or rather, this is fitting —

children.text: api mandatvam āpanno naṣṭo vāpīṣṭa-darśanāt |
children.translated_text: Even one who has merely become sluggish, or lost from the sight of a dear one —

children.text: prāyeṇa prāṇināṃ bhūyo duḥkhāvego 'dhiko bhavet ||Panc_2.174||
children.translated_text: for living beings, generally the surge of grief increases all the more. ||Panc_2.174||

children.text: tataś ca vāṣpāvasāne citrāṅgo laghupatanakam āha-bho mitra saṃjāto 'yaṃ tāvan mama mṛtyuḥ | tad yuktaṃ sampannaṃ yad bhavatā saha me darśanaṃ sañjātam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, after his tears subsided, <s>Citrāṅga</s> said to <s>Laghupatanaka</s>: O friend, my death has now arrived. So it is fitting and fortunate that I have had a meeting with you. And it is said —

children.text: prāṇātyaye samutpanne yadi syān mitra-darśanaṃ |
children.translated_text: When death is imminent, if there should be the sight of a friend,

children.text: tad dvābhyāṃ sukha-daṃ paścāj jīvato 'pi mṛtasya ca ||Panc_2.175||
children.translated_text: then it gives happiness to both — to the one who lives thereafter and to the one who dies. ||Panc_2.175||

children.text: tat kṣantavyaṃ yan mayā praṇayāt subhāṣita-goṣṭhīṣv abhihitaṃ | tathā hiraṇyaka-mantharakau mama vākyād vācyau |
children.translated_text: So may whatever I have said out of affection in our gatherings of wise sayings be forgiven. Likewise, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> and <s>Mantharaka</s> should be told on my behalf:

children.text: ajñānāj jñānato vāpi duruktaṃ yad udāhṛtam |
children.translated_text: Whatever harsh thing was spoken by me, whether from ignorance or knowingly,

children.text: mayā tat kṣamyatām adya dvābhyām api prasādataḥ ||Panc_2.176||
children.translated_text: may that be forgiven today by both of you, out of kindness. ||Panc_2.176||

children.text: tac chrutvā laghupatanaka āha-bhadra na bhetavyam asmad-vidhair mitrair vidyamānaiḥ | yāvad ahaṃ drutataraṃ hiraṇyakaṃ gṛhītvāgacchāmi | aparaṃ ye sat-puruṣā bhavanti te vyasane na vyākulatvam upayānti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> said: Dear one, there is nothing to fear while friends like us exist. I shall go most quickly and bring <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> back. Moreover, those who are good persons do not become agitated in adversity. And it is said —

children.text: sampadi yasya na harṣo vipadi viṣādo raṇe na bhīrutvaṃ | taṃ bhuvana-traya-tilakaṃ janayati jananī sutaṃ viralaṃ ||Panc_2.177||
children.translated_text: He who has no elation in prosperity, no dejection in adversity, no cowardice in battle — such a son, the ornament of the three worlds, a mother bears but rarely. ||Panc_2.177||

children.text: evam uktvā laghupatanakaś citrāṅgam āśvāsya yatra hiraṇyaka-mantharakau tiṣṭhatas tatra gatvā sarvaṃ citrāṅga-pāśa-patanaṃ kathitavān | hiraṇyakaṃ ca citrāṅga-pāśa-mokṣaṇaṃ prati kṛta-niścayaṃ pṛṣṭham āropya bhūyo 'pi satvaraṃ citrāṅga-samīpe gataḥ | so 'pi mūṣakam avalokya kiṃcij jīvitāśayā saṃśliṣṭa āha-
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, having comforted <s>Citrāṅga</s>, went to where <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> and <s>Mantharaka</s> were and told them everything about <s>Citrāṅga</s>'s fall into the snare. Then, having placed <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, who had made up his mind to free <s>Citrāṅga</s> from the snare, upon his back, he went again quickly to <s>Citrāṅga</s>'s side. He [<s>Citrāṅga</s>] too, seeing the mouse, embracing [him] with some hope of life, said —

children.text: āpan-nāśāya vibudhaiḥ kartavyāḥ suhṛdo 'malāḥ |
children.translated_text: For the destruction of calamity, the wise should make pure friends;

children.text: na taraty āpadaṃ kaścid yo 'tra mitra-vivarjitaḥ ||Panc_2.178||
children.translated_text: no one who is bereft of friends here crosses over calamity. ||Panc_2.178||

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhadra tvaṃ tāvan nīti-śāstra-jño dakṣa iti | tat katham atra kūṭa-pāśe patitaḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: Dear one, you are indeed one who knows the science of statecraft, and you are capable. So how have you fallen into this snare-trap?

children.text: sa āha-bho na kālo 'yaṃ vivādasya | tan na yāvat sa pāpātmā lubdhakaḥ samabhyeti tāvad drutataraṃ kartayemaṃ mat-pāda-pāśaṃ |
children.translated_text: He said: Friend, this is not the time for argument. So quickly cut this snare on my feet before that evil-souled fowler approaches!

children.text: tad ākarṇya vihasyāha hiraṇyakaḥ-kiṃ mayy api samāyāte lubdhakād bibheṣi tataḥ śāstraṃ prati mahatī me viraktiḥ sampannā yad bhavad-vidhā api nīti-śāstra-vida etām avasthāṃ prāpnuvanti | tena tvāṃ pṛcchāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> laughed and said: Even when I have arrived, are you afraid of the fowler? Then I have developed a great disenchantment with the science [of statecraft] — since even those like you who know the science of statecraft reach such a state. Therefore I ask you.

children.text: sa āha-bhadra karmaṇā buddhir api hanyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Dear one, by [force of] karma, even intelligence is destroyed. And it is said —

children.text: kṛtānta-pāśa-baddhānāṃ daivopahata-cetasāṃ |
children.translated_text: Of those bound by the noose of Death, whose minds are afflicted by fate,

children.text: buddhayaḥ kubja-gāminyo bhavanti mahatām api ||Panc_2.179||
children.translated_text: the intellects go crookedly, even of great ones. ||Panc_2.179||

children.text: vidhātrā racitā yā sā lalāṭe'kṣara-mālikā |
children.translated_text: The string of syllables that was written by the Creator on the forehead —

children.text: na tāṃ mārjayituṃ śaktāḥ sva-śaktyāpy atipaṇḍitāḥ ||Panc_2.180||
children.translated_text: even the supremely learned are not able to erase it by their own power. ||Panc_2.180||

children.text:
evaṃ tayoḥ pravadatoḥ suhṛd-vyasana-santapta-hṛdayo mantharakaḥ śanaiḥ śanais taṃ pradeśam ājagāma | taṃ dṛṣṭvā laghupatanako hiraṇyakam āha-aho na śobhanam āpatitam |
hiraṇyaka āha-kiṃ sa lubdhakaḥ samāyāti ?
children.translated_text:
While those two were thus conversing, <s>Mantharaka</s>, his heart burning with grief for his friend's adversity, came slowly to that place. Seeing him, <s>Laghupatanaka</s> said to <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>: Ah, something inauspicious has happened!
<s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: What — is that fowler coming?

children.text: sa āha-āstāṃ tāval lubdhaka-vārtā | eṣa mantharakaḥ samāgacchati | tad anītir anuṣṭhitānena yato vayam apy asya kāraṇān nūnaṃ vyāpādanaṃ yāsyāmo yadi sa pāpātmā lubdhakaḥ samāgamiṣyati | tad ahaṃ tāvat kham utpatiṣyāmi | tvaṃ punar bilaṃ praviṣyātmānaṃ rakṣayiṣyasi | citrāṅgo 'pi vegena dig-antaraṃ yāsyati | eṣa punar jalacaraḥ sthale kathaṃ bhaviṣyatīti vyākulo 'smi | atrāntare prāpto 'yaṃ mantharakaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: Set aside the talk of the fowler! This <s>Mantharaka</s> is approaching. He has done something contrary to good policy, for on his account we too shall surely be killed if that evil-souled fowler comes. For I shall fly up into the sky; you will enter your hole and protect yourself; <s>Citrāṅga</s> too will run swiftly to another quarter. But this one, being a water-creature, how will he fare on land? — this is what troubles me. Meanwhile, this <s>Mantharaka</s> has arrived.

children.text: hiraṇyaka āha-bhadra, na yuktam anuṣṭhitaṃ bhavatā yad atra samāyātaḥ | tad bhūyo 'pi drutataraṃ gamyatāṃ yāvad asau lubdhako na samāyāti |
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: Dear one, what you have done is not proper — that you have come here. So go back again as quickly as possible before that fowler arrives!

children.text: mantharaka āha-bhadra, kiṃ karomi ? na śaknomi tatra-stho mitra-vyasanāgni-dāghaṃ soḍhum | tenāham atrāgataḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: <s>Mantharaka</s> said: Dear one, what can I do? I cannot endure, while staying there, the burning of the fire of a friend's adversity. Therefore I have come here. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: dayita-jana-viprayogo vitta-viyogaś ca sahyāḥ syuḥ |
children.translated_text: Separation from loved ones and loss of wealth would be bearable,

children.text: yadi sumahauṣadha-kalpo vayasya-jana-saṃgamo na syāt ||Panc_2.181||
children.translated_text: if there were not the company of friends — [which is] like a great medicine. ||Panc_2.181||

children.text: varaṃ prāṇa-parityāgo na viyogo bhavādṛśaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Better the abandonment of life than separation from ones like you;

children.text: prāṇā janmāntare bhūyo na bhavanti bhavad-vidhāḥ ||Panc_2.182||
children.translated_text: life-breaths [may come] again in another birth, but ones like you will not. ||Panc_2.182||

children.text: evaṃ tasya pravadata ākarṇa-pūrita-śarāsano lubdhako 'py upāgataḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā mūṣakeṇa tasya snāyu-pāśas tat-kṣaṇāt khaṇḍitaḥ | atrāntare citrāṅgaḥ satvaraṃ pṛṣṭham avalokayan pradhāvitaḥ | laghupatanako vṛkṣam ārūḍhaḥ | hiraṇyakaś ca samīpa-varti bilaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | athāsau lubdhako mṛga-gamanād viṣaṇṇa-vadano vyartha-śramas taṃ mantharakaṃ mandaṃ mandaṃ sthala-madhye gacchantaṃ dṛṣṭavān | acintayac ca-yady api kuraṅgo dhātrāpahṛtas tathāpy ayaṃ kūrma āhārārthaṃ sampāditaḥ | tad adyāsyāmiṣeṇa me kuṭumbasyāhāra-nirvṛttir bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: While he was thus speaking, the fowler too arrived, his bow drawn to the ear. Seeing him, the mouse instantly cut the sinew-snare. Meanwhile, <s>Citrāṅga</s> quickly ran away looking back over his shoulder. <s>Laghupatanaka</s> flew up onto a tree. <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> entered a burrow nearby. Then that fowler, his face downcast at the deer's escape, his effort wasted, saw <s>Mantharaka</s> going slowly in the middle of the open ground. And he thought: Even though the deer has been snatched away by fate, still this turtle has been procured for food. So today, with his flesh, the feeding of my family will be accomplished.

children.text: evaṃ vicintya taṃ darbhaiḥ sañchādya dhanuṣu samāropya skandhe kṛtvā gṛhaṃ prati prasthitaḥ | atrāntare taṃ nīyamānam avalokya hiraṇyako duḥkhākulaḥ paryadevayat-kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ kaṣṭam āpatitam |
children.translated_text: Having thought thus, he covered him with <s>darbha</s> grass, placed him on his bow upon his shoulder, and set out toward home. Meanwhile, seeing him being carried away, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, distressed, lamented: Alas! A terrible calamity has occurred!

children.text: ekasya duḥkhasya na yāvad antaṃ
children.translated_text: Before I reach the end of one sorrow,

children.text: gacchāmy ahaṃ pāram ivārṇavasya |
children.translated_text: as of an ocean's far shore,

children.text: tāvad dvitīyaṃ samupasthitaṃ me chidreṣv anarthā bahulī-bhavanti ||Panc_2.183||
children.translated_text: a second [sorrow] has arrived upon me — in vulnerabilities, misfortunes multiply. ||Panc_2.183||

children.text: tāvad askhalitaṃ yāvat sukhaṃ yāti same pathi |
children.translated_text: One goes without stumbling only so long as [one travels] happily on an even path;

children.text: skhalite ca samutpanne viṣame ca pade pade ||Panc_2.184||
children.translated_text: but when a stumble occurs, [it happens] on rough [ground], at every step. ||Panc_2.184||

children.text: yan namraṃ saralaṃ cāpi yac cāpatsu na sīdati |
children.translated_text: That which is flexible and straight, and which does not falter in calamities —

children.text: dhanur mitraṃ kalatraṃ ca durlabhaṃ śuddha-vaṃśajam ||Panc_2.185||
children.translated_text: a bow, a friend, and a wife — [these are] hard to find, born of a pure lineage. ||Panc_2.185||

children.text: na mātari na dāreṣu na sodarye na cātmaje |
children.translated_text: Not in a mother, not in wives, not in a brother, not in a son

children.text: viśrambhas tādṛśaḥ puṃsāṃ yādṛṅ mitre nirantare ||Panc_2.186||
children.translated_text: is there such trust for men as in an inseparable friend. ||Panc_2.186||

children.text: yadi tāvat kṛtāntena me dhana-nāśo vihitas tan-mārga-śrāntasya me viśrāma-bhūtaṃ mitraṃ kasmād apahṛtaṃ | aparam api mitraṃ paraṃ mantharaka-samaṃ na syāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: If indeed fate has decreed the loss of my wealth, then why has my friend — who was a place of rest for me, weary from that path — been taken away? Moreover, there would be no other friend equal to <s>Mantharaka</s>. And it is said —

children.text: asampattau paro lābho guhyasya kathanaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Gain when there is no prosperity, the telling of a secret,

children.text: āpad-vimokṣaṇaṃ caiva mitrasyaitat phala-trayam ||Panc_2.187||
children.translated_text: and deliverance from calamity — these are the three fruits of a friend. ||Panc_2.187||

children.text: tad asya paścān nānyaḥ suhṛn me | tat kiṃ mamopary anavarataṃ vyasana-śarair varṣati hanta vidhiḥ | yata ādau tāvad vitta-nāśas tataḥ parivāra-bhraṃśas tato deśa-tyāgas tato mitra-viyoga iti | athavā svarūpam etat sarveṣām eva jantūnāṃ jīvita-dharmasya | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So after him, I have no other friend. Why does fate incessantly rain arrows of adversity upon me? For first there was the loss of wealth, then the loss of retinue, then the abandonment of one's land, then the separation from a friend. Or rather, this is the very nature of the law of life for all creatures. And it is said —

children.text: kāyaḥ saṃnihitāpāyaḥ sampadaḥ padam āpadām |
children.translated_text: The body has destruction close at hand; prosperities are the abode of calamities;

children.text: samāgamāḥ sāpagamāḥ sarvam utpādi bhaṅguram ||Panc_2.188||
children.translated_text: meetings have separations — everything that arises is perishable. ||Panc_2.188||

children.text: tathā ca-
kṣate prahārā nipatanty abhīkṣṇaṃ
children.translated_text: On a wound, blows fall repeatedly;

children.text: dhana-kṣaye vardhati jāṭharāgniḥ |
children.translated_text: when wealth is lost, the digestive fire increases;

children.text: āpatsu vairāṇi samudbhavanti
children.translated_text: in calamities, enmities arise —

children.text: cchidreṣv anarthā bahulī-bhavanti ||Panc_2.189||
children.translated_text: in vulnerabilities, misfortunes multiply. ||Panc_2.189||
And likewise —

children.text: aho sādhūktaṃ kenāpi |
children.translated_text: Ah, how well this was said by someone:

children.text: prāpte bhaye paritrāṇaṃ prīti-viśrambha-bhājanaṃ |
children.translated_text: Rescue when danger arrives, a vessel of love and trust —

children.text: kena ratnam idaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ mitram ity akṣara-dvayaṃ ||Panc_2.190||
children.translated_text: by whom was this jewel created — the two syllables 'mi-tra' (friend)? ||Panc_2.190||

children.text: atrāntare ākranda-parau citrāṅga-laghupatanakau tatraiva samāyātau | atha hiraṇyaka āha-aho kiṃ vṛthā-pralapitena | tad yāvad eṣa mantharako dṛṣṭi-gocarān na nīyate tāvad asya mokṣopāyaś cintyatām iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, <s>Citrāṅga</s> and <s>Laghupatanaka</s>, both crying out, came to that very place. Then <s>Hiraṇyaka</s> said: Ah, what use is this vain lamentation? So before this <s>Mantharaka</s> is carried beyond the range of sight, let a means of his liberation be devised. And it is said —

children.text: vyasanaṃ prāpya yo mohāt kevalaṃ paridevayet |
children.translated_text: He who, upon encountering adversity, merely laments from delusion,

children.text: krandanaṃ vardhayaty eva tasyāntaṃ nādhigacchati ||Panc_2.191||
children.translated_text: only increases his weeping — he does not reach its end. ||Panc_2.191||

children.text: kevalaṃ vyasanasyoktaṃ bheṣajaṃ naya-paṇḍitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The sole remedy for adversity, declared by those skilled in policy, is:

children.text: tasyoccheda-samārambho viṣāda-parivarjanaṃ ||Panc_2.192||
children.translated_text: the undertaking of its removal and the avoidance of despondency. ||Panc_2.192||

children.text: anyac ca-
atīta-lābhasya surakṣaṇārthaṃ
children.translated_text: For the purpose of protecting a gain already obtained,

children.text: bhaviṣya-lābhasya ca saṅgamārtham |
children.translated_text: for the purpose of achieving a future gain,

children.text: āpat-prapannasya ca mokṣaṇārthaṃ
children.translated_text: and for the purpose of freeing one who has fallen into calamity —

children.text: yan mantryate'sau paramo hi mantraḥ ||Panc_2.193||
children.translated_text: that which is deliberated upon — that indeed is the supreme counsel. ||Panc_2.193||
And further —

children.text: tac chrutvā vāyasa āha-bho yady evaṃ tat kriyatāṃ mad-vacaḥ | eṣa citrāṅgo 'sya mārge gatvā kiṃcit palvalam āsādya tasya tīre niścetano bhūtvā patatu | aham apy asya śirasi samāruhya mandaiś cañcu-prahāraiḥ śira ullekhiṣyāmi yenāsau lubdhako 'muṃ mṛtaṃ matvā mama cañcu-prahāra-pratyayena mantharakaṃ bhūmau kṣiptvā mṛgārthe dhāvati | atrāntare tvayā darbha-maya-bandhana-veṣṭanāni khaṇḍanīyāni yenāsau mantharako drutataraṃ palvalaṃ praviśati |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crow said: Friend, if so, then let my words be carried out. Let this <s>Citrāṅga</s> go to the fowler's path, reach some pool, and lie on its bank as if lifeless. And I, mounting upon his head, will slowly scratch his head with [gentle] beak-blows, so that the fowler, thinking him dead and convinced by my beak-blows, will throw <s>Mantharaka</s> on the ground and run after the deer. Meanwhile, you must cut through the grass-rope bindings so that <s>Mantharaka</s> may quickly enter the pool.

children.text: citrāṅgaḥ prāha-bho bhadro 'yaṃ dṛṣṭo mantras tvayā | nūnaṃ mantharako mukto mantavyaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Citrāṅga</s> said: Friend, this is an excellent plan you have devised! Surely <s>Mantharaka</s> must be considered as good as freed. And it is said —

children.text: siddhiṃ vā yadi vāsiddhiṃ cittotsāho nivedayet |
children.translated_text: Whether success or failure — the enthusiasm of the heart would reveal [it].

children.text: prathamaṃ sarva-jantūnāṃ prājño vetti na cetaraḥ ||Panc_2.194||
children.translated_text: the wise one knows first among all creatures — not the other. ||Panc_2.194||

children.text: tat tad evaṃ kriyatām | tathānuṣṭhite sa lubdhakas tathaiva mārgāsanna-palvala-tīrasthaṃ citrāṅgaṃ vāyasa-sanātham adrākṣīt | taṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣita-manā vyacintayat | nūnaṃ pāśa-vedanayā varāko 'yaṃ mṛgo gatvāyuḥ-śeṣa-jīvitaḥ pāśaṃ troṭayitvā katham apy etad vanāntaraṃ praviṣṭo yāvan mṛtaḥ | tad vaśyo 'yaṃ me kacchapaḥ suyantritatvāt | tad enam api tāvad gṛhṇāmīty avardhāya kacchapaṃ bhū-tale prakṣipya mṛgam upādravat |
children.translated_text: So let that be done thus. When this was carried out, the hunter saw <s>Citrāṅga</s> (the deer), accompanied by the crow, standing near a swamp by the roadside. Seeing him, he thought with a delighted mind: 'Surely this poor deer, from the pain of the snare, having gone and lived by the remainder of his lifespan, somehow broke the snare and entered this other forest, where he has now died. And this turtle of mine is well-secured.' So, having tightened [the grass-binding on the turtle], he threw the turtle on the ground and ran toward the deer.

children.text: atrāntare hiraṇyakena vajropama-daṃṣṭrā-prahāreṇa tad darbha-veṣṭanaṃ tat-kṣaṇāt khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtaṃ | mantharako 'pi tṛṇa-madhyān niṣkramya palvalaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | citrāṅgo 'py aprāptasyāpi tasyotthāya vāyasena saha drutaṃ pranaṣṭaḥ | atrāntare vilakṣo viṣāda-paro nivṛtto lubdhako yāvat paśyati tāvat kacchapo 'pi gataḥ | tataś ca tatropaviśyemaṃ ślokam apaṭhat-
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile, <s>Hiraṇyaka</s>, with diamond-like fangs, cut that grass-binding to pieces in an instant. <s>Mantharaka</s> too, emerging from within the grass, entered the swamp. <s>Citrāṅga</s> also, before [the hunter] could arrive, rose and fled swiftly with the crow. In the meanwhile, the confounded hunter, overwhelmed with despair, turned back — and saw that the turtle too was gone. Then, sitting down there, he recited this verse:

children.text: prāpto bandhanam apy ayaṃ guru-mṛgas tāvat tvayā me hṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Even this heavy deer that I had captured — you took from me;

children.text: samprāptaḥ kamaṭhaḥ sa cāpi niyataṃ naṣṭas tavādeśataḥ |
children.translated_text: and the turtle I had obtained — he too has surely been lost by your doing;

children.text: kṣut-kṣāmo 'tra vane bhramāmi śiśukais tyaktaḥ samaṃ bhāryayā
children.translated_text: wasting with hunger, I wander in this forest, abandoned by my children along with my wife;

children.text: yac cānyan na kṛtaṃ kṛtānta kurute tac cāpi sahyaṃ mayā ||Panc_2.195||
children.translated_text: and whatever else fate has not already done — even that I endure. ||Panc_2.195||

children.text: evaṃ bahu-vidhaṃ vilapya sva-gṛhaṃ gataḥ | atha tasmin dūrī-bhūte sarve'pi te kāka-kūrma-mṛgākhavaḥ paramānanda-bhājo militvā parasparam āliṅgya punar jātān ivātmano manyamānas tad eva saraḥ prāpya mahā-sukhena subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-vinodaṃ kurvantaḥ kālaṃ nayanti sma | evaṃ jñātvā vivekinā mitra-saṅgrahaḥ kāryaḥ | tathā mitreṇa sahāvyājena vartitavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Having lamented thus in many ways, he went to his own home. Then, when he was far away, all of them — crow, turtle, deer, and mouse — meeting together in supreme joy, embracing one another, considering themselves as if reborn, reached that very lake and passed their time in great happiness, entertained by conversation full of wise sayings. Knowing this, the discerning person should make a collection of friends. And one should behave with friends without deceit. And it is said:

children.text: yo mitrāṇi karoty atra na kauṭilyena vartate |
children.translated_text: He who makes friends here and does not behave with crookedness —

children.text: taiḥ samaṃ na parābhūtiṃ samprāpnoti kathañcana ||Panc_2.196||
children.translated_text: together with them, he never suffers defeat in any way. ||Panc_2.196||

children.text:
iti śrī-viṣṇu-śarma-viracite pañcatantre mitra-samprāptir nāma
dvitīyaṃ tantraṃ samāptam
||2||
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the second <s>tantra</s> (book), called <s>Mitra-samprāpti</s> (The Gaining of Friends), in the <s>Pañcatantra</s> composed by the revered <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>.
||2||

children.text:
tṛtīyaṃ tantram
atha kākolūkīyam
children.translated_text:
The Third Book
Now [begins] the <s>Kākolūkīya</s> (Of Crows and Owls)

children.text:
prastāvanā kathā
meghavarṇārimardana-vṛttāntaḥ
children.translated_text:
Introductory Story
The Account of <s>Meghavarṇa</s> and <s>Arimardana</s>

children.text: athedam ārabhyate kākolūkīyaṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ tantram | yasyāyam ādyaḥ ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now this third <s>tantra</s> (book) called <s>Kākolūkīya</s> is begun. Its opening verse is:

children.text: na viśvaset pūrva-virodhitasya
children.translated_text: One should not trust an enemy formerly hostile

children.text: śatroś ca mitratvam upāgatasya |
children.translated_text: who has assumed the guise of friendship;

children.text: dagdhāṃ guhāṃ paśya ulūka-pūrṇāṃ
children.translated_text: behold the burnt cave full of owls,

children.text: kāka-praṇītena hutāśanena ||Panc_3.1||
children.translated_text: set afire by one contrived by the crows. ||Panc_3.1||

children.text: tad yathānuśruyate-asti dakṣiṇātye janapade mahilāropyaṃ nāma nagaram | tasya samīpastho 'neka-śākhāsanātho 'tighanatara-patra-cchanno nyagrodha-pādapo 'sti | tatra ca megha-varṇo nāma vāyasa-rājo 'neka-kāka-parivāraḥ prativasati sma | sa tatra vihita-durga-racanaḥ saparijanaḥ kālaṃ nayati | tathānyo 'ri-mardano nāmolūka-rājo 'saṅkhyolūka-parivāro giri-guhā-durgāśrayaḥ prativasati sma | sa ca rātrāv abhyetya sadaiva tasya nyagrodhasya samantāt paribhramati | atholūkarājaḥ pūrva-virodha-vaśādyaṃ kañcid vāyasa-samāsādayati | taṃ vyāpādya gacchati | evaṃ nityābhigamanāc chanaiḥ śanais tan nyagrodha-pādapad-durgaṃ tena samantān nirvāyasaṃ kṛtam | athavā bhavaty evam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: As the story is heard: In the southern country there is a city called <s>Mahilāropya</s>. Near it stands a banyan tree, supported by many branches, covered with extremely dense foliage. And there dwelt a crow-king named <s>Meghavarṇa</s>, surrounded by many crows. He, having constructed fortifications there, passed his time with his retinue. Likewise, another — an owl-king named <s>Arimardana</s>, surrounded by innumerable owls — dwelt in the shelter of a mountain-cave fortress. And he would come at night and constantly circle around that banyan tree. Then the owl-king, impelled by former enmity, would seize any crow he encountered and kill him before departing. Thus, through constant attacks, he gradually cleared the entire banyan-tree fortress of crows on all sides. Or rather, so it is. And it is said:

children.text: ya upekṣeta śatruṃ svaṃ prasarantaṃ yadṛcchayā |
children.translated_text: He who ignores his own enemy advancing at will,

children.text: rogaṃ cālasya-saṃyuktaḥ sa śanais tena hanyate ||Panc_3.2||
children.translated_text: and a disease — combined with laziness — is gradually destroyed by it. ||Panc_3.2||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: jāta-mātraṃ na yaḥ śatruṃ vyādhiṃ ca praśamaṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: He who does not bring to an end an enemy or a disease at its very birth —

children.text: mahābalo 'pi tenaiva vṛddhiṃ prāpya sa hanyate ||Panc_3.3||
children.translated_text: even though very powerful, is destroyed by that very [foe] which has grown. ||Panc_3.3||

children.text: athānyedyuḥ sa vāyasa-rājaḥ sarvān sacivān āhūya provāca-bhoḥ ! utkaṭas tāvad asmākaṃ śatrur udyama-sampannaś ca kālavic ca nityam eva niśāgame sametyāsmat-pakṣa-kadanaṃ karoti | tat katham asya prativighātavyam ? vayaṃ tāvad rātrau na paśyāmaḥ | na ca divā durgaṃ vijānīmo yena gatvā praharāmaḥ | tad atra kiṃ yujyate sandhi-vigraha-yānāsana-saṃśraya-dvaidhī-bhāvānāṃ madhyāt | atha te procuḥ-yuktam abhihitaṃ devena yad eṣa praśnaḥ kṛtaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, that crow-king, having summoned all his ministers, said: 'Sirs! Our enemy is formidable, endowed with enterprise, and knows the [right] time — constantly, at nightfall, he comes and causes slaughter of our side. So how is he to be counteracted? We cannot see at night, nor do we know his fortress by day so that we might go and strike. So what is appropriate here — among peace, war, marching, encampment, seeking refuge, and double-dealing?' Then they said: 'The king has rightly asked this question.' And it is said:

children.text: apṛṣṭenāpi vaktavyaṃ sacivenātra kiṃcana |
children.translated_text: A minister should speak something even unasked;

children.text: pṛṣṭena tu viśeṣeṇa vācyaṃ pathyaṃ mahīpateḥ ||Panc_3.4||
children.translated_text: and when asked, he should especially state what is wholesome for the king. ||Panc_3.4||

children.text: yo na pṛṣṭo hitaṃ brūte pariṇāme sukhāvaham |
children.translated_text: He who, without being asked, tells what is beneficial and in the end brings happiness,

children.text: mantro na priya-vaktā ca kevalaṃ sa ripuḥ smṛtam ||Panc_3.5||
children.translated_text: and is not merely a pleasant-speaker in counsel — only he is considered an [enemy who is not that, i.e.,] true [minister]; otherwise he is remembered as a foe. ||Panc_3.5||

children.text: tasmād ekāntam āsādya kāryo mantro mahīpate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having found privacy, the king should hold counsel,

children.text: yena tasya vayaṃ kurmo niyamaṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā ||Panc_3.6||
children.translated_text: by which we may impose upon him restraint and [find] the means [to do so]. ||Panc_3.6||

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: balīyasi praṇamatāṃ kāle praharatām api |
children.translated_text: Prosperity does not come to those who bow before the powerful and also strike at the [right] time —

children.text: sampado nāvagacchanti pratīpam iva nimnagāḥ ||Panc_3.7||
children.translated_text: [flowing] backward like a river. ||Panc_3.7||

children.text: satyāḍhyo dhārmikaś cāryo bhrātṛ-saṅghātavān balī |
children.translated_text: An enemy who is wealthy in truth, righteous, noble, strong through fraternal unity,

children.text: aneka-vijayī caiva sandheyaḥ sa ripur bhavet ||Panc_3.8||
children.translated_text: and victorious in many [battles] — with him peace should be made. ||Panc_3.8||

children.text: sandhiḥ kāryo 'py anāryeṇa vijñāya prāṇa-saṃśayam |
children.translated_text: Peace should be made even with an ignoble one when danger to life is perceived;

children.text: prāṇaiḥ saṃrakṣitaiḥ sarvaṃ yato bhavati rakṣitam ||Panc_3.9||
children.translated_text: for when life is preserved, everything is preserved. ||Panc_3.9||

children.text: aneka-yuddha-vijayī sandhānaṃ yasya gacchati |
children.translated_text: One victorious in many wars, who enters into alliance —

children.text: tat-prabhāveṇa tasyāśu vaśaṃ gacchanty arātayaḥ ||Panc_3.10||
children.translated_text: by the power of that [alliance], his enemies quickly come under [his] control. ||Panc_3.10||

children.text: sandhim icchet samenāpi sandigdho vijayī yudhi |
children.translated_text: One should seek peace even with an equal when victory in battle is uncertain;

children.text: na hi sāṃśayikaṃ kuryād ity uvāca bṛhaspatiḥ ||Panc_3.11||
children.translated_text: one should not do what is doubtful — so said <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. ||Panc_3.11||

children.text: sandigdho vijayo yuddhe janānām iha yuddhyatām |
children.translated_text: Victory in battle is uncertain for people who fight here;

children.text: upāya-tritayād ūrdhvaṃ tasmād yuddhaṃ samācaret ||Panc_3.12||
children.translated_text: therefore, [only] after [exhausting] the three [other] means, should one resort to war. ||Panc_3.12||

children.text: asandadhāno mānāndhaḥ samenāpi hato bhṛśam |
children.translated_text: One who, blinded by pride, does not make peace even with an equal, is utterly destroyed —

children.text: āmakumbham ivābhittvā nāvatiṣṭheta śaktimān ||Panc_3.13||
children.translated_text: like an unfired pot [easily shattered]; the powerful one, having smashed [it], would not stand [in danger]. ||Panc_3.13||

children.text: samaṃ śaktimatā yuddham aśaktasya hi mṛtyave |
children.translated_text: Battle with a powerful one is for the weak unto death;

children.text: vṛṣatkumbhaṃ yathā bhittvā tāvat tiṣṭhati śaktimān ||Panc_3.14||
children.translated_text: just as having smashed a fired pot — so long does the powerful one endure. ||Panc_3.14||

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover:

children.text: bhūmir mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ vā vigrahasya phala-trayam |
children.translated_text: Land, allies, or gold — these are the three fruits of war;

children.text: nāsty ekam api yady eṣāṃ vigrahaṃ na samācaret ||Panc_3.15||
children.translated_text: if not even one of these [is attainable], one should not resort to war. ||Panc_3.15||

children.text: khanann ākhu-bilaṃ siṃhaḥ pāṣāṇa-śakalākulam |
children.translated_text: A lion digging a mouse's hole, filled with stone-fragments,

children.text: prāpnoti nakha-bhaṅgaṃ hi phalaṃ vā mūṣako bhavet ||Panc_3.16||
children.translated_text: would get broken claws — and the fruit would be [only] a mouse. ||Panc_3.16||

children.text: tasmān na syāt phalaṃ yatra puṣṭaṃ yuddhaṃ tu kevalam |
children.translated_text: Therefore where there would be no [worthwhile] fruit but only fattened war,

children.text: na hi tat svayam utpādyaṃ kartavyaṃ na kathañcana ||Panc_3.17||
children.translated_text: one should never produce that on one's own initiative. ||Panc_3.17||

children.text: balīyasā samākrānto vaitasīṃ vṛttim āśrayet |
children.translated_text: One overrun by a more powerful [foe] should adopt the policy of the reed (bending with the wind),

children.text: vāñchann abhraṃśinīṃ lakṣmīṃ na bhaujaṅgī kadācana ||Panc_3.18||
children.translated_text: desiring unfailing prosperity — never the policy of the serpent (rigid striking). ||Panc_3.18||

children.text: kurvan hi vaitasīṃ vṛttiṃ prāpnoti mahatīṃ śriyam |
children.translated_text: For one following the reed-policy attains great prosperity;

children.text: bhujaṅga-vṛttim āpanno vadham arhati kevalam ||Panc_3.19||
children.translated_text: one who has adopted the serpent-policy merely deserves death. ||Panc_3.19||

children.text: kaurmaṃ saṅkocam āsthāya prahārān api marṣayet |
children.translated_text: Adopting the tortoise-posture of contraction, one should endure even blows;

children.text: kāle kāle ca matimān uttiṣṭhet kṛṣṇa-sarpavat ||Panc_3.20||
children.translated_text: and at the [right] time, the wise one should rise up — like a black serpent. ||Panc_3.20||

children.text: āgataṃ vigrahaṃ vidvān upāyaiḥ praśamaṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: The wise one should bring an approaching conflict to an end by expedients;

children.text: vijayasya hy anityatvād rabhasena na sampatet ||Panc_3.21||
children.translated_text: for since victory is uncertain, one should not rush in impetuously. ||Panc_3.21||

children.text: balinā saha yoddhavyam iti nāsti nidarśanam |
children.translated_text: There is no precedent that one should fight with the powerful;

children.text: prativātaṃ na hi ghanaḥ kadācid upasarpati ||Panc_3.22||
children.translated_text: a cloud never moves against the wind. ||Panc_3.22||

children.text: śatruṇā na hi sandadhyāt suśliṣṭenāpi sandhinā |
children.translated_text: One should not make peace with an enemy — even with a well-joined treaty;

children.text: sutaptam api pānīyaṃ śamayaty eva pāvakam ||Panc_3.23||
children.translated_text: for even well-heated water extinguishes fire [i.e., the heat is temporary]. ||Panc_3.23||

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: satya-dharma-vihīnena na sandadhyāt kathañcana |
children.translated_text: With one devoid of truth and <s>dharma</s>, one should never make peace;

children.text: sugandhito 'py asādhutvād acirād yāti vikriyām ||Panc_3.24||
children.translated_text: even a fragrant [substance], through its unwholesomeness, quickly undergoes deterioration. ||Panc_3.24||

children.text: tasmāt tena yoddhavyam iti me matiḥ | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore one should fight with him — that is my opinion.' And it is said:

children.text: krūro lubdho 'laso 'satyaḥ pramādī bhīrur asthiraḥ |
children.translated_text: An enemy who is cruel, greedy, lazy, untruthful, negligent, cowardly, and unsteady,

children.text: mūḍho yodhāvamantā ca sukhocchedyo bhaved ripuḥ ||Panc_3.25||
children.translated_text: foolish, and a scorner of warriors — such an enemy can be easily overthrown. ||Panc_3.25||

children.text: aparaṃ tena parābhūtā vayam | tad yadi sandhāna-kīrtanaṃ kariṣyāmas tad bhūyo 'tyantaṃ kopaṃ kariṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, we have been humiliated by him. If we were to speak of making peace, he would become all the more excessively enraged.' And it is said:

children.text: caturthopāya-sādhye tu ripau sāntvam apakriyā |
children.translated_text: When an enemy is to be subdued by the fourth means [force], conciliation is harmful;

children.text: svedyam āma-jvaraṃ prājñaḥ ko 'mbhasā pariṣiñcati ||Panc_3.26||
children.translated_text: what wise man douses with water a fever that [should be] sweated out? ||Panc_3.26||

children.text: sāmavādāḥ sakopasya śatroḥ pratyuta dīpikāḥ |
children.translated_text: Conciliatory words to an enraged enemy are like kindling;

children.text: prataptasyeva sahasā sarpiṣas toya-bindavaḥ ||Panc_3.27||
children.translated_text: like drops of water upon heated butter, [they only cause it to flare up]. ||Panc_3.27||

children.text: pramāṇābhyadhikasyāpi mahat-sattvam adhiṣṭhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having taken his stand in great courage, even against one exceeding in size,

children.text: padaṃ mūrdhni samādhatte kesarī matta-dantinaḥ ||Panc_3.28||
children.translated_text: the lion places his foot upon the head of a rut-maddened elephant. ||Panc_3.28||

children.text: utsāha-śakti-sampanno hanyāc chatruṃ laghur gurum |
children.translated_text: One endowed with the power of enterprise should slay even a heavy enemy, though light [himself];

children.text: yathā kaṇṭhīravo nāgaṃ bhāradvājaḥ pracakṣate ||Panc_3.29||
children.translated_text: just as the lion [slays] the elephant — so says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>. ||Panc_3.29||

children.text: māyayā śatravo vadhyā avadhyāḥ syur balena ye |
children.translated_text: Enemies who cannot be slain by force should be slain by stratagem;

children.text: yathā strī-rūpam āsthāya hato bhīmena kīcakaḥ ||Panc_3.30||
children.translated_text: just as <s>Kīcaka</s> was slain by <s>Bhīma</s>, who assumed the form of a woman. ||Panc_3.30||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: mṛtyor ivogra-daṇḍasya rājño yānti vaśaṃ dviṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Enemies come under the sway of a king whose rod [of punishment] is fierce like <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death);

children.text: sarvaṃsahaṃ tu manyante tṛṇāya ripavaś ca tam ||Panc_3.31||
children.translated_text: but one who endures everything — enemies consider him as a blade of grass. ||Panc_3.31||

children.text: na jātu śamanaṃ yasya tejas tejasvi-tejasām |
children.translated_text: He whose fiery energy never quells the energies of the energetic —

children.text: vṛthā jātena kiṃ tena mātur yauvana-hāriṇā ||Panc_3.32||
children.translated_text: what use is his birth? He merely steals his mother's youth. ||Panc_3.32||

children.text: yā lakṣmīr nānuliptāṅgī vair-śoṇita-kuṅkumaiḥ |
children.translated_text: That <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) whose body is not anointed with the saffron of enemies' blood —

children.text: kāntāpi manasaḥ prītiṃ na sā dhatte manasvinām ||Panc_3.33||
children.translated_text: even though beautiful, does not bring joy to the hearts of the valiant. ||Panc_3.33||

children.text: ripu-raktena saṃsiktā tat-strī-netrāmbubhis tathā |
children.translated_text: The earth of that king which is not sprinkled with enemies' blood and with the tears of their women —

children.text: na bhūmir yasya bhūpasya kā ślāghā tasya jīvite ||Panc_3.34||
children.translated_text: what glory is there in his life? ||Panc_3.34||

children.text: balotkaṭena duṣṭena maryādā-rahitena ca |
children.translated_text: With one who is mightily powerful, wicked, and devoid of propriety —

children.text: na sandhi-vigrahau naiva vinā yānaṃ praśasyate ||Panc_3.35||
children.translated_text: neither peace nor war, nor even marching alone, is recommended. ||Panc_3.35||

children.text: dvidhākāraṃ bhaved yānaṃ bhavet prāṇārtha-rakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Marching is of two kinds: it may be for the protection of life and property,

children.text: ekam anyaj jigīṣoś ca yātrālakṣaṇam ucyate ||Panc_3.36||
children.translated_text: or it is called a campaign of one who desires conquest — that is the definition of a military expedition. ||Panc_3.36||

children.text: kārttike vātha caitre vā vijigīṣoḥ praśasyate |
children.translated_text: In <s>Kārttika</s> (October-November) or <s>Caitra</s> (March-April), marching is recommended for one who desires conquest —

children.text: yānam utkṛṣṭa-vīryasya śatru-deśe na cānyadā ||Panc_3.37||
children.translated_text: [marching] of one of superior valor, into enemy territory — and not at other times. ||Panc_3.37||

children.text: avaskanda-pradānasya sarve kālāḥ prakīrtitāḥ |
children.translated_text: All times are declared [suitable] for a sudden assault

children.text: vyasane vartamānasya śatrocchidrānvitasya ca ||Panc_3.38||
children.translated_text: upon an enemy who is in distress and beset by vulnerability. ||Panc_3.38||

children.text: svasthānaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā śūraiś cātair mahābalaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having made one's own position thoroughly secure with brave and mighty warriors,

children.text: para-deśaṃ tato gacchet praṇidhi-vyāptam agrataḥ ||Panc_3.39||
children.translated_text: one should then march into enemy territory, with spies spread out in advance. ||Panc_3.39||

children.text: ajñātavī-vadhāsāra-toya-śasyo vrajet tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who marches without knowing the forests, routes of execution, wastelands, water-sources, and crops —

children.text: para-rāṣṭraṃ na bhūyaḥ sa sva-rāṣṭram adhigacchati ||Panc_3.40||
children.translated_text: into another's kingdom — never again reaches his own kingdom. ||Panc_3.40||

children.text: tat te yuktaṃ kartum apasaraṇam | anyac ca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore it is fitting for you to retreat.' And moreover:

children.text: tan na yuktaṃ prabho kartuṃ dvitīyaṃ yānam eva ca |
children.translated_text: 'It is not fitting, Lord, to undertake the second — marching;

children.text: na vigraho na sandhānaṃ balinā tena pāpinā ||Panc_3.41||
children.translated_text: neither war nor peace-making with that powerful sinner [is appropriate]. ||Panc_3.41||

children.text: aparaṃ kāraṇāpekṣayāpasaraṇaṃ kriyate budhaiḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, the wise retreat with a view to [future] cause.' And it is said:

children.text: yad apasarati meṣaḥ kāraṇaṃ tat prahartuṃ
children.translated_text: The reason the ram retreats is in order to strike;

children.text: mṛga-patir api kopāt saṅkucaty utpatiṣṇuḥ |
children.translated_text: even the lord of beasts, out of fury, contracts before leaping;

children.text: hṛdaya-nihita-bhāvā gūḍha-mantra-pracārāḥ
children.translated_text: the intelligent, with designs hidden in [their] hearts and strategies concealed,

children.text: kim api vigaṇayanto buddhimantaḥ sahante ||Panc_3.42||
children.translated_text: disregarding something [for now], endure. ||Panc_3.42||

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover:

children.text: balavantaṃ ripuṃ dṛṣṭvā deśa-tyāgaṃ karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, seeing a powerful enemy, abandons his territory —
