children.text: yudhiṣṭhira ivāpnoti punar jīvan sa medinīm ||Panc_3.43||
children.translated_text: like <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, he obtains the earth again, living [to fight another day]. ||Panc_3.43||

children.text: yudhyate'haṅkṛtiṃ kṛtvā durbalo yo balīyasā |
children.translated_text: He who, having assumed pride, fights with one more powerful though himself weak —

children.text: sa tasya vāñchitaṃ kuryād ātmanaś ca kula-kṣayam ||Panc_3.44||
children.translated_text: he would fulfill the other's wish and bring about the destruction of his own family. // Panc_3.44 //

children.text: tad balavatābhiyuktsyāpasaraṇa-samayo 'yaṃ na sandher vigrahasya ca | evam anujīvi-mantro 'pasaraṇasya |
children.translated_text: Therefore, when attacked by a stronger [foe], this is the time for retreat — not for alliance or war.' Such was the counsel of the attendant regarding retreat.

children.text: atha tasya vacanam ākarṇya prajīvanam āha-bhadra ! tvam apy ātmano 'bhiprāyaṃ vada |
children.translated_text: Then, having heard his words, [the king] said to <s>Prajīvana</s>: 'Friend! You too state your opinion.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! mama sandhi-vigraha-yānāni trīṇy api na pratibhānti | viśeṣataś cāsanaṃ pratibhāti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Sire! To me, neither alliance, war, nor marching seem appropriate. Especially, staying firm (<s>āsana</s>) seems right. And it is said:'

children.text: nakraḥ sva-sthānam āsādya gajendram api karṣati |
children.translated_text: A crocodile, having reached its own place, drags even the lord of elephants;

children.text: sa eva pracyutaḥ sthānāc chunāpi paribhūyate ||Panc_3.45||
children.translated_text: that same [crocodile], dislodged from its place, is overpowered even by a dog. // Panc_3.45 //

children.text: tathā-
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: abhiyukto balavatā tiṣṭhan durge prayatnavān |
children.translated_text: When attacked by a stronger [foe], one should remain in a fortress with effort,

children.text: tatrasthaḥ suhṛdāhvānaṃ kurvītātma-vimuktaye ||Panc_3.46||
children.translated_text: and while stationed there, summon allies for one's own deliverance. // Panc_3.46 //

children.text: yo ripor āgamaṃ śrutvā bhaya-santrasta-mānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, upon hearing of the enemy's advance, with mind stricken by fear,

children.text: sva-sthānaṃ hi tyajet tatra na tu bhūyo viśec ca saḥ ||Panc_3.47||
children.translated_text: abandons his own position — he shall never enter it again. // Panc_3.47 //

children.text: daṃṣṭrā-virahitaḥ sarpo mada-hīno yathā gajaḥ |
children.translated_text: A snake without fangs, like an elephant without rut —

children.text: sthāna-hīnas tathā rājā gamyaḥ syāt sarva-jantuṣu ||Panc_3.48||
children.translated_text: so too a king without his position becomes accessible to all creatures. // Panc_3.48 //

children.text: nija-sthāna-sthito 'py ekaḥ śataṃ yoddhuṃ sahen naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A man stationed in his own place, even alone, can withstand a hundred [foes] in battle;

children.text: śaktānām api śatrūṇāṃ tasmāt sthānaṃ na santyajet ||Panc_3.49||
children.translated_text: therefore, even against powerful enemies, one should not abandon one's position. // Panc_3.49 //

children.text: tasmād durgaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā subhaṭāsāra-saṃyutam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having fortified the fortress, equipped with excellent warriors,

children.text: prākāra-parikhā-yuktaṃ śastrādibhir alaṅkṛtam ||Panc_3.50||
children.translated_text: furnished with ramparts and moats, adorned with weapons and the like,

children.text:
tiṣṭhen madhya-gato nityaṃ yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ |
jīvan samprāptsyati rājyaṃ mṛto vā svargam eṣyati ||Panc_3.51|| (yugmakam)
children.translated_text: one should remain stationed in the center, ever resolved for battle; living, he will obtain the kingdom — or dying, he shall go to heaven. // Panc_3.50-51 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: balināpi na bādhyante laghavo 'py eka-saṃśrayāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even small [creatures], when united in one refuge, are not harassed by the powerful —

children.text: vipakṣeṇāpi marutā yathaika-sthāna-vīrudhāḥ ||Panc_3.52||
children.translated_text: like plants rooted in one place [cannot be uprooted] even by the hostile wind. // Panc_3.52 //

children.text: mahān apy ekajo vṛkṣaḥ balavān supratiṣṭhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a great tree standing alone, though strong and well-rooted,

children.text: prasahya iva vātena śakyo dharṣayituṃ yataḥ ||Panc_3.53||
children.translated_text: can be forcibly assailed by the wind. // Panc_3.53 //

children.text: atha ye saṃhatā vṛkṣā sarvataḥ supratiṣṭhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: But those trees that stand united, well-rooted on all sides —

children.text: te na raudrānilenāpi hanyante hy eka-saṃśrayāt ||Panc_3.54||
children.translated_text: they are not destroyed even by a fierce wind, because of their united position. // Panc_3.54 //

children.text: evaṃ manuṣyam apy ekaṃ śauryeṇāpi samanvitam |
children.translated_text: Likewise, even a single man, though endowed with valor,

children.text: śakyaṃ dviṣanto manyante hiṃsanti ca tataḥ param ||Panc_3.55||
children.translated_text: is considered vulnerable by enemies, and they harm him thereafter. // Panc_3.55 //

children.text: evaṃ prajīva-mantraḥ | idam āsana-saṃjñakam |
children.translated_text: Such was the counsel of <s>Prajīvana</s>. This is what is called 'staying firm' (<s>āsana</s>).

children.text: etat samākarṇya cirañjīvinaṃ prāha-bhadra ! tvam api svābhiprāyaṃ vada |
children.translated_text: Having heard all this, [the king] said to <s>Cirañjīvī</s>: 'Friend! You too state your opinion.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! ṣāḍguṇya-madhye mama saṃśrayaḥ samyak pratibhāti | tat tasyānuṣṭhānaṃ kāryam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Sire! Among the six expedients, taking refuge (<s>saṃśraya</s>) seems most fitting to me. That should be implemented. And it is said:'

children.text: asahāyaḥ samartho 'pi tejasvī kiṃ kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: What can even a capable and spirited man do without allies?

children.text: nirvāte jvalito vahniḥ svayam eva praśāmyati ||Panc_3.56||
children.translated_text: A fire kindled in a windless place dies out by itself. // Panc_3.56 //

children.text: saṅgatiḥ śreyasī puṃsāṃ sva-pakṣe ca viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Alliance is most beneficial for men, especially in one's own faction;

children.text: tuṣair api paribhraṣṭā na prarohanti taṇḍulāḥ ||Panc_3.57||
children.translated_text: rice grains, once separated from the husk, do not sprout again. // Panc_3.57 //

children.text: tad atraiva sthitena tvayā kaścit samarthaḥ samāśrayaṇīyaḥ, yo vipat-pratikāraṃ karoti | yadi punas tvaṃ sva-sthānaṃ tyaktvānyatra yāsyasi | tat ko 'pi te vāṅ-mātreṇāpi sahāyatvaṃ na kariṣyati | uktaṃ ca, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, while remaining right here, you should take refuge with some capable [ally] who can counter the calamity. But if you abandon your own place and go elsewhere, then no one will render you even verbal assistance. And it is said, for:'

children.text: vanāni dahato vahneḥ sakhī bhavati mārutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wind is a friend to fire when it is burning forests;

children.text: sa eva dīpa-nāśāya kṛśe kasyāsti sauhṛdam ||Panc_3.58||
children.translated_text: that same [wind] destroys a lamp — who is a friend to the weak? // Panc_3.58 //

children.text: athavā naitad ekāntaṃ yad balinam ekaṃ samāśrayet | laghūnām api saṃśrayo rakṣāyai eva bhavati | uktaṃ ca, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Or rather, it is not absolutely [necessary] that one take refuge with a single powerful [ally]. Taking refuge even with the small serves for protection. And it is said, for:'

children.text: saṅghātavān yathā veṇur niviḍair veṇubhir vṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as a bamboo, united [with others], surrounded by dense bamboos,

children.text: na śakyeta samucchettuṃ durbalo 'pi yathā nṛpaḥ ||Panc_3.59||
children.translated_text: cannot be uprooted — so too a weak king [when supported]. // Panc_3.59 //

children.text: yadi punar uttama-saṃśrayo bhavati tat kim ucyate ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'But if there is refuge with a superior [ally], then what need be said? And it is said:'

children.text: mahājanasya samparkaḥ kasya nonnati-kārakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Contact with a great person — for whom does it not cause elevation?

children.text: padma-patra-sthitaṃ toyaṃ dhatte muktā-phala-śriyam ||Panc_3.60||
children.translated_text: A drop of water resting on a lotus petal assumes the splendor of a pearl. // Panc_3.60 //

children.text: tad evaṃ saṃśrayaṃ vinā na kaścit pratīkāro bhavati iti me'bhiprāyaḥ | evaṃ cirañjīvi-mantraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, without taking refuge, there is no remedy — that is my opinion.' Such was the counsel of <s>Cirañjīvī</s>.

children.text: athaivam abhihite sa meghavarṇo rājā cirantanaṃ pitṛ-sacivaṃ dīrghāyuṣaṃ sakala-nīti-śāstra-pāraṅgataṃ sthirajīvi-nāmānaṃ praṇamya provāca-tāta ! yad ete mayā pṛṣṭāḥ sacivās tāvad atra-sthitasyāpi tava tat-parīkṣārtham, yena tvaṃ sakalaṃ śrutvā yad ucitaṃ tan me samādiśasi | tad yady uktaṃ bhavati tas samādeśyam |
children.translated_text: When this had been said, King <s>Meghavarṇa</s>, bowing to his long-standing paternal minister named <s>Sthirajīvī</s> — long-lived and thoroughly versed in the entire science of polity — said: 'Father! The reason I questioned these ministers in your presence was to test them, so that you, having heard everything, may direct me to what is proper. If [anything else] should be said, please direct me.'

children.text: sa āha-vatsa ! sarvair apy etair nīti-śāstrāśrayam uktaṃ sacivaiḥ | tad upayujyate sva-kālocitaṃ sarvam eva | param eṣa dvaidhībhāvasya kālaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Child! All these ministers have spoken based on the science of polity. All of it is applicable, each at its proper time. But this is the time for the policy of double-dealing (<s>dvaidhībhāva</s>). And it is said:'

children.text: aviśvāsaṃ sadā tiṣṭhet sandhinā vigraheṇa ca |
children.translated_text: One should always maintain distrust through both alliance and war,

children.text: dvaidhī-bhāvaṃ samāśritya pāpe śatrau balīyasi ||Panc_3.61||
children.translated_text: taking recourse to double-dealing, when the enemy is wicked and powerful. // Panc_3.61 //

children.text: tac chatruṃ viśvāsyāviśvastair lobhaṃ darśayadbhiḥ sukhenocchidyate ripuḥ | uktaṃ ca-
ucchedyam api vidvāṃso vardhayanty arim ekadā |
children.translated_text: The wise sometimes nourish even an enemy who is to be destroyed —

children.text: guḍena vardhitaḥ śleṣmā yato niḥśeṣatāṃ vrajet ||Panc_3.62||
children.translated_text: for phlegm, augmented by molasses, is [then more easily] completely expelled. // Panc_3.62 //
'So, by gaining the enemy's trust through agents who pretend to be disaffected and show greed, the enemy is easily destroyed. And it is said:'

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: strīṇāṃ śatroḥ kumitrasya paṇya-strīṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Toward women, enemies, false friends, and courtesans especially —

children.text: yo bhaved eka-bhāvo 'tra na sa jīvati mānavaḥ ||Panc_3.63||
children.translated_text: he who shows single-minded [trust] does not survive in this world. // Panc_3.63 //

children.text: kṛtyaṃ deva-dvijātīnām ātmanaś ca guros tathā |
children.translated_text: The duties toward gods, Brahmins, oneself, and one's teacher —

children.text: eka-bhāvena kartavyaṃ śeṣaṃ dvaidha-samāśritam ||Panc_3.64||
children.translated_text: these should be performed with single-mindedness; in all else, one should resort to double-dealing. // Panc_3.64 //

children.text: eko bhāvaḥ sadā śasto yatīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām |
children.translated_text: Single-mindedness is always praised for ascetics with purified souls,

children.text: śrī-lubdhānāṃ na lokānāṃ viśeṣeṇa mahī-bhujām ||Panc_3.65||
children.translated_text: not for worldly people greedy for fortune — especially not for kings. // Panc_3.65 //

children.text: tad dvaidhībhāvaṃ saṃśritasya tava sva-sthāne vāso bhaviṣyati, lobhāśrayāc ca śatrum uccāṭayiṣyasi aparaṃ-yadi kiñcic chidraṃ tasya paśyasi, tad gatvā vyāpādayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having adopted double-dealing, you will remain in your own place, and through [agents showing] greed you will dislodge the enemy. Moreover — if you perceive any weakness in him, then go and destroy him.'

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-tāta mayā so 'vidita saṃśrayaḥ | tat kathaṃ tasya chidraṃ jñāsyāmi ?
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Father! His refuge is unknown to me. How then shall I discover his weakness?'

children.text: sthirajīvy āha-vatsa ! na kevalaṃ sthānaṃ, chidrāṇy api tasya prakaṭīkariṣyāmi praṇadhibhiḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Sthirajīvī</s> said: 'Child! Not only the place, but his weaknesses too I shall reveal through spies. And it is said:'

children.text: gāvo gandhena paśyanti vedaiḥ paśyanti vai dvijāḥ |
children.translated_text: Cows see by smell, Brahmins see through the <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: cārai paśyanti rājānaś cakṣurbhyām itare janāḥ ||Panc_3.66||
children.translated_text: kings see through spies, and other people through their eyes. // Panc_3.66 //

children.text: uktaṃ cātra viṣaye-
children.translated_text: And it is said regarding this matter:

children.text: yas tīrthāni nije pakṣe para-pakṣe viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: A king who knows the weak points in his own faction and especially in the enemy's faction

children.text: guptaiś cārair nṛpo vetti na sa durgatim āpnuyāt ||Panc_3.67||
children.translated_text: through secret spies — he does not come to ruin. // Panc_3.67 //

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-tāta, kāni tīrthāny ucyante ? kati saṅkhyāni ca ? kīdṛśā guptacarāḥ ? tat sarvaṃ nivedyatām iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Father, what are these weak points called? How many are they? And what are secret spies like? Let all this be explained.'

children.text: sa āha-atra viṣaye bhagavatā nāradena yudhiṣṭhiraḥ proktaḥ | yac chatru-pakṣe'ṣṭādaśa-tīrthāni, sva-pakṣe pañcadaśa | tribhis tribhir guptacarais tāni jñeyāni | tair jñātaiḥ sva-pakṣaḥ para-pakṣaś ca vaśyo bhavati | uktaṃ ca nāradena yudhiṣṭhiraṃ prati-
kaccid aṣṭadaśāny eṣu sva-pakṣe daśa pañca ca |
children.translated_text: Do you know the eighteen [weak points] in the enemy — and the fifteen in your own —

children.text: tribhis tribhir avijñātair vetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ ||Panc_3.68||
children.translated_text: through three spies each, undetected? // Panc_3.68 //

He said: 'On this subject, the blessed <s>Nārada</s> instructed <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>: there are eighteen weak points in the enemy's faction, and fifteen in one's own. Each should be known through three secret spies each. Once known, both one's own faction and the enemy's become controllable. And <s>Nārada</s> said to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:'

children.text: tīrtha-śabdenāyukta-karmābhidhīyate | tad yadi teṣāṃ kutsitaṃ bhavati tat svāmino 'bhighātāya, yadi pradhānaṃ bhavati tad-vṛddhaye syād iti | tad yathā-mantrī, purohitaḥ, senāpatiḥ, yuvarājaḥ, dauvārikaḥ, antarvāsikaḥ, praśāsakaḥ, samāhartṛ-sannidhātṛ-pradeṣṭṛ-jñāpakāḥ, sādhanādhyakṣaḥ, gajādhyakṣaḥ, kośādhyakṣaḥ, durgapāla-karapāla-sīmāpāla-protkaṭa-bhṛtyāḥ | eṣāṃ bhedena drāg ripuḥ sādhyate | sva-pakṣe ca devī, jananī, kañcukī, mālikaḥ, śayyā-pālakaḥ, spaśādhyakṣaḥ, sāṃvatsarikaḥ, bhiṣag, tāmbūla-vāhakaḥ, ācāryaḥ, aṅga-rakṣakaḥ, sthāna-cintakaḥ, chatradharaḥ, vilāsinī | eṣāṃ vaira-dvāreṇa sva-pakṣe vighātaḥ | tathā ca-
vaidya-sāṃvatsarācāryāḥ sva-pakṣe'dhikṛtāś carāḥ |
children.translated_text: The physician, the astrologer, and the teacher — these are the appointed spies in one's own faction;

children.text: tathāhi-tuṇḍikonmattāḥ sarvaṃ jānanti śatruṣu ||Panc_3.69||
children.translated_text: likewise <s>Tuṇḍika</s>-agents and madmen — they know everything about the enemy. // Panc_3.69 //

By the word 'weak point' (<s>tīrtha</s>) is meant an official. If their [conduct] is base, it leads to the destruction of the master; if excellent, to his prosperity. They are as follows: the minister, the family priest, the general, the crown prince, the chamberlain, the inner-chamber attendant, the administrator, the collector-treasurer-inspector-informants, the superintendent of resources, the superintendent of elephants, the superintendent of the treasury, the fortress-warden, the revenue-warden, the border-warden, and the frontier-chieftain servants. Through their division, the enemy is quickly subdued. And in one's own faction: the queen, the mother, the chamberlain, the garland-maker, the bed-guardian, the superintendent of spies, the court-astrologer, the physician, the betel-bearer, the teacher, the bodyguard, the strategist, the parasol-bearer, and the courtesan. Through enmity among these, harm [can come] to one's own faction. And thus:

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: kṛtvā kṛtya-vidas tīrtheṣv antaḥ praṇidhayaḥ padam |
children.translated_text: Having placed secret agents as spies among the [enemy's] weak points, those skilled in statecraft

children.text: vidāṅkurvantu mahatas talaṃ vidviṣad-ambhasaḥ ||Panc_3.70||
children.translated_text: should dry up the deep waters of the enemy's [strength] from the bottom. // Panc_3.70 //

children.text: evaṃ mantri-vākyam ākarṇyātrāntare meghavarṇa āha-tāta ! atha kiṃ nimittam evaṃvidhaṃ prāṇāntikaṃ sadaiva vāyasolūkānāṃ vairam ?
children.translated_text: Having heard the minister's words, <s>Meghavarṇa</s> then said: 'Father! Now, what is the cause of this deadly enmity between crows and owls?'

children.text: sa āha-vatsa ! kadācid dhaṃsa-śuka-kokila-cātaka-ulūka-mayūra-kapāta-pārāvata-viṣkira-prabhṛtayaḥ sarve'pi pakṣiṇaḥ sametya sodvegaṃ mantrayitum ārabdhāḥ | aho asmākaṃ tāvad vainateyo rājā, sa ca vāsudeva-bhakto na kām api cintām asmākaṃ karoti | tat kiṃ tena vṛthāsvāminā ? yo lubdhaka-pāśair nityaṃ nibadhyamānānāṃ na rakṣāṃ vidhatte | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Child! Once upon a time, swans, parrots, cuckoos, <s>cātaka</s> birds, owls, peacocks, doves, pigeons, quails, and all other birds assembled and began to deliberate anxiously: "Ah! Our king is <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa), but he is devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s> (Viṣṇu) and pays no heed to us. So what use is such a master who is merely nominal? — one who never provides protection when we are constantly being bound in the snares of hunters." And it is said:'

children.text: yo na rakṣati vitrastān pīḍyamānān paraiḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: He who does not protect creatures that are terrified and constantly tormented by others —

children.text: jantūn pārthiva-rūpeṇa sa kṛtānto na saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_3.71||
children.translated_text: he, in the form of a king, is [actually] Death itself — there is no doubt. // Panc_3.71 //

children.text: yadi na syān narapatiḥ samyaṅ netāḥ tataḥ prajāḥ |
children.translated_text: If the king is not a proper leader, then his subjects

children.text: akarṇadhārā jaladhau viplaveteha naur iva ||Panc_3.72||
children.translated_text: flounder like a ship without a helmsman on the sea. // Panc_3.72 //

children.text: ṣaḍ imān puruṣo jahyād bhinnāṃ nāvam ivārṇave |
children.translated_text: These six a man should abandon, like a broken ship in the ocean:

children.text: apravaktāram ācāryam anadhīyānam ṛtvijam ||Panc_3.73||
children.translated_text: a teacher who does not expound, a priest who does not study, // Panc_3.73 //

children.text:
arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ bhāryāṃ cāpirya-vādinīm |
grāma-kāmaṃ ca gopālaṃ vana-kāmaṃ ca nāpitam ||Panc_3.74|| (yugmam)
children.translated_text: a king who does not protect, a wife who speaks harshly, a cowherd who desires the village, and a barber who desires the forest. // Panc_3.74 //

children.text: tat, sañcityānyaḥ kaścid rājā vihaṅgamānāṃ kriyatām iti | atha tair bhadrākāram ulūkam avalokya sarvair abhihitam-yad eṣa ulūko rājāsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati, tad ānīyantāṃ nṛpābhiṣeka-sambandhinaḥ sambhārāḥ iti |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let us deliberate and appoint some other king of the birds.' Then, seeing an owl of auspicious appearance, all of them said: 'Let this owl become our king. Let the materials for the royal consecration be brought.'

children.text: atha sādhite vividha-tīrthodake, praguṇīkṛte'ṣṭottara-śata-mūlikā-saṅghāte pradatte siṃhāsane, vartite saptadvīpa-samudra-bhūdhara-vicitre dharitrī-maṇḍale, prastārite vyāghra-carmaṇi āpūriteṣu hema-kumbheṣu dīpeṣu vādyeṣu ca sajjīkṛteṣu darpaṇādiṣu māṅgalya-vastuṣu, paṭhatsu vandi-mukhyeṣu, vedoccāraṇa-pareṣu samudita-mukheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu, gīta-pare yuvati-jane, ānītāyām agra-mahiṣyāṃ kṛkālikāyām, ulūko 'bhiṣekārthaṃ yāvat siṃhāsane upaviśati tāvat kuto 'pi vāyasaḥ samāyātaḥ so 'cintayat-aho ! kim eṣa sakala-pakṣi-samāgamo mahotsavaś ca ? atha te pakṣiṇas taṃ dṛṣṭvā mithaḥ procuḥ | pakṣiṇāṃ madhye vāyasaś caturaḥ śrūyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Now, when the water from various sacred fords had been prepared, when the collection of one hundred and eight roots had been assembled, when the throne had been set in place, when the representation of the earth with its seven continents, oceans, and mountains had been drawn, when the tiger-skin had been spread, when the golden pitchers had been filled, when lamps, musical instruments, mirrors, and other auspicious objects had been made ready, when the chief bards were reciting, when the Brahmins had begun chanting the <s>Vedas</s> with upturned faces, when the young women were engaged in singing, when the chief queen — a female owl — had been brought forward, and the owl was about to sit upon the throne for the consecration — just then a crow arrived from somewhere. He thought: 'Ah! What is this great assembly of all birds and this grand celebration?' Then those birds, seeing him, said among themselves: 'Among birds, the crow is known to be clever. And it is said:'

children.text: narāṇāṃ nāpito dhūrtaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ caiva vāyasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Among men, the barber is crafty; among birds, the crow;

children.text: daṃṣṭriṇāṃ ca śṛgālas tu śvebhikṣus tapasvinām ||Panc_3.75||
children.translated_text: among the fanged, the jackal; and among ascetics, the mendicant-friar. // Panc_3.75 //

children.text: tad asyāpi vacanaṃ grāhyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore his opinion too should be heeded. And it is said:'

children.text: bahudhā bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ cintitāḥ sunirūpitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Policies deliberated in many ways by many [counselors], well-examined —

children.text: kathañcin na vilīyante vidvadbhiś cintitā nayāḥ ||Panc_3.76||
children.translated_text: somehow never dissolve [when] pondered by the learned. // Panc_3.76 //

children.text: atha vāyasaḥ sametya tān āha-aho ! kiṃ mahājana-samāgamo 'yaṃ parama-mahotsavaś ca |
children.translated_text: Then the crow, having approached them, said: 'Ah! What is this great assembly and supreme celebration?'

children.text: te procuḥ-bhoḥ ! nāsti kaścid vihaṅgamānāṃ rājā, tad asyolūkasya vihaṅga-rājyābhiṣeko nirūpitas tiṣṭhati samasta-pakṣibhiḥ | tattvam api sva-mataṃ dehi | prastāve samāgato 'si |
children.translated_text: They said: 'Sir! There is no king of birds. Therefore the coronation of this owl as king of birds has been determined by all the birds. You too should give your opinion. You have arrived at the right moment.'

children.text: athāsau kāko vihasyāha-aho ! na yuktam etat | yan mayūra-haṃsa-kokila-cakravāka-śuka-kāraṇḍava-hārīta-sārasādiṣu pakṣi-pradhāneṣu vidyamāneṣu divāndhasyāsya karāla-vaktrasyābhiṣekaḥ kriyate | tatraitan mama matam | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then that crow laughed and said: 'Ah! This is not proper — that while such eminent birds as the peacock, swan, cuckoo, <s>cakravāka</s>, parrot, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> (a kind of duck), <s>hārīta</s> (pigeon), and <s>sārasa</s> (crane) exist, this day-blind one with a hideous face should be anointed king! Here is my opinion on this matter —'

children.text: vakra-nāsaṃ sujihmākṣaṃ krūram apriya-darśanam |
children.translated_text: With a crooked nose, exceedingly squinting eyes, cruel, unpleasant to behold —

children.text: akruddhasyedṛśaṃ vaktraṃ bhavet kruddhasya kīdṛśam ||Panc_3.77||
children.translated_text: if such is his face when not angry, what would it be when angry? [Panc 3.77]

children.text: svabhāva-raudram atyugraṃ krūram apriya-vādinam |
children.translated_text: Fierce by nature, exceedingly terrible, cruel, and harsh in speech —

children.text: ulūkaṃ nṛpatiṃ kṛtvā kā naḥ siddhir bhaviṣyati ||Panc_3.78||
children.translated_text: having made an owl our king, what success will come to us? [Panc 3.78]

children.text: aparaṃ vainateye svāmini sthite kim eṣa divāndhaḥ kriyate rājā ? tad yadyapi guṇavān bhavati, tathāpy ekasmin svāmini sthite nānyo bhūpaḥ praśasyate |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, while <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>, son of <s>Vinatā</s>) stands as our lord, why should this day-blind creature be made king? Even if he be virtuous, when one master already exists, no other ruler is to be praised.'

children.text: eka eva hitārthāya tejasvī pārthivo bhuvaḥ |
children.translated_text: One sovereign alone is for the welfare of the earth, [like] the radiant one;

children.text: yugānta iva bhāsvanto bahavo 'tra vipattaye ||Panc_3.79||
children.translated_text: many [suns] at the end of a <s>yuga</s> (cosmic age) bring destruction. [Panc 3.79]

children.text: tat tasya nāmnāpi yūyaṃ pareṣām agamyā bhaviṣyatha | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'By his name alone you will become unapproachable to enemies.' And it is said —

children.text: gurūṇāṃ nāma-mātre'pi gṛhīte svāmi-sambhave |
children.translated_text: When even merely the name of the great, born as one's lord, is invoked,

children.text: duṣṭānāṃ purataḥ kṣemaṃ tat-kṣaṇād eva jāyate ||Panc_3.80||
children.translated_text: safety from the wicked arises at that very moment. [Panc 3.80]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: vyapadeśena mahatāṃ siddiḥ sañjāyate parā |
children.translated_text: By invoking the name of the great, supreme success arises;

children.text: śaśino vyapadeśena vasanti śaśakāḥ sukham ||Panc_3.81||
children.translated_text: by invoking the moon's name, the hares dwell in happiness. [Panc 3.81]

children.text: pakṣiṇa ūcuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The birds said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 1
caturdanta-nāma-mahā-gaja-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 1
The Story of the Great Elephant Named <s>Caturdanta</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścid vane caturdanto nāma mahā-gajo yūthādhipaḥ prativasati sma | tatra kadācin mahaty anāvṛṣṭiḥ sañjātā prabhūta-varṣāṇi yāvat | tayā taḍāga-hrada-palvala-sarāṃsi śoṣam upagatāni | atha taiḥ samasta-gajaiḥ sa gajarājaḥ proktaḥ-deva ! pipāsākulā gaja-kalabhā mṛta-prāyā apare mṛtāś ca | tad anviṣyatāṃ kaścij jalāśayo yatra jala-pānena svasthatāṃ vrajanti |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest there lived a great elephant named <s>Caturdanta</s> (Four-tusked), the lord of the herd. Once, a great drought occurred there lasting many years. By it, the tanks, lakes, pools, and ponds were dried up. Then all the elephants said to their elephant-king: 'Lord! The young elephants, tormented by thirst, are nearly dead, and others have died. So let some body of water be found where, by drinking, they may regain their health.'

children.text: tataś ciraṃ dhyātvā tenābhihitam-asti mahā-hrado vivikte pradeśe sthala-madhya-gataḥ pātāla-gaṅgā-jalena sadaiva pūrṇaḥ | tat tatra gamyatāṃ iti |
children.translated_text: Then, after long reflection, he said: 'There is a great lake in a secluded region, situated in the middle of dry land, always filled with water from the subterranean <s>Gaṅgā</s>. So let us go there.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭḥite pañcarātram upasarpadbhiḥ samāsāditas taiḥ sa hradaḥ | tatra svecchayā jalam avagāhyās tam anavelāyāṃ niṣkrāntāḥ | tasya ca hradasya samantāc chaśaka-bilāni asaṅkhyāni sukomala-bhūmau tiṣṭhanti | tāny api samastair api tair gajair itas tato bhramadbhiḥ paribhagnāni | bahavaḥ śaśakāḥ bhagna-pāda-śiro-grīvā vihitāḥ | kecin mṛtāḥ kecij jīva-śeṣā jātāḥ |
children.translated_text: When this was done, they reached that lake after five days of travel. There, having bathed in the water at will, they emerged at an untimely hour. Around that lake were innumerable hare-burrows in very soft ground. All those burrows were trampled by all those elephants as they wandered here and there. Many hares were left with broken legs, heads, and necks. Some died; some barely survived.

children.text: atha gate tasmin gaja-yūthe śaśakāḥ sodvegā gajapāda-kṣuṇṇa-samāvāsāḥ kecid bhagna-pādāḥ | anye jarjarita-kalevarā rudhira-plutāḥ | anye hata-śiśavo bāṣpa-pihita-locanāḥ sametya mitho mantraṃ cakruḥ-aho vinaṣṭā vayam | nityam evaitad gaja-yūtham āgamiṣyati yato nānyatra jalam asti | tat sarveṣāṃ nāśo bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, after that elephant herd departed, the hares — alarmed, their dwellings crushed by elephant-feet, some with broken legs, others with battered bodies drenched in blood, others whose young had been killed with tear-filled eyes — gathered together and took counsel among themselves: 'Alas, we are destroyed! This elephant herd will come every day since there is no water elsewhere. So all of us will perish.' And it is said —

children.text: spṛśann api gajo hanti jighrann api bhujaṅgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: An elephant kills merely by touching, a serpent kills merely by smelling;

children.text: hasann api nṛpo hanti mānayann api durjanaḥ ||Panc_3.82||
children.translated_text: a king kills even while laughing, and a wicked man even while honoring. [Panc 3.82]

children.text: tac cintyatāṃ kaścid upāyaḥ | tatraikaḥ provāca-gamyatāṃ deśa-tyāgena | kim anyat ? uktaṃ ca manunā vyāsena ca-
children.translated_text: 'So let some stratagem be devised.' One of them said: 'Let us leave this place. What else?' And it is said by <s>Manu</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s> —

children.text: tyajed ekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet |
children.translated_text: One should abandon an individual for the sake of a family; abandon a family for the sake of a village;

children.text: grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet ||Panc_3.83||
children.translated_text: abandon a village for the sake of a country; and abandon the earth for the sake of the self. [Panc 3.83]

children.text: kṣemyāṃ śasya-pradāṃ nityaṃ paśu-vṛddhi-karīm api |
children.translated_text: Even a land that is prosperous, grain-yielding, and ever-increasing cattle —

children.text: parityajen nṛpo bhūmim ātmārtham avicārayan ||Panc_3.84||
children.translated_text: a king should abandon without hesitation for his own sake. [Panc 3.84]

children.text: āpad-arthe dhanaṃ rakṣed dārān rakṣed dhanair api |
children.translated_text: One should protect wealth for times of adversity; protect one's wife even with wealth;

children.text: ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣed dārair api dhanair api ||Panc_3.85||
children.translated_text: and protect oneself always — with wives and with wealth. [Panc 3.85]

children.text: tataś cānye procuḥ-bhoḥ ! pitṛ-paitāmahaṃ sthānaṃ na śakyate sahasā tyaktum | tat kriyatāṃ teṣāṃ kṛte kācid vibhīṣikā | yat katham api daivān na samāyānti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then others said: 'Friends! An ancestral dwelling-place cannot be abandoned suddenly. So let some frightening device be created for them, so that by some fortune they may not come.' And it is said —

children.text: nirviṣeṇāpi sarpeṇa kartavyā mahatī phaṭā |
children.translated_text: Even a non-venomous serpent should spread its hood wide;

children.text: viṣaṃ bhavatu mā vāstu phaṭāṭopo bhayaṅkaraḥ ||Panc_3.86||
children.translated_text: whether there is venom or not, the display of the hood is terrifying. [Panc 3.86]

children.text: athānye procuḥ-yady evaṃ tatas teṣāṃ mahad-vibhīṣikā-sthānam asti yena nāgamiṣyanti | sā ca catura-dūtāyattā vibhīṣikā | yato vijayadatto nāmāsmat-svāmī śaśakaś candra-maṇḍale nivasati | tat preṣyatāṃ kaścin mithyā-dūto yūthādhipa-sakāśaṃ yac candras tvām atra hrada āgacchantaṃ niṣedhayati, yato 'smat-parigraho 'sya samantād vasati | evam abhihite śraddheya-vacanāt kadāpi nivartate | athānye procuḥ-yady evaṃ tad asti lambakarṇo nāma śaśakaḥ | sa ca vacana-racanā-caturo dūta-karmajñaḥ | sa tatra preṣyatām iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then others said: 'If so, then there exists a great source of intimidation for them, by which they will not come. And that intimidation depends on a clever messenger. Because our lord, a hare named <s>Vijayadata</s>, dwells in the orb of the moon. So let some false messenger be sent to the herd-leader [saying] that the Moon forbids you from coming to this lake, since his subjects dwell all around it. If spoken thus, by one whose words are credible, he may turn back.' Then others said: 'If so, there is a hare named <s>Lambakarṇa</s> (Long-ears). He is skilled in crafting speeches and knows the duty of a messenger. Let him be sent there.' And it is said —

children.text: sākāro niḥspṛho vāgmī nānā-śāstra-vicakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Dignified in bearing, free from greed, eloquent, versed in various scriptures,

children.text: para-cittāvagantā ca rājño dūtaḥ sa iṣyate ||Panc_3.87||
children.translated_text: and able to read another's mind — such is considered the king's messenger. [Panc 3.87]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yo mūrkhaṃ laulya-sampannaṃ rāja-dvārikam ācaret |
children.translated_text: He who employs a fool, restless by nature, a mere doorkeeper of the king,

children.text: mithyā-vādaṃ viśeṣeṇa tasya kāryaṃ na sidhyati ||Panc_3.88||
children.translated_text: and especially a liar — his purpose is not accomplished. [Panc 3.88]

children.text: tad anviṣyatāṃ yady asmād vyasanād ātmanāṃ sunirmuktiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'So let it be determined whether there is a good means of our deliverance from this calamity.'

children.text: athānye procuḥ-aho yuktam etat | nānyaḥ kaścid upāyo 'smākaṃ jīvitasya | tathaiva kriyatām |
children.translated_text: Then others said: 'Ah, this is proper. There is no other means for our survival. Let it be done just so.'

children.text: atha lambakarṇo gaja-yūthādhipa-samīpe nirūpito gataś ca | tathānuṣṭhite lambakarṇo 'pi gaja-mārgam āsādyāgamyaṃ sthalam āruhya taṃ gajam uvāca-bhoḥ bhoḥ duṣṭa-gaja ! kim evaṃ līlayā niḥśaṅkayātra candra-hrada āgacchasi ? tan nāgantavyaṃ nivartyatām iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lambakarṇa</s> was designated and went near the elephant herd-leader. When this was done, <s>Lambakarṇa</s> reached the elephant's path, climbed an inaccessible height, and said to the elephant: 'Ho there, wicked elephant! Why do you come thus playfully and fearlessly to this Moon-lake? You must not come! Turn back!'

children.text: tad ākarṇya vismita-manā gaja āha-bhoḥ ! kas tvam ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the elephant, his mind astonished, said: 'Who are you?'

children.text: sa āha-ahaṃ lambakarṇo nāma śaśakaś candra-maṇḍale vasāmi | sāmprataṃ bhagavatā candramasā tava pārśve prahito dūtaḥ | jānāty eva bhavān | yathārtha-vādino dūtasya na doṣaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | dūta-mukhā hi rājānaḥ sarva eva | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'I am a hare named <s>Lambakarṇa</s>, dwelling in the orb of the moon. At present, the blessed Moon has sent me as a messenger to you. Know this: no fault should be imputed to a messenger who speaks truthfully. For all kings speak through the mouths of messengers.' And it is said —

children.text: udyateṣv api śastreṣu bandhu-varga-vadheṣv api |
children.translated_text: Even when weapons are raised, even when the slaughter of kinsmen [occurs],

children.text: puruṣāṇy api jalpanto vadhyā dūtā na bhūbhujā ||Panc_3.89||
children.translated_text: messengers who speak their messages should not be killed by kings. [Panc 3.89]

children.text: tac chrutvā sa āha-bhoḥ śaśaka ! tat kathaya bhagavataś candramasaḥ sandeśam | yena satvaraṃ kriyate |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, he said: 'O hare! Then tell me the message of the blessed Moon, so that I may act upon it promptly.'

children.text: sa āha-bhavatātīta-divase yūthena sahāgacchatā prabhūtāḥ śaśakā nipātitāḥ | tat kiṃ na vetti bhavān | yan mama parigraho 'yam | tad yadi jīvitena te prayojanaṃ tadā kenāpi prayojanenāpy atra hrade nāgantavyam iti sandeśaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'When you came the other day with your herd, you trampled many hares. Do you not know that these are my subjects? So if you have any need for life, then for no reason whatsoever should you come to this lake — that is the message.'

children.text: gaja āha-atha kva vartate bhagavān svāmī candraḥ |
children.translated_text: The elephant said: 'Then where is the blessed lord, the Moon?'

children.text: sa āha-atra hrade sāmprataṃ śaśakānāṃ bhavad-yūtha-mathitānāṃ hata-śeṣāṇāṃ samāśvāsanāya samāyātas tiṣṭhati | ahaṃ punas tavāntikaṃ preṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'He is right here in this lake at present, having come to console the surviving hares who were crushed by your herd. And I have been sent to you.'

children.text: gaja āha-yady evaṃ tad darśaya me taṃ svāminaṃ yena praṇamyānyatra gacchāmi |
children.translated_text: The elephant said: 'If so, then show me that lord, so that I may bow and depart elsewhere.'

children.text: śaśaka āha-āgaccha mayā sahaikakī yena darśayāmi |
children.translated_text: The hare said: 'Come alone with me, and I shall show him.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite śaśako niśā-samaye taṃ hrada-tīre nītvā jala-madhye sthitaṃ candra-bimbam adarśayat | āha ca-bhoḥ eṣa naḥ svāmī jala-madhye samādhisthas tiṣṭhati tan-nibhṛtaṃ praṇamya vrajeti | no cet, samādhi-bhaṅga-bhayād bhūyo 'pi prabhūtaṃ kopaṃ kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: When this was done, the hare led him to the lakeside at nighttime and showed him the reflection of the moon standing in the middle of the water. And he said: 'Sir, here is our lord standing in <s>samādhi</s> (deep meditation) in the middle of the water. So bow quietly and depart! Otherwise, angered by the disturbance of his meditation, he will be even more greatly wrathful.'

children.text: atha gajo 'pi trasta-manās taṃ praṇamya punar gamanāya prasthitaḥ | śaśakaś ca tad-dinād ārabhya sa-parivārāḥ sukhena sveṣu sthāneṣu tiṣṭhanti sma |
children.translated_text: Then the elephant too, his mind fearful, bowed to him and set out to depart for good. And from that day onward, the hare with his family lived happily in their dwellings.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi vyapadeśena mahatām iti | api ca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore I say: "By invoking the name of the great..." Moreover —'

children.text: kṣudram alasaṃ kāpuruṣaṃ vyasaninam akṛtajñaṃ jīvita-kāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is mean, lazy, cowardly, addicted to vice, ungrateful, desirous only of preserving life,

children.text: pṛṣṭha-pralapana-śīlaṃ svāmitve nābhiyojayet ||Panc_3.90||
children.translated_text: and given to backbiting — such a one should not be appointed to sovereignty. [Panc 3.90]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: kṣudram arthapatiṃ prāpya nyāyānveṣaṇa-tat-parau |
children.translated_text: Having obtained a mean ruler, both [parties], intent on seeking justice,

children.text: ubhāv api kṣayaṃ prāptau purā śaśaka-piñjalau ||Panc_3.91||
children.translated_text: came to ruin — the hare and the <s>piñjala</s> (partridge) of old. [Panc 3.91]

children.text: te procuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: They said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 2
śaśa-kapiñjala-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 2
The Story of the Hare and the Partridge

children.text: kasmiṃścid vṛkṣe purāham avasam | tatrādhastāt koṭare kapiñjalo nāma caṭakaḥ prativasati sma | atha sadaivāstam anavelāyām āgatayor dvayor aneka-subhāṣita-goṣṭhyā devarṣi-brahmarṣi-rājarṣi-purāṇa-carita-kīrtanena ca paryaṭana-dṛṣṭāneka-kautūhala-prakathanena ca parama-sukham anubhavatoḥ kālo vrajati | atha kadācit kapiñjalaḥ prāṇa-yātrārtham anyaiś caṭakaiḥ sahānyaṃ pakva-śāli-prāñaṃ deśaṃ gataḥ | tato yāvan niśā-samaye'pi nāyātas tāvad ahaṃ sodvega-manās tad-viprayoga-duḥkhitaś cintitavān-aho kim adya kapiñjalo nāyātaḥ | kiṃ kenāpi pāśena baddhaḥ ? āho svit kenāpi vyāpāditaḥ ? sarvathā yadi kuśalo bhavati, yan māṃ vinā na tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: On a certain tree I once lived. There, beneath it in a hollow, a bird named <s>Kapiñjala</s> (partridge) dwelt. Now, as we two would always meet at sunset, conversing on many fine sayings, recounting the tales of divine sages, Brahman-sages, and royal sages of the <s>Purāṇas</s>, and relating the many curiosities seen during our wanderings, time passed in supreme happiness. Then once, <s>Kapiñjala</s>, for his livelihood, went with other birds to another region abundant in ripe paddy. When he did not return even at nighttime, my mind became anxious and, pained by separation from him, I thought: 'Ah, why has <s>Kapiñjala</s> not come today? Has he been caught in some snare? Or has he been killed by someone? Surely, if he is well, he would not stay away from me.'

children.text: evaṃ me cintayato bahūny anyāni vyatikrāntāni | tataś ca tatra koṭare kadācic chīghrago nāma śaśako 'stam anavelāyām āgatya praviṣṭaḥ | mayāpi kapiñjala-nirāśatvena na nivāritaḥ | athānyasminn ahani kapiñjalaḥ śāli-bhakṣaṇād atīva pīvara-tanuḥ svāśrayaṃ smṛtvā bhūyo 'py atraiva samāyātaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: While I thought thus, many other days passed. Then once, a hare named <s>Śīghraga</s> (Swift-goer) came to that hollow at sunset and entered it. I too, having given up hope for <s>Kapiñjala</s>, did not stop him. Then on another day, <s>Kapiñjala</s>, having become exceedingly fat from eating paddy, remembering his own home, came back once again to this very place. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: na tādṛg jāyate saukhyam api svarge śarīriṇām |
children.translated_text: Such happiness does not arise even in heaven for embodied beings

children.text: dāridrye'pi hi yādṛk syāt sva-deśe sva-pure gṛhe ||Panc_3.92||
children.translated_text: as arises — even in poverty — in one's own country, one's own town, one's own home. [Panc 3.92]

children.text: athāsau koṭarāntargataṃ śaśakaṃ dṛṣṭvā sākṣepam āha-bhoḥ śaśaka ! na tvayā sundaraṃ kṛtaṃ, yan mamāvasatha-sthāne praviṣṭo 'si | tac chīghraṃ niṣkramyatām |
children.translated_text: Then he, seeing the hare inside the hollow, said scornfully: 'O hare! You have not done well in entering my dwelling-place. So get out quickly!'

children.text: śaśaka āha-na tavedaṃ gṛham, kintu mamaiva | tat kiṃ mithyā paruṣāṇi jalpasi ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The hare said: 'This house is not yours, but mine! So why do you speak such false harsh words?' And it is said —

children.text: vāpī-kūpa-taḍāgānāṃ devālaya-kujanmanām |
children.translated_text: Over wells, tanks, ponds, temples, and [property of] low-born —

children.text: utsargāt parataḥ svāmyam api kartuṃ na śakyate ||Panc_3.93||
children.translated_text: beyond the time of formal abandonment, ownership cannot be established. [Panc 3.93]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ yasya yad bhuktaṃ kṣetrādyaṃ daśa vatsarān |
children.translated_text: Whatever field or the like has been visibly enjoyed by someone for ten years —

children.text: tatra bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ syād na sākṣī nākṣarāṇi vā ||Panc_3.94||
children.translated_text: there, possession is the proof, not witnesses, not documents. [Panc 3.94]

children.text: mānuṣāṇām ayaṃ nyāyo munibhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is the law for humans, as declared by sages;

children.text: tiraścāṃ ca vihaṅgānāṃ yāvad eva samāśrayaḥ ||Panc_3.95||
children.translated_text: for animals and birds, [it holds] only so long as occupancy [lasts]. [Panc 3.95]

children.text: tan mamaitad gṛham, na taveti |
children.translated_text: 'So this house is mine, not yours.'

children.text: kapiñjala āha-bhoḥ ! yadi smṛtiṃ pramāṇīkaroṣi, tad āgaccha mayā saha yena smṛti-pāṭhakaṃ pṛṣṭvā sa yasya dadāti sa gṛhṇātu |
children.translated_text: <s>Kapiñjala</s> said: 'If you accept <s>smṛti</s> (traditional law) as authority, then come with me so that, having asked a reader of <s>smṛti</s>, he may decide and give it to whomever [is rightful] — and that one shall take it.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite mayāpi cintitaṃ-kim atra bhaviṣyati ? mayā draṣṭavyo 'yaṃ nyāyaḥ | tataḥ kautukād aham api tāv anuprasthitaḥ | atrāntare tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro nāmāraṇya-mārjāras tayor vivādaṃ śrutvā mārgāsannaṃ nadī-taṭam āsādya kṛta-kuśopagraho nimīlita-nayana ūrdhva-bāhur ardha-pāda-spṛṣṭa-bhūmiḥ śrī-sūryābhimukha imāṃ dharmopadeśanām akarot-aho ! asāro 'yaṃ saṃsāraḥ | kṣaṇa-bhaṅgurāḥ prāṇāḥ | svapna-sadṛśaḥ priya-samāgamaḥ | indra-jālavat kuṭumba-parigraho 'yam | tad dharmaṃ muktvā nānyā gatir asti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: When this had been done, I too thought: 'What will happen here? I must see how this case is judged.' Then out of curiosity, I too followed those two. In the meantime, a wild cat named <s>Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭra</s> (Sharp-fang), hearing their dispute, reached the riverbank near the path, took a bunch of <s>kuśa</s> grass in his hands, closed his eyes, raised his arms, standing on one foot touching the ground, facing the blessed sun, and delivered this discourse on <s>dharma</s>: 'Alas! This <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is without substance! Life-breaths are fragile as a moment! The union with loved ones is like a dream! This grasping after family is like the illusion of <s>Indra</s>. Therefore, apart from <s>dharma</s>, there is no other path.' And it is said —

children.text: anityāni śarīrāṇi vibhavo naiva śāśvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Bodies are impermanent; wealth is never everlasting;

children.text: nityaṃ saṃnihito mṛtyuḥ kartavyo dharma-saṃgrahaḥ ||Panc_3.96||
children.translated_text: death is always near — one should accumulate <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). [Panc 3.96]

children.text: yasya dharma-vihīnāni dināny āyānti yānti ca |
children.translated_text: He whose days come and go devoid of <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: sa lohakāra-bhastreva śvasann api na jīvati ||Panc_3.97||
children.translated_text: he, like a blacksmith's bellows, breathes but does not truly live. [Panc 3.97]

children.text: nācchādayati kaupīnaṃ na daṃśa-maśakāpaham |
children.translated_text: It does not cover a loincloth, it does not ward off gadflies and mosquitoes —

children.text: śunaḥ-puccham iva vyarthaṃ pāṇḍityaṃ dharma-varjitam ||Panc_3.98||
children.translated_text: learning devoid of <s>dharma</s> is as useless as a dog's tail. [Panc 3.98]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: pulākā iva dhānyeṣu pūtikā iv pakṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: Like husks among grains, like storks among birds,

children.text: maśakā iva martyeṣu yeṣāṃ dharmo na kāraṇam ||Panc_3.99||
children.translated_text: like mosquitoes among mortals — are those for whom <s>dharma</s> is not the purpose. [Panc 3.99]

children.text: śreyaḥ puṣpa-phalaṃ vṛkṣād dadhnaḥ śreyo ghṛtaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: Better than a tree is its flower and fruit; better than curds is <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter);

children.text: śreyas tailaṃ ca puṇyākāc chreyān dharmas tu mānuṣāt ||Panc_3.100||
children.translated_text: better than an oilcake is the oil; and better than a human being is <s>dharma</s>. [Panc 3.100]

children.text: sṛṣṭā mūtra-purīṣārtham āhārāya ca kevalam |
children.translated_text: Created merely for urine and excrement, and only for consuming food —

children.text: dharma-hīnāḥ parārthāya puruṣāḥ paśavo yathā ||Panc_3.101||
children.translated_text: men devoid of <s>dharma</s> exist for others' purposes, like animals. [Panc 3.101]

children.text: sthairyaṃ sarveṣu kṛtyeṣu śaṃsanti naya-paṇḍitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those wise in policy praise steadfastness in all undertakings;

children.text: bahv-antarāya-yuktasya dharmasya tvaritā gatiḥ ||Panc_3.102||
children.translated_text: for <s>dharma</s>, which is beset with many obstacles, requires a swift pace. [Panc 3.102]

children.text: saṅkṣepāt kathyate dharmo janāḥ kiṃ vistareṇa vaḥ |
children.translated_text: In brief, <s>dharma</s> is told — O people, what need of elaboration?

children.text: paropakāraḥ puṇyāya pāpāya para-pīḍanam ||Panc_3.103||
children.translated_text: Benefiting others is meritorious; harming others is sinful. [Panc 3.103]

children.text: śrūyatāṃ dharma-sarvasvaṃ śrutvā caivāvadhāryatām |
children.translated_text: Hear the essence of all <s>dharma</s>, and having heard, reflect upon it:

children.text: ātmanaḥ pratikūlāni pareṣāṃ na samācaret ||Panc_3.104||
children.translated_text: one should not do to others what is disagreeable to oneself. [Panc 3.104]

children.text: atha tasya tāṃ dharmopadeśanāṃ śrutvā śaśaka āha-bhoḥ bhoḥ kapiñjala ! eṣa nadī-tīre tapasvī dharma-vādī tiṣṭhati | tad enaṃ pṛcchāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his discourse on <s>dharma</s>, the hare said: 'Ho! <s>Kapiñjala</s>! This ascetic standing on the riverbank is a preacher of <s>dharma</s>. Let us ask him.'

children.text: kapiñjala āha-nanu svabhāvato 'yam asmākaṃ śatru-bhūtaḥ | tad dūre sthitvā pṛcchāvaḥ | kadācid asya vrata-vaikalyaṃ sampadyeta | tato dūrastho tāv ūcatuḥ-bhos tapasvin ! dharmopadeśaka ! āvayor vivādo vartate | tad dharma-śāstra-dvāreṇāsmākaṃ nirṇayaṃ kuru | yo hīnavādī sa te bhakṣya iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kapiñjala</s> said: 'But by nature he is our enemy. So let us ask from a distance. Perhaps his vow might falter.' Then the two said from afar: 'O ascetic! O preacher of <s>dharma</s>! We have a dispute. Through the authority of the <s>dharma-śāstra</s> (legal scripture), render us a verdict. The loser shall be your food.'

children.text: sa āha-bhadrau ! mā maivaṃ vadatam | nivṛtto 'haṃ naraka-mārgād dhiṃsā-karmaṇaḥ | ahiṃsaiva dharma-mārgaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Good sirs! Do not speak thus! I have turned away from the path to hell, from acts of violence. <s>Ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) alone is the path of <s>dharma</s>.' And it is said —

children.text: ahiṃsā-pūrvako dharmo yasmāt sarva-hite rataḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> has <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) as its foremost principle, since it is devoted to the welfare of all;

children.text: yūkā-mat-kuṇa-daṃśādīṃs tasmāt tān api rakṣayet ||Panc_3.105||
children.translated_text: therefore one should protect even lice, bedbugs, gadflies, and the like. [Panc 3.105]

children.text: hiṃsakāny api bhūtāni yo hiṃsati sa nirghṛṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who kills even creatures that are themselves violent is merciless;

children.text: sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ kiṃ punar yaḥ śubhāni ca ||Panc_3.106||
children.translated_text: he goes to terrible hell — how much more he who [kills] the innocent? [Panc 3.106]

children.text: ete'pi ye yājñikā yajña-karmaṇi paśūn vyāpādayanti, te mūrkhāḥ | paramārthaṃ śruter na jānanti | tatra kilaitad uktam-ajayaiṣṭavyam | ajā vrīhayas tāvat sapta-vārṣikāḥ kathyante na punaḥ paśu-viśeṣaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Even those ritualists who slay animals in sacrificial rites are fools. They do not know the true meaning of the Vedic scripture. For there it is stated: 'One should sacrifice with <s>aja</s>.' Now <s>aja</s> means seven-year-old rice grains, not a particular animal (goat). And it is said —

children.text: vṛkṣāṃś chittvā paśūn hatvā kṛtvā rudhira-kardamam |
children.translated_text: Having felled trees, having slain animals, having made a mire of blood —

children.text: yady evaṃ gamyate svargaṃ narakaṃ kena gamyate ||Panc_3.107||
children.translated_text: if heaven is reached in this manner, by what means does one reach hell? [Panc 3.107]

children.text: tan nāhaṃ bhakṣayāmi | paraṃ jaya-parājaya-nirṇayaṃ kariṣyāmi | kintv ahaṃ vṛddho dūrān na yathāvac chṛṇomi | evaṃ jñātvā mama samīpa-vartino bhūtvā mamāgre nyāyaṃ vadataṃ, yena vijñāya, vivāda-paramārthaṃ vaco vadato me para-loka-bādhā na bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So I shall not eat [you]. But I shall render the verdict on victory and defeat. However, I am old and cannot hear properly from a distance. Knowing this, come close to me and state the case before me, so that understanding the true substance of the dispute, no sin of the other world befalls me when I pronounce judgment.' And it is said —

children.text: mānād vā yadi vā lobhāt krodhād vā yadi vā bhayāt |
children.translated_text: Whether from pride, or from greed, or from anger, or from fear —

children.text: yo nyāyam anyathā brūte sa yāti narakaṃ naraḥ ||Panc_3.108||
children.translated_text: the man who pronounces a judgment wrongly goes to hell. [Panc 3.108]

children.text: pañca paśv-anṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte |
children.translated_text: One who lies regarding animals kills five; one who lies regarding cattle kills ten;

children.text: śataṃ kanyānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte ||Panc_3.109||
children.translated_text: one who lies regarding a maiden kills a hundred; one who lies regarding a man kills a thousand. [Panc 3.109]

children.text: upaviṣṭaḥ sabhā-madhye yo na vakti sphuṭaṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, seated in the midst of an assembly, does not speak clearly —

children.text: tasmād dūreṇa sa tyājyo na yo vā kīrtayed ṛtam ||Panc_3.110||
children.translated_text: he should be shunned from afar, he who would not proclaim the truth. [Panc 3.110]

children.text: tasmād viśrabdhau mama karṇopāntike sphuṭaṃ nivedayatam | kiṃ bahunā, tena kṣudreṇa tathā tau pūrṇaṃ viśvāsitau yathā tasyotsaṅga-vartinau jātau | tataś ca tenāpi sama-kālam evaikaḥ pādāntenākrānto 'nyo daṃṣṭrākrakacena ca tato gata-prāṇau bhakṣitāv iti | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-kṣudram artha-patiṃ prāpya (91) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, trusting me, declare clearly near my ear.' In short, that wretch won their full trust so completely that they came into his lap. And then, at the very same moment, he crushed one with the tip of his paw and the other with the saw of his fangs — and having killed them both, he devoured them. Therefore I say: 'Having obtained a petty ruler...' (verse 91) and so on.

children.text: bhavanto 'py enaṃ divāndhaṃ kṣudram artha-patim āsādya rātry-andhāḥ santaḥ śaśaka-piñjala-mārgeṇa yāsyanti | evaṃ jñātvā yad ucitaṃ tad vidheyam | atha tasya tad-vacanam ākarṇya sādhv anenābhihitam ity uktā, bhūyo 'pi pārthivāthaṃ sametya mantrayiṣyāmahe iti bruvāṇāḥ sarve pakṣiṇo yathābhimataṃ jagmuḥ | kevalam avaśiṣṭo bhadrāsanopaviṣṭo 'bhiṣekābhimukho divāndhaḥ kṛkālikayā sahāste | āha ca-kaḥ ko 'tra bhoḥ ! kim adyāpi na kriyate mamābhiṣekaḥ ?
children.translated_text: You too, having encountered this petty ruler who is day-blind (the owl), being yourselves night-blind, will go the way of the hare and the partridge. Knowing this, do what is proper.' Then, hearing his words, all the birds said 'he has spoken well' and declared: 'We shall again assemble and deliberate for the sake of the king.' Saying thus, all the birds departed as they pleased. Only the day-blind one (the owl) remained, seated on the throne, facing his consecration, together with the <s>Kṛkālikā</s> (the owl's she-minister). And he said: 'Ho! Who is here? Is my consecration still not performed?'

children.text: iti śrutvā kṛkālikayābhihitam-bhadra ! kuto 'yaṃ vighnas te kākena ? gatāś ca sarve'pi vihagā yathepsitāsu dikṣu kevalam eko 'yaṃ vāyaso 'vaśiṣṭas tiṣṭhati kenāpi kāraṇena | tat tvaritam uttiṣṭha, yena tvāṃ svāśrayaṃ prāpayāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Kṛkālikā</s> said: 'My lord! Why was this obstruction caused to you by the crow? All the birds have gone in their desired directions. Only this one crow remains for some reason. So rise quickly, that I may convey you to your own abode.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sa-viṣādam ulūko vāyasam āha-bho bho duṣṭātman ! kiṃ mayā te'pakṛtaṃ yad rājyābhiṣeko me vighnitaḥ ? tad adya-prabhṛti sānvayam āvayor vairaṃ sañjātam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the owl said with sorrow to the crow: 'Ho! You wicked soul! What wrong have I done to you that my royal consecration was obstructed? From this day forth, there is hereditary enmity between us and our families.' And it is said —

children.text: rohate sāyakair viddhaṃ chinnaṃ rohati cāsinā |
children.translated_text: A wound pierced by arrows heals; one cut by a sword also heals;

children.text: vaco duruktaṃ bībhatsaṃ na prarohati vāk-kṣatam ||Panc_3.111||
children.translated_text: but a wound caused by harsh, loathsome speech — a wound by words never heals. [Panc 3.111]

children.text: ity evam abhidhāya kṛkālikayā saha svāśramaṃ gataḥ | atha bhaya-vyākulo vāyaso vyacintayat-aho ! akāraṇaṃ vairam āsāditaṃ mayā | kim idaṃ vyāhṛtam ? uktaṃ ca-
adeśa-kālajñam anāyati-kṣamaṃ
children.translated_text: A speech that is ignorant of place and time, unable to bring about the future good,

children.text: yad apriyaṃ lāghava-kāri cātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: that is unpleasant and causes disgrace to oneself,

children.text: yo 'trābravīt kāraṇa-varjitaṃ vaco
children.translated_text: he who spoke such words without reason —

children.text: na tad vacaḥ syād viṣam eva tad bhavet ||Panc_3.112||
children.translated_text: that speech would not be speech, it would be poison itself. [Panc 3.112]

Having spoken thus, he departed with the <s>Kṛkālikā</s> to his own abode. Then the crow, stricken with fear, thought: 'Alas! I have incurred enmity without cause. What have I uttered?' And it is said —

children.text: balopapanno 'pi hi buddhimān naraḥ
children.translated_text: Even a man endowed with strength, if wise,

children.text: pare nayen na svayam eva vairitām |
children.translated_text: should not bring enmity upon himself voluntarily.

children.text: bhiṣaṅ mamāstīti vicintya bhakṣayed
children.translated_text: 'I have a physician' — thinking thus, should one eat

children.text: akāraṇāt ko hi vicakṣaṇo viṣam ||Panc_3.113||
children.translated_text: poison without cause? What sensible person would? [Panc 3.113]

children.text: parivādaḥ pariṣadi na kathañcit paṇḍitena vaktavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Censure in an assembly should never be uttered by a wise man;

children.text: satyam api tan na vācyaṃ yad uktam asukhāvahaṃ bhavati ||Panc_3.114||
children.translated_text: even the truth should not be spoken if, when spoken, it brings unhappiness. [Panc 3.114]

children.text: suhṛdbhir āptair asakṛd-vicāritaṃ
children.translated_text: That which has been repeatedly deliberated by trusted, wise friends,

children.text: svayaṃ hi buddhyā pravicāritāśrayam |
children.translated_text: and has been personally examined with one's own intellect as its foundation —

children.text: karoti kāryaṃ khalu yaḥ sa buddhimān
children.translated_text: he who acts upon such [counsel] is truly wise;

children.text: sa eva lakṣmyā yaśasāṃ ca bhājanam ||Panc_3.115||
children.translated_text: he alone is the vessel of fortune and fame. [Panc 3.115]

children.text: evaṃ vicintya kāko 'pi prayātaḥ | tadā-prabhṛty asmābhiḥ saha kauśikānām anvayā-gataṃ vairam asti |
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, the crow also departed. From that time onward, there has been hereditary enmity between us and the owls.

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-tāta ! evaṃ gate'smābhiḥ kiṃ kriyate ?
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Father! This being so, what shall we do?'

children.text: sa āha-vatsa ! evaṃ gate'pi ṣāḍguṇyād aparaḥ sthūlo 'bhiprāyo 'sti | tam aṅgīkṛtya svayam evāhaṃ tad-vijayāya yāsyāmi | ripūn vañcayitvā vadhiṣyāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Son! Even so, there is another weighty plan derived from the six strategies of policy. Adopting it, I myself shall go to accomplish their defeat. I shall deceive the enemies and destroy them.' And it is said —

children.text: bahu-buddhi-samāyuktāḥ suvijñānā balotkaṭān |
children.translated_text: Those endowed with great intelligence and good judgment are capable

children.text: śaktā vañcayituṃ dhūrtā brāhmaṇaṃ chāgalad iva ||Panc_3.116||
children.translated_text: of deceiving the powerful — the cunning ones — just as [they deceived] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of his goat. [Panc 3.116]

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 3
mitra-śarma-brāhmaṇa-kathā
children.translated_text: He narrated — Story 3: The tale of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Mitraśarman</s>.

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne mitraśarmā nāma brāhmaṇaḥ kṛtāgnihotra-parigrahaḥ prativasati sma | tena kadācin māgha-māse saumyānile pravāti, meghācchādite gagane mandaṃ mandaṃ pravarṣati parjanye, paśu-prārthanārthaṃ kiñcid grāmāntaraṃ gatvā, kaścid yajamāno yācitaḥ-bho yajamāna ! āgāminyām amāvāsyāyām ahaṃ yakṣyāmi yajñam | tad dehi me paśum ekam |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Mitraśarman</s>, who maintained the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice) ritual. Once, in the month of <s>Māgha</s> (January-February), while a gentle wind blew, the sky was covered with clouds, and rain fell gently, he went to another village seeking a sacrificial animal, and petitioned a certain patron: 'O patron! On the coming new-moon day, I shall perform a sacrifice. So give me one animal.'

children.text: atha tena yasya śāstroktaḥ pīvara-tanuḥ paśuḥ pradattaḥ | so 'pi taṃ samartham itaś cetaś ca gacchantaṃ vijñāya skandhe kṛtvā satvaraṃ sva-purābhimukhaḥ pratasthe |
children.translated_text: Thereupon, the patron gave him a stout-bodied animal prescribed by scripture. He too, recognizing it as suitable, placing it going this way and that upon his shoulder, set out quickly toward his own town.

children.text: atha tasya gacchato mārge trayo dhūrtāḥ kṣut-kṣāma-kaṇṭhāḥ saṃmukhā babhūvuḥ | taiś ca tādṛśaṃ pīvara-tanuṃ skandha ārūḍham ālokya, mitho 'bhihitaṃ-aho ! asya paśor bhakṣaṇād adyatanīyo hima-pāto vyarthatāṃ nīyate | tad enaṃ vañcayitvā paśum ādāya śīta-trāṇaṃ kurmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, as he was walking on the road, three rogues with throats pinched by hunger came before him. Seeing that stout-bodied animal mounted on his shoulder, they said to each other: 'Ah! By eating this animal, today's snowfall will be rendered futile. So let us deceive him, take the animal, and ward off the cold.'

children.text: atha teṣām ekatamo veśa-parivartanaṃ vidhāya saṃmukho bhūtvāpamārgeṇa tam āhitāgnim ūce-bho bhoḥ ! bālāgnihotrin ! kim evaṃ jana-viruddhaṃ hāsya-kāryam anuṣṭhīyate ? yad eṣa sārameyo 'pavitraḥ skandhādhirūḍho nīyate | uktaṃ ca yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Then one of them, having changed his appearance, came before him and by an indirect route addressed the fire-sacrificer: 'Ho! Ho! Novice fire-sacrificer! Why is such a laughable act, contrary to all people's practice, being performed? This impure dog is being carried mounted on your shoulder!' And it is said —

children.text: śvāna-kukkuṭa-cāṇḍālāḥ sama-sparśāḥ prakīrtitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Dogs, roosters, and <s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcaste persons) are declared to have the same touch;

children.text: rāsabhoṣṭrau viśeṣeṇa tasmāt tān naiva saṃspṛśet ||Panc_3.117||
children.translated_text: donkeys and camels especially — therefore one should never touch them. [Panc 3.117]

children.text: tataś ca tena kopābhibhūtenābhihitam-aho ! kim andho bhavān ? yat paśuṃ sārameyatvena pratipādayasi ?
children.translated_text: Then, overcome with anger, he said: 'What! Are you blind? You represent this animal as a dog?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-brahman ! kopas tvayā na kāryaḥ | yathecchaṃ gamyatām |
children.translated_text: He replied: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! Do not be angry. Go as you please.'

children.text: atha yāvat kiñcid adhvano 'ntaraṃ gacchati, tāvad dvitīyo dhūrtaḥ sammukham abhyupetya tam uvāca-bhoḥ brahman ! kaṣṭaṃ kaṣṭam ! yadyapi vallabho 'yaṃ te mṛta-vatsas tathāpi skandham āropayitum ayuktam | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, when he had traveled a little further on the road, the second rogue came before him and said: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! Shame! Shame! Even though this dead calf is dear to you, it is not proper to carry it on your shoulder.' And it is said —

children.text: tiryañcaṃ mānuṣaṃ vāpi yo mṛtaṃ saṃspṛśet kudhīḥ |
children.translated_text: The foolish one who touches a dead being, whether animal or human —

children.text: pañca-gavyena śuddhiḥ syāt tasya cāndrāyaṇena vā ||Panc_3.118||
children.translated_text: his purification would be by <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow) or by the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow. [Panc 3.118]

children.text: athāsau sa-kopam idam āha-bhoḥ ! kim andho bhavān ? yat paśuṃ mṛta-vatsaṃ vadati |
children.translated_text: Then he said angrily: 'What! Are you blind? You call this animal a dead calf?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-bhagavan ! mā kopaṃ kuru | ajñānān mayābhihitam | tat tvam ātma-ruciṃ samācara iti |
children.translated_text: He replied: 'O venerable one! Do not be angry. I spoke out of ignorance. So you may do as you please.'

children.text: atha yāvat stokaṃ vanāntaraṃ gacchati tāvat tṛtīyo 'nya-veśa-dhārī dhūrtaḥ sammukhaḥ samupetya tam uvāca-bhoḥ ! ayuktam etat, yad rāsabhaṃ skandhādhirūḍhaṃ nayasi | tat tyajyatām eṣaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, when he had gone a short distance further into the forest, the third rogue, wearing a different disguise, came before him and said: 'Sir! This is improper — that you carry a donkey mounted on your shoulder! Drop this one!' And it is said —

children.text: yaḥ spṛśed rāsabhaṃ martyo jñānād ajñānato 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: The mortal who touches a donkey, whether knowingly or unknowingly —

children.text: sa-cailaṃ snānam uddiṣṭaṃ tasya pāpa-praśāntaye ||Panc_3.119||
children.translated_text: bathing with clothes on is prescribed for the pacification of that sin. [Panc 3.119]

children.text: tat tyajainaṃ yāvad anyaḥ kaścin na paśyati |
children.translated_text: So drop him before someone else sees!'

children.text: athāsau taṃ paśuṃ rāsabhaṃ manyamāno bhayād bhūmau prakṣipya sva-gṛham uddiśya palāyituṃ prārabdhaḥ | tatas te'pi trayo militvā paśum ādāya yathecchaṃ bhakṣitum ārabdhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then he, thinking the animal to be a donkey, threw it on the ground in fear and began to flee toward his own home. Then those three, having united, took the animal and began to eat it as they pleased.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bahu-buddhi-samāyuktāḥ (116) iti | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'endowed with much intelligence' (116). Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: abhinava-sevaka-vinayaiḥ prāghuṇakoktair vilāsinīr uditaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By the courtesies of a new servant, by the speeches of a host, by the praises of courtesans,

children.text: dhūrta-jana-vacana-nikarair iha kaścid avañcito nāsti ||Panc_3.120||
children.translated_text: by the multitude of words of rogues — no one in this world is undeceived. ||Panc_3.120||

children.text: kiṃ ca-durbalair api bahubhiḥ saha virodho na yuktaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover — one should not make enmity with many, even if they are weak. And it is said —

children.text: bahavo na viroddhavyā durjayā hi mahājanāḥ |
children.translated_text: Many should not be opposed, for the multitude is hard to conquer;

children.text: sphurantam api nāgendraṃ bhakṣayanti pipīlikāḥ ||Panc_3.121||
children.translated_text: even ants devour the king of serpents, though he writhes. ||Panc_3.121||

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: How is that?

children.text: sthirajīvī kathayati-
children.translated_text: <s>Sthirajīvī</s> narrates —

children.text:
kathā 4
atidarpa-nāma-sarpa-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 4
The Story of the Snake Named <s>Atidarpa</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid valmīke mahā-kāyaḥ kṛṣṇa-sarpo 'tidarpo nāma | sa kadācid vilānusāri-mārgam utsṛjyānyena laghu-dvāreṇa niṣkramitum ārabdhaḥ | niṣkrāmataś ca tasya mahā-kāyatvād daiva-vaśatayā laghu-vivaratvāc ca śarīre vraṇaḥ samutpannaḥ | atha vraṇa-śoṇita-gandhānusāriṇībhiḥ pipīlikābhiḥ sarvato vyāpto vyākulīkṛtaś ca | kati vyāpādayati kati vā tāḍayati ? atha prabhūtatvād vistārita-bahu-vraṇaḥ kṣata-sarvāṅgo 'tidarpaḥ pañcatvam upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain anthill there lived a great-bodied black snake named <s>Atidarpa</s> (excessive-pride). Once, abandoning the path that followed his burrow, he began to exit through another narrow opening. And as he was exiting, because of his great body and by the power of fate and because of the narrowness of the opening, a wound arose on his body. Then, ants following the scent of the wound's blood surrounded him from all sides and tormented him. How many could he kill? How many could he strike? Then, due to their great numbers, [his body] covered with many open wounds, his entire body lacerated, <s>Atidarpa</s> met his death.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bahavo na viroddhavyā (121) iti | tad atrāsti me kiñcid vaktavyam eva | tad avadhārya yathoktam anuṣṭhīyatām |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Many should not be opposed' (121). Now I have something to say in this matter. So having considered it, let what I say be carried out.

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-tat samādeśaya | tavādeśo nānyathā kartavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: Then command. Your command shall not be disregarded.

children.text: sthirajīvī prāha-vatsa ! samākarṇaya tarhi | sāmādīn atikramya yo mayā pañcama upāyo nirūpitaḥ | tan māṃ vipakṣa-bhūtaṃ kṛtvāni niṣṭhura-vacanair nirbhartsya | yathā vipakṣa-praṇidhīnāṃ pratyayo bhavati, tathā samāhṛta-rudhirair ālipyāsyaiva nyagrodhasyādhastāt prakṣipya māṃ gamyatāṃ parvatam ṛṣyamūkaṃ prati | tatra sa-parivāras tiṣṭha, yāvad ahaṃ samastān sapatnān supraṇītena vidhinā viśvāsyābhimukhān kṛtvā kṛtārtho jñāta-durga-madhyo divase tān andhatāṃ prāptāṃs tvāṃ nītvā vyāpādayāmi | jñātaṃ mayā samyak nānyathāsmākaṃ siddhir asti | yato durgam etad apasāra-rahitaṃ kevalaṃ vadhāya bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Sthirajīvī</s> said: Son, then listen carefully. Beyond <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and the other [three expedients], there is a fifth stratagem that I have devised. So, making me appear to be a traitor, revile me with harsh words. In such a way that the enemy's spies will be convinced, smear me with drawn blood, throw me down beneath this very banyan tree, and go with your retinue to Mount <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>. Stay there with your retinue while I, having won the trust of all the enemies by a well-executed method, having made them turn toward [us], having accomplished my purpose and learned the interior of their fortress, shall lead you [there] during the day when they have become blind, and destroy them. I have determined this properly — there is no other way for our success. For this fortress, without a means of retreat, will only serve for [our] destruction. And it is said —

children.text: apasāra-samāyuktaṃ na yajñair durgam ucyate |
children.translated_text: A fortress equipped with a means of retreat is not [merely] praised by sacrifices;

children.text: apasāra-parityaktaṃ durga-vyājena bandhanam ||Panc_3.122||
children.translated_text: a fortress devoid of a means of retreat is [merely] imprisonment in the guise of a fortress. ||Panc_3.122||

children.text: na ca tvayā mad-arthaṃ kṛpā kāryā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And you should not feel pity for me on this account. And it is said —

children.text: api prāṇa-samān iṣṭān pālitān lālitān api |
children.translated_text: Even servants dear as one's own life, protected and cherished —

children.text: bhṛtyān yuddhe samutpanne paśyec chuṣkam ivendhanam ||Panc_3.123||
children.translated_text: when battle arises, one should regard them as dry firewood. ||Panc_3.123||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: prāṇavad rakṣayed bhṛtyān svakāyam iva poṣayet |
children.translated_text: One should protect servants like one's life and nourish them like one's own body;

children.text: sadaika-divasasyārthe yatra syād ripu-saṅgamaḥ ||Panc_3.124||
children.translated_text: on that single day when there is an encounter with the enemy, [they serve their purpose]. ||Panc_3.124||

children.text: tat tvayāhaṃ nātra viṣaye pratiṣedhanīyaḥ | ity uktvā tena saha śuṣka-kalahaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ | athānye tasya bhṛtyāḥ sthirajīvinam ucchṛṅkhala-vacanair jalpantam avalokya tasya vadhāyodyatā meghavarṇenābhihitāḥ-aho ! nivartadhvaṃ yūyam | aham evāsya śatru-pakṣapātino durātmanaḥ svayaṃ nigrahaṃ kariṣyāṃi | ity abhidhāya tasyopari samāruhya, laghubhiś cañcu-prahārais taṃ nihatyāhṛta-rudhireṇa plāvayitvā tad-upadiṣṭam ṛṣyamūka-parvataṃ sa-parivāro gataḥ |
children.translated_text: So you should not prevent me in this territory. Having said this, he began to have a feigned quarrel with him. Then his other servants, seeing <s>Sthirajīvī</s> speaking insolent words, were about to kill him [when] <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: Stop, all of you! I myself shall punish this evil-souled one who sides with the enemy. Having said this, he mounted upon him, struck him with light beak-blows, and flooding him with drawn blood, went with his retinue to Mount <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> as instructed by him.

children.text: etasminn antare kṛkālikayā dviṣat-praṇidhī-bhūtayā tat sarvaṃ tad-amātya-vyasanaṃ kvacit pracalitaḥ sa-parivāra iti |
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, a lizard who was a spy of the enemy [reported] all that — his minister's calamity, [and] that he had departed somewhere with his retinue.

children.text: atholūkādhipas tad ākarṇyāstam anavelāyāṃ sāmātyaḥ sa-parijano vāyasa-vadhārthaṃ pracalitaḥ | prāha ca-tvaryatāṃ tvaryatāṃ bhītaḥ śatruḥ palāyana-paraḥ puṇyair labhyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then the owl-king, hearing that, set out at an untimely sunset with his ministers and attendants to kill the crows. And he said: Hurry, hurry! A frightened enemy, intent on flight, is obtained by [the fortunate]. And it is said —

children.text: śatroḥ pracalane chidram ekam anyaṃ ca saṃśrayam |
children.translated_text: When an enemy is departing, [exploiting] a vulnerability is one thing, and [attacking] another refuge [is another];

children.text: kurvāṇo jāyate vaśyo vyagratve rāja-sevinām ||Panc_3.125||
children.translated_text: one who creates [such opportunities] becomes master [of the situation] when the king's attendants are in disarray. ||Panc_3.125||

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇaḥ samantān nyagrodha-pādapam adhaḥ pariveṣṭya vyavasthitaḥ | yāvan na kaścid vāyaso dṛśyate, tāvac chākhāgram adhirūḍho hṛṣṭa-manā vandibhir abhiṣṭūyamāno 'rimardanas tān parijanān provāca-aho ! jñāyatāṃ teṣāṃ mārgaḥ | katamena mārgeṇa pranaṣṭāḥ kākāḥ ? tad yāvan na durgaṃ samāśrayanti, tāvad eva pṛṣṭhato gatvā vyāpādyā bhavanti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Speaking thus, he surrounded the banyan tree from all sides and took his position below. When not a single crow was visible, <s>Arimardana</s>, having climbed to the top of a branch, with a delighted mind, being praised by bards, said to his attendants: Ah! Let their path be ascertained. By which path have the crows fled? So before they take refuge in a fortress, let them be pursued from behind and killed. And it is said —

children.text: vṛttim apy āśritaḥ śatrur avadhyaḥ syāj jigīṣuṇā |
children.translated_text: An enemy who has resorted to submission should not be slain by one who desires conquest;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ saṃśrito durgaṃ sāmagryā parayā yutam ||Panc_3.126||
children.translated_text: how much less one who has taken refuge in a fortress furnished with the greatest resources? ||Panc_3.126||

children.text: athaitasmin prastāve sthirajīvī cintayāmāsa-yad ete'smac chatravo 'nulabdhāsmad-vṛttāntā yathāgatam eva yānti tato mayā na kiñcit kṛtaṃ bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Now at this juncture, <s>Sthirajīvī</s> thought: If these enemies of ours go back the way they came without obtaining any news of us, then nothing will have been accomplished by me. And it is said —

children.text: anārambho hi kāryāṇāṃ prathamaṃ buddhi-lakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Not beginning tasks at all is the first mark of intelligence;

children.text: ārabdhasyānta-gamanaṃ dvitīyaṃ buddhi-lakṣaṇam ||Panc_3.127||
children.translated_text: bringing what has been begun to completion is the second mark of intelligence. ||Panc_3.127||

children.text: tad varam anārambho na cārambha-vighātaḥ | tad aham etān śabdaṃ saṃśrāvya ātmānaṃ darśayāmi iti vicārya mandaṃ mandaṃ śabdam akarot | tac chrutvā te sakalā apy ulūkās tad-vadhāya prajagmuḥ | atha tenoktaṃ-aho ! ahaṃ sthirajīvī nāma meghavarṇasya mantrī | meghavarṇenaivedṛśīm avasthāṃ nītaḥ | tan nivedayatātma-svāmine | tena saha bahu vaktavyam asti |
children.translated_text: So better not to begin than to have the undertaking frustrated. Therefore I shall make them hear a sound and show myself. Having resolved thus, he made a faint sound. Hearing that, all those owls rushed to kill him. Then he said: Ah! I am <s>Sthirajīvī</s>, the minister of <s>Meghavar���a</s>. By <s>Meghavarṇa</s> I have been brought to this condition. So inform your master. I have much to say to him.

children.text: atha tair niveditaḥ sa ulūka-rājo vismayāviṣṭas tat-kṣaṇāt tasya sakāśaṃ gatvā provāca-bhoḥ bhoḥ ! kim etāṃ daśāṃ gatas tvam, tat kathyatām |
children.translated_text: Then, when they reported [this], that owl-king, filled with astonishment, immediately went to his presence and said: Ho! How have you come to this state? Tell me!

children.text: sthirajīvī prāha-deva ! śrūyatāṃ tad-avasthā-kāraṇam | atīta-dine sa durātmā meghavarṇo yuṣmad-vyāpādita-prabhūta-vāyasānāṃ pīḍayā yuṣmākam upari kopa-śoka-grasto yuddhārthaṃ pracalita āsīt | tato mayābhihitaṃ-svāmin ! na yuktaṃ bhavatas tad-upari gantum | balavanta ete, bala-hīnāś ca vayam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Sthiraj��vī</s> said: Lord! Hear the cause of this condition. On a past day, that evil-souled <s>Meghavarṇa</s>, afflicted with anger and grief over the many crows killed by you, had set out to make war upon you. Then I said: Master! It is not proper for you to march against them. They are powerful, and we are weak in strength. And it is said —

children.text: balīyasā hīna-balo virodhaṃ
children.translated_text: One who is weak in strength, against a more powerful [foe], a conflict —

children.text: na bhūti-kāmo manasāpi vāñchet |
children.translated_text: one desiring prosperity should not wish for even in his mind.

children.text: na vadhyate vetasa-vṛttir atra
children.translated_text: One who acts like a willow [i.e., bends] is not destroyed here;

children.text: vyaktaṃ praṇāśo 'sti pataṅga-vṛtteḥ ||Panc_3.128||
children.translated_text: clearly, one who acts like a moth meets destruction. ||Panc_3.128||

children.text: tat tasyoāyana-pradānena sandhir eva yuktaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So peace with him, through the offering of tribute, alone is proper. And it is said —
