children.text: balavantaṃ ripuṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvasvam api buddhimān |
children.translated_text: Seeing a powerful enemy, the wise one, even [giving up] all his possessions,

children.text: dattvā hi rakṣayet prāṇān rakṣitais tair dhanaṃ punaḥ ||Panc_3.129||
children.translated_text: should give [them away] and protect his life; with life protected, wealth [comes] again. ||Panc_3.129||

children.text: tac chrutvā durjana-kopitena tvat-pakṣa-pātinaṃ mām āśaṅkamānenemāṃ daśāṃ nītaḥ | tat tava pādau sāmprataṃ me śaraṇaṃ | kiṃ bahunā vijñaptena ? yāvad ahaṃ pracalituṃ śaknomi tāvat tvāṃ tasyāvāsaṃ nītvā sarva-vāyasa-kṣayaṃ vidhāsyāmi iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, angered by wicked ones and suspecting me of siding with your party, he brought me to this state. So your feet are now my refuge. What more need be said in petition? As long as I am able to move, I shall lead you to his dwelling and bring about the destruction of all the crows.

children.text: athārimardanas tad ākarṇya pitṛ-pitāmaha-kramāgata-mantribhiḥ sārdhaṃ mantrayāṃcakre | tasya ca pañca mantriṇaḥ | tad yathā-raktākṣaḥ, krūrākṣaḥ, dīptākṣaḥ, vakranāsaḥ, prākārakarṇaś ceti | tatrādau raktākṣam apṛcchat-bhadra ! eṣa tāvat tasya ripor mantrī mama hasta-gataḥ | tat kiṃ kriyatām ? iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arimardana</s>, hearing that, deliberated together with his ministers inherited from father and grandfather. And he had five ministers — namely: <s>Raktākṣa</s> (red-eye), <s>Krūrākṣa</s> (cruel-eye), <s>Dīptākṣa</s> (bright-eye), <s>Vakranāsa</s> (crooked-nose), and <s>Prākārakarṇa</s> (rampart-ear). First he asked <s>Raktākṣa</s>: Good sir! This minister of that enemy is now in my hands. So what is to be done?

children.text: raktākṣa āha-deva ! kim atra cintyate ? avicāritam ayaṃ hantavyaḥ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Raktākṣa</s> said: Lord! What is there to deliberate? He should be killed without further consideration, because —

children.text: hīnaḥ śatrur nihantavyo yāvan na balavān bhavet |
children.translated_text: A weakened enemy should be killed before he becomes powerful;

children.text: prāpta-sva-pauruṣa-balaḥ paścād bhavati durjayaḥ ||Panc_3.130||
children.translated_text: once he has attained his own manly strength, he afterwards becomes hard to conquer. ||Panc_3.130||

children.text: kiṃ ca svayam upāgatā śrīs tyajyamānā śapatīti loke pravādaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is a popular saying: fortune that comes of its own accord curses [one] when rejected. And it is said —

children.text: kālo hi sakṛd abhyeti yan naraṃ kāla-kāṅkṣiṇam |
children.translated_text: Time, which approaches a man waiting for the [right] time, comes but once;

children.text: durlabhaḥ sa punas tena kāla-karmācikīrṣatā ||Panc_3.131||
children.translated_text: it is hard to obtain again by one desiring to accomplish a deed at the [right] time. ||Panc_3.131||

children.text: śrūyate ca yathā-
children.translated_text: And it is heard that —

children.text: kaścit kṣudra-samācāraḥ prāṇināṃ kāla-sannibhaḥ |
children.translated_text: A certain one of vile conduct, resembling Death to [other] creatures,

children.text: vicacāra mahāraṇye ghoraḥ śuni-lubdhakaḥ ||Panc_3.132||
children.translated_text: wandered in the great forest — the terrible dog-hunter. ||Panc_3.132||

children.text: arimardanaḥ prāha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Arimardana</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
raktākṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 5
brāhmaṇa-sarpa-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Raktākṣa</s> narrates —
Tale 5
The Story of the Brāhmaṇa and the Serpent

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne haridatto nāma brāhmaṇaḥ | tasya ca kṛṣiṃ kurvataḥ sadaiva niṣphalaḥ kālo 'tivartate | athaikasmin divase sa brāhmaṇa uṣṇa-kālāvasāne gharmārtaḥ sva-kṣetra-madhye vṛkṣa-cchāyāyāṃ prasupto 'natidūre valmīkopari prasāritaṃ bṛhat-phaṭā-yuktaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa-nūnam eṣā kṣetra-devatā mayā kadācid api na pūjitā | tenedaṃ me kṛṣi-karma viphalībhavati | tad asyā ahaṃ pūjām adya kariṣyāmi | ity avadhārya kuto 'pi kṣīraṃ yācitvā śarāve nikṣipya valmīkāntikam upagatyovāca-bhoḥ kṣetra-pāla ! mayaitvāvantaṃ kālaṃ na jñātaṃ yat tvam atra vasasi | tena pūjā na kṛtā | tat sāmprataṃ kṣamasveti |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Haridatta</s>. Time always passed fruitlessly for him as he tilled his fields. Then one day, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, exhausted by the heat at the end of the hot season, having fallen asleep beneath the shade of a tree in the middle of his own field, saw not far away, atop an anthill, a fearsome serpent with a great spread hood, and thought: Surely this is the deity of the field, and I have never worshipped her. Therefore this farming work of mine proves fruitless. So I shall worship her today. Having resolved thus, begging milk from somewhere, placing it in a saucer, having come near the anthill, he said: O guardian of the field! For all this time I did not know that you dwell here. Therefore no worship was offered. So now forgive me!

children.text:
evam uktvā dugdhaṃ ca nivedya gṛhābhimukhaṃ prāyāt | atha prātar yāvad āgatya paśyati, tāvad dīnāram ekaṃ śarāve dṛṣṭavān | evaṃ ca pratidinam ekākī samāgatya tasmai kṣīraṃ dadāti, ekaikaṃ ca dīnāraṃ gṛhṇāti | athaikasmin divase kṣīra-nayanāya putraṃ nirūpya brāhmaṇo grāmāntaraṃ jagāma | putro 'pi kṣīraṃ tatra nītvā saṃsthāpya ca punar gṛhaṃ samāyātaḥ | dināntare tatra gatvā dīnārakaṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhītvā ca cintitavān-nūnaṃ sauvarṇa-dīnāra-pūrṇo valmīkaḥ | tad enaṃ hatvā sarvam eka-vāraṃ grahīṣyāmi ity evaṃ sampradhāryānyedyuḥ kṣīraṃ dadatā brāhmaṇa-putreṇa sarpo laguḍena tāḍitaḥ | tataḥ katham api daiva-vaśād amukta-jīvit eva roṣāt tam eva tīvra-viṣada-śanais tathādaśat, yathā
sadyaḥ pañcatvam upāgataḥ | svajanaiś ca nātidūre kṣetrasya kāṣṭha-sañcayaiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he offered the milk and set out homeward. Then the next morning, when he came and looked, he found one gold coin in the saucer. And thus every day, coming alone, he would give milk to it and take one gold coin each time. Then one day, having appointed his son to bring the milk, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> went to another village. The son too brought the milk there, placed it, and returned home. On the next day, going there, seeing the gold coin and taking it, he thought: Surely this anthill is full of gold coins. So, having killed it, I shall take all at once. Having thus resolved, the next day, while giving the milk, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s son struck the serpent with a stick. Then the serpent, somehow still alive by the power of fate, out of anger bit him with such terrible poisonous fangs that he immediately died. And his kinsmen cremated him with wood-piles not far from the field.

children.text: atha dvitīya-dine tasya pitā samāyātaḥ | svajanebhyaḥ suta-vināśa-kāraṇaṃ śrutvā tathaiva samarthitavān | abravīc ca-
children.translated_text: Then on the second day, his father arrived. Having heard from kinsmen the cause of his son's death, he acknowledged [it] in the same way. And he said —

children.text: bhūtān yo nānugṛhṇāti hy ātmanaḥ śaraṇāgatān |
children.translated_text: He who does not favor beings that have taken refuge with him as their own —

children.text: bhūtārthās tasya naśyanti haṃsāḥ padma-vane yathā ||Panc_3.133||
children.translated_text: the riches of that one perish, like swans [departing] from a lotus-pond. ||Panc_3.133||

children.text: puruṣair uktaṃ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The men said: How is that?

children.text:
brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati-
kathā 6
haima-haṃsa-kathā
children.translated_text:
The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> narrates —
Tale 6
The Story of the Golden Swans

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne citraratho nāma rājā | tasya yodhaiḥ surakṣyamāṇaṃ padmasaro nāma saras tiṣṭhati tatra ca prabhūtā jāmbūnada-mayā haṃsās tiṣṭhanti | ṣaṇmāse ṣaṇmāse piccham ekaikaṃ parityajanti | atha tatra sarasi sauvarṇo bṛhat-pakṣī samāyātaḥ | taiś coktaḥ-asmākaṃ madhye tvayā na vastavyam | yena kāraṇenāsmābhiḥ ṣaṇmāsānte picchaikaika-dānaṃ kṛtvā gṛhītam etat saraḥ | evaṃ ca kiṃ bahunā, parasparaṃ dvaidham utpannam | sa ca rājñaḥ śaraṇaṃ gato 'bravīt-deva ! ete pakṣiṇa evaṃ vadanti, yad asmākaṃ rājā kiṃ kariṣyati ? na kasyāpy āvāsaṃ dadmaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain kingdom there was a king named <s>Citragraha</s>. Under his protection by his warriors, there was a lake called <s>Padmasara</s>, and in it lived a great number of geese made of gold. Every six months, each would shed a single feather. Now a great golden bird arrived at that lake. They said to him: 'You must not dwell among us, because we have secured this lake by giving one feather every six months.' In short, a dispute arose between them. And that [golden bird] went to the king for refuge and said: 'Your Majesty! These birds say thus: "What will our king do? We do not give shelter to anyone."'

children.text: mayā coktaṃ-na śobhanaṃ yuṣmābhir abhihitam | ahaṃ gatvā rājñe nivedayiṣyāmi | evaṃ sthite devaḥ pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: 'And I said: "What you have said is not proper. I shall go and report this to the king." This being the case, Your Majesty is the authority.'

children.text: tato rājā bhṛtyān abravīt-bho bhoḥ gacchata | sarvān pakṣiṇo gatāsūn kṛtvā śīghram ānayata | rājādeśānantaram eva pracelus te |
children.translated_text: Then the king said to his servants: 'Ho, ho! Go! Kill all the birds and bring them quickly.' No sooner had the king's command been issued than they set forth.

children.text: atha laguḍa-hastān rāja-puruṣān dṛṣṭvā tatraikena pakṣiṇā vṛddhenoktam-bhoḥ svajanāḥ ! na śobhanam āpatitam | tataḥ sarvair eka-matī-bhūyotpatitavyam | taiś ca tathānuṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: Now, seeing the king's men with clubs in hand, one old bird among them said: 'O kinsmen! Something untoward has befallen us. Therefore, all of us, becoming of one mind, must fly away at once.' And they did so.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-bhūtān yo nānugṛhṇāti (133) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'He who does not favor his own people...' (verse 133).

children.text: ity uktvā punar api brāhmaṇaḥ pratyūṣe kṣīraṃ gṛhītvā tatra gatvā tāra-svareṇa sarpam astaut | tadā sarpaś ciraṃ valmīka-dvārāntar-līna eva brāhmaṇaṃ pratyuvāca-tvaṃ lobhād atrāgataḥ putra-śokam api vihāya | ataḥ paraṃ tava mama ca prītir nocitā | tava putreṇa yauvanonmādenāhaṃ tāḍito mayā sa dṛṣṭaḥ | kathaṃ mayā laguḍa-prahāro vismartavyaḥ | tvayā ca putra-śoka-duḥkhaṃ kathaṃ vismartavyam iti punar uktvā vivarāntar-gataḥ | brāhmaṇaś ca maṇiṃ gṛhītvā putra-buddhiṃ nindan sva-gṛham āgataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-citikāṃ dīpitāṃ paśya iti | tad asmin hate'yatnād eva rājyam akaṇṭakaṃ bhavato bhavati |
children.translated_text: Having said this, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> once again, at dawn, took milk and went there, and praised the serpent in a loud voice. Then the serpent, having remained hidden within the entrance of the anthill for a long time, replied to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'You have come here out of greed, having set aside even the grief for your son. Henceforth, affection between you and me is not fitting. Your son, intoxicated with the arrogance of youth, struck me; and by me he was bitten. How can I forget the blow of the club? And how can you forget the suffering of grief for your son?' Having said this again, he entered into the hole. And the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, taking the jewel, went to his own house, blaming his son's judgment. Therefore I say: 'Look at the blazing funeral pyre...' So, with him killed, your kingdom becomes free of thorns effortlessly.

children.text: tasyaitad-vacanaṃ śrutvā krūrākṣaṃ papraccha-bhadra ! tvaṃ tu kiṃ manyase ?
children.translated_text: Having heard his words, he asked <s>Krūrākṣa</s>: 'Good sir, what do you think?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! nirdayam etad yad anenābhihitam | yat kāraṇaṃ śaraṇāgato na vadhyate suṣṭhu | khalv idam ākhyānam-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Your Majesty! What this one has said is merciless. For a refugee should not be killed. This is a fine tale indeed —'

children.text: śrūyate hi kapotena śatruḥ śaraṇam āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: It is heard that by a pigeon, an enemy who had come seeking refuge

children.text: pūjitaś ca yathā-nyāyaṃ svaiś ca māṃsair nimantritaḥ ||Panc_3.134||
children.translated_text: was honored as was proper, and even invited [to partake] of his own flesh. // Panc_3.134 //

children.text: arimardano 'bravīt-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Arimardana</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
krūrākṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 7
kapota-lubdhaka-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Krūrākṣa</s> narrates:
Tale 7
The Story of the Pigeon and the Fowler

children.text: kaścid kṣudra-samācāraḥ prāṇināṃ kāla-sannibhaḥ |
children.translated_text: A certain man of vile conduct, resembling Death to living beings,

children.text: vicacāra mahāraṇye ghoraḥ śakuni-lubdhakaḥ ||Panc_3.135||
children.translated_text: wandered in the great forest — a terrible bird-catcher. // Panc_3.135 //

children.text: naiva kaścit suhṛt tasya na sambandhī na bāndhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: He had no friend at all, no relative, no kinsman;

children.text: sa taiḥ sarvaiḥ parityaktas tena raudreṇa karmaṇā ||Panc_3.136||
children.translated_text: he was abandoned by all of them because of his cruel deeds. // Panc_3.136 //

children.text: athavā-
children.translated_text: Or rather —

children.text: ye nṛśaṃsā durātmanaḥ prāṇināṃ prāṇa-nāśakāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are cruel, evil-souled, and destroyers of the lives of living beings —

children.text: udvejanīyā bhūtānāṃ vyālā iva bhavanti te ||Panc_3.137||
children.translated_text: they become, like serpents, sources of terror to all creatures. // Panc_3.137 //

children.text: sa pañjarakam ādāya pāśaṃ ca laguḍaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Taking his cage, his snare, and his club,

children.text: nityam eva vanaṃ yāti sarva-prāṇi-vihiṃsakaḥ ||Panc_3.138||
children.translated_text: he would go into the forest every day, a harmer of all living beings. // Panc_3.138 //

children.text: anyedyur bhramatas tasya vane kāpi kapotikā |
children.translated_text: One day, as he was wandering, a certain she-pigeon in the forest

children.text: jātā hasta-gatā tāṃ sa prākṣipat pañjcarāntare ||Panc_3.139||
children.translated_text: fell into his hands; he threw her into the cage. // Panc_3.139 //

children.text: atha kṛṣṇā diśaḥ sarvā vanasthasyābhavan ghanaiḥ
vāta-vṛṣṭiś ca mahato kṣaya-kāla ivābhavat ||Panc_3.140||
children.translated_text: and a great storm of wind and rain arose, as if it were the time of universal destruction. // Panc_3.140 //
Then all the directions became dark for the one [stranded] in the forest, due to clouds,

children.text: tataḥ sa trasta-hṛdayaḥ kampamāno muhur muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then he, his heart terrified, trembling again and again,

children.text: anveṣayan paritrāṇam āsasāda vanaspatim ||Panc_3.141||
children.translated_text: seeking shelter, found a great tree. // Panc_3.141 //

children.text: muhūrtaṃ paśyate yāvad viyad vimala-tārakam |
children.translated_text: For a moment he gazes at the sky, clear with stars,

children.text: prāpya vṛkṣaṃ vadaty evaṃ yo 'tra tiṣṭhati kaścana ||Panc_3.142||
children.translated_text: and having reached the tree, speaks thus: 'Whoever dwells here — // Panc_3.142 //

children.text: tasyāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptaḥ sa paritrātu mām iti |
children.translated_text: I have come to him for refuge; let him protect me.'

children.text: śītena bhidyamānaṃ ca kṣudhayā gata-cetanam ||Panc_3.143||
children.translated_text: His body was being split by cold, and his consciousness was gone from hunger. // Panc_3.143 //

children.text: atha tasya taroḥ skandhe kapotaḥ suciroṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, on a branch of that tree, a pigeon who had long dwelt there,

children.text: bhāryā-virahitas tiṣṭhan vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ ||Panc_3.144||
children.translated_text: separated from his wife, stood lamenting, deeply grieved: // Panc_3.144 //

children.text: vāta-varṣo mahān āsīn na cāgacchati me priyā |
children.translated_text: 'There was a great storm of wind and rain, and my beloved has not come;

children.text: tayā virahitaṃ hy etac chūnyam adya gṛhaṃ mama ||Panc_3.145||
children.translated_text: deprived of her, this home of mine is empty today. // Panc_3.145 //

children.text: pativratā pati-prāṇā patyuḥ priya-hite ratā |
children.translated_text: Devoted to her husband, her husband being her very life, delighting in what is dear and beneficial to her lord —

children.text: yasya syād īdṛśī bhāryā dhanyaḥ sa puruṣo bhuvi ||Panc_3.146||
children.translated_text: blessed is the man on earth who has such a wife. // Panc_3.146 //

children.text: na gṛhaṃ gṛham ity āhur gṛhiṇī gṛham ucyate |
children.translated_text: It is not the dwelling that is called a home — the housewife is called the home;

children.text: gṛhaṃ tu gṛhiṇī-hīnam araṇya-sadṛśaṃ matam ||Panc_3.147||
children.translated_text: a home without a housewife is considered like a wilderness.' // Panc_3.147 //

children.text: pañjara-sthā tataḥ śrutvā bhartur duḥkhānvitaṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the she-pigeon, from within the cage, hearing her husband's grief-laden words,

children.text: kapotikā susantuṣṭā vākyaṃ cedam athāha sā ||Panc_3.148||
children.translated_text: well-contented, spoke these words: // Panc_3.148 //

children.text: na sā strīty abhimantavyā yasyāṃ bhartā na tuṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'She is not to be regarded as a wife in whom the husband finds no satisfaction;

children.text: tuṣṭe bhartari nārīṇāṃ tuṣṭāḥ syuḥ sarva-devatāḥ ||Panc_3.149||
children.translated_text: when the husband is satisfied, all the deities are satisfied for women. // Panc_3.149 //

children.text: dāvāgninā vidagdheva sa-puṣpa-stavakā latā |
children.translated_text: Like a creeper with clusters of flowers scorched by a forest fire,

children.text: bhasmībhavatu sā nārī yasyāṃ bhartā na tuṣyati ||Panc_3.150||
children.translated_text: let that woman be reduced to ashes in whom the husband finds no satisfaction. // Panc_3.150 //

children.text: mitaṃ dadāti hi pitā mitaṃ bhrātā mitaṃ sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: A father gives in measure; a brother gives in measure; a son gives in measure;

children.text: amitasya hi dātāraṃ bhartāraṃ kā na pūjayet ||Panc_3.151||
children.translated_text: who would not honor the husband, the giver of the immeasurable? // Panc_3.151 //'

children.text: punaś cābravīt-
children.translated_text: And she said further —

children.text: śṛṇuṣvāvahitaḥ kānta yat te vakṣyāmy ahaṃ hitam |
children.translated_text: 'Listen attentively, dear husband, to what I shall tell you for your benefit:

children.text: prāṇair api tvayā nityaṃ saṃrakṣyaḥ śaraṇāgataḥ ||Panc_3.152||
children.translated_text: one who has come seeking refuge must always be protected, even at the cost of one's own life. // Panc_3.152 //

children.text: eṣa śākunikaḥ śete tavāvāsaṃ samāśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: This fowler lies here, having taken shelter in your abode;

children.text: śītārtaś ca kṣudhārtaś ca pūjām asmai samācara ||Panc_3.153||
children.translated_text: afflicted by cold and afflicted by hunger — show him hospitality. // Panc_3.153 //'

children.text: śrūyate ca-
children.translated_text: And it is heard —

children.text: yaḥ sāyam atithiṃ prāptaṃ yathā-śakti na pūjayet |
children.translated_text: 'He who does not honor, according to his ability, a guest arrived at evening —

children.text: tasyāsau duṣkṛtaṃ dattvā sukṛtaṃ cāpakarṣati ||Panc_3.154||
children.translated_text: that [guest] gives him his own bad deeds and takes away his good deeds. // Panc_3.154 //

children.text: mā cāsmai tvaṃ kṛthā dvaiṣaṃ baddhāneneti mat-priyā |
children.translated_text: And do not bear hatred toward him because he has bound me, your beloved;

children.text: sva-kṛtair eva baddhāhaṃ prāktanaiḥ karma-bandhanaiḥ ||Panc_3.155||
children.translated_text: I am bound by my own past deeds, by the bonds of prior <s>karma</s>. // Panc_3.155 //

children.text: dāridrya-roga-duḥkhāni bandhana-vyasanāni ca |
children.translated_text: Poverty, disease, sorrow, bondage, and calamity —

children.text: ātmāparādha-vṛkṣasya phalāny etāni dehinām ||Panc_3.156||
children.translated_text: these are the fruits of the tree of one's own transgressions for embodied beings. // Panc_3.156 //

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ dveṣam utsṛjya mad-bandhana-samudbhavam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, casting aside the hatred born from my captivity,

children.text: dharme manaḥ samādhāya pūjayainaṃ yathā-vidhi ||Panc_3.157||
children.translated_text: fix your mind on <s>dharma</s> and honor him according to the proper rites.' // Panc_3.157 //

children.text: tasyās tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā dharma-yukti-samanvitam |
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of hers, full of righteous reasoning,

children.text: upagamya tato 'dhṛṣṭaḥ kapotaḥ prāha lubdhakam ||Panc_3.158||
children.translated_text: the pigeon, humbly approaching, spoke to the fowler: // Panc_3.158 //

children.text: bhadra susvāgataṃ te'stu brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te |
children.translated_text: 'Good sir, welcome to you! Tell me, what shall I do for you?

children.text: santāpaś ca na kartavyaḥ sva-gṛhe vartate bhavān ||Panc_3.159||
children.translated_text: And do not grieve — you are in your own home.' // Panc_3.159 //

children.text: tasya tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā pratyuvāca vihaṅgamam |
children.translated_text: Hearing those words, [the fowler] replied to the bird:

children.text: kapota khalu śītaṃ me hima-trāṇaṃ vidhīyatām ||Panc_3.160||
children.translated_text: 'O pigeon, I am cold indeed — let protection from the frost be provided.' // Panc_3.160 //

children.text: sa gatvāṅgārakaṃ nītvā pātayāmāsa pāvakam |
children.translated_text: He went, brought a live ember, and made fire fall;

children.text: tataḥ śuṣkeṣu parṇeṣu tam āśu samadīpayat ||Panc_3.161||
children.translated_text: then, on the dry leaves, he quickly kindled it. // Panc_3.161 //

children.text: susandīptaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā tam āha śaraṇāgatam |
children.translated_text: Then, having made it blaze brightly, he said to the one who had come seeking refuge:

children.text: pratāpayasva viśrabdhaṃ sva-gātrāṇy atra nirbhayaḥ ||Panc_3.162||
children.translated_text: 'Warm your limbs confidently here, without fear. // Panc_3.162 //

children.text: udgatena ca jīvāmo vayaṃ sarve vanaukasaḥ |
children.translated_text: We who dwell in the forest live only on what grows [naturally];

children.text: na cāsti vibhavaḥ kaścin nāśaye yena te kṣudham ||Panc_3.163||
children.translated_text: I have no means at all by which I might relieve your hunger. // Panc_3.163 //

children.text: sahasraṃ bharate kaścic chatamanyo daśāparaḥ |
children.translated_text: One [man] supports a thousand; another, a hundred; yet another, ten;

children.text: mama tv akṛta-puṇyasya kṣudrasyātmāpi durbharaḥ ||Panc_3.164||
children.translated_text: but for me, of little merit and small [stature], even my own self is hard to sustain. // Panc_3.164 //

children.text: ekasyāpy atither annaṃ yaḥ pradātuṃ na śaktimān |
children.translated_text: He who is unable to give food even to a single guest —

children.text: tasyāneka-parikleśe gṛhe kiṃ vasataḥ phalam ||Panc_3.165||
children.translated_text: what fruit is there for him in dwelling in a household full of many afflictions? // Panc_3.165 //

children.text: tat tathā sādhayāmy etac charīraṃ duḥkha-jīvitam |
children.translated_text: So I shall dispose of this body of wretched life

children.text: yathā bhūyo na vakṣyāmi nāstīty arthi-samāgame ||Panc_3.166||
children.translated_text: in such a way that I shall never again say "I have nothing" when a supplicant comes.' // Panc_3.166 //

children.text: sa ninindi kilātmānaṃ na tu taṃ lubdhakaṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: He reproached himself but did not [reproach] that fowler again;

children.text: uvāca tarpayiṣye tvāṃ muhūrtaṃ pratipālaya ||Panc_3.167||
children.translated_text: [he] said: 'I shall satisfy you — wait but a moment.' // Panc_3.167 //

children.text: evam uktvā sa dharmātmā prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā |
children.translated_text: Having said this, that righteous soul, with a joyful inner spirit,

children.text: tam agniṃ samparikramya praviveśa sva-veśmavat ||Panc_3.168||
children.translated_text: circumambulated that fire and entered it as if it were his own home. // Panc_3.168 //

children.text: tatas taṃ lubdhako dṛṣṭvā kṛpayā pīḍito bhṛśam |
children.translated_text: Then the fowler, seeing the pigeon fallen into the fire,

children.text: kapotam agnau patitaṃ vākyam etad abhāṣata ||Panc_3.169||
children.translated_text: intensely afflicted with compassion, spoke these words: // Panc_3.169 //

children.text: yaḥ karoti naraḥ pāpaṃ na tasyātmā dhruvaṃ priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'A man who commits sin — surely his own self is not dear to him;

children.text: ātmanā hi kṛtaṃ pāpam ātmanaiva hi bhujyate ||Panc_3.170||
children.translated_text: for sin committed by the self is indeed suffered by the self alone. // Panc_3.170 //

children.text: so 'haṃ pāpa-matiś caiva pāpa-karma-rataḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: I am of sinful mind and always devoted to sinful deeds;

children.text: patiṣyāmi mahā-ghore narake nātra saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_3.171||
children.translated_text: I shall fall into a terrible hell — there is no doubt in this. // Panc_3.171 //

children.text: nūnaṃ mama nṛśaṃsasya pratyādarśaḥ sudarśitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Surely, a perfect example has been shown to me, a cruel wretch,

children.text: prayacchatā sva-māṃsāni kapotena mahātmanā ||Panc_3.172||
children.translated_text: by this great-souled pigeon offering his own flesh. // Panc_3.172 //

children.text: adya-prabhṛti dehaṃ svaṃ sarva-bhoga-vivarjitam |
children.translated_text: From this day forth, I shall desiccate this body of mine, devoid of all pleasures,

children.text: toyaṃ svalpaṃ yathā grīṣmaḥ śoṣayiṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ ||Panc_3.173||
children.translated_text: as summer [desiccates] a small [pool of] water. // Panc_3.173 //

children.text:
śīta-vātātapa-sahaḥ kṛśāṅgo malinas tathā |
upavāsair bahuvidhaiś cariṣye dharmam uttamam ||Panc_3.174|| tato yaṣṭiṃ śalākāṃ ca jālakaṃ pañjaraṃ tathā |
babhañja lubdhako dīnāṃ kāpotīṃ ca mumoca tām ||Panc_3.175||
children.translated_text: his net, and his cage, and released the pitiable she-pigeon. // Panc_3.175 //

Enduring cold, wind, and heat, with emaciated limbs, unwashed,
through many kinds of fasting I shall practice the highest <s>dharma</s>.' // Panc_3.174 // Then the fowler broke his staff, his snare-stick,

children.text: lubdhakena tato muktā dṛṣṭvāgnau patitaṃ patim |
children.translated_text: Then the she-pigeon, released by the fowler, seeing her husband fallen in the fire,

children.text: kapotī vilalāpārtā śoka-santapta-mānasā ||Panc_3.176||
children.translated_text: lamented piteously, her mind scorched with grief: // Panc_3.176 //

children.text: na kāryam adya me nātha jīvitena tvayā vinā |
children.translated_text: 'There is no purpose for me in life today without you, my lord;

children.text: dīnāyāḥ pati-hīnāyāḥ kiṃ nāryā jīvite phalam ||Panc_3.177||
children.translated_text: for a wretched woman deprived of her husband, what fruit is there in living? // Panc_3.177 //

children.text: māno darpas tv ahaṅkāraḥ kulaṃ pūjā ca bandhuṣu |
children.translated_text: Honor, pride, self-regard, family dignity, worship among kinsmen,

children.text: dāsa-bhṛtya-janeṣv ājñā vaidhavyena praṇaśyati ||Panc_3.178||
children.translated_text: and authority over servants and household — [all] perishes with widowhood.' // Panc_3.178 //

children.text: evaṃ vilapya bahuśaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ bhṛśa-duḥkhitā |
children.translated_text: Having lamented thus at length, pitifully, deeply grieved,

children.text: pativratā susandīptaṃ tam evāgniṃ viveśa sā ||Panc_3.179||
children.translated_text: that devoted wife entered that very fire, blazing brightly. // Panc_3.179 //

children.text: tato divyāmbara-dharā divyābharaṇa-bhūṣitā |
children.translated_text: Then, wearing celestial garments, adorned with celestial ornaments,

children.text: bhartāraṃ sā vimānasthaṃ dadarśa svaṃ kapotikā ||Panc_3.180||
children.translated_text: that she-pigeon beheld her husband seated in a celestial chariot. // Panc_3.180 //

children.text: so 'pi divya-tanur bhūtvā yathārtham idam abravīt |
children.translated_text: He too, having assumed a divine body, spoke these fitting words:

children.text: aho mām anugacchantyā kṛtaṃ sādhu śubhe tvayā ||Panc_3.181||
children.translated_text: 'Ah, O auspicious one, you have done well by following me! // Panc_3.181 //

children.text: tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdha-koṭī ca yāni romāṇi mānuṣe |
children.translated_text: Three and a half <s>koṭis</s> — as many as are the hairs on a human body —

children.text: tāvat kālaṃ vaset svarge bhartāraṃ yānugacchati ||Panc_3.182||
children.translated_text: for that many [years] does she who follows her husband dwell in heaven.' // Panc_3.182 //

children.text: kapota-dehaḥ sūryāste pratyahaṃ sukham anvabhūt |
children.translated_text: Every day until sunset, the one in the pigeon's body experienced happiness;

children.text: kapota-dehavatsāsīt prāk puṇya-prabhavaṃ hitam ||Panc_3.183||
children.translated_text: as one in the pigeon's body, from the power of former merit, there was prior blessing. // Panc_3.183 //

children.text: harṣāviṣṭas tato vyādho viveśa ca vanaṃ dhanam |
children.translated_text: Then the hunter, filled with elation, entered the forest

children.text: prāṇi-hiṃsāṃ parityajya bahu-nirvedavān bhṛśam ||Panc_3.184||
children.translated_text: and, abandoning the harming of living beings, became deeply disenchanted [with worldly life]. // Panc_3.184 //

children.text: tatra dāvānalaṃ dṛṣṭvā viveśa viratāśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: There, seeing a forest fire, he entered it, his desires extinguished;

children.text: nirdagdha-kalmaṣo bhūtvā svarga-saukhyam avāptavān ||Panc_3.185||
children.translated_text: having burned away his sins, he attained the bliss of heaven. // Panc_3.185 //

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-śrūyate hi kapotena (134) ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'It is heard that by a pigeon...' (verse 134) and so on.

children.text: tac chrutvārimardano dīptākṣaṃ pṛṣṭavān-evam avasthite kiṃ bhavān manyate ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Arimardana</s> asked <s>Dīptākṣa</s>: 'This being the case, what do you think?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! na hantavya evāyam | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Your Majesty! This one should certainly not be killed. For —'

children.text: yā mamodvijate nityaṃ sā mamādyāvagūhate |
children.translated_text: 'She who always shrinks from me now embraces me;

children.text: priya-kāraka bhadraṃ te yan mamāsti harasva tat ||Panc_3.186||
children.translated_text: O benefactor, blessings to you! Whatever I have, take it.' // Panc_3.186 //

children.text: coreṇa cāpy uktam-
children.translated_text: And the thief also said —

children.text: hartavyaṃ te na paśyāmi hartavyaṃ ced bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'I see nothing to take; but if there should be something to take,

children.text: punar apy āgamiṣyāmi yadīyaṃ nāvagūhate ||Panc_3.187||
children.translated_text: I shall come again, if she does not embrace [you].' // Panc_3.187 //

children.text: arimardanaḥ pṛṣṭavān-kā ca nāvagūhate ? kaś cāyaṃ cauraḥ ? iti vistarataḥ śrotum icchāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Arimardana</s> asked: 'And who is it that does not embrace? And who is this thief? I wish to hear in detail.'

children.text:
dīptākṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 8
kāmātura-vaṇik-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Dīptākṣa</s> narrates:
Story 8
The story of the desire-stricken merchant

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne kāmāturo nāma vṛddha-vaṇik | tena ca kāmopahṛta-cetasā, mṛta-bhāryeṇa kācin nirdhana-vaṇik-sutā, prabhūtaṃ dhanaṃ dattvodvāhitā | atha sā duḥkhābhibhūtā taṃ vṛddha-vaṇijaṃ draṣṭum api na śaśāka | yuktaṃ caitat-
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was an old merchant named <s>Kāmātura</s> (Desire-Stricken). He, with his mind overpowered by desire, being a widower, married a certain poor merchant's daughter by giving abundant wealth. Now she, overwhelmed with misery, could not bear even to look at that old merchant. And this is fitting:

children.text: śvetaṃ padaṃ śirasi yat tu śiroruhāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The white step [of grey hair] upon the head — that upon [one's] locks —

children.text: sthānaṃ paraṃ paribhavasya tad eva puṃsām |
children.translated_text: that is indeed the supreme seat of humiliation for men;

children.text: āropitāsthi-śakalaṃ parihṛtya yānti
children.translated_text: avoiding [him] as if a bone-fragment had been placed [on his head], young women flee

children.text: cāṇḍāla-kūpam iva dūrataraṃ taruṇyaḥ ||Panc_3.188||
children.translated_text: far away, as from a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>'s well. ||Panc_3.188||

children.text: tathā ca-
gātraṃ saṅkucitaṃ gatir vigalitā dantāś ca nāśaṅgatā
children.translated_text: The body shrunken, the gait unsteady, the teeth gone without return,

children.text: dṛṣṭir bhrāmyati rūpam apy upahataṃ vaktraṃ ca lālāyate |
children.translated_text: the vision wavering, the form decayed, the mouth drooling;

children.text: vākyaṃ naiva karoti bāndhava-janaḥ patnī na śuśrūṣate
children.translated_text: his words are disregarded by kinsmen, his wife does not serve [him],

children.text: dhik kaṣṭaṃ jarayābhibhūta-pūruṣaṃ putro 'py avajñāyate ||Panc_3.189||
children.translated_text: alas, the wretch! — a man overpowered by old age is treated with contempt even by his own son. ||Panc_3.189||
And also:

children.text: atha kadācit sā tena sahaikaśayane parāṅmukhī yāvat tiṣṭhati tāvad gṛhe cauraḥ praviṣṭaḥ | sāpi taṃ cauraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaya-vyākulitā vṛddham api taṃ patiṃ gāḍhaṃ samāliliṅga | so 'pi vismayāt pulakāñcita-sarva-gātraś cintayāmāsa-aho kim eṣā mām adyāvagūhate ? yāvan nipuṇatayā paśyati tāvat gṛha-koṇaika-deśe cauraṃ dṛṣṭvā vyacintayat-nūnam eṣāsya bhayān mām āliṅgati iti jñātvā taṃ cauram āha-yā mamodvijate (186) ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Then once, as she was lying with her back turned to him on their shared bed, a thief entered the house. She too, seeing that thief, agitated with fear, tightly embraced even that old husband. And he, his entire body thrilling with goosebumps from astonishment, thought: 'Ah, why does she embrace me today?' As he looked carefully, he saw the thief in a corner of the house and thought: 'Surely she embraces me out of fear of him.' Knowing this, he addressed the thief: 'She who is terrified of me...' (verse 186) and so on.

children.text: tac chrutvā cauro 'py āha-hartavyaṃ te na paśyāmi (187) ity ādi | tasmāc caurasyāpy upakāraḥ śreyaś cintyate kiṃ punaḥ śaraṇāgatasya | api cāyaṃ tair viprakṛto 'smākam eva puṣṭaye bhaviṣyati tadīya-randhra-darśanāya ceti anena kāraṇenāyam avadhya iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the thief too said: 'I see nothing worth taking from you...' (verse 187) and so on. Therefore, even a thief's benefit is to be considered as something good — how much more so that of one who has taken refuge! Moreover, this one [the crow <s>Sthirajīvī</s>], having been mistreated by them, will be useful for our growth and for revealing their weaknesses.' For this reason he should not be killed.

children.text: etad ākarṇyārimardano 'nyaṃ sacivaṃ vakranāsaṃ papraccha-bhadra ! sāmpratam evaṃ sthite kiṃ karaṇīyam iti ?
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Arimardana</s> asked another minister, <s>Vakranāsa</s>: 'Good sir! Now, things being thus, what should be done?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! avadhyo 'yam | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Your Majesty! This one should not be killed. Because:

children.text: śatravo 'pi hitārthaiva vivadantaḥ parasparam |
children.translated_text: Even enemies, disputing with each other, serve one's interest;

children.text: caureṇa jīvitaṃ dattaṃ rākṣasena tu go-yugam ||Panc_3.190||
children.translated_text: the thief gave [him] his life, and the <s>Rākṣasa</s> [gave him] a pair of oxen. ||Panc_3.190||

children.text: arimardanaḥ prāha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Arimardana</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
vakranāsaḥ kathayati-
kathā 10
droṇākhya-brāhmaṇa-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Vakranāsa</s> narrates:
Story 10
The story of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Droṇa</s>

children.text:
asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne daridro droṇa-nāmā brāhmaṇaḥ, pratigraha-dhanaḥ satataṃ viśiṣṭa-vastrānulepana-gandha-mālyālaṅkāra-tāmbūlādi-bhoga-parivarjitaḥ, prarūḍha-keśa-śmaśru-nakha-romopacitaḥ, śītoṣṇa-vāta-varṣādibhiḥ pariśoṣita-śarīraḥ, tasya ca kenāpi yajamānenānukampayā śiśu-go-yugaṃ dattam | brāhmaṇena ca bāla-bhāvād ārabhya yācita-ghṛta-taila-yavasādibhiḥ saṃvardhya supuṣṭaṃ kṛtam | tac ca dṛṣṭvā sahasaiva kaścic cauraś cintitavān-aham asya brāhmaṇasya go-yugam idam apahariṣyāmi | iti niścitya niśāyāṃ bandhana-pāśaṃ gṛhītvā, yāvat prasthitas tāvad ardha-mārge pravirala-tīkṣṇa-danta-paṅktir unnata-nāsā-vaṃśaḥ, prakaṭa-raktānta-nayanaḥ upacita-snāyu-santatanata-gātraḥ śuṣka-kapolaḥ
suhuta-hutavaha-piṅgala-śmaśru-keśa-śarīraḥ kaścid dṛṣṭaḥ | dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ tīvra-bhaya-trasto cauro 'bravīt-ko bhavān ? iti |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a poor <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Droṇa</s>, whose wealth was from gifts received. He was perpetually deprived of the enjoyment of fine garments, unguents, perfumes, garlands, ornaments, betel, and the like — his hair, beard, nails, and body-hair overgrown, his body dried out by cold, heat, wind, rain, and the rest. And a certain patron gave him, out of pity, a pair of young oxen. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, from their infancy onward, nourished them well with begged ghee, oil, fodder, and the like, and made them plump. Seeing that, a certain thief thought: 'I shall steal this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s pair of oxen.' Having resolved thus, at night, taking a binding-rope, as he set out — halfway along the road he saw someone with a sparse row of sharp teeth, a tall bridge of the nose, prominent blood-red eyes, a body stretched taut with sinews, hollow cheeks, and tawny beard, hair, and body — [colored] like well-kindled fire. Seeing him, the thief, terrified with intense fear, said: 'Who are you?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-ahaṃ krūra-karmā cauro daridra-brāhmaṇasya go-yugaṃ hartuṃ prasthito 'smi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'I am a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) named <s>Krūrakarmā</s> (Cruel-Doer). I have set out to steal the poor <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s pair of oxen.'

children.text: atha jāta-pratyayo rākṣaso 'bravīt-bhadra ! ṣaṣṭhāhna-kāliko 'ham | atas tam eva brāhmaṇam adya bhakṣayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, having gained confidence, said: 'Good sir! I eat [only] once every six days. Therefore I shall devour that very <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> today.'

children.text: atha tau tatra gatvaikānte kānlam anveṣayantau sthitau | prasupte ca brāhmaṇe tad-bhakṣaṇārthaṃ prasthitaṃ rākṣasaṃ dṛṣṭvā cauro 'bravīt-bhadra ! naiṣanyāyo yato go-yuge mayāpahṛte paścāt tvam enaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhakṣaya |
children.translated_text: Then the two went there and stood in a secluded spot, waiting for the right time. When the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was asleep and the <s>Rākṣasa</s> had set out to devour him, the thief said: 'Good sir! This is not right — first let me steal the pair of oxen, and afterwards you may devour this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-kadācid ayaṃ brāhmaṇo go-śabdena budhyeta tadānarthako 'yaṃ mamārambhaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: He said: 'If the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should wake up from the sound of the oxen, then my enterprise would be fruitless.'

children.text: cauro 'py abravīt-tavāpi yadi bhakṣaṇāyopasthitasya eko 'py antarāyaḥ syāt | tadāham api na śaknomi go-yugam apahartum | ataḥ prathamaṃ mayāpahṛte go-yuge paścāt tvayā brāhmaṇo bhakṣitavyaḥ | itthaṃ cāham ahamikayā tayor vivadatoḥ samutpanne dvaidhe pratirava-vaśād brāhmaṇo jajāgāra |
children.translated_text: The thief too said: 'And if there should be any obstacle to your devouring [him] as well, then I too would be unable to steal the oxen. Therefore, first let me steal the oxen, and afterwards you may devour the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' Thus, with [cries of] 'I first! I first!' — as the two disputed, a division arose between them. From the commotion of their altercation, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> awoke.

children.text: atha taṃ cauro 'bravīt-brāhmaṇa ! tvām evāyaṃ rākṣaso bhakṣayitum icchati iti |
children.translated_text: Then the thief said to him: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! This <s>Rākṣasa</s> here wishes to devour you!'

children.text: rākṣaso 'py āha-brāhmaṇa ! cauro 'yaṃ go-yugaṃ te'pahartum icchati |
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> too said: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! This thief here wishes to steal your pair of oxen!'

children.text: evaṃ śrutvotthāya brāhmaṇaḥ sāvadhāno bhūtveṣṭa-devatā-mantra-dhyānenātmānaṃ rākṣasād udgūrṇa-laguḍena caurād go-yugaṃ rarakṣa |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> rose, became alert, and through meditation on the <s>mantra</s> of his chosen deity protected himself from the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and with a raised cudgel [protected] his oxen from the thief.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-śatravo 'pi hitārthaiva (190) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Even enemies serve one's interest...' (verse 190).

children.text: atha tasya vacanam avadhāryārimardanaḥ punar api prākārakarṇam apṛcchat-kathaya, kim atra manyate bhavān ?
children.translated_text: Then, having considered his words, <s>Arimardana</s> asked yet another minister, <s>Prākārakarṇa</s>: 'Tell me, what does your lordship think in this matter?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! avadhya evāyam, yato rakṣitenānena kadācit paraspara-prītyā kālaḥ sukhena gacchati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Your Majesty! This one should indeed not be killed, because if protected by us, at some time, through mutual affection, time passes happily.' And it is said:

children.text: parasparasya marmāṇi ye na rakṣanti jantavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Creatures who do not guard each other's vital points —

children.text: ta eva nidhanaṃ yānti valmīkodara-sarpavat ||Panc_3.191||
children.translated_text: they go to destruction, like a serpent in the belly of an anthill. ||Panc_3.191||

children.text: arimardano 'bravīt-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Arimardana</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: prākārakarṇaḥ kathayati-
children.translated_text: <s>Prākārakarṇa</s> narrates:

children.text:
kathā 10
valmīkodara-gata-sarpa-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 10
The story of the serpent in the anthill's belly

children.text: asti kasmiṃścin nagare devaśaktir nāma rājā | tasya ca putro jaṭhara-valmīkāśrayeṇorageṇa pratidinaṃ pratyaṅgaṃ kṣīyate | anekopacāraiḥ sad-vaidyaiḥ sac-chāstropadiṣṭauṣadha-yuktyāpi cikitsyamāno na svāsthyam eti | athāsau rājaputro nirvedād deśāntaraṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain city there was a king named <s>Devaśakti</s>. His son was wasting away, limb by limb, day after day, because of a serpent dwelling in his stomach-anthill. Even when treated by good physicians with medicines prescribed by proper <s>śāstras</s> and many remedies, he did not regain his health. Then that prince, out of despair, went to another country.

children.text: kasmiṃścin nagare bhikṣāṭanaṃ kṛtvā mahati devālaye kālaṃ yāpayati | atha tatra nagare balir nāma rājāste | tasya ca dve duhitarau yauvana-sthe tiṣṭhataḥ | te ca pratidivasam ādityodaye pituḥ pādāntikam āgatya namaskāraṃ cakratuḥ | tatra caikābravīt-vijayasva mahārāja ! yasya prasādāt sarvaṃ sukhaṃ labhyate |
children.translated_text: In a certain city, having begged for alms, he passed his time in a great temple. Now in that city there was a king named <s>Bali</s>. He had two daughters who had reached the age of youth. They would come daily at sunrise to their father's feet and make obeisance. There, one said: 'May you be victorious, great king! By whose grace all happiness is obtained.'

children.text: dvitīyā tu-vihitaṃ bhuṅkṣva mahārāja ! iti bravīti |
children.translated_text: The second, however, said: 'Enjoy what is ordained, great king!'

children.text: tac chrutvā prakupito rājābravīt-bho mantriṇaḥ ! enāṃ duṣṭa-bhāṣiṇīṃ kumārikāṃ kasyacid vaideśikasya prayacchata tena nija-vihitam iyam eva bhuṅkte |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king said angrily: 'O ministers! Give this wicked-speaking girl to some foreigner, so that she may enjoy what her own fate has ordained!'

children.text: atha tatheti pratipadyālpa-parivārā sā kumārikā mantribhis tasya deva-kulāśrita-rāja-putrasya pratipāditā | sāpi prahṛṣṭa-manasā taṃ patiṃ devavat pratipadyādāya cānya-viṣayaṃ gatā |
children.translated_text: Then, accepting this with 'So be it,' the ministers gave that princess, with a small retinue, to that prince who had taken refuge in the temple. And she, with a delighted mind, received that husband like a god, took him, and went to another territory.

children.text: tataḥ kasmiṃścid dūratara-nagara-pradeśe taḍāga-taṭe rāja-putram āvāsa-rakṣāyai nirūpya svayaṃ ca ghṛta-taila-lavaṇa-taṇḍulādi-kraya-nimittaṃ sa-parivārā gatā | kṛtvā ca kraya-vikrayaṃ yāvad āgacchati tāvat sa rāja-putro valmīkopari kṛta-mūrdhā prasuptaḥ | tasya ca mukhād bhujagaḥ phaṇāṃ niṣkāsya vāyum aśnāti | tatraiva ca valmīke'paraḥ sarpo niṣkramya tathaivāsīt |
children.translated_text: Then, in a certain distant city, having settled the prince at a tank's bank for the protection of their dwelling, she herself went with her retinue to purchase ghee, oil, salt, rice, and the like. After buying and selling, as she was returning, the prince had fallen asleep with his head resting upon the anthill. From his mouth, a serpent had extended its hood and was breathing the air. And right there, in that same anthill, another serpent had emerged and was sitting likewise.

children.text: atha tayoḥ paraspara-darśanena krodha-saṃrakta-locanayor madhyād valmīkasthena sarpeṇoktam-bho bho durātman ! kathaṃ sundara-sarvāṅgaṃ rāja-putram itthaṃ kadarthayasi ?
children.translated_text: Then, the two — their eyes reddened with anger at the sight of each other — from between them, the anthill-dwelling serpent said: 'Ho, ho, wicked one! How do you thus torment this handsome prince, beautiful in all his limbs?'

children.text: mukhastho 'rir abravīt-bho bhoḥ ! tvayāpi durātmanāsya valmīkasya madhye katham idaṃ dūṣitaṃ hāṭaka-pūrṇaṃ kalaśa-yugalam ity evaṃ parasparasya marmāṇy udghāṭitavantau |
children.translated_text: The mouth-dwelling enemy said: 'Ho, ho! And you, wicked one — how do you corrupt this anthill in whose midst are two jars full of gold?' Thus the two exposed each other's vital secrets.

children.text: punar valmīkastho 'hir abravīt-bho durātman ! bheṣajam idaṃ te kiṃ ko 'pi na jānāti yaj jīrṇotkālita-kāñjikā-rājikā-pānena bhavān vināśam upayāti |
children.translated_text: Again the anthill-dwelling serpent said: 'Ho, wicked one! Does no one know this remedy of yours? — that by drinking soured gruel boiled with mustard, you would be destroyed!'

children.text: athodarastho 'hir abravīt-tavāpy etad bheṣajaṃ kiṃ kaścid api na vetti yad uṣṇa-tailena mahoṣṇodakena vā tava vināśaḥ syād iti | evaṃ ca sā rāja-kanyā viṭapāntaritā tayoḥ parasparālāpān marma-mayān ākarṇya tathaivānuṣṭhitavatī |
children.translated_text: Then the belly-dwelling serpent said: 'And does no one know this remedy of yours? — that by hot oil or very hot water, your destruction would come about!' And thus the princess, hidden behind a tree-trunk, heard these mutual revelations of vital secrets and acted accordingly.

children.text: vidhāya vyaṅgaṃ nīrogaṃ bhartāraṃ nidhiṃ ca paramam āsādya svadeśābhimukhaṃ prāyāt | pitṛ-mātṛ-svajanaiḥ pratipūjitā vihitopabhogaṃ prāpya sukhenāvasthitā | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-parasparasya marmāṇi iti |
children.translated_text: Having cured her husband and rendered [him] free of disease, and having obtained a supreme treasure, she set out toward her own country. Honored by her parents, relatives, and kin, she attained the enjoyment that was ordained and lived in happiness. Therefore I say: 'Those who guard each other's vital points...'

children.text: tac ca śrutvā svayam arirdano 'py evaṃ samarthitavān | tathā cānuṣṭhitam | dṛṣṭvāntar-līnaṃ vihasya raktākṣaḥ punar abravīt-kaṣṭam | vināśito 'yaṃ bhavadbhir anyāyena svāmī | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Arimardana</s> himself agreed thus. And it was so carried out. Seeing [the crow <s>Sthirajīvī</s>] hidden within [their ranks], <s>Raktākṣa</s> laughed and said again: 'Terrible! This master of yours has been unjustly destroyed by you all.' And it is said:

children.text: apūjyā yatra pūjyante pūjyānāṃ tu vimānanā |
children.translated_text: Where the unworthy are honored and the worthy are disrespected —

children.text: trīṇi tatra pravartante durbhikṣaṃ maraṇaṃ bhayam ||Panc_3.192||
children.translated_text: three things prevail there: famine, death, and fear. ||Panc_3.192||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: pratyakṣe'pi kṛte pāpe mūrkhaḥ sāmnā praśāmyati |
children.translated_text: Even when a sin has been committed in plain sight, the fool is pacified by sweet words;

children.text: ratha-kāraḥ svakāṃ bhāryāṃ sajārāṃ śirasāvahat ||Panc_3.193||
children.translated_text: the chariot-maker carried his own wife, together with her paramour, upon his head. ||Panc_3.193||

children.text: mantriṇaḥ prāhuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The ministers said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
raktākṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 11
vīravara-rathakāra-tat-patnī-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Raktākṣa</s> narrates:
Story 11
The story of the hero <s>Vīravara</s>, the chariot-maker, and his wife

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne vīravaro nāma rathakāraḥ | tasya bhāryā kāmadamanī | sā puṃścalī janāpavāda-saṃyuktā | so 'pi tasyāḥ parīkṣaṇārthaṃ vyacintayat-atha mayāsyāḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ kartavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a chariot-maker named <s>Vīravara</s>. His wife was <s>Kāmadamanī</s>. She was an unchaste woman, linked with public reproach. And he, in order to test her, thought: 'Now I should test her.' And it is said:

children.text: yadi syāt pāvakaḥ śītaḥ proṣṇī vā śaśa-lāñchanaḥ |
children.translated_text: If fire were cold, or the hare-marked Moon were hot,

children.text: strīṇāṃ tadā satītvaṃ syād yadi syād durjano hitaḥ ||Panc_3.194||
children.translated_text: then women would be chaste — and then a wicked person would be kind. ||Panc_3.194||

children.text: jānāmi caināṃ loka-vacanād asatīm | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'I know her to be unchaste from public rumor.' And it is said:

children.text: yac ca vedeṣu śāstreṣu na dṛṣṭaṃ na ca saṃśrutam |
children.translated_text: What is not seen in the <s>Vedas</s> or in the <s>śāstras</s>, what is not heard of [there] —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ vetti loko 'yaṃ yat syād brahmāṇḍa-madhyagam ||Panc_3.195||
children.translated_text: all that this world knows — whatever exists within the egg of <s>Brahmā</s> (the universe). ||Panc_3.195||

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya bhāryām avocat-priye ! prabhāte'haṃ grāmāntaraṃ yāsyāmi | tatra katicid dināni lagiṣyanti | tat tvayā kim api pātheyaṃ mama yogyaṃ vidheyam |
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, he said to his wife: 'Dear one! At dawn I shall go to another village. It will take some days there. So you must prepare some suitable provisions for my journey.'

children.text: sāpi tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā harṣita-cittā | autsukyāt sarva-kāryāṇi santyajya siddham annaṃ ghṛta-śarkarā-prāyam akarot | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: And she, hearing his words, with a delighted mind, abandoning all other tasks out of eagerness, prepared cooked food, rich in ghee and sugar. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: durdivase ghana-timire varṣati jalade mahāṭavī-prabhṛtau |
children.translated_text: On a foul day, in dense darkness, when the rain-cloud pours down, in a great forest and the like,

children.text: patyur videśa-gamane parama-sukhaṃ jaghana-capalāyāḥ ||Panc_3.196||
children.translated_text: and [especially] when the husband goes abroad — that is the supreme happiness of a woman fickle in the hips. ||Panc_3.196||

children.text: athāsau pratyūṣe utthāya sva-gṛhān nirgataḥ sāpi taṃ prasthitaṃ vijñāya prahasita-vadanāṅga-saṃskāraṃ kurvāṇā kathañcit taṃ divasam atyavāhayat | atha pūrva-paricita-viṭa-gṛhe gatvā taṃ pratyuktavatī-sa durātmā me patir grāmāntaraṃ gataḥ | tat tvayāsmad-gṛhe prasupte jane samāgantavyam |
children.translated_text: Then he, rising at dawn, left his house. And she, knowing him to have departed, with a smiling face, adorning her limbs, somehow passed that day. Then, going to the house of a rake she had known before, she told him: 'That wicked husband of mine has gone to another village. So you must come to my house when the household is asleep.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite sa rathakāro 'raṇye dinam ativāhya pradoṣe sva-gṛhe'padvāreṇa praviśya śayyādhas-tale nibhṛto bhūtvā sthitaḥ | etasminn antare sa devadattaḥ samāgatya tatra śayane upaviṣṭaḥ | dṛṣṭvā roṣāviṣṭa-citto rathakāro vyacintayat-kim enam utthāya hanmi ? athavā helayaiva prasuptau dvāv apy etau vyāpādayāmi ? paraṃ paśyāmi tāvad asyāś ceṣṭitam | śṛṇomi cānena sahālāpam |
children.translated_text: When this had been done, the carpenter, having spent the day in the forest, entered his own house at nightfall by a back door and, hiding beneath the bed, remained still. In the meanwhile, that <s>Devadatta</s> arrived and sat upon the bed. The carpenter, seeing this, his mind filled with rage, thought: 'Should I rise and kill him? Or shall I casually destroy both of them while they are asleep? But let me first observe her conduct and listen to her conversation with him.'

children.text: atrāntare sā gṛha-dvāraṃ nibhṛtaṃ pidhāya śayana-talam ārūḍhā | tasyās tatrārohayantyā rathakāra-śarīre pādo vilagnaḥ | tataḥ sā vyacintayat-nūnam etena durātmanā rathakāreṇa mat-parīkṣaṇārthaṃ bhāvyam | tataḥ strī-caritra-vijñānaṃ kim api karomi |
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile, she quietly bolted the front door and climbed onto the bed. As she was climbing up, her foot touched the carpenter's body. Then she thought: 'Surely this wicked carpenter must be here to test me.' So she performed some feminine stratagem.

children.text: evaṃ tasyāś cintayanyā sa devadattaḥ sparśotsuko babhūva | atha tayā kṛtāñjali-puṭayābhihitaṃ-bhoḥ mahānubhāva ! na me śarīraṃ tvayā sparśanīyaṃ yato 'haṃ pativratā mahāsatī ca | no cec chāpaṃ dattvā tvāṃ bahsmasātkariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: While she was thinking thus, that <s>Devadatta</s> became eager to touch her. Then she, with palms joined in supplication, said: 'O noble sir! My body must not be touched by you, for I am devoted to my husband and a great chaste woman. Otherwise, I shall curse you and reduce you to ashes!'

children.text: sa āha-yady evaṃ tarhi tvayā kim aham āhūtaḥ ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'If so, then why have you summoned me?'

children.text: sābravīt-bhoḥ śṛṇuṣvaikāgra-manāḥ | aham adya pratyūṣe devatā-darśanārthaṃ caṇḍkāyatanaṃ gatā tatrākasmāt khe vāṇī sañjātā-putri kiṃ karomi ? bhaktāsi me tvaṃ, paraṃ ṣaṇmāsābhyantare vidhi-niyogād vidhavā bhaviṣyasi |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Noble sir, listen with undivided attention. Today at dawn I went to the temple of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> to see the deity. There suddenly a voice arose from the sky: "Daughter, what shall I do? You are my devotee, but within six months, by the decree of fate, you will become a widow."'

children.text: tato mayābhihitaṃ-bhagavati ! yathā tvam āpadaṃ vetsi, tathā tat-pratīkāram api jānāsi | tad asti kaścid upāyo yena me patiḥ śata-saṃvatsara-jīvī bhavati ?
children.translated_text: 'Then I said: "Goddess! Just as you know the calamity, so too you know its remedy. Is there some means by which my husband may live a hundred years?"'

children.text: tatas tayābhihitam-vatse, sann api nāsti, yatas tavāyattaḥ sa pratīkāraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Then she said: "Child, there is [a means], yet there is not — because that remedy depends upon you."'

children.text: tac chrutvā mayābhihitam-devi ! yadi tan mama prāṇair bhavati tad ādeśaya yena karomi |
children.translated_text: 'Hearing that, I said: "Goddess! If it can be done even at the cost of my life, then command me, and I shall do it."'

children.text: atha devyābhihitam-yady adya para-puruṣeṇa sahaikasmin śayane samāruhyāliṅganaṃ karoṣi tat tava bhartṛ-sakto 'pamṛtyus tasya sañcarati | bhartāpi tena punar varṣa-śataṃ jīvati | tena tvaṃ mayābhyarthitaḥ | tad yat kiñcit kartu-manās tat kuruṣva | na hi devatā-vacanam anyathā bhaviṣyatīti niścayaḥ | tato 'ntarhāsa-vikāsa-mukhaḥ sa tad-ucitam ācacāra |
children.translated_text: 'Then the goddess said: "If today you climb onto a bed with another man and embrace him, then the untimely death attached to your husband will pass to that man, and your husband will live another hundred years." Therefore you were summoned by me. So whatever you intend to do, do it. For there is certainty that the word of a deity will not prove otherwise.' Then he, his face blooming with a suppressed smile, performed what was appropriate to that [situation].

children.text: so 'pi rathakāro mūrkhas tasyās tad-vacanam ākarṇya pulakāñcita-tanuḥ śayyādhastalān niṣkramya tām uvāca-sādhu pativrate ! sādhu kula-nandini ! ahaṃ durjana-vacana-śaṅkita-hṛdayas tvat-parīkṣā-nimittaṃ grāmāntara-vyājaṃ kṛtvā khaṭvādhas-tale nibhṛtaṃ līnaḥ | tad ehi, āliṅga mām | tvaṃ sva-bhartṛ-bhaktānāṃ mukhyā nārīṇāṃ, yad evaṃ brahma-vrataṃ para-saṅge'pi pālitavatī | yad āyur buddhi-kṛte'pamṛtyu-vināśārthaṃ catvam evaṃ kṛtavatī | tām evam uktvā sasneham āliṅgitavān |
children.translated_text: And that fool of a carpenter, hearing her words, his body thrilling with horripilation, came out from beneath the bed and said to her: 'Well done, O devoted wife! Well done, O joy of the family! I, my heart suspicious because of wicked men's words, hid secretly beneath the bed under the pretense of going to another village, in order to test you. So come, embrace me! You are the foremost among women devoted to their husbands, since you have observed your sacred vow [of chastity] even in the company of another man — since for the sake of destroying the untimely death [looming over] my allotted lifespan, you have done this.' Having spoken thus to her, he embraced her with affection.

children.text: sva-skandhe tām āropya tām api devadattam uvāca-bho mahānubhāva ! mat-puṇyais tvam ihāgataḥ | tvat-prasādān mayā prāptaṃ varṣa-śata-pramāṇam āyuḥ | tat tvam api mām āliṅgya mat-skandhe samāroha iti jalpann anicchantam api devadattam āliṅgya balāt svakīya-skandhe āropitavān |
children.translated_text: Mounting her upon his own shoulder, he also said to <s>Devadatta</s>: 'O noble sir! By my merit you have come here. By your grace I have obtained a lifespan of a hundred years. So you too, embrace me and mount upon my shoulder!' — thus babbling, he embraced the unwilling <s>Devadatta</s> and forcibly mounted him upon his own shoulder.

children.text: tataś ca nṛtyaṃ kṛtvā-he brahma-vrata-dharāṇāṃ dhurīṇa ! tvayāpi mayy upakṛtam ity ādy uktvā skandhād uttārya yatra yatra svajana-gṛha-dvārādiṣu babhrāma tatra tatra tayor ubhayor api tad-guṇa-varṇanam akarot |
children.translated_text: Then, having danced, [saying:] 'O foremost among observers of the sacred vow! You too have done me a kindness!' — and speaking such things, having set him down from his shoulder, wherever he wandered — to the houses and doors of his kinsmen — everywhere he proclaimed the virtues of those two.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-pratyakṣe'pi kṛte pāpe (193) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Even when sin is committed before one's very eyes...' [and so on]. (193)

children.text: tat sarvathā mūlotkhātā vayaṃ vinaṣṭāḥ smaḥ | suṣṭhu khalv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'In every way, we are uprooted and destroyed. Well indeed is this said:'

children.text: mitra-rūpā hi ripavaḥ sambhāvyante vicakṣaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Enemies in the guise of friends are to be expected by the discerning —

children.text: ye hitaṃ vākyam utsṛjya viparītopasevinaḥ ||Panc_3.197||
children.translated_text: those who abandon salutary counsel and serve the opposite. // Panc_3.197 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: santo 'py arthā vinaśyanti deśa-kāla-virodhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even good policies come to ruin when opposed to [proper] place and time,

children.text: aprājñān mantriṇaḥ prāpya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ||Panc_3.198||
children.translated_text: having fallen to unwise ministers — like darkness at sunrise. // Panc_3.198 //

children.text: tatas tad-vaco 'nādṛtya sarve te sthirajīvinam utkṣipya sva-durgam ānetum ārabdhāḥ | athānīyamānaḥ sthirajīvy āha-deva ! adyākiñcitkareṇaitad avasthena kiṃ mayopasaṅgṛhītena ? yat kāraṇam icchāmi dīptaṃ vahnim anupraveṣṭum | tad arhasi mām agni-pradānena samuddhartum |
children.translated_text: Then, disregarding his words, they all lifted up <s>Sthirajīvī</s> and began to carry him to their own fortress. And <s>Sthirajīvī</s>, being carried, said: 'Sire! Now in my present powerless condition, what use am I to you? The reason is: I wish to enter blazing fire. So please save me by granting me fire.'

children.text: atha raktākṣasyāntargata-bhāvaṃ jñātvāha-kim-artham agni-patanam icchasi ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Raktākṣa</s>, understanding his hidden intention, said: 'For what reason do you wish to fall into fire?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-ahaṃ tāvad yuṣmad-artham imām āpadaṃ meghavarṇena prāpitaḥ | tad icchāmi teṣāṃ vaira-yātanārtham ulūkatvam iti |
children.translated_text: He said: 'I was brought to this calamity by <s>Meghavarṇa</s> for your sake. So I wish to be reborn as an owl, for the purpose of repaying my enmity against them.'

children.text: tac ca śrutvā rājanīti-kuśalo raktākṣaḥ prāha-bhadra ! kuṭilas tvaṃ kṛtaka-vacana-caturaś ca | tāvad ulūka-yoni-gato 'pi svakīyām eva vāyasa-yoniṃ bahu manyase | śrūyate caitad ākhyānakam |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Raktākṣa</s>, skilled in royal policy, said: 'Friend! You are crooked and clever in crafting false speech. Even when born in owl-form, you would still esteem your own crow-birth.' And this tale is heard:

children.text: sūryaṃ bhartāram utsṛjya parjanyaṃ mārutaṃ girim |
children.translated_text: Abandoning the Sun as husband, and the Rain-cloud, the Wind, the Mountain —

children.text: sva-jātiṃ mūṣikā prāptā svajātir duratikramā ||Panc_3.199||
children.translated_text: the mouse-maiden attained her own species; one's own species is hard to transcend. // Panc_3.199 //

children.text: mantriṇaḥ procuḥ--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The ministers said: 'How is that?'

children.text: raktākṣaḥ kathayati-
children.translated_text: <s>Raktākṣa</s> narrates:

children.text:
kathā 11
śālaṅkāyana-rakṣita-mūṣikā-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 11
The story of the mouse protected by <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne śālaṅkāyano nāma tapodhano jāhnavyāṃ snānārthaṃ gataḥ | tasya ca sūryopasthānaṃ kurvatas tatra pradeśe mūṣikā kācit kharatara-nakhāgra-puṭena śyenena gṛhītā | dṛṣṭvā sa muniḥ karuṇārdra-hṛdayo muñca muñceti kurvāṇas tasyopari pāṣāṇa-khaṇḍaṃ prākṣipat | so 'pi pāṣāṇa-khaṇḍa-prahāra-vyākulendriyo bhraṣṭa-mūṣiko bhūmau nipapāta mūṣikāpi bhaya-trastā kartavyam ajānantī rakṣa rakṣeti jalpantī muni-caraṇāntikam upāviśat | śyenenāpi cetanaṃ labdhvā munir ukto, yad-bho mune ! na yuktam anuṣṭhitaṃ bhavatā yad ahaṃ pāṣāṇena tāḍitaḥ | kiṃ tvam adharmān na bibheṣi ? tat samarpaya mām enām mūṣikām | no cet prabhūtaṃ pātakam avāpsyasi |
children.translated_text: In a certain town, an ascetic named <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s> went to the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges) for his bath. While he was performing his worship of the sun, in that very spot a certain mouse was seized by a hawk with sharp claw-tips. Seeing this, that sage, his heart moist with compassion, crying 'Release! Release!', hurled a stone-fragment at it. That [hawk], its senses bewildered by the blow of the stone, dropped the mouse and fell to the ground. The mouse too, terrified with fear, not knowing what to do, crying 'Save me! Save me!', sat down at the sage's feet. Then the hawk, having regained consciousness, said to the sage: 'Ho, sage! What you have done is not proper — that you struck me with a stone. Do you not fear <s>adharma</s>? So hand over this mouse to me. Otherwise you shall incur a great sin.'

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ śyenaṃ provāca saḥ-bho vihaṅgādhama ! rakṣaṇīyāḥ prāṇināṃ prāṇāḥ | daṇḍanīyā duṣṭāḥ | sammānanīyāḥ sādhavaḥ | pūjanīyā guravaḥ | stutyā devāḥ | tat kim asambaddhaṃ prajalpasi ?
children.translated_text: He [the sage] said to the hawk who was speaking thus: 'O vilest of birds! The lives of living beings must be protected. The wicked must be punished. The virtuous must be honored. Teachers must be worshipped. Gods must be praised. So why do you babble irrelevantly?'

children.text: śyena āha-mune ! na tvaṃ sūkṣma-dharmaṃ vetsi | iha hi sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ vidhinā sṛṣṭiṃ kurvatāhāro 'pi vinirmitaḥ | tato yathā bhavatām annaṃ tathāsmākaṃ mūṣikādayo vihitāḥ | tat svāhāra-kāṅkṣiṇaṃ māṃ kiṃ dūṣayasi ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The hawk said: 'O sage! You do not know the subtle <s>dharma</s>. For the Creator, in creating all living beings, also fashioned their food. Just as grain is [ordained] for you, so mice and the like are ordained for us. So why do you blame me who merely desires my own food? And it is said:'

children.text: yady asya vihitaṃ bhojyaṃ na tat tasya praduṣyati |
children.translated_text: If food has been ordained for a creature, eating it is not sinful;

children.text: abhakṣye bahu-doṣaḥ syāt tasmāt kāryo na vyatyayaḥ ||Panc_3.200||
children.translated_text: but in [eating] what is not [ordained as] food, there is much sin — therefore no reversal should be made. // Panc_3.200 //

children.text: bhakṣyaṃ yathā dvijātīnāṃ madyapānāṃ yathā haviḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as [certain things] are food for the twice-born, just as <s>havis</s> (oblation) [is proper] for those who drink <s>soma</s> —

children.text: abhakṣyaṃ bhakṣyatām eti tathānyeṣām api dvija ||Panc_3.201||
children.translated_text: so too what is [normally] not food becomes food for others, O twice-born. // Panc_3.201 //

children.text: bhakṣyaṃ bhakṣyatāṃ śreya abhakṣyaṃ tu mahad agham |
children.translated_text: Eating what is [one's ordained] food brings well-being; [eating] what is not food brings great sin.

children.text: tat kathaṃ māṃ vṛthācāra tvaṃ daṇḍayitum arhasi ||Panc_3.202||
children.translated_text: So how can you, O one of vain conduct, presume to punish me? // Panc_3.202 //

children.text: aparaṃ munīnāṃ na caiṣa dharmo yatas tair dṛṣṭaṃ śrutam aśrutam alaulyatvam aśatrutvaṃ praśasyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, this is not the <s>dharma</s> of sages, for by them equanimity, freedom from greed, and freedom from enmity toward the seen, heard, and unheard are praised. And it is said:'

children.text: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Equal toward foe and friend, equal toward clod, stone, and gold,

children.text: suhṛn-mitre hy udāsīno madhyastho dveṣya-bandhuṣu |
children.translated_text: toward well-wishers, friends, neutrals, mediators, and enemies and kinsmen —

children.text: sādhuṣv api ca pāpeṣu sama-buddhir viśiṣyate ||Panc_3.203||
children.translated_text: he who is of equal mind toward the virtuous and the wicked is distinguished. // Panc_3.203 //

children.text: sādhūnāṃ niravadyānāṃ sadācāra-vicāriṇām |
yogī yuñjīta satataṃ satatam ātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ ||Panc_3.204|
children.translated_text: a <s>yogī</s> should constantly engage his mind, stationed in solitude. // Panc_3.204 //
Of the virtuous, the blameless, those observing righteous conduct —

children.text: tat tvam anena karmaṇā bhraṣṭa-tapāḥ sañjātaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, by this action of yours, your austerity has fallen. And it is said:'

children.text: muñca muñca pataty eko mā muñceti dvitīyakaḥ |
children.translated_text: One says 'Release! Release!' — and his [washed cloth] falls; the second says 'Don't release!' —

children.text: ubhayoḥ patanaṃ dṛṣṭvā maunaṃ sarvārtha-sādhanam ||Panc_3.205||
children.translated_text: seeing the fall of both, silence is the accomplisher of all purposes. // Panc_3.205 //

children.text: śālaṅkāyana āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
śyena āha-
kathā 12
?
children.translated_text:
The hawk said:
Story 12

children.text: kasmiṃścid nadī-taṭa ekata-dvita-tritābhidhānās trayo 'pi bhrātaro munayas tapaḥ kurvanti | teṣāṃ ca tapaḥ-prabhāvād ākāśasthā dhauta-potikā nirālambā jalārdrā bhū-sparśana-bhayena snāna-samaye tiṣṭhanti | athānye-dyur mamaiva kācin maṇḍūkikā kenāpi gṛdhreṇa balena nītā | atha tāṃ gṛhītā vilokya teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhena karuṇārdra-hṛdayena bhavateva vyāhṛtaṃ-muñca muñceti | atrāntare tasya dhauta-potikākāśād bhūmau patitā | tāṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā dvitīyena tad-bhayārtena mā muñcety abhihitaṃ yāvat tasyāpi papāta | tatas tṛtīyo dvayor api dhauta-potikāṃ bhūmau patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: On a certain riverbank, three brother-sages named <s>Ekata</s>, <s>Dvita</s>, and <s>Trita</s> perform austerities. By the power of their austerities, their washed garments remain in the sky, unsupported, wet with water, without touching the ground, during their bathing time [for fear of touching the earth]. Now, on another day, a certain frog of mine was carried away by force by some vulture. Seeing it seized, the eldest of them, his heart moist with compassion — just like you — cried 'Release! Release!' Immediately his washed garment fell from the sky to the ground. Seeing it fallen, the second, frightened by that [event], said 'Don't release!' — whereupon his [garment] too fell. Then the third, seeing the washed garments of both fallen to the ground, remained silent.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-muñca muñca pataty eka ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'One says "Release! Release!" and his falls...' and so on.

children.text: tac chrutvā munir vihasyāha-bho mūrkha vihaṅgama ! kṛta-yuge dharmaḥ sa āsīt, yataḥ kṛta-yuge pāpālāpato 'pi pāpaṃ jāyate tena dhauta-potike patite aśiṣṭālāpena na sad-apavacana-doṣataḥ | eṣa punaḥ kali-yugaḥ | atra sarvo 'pi pāpātmā | tat karma kṛtaṃ vinā pāpaṃ na lagati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the sage laughed and said: 'O foolish bird! That <s>dharma</s> existed in the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> (Golden Age), because in the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> sin arises even from sinful speech — therefore the washed garments fell from [mere] improper utterance, not from the fault of insulting a virtuous person. But this is the <s>Kali Yuga</s>. Here everyone is sinful. Therefore, sin does not attach without [actual] sinful action performed. And it is said:'

children.text: sañcarantīha pāpāni yugeṣv anyeṣu dehinām |
children.translated_text: In other ages, the sins of embodied beings merely wander about [without attaching];

children.text: kalau tu pāpa-saṃyukte yaḥ karoti sa lipyate ||Panc_3.206||
children.translated_text: but in the <s>Kali</s> [age], joined with sin — only he who performs [the act] is stained. // Panc_3.206 //

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: āsanāc chayanād yānāt saṃgateś cāpi bhojanāt |
children.translated_text: From sitting, lying, riding, association, and eating together —

children.text: kṛte sañcarate pāpaṃ taila-bindur ivāmbhasi ||Panc_3.207||
children.translated_text: in the <s>Kṛta</s> [age], sin is transmitted like a drop of oil on water. // Panc_3.207 //

children.text: tat kiṃ vṛthā pralapitena ? gaccha tvam | no cec chāpayiṣyāmi | atha gate śyene mūṣikayā sa munir abhihitaḥ-bhagavan ! naya māṃ svāśrayam | no ced anyo duṣṭa-pakṣī māṃ vyāpādayiṣyati | tad ahaṃ tatraivāśrame tvad-dattānnāhāra-muṣṭyā kālaṃ neṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: 'So enough with vain prattle! Go! Otherwise I shall curse you.' Then, when the hawk had departed, the mouse said to the sage: 'Sir! Take me to a safe refuge. Otherwise some other wicked bird will kill me. I shall pass my time in your very hermitage, sustained by a morsel of food given by you.'

children.text: so 'pi dākṣiṇyavān sa-karuṇo vyacintayat-kathaṃ mayā mūṣikā haste dhṛtvā neyā jana-hāsya-kāriṇī | tad enāṃ kumārikāṃ kṛtvā nayāmi | evaṃ sā kanyakā kṛtā | tathānuṣṭhite kanyā-sahitaṃ munim avalokya patnī papraccha-bhagavan ! kuta iyaṃ kanyā ?
children.translated_text: And he, being courteous and compassionate, thought: 'How can I carry a mouse in my hand — it would make people laugh. So let me transform her into a girl and take her.' Thus she was made into a maiden. When this was done, his wife, seeing the sage accompanied by a girl, asked: 'Sir! Whence is this girl?'

children.text: sa āha-eṣā mūṣikā śyena-bhayāc charaṇārthinī kanyā-rūpeṇa tava gṛham ānītā | tat tvayā yatnena rakṣaṇīyā | bhūyo 'py enāṃ mūṣikāṃ kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'This is a mouse who, fearing a hawk, sought refuge — brought to your house in the form of a girl. She must be protected by you with care. In time, I shall make her a mouse again.'

children.text: sā prāha-bhagavan ! maivaṃ kārṣīḥ | asyās tvaṃ dharma-pitā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: She said: 'Sir! Do not do so. You are her father by <s>dharma</s>. And it is said:'

children.text: janitā copanetā ca yas tu vidyāṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: The begetter, the one who performs the investiture, the one who imparts learning,

children.text: anna-dātā bhaya-trātā pañcaite pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ ||Panc_3.208||
children.translated_text: the giver of food, the savior from fear — these five are remembered as fathers. // Panc_3.208 //

children.text: tat tvayāsyāḥ prāṇa-pradattā | aparaṃ mamāpy apatyaṃ nāsti | tasmād eṣā mama sutā bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'For you have given her life. Moreover, I have no offspring. Therefore she shall be my daughter.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite sā kanyā śukla-pakṣa-candra-kalikeva nityaṃ vṛddhiṃ prāpnoti | sāpi tasya muneḥ śuśrūṣāṃ kurvatī sapatnīkasya yauvanam āśv ayāt | atha tāṃ yauvanonmukhīm avalokya śālaṅkāyanaḥ sva-patnīm uvāca-priye ! yauvanonmukhī vartata iyaṃ kanyā | anarhā sa sāmprataṃ mad-gṛha-vāsasya | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: When this was done, that girl, like the crescent moon of the bright fortnight, grew constantly. And she, serving that sage and his wife, quickly reached youth. Then, seeing her approaching womanhood, <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s> said to his wife: 'Dear one! This girl is approaching womanhood. She is no longer worthy of dwelling in my house now.' And it is said —

children.text: anūḍhā mandire yasya rajaḥ prāpnoti kanyakā |
children.translated_text: He in whose house an unmarried maiden reaches her menses —

children.text: patanti pitaras tasya svarga-sthā api tair guṇaiḥ ||Panc_3.209||
children.translated_text: his ancestors fall [from heaven], even though they dwell in heaven, by those sins. [Panc 3.209]

children.text: varaṃ varayate kanyā mātā vittaṃ pitā śrutam |
children.translated_text: The maiden chooses the groom's form; the mother [values] wealth; the father, learning;

children.text: bāndhavāḥ kulam icchanti miṣṭānnam itare janāḥ ||Panc_3.210||
children.translated_text: relatives desire lineage; and other people [want] fine food [at the wedding feast]. [Panc 3.210]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: yāvan na lajjate kanyā yāvat krīḍati pāṃsunā |
children.translated_text: While the maiden is not yet bashful, while she still plays in the dust,

children.text: yāvat tiṣṭhati go-mārge tāvat kanyāṃ vivāhayet ||Panc_3.211||
children.translated_text: while she still walks in the cow-path — until then one should arrange the maiden's marriage. [Panc 3.211]

children.text: mātā caiva pitā caiva jyeṣṭha-bhrātā tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The mother, the father, and the eldest brother —

children.text: trayas te narakaṃ yānti dṛṣṭvā kanyāṃ rajasvalām ||Panc_3.212||
children.translated_text: these three go to hell if they see the maiden [reach her] menses [unmarried]. [Panc 3.212]

children.text: kulaṃ ca śīlaṃ ca sanāthatāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Lineage, character, nobility,

children.text: vidyāṃ ca vittaṃ ca vapur vayaś ca |
children.translated_text: learning, wealth, beauty, and age —

children.text: etān guṇān saptān sapta parīkṣya deyā
children.translated_text: examining these seven qualities, the wise should give the maiden;

children.text: kanyā budhaiḥ śeṣam acintanīyam ||Panc_3.213||
children.translated_text: the rest is not to be considered. [Panc 3.213]

children.text: tad yad yasyā rocate tad bhagavantaṃ ādityam ākārya tasmai prayacchāmi | uktaṃ ca-
aniṣṭaḥ kanyakāyā yo varo rūpānvito 'pi yaḥ |
children.translated_text: A groom who is unwanted by the maiden — even if he be handsome —

children.text: yadi syāt tasya no deyā kanyā śreyo 'bhivāñchatā ||Panc_3.214||
children.translated_text: to him the maiden should not be given by one who desires her welfare. [Panc 3.214]
'So let me summon the blessed <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) and give her to whomever she likes.' And it is said —

children.text: sā prāha-ko doṣo 'tra viṣaye ? evaṃ kriyatām |
children.translated_text: She said: 'What fault is there in this matter? Let it be done so.'

children.text: atha muninā ravir āhūtaḥ | veda-mantrāmantraṇa-prabhāvāt tat-kṣaṇād evābhyupagamyādityaḥ provāca-bhagavan ! vada drutaṃ kim-artham āhūtaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then the sage summoned the Sun. By the power of <s>Vedic</s> <s>mantras</s>, <s>Āditya</s> came at that very moment and said: 'Venerable one! Speak quickly — for what purpose have I been summoned?'

children.text: sa āha-eṣā madīyā kanyakā tiṣṭhati | yady eṣā tvāṃ vṛṇoti tarhy udvahasva tām iti | evam uktvā bhagavāṃs tasyā darśitaḥ | provāca-putri ! kiṃ tava rocata eṣa bhagavāṃs trailokya-dīpaḥ ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'Here stands this maiden of mine. If she chooses you, then marry her.' Having said this, the blessed one was shown to her. He said: 'Daughter! Does this blessed one, the lamp of the three worlds, please you?'

children.text: sā prāha-tāta ! atidahanātmako 'yam | nāham enam abhilaṣāmi | asmād api ya utkṛṣṭataraḥ sa āhūyatām |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Father! He is of an extremely burning nature. I do not desire him. Let someone even superior to him be summoned.'

children.text: atha tasyās tad-vacanam ākarṇya bhāsvaro 'pi tāṃ mūṣikāṃ viditvā niḥspṛhas tam uvāca-bhagavan ! asti mamāpy adhiko megho yenācchāditasya me nāmāi na jñāyate ?
children.translated_text: Then, hearing her words, <s>Bhāsvara</s> (the Sun) too, knowing her to be [originally] a mouse, said without longing: 'Venerable one! Is there one greater even than me — the cloud, by whom when I am covered, even my name is not known?'

children.text: atha muninā megham apy āhūya kanyābhihitā-eṣa te rocate ?
children.translated_text: Then the sage, having summoned the cloud too, said to the maiden: 'Does this one please you?'
