children.text: sā prāha-kṛṣṇa-varṇo 'yaṃ jaḍātmā ca | tad asmād anyasya kasyacit pradhānasya māṃ prayaccha |
children.translated_text: She said: 'He is dark-colored and dull of nature. So give me to some other eminent one.'

children.text: atha muninā megho 'pi pṛṣṭaḥ-bhoḥ ! tvatto 'py adhikaḥ ko 'py asti ?
children.translated_text: Then the sage asked the cloud: 'Sir! Is there anyone greater even than you?'

children.text: sa āha-matto 'py adhiko 'sti vāyuḥ | vāyunā hato 'haṃ sahasradhā yāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Greater even than me is the wind. Struck by the wind, I am scattered in a thousand pieces.'

children.text: tac chrutvā muninā vāyur āhūtaḥ, āha ca-putrike kim eṣa vāyus te vivāhāya uttamaḥ pratibhāti ?
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the sage summoned the wind and said: 'Little daughter, does this wind seem to you the best for marriage?'

children.text: sā āha-prabalo 'py ayaṃ cañcalaḥ | tad abhyadhikaḥ kaścid āhūyatām |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Though he is powerful, he is fickle. So let someone superior be summoned.'

children.text: munir āha-bho vāyo ! tvatto 'py adhiko 'sti kaścit ?
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'O Wind! Is there anyone greater even than you?'

children.text: sa āha-matto 'py adhiko 'sti parvato yena saṃstabhya balavān apy ahaṃ dhriye |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Greater even than me is the mountain, by whom I am held in check, powerful though I am.'

children.text: atha muniḥ parvatam āhūya kanyāyā adarśayat-putrike ! tvām asmai prayacchāmi ?
children.translated_text: Then the sage summoned the mountain and showed him to the maiden: 'Little daughter! Shall I give you to this one?'

children.text: sā āha-tāta ! kaṭhinātmako 'yaṃ stabdhaś ca | tad anyasmai dehi mām |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Father! He is hard by nature and stiff. So give me to another.'

children.text: atha sa muninā pṛṣṭaḥ, yad-bhoḥ parvata-rāja ! tvatto 'py adhiko 'sti kaścit ?
children.translated_text: Then the sage asked him: 'O king of mountains! Is there anyone greater even than you?'

children.text: sa āha-santi matto 'py adhikā mūṣikāḥ, ye mad-dehaṃ balāt sarvato bhedayanti |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Greater even than me are the mice, who forcefully burrow through my body from all sides.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya munir mūṣakam āhūya tasyā adarśayat-putrike ! eṣa te pratibhāti mūṣaka-rājo yena yathocitam anuṣṭhīyate | sāpi taṃ dṛṣṭvā sva-jātīya eṣa iti manyamānā pulakodbhūṣita-śarīrā provāca-tāta ! māṃ mūṣikāṃ kṛtvāsmai prayaccha yena svajāti-vihitaṃ gṛha-dharmam anutiṣṭhāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the sage summoned a mouse and showed him to her: 'Little daughter! Does this king of mice please you, so that proper arrangements may be made?' And she, seeing him, thinking 'he is of my own kind,' her body thrilling with goosebumps, said: 'Father! Make me into a mouse-maiden and give me to him, so that I may fulfill the household duties proper to my own species.'

children.text: tac chrutvā tena strī-dharma-vicakṣaṇena tāṃ mūṣikāṃ kṛtvā mūṣakāya pradattā |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, he, skilled in the laws of womanhood, transformed her into a mouse-maiden and gave her to the mouse.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-sūryaṃ bhartāram utsṛjya ityādi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Rejecting the Sun as husband...' and so on.

children.text: atha raktākṣa-vacanam anādṛtya taiḥ sva-vaṃśa-vināśāya sa sva-durgam upanītaḥ | nīyamānaś cāntar-līnam avahasya sthirajīvy acintayat-
children.translated_text: Then, disregarding the words of <s>Raktākṣa</s> (Red-eye), they brought that one [the crow <s>Sthirajīvī</s>] into their own fortress — for the destruction of their own race. And <s>Sthirajīvī</s>, being carried inside, laughed inwardly and thought:

children.text: hanyatām iti yenoktaṃ svāmino hita-vādinā |
children.translated_text: He who spoke 'Let him be killed' — a well-wisher speaking for his master's benefit —

children.text: sa evaiko 'tra sarveṣāṃ nīti-śāstrārtha-tattva-vit ||Panc_3.215||
children.translated_text: he alone among all these is the knower of the true meaning of the science of statecraft. [Panc 3.215]

children.text: tad yadi tasya vacanam acariṣyann ete, tato na svalpo 'py anartho 'bhaviṣyad eteṣām |
children.translated_text: 'If these had followed his advice, then not even the slightest harm would have befallen them.'

children.text: atha durga-dvāraṃ prāpyārimardano 'bravīt-bho bho hitaiṣiṇo 'sya sthirajīvino yathā-samīhitaṃ sthānaṃ prayacchata |
children.translated_text: Then, upon reaching the fortress gate, <s>Arimardana</s> (Enemy-crusher) said: 'Ho! You well-wishers of this <s>Sthirajīvī</s>, give him a place as he desires.'

children.text: tac ca śrutvā sthirajīvī vyacintayat-mayā tāvad eteṣāṃ vadhopāyaś cintanīyaḥ | sa mayā madhyasthena na sādhyate | yato madīyam iṅgitādikaṃ vicārayantas te'pi sāvadhānā bhaviṣyanti | tad durga-dvāram adhiśrito 'bhipretaṃ sādhayāmi | iti niścityolūka-patim āha-deva ! yuktam idaṃ yat svāminā proktam | param aham api nītijñas te'hitaś ca | yadyapy anuraktaḥ śucis tathāpi durga-madhye āvāso nārhaḥ | tad ahaṃ atraiva durga-dvāra-sthaḥ pratyahaṃ bhavat-pāda-padma-rajaḥ pavitrī-kṛta-tanuḥ sevāṃ kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Sthirajīvī</s> thought: 'Now I must devise the means of their destruction. That cannot be accomplished by me from the inside. Because, observing my gestures and such, they too will become cautious. So, stationed at the fortress gate, I shall accomplish my purpose.' Having resolved thus, he said to the owl-king: 'Lord! What the master has said is proper. But I too know statecraft and am devoted to you. Though I am loyal and pure, I do not deserve to dwell inside the fortress. So I shall remain here at the fortress gate, my body purified daily by the dust of your lotus-feet, and perform service.'

children.text: tatheti pratipanne pratidinam ulūka-pati-sevakās te prakāmam āhāraṃ kṛtvolūka-rājādeśāt prakṛṣṭa-māṃsāhāraṃ sthirajīvine prayacchanti | atha katipayair evāhobhir mayūra iva sa balavān saṃvṛttaḥ | atha raktākṣaḥ sthirajīvinaṃ poṣyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa-vismayo mantri-janaṃ rājānaṃ ca praty āha-aho mūrkho 'yaṃ mantri-jano bhavāṃś cety evam aham avagacchāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: When this was agreed to, the servants of the owl-king daily, after eating abundantly, would give <s>Sthirajīvī</s> excellent meat-food by the owl-king's order. Then in just a few days, like a peacock, he became powerful. Then <s>Raktākṣa</s>, seeing <s>Sthirajīvī</s> being fattened, said with astonishment to the ministers and the king: 'Ah, these ministers and you too are fools — this is my understanding.' And it is said —

children.text: pūrvaṃ tāvad ahaṃ mūrkho dvitīyaḥ paśu-bandhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: First I was a fool; second, the bird-catcher;

children.text: tato rājā ca mantrī ca sarvaṃ vai mūrkha-maṇḍalam ||Panc_3.216||
children.translated_text: then the king and the minister — the whole circle is foolish. [Panc 3.216]

children.text: te prāhuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: They said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
raktākṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 13
svarṇa-ṣṭhīvī-sindhuka-pakṣī-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Raktākṣa</s> narrates:
Story 13
The Story of the Gold-Spitting <s>Sindhuka</s> Bird

children.text:
asti kasmiṃścit parvataika-deśe mahān vṛkṣaḥ | tatra ca sindhuka-nāmā ko 'pi pakṣī prativasati sma | tasya purīṣe suvarṇam utpadyate | atha kadācit tam uddiśya vyādhaḥ ko 'pi samāyayau | sa ca pakṣī tad-agrata eva purīṣam utsasarja | atha pāta-sama-kālam eva tat-suvarṇībhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyādho vismayam agamat-aho mama śiśu-kālād ārabhya śakuni-bandha-vyasanino 'śīti-varṣāṇi samabhūvan,na ca kadācit pakṣi-purīṣe suvarṇaṃ dṛṣṭam iti vicintya tatra vṛkṣe pāśaṃ babandha | athāsāv api pakṣī mūrkhas tatraiva viśvasta-citto yathā-pūrvam upaviṣṭas tat-kālam eva pāśena baddhaḥ | vyādhas tu taṃ pāśād unmucya pañjarake saṃsthāpya nijāvāsaṃ nītavān | atha cintayāmāsa-kim anena sāpāyena pakṣiṇāhaṃ kariṣyāmi ? yadi kadācit ko
'py amum īdṛśaṃ jñātvā rājñe nivedayiṣyati tan nūnaṃ prāṇa-saṃśayo me bhavet | ataḥ svayam eva pakṣiṇaṃ rājñe nivedayāmi | iti vicārya tathaivānuṣṭhitavān |
children.translated_text: On a certain mountain-slope there was a great tree. There lived a certain bird named <s>Sindhuka</s>. Gold was produced in his droppings. Once, a certain hunter came in search of him. That bird dropped its excrement right in front of him. Seeing it turn to gold the very moment it fell, the hunter was astonished: 'In my eighty years since childhood spent in the pursuit of catching birds, I have never seen gold in bird-droppings!' Thinking thus, he set a snare on that tree. And that foolish bird, trusting as before, sat on that very spot and was immediately caught in the snare. The hunter, freeing him from the snare, placed him in a cage and carried him to his own dwelling. Then he thought: 'What shall I do with this dangerous bird? If someday someone discovers his nature and reports it to the king, then surely my life will be in danger. So I myself shall present the bird to the king.' Having thus deliberated, he did exactly so.

children.text: atha rājāpi taṃ pakṣiṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikasita-nayana-vadana-kamalaḥ parāṃ tuṣṭim upagataḥ | prāha caivaṃ-haṃho rakṣā-puruṣāḥ ! enaṃ pakṣiṇaṃ yatnena rakṣata | aśana-pānādikaṃ cāsya yathecchaṃ prayacchata |
children.translated_text: Then the king too, seeing that bird, his eyes and lotus-face blooming with delight, attained supreme satisfaction. And he said: 'Ho, guardsmen! Guard this bird with care. Give him food and drink as he pleases.'

children.text: atha mantriṇābhihitam-kim anenāśraddheya-vyādha-vacana-mātra-parigṛhītenāṇḍajena ? kiṃ kadācit pakṣī-purīṣe suvarṇaṃ sambhavati ? tan mucyatāṃ pañjara-bandhanād ayaṃ pakṣī | iti mantri-vacanād rājñā mocito 'sau pakṣy unnata-dvāra-toraṇe samupaviśya suvarṇa-mayīṃ viṣṭhāṃ vidhāya-pūrvaṃ tāvad ahaṃ mūrkhaḥ iti ślokaṃ paṭhitvā yathā-sukham ākāśa-mārgeṇa prāyāt |
children.translated_text: Then the minister said: 'What [use is] this creature, accepted merely on the unreliable words of a hunter? Does gold ever come from bird-droppings? So let this bird be freed from the cage.' By the minister's words, the king released that bird. And that bird, perching on the high arch of the gateway, produced golden excrement and, reciting the verse 'First I was a fool...', departed at will through the sky.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-pūrvaṃ tāvad ahaṃ mūrkhaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'First I was a fool...' and so on.

children.text: atha te punar api pratikūla-daivatayā hitam api raktākṣa-vacanam anādṛtya bhūyas taṃ prabhūta-māṃsādi-vividhāhāreṇa poṣayāmāsuḥ | atha raktākṣaḥ sva-vargam āhūya rahaḥ provāca-aho ! etāvad evāsmad-bhūpateḥ kuśalaṃ durgaṃ ca | tad upadiṣṭaṃ mayā yat kula-kramāgataḥ sacivo 'bhidhatte | tad vayam anyat parvata-durgaṃ samprati samāśrayāmaḥ | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then they, due to adverse fate, again disregarding the beneficial words of <s>Raktākṣa</s>, continued to feed him abundant meat and various foods. Then <s>Raktākṣa</s>, summoning his own faction in secret, said: 'Ah! This much is [left of] our king's well-being and fortress. What I had advised is what the hereditary minister declares. So let us now take refuge in another mountain-fortress.' And it is said —

children.text: anāgataṃ yaḥ kurute sa śobhate
children.translated_text: He who provides against the future shines;

children.text: sa śocate yo na karoty anāgatam |
children.translated_text: he who does not provide against the future grieves.

children.text: vane vasann eva jarām upāgato
children.translated_text: Having grown old dwelling in the forest,

children.text: bilasya vācā na kadāpi hi śrutā ||Panc_3.217||
children.translated_text: the voice of the burrow was never heard [again]. [Panc 3.217]

children.text: te procuḥ-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: They said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
raktākṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 14
kharanakhara-siṃha-kathā
children.translated_text:
<s>Raktākṣa</s> narrates:
Story 14
The Story of the Lion <s>Kharanakhara</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe kharanakharo nāma siṃhaḥ prativasati sma | sa kadācid itaś cetaś ca paribhraman kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭho na kiñcid api sattvam āsasāda | tataś cāstam anasamaye mahatīṃ giri-guhām āsādya praviṣṭaś cintayāmāsa-nūnam etasyāṃ guhāyāṃ rātrau kenāpi sattvenāgantavyam | tan nibhṛto bhūtvā tiṣṭhāmi |
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there lived a lion named <s>Kharanakhara</s> (Sharp-claws). Once, wandering here and there, his throat parched with hunger, he could not find any creature at all. Then, at sunset, reaching a great mountain-cave, he entered it and thought: 'Surely some creature must come to this cave at night. So I shall remain hidden and wait.'

children.text: etasminn antare tat-svāmī dadhipuccho nāma śṛgālaḥ samāyātaḥ | sa ca yāvat paśyati tāvat siṃha-pada-paddhatir guhāyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ, na ca niṣkrāntā iti dṛṣṭavān | tataś cācintayat-aho vinaṣṭo 'smi, nūnam asyāntargatena siṃhena bhāvyam | tat kiṃ karomi ? kathaṃ jñāsyāmi ? evaṃ vicintya dvārasthaḥ phūtkartum ārabdhaḥ-aho bila ! aho bila ! ity uktvā tūṣṇīṃbhūya bhūyo 'pi tathaiva pratyabhāṣata-bhoḥ ! kiṃ na smarasi yan mayā tvayā saha samayaḥ kṛto 'sti ? yan mayā bāhyāt samāgatena tvaṃ vaktavyaḥ, tvayā cāham ākaraṇīyaḥ iti | tad yadi māṃ nāhvayasi tato 'haṃ dvitīyaṃ bilaṃ yāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: In the meantime, its owner, a jackal named <s>Dadhipuccha</s> (Curd-tail), arrived. As he looked, he saw the tracks of a lion entering the cave but not coming out. Then he thought: 'Ah, I am doomed! Surely there must be a lion inside. So what shall I do? How shall I ascertain this?' Thinking thus, standing at the entrance, he began to call out: 'Ho cave! Ho cave!' Having said this and remaining silent, he spoke again in the same way: 'Sir! Do you not remember the agreement you and I made? That when I come from outside, I am to call to you, and you are to call back to me? So if you do not call me, I shall go to another burrow!'

children.text: atha tac chrutvā siṃhaś cintitavān-nūnam eṣā guhāsya samāgatasya sadā samāhvānaṃ karoti | param adya mad-bhayān na kiṃcid brūte | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that, the lion thought: 'Surely this cave always calls back to him when he comes. But today, out of fear of me, it says nothing. Or rather, this is well said —'

children.text: bhaya-santrasta-manasāṃ hasta-pādādikāḥ kriyāḥ |
children.translated_text: For those whose minds are stricken with fear, the actions of hands, feet, and such

children.text: pravartante na vāṇī ca vepathuś cādhiko bhavet ||Panc_3.218||
children.translated_text: do not function, nor does speech — and trembling becomes excessive. [Panc 3.218]

children.text: tad aham asyāhvānaṃ karomi yena tad-anusāreṇa praviṣṭo 'yaṃ me bhojyatāṃ yāsyati | evaṃ sampradhārya siṃhas tasyāhvānam akarot | atha siṃha-śabdena sā guhā pratirava-sampūrṇā anyān api dūra-sthān araṇya-jīvāṃs trāsayāmāsa | śṛgālo 'pi palāyamāna imaṃ ślokam apaṭhat-anāgataṃ yaḥ kurute sa śobhate ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall call out to him, so that following my call he will enter and become my meal. Having thus deliberated, the lion let out his call. Then that cave, filled with the reverberating echo of the lion's roar, terrified even other forest creatures standing far away. The jackal too, as he fled, recited this verse: 'He who acts with foresight shines forth,' and so on.

children.text: tad evaṃ matvā yuṣmābhir mayā saha gantavyam iti | evam abhidhāyātmānuyāyi-parivārānugato dūra-deśāntaraṃ raktākṣo jagāma |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having considered this, you must all come with me. Having said this, <s>Raktākṣa</s> (Red-Eye), accompanied by his retinue of followers, departed to a far-distant land.

children.text: atha raktākṣe gate sthirajīvy atihṛṣṭa-manā vyacintayat-aho ! kalyāṇam asmākam upasthitam, yad raktāṃśo gataḥ sa dīrghadarśī ete ca mūḍha-manasaḥ | tato mama sukha-ghātyāḥ sañjātāḥ | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Now when <s>Raktākṣa</s> had gone, <s>Sthirajīvī</s> (Steady-Liver), his mind exceedingly delighted, reflected: Ah! Good fortune has arrived for us, since <s>Raktākṣa</s>, that far-sighted one, has departed, and these remaining ones are dull-witted. Thus they have become easy prey for me. And it is said:

children.text: na dīrgha-darśino yasya mantriṇaḥ syur mahīpateḥ |
children.translated_text: A king whose ministers are not far-sighted,

children.text: kramāyātā dhruvaṃ tasya na cirāt syāt parikṣayaḥ ||Panc_3.219||
children.translated_text: for him, ruin that has been gradually approaching will surely come before long. [Panc 3.219]

children.text: athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is well said:

children.text: mantri-rūpā hi ripavaḥ sambhāvyās te vicakṣaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are in the guise of ministers but are actually enemies should be suspected by the wise,

children.text: ye santaṃ nayam utsṛjya sevante pratilomataḥ ||Panc_3.220||
children.translated_text: who, abandoning sound policy, serve in a contrary manner. [Panc 3.220]

children.text: evaṃ vicintya sva-kulāya ekaikāṃ vana-kāṣṭhikāṃ guhā-pradīpanārthaṃ dine dine prakṣipati | na ca te mūrkhā ulūkā vijānanti, yad eṣa kulāyam asmad-dāhāya vṛddhiṃ nayati | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, he threw one stick of forest wood each day into his nest for the purpose of setting the cave ablaze. But those foolish owls did not realize that he was enlarging his nest for the purpose of burning them. Or rather, this is well said:

children.text: amitraṃ kurute mitraṃ mitraṃ dveṣṭi hinasti ca |
children.translated_text: He makes an enemy his friend, hates and harms his own friend,

children.text: śubhaṃ vetty aśubhaṃ pāpaṃ bhadraṃ daiva-hato naraḥ ||Panc_3.221||
children.translated_text: regards what is auspicious as inauspicious — such is a man whom fate has doomed. [Panc 3.221]

children.text: atha kulāya-vyājena durga-dvāre kṛte kāṣṭha-nicaye, sañjāte sūryodaye, andhatāṃ prāpteṣūlūkeṣu satsu sthirajīvī śīghram ṛṣyamūkaṃ gatvā meghavarṇam āha-svāmin ! dāha-sādhyā kṛtā ripu-guhāḥ | tat saparivāraḥ sametyaikaikā vana-kāṣṭhikāṃ jvalantī gṛhītvā guhā-dvāre'smat-kulāye prakṣipa yena sarve śatravaḥ kumbhīpāka-naraka-prāyeṇa duḥkhena mriyante |
children.translated_text: Now, when a pile of wood had been amassed at the fortress entrance under the pretext of a nest, and when the sun had risen and the owls had become day-blind, <s>Sthirajīvī</s> swiftly went to <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s> and said to <s>Meghavarṇa</s>: My lord! The enemy's fortress has been made ready for burning. Therefore, come with your retinue, each one taking a burning stick of forest wood and cast it upon my nest at the cave entrance, so that all the enemies may die a death as painful as the <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> (cauldron) hell.

children.text: tac chrutvā prahṛṣṭo meghavarṇa āha-tāta ! kathayātma-vṛttāntam | cirād adya dṛṣṭo 'si |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the delighted <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: Father! Tell me of your experiences. It has been so long since I last saw you.

children.text: sa āha-vatsa ! nāyaṃ kathanasya kālaḥ | yataḥ kadācit tasya ripo kaścit praṇidhir mamehāgamanaṃ nivedayiṣyati | yaj jñānād andho 'nyatrāpasaraṇaṃ kariṣyati | tat tvaryatām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He replied: My son! This is not the time for storytelling. For at some point, some spy of that enemy may report my arrival here, and upon learning of it, that blind one may flee elsewhere. Therefore make haste! It is said:

children.text: śīghra-kṛtyeṣu kāryeṣu vilambayati yo naraḥ |
children.translated_text: The man who delays in matters requiring swift action,

children.text: tat kṛtyaṃ devatās tasya kopād vighnanty asaṃśayam ||Panc_3.222||
children.translated_text: the gods, in their anger, will surely obstruct his undertaking. [Panc 3.222]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: yasya yasya hi kāryasya phalitasya viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Of any task, especially one that has come to fruition,

children.text: kṣipram akriyamāṇasya kālaḥ pibati tat-phalam ||Panc_3.223||
children.translated_text: if not carried out quickly, time drinks up its reward. [Panc 3.223]

children.text: tad-guhāyām āyātasya te hata-śatroḥ sarvaṃ savistaraṃ nirvyākulatayā kathayiṣyāmi athāsau tad-vacanam ākarṇya sa-parijana ekaikāṃ jvalantīṃ vana-kāṣṭhikāṃ cañcv-agreṇa gṛhītvā tad-guhā-dvāraṃ prāpya sthirajīvi-kulāye prākṣipat | tataḥ sarve te divāndhā raktākṣa-vākyāni smaranto dvārasyāvṛtatvād aniḥsaranto guhā-madhye kumbhīpāka-nyāyam āpannā mṛtāś ca | evaṃ śatrūn niḥśeṣatāṃ nītvā bhūyo 'pi meghavarṇas tad eva nyagrodha-pādapa-durgaṃ jagāma | tataḥ siṃhāsana-stho bhūtvā sabhā-madhye pramudita-manāḥ sthirajīvinam apṛcchat-tāta ! kathaṃ tvayā śatru-madhye gatena etāvat-paryantaṃ kālo nītaḥ ? tad atra kautukam asmākaṃ vartate, tat kathyatām | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: When you have returned from that cave with your enemies slain, I shall narrate everything to you in full detail and at ease. Then, hearing his words, <s>Meghavarṇa</s> together with his retinue, each one grasping a burning forest stick in the tip of his beak, reached the entrance of that cave and cast it upon <s>Sthirajīvī</s>'s nest. Thereupon all those day-blind owls, remembering the words of <s>Raktākṣa</s>, unable to escape because the entrance was blocked, met with a fate like that of the <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> (cauldron) hell inside the cave and perished. Having thus annihilated the enemies completely, <s>Meghavarṇa</s> once again returned to the very same fortress in the banyan tree. Then, seated upon his throne in the midst of the assembly, his mind filled with joy, he asked <s>Sthirajīvī</s>: Father! How did you, dwelling among the enemy, endure all that time? We are most curious about this; please tell us. For:

children.text: vara-magnau pradīpte tu prapātaḥ puṇya-karmaṇām |
children.translated_text: Better to plunge into fire or leap from a precipice — such is the way of the righteous —

children.text: na cārijana-saṃsargo muhūrtam api sevitaḥ ||Panc_3.224||
children.translated_text: than to endure the company of enemies even for a moment. [Panc 3.224]

children.text: tad ākarṇya sthirajīvy āha-bhadra ! āgāmi-phala-vāñchayā kaṣṭam api sevako na jānāti | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Sthirajīvī</s> said: Dear one! In the hope of future reward, a servant does not even feel hardship. And it is said:

children.text: kāryasyāpekṣayā bhuktaṃ viṣam apy amṛtāyate |
children.translated_text: Even poison, when consumed for the sake of a goal, becomes <s>amṛta</s> (nectar),

children.text: sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ yatra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||Panc_3.225||
children.translated_text: for all living beings — in this matter there should be no deliberation. [Panc 3.225]

children.text: upanata-bhaye yo yo mārgo hitārtha-karo bhavet- sa sa nipuṇayā buddhyā sevyo mahān kṛpaṇo 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: When danger is at hand, whatever path serves one's purpose — that path should be followed with keen intelligence, whether it be great or lowly.

children.text: karikara-nibhau jyāghātā kau mahāstra-viśāradau valaya-racitau strīvad bāhū kṛtau na kirīṭinā ||Panc_3.226||
children.translated_text: Did not <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) make his arms — mighty as elephant trunks, scarred by bowstring strikes, skilled in great weapons — adorned with bangles like a woman's? [Panc 3.226]

children.text: śaktenāpi satā janena viduṣā kālāntarāpekṣiṇā
children.translated_text: Even a capable, virtuous, learned person who bides his time

children.text: vastavyaṃ khalu vākya-vajra-viṣame kṣudre'pi pāpe jane |
children.translated_text: must indeed dwell among base and wicked people whose words cut like thunderbolts.

children.text: darvī-vyagra-kareṇa dhūma-malinenāyāsa-yukte ca
children.translated_text: Did not <s>Bhīma</s>, of immense strength, with ladle in hand, soiled by smoke,

children.text: bhīmenātibalena matsya-bhavane kiṃ noṣitaṃ sūdavat ||Panc_3.227||
children.translated_text: and weary, live like a cook in the house of <s>Matsya</s> (King <s>Virāṭa</s>)? [Panc 3.227]

children.text: yad vā tad vā viṣama-patitaḥ sādhu vā garhitaṃ vā
children.translated_text: This way or that, fallen into adversity, whether it be honorable or contemptible,

children.text: kālāpekṣī hṛdaya-nihitaṃ buddhimān karma kuryāt |
children.translated_text: the wise man, biding his time, should carry out the plan held firm in his heart.

children.text: kiṃ gāṇḍīva-sphurad-uru-guṇāsphālana-krūra-pāṇir
children.translated_text: Did not <s>Savyasācī</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), whose cruel hands twanged the mighty string of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>,

children.text: nāsīl līlā-naṭana-vilasan mekhalī savyasācī ||Panc_3.228||
children.translated_text: become one who wore a girdle and danced playfully? [Panc 3.228]

children.text: siddhiṃ prārthayatā janena viduṣā tejo nigṛhya svakaṃ
children.translated_text: A learned person seeking success must suppress his own splendor,

children.text: sattvotsāhavatāpi daiva-vidhiṣu sthairyaṃ prakārya kramāt |
children.translated_text: and though possessed of courage and vigor, must cultivate steadfastness in the course of destiny's decrees.

children.text: devendra-draviṇeśvarāntaka-samair apy anvito bhrātṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Even accompanied by brothers equal to <s>Devendra</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: kiṃ kliṣṭaḥ suciraṃ virāṭa-bhavane śrīmān na dharmātmajaḥ ||Panc_3.229||
children.translated_text: did not the glorious <s>Dharmātmaja</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) suffer long in the house of <s>Virāṭa</s>? [Panc 3.229]

children.text: rūpābhijana-sampanno mādrī-putrau balānvitau |
children.translated_text: The two sons of <s>Mādrī</s>, endowed with beauty, noble birth, and strength,

children.text: gokarma-rakṣā-vyāpāre virāṭa-preṣyatāṃ gatau ||Panc_3.230||
children.translated_text: were reduced to servitude under <s>Virāṭa</s>, employed in the tending of cattle and horses. [Panc 3.230]

children.text: rūpeṇāpratimena yauvana-guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhe kule janmanā
children.translated_text: She whose beauty was unmatched, who excelled in the virtues of youth, born in the noblest lineage,

children.text: kāntyā śrīr iva yātra sāpi vidaśāṃ kāla-kramād āgatā |
children.translated_text: whose radiance was like <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune) herself — even she was brought to a wretched state by the course of time.

children.text: sairandhrīti sa-garvitaṃ yuvatibhiḥ sākṣepam ākhyātayā
children.translated_text: Called '<s>Sairandhrī</s>' (a lady's maid) by the haughty young women, spoken of with contempt,

children.text: draupadyā nanu matsya-rāja-bhavane dhṛṣṭaṃ na kiṃ candanam ||Panc_3.231||
children.translated_text: did not <s>Draupadī</s> boldly apply sandalwood paste in the house of the fish-king (<s>Virāṭa</s>)? [Panc 3.231]

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-tāta ! asi-dhārā-vratam idaṃ manye yad ariṇā saha saṃvāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: Father! I consider this — living with the enemy — to be a vow upon the razor's edge.

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! evam etat | paraṃ na tādṛṅ-mūrkha-samāgamaḥ kvāpi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ | na ca mahāprajñam aneka-śāstreṣv apratima-buddhiṃ raktākṣaṃ vinā dhīmān | yat-kāraṇaṃ tena madīyaṃ yathāvasthitaṃ cittaṃ jñātam | ye punar anye mantriṇas te mahā-mūrkhā mantri-mātra-vyapadeśopajīvino 'tattva-kuśalā, yair idam api na jñātam | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: He replied: Your Majesty! It is indeed so. But never have I seen anywhere such a gathering of fools. Nor was there anyone wise among them, of incomparable intelligence versed in many <s>śāstras</s> (sciences), except <s>Raktākṣa</s>. For this reason, he alone discerned the true state of my mind. As for the other ministers, they were utter fools, living merely by the title of minister, unskilled in the essence of things, who did not even recognize this much:

children.text: arito 'bhyāgato bhṛtyo duṣṭas tat-saṅga-tat-paraḥ |
children.translated_text: A servant who has come from the enemy, wicked, devoted to association with the foe,

children.text: apasarpa-sadharmatvān nityodvegī ca dūṣitaḥ ||Panc_3.232||
children.translated_text: one who is like a spy by nature, always causing anxiety — he is corrupt. [Panc 3.232]

children.text: āsane śayane yāne pāna-bhojana-vastuṣu |
children.translated_text: In matters of seating, sleeping, traveling, drinking, eating, and possessions,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāntaraṃ pramatteṣu praharanty arayo 'riṣu ||Panc_3.233||
children.translated_text: enemies, finding an opening when their foes are off guard, strike. [Panc 3.233]

children.text: tasmāt sarva-prayatnena trivarga-nilayaṃ budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, with every effort, a wise man should

children.text: ātmānam ādṛto rakṣet pramādād dhi vinaśyati ||Panc_3.234||
children.translated_text: protect himself, the abode of the three aims of life, with diligence, for through negligence one perishes. [Panc 3.234]

children.text: sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: And this is well said:

children.text: santāpayanti kam apathya-bhujaṃ na rogā
children.translated_text: What diseases do not afflict one who eats unwholesome food?

children.text: durmantriṇaṃ kam upayānti na nīti-doṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: What policy errors do not befall one with bad ministers?

children.text: kaṃ śrīr na darpayati kaṃ na nihanti mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: Whom does prosperity not intoxicate? Whom does death not slay?

children.text: kaṃ svīkṛtā na viṣayā paripīḍayanti ||Panc_3.235||
children.translated_text: Whom do sense pleasures, once embraced, not torment? [Panc 3.235]

children.text: lubdhasya naśyati yaśaḥ piśunasya maitrī
children.translated_text: The greedy man's fame perishes, the slanderer's friendships perish,

children.text: naṣṭa-kriyasya kula artha-parasya dharmaḥ |
children.translated_text: the family of one who neglects his duties perishes, and the righteousness of one devoted solely to wealth perishes.

children.text: vidyā-phalaṃ vyasaninaḥ kṛpaṇasya saukhyaṃ
children.translated_text: The fruits of learning perish for the dissolute, happiness perishes for the miser,

children.text: rājyaṃ pramatta-sacivasya narādhipasya ||Panc_3.236||
children.translated_text: and the kingdom perishes for a king whose minister is negligent. [Panc 3.236]

children.text: tad rājan ! asi-dhārā-vrataṃ mayācaritam aritam ari-saṃsargād iti yad bhavatoktaṃ, tan mayā sākṣād evānubhūtam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore, O King! What you have said — that living with the enemy is a vow upon the razor's edge — that I have experienced firsthand through my sojourn among the foes. And it is said:

children.text: apamānaṃ puraskṛtya mānaṃ kṛtvā tu pṛṣṭhataḥ |
children.translated_text: Placing humiliation before him and casting honor behind,

children.text: svārtham abhyuddharet prājñaḥ kārya-dhvaṃso hi mūrkhatā ||Panc_3.237||
children.translated_text: the wise man should advance his own purpose, for the ruin of one's goal is foolishness. [Panc 3.237]

children.text: skandhenāpi vahec chatruṃ kālam āsādya buddhimān |
children.translated_text: The wise man, when the time demands it, should carry even an enemy upon his shoulders.

children.text: mahatā kṛṣṇa-sarpeṇa maṇḍūkā bahavo hatāḥ ||Panc_3.238||
children.translated_text: By a great black serpent were many frogs slain. [Panc 3.238]

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: How is that?

children.text: sthirajīvī kathayati-
children.translated_text: <s>Sthirajīvī</s> narrates:

children.text:
kathā 15
mandaviṣa-sarpa-kathā
children.translated_text: Tale 15: The Story of <s>Mandaviṣa</s> the Serpent

children.text: asti varuṇādri-samīpa ekasmin pradeśe pariṇata-vayā manda-viṣo nāma kṛṣṇa-sarpaḥ | sa evaṃ citte sañcintitavān-kathaṃ nāma mayā sukhopāya-vṛttyā vartitavyam iti | tato bahu-maṇḍūkaṃ hradam upagamya dhṛti-parītam ivātmānaṃ darśitavān |
children.translated_text: Near <s>Varuṇādri</s> (Varuṇa's mountain), in a certain place, there lived an aged black serpent named <s>Mandaviṣa</s> (Mild-Venom). He reflected in his mind thus: How can I contrive to live by an easy means of obtaining food? Then, approaching a pond full of frogs, he displayed himself as though overcome with dejection.

children.text: atha tathā sthite saudaka-prānta-gatenaikena maṇḍūkena pṛṣṭaḥ-māma ! kim adya yathā-pūrvam āhārārthaṃ na viharasi |
children.translated_text: Now, while he was sitting thus, a frog at the water's edge asked him: Uncle! Why do you not roam about today in search of food as you used to?

children.text: so 'bravīt-bhadra ! kuto me manda-bhāgyasyāhārābhilāṣaḥ ? yat kāraṇam adya rātrau pradoṣa eva mayāhārārthaṃ viharamāṇena dṛṣṭa eko maṇḍūkaḥ | tad-grahaṇārthaṃ mayā kramaḥ sajjitaḥ | so 'pi māṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyu-bhayena svādhyāya-prasaktānāṃ brāhmaṇānām antaram apakrānto na vibhāvito mayā kvāpi gataḥ | tat-sādṛśya-mohita-cittena mayā kasyacid brāhmaṇasya sūnor hrada-taṭa-jalāntaḥ-stho 'ṅguṣṭho daṣṭaḥ | tato 'sau sapadi pañcatvam upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: He replied: Good one! How could an unfortunate wretch like me have any desire for food? For this very night, at dusk, as I was roaming in search of food, I spotted a frog. As I made my move to seize him, he fled into the midst of some <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> absorbed in their Vedic recitation, and I lost sight of where he went. Confused by the resemblance, I bit the toe of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s son who was standing in the water at the bank of the pond. Thereupon he instantly died.

children.text: atha tasya pitrā duḥkhitenāhaṃ śapto yathā-durātman ! tvayā niraparādho mat-suto daṣṭaḥ | tad anena doṣeṇa tvaṃ maṇḍūkānāṃ vāhanaṃ bhaviṣyasi, tat-prasāda-labdha-jīvikayā vartiṣye iti | tato 'haṃ yuṣmākaṃ vāhanārtham āgato 'smi |
children.translated_text: Then his grief-stricken father cursed me thus: Wretch! You have bitten my innocent son! By this sin you shall become a vehicle for frogs, and you shall live only by the food obtained through their favor. Therefore I have come here to serve as your vehicle.

children.text: tena ca sarva-maṇḍūkānām idam āveditam | tatas taiḥ prahṛṣṭa-manobhiḥ sarvair eva gatvā jala-pāda-nāmno dardura-rājasya vijñaptam | athāsāv api mantri-parivṛto 'tyadbhutam idam iti manyamāno sa-sambhramaṃ hradād uttīrya manda-viṣasya phaṇinaḥ phaṇā-pradeśam adhirūḍhaḥ | śeṣā api yathā-jyeṣṭhaṃ tat-pṛṣṭhopari samāruruhuḥ | kiṃ bahunā, uparita-sthānam aprāptavantas tasyānupadaṃ dhāvanti | mandaviṣo 'pi teṣāṃ tuṣṭy-artham aneka-prakārān gati-viśeṣān adarśayat | atha jalapādo labdha-sukhas tam āha-
children.translated_text: That frog informed all the other frogs of this. Then all of them, their minds delighted, went and reported it to the frog-king named <s>Jalapāda</s> (Water-Foot). He too, surrounded by his ministers, thinking this to be most extraordinary, eagerly climbed out of the pond and mounted the hood of the serpent <s>Mandaviṣa</s>. The rest also climbed upon his back in order of seniority. In short, those who could not find a place on top ran along behind him. <s>Mandaviṣa</s> too, for their delight, displayed various kinds of special gaits. Then <s>Jalapāda</s>, having enjoyed the ride, said to him:

children.text: na tathā kariṇā yānaṃ turageṇa rathena vā |
children.translated_text: Neither the ride on an elephant, nor on a horse, nor in a chariot,

children.text: nara-yānena vā yānaṃ yathā mandaviṣeṇa me ||Panc_3.239||
children.translated_text: nor a ride carried by men, compares to my ride upon <s>Mandaviṣa</s>. [Panc 3.239]

children.text: athānyedyur manda-viṣaś chadmanā mandaṃ mandaṃ visarpati | tac ca dṛṣṭvā jalapādo 'bravīt-bhadra ! mandaviṣa ! yathā-pūrvaṃ kim adya sādhu nohyate ?
children.translated_text: Now the next day, <s>Mandaviṣa</s> deliberately slithered slowly, ever so slowly. Seeing this, <s>Jalapāda</s> said: Good <s>Mandaviṣa</s>! Why are you not carrying me as well as before today?

children.text: mandaviṣo 'bravīt-deva adyāhāra-vaikalyān na me voḍhuṃ śaktir asti |
children.translated_text: <s>Mandaviṣa</s> replied: Your Majesty, today, due to lack of food, I do not have the strength to carry you.

children.text: athāsāv abravīt-bhadra ! bhakṣaya kṣudra-maṇḍūkān |
children.translated_text: Then he said: Good one! Eat the small frogs.

children.text: tac chrutvā praharṣita-sarva-gātro mandaviṣaḥ sa-sambhramam abravīt-mamāyam eva vipra-śāpo 'sti | tat tavānenānujñā-vacanena prīto 'smi |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Mandaviṣa</s>, every limb thrilling with joy, said eagerly: This is precisely the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s curse upon me. Therefore I am delighted by this permission of yours.

children.text: tato 'sau nairantaryeṇa maṇḍūkān bhakṣayan katipayair evāhobhir balavān saṃvṛttaḥ | prahṛṣṭaś cāntar-līnam avahasyedam abravīt-
children.translated_text: Thereupon, devouring frogs without interruption, he grew strong within just a few days. And, inwardly laughing with delight, he said:

children.text: maṇḍūkā vividhā hy ete chala-pūrvopasādhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: These various frogs, obtained through trickery,

children.text: kiyantaṃ kālam akṣīṇā bhaveyuḥ khāditā mama ||Panc_3.240||
children.translated_text: how long can they last unconsumed, being eaten by me? [Panc 3.240]

children.text: jala-pādo 'pi mandaviṣeṇa kṛta-kavaca-navyāmohita-cittaḥ kim api nāvabudhyate | atrāntare'nyo mahākāyaḥ kṛṣṇa-sarpas tam uddeśaṃ samāyātaḥ | taṃ ca maṇḍūkair vāhyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismaya-gatam | āha ca-vayasya ! yad asmākam aśanaṃ taiḥ kathaṃ vāhyase | viruddham etat |
children.translated_text: <s>Jalapāda</s> too, his mind deluded by the armor of a fresh trick made by <s>Mandaviṣa</s>, perceived nothing. In the meantime, another great black serpent arrived at that spot. Seeing him being carried by the frogs, he was astonished. And he said: 'Friend! They who are our food — how are you being carried by them? This is contrary [to nature].'

children.text: mandaviṣo 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: <s>Mandaviṣa</s> said —

children.text: sarvam etad vijānāmi yathā vāhyo 'smi darduraiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I know all this — how I am being carried by frogs;

children.text: kiñcit kālaṃ pratīkṣe'haṃ ghṛtāndho brāhmaṇo yathā ||Panc_3.241||
children.translated_text: I am waiting for a certain time, just like the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> blinded by <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee).' [Panc 3.241]

children.text: so 'bravīt-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
mandaviṣaḥ kathayati-
kathā 16
ghṛtāndha-brāhmaṇa-kathā
children.translated_text: <s>Mandaviṣa</s> narrates — Story 16: The tale of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> blinded by ghee.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne yajñadatto nāma brāhmaṇaḥ | tasya bhāryā puṃścaly anyāsakta-manā ajasraṃ viṭāyasa-khaṇḍa-ghṛtān ghṛta-pūrān kṛtvā bhartuś caurikayā prayacchati | atha kadācid bhartā dṛṣṭvābravīt-bhadre ! kim etat paripacyate ? kutra vājasraṃ nayasīdam ? tat kathaya satyam |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Yajñadatta</s>. His wife, a wanton woman whose mind was attached to another man, constantly made <s>ghṛta</s>-filled cakes with pieces of iron for her paramour, and gave them to him by stealing from her husband. Then one day, the husband saw and said: 'Good wife! What is being cooked? Where do you constantly take this? Tell me the truth.'

children.text: sā cotpanna-pratibhā kṛtaka-vacanair bhartāram abravīt-asty atra nātidūre bhagavatyā devyā āyatanam | tatrāham upoṣitā satī baliṃ bhakṣya-viśeṣāṃś cāpūrvān nayāmi |
children.translated_text: And she, quick-witted, spoke to her husband with fabricated words: 'Not very far from here there is a temple of the blessed Goddess. There, having fasted, I bring offering and special delicacies.'

children.text: atha tat paśyatā gṛhītvā tat sakalaṃ devyāyatanābhimukhī pratasthe | yat kāraṇaṃ devyā niveditenānena madīyo bhartaivaṃ maṃsyate yat mama brāhmaṇī bhagavatyāḥ kṛte nadyām avatīrya yāvat snānaṃ karoti tāvat tad bhartāpi mārgāntareṇāgatya devyāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'dṛśyo 'vatasthe |
children.translated_text: Then, wanting to observe this, he took all of it and set out toward the Goddess's temple. For this reason — when it would be offered to the Goddess, this husband of mine will think: 'My wife does this for the sake of the blessed Goddess.' Having descended into the river to bathe, while she was bathing, her husband also, having come by another path, stood behind the Goddess's image, unseen.

children.text: atha sā brāhmaṇī snātvā devy-āyatanam āgatya snānānulepana-mālya-dhūpa-bali-kriyādikaṃ kṛtvā devīṃ praṇamya vyajijñapat-bhagavati ! kena prakāreṇa mama bhartāndho bhaviṣyati ?
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, having bathed, having come to the Goddess's temple, having performed bathing, anointing, garlands, incense, offering, and other rites, bowing to the Goddess, prayed: 'O blessed Goddess! By what means will my husband become blind?'

children.text: tac chrutvā svara-bhedena devī-pṛṣṭha-sthito brāhmaṇo jagāda-yadi tvam ajasraṃ ghṛta-pūrādi-bhakṣyaṃ tasmai bhartre prayacchasi, tataḥ śīghram andho bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, standing behind the Goddess, spoke in a disguised voice: 'If you constantly give <s>ghṛta</s>-filled cakes and other sweets to that husband of yours, then he will quickly become blind.'

children.text: sā tu bandhakī kṛtaka-vacana-vañcita-mānasā tasmai brāhmaṇāya tad eva nityaṃ pradadau | athānyedyur brāhmaṇenābhihitam-bhadre, nāhaṃ sutarāṃ paśyāmi |
children.translated_text: And that wanton woman, her mind deceived by the fabricated words, gave that very thing to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> daily. Then one day the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'Dear one, I can no longer see properly.'

children.text: tac chrutvā cintitam anayā-devyāḥ prasādo 'yaṃ prāpta iti | atha tasyā hṛdaya-vallabho viṭas tat-sakāśam-andhībhūto 'yaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ kiṃ mama kariṣyatīti niḥśaṅkaṃ pratidinam abhyeti | athānyedyus taṃ praviśantam abhyāśa-gataṃ dṛṣṭvā keśair gṛhītvā laguḍa-pārṣṇi-prabhṛti-prahārais tāvad atāḍayat yāvad asau pañcatvam āpa | tām api puṣṭa-patnīṃ vicchanna-nāsikāṃ kṛtvā visasarja |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, she thought: 'This is the Goddess's blessing that has been obtained.' Then her beloved paramour, [thinking] 'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has become blind — what will he do to me?' came to her fearlessly every day. Then one day, seeing him enter and approach closely, the [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] seized him by the hair and beat him so severely with a club and his heels that the paramour died. That well-fed wife too he disfigured by cutting off her nose and cast her out.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-skandhenāpi vahec chatrum (238) ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'One should even carry an enemy on one's shoulder...' (verse 238) and so on.

children.text: atha rājan ! yathā mandaviṣeṇa buddhi-balena maṇḍūkā nihatās tathā mayāpi sarve vairiṇaḥ | sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: So, O king! Just as <s>Mandaviṣa</s> destroyed the frogs through the power of intelligence, so have I destroyed all the enemies. And this is well said —

children.text: vane prajvalito vahnir dahan mūlāni rakṣati |
children.translated_text: A fire ignited in the forest protects the roots while burning [the foliage];

children.text: samūlonmūlanaṃ kuryād vāyur yo mṛdu-śītalaḥ ||Panc_3.242||
children.translated_text: but a wind that is gentle and cool uproots them completely. [Panc 3.242]

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-tāta ! satyam evaitat | ye mahātmāno bhavanti te mahā-sattvā āpad-gatā api prārabdhaṃ na tyajanti | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Father! This is indeed true. Those who are great-souled, even when met with calamity, do not abandon what they have undertaken. And it is said —

children.text: mahattvam etan mahatāṃ nayālaṅkāra-dhāriṇām |
children.translated_text: This is the greatness of the great, who bear the ornaments of statecraft:

children.text: na muñcanti yad ārabdhaṃ kṛcchre'pi vyasanodaye ||Panc_3.243||
children.translated_text: they do not abandon what they have undertaken, even in hardship and the onset of adversity. [Panc 3.243]

children.text: tathā ca-
prārabhyate na khalu vighna-bhayena nīcaiḥ
children.translated_text: The base do not even begin, fearing obstacles;

children.text: prārabhya vighna-vihatā viramanti madhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: the middling begin but desist when thwarted by obstacles;

children.text: vighnaiḥ sahasra-guṇitair api hanyamānāḥ
children.translated_text: but the best, even when struck by obstacles multiplied a thousandfold,

children.text: prārabdham uttama-guṇā na parityajanti ||Panc_3.244||
children.translated_text: do not abandon what they have undertaken. [Panc 3.244]
And likewise —

children.text: tat kṛtaṃ niṣkaṇṭakaṃ mama rājyaṃ śatrūn niḥśeṣatāṃ nayatā tvayā | athavā yuktam etan naya-vedinām | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: So you have made my kingdom free of thorns by utterly annihilating the enemies. Or rather, this is fitting for those who know statecraft. And it is said —

children.text: ṛṇa-śeṣaṃ cāgni-śeṣaṃ ca śatru-śeṣaṃ tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: A remnant of debt, a remnant of fire, a remnant of enemies,

children.text: vyādhi-śeṣaṃ ca niḥśeṣaṃ kṛtvā prājño na sīdati ||Panc_3.245||
children.translated_text: and a remnant of disease — the wise man does not perish who makes these entirely gone. [Panc 3.245]

children.text: so 'bravīt-deva ! bhāgyavān tvam evāsi, yasyārabdhaṃ sarvam eva saṃsiddhyati | tan na kevalaṃ śauryaṃ kṛtyaṃ sādhayati, kintu prajñayā yat kriyate tad eva vijayāya bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Lord! You alone are fortunate, for everything you undertake succeeds. It is not valor alone that accomplishes objectives; rather, what is done through wisdom — that alone leads to victory.' And it is said —

children.text: śastrair hatā na hi hatā ripavo bhavanti
children.translated_text: Enemies slain by weapons are not truly slain;

children.text: prajñā-hatās tu ripavaḥ suhatā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: but enemies slain by wisdom are well and truly slain.

children.text: śastaṃ nihanti puruṣasya śarīram ekaṃ
children.translated_text: A weapon destroys only a man's single body;

children.text: prajñā kulaṃ ca vibhavaś ca yaśaś ca hanti ||Panc_3.246||
children.translated_text: but wisdom destroys his family, wealth, and fame. [Panc 3.246]

children.text: tad evaṃ prajñā-puruṣakārābhyāṃ yuktasyāyatnena kārya-siddhayaḥ sambhavanti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, for one equipped with both wisdom and effort, accomplishments come about effortlessly. And it is said —

children.text: prasarati matiḥ kāryārambhe dṛḍhībhavati smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Intellect expands at the commencement of a task; determination becomes firm;

children.text: svayam upanayann arthān mantro na gacchati viplavam |
children.translated_text: the counsel that itself brings forth results does not go to ruin;

children.text: sphurati saphalas tarkaś cittaṃ samunnatim aśnute
children.translated_text: reasoning becomes fruitful; the mind attains elevation;

children.text: bhavati ca ratiḥ ślāghye kṛtye narasya bhaviṣyataḥ ||Panc_3.247||
children.translated_text: and there arises delight in praiseworthy action for the man who is destined to prosper. [Panc 3.247]

children.text: tathā ca naya-tyāga-śaurya-sampanne puruṣe rājyam iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise, kingship belongs to a man endowed with statecraft, generosity, and valor. And it is said —

children.text: tyāgini śūre viduṣi ca saṃsarga-rucir jano guṇī bhavati |
children.translated_text: In one who is generous, brave, and learned, people delight in association and become virtuous;

children.text: guṇavati dhanaṃ dhanāc chrīḥ śrīmaty ājñā tato rājyam ||Panc_3.248||
children.translated_text: with the virtuous comes wealth; from wealth, splendor; in the splendid, authority; and from that, sovereignty. [Panc 3.248]

children.text: meghavarṇa āha-nūnaṃ sadyaḥ-phalāni nīti-śāstrāṇi yat tvayānukṛtyenānupraviśyāri-mardanaḥ saparijano niḥśeṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Meghavarṇa</s> said: 'Surely the treatises of statecraft bear immediate fruit, since by you, having infiltrated through impersonation and crushed the enemy, the foe with all his retinue has been annihilated.'

children.text: sthirajīvy āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Sthirajīvī</s> said —

children.text: tīkṣṇopāya-prāpti-gamyo 'pi yo 'rthas
children.translated_text: Even an objective attainable through sharp stratagem —

children.text: tasyāpy ādau saṃśrayaḥ sādhu yuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: for that too, an approach through submission is first rightly employed.

children.text: uttuṅgāgraḥ sāra-bhūto vanānāṃ
children.translated_text: The lord of trees, lofty-topped, the essence of forests,

children.text: mānyābhyarcya cchidyate pādapendraḥ ||Panc_3.249||
children.translated_text: is cut down after being honored by the venerable [i.e., the woodcutter marks it first with worship]. [Panc 3.249]

children.text: athavā svāmin ! kiṃ tenābhihitena ? yad anantara-jāle kriyā-rahitam asukha-sādhyaṃ vā bhavati | sādhu cedam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Or rather, master! What use is something spoken about if, in the immediate chain of events, it is devoid of action or is difficult to accomplish? And this is well said —

children.text: aniścitair adhyavasāya-bhīrubhir
children.translated_text: Words of those who are irresolute, timid in determination,

children.text: yatheṣṭa-saṃlāpa-rati-prayojanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: whose purpose is mere delight in talking as they please —

children.text: phale visaṃvādam upāgatā giraḥ
children.translated_text: such words, having arrived at disappointment in their result,

children.text: prayānti loke parihāsa-vastutām ||Panc_3.250||
children.translated_text: become in the world merely objects of ridicule. [Panc 3.250]

children.text: na ca laghuṣv api kartavyeṣu dhīmadbhir anādaraḥ kartavyaḥ | yataḥ-
śakṣyāmi kartum idam alpam ayatna-sādhyam
children.translated_text: 'I can do this — it is small and easy to accomplish' —

children.text: anādaraḥ ka iti kṛtyam upekṣamāṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: neglecting a task with such disregard,

children.text: kecit pramatta-manasaḥ paritāpa-duḥkham
children.translated_text: some men, their minds careless,

children.text: āpat-prasaṅga-sulabhaṃ puruṣā prayānti ||Panc_3.251||
children.translated_text: arrive at the anguish and grief easily brought about by calamity. [Panc 3.251]
And even in minor tasks, the wise should not show carelessness. For —

children.text: tad adya jitārer mad-vibhor yathā-pūrvaṃ nidrā-lābho bhaviṣyati | ucyate caitat-
children.translated_text: So today, now that the enemy is conquered, my lord shall have sleep as before. And this is said —

children.text: niḥsarpe baddha-sarpe vā bhavane suṣyate sukham |
children.translated_text: In a house free of serpents, or where they are bound, one sleeps in comfort;

children.text: sadā dṛṣṭa-bhujaṅge tu nidrā duḥkhena labhyate ||Panc_3.252||
children.translated_text: but where a serpent is constantly seen, sleep is obtained only with difficulty. [Panc 3.252]

children.text: tathā ca-
vistīrṇa-vyavasāya-sādhya-mahatāṃ snighdopayuktāśiṣāṃ
children.translated_text: Of great tasks achievable through expansive enterprise, blessed with the wishes of the affectionate,

children.text: kāryāṇāṃ naya-sāhasonnati-matām icchāpad-ārohiṇām |
children.translated_text: of undertakings imbued with the elevation of statecraft and daring, climbing the summit of ambition,

children.text: mānotseka-parākrama-vyasaninaḥ pāraṃ na yāvad-gatāḥ
children.translated_text: as long as men addicted to the pride, valor, and adventure [of such tasks] have not reached the far shore —

children.text: sāmarṣe hṛdaye'vakāśa-viṣayā tāvat kathaṃ nirvṛtiḥ ||Panc_3.253||
children.translated_text: how can there be contentment in the domain of their indignant hearts? [Panc 3.253]
And likewise —

children.text: tad avasita-kāryārambhasya viśrāmyatīva me hṛdayam | tad idam adhunā nihata-kaṇṭakaṃ rājyaṃ prajā-pālana-tatparo bhūtvā putra-pautrādi-krameṇācala-cchatrāsana-śrīḥ ciraṃ bhuṅkṣva | api ca-
children.translated_text: So now that the undertaking is completed, my heart rests at ease. So now enjoy this kingdom freed of thorns, devoted to the protection of your subjects, through the succession of sons and grandsons, with unshakeable parasol-and-throne glory, for a long time. Moreover —

children.text: prajā na rañjayed yas tu rājā rakṣādibhir guṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: That king who does not gratify his subjects through the virtues of protection and the like —

children.text: ajāgala-stanasyeva tasya rājyaṃ nirarthakam ||Panc_3.254||
children.translated_text: his sovereignty is as useless as the teats on a goat's neck. [Panc 3.254]

children.text: guṇeṣu rāgo vyasaneṣv anādaro
children.translated_text: The king who has attachment to virtues, disregard for vices,

children.text: ratiḥ subhṛtyeṣu ca yasya bhūpateḥ |
children.translated_text: and delight in good servants —

children.text: ciraṃ sa bhuṅkte cala-cāmarāṃśukāṃ
children.translated_text: he long enjoys the royal splendor adorned with waving <s>cāmara</s> fans

children.text: sitātapatrābharaṇāṃ nṛpa-śriyam ||Panc_3.255||
children.translated_text: and white parasol ornaments. [Panc 3.255]

children.text: na ca tvayā prāpta-rājyo 'ham iti matvā śrī-madenātmā vyasayitavyaḥ | yat kāraṇam-calā hi rājño vibhūtayaḥ vaṃśārohaṇavad rājya-lakṣmī-durārohā, kṣaṇa-vinipāta-ratā, prayatna-śatair api dhāryamāṇā durdharā, praśastārādhitāpy ante vipralambhinī, vānara-jātir iva vidrutāneka-cittā, padma-patram ivāghaṭita-saṃśleṣā, pavana-gatir ivāticapalā, anārya-saṅgatir ivāsthirā, āśīviṣa iva durupacārā, sandhyābhra-lekheva muhūrta-rāgā, jala-budbudāvalīva svabhāva-bhaṅgurā, śarīra-prakṛtir iva kṛtaghnā, svapna-labdha-dravya-rāśir iva kṣaṇa-dṛṣṭa-naṣṭā | api ca-
children.translated_text: And you should not, thinking 'I have obtained sovereignty,' ruin yourself through the intoxication of prosperity. For — the fortunes of a king are indeed fickle: royal splendor is hard to mount like climbing a bamboo; prone to falling at any moment; difficult to hold even with a hundred efforts; ultimately deceptive even when well-worshipped; restless in many minds like the monkey race; unattached like a lotus petal; exceedingly fickle like the movement of wind; unstable like the company of the ignoble; hard to manage like a venomous serpent; colored for but a moment like a streak of evening cloud; fragile by nature like a row of water bubbles; ungrateful like the constitution of the body; vanishing the instant it is seen like a heap of wealth obtained in a dream. Moreover —

children.text: yadaiva rājye kriyate'bhiṣekas
children.translated_text: At the very moment when consecration to sovereignty is performed,

children.text: tadaiva buddhir vyasaneṣu yojyā |
children.translated_text: at that very moment one's mind should be applied to [anticipating] adversities;

children.text: ghaṭā hi rājñām abhiṣeka-kāle
children.translated_text: for the water-pots of kings at the time of consecration

children.text: sahāmbhasaivāpadam udgiranti ||Panc_3.256||
children.translated_text: pour forth calamity along with the water itself. [Panc 3.256]

children.text: na ca kaścid anadhigamanīyo nāmāsty āpadām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And there is no one who is beyond the reach of calamities. And it is said —

children.text: rāmasya vrajanaṃ vane nivasanaṃ pāṇḍoḥ sutānāṃ vane
children.translated_text: The exile of <s>Rāma</s> to the forest, the dwelling of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s sons in the forest,

children.text: vṛṣṇīnāṃ nidhanaṃ nalasya nṛpate rājyāt paribhraṃśanam |
children.translated_text: the destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, King <s>Nala</s>'s fall from his kingdom,

children.text: nāṭyācāryakam arjunasya patanaṃ sañcintya laṅkeśvare
children.translated_text: the acting-mastery of <s>Arjuna</s>, the fall of the Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> —

children.text: sarve kāla-vaśāj jano 'tra sahate kaḥ kaṃ paritrāyate ||Panc_3.257||
children.translated_text: all people endure [such fates] by the power of time — who protects whom? [Panc 3.257]

children.text: kva sa daśarathaḥ svarge bhūtvā mahendra-suhṛd gataḥ
children.translated_text: Where is that <s>Daśaratha</s>, who went to heaven having become <s>Mahendra</s>'s friend?

children.text: kva sa jalanidher velāṃ baddhvā nṛpaḥ sagaras tathā |
children.translated_text: Where is that King <s>Sagara</s> who bound the ocean's shore?

children.text: kva sa karatalāj jāto vainyaḥ kva sūrya-tanur manuḥ
children.translated_text: Where is <s>Vainya</s> (Pṛthu), born from the palm? Where is <s>Manu</s>, offspring of the sun?

children.text: nanu balavatā kālenaite prabodhya nimīlitāḥ ||Panc_3.258||
children.translated_text: Indeed, by mighty Time they were awakened and then closed [into oblivion]. [Panc 3.258]

children.text: māndhātā kva gatas triloka-vijayī rājā kva satyavrataḥ
children.translated_text: Where has gone <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, conqueror of the three worlds? Where is King <s>Satyavrata</s>?

children.text: devānāṃ nṛpatir gataḥ kva nahuṣaḥ sac-chāstravān keśavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where has gone <s>Nahuṣa</s>, king of the gods? Where is <s>Keśava</s>, versed in true scripture?

children.text: manyante sarathāḥ sa-kuñjara-varāḥ śakrāsanādhyāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: They who thought themselves [secure] with chariots, with the best of elephants, seated on <s>Śakra</s>'s throne —

children.text: kālenaiva mahātmanā tv anukṛtāḥ kālena nirvāsitāḥ ||Panc_3.259||
children.translated_text: by great Time they were imitated and by Time they were banished. [Panc 3.259]

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: sa ca nṛpatis te sacivās tāḥ pramadās tāni kānana-vanāni |
children.translated_text: That king, those ministers, those women, those parks and forests —

children.text: sa ca te ca tāś ca tāni ca kṛtānta-dṛṣṭāni naṣṭāni ||Panc_3.260||
children.translated_text: he and they and those and all — seen by Death, they perished. [Panc 3.260]

children.text: evaṃ matta-kari-karṇa-cañcalāṃ rājya-lakṣmīm avāpya nyāyaika-niṣṭho bhūtvopabhuṅkṣva |
children.translated_text: Thus, having obtained royal splendor as fickle as the ear of a rutting elephant, remain devoted solely to righteousness and enjoy it.'

children.text:
iti śrī-viṣṇu-śarma-viracite pañcatantre kākolūkīyaṃ nāma
tṛtīyaṃ tantraṃ samāptam
||3||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>tantra</s> (book), named <s>Kākolūkīyam</s> (Of Crows and Owls), in the <s>Pañcatantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>. ||3||

children.text: caturtha-tantram
children.translated_text: The Fourth <s>Tantra</s> (Book).

children.text: atha labdha-praṇāśam
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Labdhapraṇāśam</s> (Loss of What Was Gained).

children.text: athedam ārabhate labdha-praṇāśaṃ nāma caturthaṃ tantram | yasyāyam ādimaḥ ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now begins the fourth <s>tantra</s> named <s>Labdhapraṇāśam</s> (Loss of What Was Gained). Its opening verse is —

children.text: samutpanneṣu kāryeṣu buddhir yasya na hīyate |
children.translated_text: He whose intellect does not falter when emergencies arise —

children.text: sa eva durgaṃ tarati jalastho vānaro yathā ||Panc_4.1||
children.translated_text: he alone crosses through the difficult pass, like a monkey in water. [Panc 4.1]

children.text:
tad yathānuśrūyate-
prastāvanā-kathā
vānara-makara-vṛttāntaḥ
children.translated_text: As the story goes — Introductory tale: The episode of the monkey and the crocodile.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścit samudropakaṇṭhe mahān jambū-pādapaḥ sadā-phalaḥ | tatra ca raktamukho nāma vānaraḥ prativasati sma | tatra ca tasya taror adhaḥ kadācit karālamukho nāma makaraḥ samudra-salilān niṣkramya sukomala-bālukā-sanāthe tīropānte nyaviśata | tataś ca raktamukhena sa proktaḥ-bhoḥ ! bhavān samabhyāgato 'tithiḥ | tad bhakṣayatu mayā dattāny amṛta-tulyāni jambū-phalāni | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: On the shore of a certain ocean there stood a great <s>Jambū</s> (rose-apple) tree, ever-bearing fruit. There lived a monkey named <s>Raktamukha</s> (Red-face). And beneath that tree, a crocodile named <s>Karālamukha</s> (Terrible-face), having emerged from the ocean waters, settled on the shore blessed with soft, fine sand. Then <s>Raktamukha</s> said to him: 'Sir! You have come as a guest. So eat these <s>Jambū</s> fruits, equal to nectar, given by me.' And it is said —

children.text: priyo vā yadi vā dveṣyo mūrkho vā yadi paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether dear or hostile, whether foolish or learned —

children.text: vaiśvadevāntam āpannaḥ so 'tithiḥ svarga-saṅkramaḥ ||Panc_4.2||
children.translated_text: he who arrives at the end of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering — that guest is a bridge to heaven. [Panc 4.2]

children.text: na pṛcchec caraṇaṃ gotraṃ na ca vidyāṃ kulaṃ na ca |
children.translated_text: One should not ask about the conduct, lineage, learning, or family

children.text: atithiṃ vaiśvadevānte śrāddhe ca manur abravīt ||Panc_4.3||
children.translated_text: of a guest [who arrives] at the end of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [offering] or at a <s>Śrāddha</s> — so declared <s>Manu</s>. ||Panc_4.3||

children.text: dūra-mārga-śrama-śrāntaṃ vaiśvadevāntam āgatam |
children.translated_text: He who honors a guest who has come wearied from a long journey,

children.text: atithiṃ pūjayed yas tu sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||Panc_4.4||
children.translated_text: arriving at the end of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> — he attains the highest goal. ||Panc_4.4||

children.text: apūjito 'tithir yasya gṛhād yāti viniḥśvasan |
children.translated_text: He from whose house a guest departs unhonored, sighing,

children.text: gacchanti pitaras tasya vimukhāḥ saha daivataiḥ ||Panc_4.5||
children.translated_text: his ancestors, together with the gods, turn their faces away from him. ||Panc_4.5||

children.text: evam uktvā tasmai jambū-phalāni dadau | so 'pi tāni bhakṣayitvā tena saha ciraṃ goṣṭhī-sukham anubhūya bhūyo 'pi sva-bhavanam agāt | evaṃ nityam eva tau vānara-makarau jambū-cchāyā-sthitau vividha-śāstra-goṣṭhyā kālaṃ nayantau sukhena tiṣṭhataḥ | so 'pi makaro bhakṣita-śeṣāṇi jambū-phalāni gṛhaṃ gatvā sva-patnyai prayacchati | athānyatame divase tayā sa pṛṣṭaḥ-nātha ! kvaivaṃvidhāny amṛta-phalāni prāpnoṣi ?
children.translated_text: Having said this, he gave him <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) fruits. And he, having eaten those, having enjoyed the pleasure of conversation with him for a long time, went again to his own home. Thus constantly, those two — the monkey and the crocodile — remaining beneath the shade of the <s>jambū</s> tree, passed their time happily with discussions of various sciences. And that crocodile would take home the remaining <s>jambū</s> fruits after eating and give them to his wife. Then one day she asked him: Lord! Where do you obtain such ambrosia-like fruits?

children.text: sa āha-bhadre ! mamāsti parama-suhṛd raktamukho nāma vānaraḥ | sa prīti-pūrvakam imāni phalāni prayacchati |
children.translated_text: He said: Good wife! I have a dearest friend, a monkey named <s>Raktamukha</s> (red-face). He gives these fruits with love.

children.text: atha tayābhihitam-yaḥ sarvadaivāmṛta-prāyāṇīdṛśāni phalāni bhakṣayati, tasya hṛdayam amṛta-mayaṃ bhaviṣyati | tad yadi bhāryayā te prayojanaṃ, tatas tasya hṛdayaṃ mahyaṃ prayaccha | yena tad bhakṣayitvā jarā-maraṇa-rahitā tvayā saha bhogān bhunajmi |
children.translated_text: Then she said: One who always eats such fruits that are like ambrosia — his heart must be made of ambrosia. So if you have any use for your wife, then give me his heart. By eating it, I shall become free from old age and death and enjoy pleasures together with you.

children.text: sa āha-bhadre ! mā maivaṃ vada | yataḥ sa pratipanno 'smākaṃ bhrātā | aparaṃ phala-dātā | tato vyāpādayituṃ na śakyate | tat tyajainaṃ mithāgrahaṇam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Good wife! Do not speak thus! For he is an accepted brother of ours. Moreover, he is a giver of fruits. Therefore he cannot be killed. So give up this wrong insistence. And it is said —

children.text: ekaṃ prasūyate mātā dvitīyaṃ vāk prasūyate |
children.translated_text: A mother gives birth to one [brother]; speech gives birth to a second;

children.text: vāg-jātam adhikaṃ procuḥ sodaryād api bāndhavāt ||Panc_4.6||
children.translated_text: the speech-born [brother], they say, is superior even to the one born of the same womb. ||Panc_4.6||

children.text: atha makary āha-tvayā kadācid api mama vacanaṃ nānyathā kṛtam | tan nūnaṃ sā vānarī bhaviṣyati, yatas tasyā anurāgataḥ sakalam api dinaṃ tatra gamayasi | tat tvaṃ jñāto mayā samyak | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then the female crocodile said: You have never disregarded my word. So surely that must be a she-monkey, since out of passion for her you spend the entire day there. So I have understood you properly. For —

children.text: sāhlādaṃ vacanaṃ prayacchati na me no vāñchitaṃ kiñcana
children.translated_text: You do not give me affectionate words, nor any desired thing;

children.text: prāyaḥ procchvasiṣi drutaṃ hutavaha-jvālā samaṃ rātriṣu |
children.translated_text: you mostly sigh quickly at nights, like flames of fire;

children.text: kaṇṭhāśleṣa-parigrahe śithilatā yan nādarāc cumbase
children.translated_text: there is slackness in the embrace of the neck, and you do not kiss with affection —

children.text: tat te dhūrta hṛdi sthitā priyatamā kācin mamevāparā ||Panc_4.7||
children.translated_text: so, O rogue, there is some other beloved lodged in your heart besides me. ||Panc_4.7||

children.text: so 'pi patnyāḥ pādopasaṅgrahaṃ kṛtvāṅkopari nidhāya tasyāḥ kopa-koṭim āpannāyāḥ sudīnam uvāca-
children.translated_text: And he, having grasped his wife's feet and placed them on his lap, said pitifully to her who had reached the extreme of anger —

children.text: mayi te pāda-patite kiṅkaratvam upāgate |
children.translated_text: When I have fallen at your feet, become your slave —

children.text: tvaṃ prāṇa-vallabhe kasmāt kopane kopam eṣyasi ||Panc_4.8||
children.translated_text: why, O life's beloved, would you be angry in anger? ||Panc_4.8||

children.text: sāpi tad-vacanam ākarṇyāśru-pluta-mukhī tam uvāca-
children.translated_text: And she, hearing his words, her face flooded with tears, said to him —

children.text: sārdhaṃ manoratha-śatais tava dhūrta kāntā
children.translated_text: Together with a hundred wishes, O rogue, that mistress of yours

children.text: saiva sthitā manasi kṛtrima-bhāva-ramyā |
children.translated_text: remains lodged in your mind, charming with artificial feelings;

children.text: asmākam asti na kathañcid ihāvakāśaṃ
children.translated_text: for us there is no room here at all —

children.text: tasmāt kṛtaṃ caraṇa-pāta-viḍambanābhiḥ ||Panc_4.9||
children.translated_text: so enough with these mockeries of falling at [my] feet! ||Panc_4.9||

children.text: aparaṃ sā yadi tava vallabhā na bhavati, tat kiṃ mayā bhaṇito 'pi tāṃ na vyāpādayasi | atha yadi sa vānaras tat kas tena saha tava snehaḥ ? tat kiṃ bahunā ? yadi tasya hṛdayaṃ na bhakṣayāmi, tan mayā prāyopaveśanaṃ kṛtaṃ viddhi |
children.translated_text: Moreover, if she is not your beloved, then why do you not kill her even when told by me? But if it is a male monkey, then what affection do you have with him? What more [need be said]? If I do not eat his heart, know that I have undertaken a fast unto death!

children.text: evaṃ tasyās tan niścayaṃ jñātvā cintā-vyākulita-hṛdayaḥ sa provāca-athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Thus knowing her resolve, his heart agitated with worry, he said: Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: vajra-lepasya mūrkhasya nārīṇāṃ karkaṭasya ca |
children.translated_text: Of adamantine paste, a fool, women, a crab,

children.text: eko grahas tu mīnānāṃ nīlī-madya-payos tathā ||Panc_4.10||
children.translated_text: and of fish, indigo, and wine with milk — there is only one grasp [i.e., they never let go]. ||Panc_4.10||

children.text: tat kiṃ karomi ? kathaṃ sa me vadhyo bhavati | iti vicintya vānara-pārśvam agamat | vānaro 'pi cirād āyāntaṃ taṃ sodvegam avalokya provāca-bho mitra ! kim adya cira-velāyāṃ samāyāto 'si ? kasmāt sāhlādaṃ nālapasi ? na subhāṣitāni paṭhasi |
children.translated_text: So what shall I do? How can he be killed by me? Having deliberated thus, he went to the monkey's side. The monkey too, seeing him arriving after a long time, looked at him with anxiety and said: O friend! Why have you come today so late? Why do you not speak cheerfully? Why do you not recite wise sayings?

children.text: sa āha-mitra ! ahaṃ tava bhrātṛ-jāyayā niṣṭhuratarair vākyair abhihitaḥ-bhoḥ kṛtaghna ! mā me tvaṃ svamukhaṃ darśaya, yatas tvaṃ pratidinaṃ mitram upajīvasi | na ca tasya punaḥ pratyupakāraṃ gṛha-darśana-mātreṇāpi karoṣi | tat te prāyaścittam api nāsti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: Friend! I have been spoken to with very harsh words by your sister-in-law: 'O ungrateful one! Do not show me your face, since every day you live off your friend, and you never reciprocate him even with so much as a visit to your home. So there is no atonement for you either.' And it is said —

children.text: brahmaghne ca surāpe ca caure bhagna-vrate śaṭhe |
children.translated_text: For a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a drinker of liquor, a thief, a breaker of vows, and a rogue —

children.text: niṣkṛtir vihitā sadbhiḥ kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ ||Panc_4.11||
children.translated_text: atonement has been prescribed by the good; for the ungrateful there is no atonement. ||Panc_4.11||

children.text: tat tvaṃ mama devaraṃ gṛhītvādya pratyupakārārthaṃ gṛham ānaya | no cet tvayā saha me para-loke darśanam iti | tad ahaṃ tayaivaṃ proktas tava sakāśam āgataḥ | tad adya tayā saha tvad-arthe kalahāyato mameyatī velā vilagnā | tad āgaccha me gṛham | tava bhrātṛ-patnī racita-catuṣkā praguṇita-vastra-maṇi-māṇikyādy-ucitābharaṇā dvāra-deśa-baddha-vandana-mālā sotkaṇṭhā tiṣṭhati | markaṭa āha-bho mitra ! yuktam abhihitaṃ mad-bhrātṛ-patnyā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So you should take my brother-in-law and bring him home today for the purpose of reciprocation. Otherwise there will be no meeting between me and you in the next world. So, having been told thus by her, I have come to you. Now today, while quarreling with her on your account, this much time has been lost for me. So come to my house! Your sister-in-law stands at the threshold with a four-fold [arrangement prepared], adorned with proper garments, gems, rubies and other fitting ornaments, with welcome-garlands hung at the doorway, eager [to meet you]. The monkey said: O friend! What your wife has said is proper. And it is said —

children.text: varjayet kaulikākāraṃ mitraṃ prājñataro naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A wise man should avoid a friend who acts like a weaver —

children.text: ātmanaḥ sammukhaṃ nityaṃ ya ākarṣati lolupaḥ ||Panc_4.12||
children.translated_text: who always draws [others] toward himself, greedy. ||Panc_4.12||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: dadāti pratigṛhṇāti guhyam ākhyāti pṛcchati |
children.translated_text: Giving and receiving, telling and asking secrets,

children.text: bhuṅkte bhojayate caiva ṣaḍ-vidhaṃ prīti-lakṣaṇam ||Panc_4.13||
children.translated_text: eating and feeding — these are the six marks of affection. ||Panc_4.13||

children.text: paraṃ vayaṃ vanacarāḥ yuṣmadīyaṃ ca jalānte gṛham | tat kathaṃ śakyate tatra gantum | tasmāt tām api me bhrātṛ-patnīm atrānaya yena praṇamya tasyā āśīrvādaṃ gṛhṇāmi |
children.translated_text: But we are forest-dwellers and your home is in the middle of water. So how is it possible to go there? Therefore bring that sister-in-law of mine here too, so that having bowed I may receive her blessings.

children.text: sa āha-bho mitra ! asti samudrāntare suramye pulina-pradeśe'smad-gṛham æ tan mama pṛṣṭham ārūdhaḥ sukhenākṛta-bhayo gaccha |
children.translated_text: He said: O friend! Our home is on a beautiful sandbank in the middle of the ocean. So, mounted on my back, go without fear and at ease.

children.text: so 'pi tac chrutvā sānandam āha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tat kiṃ vilambyate | tvaryatām | eṣo 'haṃ tava pṛṣṭhām ārūḍhaḥ |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing that, said with joy: Good friend! If so, then why delay? Hurry! Here I am, mounted on your back!

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite'gādhe jaladhau gacchantaṃ marakam ālokya bhaya-trasta-manā vānaraḥ provāca-bhrātaḥ ! śanaiḥ śanair gamyatām | jala-kallolaiḥ plāvyate me śarīram |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, the monkey, seeing the crocodile going in the fathomless ocean, his mind terrified with fear, said: Brother! Go slowly, slowly! My body is being splashed by the waves.

children.text: tad ākarṇya makaraś cintayāmāsa-asāv agādhaṃ jalaṃ prāpto me vaśaḥ sañjātaḥ | mat-pṛṣṭha-gatas tila-mātram api calituṃ na śaknoti | tasmāt kathayāmy asya nijābhiprāyam, yenābhīṣṭa-devatā-smaraṇaṃ karoti | āha ca-mitra, tvaṃ mayā vadhāya samānīto bhāryā-vākyena viśvāsya | tat smaryatām abhīṣṭa-devatā |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crocodile thought: He has entered deep water, he is in my power. He cannot move even a sesame-seed's distance from my back. Therefore I shall tell him my true intention, so that he may remember his chosen deity. And he said: Friend, you have been brought by me for killing, having been deceived by my wife's words. So remember your chosen deity.

children.text: sa āha-bhrātaḥ ! kiṃ mayā tasyās tavāpi cāpakṛtaṃ yena me vadhopāyaś cintitaḥ ?
children.translated_text: He said: Brother! What wrong have I done to her or to you, that a means of killing me has been devised?

children.text: makara āha-bhoḥ ! tasyās tāvat tava hṛdayasyāmṛtamaya-phala-rasāsvādana-mṛṣṭasya bhakṣaṇe dohadaḥ sañjātaḥ | tenaitad anuṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: Friend! She has developed a craving to eat your heart, which is delicious from the savoring of ambrosia-like fruit-juice. Therefore this has been carried out.

children.text: pratyutpanna-matir vānara āha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tat kiṃ tvayā mama tatraiva na vyāhṛtam ? yena sva-hṛdayaṃ jambū-koṭare sadaiva mayā suguptaṃ kṛtam | tad bhrātṛ-patnyā arpayāmi | tvayāhaṃ śūnya-hṛdayo 'tra kasmād ānītaḥ ?
children.translated_text: The monkey, being of ready wit, said: Good friend! If so, then why did you not tell me that there itself? For I always keep my own heart well-hidden in the hollow of the <s>jambū</s> tree. So I will give it to my sister-in-law. Why have you brought me here empty-hearted?

children.text: tad ākarṇya makaraḥ sānandam āha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tad arpaya me hṛdayam | yena sā duṣṭa-patnī tad bhakṣayitvānaśanād utthiṣṭhati | ahaṃ tvāṃ tam eva jambū-pādapaṃ prāpayāmi | evam uktvā nivartya jambū-talam agāt | vānaro 'pi katham api jalpita-vividha-devatopacāra-pūjas tīram āsāditavān | tataś ca dīrghatara-caṅkramaṇena tam eva jambū-pādapam ārūḍhaś cintayāmāsa-aho ! labdhās tāvat prāṇāḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crocodile said with joy: Good friend! If so, then give me the heart, so that my wicked wife, having eaten it, will rise from her fast. I shall take you to that very <s>jambū</s> tree. Having said this, he turned back and went to the base of the <s>jambū</s> tree. The monkey too, somehow making various prayers and worship to deities in speech, reached the shore. Then with a very long leap he climbed that very <s>jambū</s> tree and thought: Ah! My life has been obtained! Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: na viśvased aviśvaste viśvaste'pi na viśvaset |
children.translated_text: One should not trust the untrustworthy, nor trust even the trustworthy;

children.text: viśvāsād bhayam utpannaṃ mūlāny api nikṛntati ||Panc_4.14||
children.translated_text: fear born from trust cuts even the roots. ||Panc_4.14||

children.text: tan mamaitad adya punar janma-dinam iva sañjātam |
children.translated_text: So today is as if a second birthday has come for me.

children.text: iti cintayamānaṃ makara āha-bho mitra ! arpaya tad dhṛdayaṃ yathā te bhrātṛ-patnī bhakṣayitvānaśanād uttiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: While he was thus thinking, the crocodile said: O friend! Give me that heart so that your sister-in-law, having eaten it, may rise from her fast.

children.text: atha vihasya nirbhartsayan vānaras tam āha-dhig dhiṅ mūrkha viśvāsa-ghātaka ! kiṃ kasyacid dhṛdaya-dvayaṃ bhavati ? tad āśu gamyatāṃ jambū-vṛkṣasyādhastān na bhūyo 'pi tvayātrāgantavyam | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then the monkey, laughing and rebuking him, said: Shame, shame on you, fool, betrayer of trust! Does anyone have two hearts? So go away quickly from beneath the <s>jambū</s> tree — you should never come here again! And it is said, for —

children.text: sakṛd duṣṭaṃ ca yo mitraṃ punaḥ sandhātum icchati |
children.translated_text: He who wishes to reunite with a friend who has once proved treacherous —

children.text: sa mṛtyum upagṛhṇāti garbham aśvatarī yathā ||Panc_4.15||
children.translated_text: he embraces death, like a she-mule [embraces] a fetus. ||Panc_4.15||

children.text: tac chrutvā makaraḥ saṃvilakṣaṃ cintitavān-aho ! mayātimūḍhena kim asya sva-cittābhiprāyo niveditaḥ | tad yady asau punar api kathañcid viśvāsaṃ gacchati, tad bhūyo 'pi viśvāsayāmi | āha ca-mitra ! hāsyena mayā te'bhiprāyo labdhaḥ | tasyā na kiñcit tava hṛdayena prayojanam | tad āgaccha prāghuṇika-nyāyenāsmad-gṛham |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crocodile thought with embarrassment: Ah! Being extremely foolish, why did I reveal to him my inner intention? So if he somehow comes to trust [me] again, then I shall win his trust again. And he said: Friend! I was testing you in jest. She has no use for your heart at all. So come as a guest to our home.

children.text: vānara āha-bho duṣṭa ! gamyatām | adhunā nāham āgamiṣyāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The monkey said: O wicked one! Go away! I shall not come now. And it is said —

children.text: bubhukṣitaḥ kiṃ na karoti pāpaṃ
children.translated_text: What sin does a hungry one not commit?

children.text: kṣīṇā janā niṣkaruṇā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: Impoverished people become merciless.

children.text: ākhyāhi bhadre priya-darśanasya
children.translated_text: Tell me, O good one, of the fair-looking one —

children.text: na gaṅgadattaḥ punar eti kūpam ||Panc_4.16||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> does not go to the well again! ||Panc_4.16||

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: How is that?

children.text: sa āha-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text:
kathā 1
gaṅgadatta-priyadarśana-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 1
The Story of <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> and <s>Priyadarśana</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścit kūpe gaṅgadatto nāma maṇḍūka-rājaḥ prativasati sma | sa kadācid dāyādair udvejito 'raghaṭṭa-ghaṭīm āruhya niṣkrāntaḥ | atha tena cintitam-yat kathaṃ tesāṃ dāyādānāṃ mayā pratyapakāraḥ kartavyaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
