children.translated_text: In a certain well there dwelt a frog-king named <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>. Once, harassed by his kinsmen, he climbed into a bucket of the water-wheel and came out. Then he thought: How shall I take revenge against those kinsmen? And it is said —

children.text: āpadi yenāpakṛtaṃ yena ca hasitaṃ daśāsu viṣamāsu |
children.translated_text: He by whom harm was done to [one] in distress, and he by whom [one] was mocked in adverse conditions —

children.text: apakṛtya tayor ubhayoḥ punar api jātaṃ naraṃ manye ||Panc_4.17||
children.translated_text: having retaliated against both of them, I consider a man truly born again. ||Panc_4.17||

children.text: evaṃ cintayan bile praviśantaṃ kṛṣṇasarpam apaśyat | taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyo 'py acintayat-yad enaṃ tatra kūpe nītvā sakala-dāyādānām ucchedaṃ karomi | uktaṃ ca-
śatrubhir yojayec chatruṃ balinā balavattaram |
children.translated_text: One should set an enemy against an enemy, a more powerful one against the strong,

children.text: sva-kāryāya yato na syāt kācit pīḍātra tat-kṣaye ||Panc_4.18||
children.translated_text: for one's own purpose — since there will be no harm from their mutual destruction. ||Panc_4.18||
While thinking thus, he saw a black serpent entering a hole. Seeing it, he thought further: I shall take this one to the well and bring about the destruction of all my kinsmen. And it is said —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: śatrum unmūlayet prājñas tīkṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇena śatruṇā |
children.translated_text: The wise one should uproot an enemy with a sharp enemy;

children.text: vyathā-karaṃ sukhārthāya kaṇṭakenaiva kaṇṭakam ||Panc_4.19||
children.translated_text: causing pain for the sake of comfort — [like removing] a thorn with a thorn. ||Panc_4.19||

children.text: evaṃ sa vibhāvya bila-dvāraṃ gatvā tam āhūtavān-ehy ehi priya-darśana ! ehi !
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, going to the entrance of the hole, he called out: Come, come, <s>Priyadarśana</s>! Come!

children.text: tac chrutvā sarpaś cintayāmāsa-ya evaṃ mām āhvayati | svajātīyo na bhavati | yato naiṣā sarpa-vāṇī | anyena kenāpi saha mama martya-loke sandhānaṃ nāsti | tad atraiva durge sthitas tāvad vedmi ko 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the serpent thought: The one who calls me thus is not of my own species, for this is not a serpent's voice. And I have no alliance with anyone else in the mortal world. So, remaining here in this very fortress, I shall know who this will be. And it is said —

children.text: yasya na jāyate śīlaṃ na kulaṃ na ca saṃśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose character is not known, nor his family, nor his allegiance —

children.text: na tena saṅgatiṃ kuryād ity uvāca bṛhaspatiḥ ||Panc_4.20||
children.translated_text: one should not make association with him — so declared <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. ||Panc_4.20||

children.text: kadācitko 'pi mantravādy auṣadha-caturo vā mām āhūya bandhane kṣipati | athavā kaścit puruṣo vairam āśritya kasyacid bhakṣaṇārthe mām āhvayati | āha ca-bhoḥ ! ko bhavān ?
children.translated_text: 'Some spell-caster or one skilled in medicines might summon me and throw me into captivity. Or perhaps some man, out of enmity, might invite me for someone else's meal.' And he [the crocodile] said: 'Sir! Who are you?'

children.text: sa āha-ahaṃ gaṅgadatto nāma maṇḍūkādhipatis tvat-sakāśe maitry-artham abhyāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'I am <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, lord of the frogs, and I have come to your presence for the purpose of friendship.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sarpa āha-bho ! aśraddheyam etat yat-tṛṇānāṃ vahninā saha saṅgamaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the serpent said: 'Sir! This is unbelievable — that grass should have fellowship with fire!' And it is said —

children.text: yo yasya jāyate vadhyaḥ sa svapne'pi kathañcana |
children.translated_text: He who is born to be killed by another — even in a dream, somehow,

children.text: na tat-samīpam abhyeti tat kim evaṃ prajalpasi ||Panc_4.21||
children.translated_text: he does not approach that one's vicinity; so why do you prattle thus? // Panc_4.21 //

children.text: gaṅgadatta āha-bhoḥ ! satyam etat | svabhāva-vairī tvam asmākam | paraṃ para-paribhavāt prāpto 'haṃ te sakāśam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> said: 'Sir! This is true. You are our natural enemy. But I have come to you because of humiliation by others.' And it is said —

children.text: sarva-nāśe ca sañjāte prāṇānām api saṃśaye |
children.translated_text: When total destruction has arisen and even life is in doubt,

children.text: api śatruṃ praṇamyāpi rakṣet prāṇāndhanāni ca ||Panc_4.22||
children.translated_text: one should protect one's life and wealth even by bowing to the enemy. // Panc_4.22 //

children.text: sarpa āha-kathaya kasmāt te paribhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: The serpent said: 'Tell me — from whom comes your humiliation?'

children.text: sa āha-dāyādebhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'From my kinsmen.'

children.text: so 'py āha-kva te āśrayo vāpyāṃ kūpe taḍāge hrade vā | tat kathaya svāśrayam |
children.translated_text: The serpent also said: 'Where is your abode — in a pond, a well, a tank, or a lake? Tell me your dwelling place.'

children.text: tenoktam-pāṣāṇa-caya-nibaddhe kūpe |
children.translated_text: He replied: 'In a well constructed of piled stones.'

children.text: sarpa āha-aho apadā vayam | tatrāsti tatra me praveśaḥ | praviṣṭasya ca sthānaṃ nāsti | yatra sthitas tava dāyādān vyāpādayāmi | tad gamyatām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The serpent said: 'Ah, but I am footless. Can I gain entry there? And even if I enter, there is no place [for me to stay]. Where I can stand, I will destroy your kinsmen. So proceed.' And it is said —

children.text: yac chakyaṃ grasituṃ yasya grastaṃ pariṇamec ca yat |
children.translated_text: That which one is able to swallow, which when swallowed is digested,

children.text: hitaṃ ca pariṇāme yat tad ādyaṃ bhūtim icchatā ||Panc_4.23||
children.translated_text: and which is beneficial in its result — that should be consumed first by one who desires prosperity. // Panc_4.23 //

children.text: gaṅgadatta āha-bhoḥ ! samāgaccha tvam | ahaṃ sukhopāyena tatra tava praveśaṃ kārayiṣyāmi | tathā tasya madhye jalopānte ramyataraṃ koṭaram asti | tatra sthitas tvaṃ līlayā dāyādān vyāpādayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> said: 'Sir! Come along. I shall have you enter there comfortably by an easy means. Moreover, in its middle, at the water's edge, there is a most delightful hollow. Stationed there, you will effortlessly destroy my kinsmen.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sarpo vyacintayat-ahaṃ tāvat pariṇata-vayāḥ | kadācit kathañcin mūṣakam ekaṃ prāpnomi | tat sukhāvaho jīvanopāyo 'yam anena kulāṅgāreṇa darśitaḥ | tad gatvā tān maṇḍūkān bhakṣayāmi iti | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the serpent reflected: 'I am now advanced in age. Sometimes, with difficulty, I obtain a single mouse. So this is a comfortable means of livelihood shown to me by this disgrace to his family. I shall go and eat those frogs.' Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: yo hi prāṇa-parikṣīṇaḥ sahāya-parivarjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is depleted in vitality and bereft of allies —

children.text: sa hi sarva-sukhopāyāṃ vṛttim āracayed budhaḥ ||Panc_4.24||
children.translated_text: that wise one should undertake a livelihood [that provides] all comforts. // Panc_4.24 //

children.text:
evaṃ vicintya tam āha-bho gaṅgadatta ! yady evaṃ tad-agre bhava | yena tatra gacchāvaḥ |
gaṅgadatta āha-bhoḥ priyadarśana ! ahaṃ tvāṃ sukhopāyena tatra neṣyāmi, sthānaṃ ca darśayiṣyāmi ta eva bhakṣaṇīyāḥ iti |
children.translated_text:
Having thus reflected, he said to him: 'O <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>! If so, then go ahead, so that we may go there.'
<s>Gaṅgadatta</s> said: 'O <s>Priyadarśana</s>! I shall take you there comfortably and show you the place — those very ones are to be eaten.'

children.text: sarpa āha-sāmprataṃ tvaṃ me mitraṃ jātam | tan na bhetavyam | tava vacanena bhakṣaṇyās te dāyādāḥ |
children.translated_text: The serpent said: 'Now you have become my friend. So there is nothing to fear. At your word, those kinsmen of yours shall be eaten.'

children.text: evam uktvā bilān niṣkramya tam āliṅgya ca tenaiva saha prasthitaḥ | atha kūpam āsādyāra-ghaṭṭa-ghaṭikā-mārgeṇa sarpas tenātmanā svālayaṃ nītaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he came out of his hole, embraced him, and set out together with him. Then, having reached the well, the serpent was led by him to his own abode through the passage of the water-wheel buckets.

children.text: gaṅgadatta āha-bhadra ! kutaḥ tvayā mitra-kṛtyam | tat sāmpratam anenaiva ghaṭikā-yantra-mārgeṇa gamyatām iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> said: 'Good friend! Where to begin your friendly service? For now, go through this very passage of the bucket-mechanism.'

children.text: sarpa āha-bho gaṅgadatta ! na samyag abhihitaṃ tvayā | katham ahaṃ tatra gacchāmi ? madīya-bila-durgam anyena ruddhaṃ bhaviṣyati | tasmād atra-sthasya me maṇḍūkam ekaikaṃ sva-vargīyaṃ prayaccha | no cet sarvān api bhakṣayiṣyāmi iti |
children.translated_text: The serpent said: 'O <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>! What you have said is not right. How shall I go back that way? My own fortress-hole will be blocked by someone else. Therefore, staying here, give me one frog of your own clan each [day] — otherwise I shall eat them all.'

children.text: tac chrutvā gaṅgadatto vyākula-manā vyācintayat-aho kim etan mayā kṛtaṃ sarpam ānayatā | tad yadi niṣedhayiṣyāmi tat sarvān api bhakṣayiṣyati | athavā yuktam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, his mind agitated, reflected: 'Alas, what have I done by bringing this serpent! If I refuse him, he will eat them all.' Indeed, it is rightly said —

children.text: yo 'mitraṃ kurute mitraṃ vīryābhyadhikam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who makes an enemy mightier than himself into a friend —

children.text: sa karoti na sandehaḥ svayaṃ hi viṣa-bhakṣaṇam ||Panc_4.25||
children.translated_text: there is no doubt that he brings about his own consuming of poison. // Panc_4.25 //

children.text: tat prayacchāmy asyaikaikaṃ pratidinaṃ suhṛdam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So I shall give him one friend each day.' And it is said —

children.text: sarvasva-haraṇe yuktaṃ śatruṃ buddhi-yutā narāḥ |
children.translated_text: Wise men placate an enemy bent on seizing everything

children.text: toṣayanty alpa-dānena bāḍavaṃ sāgaro yathā ||Panc_4.26||
children.translated_text: with a small gift — as the ocean [appeases] the submarine fire. // Panc_4.26 //

children.text: tathā ca-
yo durbalo 'ṇūn api yācyamāno
children.translated_text: He who is weak, when asked for even small things

children.text: balīyasā yacchati naiva sāmnā |
children.translated_text: by one stronger, does not yield even with conciliation,

children.text: prayacchate naiva ca darśyamānaṃ
children.translated_text: and does not yield even what is pointed out [as owed] —

children.text: khārīṃ sa cūrṇasya punar dadāti ||Panc_4.27||
children.translated_text: he ends up giving a whole measure of powder [i.e., everything]. // Panc_4.27 //
And likewise —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: sarva-nāśe samutpanne ardhaṃ tyajati paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: When total destruction has arisen, the wise man sacrifices half;

children.text: ardhena kurute kāryaṃ sarva-nāśo hi dustaraḥ ||Panc_4.28||
children.translated_text: with the other half he accomplishes his purpose — for total destruction is hard to overcome. // Panc_4.28 //

children.text: na svalpasya kṛte bhūri nāśayen matimān naraḥ |
children.translated_text: An intelligent man should not destroy much for the sake of little;

children.text: etad eva hi pāṇḍityaṃ yat svalpād bhūri-rakṣaṇam ||Panc_4.29||
children.translated_text: this indeed is wisdom — the protection of the greater by [sacrificing] the lesser. // Panc_4.29 //

children.text: evaṃ niścintya nityam ekaikam ādiśati | so 'pi taṃ bhakṣayitvā tasya parokṣe'nyān api bhakṣayati | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, he daily designated one [frog]. And the serpent, having devoured that one, also devoured others behind his back. Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: yathā hi malinair vastrair yatra tatropaviśyate |
children.translated_text: Just as with soiled garments, one sits down anywhere and everywhere,

children.text: evaṃ calita-vittas tu vitta-śeṣaṃ na rakṣati ||Panc_4.30||
children.translated_text: so too one whose wealth has been disturbed does not guard the remainder of his wealth. // Panc_4.30 //

children.text: athānya-dine tenāparān maṇḍūkān bhakṣayitvā gaṅgadatta-suto yamunādatto bhakṣitaḥ | taṃ bhakṣitaṃ matvā gaṅgadattas tāra-svareṇa dhig dhik pralāpa-paraḥ kathañcid api na virarāma | tataḥ sva-patnyābhihitaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, on another day, having devoured the other frogs, the serpent ate <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>'s son, <s>Yamunādatta</s>. Knowing him to be eaten, <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, crying out in a loud voice, given over to wailing 'Woe! Woe!' could not be calmed at all. Then his own wife said to him —

children.text: kiṃ krandasi durākranda sva-pakṣa-kṣaya-kāraka |
children.translated_text: 'Why do you cry, you of vile cries, you who brought about the destruction of your own clan?

children.text: sva-pakṣasya kṣaye jāte ko nas trātā bhaviṣyati ||Panc_4.31||
children.translated_text: When the clan has been destroyed, who will be our protector?' // Panc_4.31 //

children.text: tad adyāpi vicintyatām ātmano niṣkramaṇam asya vadhopāyaś ca | atha gacchatā kālena sakalam api kavalitaṃ maṇḍūka-kulam | kevalam eko gaṅgadattas tiṣṭhati | tataḥ priyadarśanena bhaṇitam-bhoḥ gaṅgadatta ! bubhukṣito 'ham | niḥśeṣitāḥ sarve maṇḍūkāḥ | tad dīyatāṃ me kiñcid bhojanaṃ yato 'haṃ tvayātrānītaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'So even now, think of a way to escape and a means to kill him.' Then, as time passed, the serpent devoured the entire frog clan. Only <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> alone remained. Then <s>Priyadarśana</s> said: 'O <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>! I am hungry. All the frogs are exhausted. So give me some food, since it was you who brought me here.'

children.text: sa āha-bho mitra ! na tvayātra viṣaye mayāvasthitena kāpi cintā kāryā | tad yadi māṃ preṣayati tato 'nya-kūpa-sthān api maṇḍūkān viśvāsyātrānayāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'O friend! You need not have any concern about this while I am here. If you will send me out, I shall bring frogs from other wells too, having won their trust.'

children.text: sa āha-mama tāvat tvam abhakṣyo bhrātṛ-sthāne | tad yady evaṃ karoṣi tat sāmprataṃ pitṛ-sthāne bhavasi | tad evaṃ kriyatām iti |
children.translated_text: He said: 'You are not to be eaten by me — you are like a brother to me. So if you do this, you will now be like a father to me. So let it be done thus.'

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇyāra-ghaṭṭa-ghaṭikām āśritya vividha-devatopakalpita-pūjopayācitas tat-kūpād viniṣkrāntaḥ | priyadarśano 'pi tad-ākāṅkṣayā tatrasthaḥ pratīkṣamāṇas tiṣṭhati | atha cirād anāgate gaṅgadatte priyadarśano 'nya-koṭara-nivāsinīṃ godhām uvāca-bhadre ! kriyatāṃ stokaṃ sāhāyyam | yataś cira-paricitas te gaṅgadattaḥ | tad gatvā tat-sakāśaṃ kutracij jalāśaye'nviṣya mama sandeśaṃ kathaya | yenāgamyatām ekākināpi bhavatā drutataraṃ yady anye maṇḍūkā nāgacchanti | ahaṃ tvayā vinā nātra vastuṃ śaknomi | tathā yady ahaṃ tava viruddham ācarāmi tat sukṛtam antare mayā vidhṛtam |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing that, clinging to the bucket of the water-wheel, worshipped with offerings to various deities and with prayers, emerged from that well. <s>Priyadarśana</s> too, expectant, stood there waiting. Then, when <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> did not come for a long time, <s>Priyadarśana</s> said to a monitor lizard dwelling in another hollow: 'Good lady! Do me a small favor. For you have long been acquainted with <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>. So go to him, search for him at some water-body, and deliver my message: "Come quickly, even alone, if other frogs will not come. I cannot live here without you." Also, if I have done anything hostile to you, then let my merit be forfeit.'

children.text: godhāpi tad-vacanād gaṅgadattaṃ drutataram anviṣyāha-bhadra gaṅgadatta ! sa tava suhṛt-priyadarśanas tava mārgaṃ samīkṣamāṇas tiṣṭhati | tac chīghram āgamyatām iti |
children.translated_text: The monitor lizard too, at his word, quickly sought out <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> and said: 'Good <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>! That friend of yours, <s>Priyadarśana</s>, stands watching for your return. So come quickly.'

children.text: aparaṃ ca tena tava virūpa-karaṇe sukṛtam antare dhṛtam | tan-niḥśaṅena manasā samāgamyatām | tad ākarṇya gaṅgadatta āha-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, he has pledged his merit as surety against doing you harm.' So come with a fearless mind.' Hearing that, <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> said —

children.text: bubhukṣitaḥ kiṃ na karoti pāpaṃ
children.translated_text: 'What sin does a hungry one not commit?

children.text: kṣīṇā narā niṣkaruṇā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: Men who are depleted become merciless.

children.text: ākhyāhi bhadre priya-darśanasya
children.translated_text: Tell him, good lady, tell <s>Priyadarśana</s>:

children.text: na gaṅgadattaḥ punar eti kūpam ||Panc_4.32||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> will not return to the well.' // Panc_4.32 //

children.text: evam uktvā sa tāṃ visarjayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he dismissed her.

children.text: tad bho duṣṭa-jalacara ! aham api gaṅgadatta iva tvad-gṛhe na kathañcid api yāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: 'So, you wicked aquatic creature! I too, like <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, will by no means go to your home.'

children.text: tac chrutvā makara āha-bho mitra ! athavātrāham anaśanāt prāṇa-tyāgaṃ tavopari kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crocodile said: 'O friend! Or else, right here, I shall give up my life by fasting on your account.'

children.text: vānara āha-mūḍha ! kim ahaṃ lambakarṇo mūrkhaḥ ? dṛṣṭvāpāyo 'pi svayam eva tatra gatvātmānaṃ vyāpādayāmi |
children.translated_text: The monkey said: 'Fool! Am I that dull-witted donkey <s>Lambakarṇa</s>? That even after seeing danger I would go there myself and get myself killed?'

children.text: āgataś ca gataś caiva gatvā yaḥ punar āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who came and went, and having gone, came back again —

children.text: akarṇa-hṛdayo mūrkhas tatraiva nidhanaṃ gataḥ ||Panc_4.33||
children.translated_text: that fool without ears and heart met his death right there.' // Panc_4.33 //

children.text:
makara āha-bhadra ! sa ko lambha-karṇaḥ | kathaṃ dṛṣṭāpāyo 'pi mṛtaḥ ? tan me nivedyatām |
vānara āha-
kathā 2
karāla-kesara-kathā
children.translated_text:
The crocodile said: 'Good friend! Who is this <s>Lambakarṇa</s>? How did he die even after seeing danger? Tell me that.'
The monkey said:
Tale 2
The Story of <s>Karālakesara</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe karāla-kesaro nāma siṃhaḥ prativasati sma | tasya ca dhūsarako nāma śṛgālaḥ sadaivānuyāyī paricārako 'sti | atha kadācit tasya hastinā saha yudhyamānasya śarīre gurutarāḥ prahārāḥ sañjātāḥ | yaiḥ padam ekam api calituṃ na śaknoti | tasyācalanāc ca dhūsarakaḥ kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭho daurbalyaṃ gataḥ | anyasminn ahani tam avocat-svāmin ! bubhukṣaya pīḍito 'ham | padāt padam api calituṃ na śaknomi | tat kathaṃ te śuśrūṣāṃ karomi ?
children.translated_text: In a certain forest region there lived a lion named <s>Karālakesara</s>. And he had a jackal named <s>Dhūsaraka</s> who was always his follower and attendant. Now one day, while fighting with an elephant, very heavy blows were inflicted on his body, by which he could not move even a single step. And because of his immobility, <s>Dhūsaraka</s>, his throat emaciated with hunger, became weak. On another day he said to him: 'Master! I am tormented by hunger. I cannot move even a step. So how shall I serve you?'

children.text: siṃha āha-bhoḥ ! gaccha anveṣaya kiñcit sattvam | yenemām avasthāṃ gato 'pi vyāpādayāmi |
children.translated_text: The lion said: 'Go! Seek out some creature, so that even in this condition I may kill it.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya śṛgālo 'nveṣayan kañcit samīpa-vartinaṃ grāmam āsāditavān | tatra lambakarṇo nāma gardabhas taḍāgopānte pravirala-dūrvāṅkurān kṛcchrād āsvādayan dṛṣṭaḥ | tataś ca samīpa-vartinā bhūtvā tenābhihitaḥ-māma ! namaskāro 'yaṃ madīyaḥ sambhāvyatām | cirād dṛṣṭo 'si | tat kathaya kim evaṃ durbalatāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the jackal, searching, came upon a certain village nearby. There he spotted a donkey named <s>Lambakarṇa</s>, at the edge of a pond, laboriously nibbling sparse shoots of <s>dūrvā</s> grass. Then, having come close to him, he said: 'Uncle! Accept this greeting of mine. It has been long since I last saw you. So tell me — why have you become so weak?'

children.text: sa āha-bho bhaginī-putra ! kiṃ kathayāmi | rajako 'tinirdayātibhāreṇa māṃ pīḍayati | ghāsa-muṣṭim api na prayacchati | kevalaṃ dūrvāṅkurān dhūi-miśritān bhakṣayāmi | tat kuto me śarīre puṣṭiḥ ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'O nephew! What can I say? The washerman, excessively cruel, torments me with excessive loads. He does not even give me a handful of fodder. I eat only <s>dūrvā</s> shoots mixed with dust. So whence would there be nourishment in my body?'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-māma ! yady evaṃ tad asti marakata-sadṛśa-śaṣpa-prāyo nadī-sanātho ramaṇīyataraḥ pradeśaḥ | tatrāgatya mayā saha subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-sukham anubhavaṃs tiṣṭha |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Uncle! If so, then there is a region abounding in emerald-like grass, bordered by a river, most delightful. Come there and, in my company, enjoy the pleasure of conversing in fine sayings.'

children.text: lambakarṇa āha-bho bhaginī-suta ! yuktam uktaṃ bhavatā | paraṃ vayaṃ grāmyāḥ paśavo 'raṇya-cāriṇāṃ vadhyāḥ | tat kiṃ tena bhavya-pradeśena |
children.translated_text: <s>Lambakarṇa</s> said: 'O nephew! What you say is fitting. But we are domesticated animals, liable to be killed by forest-dwellers. So what good is that beautiful place?'

children.text: śṛgāla āha- māma ! maivaṃ vada | mad-bhuja-pañjara-parirakṣitaḥ sa deśaḥ | tatrāsti na kaścid aparasya tatra praveśaḥ | paramam anenaiva doṣeṇa rajaka-kadarthitās tatra tisro rāsabhyo 'nāthāḥ santi | tāś ca puṣṭim āpannā yauvanotkaṭā idaṃ mām ūcuḥ-yadi tvam asmākaṃ satyo mātulas tadā kaṃcid grāmāntaraṃ gatvāsmad-yogyaṃ kaścit patim ānaya | tad-arthe tvām ahaṃ tatra nayāmi |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Uncle! Do not say so! That region is protected by the cage of my arms. There is no entry for anyone else there. In fact, precisely because of this disadvantage — being mistreated by washermen — there are three she-donkeys there, ownerless. And they, having grown plump and bursting with youth, said this to me: "If you are truly our uncle, then go to some other village and bring us a husband worthy of us." It is for their sake that I am taking you there.'

children.text: atha śṛgāla-vacanāni śrutvā kāma-pīḍitāṅgas tam avocat-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tad-agre bhava yenāgacchāmi | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the jackal's words, his body tormented by desire, he said to him: 'Good friend! If so, then lead the way, so that I may come.' Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: nāmṛtaṃ na viṣaṃ kiñcid ekāṃ muktvā nitambinīm |
children.translated_text: Nothing is ambrosia and nothing is poison except one thing — a woman;

children.text: yasyāḥ saṅgena jīvyeta mriyate ca viyogataḥ ||Panc_4.34||
children.translated_text: by union with whom one lives, and by separation from whom one dies. // Panc_4.34 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: yāsāṃ nāmnāpi kāmaḥ syāt saṅgamaṃ darśanaṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: Those by whose very name desire would arise, even without meeting or seeing —

children.text: tāsāṃ dṛk-saṅgamaṃ prāpya yan na dravati kautukam ||Panc_4.35||
children.translated_text: upon meeting the gaze of those [she-donkeys], does not melt with curiosity. ||Panc_4.35||

children.text: tatrānuṣṭhite śṛgālena saha siṃhāntikam āgataḥ | siṃho 'pi vyathākulitas taṃ dṛṣṭvā yāvat samuttiṣṭhati tāvad rāsabhaḥ palāyitum ārabdhavān | atha tasya palāyamānasya siṃhena tala-prahāro dattaḥ | sa ca manda-bhāgyasya vyavasāya iva vyarthatāṃ gataḥ | atrāntare śṛgālaḥ kopāviṣṭas tam uvāca-bhoḥ ! kim evaṃvidhaḥ prahāras te | yad gardabho 'pi tava purato balād gacchati | tat kathaṃ gajena saha yuddhaṃ kariṣyasi ? tad dṛṣṭaṃ te balam |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, [the donkey] came with the jackal to the lion's side. The lion too, distressed [by his wounds], upon seeing him, was about to rise — but the donkey began to flee. Then the lion struck the fleeing [donkey] with a blow of his paw. But that [blow], like the resolution of an unfortunate man, went in vain. In the meanwhile, the jackal said angrily: 'Hey! What kind of a blow is that? When even a donkey escapes from you by force, how will you fight with an elephant? Now you have seen your own strength!'

children.text: atha savilakṣa-smitaṃ siṃha āha-bhoḥ ! kim ahaṃ karomi | mayā na kramaḥ sajjīkṛta āsīt | anyathā gajo 'pi mat-kramākrāntā na gacchati |
children.translated_text: Then the lion said with an embarrassed smile: 'Hey! What can I do? My stride had not been readied. Otherwise, not even an elephant, struck by my stride, could get away.'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-adyāpy eka-vāraṃ tavāntike tam āneṣyāmi | paraṃ tvayā sajjīkṛta-krameṇa sthātavyam |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Even today, one more time, I shall bring him to your side. But you must stand with your stride readied.'

children.text: siṃha āha-bhadra ! yo māṃ pratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā gataḥ sa punaḥ katham atrāgamiṣyati ? tad anyat kim api sattvam anviṣyatām |
children.translated_text: The lion said: 'Friend! He who has seen me face-to-face and fled — how will he come here again? So seek some other creature.'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-kiṃ tavānena vyāpāreṇa ? tvaṃ kevalaṃ sajjita-kramas tiṣṭha |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'What concern is that of yours? Just stand with your stride readied.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite śṛgālo 'pi yāvad rāsabha-mārgeṇa gacchati, tāvat tatraiva sthāne caran dṛṣṭaḥ | atha śṛgālaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāsabhaḥ prāha-bho bhaginī-suta ! śobhana-sthāne tvayāhaṃ nītaḥ | drāṅ mṛtyu-vaśaṃ gataḥ | tat kathaya kiṃ tat sattvaṃ yasyātiraudra-vajra-sadṛśa-kara-prahārād ahaṃ muktaḥ |
children.translated_text: When this was agreed, the jackal set out along the donkey's path. He found [the donkey] grazing in that same spot. Seeing the jackal, the donkey said: 'Ho, nephew! You took me to a fine place! I nearly fell into Death's power! So tell me — what was that creature, from whose terribly fierce, thunderbolt-like blow of the paw I barely escaped?'

children.text: tac chrutvā prahasan śṛgāla āha-bhadra ! rāsabhī tvām āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā sānurāgam āliṅgituṃ samutthitā | tvaṃ ca kātaratvān naṣṭaḥ | sā punar na śaktā tvāṃ vinā sthātum | tayā tu naśatas te'valambanārthaṃ hastaḥ kṣiptaḥ | nānya-kāraṇena | tad āgaccha | sā tvat-kṛte prāyopaveśanopaviṣṭā tiṣṭhati | etad vadati-yal lambakarṇo yadi me bhartā na bhavati tad aham agnau jalaṃ vā praviśāmi | punas tasya viyogaṃ soḍhuṃ na śaknomi iti | tat prasādaṃ kṛtvā tatrāgamyatām | no cet tava strī-hatyā bhaviṣyati | aparaṃ bhagavān kāma-kopaṃ tavopari kariṣyati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the jackal said with a laugh: 'Friend! That was a she-donkey! She rose with affection to embrace you as you approached. And you, out of cowardice, fled! She is unable to live without you. She has again — as you were running — stretched out her hand to hold you back. There is no other reason. So come! She has sat down in a fast unto death for your sake. She keeps saying: "If <s>Lambakarṇa</s> (Long-ears) does not become my husband, then I shall enter fire or water. I cannot bear separation from him again." So please show grace and come there. Otherwise you will incur the sin of killing a woman. Moreover, the blessed god of Love will be angry with you.' And it is said:

children.text: strī-mudrāṃ makaradhvajasya jayinīṃ sarvārdha-sampat-karīṃ
children.translated_text: The victorious seal-mark of <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (the God of Love), which brings all half-shared prosperity —

children.text: te mūḍhāḥ pravihāya yānti kudhiyo mithyā-phalānveṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: those fools who, abandoning it, go in pursuit of false fruits —

children.text: te tenaiva nihatya nirdayataraṃ nagnīkṛtā muṇḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: some of them are mercilessly struck down by him, stripped naked, and tonsured;

children.text: kecid rakta-paṭīkṛtāś ca jaṭilāḥ kāpālikāś cāpare ||Panc_4.36||
children.translated_text: some are made to wear red rags; and others become <s>jaṭilas</s> (matted-hair ascetics) or <s>Kāpālikas</s>. ||Panc_4.36||

children.text: athāsau tad-vacanaṃ śraddheyatayā śrutvā bhūyo 'pi tena saha prasthitaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Then he, hearing those words as trustworthy, set out again with him. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: jānann api naro daivāt prakaroti vigarhitam |
children.translated_text: A man, even though knowing [better], by fate performs what is reprehensible;

children.text: karma kiṃ kasyacil loke garhitaṃ rocate katham ||Panc_4.37||
children.translated_text: why would any reprehensible deed appeal to someone in this world? ||Panc_4.37||

children.text: atrāntare sajjita-krameṇa siṃhena sa lambakarṇo vyāpāditaḥ | tatas taṃ hatvā śṛgālaṃ rakṣakaṃ nirūpya svayaṃ snānārthaṃ nadyāṃ gataḥ | śṛgālenāpi laulyotsukyāt tasya karṇa-hṛdayaṃ bhakṣitam | atrāntare siṃho yāvat snātvā kṛte devārcanaḥ pratarpita-pitṛ-gaṇaḥ samāyāti tāvat karṇa-hṛdaya-rahito rāsabhas tiṣṭhati | taṃ dṛṣṭvā kopa-parītātmā siṃhaḥ śṛgālam āha-pāpa ! kim idam anucitaṃ karma samācaritam ? yat karṇa-hṛdaya-bhakṣaṇenāyam ucchiṣṭatāṃ nītaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile, the lion, with his stride readied, killed that <s>Lambakarṇa</s> (Long-ears). Then, having killed him and appointing the jackal as guard, he himself went to the river for bathing. And the jackal, from eager greed, ate the [donkey's] ears and heart. In the meanwhile, when the lion returned — having bathed, performed the worship of the gods, and propitiated the ancestors — the donkey stood there without ears or heart. Seeing that, the lion, his soul filled with anger, said to the jackal: 'Wretch! What improper deed have you committed? By eating the ears and heart, you have made this into leavings!'

children.text: śṛgālaḥ sa-vinayam āha-svāmin ! mā maivaṃ vada | yat karṇa-hṛdaya-rahito 'yaṃ rāsabha āsīt, tenehāgatya tvām avalokya bhūyo 'py āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: The jackal said respectfully: 'Master! Do not, do not speak thus! This donkey was without ears or heart — that is precisely why, having come here and seen you, he came back again.'

children.text: atha tvad-vacanaṃ śraddheyaṃ matvā siṃhas tenaiva saṃvibhajya niḥśaṅkita-manās taṃ bhakṣitavān |
children.translated_text: Then the lion, considering his words trustworthy, sharing [the meat] with him, ate it with an untroubled mind.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-āgataś ca gataś caiva iti | tan mūrkha ! kapaṭaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā | paraṃ yudhiṣṭhireṇeva satya-vacanena vināśitam | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Having come and gone...' and so on. So, fool! You have practiced deception. But [you are ruined] just as by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s truthful speech [he was] destroyed. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: svārtham utsṛjya yo dambhī satyaṃ brūte sumanda-dhīḥ |
children.translated_text: The hypocrite of dull mind who, abandoning self-interest, speaks the truth —

children.text: sa svārthād bhraśyate nūnaṃ yudhiṣṭhira ivāparaḥ ||Panc_4.38||
children.translated_text: he surely falls from his own interest, like another <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. ||Panc_4.38||

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 3
yudhiṣṭhirākhya-kumbhakāra-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 3
The story of the potter named <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścit adhiṣṭhāne kumbhakāraḥ prativasati sma | sa kadācit pramādād ardha-magna-kharpara-tīkṣṇāgrasyopari mahatā vegena dhāvan patitaḥ | tataḥ khapara-koṭyā pāṭita-lalāī̀oo rudhira-plāvita-tanuḥ kṛcchrād utthāya svāśrayaṃ gataḥ | tataś cāpathya-sevanāt sa prahāras tasya karālatāṃ gataḥ kṛcchreṇa nīrogatāṃ nītaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a potter. Once, by carelessness, running at great speed over a half-buried potsherd with a sharp edge, he fell upon it. Then, with his forehead split by the potsherd's point, his body drenched in blood, he somehow got up and went to his dwelling. Then, from improper treatment, that wound developed into a terrible scar — [yet] with difficulty he was brought back to health.

children.text: atha kadācid durbhikṣa-pīḍite deśe ca kumbhakāraḥ kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭhaḥ kaiścid rāja-sevakaiḥ saha deśāntaraṃ gatvā kasyāpi rājñaḥ sevako babhūva | so 'pi rājā tasya lalāṭe vikarālaṃ prahāra-kṣataṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa, yad-vīraḥ puruṣaḥ kaścid ayam | nūnaṃ tena lalāṭa-paṭṭe sammukha-prahāraḥ |
children.translated_text: Then once, when the country was stricken with famine, the potter, his throat withered from hunger, went with some royal servants to another land and became a servant of a certain king. That king too, seeing the terrible wound-scar on his forehead, thought: 'This must be some heroic man. Surely he received this frontal blow facing the enemy.'

children.text: atas taṃ samānādibhiḥ sarveṣāṃ rāja-putrāṇāṃ madhye viśeṣa-prasādena paśyati sma | te'pi rāja-putrās tasya taṃ prasādātirekaṃ paśyantaṃ paramerṣyā-dharmaṃ vahanto rāja-bhayān na kiñcid ūcuḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, he regarded him with special favor among all the princes, by means of gifts of honor and the like. Those princes too, seeing that excessive favor toward him, bearing the sin of supreme envy, said nothing out of fear of the king.

children.text: athānyasminn ahani tasya bhūpater vīra-sambhāvanāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ vigrahe samupasthite prakalpyamāneṣu gajeṣu saṃnahyamāneṣu vājiṣu yodheṣu | praguṇīkriyamāṇeṣu tena bhūbhujā sa kumbhakāraḥ prastāvānugataṃ pṛṣṭo nirjane-bho rāja-putra ! kiṃ te nāma ? kā ca jātiḥ ? kasmin saṅgrāme prahāro 'yaṃ te lalāṭe lagnaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then on another day, when that king's battle with the enemy had arrived — as elephants were being assigned, horses and warriors were being armored, and preparations were being made — the king asked that potter in private, in a manner relevant to the occasion: 'O prince! What is your name? And what is your caste? In which battle was this wound affixed to your forehead?'

children.text: sa āha-deva ! nāyaṃ śastra-prahāraḥ | yudhiṣṭhirābhidhaḥ kulālo 'haṃ prakṛtyā | mad-gehe'neka-kharparāṇy āsan | atha kadācin madya-pānaṃ kṛtvā nirgataḥ pradhāvan kharparopari patitaḥ | tasya prahāra-vikāro 'yaṃ me lalāṭe evaṃ vikarālatāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Your Majesty! This is not a weapon-wound. I am by birth a potter named <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. In my house there were many potsherds. Once, having drunk wine, I went out, ran [over them], and fell on a potsherd. This disfigurement on my forehead is the result of that wound.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya rājā sa-vrīḍam āha-aho vañcito 'haṃ rājāputrānukāriṇānena kulālena | tad dīyatāṃ drāg etasya candrārdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king said with embarrassment: 'Alas! I have been deceived by this potter who resembles a prince! So let him be quickly given a half-moon [mark of discharge].'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite kumbhakāra āha-mā maivaṃ kuru | paśya me raṇe hasta-lāghavam |
children.translated_text: When this was about to be carried out, the potter said: 'Do not, do not do this! Behold my dexterity in battle!'

children.text: rājā prāha-sarva-guṇa-sampanno bhavān | tathāpi gamyatām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The king said: 'You are endowed with all qualities. Still, depart. And it is said:'

children.text: śūdraś ca kṛta-vighnaś ca darśanīyo 'si putraka |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Śūdra</s>! You are an obstacle, and yet you are [still] handsome to see, my boy;

children.text: yasmin kule tvam utpanno gajas tatra na hanyate ||Panc_4.39||
children.translated_text: in the family where you were born, elephants are not killed [i.e., your people have no warrior tradition]. ||Panc_4.39||

children.text: kulāla āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The potter said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
rājā kathayati-
kathā 4
siṃha-dampatī-kathā
children.translated_text:
The king narrates:
Story 4
The story of the lion couple

children.text: kasmiṃścid uddeśe siṃha-dampatī prativasataḥ sma | atha siṃhī putra-dvayam ajījanat | siṃho 'pi nityam eva mṛgān vyāpādya siṃhyai dadāti | athānyasmin ahani tena kim api nāsāditam | yena bhramato 'pi tasya ravir astaṃ gataḥ | atha tena sva-gṛham āgacchatā śṛgāla-śiśuḥ prāptaḥ | sa ca bālako 'yam ity avadhārya yatnena daṃṣṭrāmadhya-gataṃ kṛtvā siṃhyā jīvantam eva samarpitavān | tataḥ siṃhyābhihitam-bhoḥ kānta ! tvayānītaṃ kiñcid asmākaṃ bhojanam ?
children.translated_text: In a certain region, a lion couple dwelt. Then the lioness gave birth to two cubs. The lion too would daily kill deer and give [them] to the lioness. On another day, he found nothing; though he roamed, the sun set on him. Then, while coming to his own home, he encountered a jackal cub. And he, determining 'This is a baby,' carefully placed it between his fangs and presented it alive to the lioness. Then the lioness said: 'Dear husband! Have you brought anything for us to eat?'

children.text: siṃha āha-priye ! mayādyainaṃ śṛgāla-śiśuṃ parityajya na kiñcit sattvam āsāditam | sa ca mayā bālo 'yam iti matvā na vyāpādito viśeṣāt svajātīyaś ca | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The lion said: 'Dear one! Today I have found no creature except this jackal cub, which I have spared. He was not killed by me, thinking "This is a baby" — and especially because he is of a related species.' And it is said:

children.text: strī-vipraliṅgi-bāleṣu prahartavyaṃ na karhicit |
children.translated_text: Against women, cross-dressers, and children, one should never strike;

children.text: prāṇa-tyāge'pi sañjāte viśvasteṣu viśeṣataḥ ||Panc_4.40||
children.translated_text: even when one's life is at stake — especially against those who have placed their trust. ||Panc_4.40||

children.text: idānīṃ tvam enaṃ bhakṣayitvā pathyaṃ kuru | prabhāte'nyat kiñcid upārjayiṣyāmi | sā prāha-bhoḥ kānta ! tvayā bālako 'yam iti vicintya na hataḥ | tat katham enam ahaṃ svodarārthe vināśayāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Now you may eat this and sustain yourself. At dawn I shall procure something else.' She said: 'Dear husband! Since you, thinking "This is a baby," did not kill him, how then shall I destroy him for the sake of my own belly?' And it is said:

children.text: akṛtyaṃ naiva kartavyaṃ prāṇa-tyāge'py upasthite |
children.translated_text: What should not be done should never be done, even when death is at hand;

children.text: na ca kṛtyaṃ parityājyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ||Panc_4.41||
children.translated_text: nor should what ought to be done be abandoned — this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>. ||Panc_4.41||

children.text: tasmān mamāyaṃ tṛtīyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati | ity evam uktvā tam api svastana-kṣīreṇa parāṃ puṣṭim anayat | evaṃ te trayo 'pi śiśavaḥ parasparam ajñāta-jāti-viśeṣā ekācāra-vihārā bālya-samayaṃ nirvāhayanti | atha kadācit tatra vane bhramann araṇya-gajaḥ samāyātaḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā tau siṃha-sutau dvāv api kupitānanau taṃ prati pracalitau yāvat tāvat tena śṛgāla-sutenābhihitam-aho ! gajo 'yaṃ yuṣmat-kula-śatruḥ | tan na gantavyam etasyābhimukham |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore he shall be my third son.' Having spoken thus, she nourished him too to full growth with her own milk. Thus those three cubs, unaware of each other's difference of species, sharing one conduct and play, passed their childhood. Then one day, a wild elephant came wandering in that forest. Seeing him, the two lion-cubs, their faces angry, moved toward him — but that jackal's son said: 'Ho! This elephant is the hereditary enemy of your family. So you must not go toward him.'

children.text: evam uktvā gṛhaṃ pradhāvitaḥ | tāv api jyeṣṭha-bāndhava-bhaṅgān nirutsāhatāṃ gatau | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Having said this, he ran home. Those two also, from the discouragement of their elder kinsman's retreat, lost their enthusiasm. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: ekenāpi sudhīreṇa sotsāhena raṇaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: By even one man of great courage and enthusiasm for battle,

children.text: sotsāhaṃ jāyate sainyaṃ bhagne bhaṅgam avāpnuyāt ||Panc_4.42||
children.translated_text: the entire army becomes enthusiastic; but when [he is] broken, [they too] suffer defeat. ||Panc_4.42||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: ata eva vāñchanti bhūpā yodhān mahābalān |
children.translated_text: For this very reason kings desire warriors who are mighty,

children.text: śūrān vīrān kṛtotsāhān varjayanti ca kātarān ||Panc_4.43||
children.translated_text: heroic, brave, and full of enterprise — and reject the cowardly. ||Panc_4.43||

children.text: atha tau dvāv api gṛhaṃ prāpya pitror agrato jyeṣṭha-bhrātṛ-ceṣṭitam ūcatuḥ-yathā gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā dūrato 'pi naṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the two, having reached home, in the presence of their parents reported the behavior of their elder brother — that upon seeing the elephant, he had fled from afar.

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇya kopāviṣṭa-manāḥ prasphuritādhara-pallavas tāmralocanas triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭiṃ kṛtvā tau nirbhartsayan paruṣatara-vacanāny uvāca-tataḥ siṃhyai kānte nītvā prabodhito 'sau-vatsa ! maivaṃ kadācij jalpa | bhavadīya-laghu-bhrātarāv etau |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing that — his mind filled with anger, his lower lip quivering, his eyes reddened, making a triple-crested frown on his brow — rebuking them, spoke very harsh words. Then the lioness, having taken him aside to a private place, admonished him: 'Son! Never speak thus. These are your younger brothers.'

children.text: athāsau prabhūta-kopāviṣṭas tām uvāca-kim aham etābhyāṃ śauryeṇa rūpeṇa vidyābhyāsena kauśalena vā hīnaḥ ? yena mām upahasataḥ | tan mayāvaśyam etau vyāpādanīyau |
children.translated_text: Then he, filled with great anger, said to her: 'Am I inferior to them in valor, in appearance, in learning, or in skill? Why then do they mock me? I shall certainly kill them both!'

children.text: tad ākarṇya siṃhī tasya jīvitam icchanty antar vihasya prāha-tat samyak śṛṇu | tvaṃ śṛgālī-sutaḥ | kṛpayā mayā svastana-kṣīreṇa puṣṭiṃ nītaḥ | tad yāvad etau mat-putrau śiśutvāt tvāṃ śṛgālaṃ na jānītaḥ, tāvad drutataraṃ gatvā svajātīyānāṃ madhye bhava | no ced ābhyāṃ hato mṛtyu-pathaṃ sameṣyasi | so 'pi tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā bhaya-vyākula-manāḥ śanaiḥ śanair apasṛtya sva-jātyā militaḥ | tasmāt tvaṃ api yāvad ete rāja-putrās tvāṃ kulālaṃ najānanti, tāvad drutataram apasara | no ced eteṣāṃ sakāśād viḍambanāṃ prāpya mariṣyāmi | kulālo 'pi tad ākarṇya satvaraṃ praṇaṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the lioness — desiring his safety — laughed inwardly and said: 'Then listen well. You are a jackal's son. Out of compassion, I nourished you to fullness with my own milk. So, before these sons of mine realize from your youth that you are a jackal, go quickly and be among your own kind. Otherwise, killed by them, you will meet the path of death.' And he, hearing her words, his mind agitated with fear, slowly, slowly withdrew and joined his own species. Therefore you too — before these princes recognize you as a potter — depart quickly. Otherwise you will suffer humiliation at their hands and perish.' The potter too, hearing that, disappeared quickly.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-svārtham utsṛjya yo dambhī (38) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'The hypocrite of dull mind who abandons self-interest...' (verse 38).

children.text: dhiṅ mūrkha ! yat tvayā striyo 'rtha etat-kāryam anuṣṭhātum ārabdham | na hi strīṇāṃ kathañcid viśvāsam upagacchet | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Shame on you, fool! That you have undertaken this deed for a woman's sake! One should never trust women under any circumstances.' And it is said —

children.text: yad-arthe sva-kulaṃ tyaktaṃ jīvitārdhaṃ ca hāritam |
children.translated_text: She for whose sake I abandoned my own family and gave up half my life —

children.text: sā māṃ tyajati niḥsnehā kaḥ strīṇāṃ viśvasen naraḥ ||Panc_4.44||
children.translated_text: she, devoid of affection, abandons me — what man should trust women? [Panc 4.44]

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text: vānara āha-
children.translated_text: The monkey said:

children.text:
kathā 5
brāhmaṇa-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 5
The Story of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne ko 'pi brāhmaṇaḥ | tasya ca bhāryā prāṇebhyo 'py atipriyāsīt | so 'pi pratidinaṃ kuṭumbena saha kalahaṃ kurvāṇā na viśrāmyati | so 'pi brāhmaṇaḥ kalaham asahamāno bhāryā-vātsalyāt sva-kuṭumbaṃ parityajya brāhmaṇyā saha viprakṛṣṭaṃ deśāntaraṃ gataḥ | atha mahāṭavī-madhye brāhmaṇyābhihitaḥ-ārya-putra ! tṛṣṇā māṃ bādhate | tad udakaṃ kvāpy anveṣaya |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. His wife was dearer to him than life itself. She, quarreling daily with the household, never ceased. That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too, unable to bear the quarrel, out of affection for his wife, abandoned his own family and went with the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> to a distant foreign land. Then, in the midst of a great forest, the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> said: 'Noble husband! Thirst afflicts me. So search for water somewhere.'

children.text: athāsau tad-vacanānantaraṃ yāvad-udakaṃ gṛhītvā samāgacchati tāvat tāṃ mṛtām apaśyat | ativallabhatayā viṣādaṃ kurvan yāvad vilapati tāvad ākāśe vācaṃ śṛṇoti | yathā hi-yadi brāhmaṇa tvaṃ svakīya-jīvitasyārdhaṃ dadāsi tatas te jīvati brāhmaṇī |
children.translated_text: Then, right after her words, by the time he returned bringing water, he found her dead. Overcome with grief due to his excessive love, as he was lamenting, he heard a voice from the sky, saying: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, if you give half of your own life, then your <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> will live.'

children.text: tac chrutvā brāhmaṇena śucībhūya tisṛbhir vācobhiḥ svajīvitārdhaṃ dattam | vāk-samam eva ca brāhmaṇī jīvitā sā | atha tau jalaṃ pītvā vana-phalāni bhakṣayitvā gantum ārabdhau | tataḥ krameṇa kasyacin nagarasya pradeśe puṣpa-vāṭikāṃ praviśya brāhmaṇo bhāryām abhihitavān-bhadre, yāvad ahaṃ bhojanaṃ gṛhītvā samāgacchāmi tāvad atra tvayā sthātavyam |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having purified himself, gave half his life with three utterances. And simultaneously with his words, she came back to life. Then both, having drunk water and eaten forest fruits, began their journey. Then gradually, reaching the outskirts of a certain city, entering a flower-garden, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said to his wife: 'Dear one, remain here until I bring food and return.'

children.text: ity abhidhāya brāhmaṇo nagara-madhye jagāma | atha tasyāṃ puṣpa-vāṭikāyāṃ paṅgura ara-ghaṭṭaṃ khelayan divya-girā gītam udgirati | tac ca śrutvā kusumeṣuṇārditā brāhmaṇyā tat-sakāśaṃ gatvābhihitam-bhadra ! yarhi māṃ na kāmayase, tan mat-saktā strī-hatyā tava bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Having said this, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> went into the city. Now in that flower-garden, a lame man, playing a water-wheel, was singing a song in a divine voice. Hearing that, the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, struck by <s>Kusuma-iṣu</s> (the flower-arrowed one, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>), went to him and said: 'Good sir! If you do not desire me, then the sin of a woman's death caused by attachment to you will fall upon you.'

children.text: paṅgur abravīt-kiṃ vyādhi-grastena mayā kariṣyasi ?
children.translated_text: The lame man said: 'What will you do with me, afflicted by disease?'

children.text: sābravīt-kim anenoktena ? avaśyaṃ tvayā saha mayā saṅgamaḥ kartavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: She said: 'What use is such talk? I must by all means have union with you.'

children.text: tac chrutvā tathā kṛtavān | suratānantaraṃ sābravīt-itaḥ-prabhṛti yāvaj-jīvaṃ mayātmā bhavate dattaḥ | iti jñātvā bhavān apy asmābhiḥ sahāgacchatu |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, he did so. After lovemaking she said: 'From now on, for as long as I live, I have given myself to you. Knowing this, you too should come with us.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-evam astu |
children.translated_text: He said: 'So be it.'

children.text: atha brāhmaṇo bhojanaṃ gṛhītvā samāgatya tayā sahabhoktum ārabdhaḥ sābravīt-eṣa paṅgur bubhukṣitaḥ | tad etasyāpi kiyantam api grāsaṃ dehi iti |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having brought food, began to eat with her. She said: 'This lame man is hungry. So give him some morsels of food too.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite brāhmaṇyābhihitaṃ-brāhmaṇa, sahāya-hīnas tvaṃ yadā grāmāntaraṃ gacchasi, tadā mama vacana-sahāyo 'pi nāsti | tad enaṃ paṅguṃ gṛhītvā gacchāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: When this was done, the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> said: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, when you travel without a companion to another village, I have no one even for conversation. So let us take this lame man along.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-na śaknomy ātmānam apy ātmanāṃ voḍhum | kiṃ punar enaṃ paṅgum ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'I cannot even carry myself by myself. How then can I carry this lame man?'

children.text: sābravīt-peṭābhyantara-stham enam ahaṃ neṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: She said: 'I shall carry him inside a basket.'

children.text: atha tat-kṛtaka-vacana-vyāmohita-cittena tena pratipannam | tathānuṣṭhite'nyasmin dine kūpopakaṇṭhe viśrānto brāhmaṇas tayā ca paṅgu-puruṣāsaktayā samprerya kūpāntaḥ pātitaḥ | sāpi paṅguṃ gṛhītvā kasmiṃścin nagare praviṣṭā | tatra śulka-caurya-rakṣā-nimittaṃ rāja-puruṣair itas tato bhramadbhis tan-mastaka-sthā peṭī dṛṣṭā balād ācchidya rājāgre nītā | rājā ca yāvat tām udghāṭayati tāvat taṃ paṅguṃ dadarśa | tataḥ sā brāhmaṇī vilāpaṃ kurvatī rāja-puruṣānupadam eva tatrāgatā | rājñā pṛṣṭā-ko vṛttāntaḥ ? iti |
children.translated_text: Then he, his mind deluded by her contrived words, agreed. When this was done, on another day, while the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was resting near a well, she, attached to the lame man, pushed him into the well. And she, taking the lame man, entered a certain city. There, royal guards roaming about for the purpose of preventing smuggling saw the basket on her head, forcibly took it, and brought it before the king. When the king opened it, he saw the lame man. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, lamenting, came following the royal guards to that place. The king asked: 'What is this story?'

children.text: sābravīt-mamaiṣa bhartā vyādhi-bādhito dāyāda-samūhair udvejito mayā sneha-vyākulita-mānasayā śirasi kṛtvā bhavadīya-nagara ānītaḥ |
children.translated_text: She said: 'This is my husband, afflicted by disease, driven out by his kinsmen. I, with a mind overwhelmed by love, have carried him on my head and brought him to your city.'

children.text: tac chrutvā rājābravīt-brāhmaṇi ! tvaṃ me bhaginī | grāma-dvayaṃ gṛhītvā bhartā saha bhogān bhuñjānā sukhena tiṣṭha |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king said: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>! You are like a sister to me. Take two villages and, with your husband, live happily enjoying their produce.'

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇo daiva-vaśāt kenāpi sādhunā kūpād uttāritaḥ paribhramaṃs tad eva nagaram āyātaḥ | tayā duṣṭa-bhāryayā dṛṣṭā rājñe niveditaḥ-rājan ! ayaṃ mama bhartur vairī samāyātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, by the working of fate, was rescued from the well by some holy man and, wandering about, arrived at that very city. Seen by his wicked wife, she reported to the king: 'O king! This enemy of my husband has arrived.'

children.text: rājñāpi vadha ādiṣṭaḥ | sābravīt-deva, anayā mama saktaṃ kiñcit gṛhītam asti | yadi tvaṃ dharma-vatsalaḥ, tad dāpaya |
children.translated_text: The king too ordered his execution. She said: 'Lord, this man has taken something that belongs to me. If you are devoted to <s>dharma</s>, then make him return it.'

children.text: rājābravīt-bhadre ! yat tvayāsya saktaṃ kiñcit gṛhītam asti tat samarpaya |
children.translated_text: The king said: 'Good woman! Whatever of yours this man has taken, let him return it.'

children.text: sā prāha-deva, mayā na kiñcid gṛhītam |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Lord, I have taken nothing of his.'

children.text: brāhmaṇa āha-yan mayā trivācikaṃ sva-jīvitārdhaṃ dattam, tad dehi |
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'That half of my life which I gave with three utterances — give it back!'

children.text: atha sā rāja-bhayāt tatraiva trivācikam eva jīvitārdham anena dattam iti jalpantī prāṇair vimuktā | tataḥ sa-vismayaṃ rājābravīt-kim etat iti | brāhmaṇenāpi pūrva-vṛttāntaḥ sakalo 'pi tasmai niveditaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then she, out of fear of the king, right there, uttering 'the half of life given by him with three utterances' — was released from life [died]. Then the king said with amazement: 'What is this?' And the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> related the entire former account to him.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-yad-arthe sva-kulaṃ tyaktam (44) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'She for whose sake I abandoned my family...' (verse 44) and so on.

children.text: vānaraḥ punar āha-sādhu cedam upākhyānakaṃ śrūyate-
children.translated_text: The monkey said again: 'And this little tale too is aptly heard —'

children.text: na kiṃ dadyān na kiṃ kuryāt strībhir abhyarthito naraḥ |
children.translated_text: What would a man not give, what would he not do, when entreated by women?

children.text: anaśvā yatra hreṣante śiraḥ parvaṇi muṇḍitam ||Panc_4.45||
children.translated_text: Where horses that are not horses neigh, the head is shaved on a festival day. [Panc 4.45]

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text: vānaraḥ kathayati-
children.translated_text: The monkey narrates:

children.text: kathā 6
children.translated_text: Story 6

children.text: atiprakhyāta-bala-pauruṣo 'neka-narendra-mukuṭa-marīci-jāla-jaṭilī-kṛta-pāda-pīṭhaḥ śarac-chaśāṅka-kiraṇa-nirmala-yaśāḥ samudra-paryantāyāḥ pṛthivyā bhartā nando nāma rājā | yasya sarva-śāstrādhigata-samasta-tattvaḥ sacivo vararucir nāma | tasya ca praṇaya-kalahena jāyā kupitā | sā cātīva vallabhāneka-prakāraṃ paritoṣyamāṇāpi na prasīdati | bravīti ca bhartā-bhadre ! yena prakāreṇa tuṣyati taṃ vada | niścitaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: There was a king named <s>Nanda</s>, of exceedingly renowned strength and prowess, the soles of whose footstool were encrusted with the rays from the crown-jewels of many kings, whose fame was as pure as the rays of the autumn moon, and who was the lord of the earth extending to the ocean. His minister was named <s>Vararuci</s>, who had mastered the truths of all the sciences. His wife had become angry with him through a lovers' quarrel. And she, though exceedingly dear and appeased in many ways, would not be placated. Her husband said: 'Dear one! Tell me the way by which you will be satisfied. I shall certainly do it.'

children.text: tataḥ kathañcit tayoktaṃ-yadi śiro muṇḍayitvā mama pādayor nipatasi, tadā prasādābhimukhī bhavāmi |
children.translated_text: Then somehow she said: 'If you shave your head and fall at my feet, then I shall become gracious toward you.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite prasannāsīt | atha nandasya bhāryāpi tathaiva ruṣṭā prasādyamānāpi na tuṣyati | tenoktam-bhadre ! tvayā vinā muhūrtam api na jīvāmi | pādayoḥ patitvā tvāṃ prasādayāmi |
children.translated_text: When this was done, she was pleased. Now <s>Nanda</s>'s wife too was similarly angered and, though being appeased, would not be satisfied. He said: 'Dear one! Without you I cannot live even a moment. Falling at your feet I entreat you.'

children.text: sābravīt-yadi khalīnaṃ mukhe prakṣityāhaṃ tava pṛṣṭhe samāruhya tvāṃ dhāvayāmi | dhāvitas tu yady aśvavad dhreṣase, tadā prasannā bhavāmi |
children.translated_text: She said: 'If you put a bit in your mouth and I mount your back and make you gallop, and if when galloping you neigh like a horse, then I shall be pleased.'

children.text: rājñāpi tathaivānuṣṭhitam | atha prabhāta-samaye sabhāyām upaviṣṭasya rājñaḥ samīpe vararucir āyātaḥ | taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā rājā papraccha-bho vararuce ! kiṃ parvaṇi muṇḍitaṃ śiras tvayā ?
children.translated_text: The king too did exactly so. Then in the morning, when the king was seated in the assembly hall, <s>Vararuci</s> came near him. Seeing him, the king asked: 'O <s>Vararuci</s>! Why is your head shaved on a festival day?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-na kiṃ dadyāt (45) ity ādi | tad bho dusṭa makara ! tvam api nanda-vararuci-vat strī-vaśyaḥ | tato bhadra āgatena tvayā māṃ prati vadhopāya-prayāsaḥ prārabdhaḥ | paraṃ sva-vāg-doṣeṇaiva prakaṭībhūtaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: He said: 'What would a man not give...' (verse 45) and so on. 'So you too, O wicked crocodile, are subject to a woman's will, like <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Vararuci</s>! Therefore, good sir, you came to me and began to contrive a means for my death. But it has been revealed by the very fault of your own speech. Or rather, this is well said —'

children.text: ātmano mukha-doṣeṇa badhyante śuka-sārikāḥ |
children.translated_text: By the fault of their own mouths, parrots and <s>sārikā</s> (mynahs) are caught;

children.text: bakās tatra na badhyante maunaṃ sarvārtha-sādhanam ||Panc_4.46||
children.translated_text: herons are not caught there — silence is the means of accomplishing all purposes. [Panc 4.46]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: suguptaṃ rakṣyamāṇo 'pi darśayan dāruṇaṃ vapuḥ |
children.translated_text: Though well-concealed and guarded, [yet] showing its terrible form,

children.text: vyāghra-carma-praticchanno vāk-kṛte rāsabho hataḥ ||Panc_4.47||
children.translated_text: the donkey covered in a tiger's skin was killed because of its voice. [Panc 4.47]

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text: vānaraḥ kathayati-
children.translated_text: The monkey narrates:

children.text:
kathā 8
śuddhapaṭa-nāma-rajaka-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 8
The Story of the Washerman Named <s>Śuddhapaṭa</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne śuddhapaṭo nāma rajakaḥ prativasati sma | tasya ca gardabha eko 'sti | so 'pi ghāsābhāvād atidurbalatāṃ gataḥ | atha tena rajakenāṭavyāṃ paribhramatā mṛta-vyāghro dṛṣṭaḥ | cintitaṃ ca-aho ! śobhanam āpatitam | anena vyāghra-carmaṇā praticchādya rāsabhaṃ rātrau yava-kṣetreṣūtsrakṣyāmi | yena vyāghraṃ matvā samīpa-vartinaḥ kṣetra-pālā enaṃ na niṣkāsayiṣyanti |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a washerman named <s>Śuddhapaṭa</s> (Clean-cloth). He had one donkey. That donkey too, due to lack of grass, had become extremely weak. Then that washerman, wandering in the forest, saw a dead tiger. He thought: 'Ah! Something excellent has come my way. Covering the donkey with this tiger-skin, I shall let him loose at night in the barley-fields. Thinking him a tiger, the field-guards nearby will not drive him away.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite rāsabho yathecchayā yava-bhakṣaṇaṃ karoti | pratyūṣe bhūyo 'pi rajakaḥ svāśrayaṃ nayati | evaṃ gacchatā kālena sa rāsabhaḥ pīvara-tanur jātaḥ | kṛcchrād bandhana-sthānam api nīyate | athānyasminn ahani sa madhoddhato dūrād rāsabhī-śabdam aśṛṇot | tac-chravaṇa-mātreṇaiva svayaṃ śabdayitum ārabdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: When this was done, the donkey ate barley to his heart's content. At dawn, the washerman would take him back to his shelter. As time passed thus, that donkey became fat-bodied. He was led to the tethering-place only with difficulty. Then one day, excited by rut, he heard from afar the sound of a she-donkey. The very moment he heard it, he himself began to bray.

children.text: atha te kṣetra-pālā rāsabho 'yaṃ vyāghra-carma-praticchanna iti jñātvā laguḍa-śara-pāṣāṇa-prahārais taṃ vyāpāditavantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those field-guards, knowing him to be a donkey covered in a tiger's skin, killed him with blows of clubs, arrows, and stones.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-suguptaṃ rakṣyamāṇo 'pi (47) iti | tat kiṃ śyāmalakavad atyapamāna-sahanād ardha-candra-dānena yāsyasi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Though well-concealed and guarded...' (verse 47) and so on. 'So will you depart like <s>Śyāmalaka</s>, through enduring much humiliation, by being given the half-moon (a kick)?'

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
vānara āha-
kathā 9
mahādhana-īśvara-nāma-bhāṇḍapati-kathā
children.translated_text:
The monkey said:
Story 9
The Story of the Merchant <s>Mahādhana Īśvara</s>

children.text:
asty atra dharā-pīṭhe vikaṇṭakaṃ nāma puram | tatra mahā-dhana īśvaro nāma bhāṇḍa-patiḥ | tasya catvāro jāmātṛkā avantī-pīṭhāt prāghūrṇikā vikaṇṭaka-pure samāyātāḥ | te ca yena mahatā gauraveṇābhyarcitā bhojānācchādanādibhiḥ | evaṃ teṣāṃ tatra vasatāṃ māsa-ṣaṭkaṃ sañjātam | tata īśvareṇa svabhāryoktā yad ete jāmātaraḥ parama-gauraveṇāvarjitāḥ svāmi gṛhāṇi na gacchanti, tat kiṃ kathyate ? vināpamānaṃ na yāsyanti | tad adya bhojana-velāyāṃ pāda-prakṣālanārthaṃ jalaṃ na deyaṃ yenāpamānaṃ jñātvā parityajya gacchantīti |
tathānuṣṭhite gargaḥ pāda-prakṣālanāpamānāt, somo laghv-āsana-dānāt, dattaḥ kadaśanato yātaḥ | evaṃ te trayo 'pi parityajya gatāḥ | caturthaḥ śyāmalako yāvan na yāti tāvad ardha-candra-pradānena niṣkāsitaḥ |
children.translated_text:
Here on this earth there is a city named <s>Vikaṇṭaka</s>. There lived a merchant named <s>Mahādhana Īśvara</s> (Great-wealth Lord). His four sons-in-law came from the city of <s>Avantī</s> as wandering mendicants to <s>Vikaṇṭaka</s>. And they were honored with great respect — food, clothing, and the like. While they dwelt there thus, six months passed. Then <s>Īśvara</s> said to his wife: 'These sons-in-law, won over with supreme honor, do not go to their own homes. So what is to be said? Without insult they will not leave. So today at mealtime, water for washing feet should not be given, so that knowing the insult, they may leave.'
When this was done, <s>Garga</s> left because of the insult of no foot-washing water; <s>Soma</s> left because of being given a low seat; <s>Datta</s> left because of bad food. Thus three departed. The fourth, <s>Śyāmalaka</s>, who still would not leave, was expelled by the giving of the half-moon (a kick).

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-
children.translated_text: Therefore I say —

children.text: gargo hi pāda-śaucāl laghv-āsana-dānato gataḥ somaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Garga</s> left due to the foot-washing [insult]; <s>Soma</s> due to the low seat;

children.text: dattaḥ kadaśana-bhojyāc chyāmalakaś cārdha-candreṇa ||Panc_4.48||
children.translated_text: <s>Datta</s> due to the bad food; and <s>Śyāmalaka</s> by the half-moon [kick]. [Panc 4.48]

children.text: tat kim ahaṃ rathakāravan mūrkho yataḥ svayam api dṛṣṭvā te vikāra-paścād viśvasimi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So am I a fool like the cartwright, that even after seeing your treachery with my own eyes, I would still trust you?' And it is said —

children.text: pratyakṣe'pi kṛte pāpe mūrkhaḥ sāmnā praśāmyati |
children.translated_text: Even when sin is committed before one's eyes, a fool is pacified by gentle words;

children.text: rathakāraḥ svakāṃ bhāryāṃ sajārāṃ śirasāvahat ||Panc_4.49||
children.translated_text: the cartwright carried his own wife, along with her paramour, on his head. [Panc 4.49]

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text: vānaraḥ kathayati-
children.translated_text: The monkey narrates:

children.text:
kathā 10
rathakāra-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 10
The Story of the Cartwright

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne kaścid rathakāraḥ prativasati sma | tasya bhāryā puṃśalīti janāpavāda-saṃyuktā | so 'pi tasyāḥ parīkṣārthaṃ vyacintayat-kathaṃ mayāsyāḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ kartavyam | na caitad yujyate kartuṃ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a certain cartwright. His wife was reputed among people to be an adulteress. He too, wishing to test her, thought: 'How should I test her? And this is not proper to do, because —'

children.text: nadīnāṃ ca kulānāṃ ca munīnāṃ ca mahātmanām |
children.translated_text: Of rivers, of families, of sages, and of great souls —

children.text: parīkṣā na prakartavyā strīṇāṃ duścaritasya ca ||Panc_4.49||
children.translated_text: the inquiry into the unchaste conduct of women should not be undertaken. // Panc_4.49 //

children.text: vasor vīryotpannām abhajata munir matsya-tanayāṃ
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Vasu</s> (Parāśara) wedded the fish-born daughter (<s>Matsyagandhā</s>) born of <s>Vasu</s>'s virility;

children.text: tathā jāto vyāso śata-guṇa-nivāsaḥ kim aparam |
children.translated_text: thus was born <s>Vyāsa</s>, of a hundredfold noble dwelling — what more [can be said]?

children.text: svayaṃ vedān vyasyan śamita-kuru-vaṃśa-prasavitā
children.translated_text: He himself, dividing the <s>Vedas</s>, became the progenitor of the pacified <s>Kuru</s> lineage —

children.text: sa evābhā̆c chrīmān ahaha viṣamā karma-gatayaḥ ||Panc_4.50||
children.translated_text: that very one became illustrious — ah, how inscrutable are the ways of <s>karma</s>! // Panc_4.50 //

children.text: kulānām iti pāṇḍavānām api mahātmanāṃ notpattir adhigantavyā yataḥ te kṣetrajā iti | strī-duścaritaṃ sandhukṣyamāṇam aneka-doṣān prakaṭayati strīṇām iti | tathā ca-
children.translated_text: The origins of noble families — even of the great <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> — should not be investigated, since they were <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born). The unchaste conduct of women, when fanned, reveals the many faults of women. And also:

children.text: yadi syāt pāvakaḥ śītaḥ proṣṇo vā śaśa-lāñchanaḥ |
children.translated_text: If fire were cold, or the hare-marked [moon] were hot,

children.text: strīṇāṃ tadā satītvaṃ syād yadi syād durjano hitaḥ ||Panc_4.51||
children.translated_text: then women would be chaste — if [ever] a villain were benevolent. // Panc_4.51 //

children.text: yathāpi śuddhām aśuddhāṃ vāpi jānāmi loka-vacanāt | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Just as I may know [her to be] pure or impure from the words of the world.' And it is said:

children.text: yan na vedeṣu śāstreṣu na dṛṣṭaṃ na ca saṃśrutam |
children.translated_text: What is not found in the <s>Vedas</s> or the <s>śāstras</s>, what has not been seen or heard —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ vetti loko 'yaṃ yat syād brahmāṇḍa-madhyagam ||Panc_4.52||
children.translated_text: all that this world knows, whatever lies within the universe. // Panc_4.52 //

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya tām avocata-priye, ahaṃ prātar grāmāntaraṃ yāsyāmi tatra dināni katicil lagiṣyanti | tat tvayā kiñcit pātheyaṃ mama yogyaṃ kāryam |
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, he said to her: 'Darling, I shall go to another village tomorrow morning; I shall be away for some days. So prepare some suitable provisions for my journey.'

children.text: sāpi tad ākarṇya harṣita-cittautsukyena sarva-kāryāṇi santyajya siddham annaṃ ghṛta-śarkarā-prāyam akarot | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: And she, hearing that, with a heart delighted and eager, abandoning all [other] tasks, prepared cooked food rich with ghee and sugar. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: durdivase ghana-timire duḥkha-cārāsu nagara-vīthīṣu |
children.translated_text: On a gloomy day, in the dark, on the city streets difficult to traverse,

children.text: patyau videśa-yāte parama-sukhaṃ jaghana-capalāyāḥ ||Panc_4.53||
children.translated_text: when the husband has gone abroad — supreme is the happiness of the hip-restless woman. // Panc_4.53 //

children.text: athāsau pratyūṣe utthāya sva-gṛhān nirgataḥ | sāpi taṃ prasthitaṃ vijñāya prahasita-vadanāṅga-satkāraṃ kurvāṇā kathañcit taṃ divasam atyavāhayat | tataś ca pūrva-paricitaṃ viṭa-gṛhaṃ gatvā tam abhyarthoktavatī yad-grāmāntaraṃ gataḥ sa durātmā me patiḥ | tad adya tvayāsmad-gṛhe prasupte jane samāgantavyam |
children.translated_text: Then he, rising at dawn, left his house. And she, knowing that he had departed, with a laughing face making a show of courtesy, somehow passed that day. Then, going to the house of her previously acquainted paramour, she said to him imploringly: 'That wicked husband of mine has gone to another village. So today, when everyone in the house is asleep, you must come to our house.'

children.text:
tathānuṣṭhite sa rathakāro 'py araṇye dinam ativāhya pradoṣe sva-gṛham apara-dvāreṇa praviṣṭaḥ śayyā-tale nibhṛto bhūtvā sthitaḥ | atrāntare sa devadattaḥ śayana āgatyopaviṣṭaḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā rathakāro roṣāviṣṭa-citto vyacintayat-kim enam utthāya vināśayāmy athavā dvāv apy etau suptau helayā hanmi | paraṃ paśyāmi tāvac ceṣṭitam asyāḥ śṛṇomi cānena sahālāpān | atrāntare sā gṛha-dvāraṃ nibhṛtaṃ pidhāya śayana-talam ārūḍhā | tasyās tac-chayanam ārohantyā rathakāra-śarīre pādo lagnaḥ | tato vyacintayat-nūnam etena durātmanā rathakāreṇa mat-parīkṣārthaṃ bhāvyam | tat-strī-carita-vijñānaṃ kim api karomi | evaṃ tasyāś cintayantyāḥ sa devadattaḥ sparśotsukyo babhūva | tataś ca tayākṛtāūjali-puṭayābhihitaṃ-bho
mahānubhava ! na me gātraṃ tvayā spraṣṭavyam, yato 'haṃ pativratā mahā-satī ca | no cec chāpaṃ dattvā tvāṃ bhasmasāt kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: When this was arranged, the carpenter too, having spent the day in the forest, entered his house at dusk by the back door and, hiding beneath the bed, remained still. In the meanwhile, that <s>Devadatta</s> came and sat on the bed. Seeing him, the carpenter, his mind filled with rage, thought: 'Should I rise and destroy him, or shall I casually kill both of them while asleep? But let me first observe her conduct and listen to her conversation with him.' In the meanwhile, she quietly bolted the front door and climbed onto the bed. As she climbed onto the bed, her foot touched the carpenter's body. Then she thought: 'Surely this wicked carpenter must be here to test me. So let me perform some feminine stratagem.' While she was thinking thus, that <s>Devadatta</s> became eager to touch her. Then she, with palms joined in supplication, said: 'O noble sir! My body must not be touched by you, for I am devoted to my husband and a great chaste woman. Otherwise, I shall curse you and reduce you to ashes!'

children.text: sa āha-yady evaṃ tarhi kim arthaṃ tvayāhūtaḥ ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'If so, then why have you summoned me?'

children.text:
sā prāha-bhoḥ ! śṛṇuṣvaikāgra-manāḥ | aham adya pratyūṣe devatā-darśanārthaṃ caṇḍikāyatanaṃ gatā | tatrākasmāt khe vāṇī sañjātā-putri, kiṃ karomi | bhaktāsi me tvam | paraṃ ṣaṇmāsābhyantare vidhi-niyogād vidhavā bhaviṣyasi | tato mayābhihitaṃ-bhagavati ! yayā tvam āpadaṃ vetsi tathā tat-partīkāram api jānāsi | tad asti kaścid upāyo yena me patiḥ śata-saṃvatsara-jīvī bhavati | tatas tayābhihitaṃ-vatse, sann api nāsti yatas tavāyattaḥ sa pratīkāraḥ | tac chrutvā mayābhihitaṃ-devi ! yan mat-prāṇair bhavati tad ādeśaya yena karomi | tato devyābhihitaṃ-yady adya dine para-puruṣeṇa sahaikasmiñ chayane samāruhyāliṅganaṃ karoṣi, tadā tava bhartṛ-sakto 'pamṛtyus tasya sañcarita, tvad-bhartā punar varṣa-śataṃ jīvati | tena mayā tvam abhyarthitaḥ | tayo
yat kiñcit kartum anās tat kuruṣva, nahi devatā-vacanam anyathā bhaviṣyatīti niścayaḥ | tato 'ntarhāsa-vikāsa-mukhaḥ sa tad-ucitam ācacāra |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Noble sir! Listen with undivided attention. Today at dawn I went to the temple of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> to see the deity. There suddenly a voice arose from the sky: "Daughter, what shall I do? You are my devotee. But within six months, by the decree of fate, you will become a widow." Then I said: "Goddess! Just as you know the calamity, so too you know its remedy. Is there some means by which my husband may live a hundred years?" Then she said: "Child, there is [a means], yet there is not — because that remedy depends upon you." Hearing that, I said: "Goddess! If it can be done even at the cost of my life, then command me, and I shall do it." Then the goddess said: "If today you climb onto a bed with another man and embrace him, then the untimely death attached to your husband will pass to that man, and your husband will live another hundred years." Therefore you were summoned by me. So whatever you intend to do, do it. For there is certainty that the word of a deity will not prove otherwise.' Then he, his face blooming with a suppressed smile, performed what was appropriate to that [situation].

children.text:
so 'pi rathakāro mūrkhas tasyās tad-vacanam ākarṇya pulakāṅkita-tanuḥ śayyā-talān niṣkramya tām uvāca-sādhu pativrate ! sādhu kula-nandini ! sādhu ! ahaṃ durjana-vacana-śaṅkita-hṛdayas tvat-parīkṣārthaṃ grāmāntara-vyājaṃ kṛtvātra nibhṛtaṃ khaṭvā-tale līnaḥ sthitaḥ | tad ehi, āliṅgaya mām | tvaṃ sva-bhartṛ-bhaktānāṃ mukhyā nārīṇāṃ, yad evaṃ brahma-vrataṃ para-saṅge'pi pālitavatī | mad-āyur-vṛddhi-kṛte'pamṛtyu-vināśārthaṃ ca tvam evaṃ kṛtavatī | tām evam uktvā sa-sneham āliṅgitavān | sva-skandhe tām āropya tam api devadattam uvāca-bhoḥ mahānubhāva ! mat-puṇyais tvam ihāgataḥ | tvat-prasādāt prāptām adya mayā varṣa-śata-pramāṇam āyuḥ | tatas tvam api māṃ samāliṅgaya skandhaṃ me samāroha | iti jalpann anicchantam
api devadattaṃ balād āliṅgya skandhe samāropitavān | tataś ca tūrya-dhvani-cchandena nṛtyan sakala-gṛha-dvāreṣu babhrāma |
children.translated_text: And that fool of a carpenter, hearing her words, his body thrilling with horripilation, came out from beneath the bed and said to her: 'Well done, O devoted wife! Well done, O joy of the family! Well done! I, my heart suspicious because of wicked men's words, hid here secretly beneath the cot under the pretense of going to another village, in order to test you. So come, embrace me! You are the foremost among women devoted to their husbands, since you have observed your sacred vow [of chastity] even in the company of another man — since for the increase of my lifespan and for the destruction of untimely death, you have done this.' Having spoken thus to her, he embraced her with affection. Mounting her upon his own shoulder, he also said to <s>Devadatta</s>: 'O noble sir! By my merit you have come here. By your grace I have today obtained a lifespan of a hundred years. So you too, embrace me and mount upon my shoulder.' Thus babbling, he embraced the unwilling <s>Devadatta</s> and forcibly mounted him upon his shoulder. Then, dancing to the rhythm of trumpet-sounds, he wandered to every house and doorway.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-pratyakṣe'pi kṛte pāpe (49) | tan mūḍha ! dṛṣṭa-vikāras tvam, tat kathaṃ tatra gṛhaṃ gacchāmi | athavā yan māṃ tvaṃ viśvāsayasi tat te doṣo nāsti, yat īdṛśī svabhāva-duṣṭā yuṣmaj-jātir yā śiṣṭa-saṅgād api saumyatvaṃ na yāti | athavā svabhāvo 'yaṃ duṣṭānām | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Even when sin is committed before one's very eyes...' (49). So, fool! You have been seen in your altered state — how then should I go to your house? Or rather, that you try to win my trust — the fault is not yours; rather, such is the nature of your naturally wicked species, which does not attain gentleness even through the company of the virtuous. Or rather, this is the nature of the wicked. And it is said:

children.text: sadbhiḥ sambodhyamāno 'pi durātmā pāpa-pauruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even when admonished by the good, a wicked soul of evil prowess

children.text: ghṛṣyamāṇa ivāṅgāro nirmalatvaṃ na gacchati ||Panc_4.54||
children.translated_text: does not attain purity — like a charcoal, even when polished. // Panc_4.54 //

children.text: tan mūrkha ! strī-lubdha ! strī-jita ! anye'pi ye tvad-vidhā bhavanti te sva-kāryaṃ vibhavaṃ mitraṃ ca parityajanti tat-kṛte | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So, fool! Woman-crazed! Woman-conquered! Others too who are like you abandon their own purpose, prosperity, and friends for their sake. And it is said:'

children.text: yā mamodvijate nityaṃ sādya mām avagūhate |
children.translated_text: 'She who always shuns me — today she embraces me!

children.text: priya-kāraka bhadraṃ te yan mamāsti harasva tat ||Panc_4.55||
children.translated_text: O benefactor, blessings to you! Whatever is mine, take it!' // Panc_4.55 //

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text: vānaro 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: The monkey said:

children.text:
kathā 11
kāmātura-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 11
The story of <s>Kāmātura</s>

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne kāmāturo nāma mahādhano vṛddha-vaṇik | tena mṛta-bhāryeṇa kāmopahata-cetasā kācin nirdhana-vaṇik-sutā prabhūtaṃ vittaṃ dattvodvāhitā | atha sā duḥkhābhibhūtā taṃ vṛddha-vaṇijaṃ draṣṭum api na śaśāka | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a very wealthy old merchant named <s>Kāmātura</s> (Passion-afflicted). After his wife died, his mind overcome by desire, he married a certain poor merchant's daughter by giving abundant wealth. She, overcome with unhappiness, could not even bear to look at that old merchant. Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: śvetaṃ padaṃ śirasi yat tu śiroruhāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: That white footprint on the head — the gray among the hairs —

children.text: sthānaṃ paraṃ paribhavasya tad eva puṃsām |
children.translated_text: that is the supreme abode of humiliation for men.

children.text: āropitāsthi-śakalaṃ parihṛtya yānti
children.translated_text: Young women leave far behind the one upon whom a fragment of bone has been placed [i.e., who is old] —

children.text: cāṇḍāla-kūpam iva dūrataraṃ taruṇyaḥ ||Panc_4.56||
children.translated_text: like an outcaste's well, [shunning him] from a great distance. // Panc_4.56 //

children.text: tathā ca-
gātraṃ saṅkucitaṃ gati-vigalitā dantāś ca nāśaṃ gatāh
children.translated_text: The body is shrunken, the gait unsteady, the teeth gone,

children.text: dṛṣṭir bhrāmyati rūpam eva hrasate vaktraṃ ca lālāyate |
children.translated_text: the sight wanders, the form itself diminishes, and the mouth drools.

children.text: vākyaṃ naiva karoti bāndhava-janaḥ patnī na śuśrūṣate
children.translated_text: Words are spoken [but] kinsmen pay no heed, the wife does not attend [him] —

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ jarayābhibhūta-puruṣaḥ putrair avajñāyate ||Panc_4.57||
children.translated_text: alas, the pitiable man overwhelmed by old age is despised even by his sons! // Panc_4.57 //
And also:
