children.text: atha kadācit sā tena sahaika-śayane parāṅ-mukhī yāvat tiṣṭhati tāvat tasya gṛhe cauraḥ praviṣṭaḥ | sāpi taṃ cauram avalokya bhaya-vyākulā vṛddham api patiṃ gāḍhaṃ samāliliṅga | so 'pi vismayāt pulakāṅkita-sarva-gātraś cintayāmāsa-aho ! kim eṣā mām adyāvagūhate | aho citram etat ! tataś ca yāvan nipuṇatayāvalokayati tāvat cauraḥ praviṣṭaḥ koṇaika-deśe tiṣṭhati | punar apy acintayat-nūnam eṣā caurasya bhayān mām āliṅgati | taj jñātvā cauram āha-yā mamodvijate nityaṃ sādya (55) iti | bhūyo 'pi nirgacchantam avādīt-bho cora ! nityam eva tvayā rātrāv āgantavyaṃ madīyo 'yaṃ vibhavas tvadīya iti |
children.translated_text: Now once, as she lay on the same bed with him, turned away, a thief entered his house. And she, seeing that thief, agitated with fear, tightly embraced even her old husband. He too, his entire body thrilling with goosebumps from astonishment, thought: 'Ah! Why does she embrace me today? What a wonder!' Then, looking carefully, [he saw] a thief had entered and stood in one corner. He thought again: 'Surely she embraces me out of fear of the thief.' Knowing this, he said to the thief: 'She who always shuns me — today she [embraces me]...' (55) [and so on]. Moreover, as [the thief] was leaving, he said: 'O thief! You must always come at night. This property of mine is yours.'

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-yā mamodvijate ity ādi | kiṃ bahunā, tena ca strī-lubdhena svaṃ sarvaṃ caurasya samarpitam | tvayāpi tathānuṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'She who always shuns me' and so on. In short, that woman-crazed one surrendered all his possessions to the thief. You too have acted likewise.

children.text: athaiva tena saha vadato makarasya jalacareṇaikenāgatyābhihitam-bho makara ! tvadīyā bhāryānaśanopaviṣṭā tvayi cirayati praṇayābhibhavād vipannā | evaṃ tad-vajra-pāta-sadṛśa-vacanam ākarṇyātīvra-vyākulita-hṛdayaḥ pralapitam evaṃ cakāra-aho kim idaṃ sañjātaṃ me manda-bhāgasya | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Now, while [the monkey] was speaking with him thus, a certain aquatic creature came and said: 'O crocodile! Your wife, having taken a vow of fasting, — since you have been away so long — has become undone by the force of her love.' Hearing those words, like a thunderbolt, [the crocodile], his heart exceedingly agitated, lamented thus: 'Ah! What has befallen wretched me! And it is said:'

children.text: na gṛhaṃ gṛham ity āhur gṛhiṇī gṛham ucyate |
children.translated_text: A house is not called a home — the housewife is called the home;

children.text: gṛhaṃ tu gṛhiṇī-hīnaṃ kāntārān nātiricyate ||Panc_4.58||
children.translated_text: a house without a housewife is no better than a wilderness. // Panc_4.58 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: vṛkṣa-mūle'pi dayitā yatra tiṣṭhati tad gṛham |
children.translated_text: Even at the foot of a tree, wherever the beloved stands — that is a home;

children.text: prāsādo 'pi tayā hīno 'raṇya-sadṛśaḥ smṛtaḥ ||Panc_4.59||
children.translated_text: even a palace without her is regarded as a forest. // Panc_4.59 //

children.text: mātā yasya gṛhe nāsti bhāryā ca priya-vādinī |
children.translated_text: He in whose home there is no mother or wife who speaks sweetly —

children.text: araṇyaṃ tena gantavyaṃ yathāraṇyaṃ tathā gṛham ||Panc_4.60||
children.translated_text: he should go to the forest, for his home is just like a forest. // Panc_4.60 //

children.text: tan mitra ! kṣamyatām | mayā te'parādhaḥ kṛtaḥ | sampraty ahaṃ tu strī-viyogād vaiśvānara-praveśaṃ kariṣyāmi | tan mūḍha ! ānande'pi jāte tvaṃ viṣādaṃ gataḥ | tādṛg-bhāryāyāṃ mṛtāyām utsavaḥ kartuṃ yujyate | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'So friend! Forgive me. I have wronged you. Now I shall enter fire from [grief at] separation from my wife.' 'So, fool! Even when joy has arisen, you have fallen into despondency. When such a wife dies, a celebration should be held.' And it is said, for:

children.text: yā bhāryā duṣṭa-caritrā satataṃ kalaha-priyā |
children.translated_text: A wife who is of wicked conduct, who constantly delights in quarrel —

children.text: bhāryā-rūpeṇa sā jñeyā vidagdhair dāruṇā jarā ||Panc_4.61||
children.translated_text: she, in the form of a wife, should be known by the wise as cruel old age itself. // Panc_4.61 //

children.text: tasmāt sarva-prayatnena nāmāpi parivarjayet |
children.translated_text: Therefore, with every effort, one should avoid even the name

children.text: strīṇām iha hi sarvāsāṃ ya icchet sukham ātmanaḥ ||Panc_4.62||
children.translated_text: of all women here — he who desires his own happiness. // Panc_4.62 //

children.text: yad-antas tan na jihvāyāṃ yaj jihvāyāṃ na tad-bahiḥ |
children.translated_text: What is inside [them] is not on the tongue; what is on the tongue is not outside;

children.text: yad-bahis tan na kurvanti vicitra-caritāḥ striyaḥ ||Panc_4.63||
children.translated_text: what is outside they do not actually do — such is the varied conduct of women. // Panc_4.63 //

children.text: ke nāma na vinaśyanti mithyā-jñānān nitambinīm |
children.translated_text: Who indeed does not perish from the false apprehension of a broad-hipped woman?

children.text: ramyāṃ te upasarpanti dīpābhāṃ śalabhā yathā ||Panc_4.64||
children.translated_text: Those who approach her, thinking her delightful, [perish] like moths toward a flame. // Panc_4.64 //

children.text: antar-viṣa-mayā hy etā bahiś caiva manoramāḥ |
children.translated_text: For these are poisonous within and charming without —

children.text: guñjā-phala-samākārā yoṣitaḥ kena nirmitāḥ ||Panc_4.65||
children.translated_text: like the <s>guñjā</s> berry in appearance — by whom were women created? // Panc_4.65 //

children.text: tāḍitā api daṇḍena śastrair api vikhaṇḍitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even when beaten with a rod, even when cut with weapons,

children.text: na vaśaṃ yoṣito yānti na dānair na ca saṃstavaiḥ ||Panc_4.66||
children.translated_text: women do not come under control — neither by gifts nor by praise. // Panc_4.66 //

children.text: āstāṃ tāvat kim anyena daurātmyeneha yoṣitām |
children.translated_text: Enough — what more need be said about the wickedness of women here?

children.text: vidhṛtaṃ svodareṇāpi ghnanti putram api svakam ||Panc_4.67||
children.translated_text: Even carried in their own womb, they kill even their own son. // Panc_4.67 //

children.text: rūkṣāyāṃ sneha-sad-bhāvaṃ kaṭhorāyāṃ sumārdavam |
children.translated_text: In one who is dry, [he imagines] the presence of affection; in one who is hard, supreme softness;

children.text: nīrasāyāṃ rasaṃ bālo bālikāyāṃ vikalpayet ||Panc_4.68||
children.translated_text: in one who is juiceless, flavor — the boy imagines [these] in the girl. // Panc_4.68 //

children.text: makara āha-bho mitra ! astv etat | paraṃ kiṃ karomi ? mamānartha-dvayam etat sañjātam | ekas tāvad gṛha-bhaṅgaḥ | aparas tvad-vidhena mitreṇa saha citta-viśleṣaḥ | athavā bhavaty evaṃ daiva-yogāt | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: O friend! Let that be so. But what can I do? A double misfortune has befallen me. One is the destruction of my household; the other is the estrangement from a friend like you. Or rather, it happens thus by the conjunction of fate. And it is said, for —

children.text: yādṛśaṃ mama pāṇḍityaṃ tādṛśaṃ dviguṇaṃ tava |
children.translated_text: Such as is my learning, yours is double of that;

children.text: nābhūj jāro na bhartā ca kiṃ nirīkṣasi nagnike ||Panc_4.69||
children.translated_text: there was no lover nor a husband — what are you gazing at, O naked one? ||Panc_4.69||

children.text: vānara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The monkey said: How is that?

children.text:
makaro 'bravīt-
kathā 12
hālika-dampatī-kathā
children.translated_text:
The crocodile said —
Tale 12
The Story of the Plowman Couple

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne hālika-dampatī prativasataḥ sma | sā ca hālika-bhāryā patyur vṛddha-bhāvāt sadaivānya-cittā na kathañcid gṛhe sthairyam ālambate | kevalaṃ para-puruṣān anveṣamāṇā paribhramati | atha kenacit para-vittāpahārakeṇa dhūrtena sā lakṣitā vijane proktā ca-subhage ! mṛta-bhāryo 'ham | tvad-darśanena smara-pīḍitaś ca | tad dīyatāṃ me rati-dakṣiṇā |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there dwelt a plowman couple. That plowman's wife, because of her husband's old age, was always thinking of another man and never maintained any steadfastness in the house. She merely wandered about seeking other men. Then a certain rogue, a thief of others' property, noticed her and said to her in a secluded place: Fair one! I am a widower. And seeing you, I am afflicted by love. So grant me the reward of love.

children.text: tatas tayābhihitam-bhoḥ subhaga ! yady evaṃ tad asti me patyuḥ prabhūtaṃ dhanam | sa ca vṛddhatvāt pracalitum apy asamarthaḥ | tatas tad-dhanam ādāyāham āgacchāmi | yena tvayā sahānyatra gatvā yathecchayā rati-sukham anubhaviṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Then she said: O handsome one! If so, then my husband has abundant wealth. And he, due to old age, is unable even to stir. So, taking that wealth, I shall come. And going elsewhere with you, I shall enjoy the pleasure of love as I wish.

children.text: so 'bravīt-rocate mahyam apy etat | tat pratyūṣe'tra sthāne śīghram eva samāgantavyam, yena śubhataraṃ kiñcin nagaraṃ gatvā tvayā saha jīva-lokaḥ saphalīkriyate |
children.translated_text: He said: This pleases me too. So at dawn you must come quickly to this very place, so that having gone to some fine city, life in this world may be made fruitful together with you.

children.text: sāpi tatheti pratijñāya prahasita-vadanā sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā rātrau prasupte bhartari sarvaṃ vittam ādāya pratyūṣa-samaye tat-kathita-sthānam upādravat | dhūrto 'pi tām agre vidhāya dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āśritya satvara-gatiḥ prasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: And she, having assented with 'so be it,' went home with a smiling face. At night, when her husband was asleep, taking all the wealth, she hastened at dawn to the place he had indicated. The rogue too, placing her in front, heading southward, set out with quick pace.

children.text: evaṃ tayor vrajator yojana-dvaya-mātreṇāgrataḥ kācin nadī samupasthitā | tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhūrtaś cintayāmāsa-kim aham anayā yauvana-prānte vartamānayā kariṣyāmi | kiṃ ca kadāpy asyāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ ko 'pi sameṣyati | tan me mahān anarthaḥ syāt | tat kevalam asyā vittam ādāya gacchāmi |
children.translated_text: Thus as the two were traveling, at a distance of about two <s>yojanas</s> ahead, a certain river appeared. Seeing it, the rogue thought: What will I do with this one who is at the end of her youth? Moreover, someone may sometime come after her. Then there would be great trouble for me. So I shall just take her wealth and go.

children.text: iti niścitya tām uvāca-priye ! sudustareyaṃ mahānadā | tad ahaṃ dravya-mātrāṃ pāre dhṛtvā samāgacchāmi | tatas tvām ekākinīṃ sva-pṛṣṭham āropya sukhenottārayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: Having resolved thus, he said to her: Beloved! This great river is very difficult to cross. So I, placing just the goods on the far side, shall come back. Then I shall carry you alone on my back and cross easily.

children.text:
sā prāha-subhaga ! evaṃ kriyatām | ity uktvāśiṣaṃ vittaṃ tasmai samarpayāmāsa |
atha tenābhihitaṃ-bhadre ! paridhānācchādana-vastram api samarpaya | yena jala-madhye niḥśaṅkaṃ vrajasi | tathānuṣṭhite dhūrto vittaṃ vastra-yugalaṃ cādāya yathācintita-viṣayaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text:
She said: Handsome one! Let it be done so. Having said this, she entrusted all the wealth to him.
Then he said: Good woman! Hand over even your upper and lower garments, so that you may go through the water without apprehension. When this was done, the rogue, taking the wealth and the pair of garments, went to the destination he had planned.

children.text: sāpi kaṇṭha-niveśita-hasta-yugalā sodvegā nadī-pulina-deśa upaviṣṭā yāvat tiṣṭhati tāvad etasminn antare kācic chṛgālikā māṃsa-piṇḍa-gṛhīta-vadanā tatrājagāma | āgatya ca yāvat paśyati, tāvan nadī mahān matsyaḥ salilān niṣkramya bahiḥ sthita āste | evaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sā māṃsa-piṇḍaṃ samutsṛjya taṃ matsyaṃ pratyupādravat | atrāntaraṃ ākāśād āvatīrthaṃ ko 'pi pratyupādravat | atrāntaram ākāśād avatīrya ko 'pi gṛdhras taṃ māṃsa-piṇḍam ādāya punaḥ kham utpatāta | matsyo 'pi śṛgālikāṃ dṛṣṭvā nadyāṃ praviveśa | sā śṛgālikāṃ dṛṣṭvā nadyāṃ praviveśa | sā śṛgālikā vyartha-śramā gṛdhram avalokayantī tayā nagnikayā sa-smitam abhihitā-
children.translated_text: And she, her pair of hands placed at her throat, sat anxiously on the riverbank. While she was thus waiting, in the meantime a certain she-jackal came there with a piece of meat held in her mouth. Having come and looking, she saw a large fish that had emerged from the water and was sitting outside. Seeing this, she released the piece of meat and rushed toward that fish. In the meantime, some vulture descended from the sky and seized that piece of meat and flew up again into the sky. The fish too, seeing the she-jackal, entered the river. That she-jackal, her effort wasted, looking at the vulture — was addressed by that naked woman with a smile:

children.text: gṛdhreṇāpahṛtaṃ māṃsaṃ matsyo 'pi salilaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: The meat was carried off by the vulture, the fish too has gone into the water —

children.text: matsya-māṃsa-paribhraṣṭe kiṃ nirīkṣyasi jambuke ||Panc_4.70||
children.translated_text: deprived of both fish and meat, what are you gazing at, O jackal? ||Panc_4.70||

children.text: mitraṃ hy amitratāṃ yātam aparaṃ me priyā mitrā |
children.translated_text: My friend has indeed become an enemy; the other — my dear friend [the wealth] —

children.text: gṛham anyena ca vyāptaṃ kim adyāpi bhaviṣyati ||Panc_4.71||
children.translated_text: and my home is occupied by another — what now will become [of me]? ||Panc_4.71||

children.text: athavā yuktam idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is rightly said —

children.text: kṣate prahārā nipatanty abhīkṣṇam anna-kṣaye vardhati jāṭharāgniḥ |
children.translated_text: On a wound, blows fall repeatedly; when food is gone, the digestive fire increases;

children.text: āpatsu vairāṇi samudbhavanti vāme vidhau sarvam idaṃ narāṇām ||Panc_4.72||
children.translated_text: in calamities, enmities arise — when fate is adverse, all this [befalls] men. ||Panc_4.72||

children.text: tat kiṃ karomi ? kim anena saha yuddhaṃ karomi ? kiṃ vā sāmnaiva sambodhya gṛhān niḥsārayāmi ? kiṃ vā bhedaṃ dānaṃ vā karomi ? athavāmum eva vānara-mitraṃ pṛcchāmi ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So what shall I do? Shall I fight with him? Or shall I address him conciliatorily and evict him from the house? Or shall I use dissension or bribery? Or rather, shall I ask this monkey-friend? And it is said —

children.text: yaḥ pṛṣṭvā kurute kāryaṃ praṣṭavyān sva-hitān gurūn |
children.translated_text: He who acts after consulting elders who are well-wishers and worth consulting —

children.text: na tasya jāyate vighnaḥ kasmiṃścid api karmaṇi ||Panc_4.73||
children.translated_text: no obstacle arises for him in any undertaking. ||Panc_4.73||

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya bhūyo 'pi tam eva jambū-vṛkṣam ārūḍhaṃ kapim apṛcchat-bho mitra ! paśya me manda-bhāgyatām | tat samprati gṛham api me balavattareṇa makareṇa ruddham | tad ahaṃ tvāṃ praṣṭum abhyāgataḥ | kathaya kiṃ karomi ? sāmādīnām upāyānāṃ madhye kasyātra viṣayaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, he again asked the monkey who had climbed that very <s>jambū</s> tree: O friend! See my ill fortune! Now even my home has been blocked by a stronger crocodile. So I have come to consult you. Tell me, what shall I do? Among the expedients beginning with conciliation, which one applies here?

children.text: sa āha-bhoḥ kṛtaghna pāpa-cārin ! mayā niṣiddho 'pi kiṃ bhūyo mām anusarasi | nāhaṃ tava mūrkhasyopadeśam api dāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: O ungrateful, evil-doer! Though forbidden by me, why do you follow me again? I shall not give advice even to a fool like you!

children.text: tac chrutvā makaraḥ prāha-bho mitra ! sāparādhasya me pūrva-sneham anusmṛtya hitopadeśaṃ dehi |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the crocodile said: O friend! Remembering our former affection, give beneficial advice even to an offender like me.

children.text: vānara āha-nāhaṃ te kathayiṣyāmi | yad bhāryā-vākyena bhavatāhaṃ samudre prakṣiptuṃ nītaḥ | tad evaṃ na yuktam | yadyapi bhāryā sarva-lokād api vallabhā bhavati, tathāpi na mitrāṇi bāndhavāś ca bhāryā-vākyena samudre prakṣipyante | tan mūrkha ! mūḍhatvena nāśas tava mayā prāg eva nivedita āsīt, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: The monkey said: I shall not tell you. Because at your wife's word you took me to be thrown into the ocean. That indeed is not proper. Even though a wife is dearer than all the world, still friends and kinsmen should not be thrown into the ocean at a wife's word. So, fool! I had told you before that your destruction [would come] through stupidity, for —

children.text: satāṃ vacanam ādiṣṭaṃ madena na karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, out of intoxication, does not heed the words enjoined by the good —

children.text: sa vināśam avāpnoti ghaṇṭoṣṭra iva satvaram ||Panc_4.74||
children.translated_text: he meets destruction quickly, like the bell-camel. ||Panc_4.74||

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 13
ujjvalaka-rathakāra-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said —
Tale 13
The Story of <s>Ujjvalaka</s> the Chariot-maker

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne ujjvalako nāma rathakāraḥ prativasati sma | sa cātīva dāridryopahataś cintitavān-aho ! dhig iyaṃ daridratāsmad-gṛhe | yataḥ sarvo 'pi janaḥ sva-karmaṇaiva ratas tiṣṭhati | asmadīyaḥ punar vyāpāro nātrādhiṣṭhāne'rhati | yataḥ sarva-lokānāṃ cirantanāś caturbhūmikā gṛhāḥ santi | mama ca nātra | tat kiṃ madīyena rathakāratvena prayojanam ? iti cintayitvā deśān niṣkrāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there dwelt a chariot-maker named <s>Ujjvalaka</s>. Afflicted by extreme poverty, he thought: Ah! Curse this poverty in our house! For everyone else remains content with his own occupation. But our trade is not viable here in this town, since everyone has old four-storied houses, but I have none here. So what use is my chariot-making? Having thought thus, he left the country.

children.text: yāvat kiñcid vanaṃ gacchati tāvad gahvarākāra-vana-gahana-madhye sūryāstam anavelāyāṃ sva-yūthād bhraṣṭāṃ prasava-vedanayā pīḍyamānām uṣṭrīm apaśyat | sa ca dāseraka-yuktām uṣṭrīṃ gṛhītvā sva-sthānābhimukhaḥ prasthitaḥ | gṛham āsādya rajjuṃ gṛhītvā tām uṣṭrikāṃ babandha | tataś ca tīkṣṇaṃ paraśum ādāya tasyāḥ pallavānayanārthaṃ parvataika-deśe gataḥ | tatra ca nūtanāni komalāni bahūni pallavāni cchittvā śirasi samāropya tasyāgre nicikṣepa | tayā ca tāni śanaiḥ śanair bhakṣitāni | paścāt pallava-bhakṣaṇa-prabhāvād aharniśaṃ pīvara-tanur uṣṭrī sañjātā | so 'pi dāserako mahān uṣṭraḥ sañjātaḥ | tataḥ sa nityam eva dugdhaṃ gṛhītvā sva-kuṭumbaṃ paripālayati |
children.translated_text: As he went into a certain forest, in the midst of a dense thicket shaped like a cave, at an untimely sunset, he saw a she-camel separated from her herd, afflicted by labor pains. And he, taking the she-camel along with her young calf, set out toward his own place. Having reached home, he tied that she-camel with a rope. Then, taking a sharp axe, he went to a part of the mountain to bring leaves for her. There, having cut many fresh tender leaves, placing them on his head, he threw them before her. And she ate them slowly. Afterwards, by the power of eating leaves, day and night the she-camel became fat-bodied. And that calf too became a great bull-camel. Then he always took milk and sustained his family.

children.text: atha rathakāreṇa vallabhatvād dāseraka-grīvāyāṃ mahatī ghaṇṭā pratibaddhā | paścād rathakāro vyacintayat-aho ! kim anyair duṣkṛta-karmabhiḥ | yāvan mamaitasmād evoṣṭrāparipālanād asya kuṭumbasya bhavyaṃ sañjātam | tat kim anyena vyāpāreṇa ?
children.translated_text: Now, out of fondness, the chariot-maker tied a great bell on the neck of the [first] calf. Afterwards the chariot-maker thought: Ah! What [use are] other ill-done trades? Since from this very camel-rearing alone, prosperity has come to this family. So what need of any other trade?

children.text: evaṃ vicintya gṛham āgatya priyām āha-bhadre ! samīcīno 'yaṃ vyāpāraḥ | tava sammatiś cet kuto 'pi dhanikāt kiñcid dravyam ādāya mayā gurjara-deśe gantavyaṃ kalabha-grahaṇāya | tāvat tvayaitau yatnena rakṣaṇīyau | yāvad aham aparām uṣṭrīṃ nītvā samāgacchāmi |
children.translated_text: Having thought thus, coming home, he said to his wife: Good woman! This is a proper trade. If you agree, I should borrow some money from some wealthy person and go to the <s>Gurjara</s> (Gujarat) country to acquire [more] young camels. Meanwhile you should carefully look after these two until I bring back another she-camel.

children.text: tataś ca gurjara-deśaṃ gatvoṣṭrīṃ gṛhītvā sva-gṛham āgataḥ | kiṃ bahunā ? tena tathā kṛtaṃ yathā tasya pracurā uṣṭrāḥ karabhāś ca sammilitāḥ | tatas tena mahad uṣṭra-yūthaṃ kṛtvā rakṣā-puruṣo dhṛtaḥ | tasya prativarṣaṃ vṛttyā karabham ekaṃ prayacchati | prativarṣam anyac cāharniśaṃ dugdha-pānaṃ tasya nirūpitam | evaṃ rathakāro 'pi nityam evoṣṭrī-karabha-vyāpāraṃ kurvan sukhena tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: Then having gone to the <s>Gurjara</s> country, taken a she-camel, and returned home — in short, he did such that he accumulated many camels and young camels. Then, having made a great camel-herd, he hired a guard. He gave him one young camel per year as wages. And every year, drinking of milk day and night was also allotted to him. Thus the chariot-maker lived happily, constantly engaging in the trade of she-camels and young camels.

children.text: atha te dāserakā adhiṣṭhānopavanāhārthaṃ gacchanti | komala-vallīr yathecchayā bhakṣayitvā mahati sarasi pānīyaṃ pītvā sāyantana-samaye mandaṃ mandaṃ līlayā gṛham āgacchanti | sa ca pūrva-dāserako madātirekāt pṛṣṭha āgatya milati | tatas taiḥ kalabhair abhihitam-aho ! manda-matir ayaṃ dāserako yathā yūthād bhraṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭhe sthitvā ghaṇṭāṃ vādayann āgacchati | yadi kasyāpi duṣṭa-sattvasya mukhe patiṣyati, tan nūnaṃ mṛtyum avāpsyati |
children.translated_text: Now those calves would go to the gardens near the town for grazing. Having eaten tender vines as they wished and drunk water at a great lake, in the evening they would come home slowly and playfully. And that first calf, out of excessive pride, would come at the rear. Then those [other] young camels said: Ah! This slow-witted calf, having become separated from the herd, standing at the back, ringing his bell, comes along. If he falls into the mouth of some fierce beast, he will surely meet death.

children.text: atha tasya tad-vanaṃ gāhamānasya kaścit siṃho ghaṇṭā-ravam ākarṇya samāyātaḥ | yāvad avalokayati, tāvad uṣṭrī-dāserakāṇāṃ yūthaṃ gacchati | ekas tu punaḥ pṛṣṭhe krīḍāṃ kurvan vallarīś caran yāvat tiṣṭhati, tāvad anye dāserakāḥ pānīyaṃ pītvā sva-gṛhe gatāḥ | so 'pi vanān niṣkramya yāvad diśo 'valokayati, tāvan na kañcin mārgaṃ paśyati vetti ca | yūthād bhraṣṭo mandaṃ mandaṃ bṛhac-chabdaṃ kurvan yāvat kiyad-dūraṃ gacchati, tāvat tac-chabdānusārī siṃho 'pi kramaṃ kṛtvā nibhṛto 'yaṃ vyavasthitaḥ | tato yāvad uṣṭraḥ samīpam āgataḥ, tāvat siṃhena lambhayitvā grīvāyāṃ gṛhīto māritaś ca |
children.translated_text: Now, as he was roaming in that forest, a certain lion, hearing the sound of the bell, came. Looking, he saw the herd of she-camels and calves going. But one [calf], playing at the rear, eating creepers — while he was lingering, the other calves had drunk water and gone to their homes. And he too, coming out of the forest, looking in all directions, could not see or know any path. Separated from the herd, going slowly and making a loud sound for some distance, the lion too, following that sound, took position and remained hidden. Then, when the camel came near, the lion leaped upon him, seized him by the neck, and killed him.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-satāṃ vacanam ādiṣṭam (74) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'He who does not heed the words enjoined by the good' (74).

children.text: atha tac chrutvā makaraḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that, the crocodile said —

children.text: upadeśa-pradātṝṇāṃ narāṇāṃ hitam icchatām |
children.translated_text: For men who give instruction, who desire the welfare [of others],

children.text: parasminn iha loke ca vyasanaṃ nopapadyate ||Panc_4.75||
children.translated_text: no adversity befalls them in this world or the next. ||Panc_4.75||

children.text: tata sarvathā kṛtaghnasyāpi me kuru prasādam upadeśa-pradānena | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So by all means, show grace to me, even though ungrateful, by giving instruction. And it is said —

children.text: upakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sādhutve tasya ko guṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is good to benefactors — what merit is there in his goodness?

children.text: apakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sa sādhuḥ sadbhir ucyate ||Panc_4.76||
children.translated_text: He who is good to those who do him harm — he is called good by the good. ||Panc_4.76||

children.text: tad ākarṇya vānaraḥ prāha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tarhi tatra gatvā tena saha yuddhaṃ kuru | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the monkey said: Good friend! If so, then go there and fight with him. And it is said —

children.text: hatas tvaṃ prāpsyasi svargaṃ jīvan gṛham atho yaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Killed, you will attain heaven; living, you [will gain] your home and also fame.

children.text: yudhyamānasya te bhāvi guṇa-dvayam anuttamam ||Panc_4.77||
children.translated_text: For you who fight, the outcome will be a pair of unsurpassed merits. ||Panc_4.77||

children.text: uttamaṃ praṇipātena śūraṃ bhedena yojayet |
children.translated_text: One who is superior [should be won] through supplication; a brave one should be set [against another] through dissension;

children.text: nīcam alpa-pradānena sama-śaktiṃ parākramaiḥ ||Panc_4.78||
children.translated_text: a low one [should be won] through a small gift; one of equal strength through valor. ||Panc_4.78||

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 14
mahācaturakākhya-śṛgāla-kathā
children.translated_text: He narrated — Story 14: The tale of the jackal named <s>Mahācaturaka</s> (the Exceedingly Clever).

children.text: āsīt kasmiṃścid deśe mahā-caturako nāma śṛgālaḥ | tena kadācid araṇye svayaṃ mṛto gajaḥ samāsāditaḥ | tasya samantāt paribhramati, paraṃ kaṭhināṃ tvacaṃ bhettuṃ na śaknoti | athātrāvasara itaś cetaś ca vicaran kaścit siṃhas tatraiva pradeśe samāyayau |
children.translated_text: In a certain country there was a jackal named <s>Mahācaturaka</s>. Once, in the forest, he came upon an elephant that had died on its own. He circled around it on all sides, but could not pierce the tough skin. Then, at this juncture, while wandering here and there, a certain lion arrived at that very spot.

children.text: atha siṃhaṃ samāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā sa kṣiti-tala-vinyasta-mauli-maṇḍalaḥ saṃyojita-kara-yugalaḥ sa-vinayam uvāca-svāmin ! tvadīyo 'haṃ lāguḍikaḥ sthitas tvad-arthe gajam imaṃ rakṣāmi | tad enaṃ bhakṣayatu svāmī |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the lion approach, he — with his crown placed on the ground, his palms joined, spoke humbly: 'Master! I am your servant, a doorkeeper, guarding this elephant for your sake. So let the master eat it.'

children.text: taṃ praṇataṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃhaḥ prāha-bhoḥ ! nāham anyena hataṃ sattvaṃ kadācid api bhakṣayāmi | tat tavaiva gajo 'yaṃ mayā prasādīkṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Seeing him prostrate, the lion said: 'Sir! I never eat a creature killed by another. So this elephant is yours — a gift of grace from me.'

children.text: tac chrutvā śṛgālaḥ sānandam āha-yuktam idaṃ svāmino nija-bhṛtyeṣu | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
antyāvastho 'pi mahān svāmi-guṇān na jahāti śuddhatayā |
children.translated_text: Even one in the direst condition, if great, does not abandon his lordly virtues, out of purity;

children.text: na śveta-bhāvam ujjhati śaṅkhaḥ śikhi-bhukta-mukto 'pi ||Panc_4.79||
children.translated_text: a conch shell, even when swallowed and disgorged by a peacock, does not abandon its whiteness. [Panc 4.79]
Hearing that, the jackal said joyfully: 'This is fitting of a master toward his own servants.' And it is said —

children.text: atha siṃhe gate kaścid vyāghraḥ samāyayau | tam api dṛṣṭvāsau vyacintayat-aho ! ekas tāvad durātmā praṇipātenāpavāhitaḥ | tat katham idānīm enam apavāhayiṣyāmi ? nūnaṃ śūro 'yam | na khalu bhedaṃ vinā sādhyo bhaviṣyati | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, when the lion had gone, a certain tiger arrived. Seeing him too, he thought: 'Ah! One wicked one has been sent away through prostration. So how shall I now send this one away? He is surely brave. Without dissension, he will certainly not be managed.' And it is said —

children.text: na yatra śakyate kartuṃ sāma dānam athāpi vā |
children.translated_text: Where neither conciliation nor gifts can be employed,

children.text: bhedas tatra prayoktavyo yataḥ sa vaśa-kārakaḥ ||Panc_4.80||
children.translated_text: there dissension must be used, for it brings [the enemy] under control. [Panc 4.80]

children.text: kiṃ ca sarva-guṇa-sampanno 'pi bhedena badhyate | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
antaḥ-sthenāviruddhena suvṛttenāticāruṇā |
children.translated_text: A pearl that is unbored from within, well-formed, and exceedingly beautiful —

children.text: antar-bhinnena samprāptaṃ mauktikenāpi bandhanam ||Panc_4.81||
children.translated_text: even that, once bored from within, attains bondage [i.e., is strung into a necklace]. [Panc 4.81]
Moreover, even one endowed with all virtues is caught through dissension. And it is said —

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya tasyābhimukho bhūtvā garvād unnata-kandharaḥ sa-sambhramam uvāca-māma ! katham atra bhavān mṛtyu-mukhe praviṣṭaḥ | yenaiṣa gajaḥ siṃhena vyāpāditaḥ | sa ca mām etad rakṣaṇaṃ niyujya nadyāṃ snānārthaṃ gataḥ | tena ca gacchatā mama samādiṣṭam-yadi kaścid iha vyāghraḥ samāyāti, tvayā suguptaṃ mām āvedanīyam | yena vanam idaṃ mayā nirvyāghraṃ kartavyam | yataḥ pūrvaṃ vyāghreṇaikena mayā vyāpādito gajaḥ śūnye bhakṣayitvocchiṣṭatāṃ nītaḥ | tad-dinād ārabhya vyāghrān prati prakupito 'smi |
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, turning to face him with neck raised proudly and in a great show of alarm, he said: 'Uncle! How have you entered the jaws of death here? For this elephant was killed by a lion. And he, having appointed me to guard it, has gone to the river for bathing. And as he left, he instructed me: "If any tiger comes here, you must secretly inform me, so that I may make this forest free of tigers. For previously a tiger killed and ate an elephant I had slain, leaving it as scraps. From that day onward, I am enraged against tigers."'

children.text: tac chrutvā vyāghraḥ santrastam āha-bho bhāgineya ! dehi me prāṇa-dakṣiṇām | tvayā tasyātra cirāyāyātasyāpi madīyā kāpi vārtā nākhyeyā | evam abhidhāya satvaraṃ palāyāñcakre |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the tiger said in alarm: 'O nephew! Give me the gift of my life! You must not tell him anything about me, even if he is long in coming back.' Having spoken thus, he fled quickly.

children.text: atha gate vyāghre tatra kaścid dvīpī samāyātaḥ | tam api dṛṣṭvāsau vyacintayat-dṛḍha-daṃṣṭro 'yaṃ citrakaḥ | tad asya pārśvād asya gajasya yathā carma-cchedo bhavati tathā karomi | evaṃ niścitya tam apy uvāca-bho bhaginī-suta ! kim iti cirād dṛṣṭo 'si | kathaṃ ca bubhukṣita iva lakṣyase ? tad atithir asi me | eṣa gajaḥ siṃhena hatas tiṣṭhati | ahaṃ cāsya tad-ādiṣṭo rakṣā-pālaḥ | paraṃ tathāpi yāvat siṃho na samāyāti, tāvad asya gajasya māṃsaṃ bhakṣayitvā tṛptiṃ kṛtvā drutataraṃ vraja |
children.translated_text: Then, after the tiger had gone, a certain leopard arrived. Seeing him too, he thought: 'This <s>Citraka</s> (leopard) has strong fangs. So I shall arrange it so that a cut in the hide of this elephant is made at his side.' Having thus resolved, he said to him: 'O sister's son! Why have you been seen after so long? And why do you appear to be hungry? You are my guest. This elephant, killed by a lion, lies here. And I have been appointed by him as its guard. But nevertheless, before the lion returns, eat the flesh of this elephant and, having satisfied yourself, depart quickly.'

children.text: sa āha-māma, tad evaṃ tan na kāryaṃ me māṃsāśanena, yato jīvan naro bhadra-śatāni paśyati | uktaṃ ca-yac chakyaṃ grasitaṃ yasya grastaṃ pariṇamec ca yat (23) ity ādi | tat sarvathā tad eva bhujyate yad eva pariṇamati | tad aham ito 'payāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Uncle! Then this should not be done — my eating flesh — for a man who lives sees a hundred blessings.' And it is said: 'What can be swallowed, what when swallowed can be digested...' (verse 23) and so on. In all cases, one should eat only what is digestible. So I shall depart from here.

children.text: śṛgāla āha-bho adhīra ! viśrabdho bhūtvā bhakṣaya tvam | tasyāgamanaṃ dūrato 'pi tavāhaṃ nivedayiṣyāmi | tathānuṣṭhite dīvpinā bhinnāṃ tvacaṃ vijñāya jambūkenābhihitam-bho bhaginī-suta ! gamyatām | eṣa siṃhaḥ samāyāti |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'O timid one! Eat with confidence! I shall inform you of his coming from a great distance.' When this had been done, noticing that the leopard had cut through the hide, the jackal said: 'O sister's son! Go now! The lion is coming.'

children.text: tac chrutvā citrako dūraṃ praṇaṣṭaḥ | atha yāvad asau tad-bheda-kṛta-dvāreṇa kiñcin māṃsaṃ bhakṣayati, tāvad atisaṅkruddho 'paraḥ śṛgālaḥ samāyayau | atha tam ātma-tulya-parākramaṃ dṛṣṭvā-uttamaṃ praṇipātena śūraṃ bhedena yojayet (78) iti ślokaṃ paṭhan tad-abhimukha-kṛta-prayāṇaḥ sva-daṃṣṭrābhis taṃ vidārya diśo bhāgaṃ kṛtvā svayaṃ sukhena cira-kālaṃ hasti-māṃsaṃ bubhuje |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the leopard fled far away. Then, just as he was eating some flesh through the opening made by the [leopard's] breach, another jackal, very angry, arrived. Seeing him, of prowess equal to his own, reciting the verse 'The best one by prostration, the brave one by dissension...' (verse 78), he rushed toward him, tore him apart with his own fangs, put him to flight, and himself ate the elephant's flesh comfortably for a long time.

children.text: evaṃ tvam api taṃ ripuṃ sva-jātīyaṃ yuddhena paribhūya diśo-bhāgaṃ kuru | no cet paścād baddha-mūlād asmāt tvam api vināśam avāpsyasi | uktaṃ ca yataḥ-
children.translated_text: So you too should vanquish that enemy of your own kind by battle and put him to flight. Otherwise, afterward you will also meet your destruction from this firmly rooted one. And it is said —

children.text: sambhāvyaṃ goṣu sampannaṃ sambhāvyaṃ brāhmaṇe tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: From cows, abundance is to be expected; from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, austerity is to be expected;

children.text: sambhāvyaṃ strīṣu cāpalyaṃ sambhāvyaṃ jātito bhayam ||Panc_4.82||
children.translated_text: from women, fickleness is to be expected; from one's own kin, danger is to be expected. [Panc 4.82]

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: subhikṣāṇi vicitrāṇi śithilāḥ paura-yoṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Varied plenty, and yielding town-women —

children.text: eko doṣo videśasya svajātir yad virudhyate ||Panc_4.83||
children.translated_text: the one fault of a foreign land is that one's own kinsman opposes. [Panc 4.83]

children.text: makara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The crocodile said: 'How is that?'

children.text: vānaro 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: The monkey narrated —

children.text:
kathā 15
citrāṅga-nāma-sārameya-kathā
children.translated_text: Story 15: The tale of the dog named <s>Citrāṅga</s>.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne citrāṅgo nāma sārameyaḥ | tatra ca cira-kālaṃ durbhikṣaṃ patitam | annābhāvāt sārameyādayo niṣkulatāṃ gantum ārabdhāḥ | atha citrāṅgaḥ kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭhas tad-bhayād deśāntaraṃ gataḥ | tatra ca kasmiṃścit pure kasyacid gṛha-medhino gṛhiṇyāḥ prasādena pratidinaṃ gṛhaṃ praviśya vividhānnāni bhakṣayan parāṃ tṛptiṃ gacchati | paraṃ tad-gṛhād bahir niṣkrānto 'nyair madoddhata-sārameyaiḥ sarva-dikṣu parivṛtya sarvāṅgaṃ daṃṣṭrābhir vidāryate | tatas tena vicintitavān-aho ! varaṃ sva-deśo yatra durbhikṣe'pi sukhena sthīyate | na ca ko 'pi yuddhaṃ karoti | tad evaṃ sva-nagaraṃ vrajāmi ity avadhārya sva-sthānaṃ prati jagāma |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there was a dog named <s>Citrāṅga</s> (Spotted-limbs). There, a long famine fell upon the land. Due to the absence of food, dogs and others began to perish. Then <s>Citrāṅga</s>, his throat emaciated with hunger, went to another country out of fear. And there, in a certain city, through the grace of a certain householder's wife, entering the house each day, eating various foods, he attained the highest satisfaction. But when he emerged from that house, other dogs, intoxicated with pride, surrounded him on all sides and tore his entire body with their fangs. Then he thought: 'Ah! Better is one's own land, where even in famine one dwells in comfort. And no one wages war. So I shall return to my own town.' Having thus resolved, he went back to his own place.

children.text: athāsau deśāntarāt samāyātaḥ sarvair api svajanaiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ-bhoś citrāṅga ! kathayāsmākaṃ deśāntara-vārtām | kīdṛg deśaḥ ? kiṃ ceṣṭitaṃ lokasya ? ka āhāraḥ ? kaś ca vyavahāras tatra iti |
children.translated_text: Then, having returned from abroad, he was asked by all his kinsmen: 'O <s>Citrāṅga</s>! Tell us the news of foreign lands. What kind of country is it? What are the customs of the people? What is the food? And what are the dealings there?'

children.text: sa āha-kiṃ kathyate videśasya svarūpa-viṣayaḥ ? subhikṣāṇi vicitrāṇi śithilāḥ paura-yoṣitaḥ (83) iti paṭhati |
children.translated_text: He said: 'What can be told about the nature of foreign lands?' And he recited: 'Varied plenty, and yielding town-women...' (verse 83) and so on.

children.text: so 'pi makaras tad-upadeśaṃ śrutvā kṛta-maraṇa-niścayo vānaram anujñāpya svāśrayaṃ gataḥ | tatra ca tena sva-gṛha-praviṣṭenātatāyinā saha vigrahaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍha-sattvāvaṣṭambhanāc ca taṃ vyāpādya svāśrayaṃ ca labdhvā sukhena cira-kālam atiṣṭhat | sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: That crocodile too, hearing that advice, having resolved upon death, took leave of the monkey, and went to his own abode. There, having entered his own home, having waged war against the usurper, and by his firm determination having slain him and having recovered his home, he lived happily for a long time. Well is this said —

children.text: akṛtvā pauruṣaṃ yā śrīḥ kiṃ tayālasa-bhāgyayā |
children.translated_text: What is that prosperity which comes without exerting manly effort? What use is that fortune of the lazy?

children.text: kuraṅgo 'pi samaśnāti daivād upanataṃ tṛṇam ||Panc_4.84||
children.translated_text: Even a deer eats by fate the grass that comes before it. [Panc 4.84]

children.text:
iti śrī-viṣṇu-śarma-viracite pañcatantre labdha-praṇāśaṃ nāma
caturthaṃ tantraṃ samāptam
||4||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>tantra</s> (book), named <s>Labdhapraṇāśam</s> (Loss of What Was Gained), in the <s>Pañcatantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>. ||4||

children.text: pañcamaṃ tantram
children.translated_text: The Fifth <s>Tantra</s> (Book).

children.text: aparīkṣita-kārakam
children.translated_text: <s>Aparīkṣitakārakam</s> (Acting Without Investigation).

children.text: kṣapaṇaka-kathā
children.translated_text: The story of the <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s> (mendicant).

children.text: athedam ārabhyate'parīkṣita-kārakaṃ nāma pañcamaṃ tantram | tasyāyam ādimaḥ ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now begins the fifth <s>tantra</s> named <s>Aparīkṣitakārakam</s> (Acting Without Investigation). Its opening verse is —

children.text: kudṛṣṭaṃ kuparijñātaṃ kuśrutaṃ kuparīkṣitam |
children.translated_text: What is ill-seen, ill-understood, ill-heard, and ill-examined —

children.text: tan nareṇa na kartavyaṃ nāpitenātra yat kṛtam ||Panc_5.1||
children.translated_text: that should not be done by a man, as was done by the barber in this case. [Panc 5.1]

children.text: tad yathānuśrūyate-asti dākṣiṇātye janapade pāṭaliputraṃ nāma nagaram | tatra maṇibhadro nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati sma | tasya ca dharmārtha-kāma-mokṣa-karmāṇi kurvato vidhi-vaśād dhana-kṣayaḥ sañjātaḥ | tato vibhava-kṣayād apamāna-paramparayā paraṃ viṣādaṃ gataḥ | athānyadā rātrau suptiś cintitavān-aho dhig iyaṃ daridratā | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: As the story goes — in a southern country there is a city named <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. There lived a merchant named <s>Maṇibhadra</s>. While he was engaged in the duties of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), by the power of fate, a loss of wealth occurred. Then, due to the loss of prosperity, through a succession of humiliations, he fell into the deepest despair. Then one night, lying sleepless, he thought: 'Alas! Curse this poverty!' And it is said —

children.text: śīlaṃ śaucaṃ kṣāntir dākṣiṇyaṃ madhuratā kule janma |
children.translated_text: Character, purity, forbearance, courtesy, sweetness, noble birth —

children.text: na virājanti hi sarve vitta-vihīnasya pusuṣasya ||Panc_5.2||
children.translated_text: none of these shine in a man devoid of wealth. [Panc 5.2]

children.text: māno vā darpo vā vijñānaṃ vibhramaḥ subuddhir vā |
children.translated_text: Pride, or self-respect, or learning, or grace, or good judgment —

children.text: sarvaṃ praṇaśyati samaṃ vitta-vihīno yadā puruṣaḥ ||Panc_5.3||
children.translated_text: all these perish together when a man is devoid of wealth. [Panc 5.3]

children.text: pratidivasaṃ yāti layaṃ vasanta-vātāhateva śiśira-śrīḥ |
children.translated_text: Day by day it wanes — like the beauty of winter struck by the spring breeze —

children.text: buddhir buddhimatām api kuṭumba-bhara-cintayā satatam ||Panc_5.4||
children.translated_text: the intellect even of the intelligent, constantly [burdened] with worry over maintaining the family. [Panc 5.4]

children.text: naśyati vipulamater api buddhiḥ puruṣasya manda-vibhavasya |
children.translated_text: The intellect of a man of even vast understanding perishes when his means are meager,

children.text: ghṛta-lavaṇa-taila-taṇḍula-vastrendhana-cintayā satatam ||Panc_5.5||
children.translated_text: due to constant worry about ghee, salt, oil, rice, clothing, and firewood. [Panc 5.5]

children.text: gaṇanam iva naṣṭa-tārakaṃ
children.translated_text: Like a sky from which the stars have vanished,

children.text: suṣkam iva saraḥ śmaśānam iva raudram |
children.translated_text: like a dried-up lake, like a terrifying cremation-ground —

children.text: priya-darśanam api rūkṣaṃ
children.translated_text: even though pleasant to look at, harsh

children.text: bhavati gṛhaṃ dhana-vihīnasya ||Panc_5.6||
children.translated_text: is the home of one devoid of wealth. [Panc 5.6]

children.text: na vibhāvyante laghavo vitta-vihīnāḥ puro 'pi nivasantaḥ |
children.translated_text: The lowly who are devoid of wealth are not perceived, even while living right before one's eyes —

children.text: satataṃ jāta-vinaṣṭāḥ payasām iva budbudāḥ payasi ||Panc_5.7||
children.translated_text: constantly arising and perishing, like bubbles of water upon water. [Panc 5.7]

children.text: sukulaṃ kuśalaṃ sujanaṃ vihāya kula-kuśala-śīla-vikale'pi |
children.translated_text: Abandoning one of good family, good conduct, and good character, upon one who is deficient in family, conduct, and virtue,

children.text: āḍhye kalpa-tarāv iva nityaṃ rajyanti jana-nivahāḥ ||Panc_5.8||
children.translated_text: if wealthy — as upon a wish-fulfilling tree — crowds of people always dote. [Panc 5.8]

children.text: viphalam iha pūrva-sukṛtaṃ vidyāvanto 'pi kula-samudbhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Vain is the past merit of those who are learned and born of good family —

children.text: yasya yadā vibhavaḥ syāt tasya tadā dāsatāṃ yānti ||Panc_5.9||
children.translated_text: whoever has prosperity at a given time, to him at that time they become servants. [Panc 5.9]

children.text: laghur ayam āha na lokaḥ kāmaṃ garjantam api patiṃ payasām |
children.translated_text: The world says 'He is lowly' — it does not care, even though the lord of waters thunders;

children.text: sarvam alajjākaram iha yad yat kurvanti paripūrṇāḥ ||Panc_5.10||
children.translated_text: everything shameless that the full and prosperous do here is [accepted]. [Panc 5.10]

children.text: evaṃ sampradhārya bhūyo 'py acintayat-tad aham anaśanaṃ kṛtvā prāṇān utsṛjāmi | kim anena vyartha-jīvita-vyasanena ? evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā suptaḥ | atha tasya svapne padmanidhiḥ kṣapaṇaka-rūpo darśanaṃ dattvā provāca-bhoḥ śreṣṭhin ! mā tvaṃ vairāgyaṃ gaccha | ahaṃ padmanidhis tava pūrva-puruṣopārjitaḥ | tad anenaiva rūpeṇa prātas tvad-gṛham āgamiṣyāmi | tat tvayāhaṃ laguḍa-prahāreṇa śirasi tāḍanīyaḥ, yena kanaka-mayo bhūtvākṣayo bhavāmi |
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, he thought again: 'Then I shall fast unto death and give up my life. What use is this vice of futile living?' Having thus resolved, he fell asleep. Then in his dream, the treasure-spirit <s>Padmanidhi</s>, appearing in the form of a <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s> (mendicant), showed himself and said: 'O merchant! Do not fall into despair. I am <s>Padmanidhi</s>, earned by your forefathers. So I shall come to your house tomorrow morning in this very form. Then you must strike me on the head with a club, whereby I shall become made of gold and be inexhaustible.'

children.text: atha prātaḥ prabuddhaḥ san svapnaṃ smaraṃś cintā-cakram ārūḍhas tiṣṭhati-aho satyo 'yaṃ svapnaḥ kiṃ vā asatyo bhaviṣyati, na jñāyate | athavā nūnaṃ mithyānena bhāvyam | yato 'ham ahar-niśaṃ kevalaṃ vittam eva cintayāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then, waking in the morning, remembering the dream, he remained caught in a whirl of thought: 'Ah, will this dream be true or false — it is not known. Or rather, surely it must be false. For I think of nothing but wealth day and night.' And it is said —

children.text: vyādhitena sa-śokena cintā-grastena jantunā |
children.translated_text: A dream seen by one who is diseased, grief-stricken, consumed by worry,

children.text: kāmārtenātha mattena dṛṣṭaḥ svapno nirarthakaḥ ||Panc_5.11||
children.translated_text: tormented by desire, or intoxicated — is meaningless. [Panc 5.11]

children.text: etasminn antare tasya bhāryayā kaścin nāpitaḥ pāda-prakṣālanāyāhūtaḥ atrāntare ca yathā-nirdiṣṭaḥ kṣapaṇakaḥ sahasā prādurbabhūva | atha sa tam ālokya prahṛṣṭa-manā yathāsanna-kāṣṭha-daṇḍena taṃ śirasy atāḍayat | so 'pi suvarṇa-mayo bhūtvā tat-kṣaṇāt bhūmau nipatitaḥ | atha taṃ sa śreṣṭhī nibhṛtaṃ sva-gṛha-madhye kṛtvā nāpitaṃ santoṣya provāca-tad etad dhanaṃ vastrāṇi ca mayā dattāni gṛhāṇa | bhadra ! punaḥ kasyacin nākhyeyo 'yaṃ vṛttāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile, a certain barber had been summoned by his wife to wash her feet. At that very moment, the <s>kṣapaṇaka</s> (Jain monk) who had been pointed out suddenly appeared. Then, seeing him, [the merchant,] his mind delighted, struck him on the head with a wooden staff that was close at hand. And that one, having become golden, fell to the ground at that very instant. Then the merchant, having secretly placed him inside his house, satisfied the barber and said: 'Take this wealth and these garments that I have given. Good sir! And do not tell this account to anyone else.'

children.text: nāpito 'pi sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā vyacintayat-nūnam ete sarve'pi nagnakāḥ śirasi tāḍitāḥ kāñcana-mayā bhavanti | tad aham api prātaḥ prabhūtān āhūya laguḍaiḥ śirasi hanmi, yena prabhūtaṃ hāṭakaṃ me bhavati | evaṃ cintayato mahatā kaṣṭena niśāticakrāma |
children.translated_text: The barber too, having gone to his own house, thought: 'Surely, all these naked monks become golden when struck on the head. So I too, tomorrow morning, shall summon a great many of them and strike them on the head with clubs, whereby a great deal of gold will be mine.' While he was thinking thus, with great difficulty the night passed.

children.text: atha prabhāte'bhyutthāya bṛhal laguḍam ekaṃ praguṇīkṛtya, kṣapaṇaka-vihāraṃ gatvā jinendrasya pradakṣiṇa-trayaṃ vidhāya, jānubhyām avaniṃ gatvā vaktra-dvāra-nyastottarīyāñcalas tāra-svareṇemaṃ ślokam apaṭhat-
children.translated_text: Then, rising at dawn, having readied a large club, going to the <s>kṣapaṇaka</s> monastery, performing three circumambulations of the <s>Jinendra</s> (the Jain Lord), falling to his knees upon the ground, with the end of his upper garment placed at his mouth, he recited this verse in a loud voice —

children.text: jayanti te jinā yeṣāṃ kevala-jñāna-śālinām |
children.translated_text: Victorious are those <s>Jinas</s>, endowed with absolute knowledge,

children.text: ā janmanaḥ smarotpattau mānasenoṣarāyitam ||Panc_5.12||
children.translated_text: from whose birth, at the arising of recollection, the mind has become barren. // Panc_5.12 //

children.text: anyac ca-
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: sā jihvā yā jinaṃ stauti tac-cittaṃ yaj jine ratam |
children.translated_text: That tongue alone is [worthy] which praises the <s>Jina</s>; that mind which delights in the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: tau eva tu karau ślāghyau yau tat-pūjā-karau karau ||Panc_5.13||
children.translated_text: and those hands alone are praiseworthy which are the hands that worship him. // Panc_5.13 //

children.text: tathā ca-
dhyāna-vyājam upetya cintayasi kām unmīlya cakṣuḥ kṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Under the pretense of meditation, you are thinking of whom? Opening your eyes for a moment,

children.text: paśyānaṅga-śarāturaṃ janam imaṃ trātāpi no rakṣasi |
children.translated_text: behold these people tormented by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love) — you are a savior, yet you do not save them.

children.text: mithyā-kāruṇiko 'si nirghṛṇataras tvattaḥ kuto 'nyaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: You are falsely compassionate — who is a more heartless man than you?

children.text: serṣyaṃ māra-vadhūbhir ity abhihito bauddho jinaḥ pātu vaḥ ||Panc_5.14||
children.translated_text: 'Thus jealously addressed by the wives of <s>Māra</s>' — may the <s>Jina</s> of the Buddhists protect you! // Panc_5.14 //
And likewise —

children.text: evaṃ saṃstūya, tataḥ pradhāna-kṣapaṇakaṇam āsādya kṣiti-nihita-jānu-caraṇaḥ-namo 'stu vande ity uccārya, labdha-dharma-vṛddhy-āśīrvādaḥ sukha-mālikānugraha-labdha-vratādeśa uttarīya-nibaddha-granthiḥ sapraśrayam idam āha-bhagavan adya viharaṇa-kriyā samasta-muni-sametenāsmad-gṛhe kartavyā |
children.translated_text: Having thus praised [the Jina], he then approached the chief <s>kṣapaṇaka</s>, and with knees and feet placed on the ground, uttering 'I salute, I bow,' having received a blessing for the increase of <s>dharma</s>, having obtained the instruction of vows through the grace of <s>Sukhamālikā</s>, with a knot tied in his upper garment, he said respectfully: 'Venerable sir, today the ceremony of the procession is to be performed in our house, with the entire assembly of monks.'

children.text: tac chrutvā nāpita āha-bhagavan ! vedmy ahaṃ yuṣmad-dharmam | paraṃ bhavato bahu-śrāvakā āhvayanti | sāmprataṃ punaḥ pustakācchādana-yogyāni karpaṭāni bahu-mūlyāni praguṇīkṛtāni | tathā pustakānāṃ lekhanārthaṃ lekhakānāṃ ca vittaṃ sañcitam āste tat sarvathā kālocitaṃ kāryam |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the barber said: 'Venerable sir! I know your customs. But many lay devotees invite you. At present, moreover, costly cloths suitable for covering manuscripts have been prepared, and wealth has been collected for the scribes to copy the manuscripts. So in every way, the deed must be done at the proper time.'

children.text: tato nāpito 'pi sva-gṛhaṃ gataḥ | tatra ca gatvā khadira-mayaṃ laguḍaṃ sajjīkṛtya kapāṭa-yugalaṃ dvāri samādhāya sārdha-praharaika-samaye bhūyo 'pi vihāra-dvāram āśritya sarvān bhakti-yuktān api paricita-śrāvakān parityajya prahṛṣṭa-manasas tasya pṛṣṭhato yayuḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Then the barber too went to his own house. And having gone there, having readied a club made of <s>khadira</s> wood, having placed the two door-panels at the entrance, at the time of one and a half <s>praharas</s> [after noon], going once again to the monastery gate, leaving aside all the familiar lay devotees — even those full of devotion — [the monks,] with joyful hearts, followed behind him. Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: ekākī gṛha-santyaktaḥ pāṇi-pātro digambaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Alone, having left his home, his alms-bowl his only vessel, naked —

children.text: so 'pi sambādhyate loke tṛṣṇayā paśya kautukam ||Panc_5.15||
children.translated_text: even he is beset in this world by desire — behold the wonder! // Panc_5.15 //

children.text: jīryante jīryataḥ keśā dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ |
children.translated_text: The hair wastes away as one ages; the teeth waste away as one ages;

children.text: cakṣuḥ śrotre ca jīryete tṛṣṇaikā taruṇāyate ||Panc_5.16||
children.translated_text: the eyes and ears waste away — desire alone grows young. // Panc_5.16 //

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ gṛha-madhye tān praveśya dvāraṃ nibhṛtaṃ pidhāya, laguḍa-prahāraiḥ śirasy atāḍayat | te'pi tāḍyamānā eke mṛtāḥ, anye bhinna-mastakā phūtkartum upacakramire | atrāntare tam ākrandam ākarṇya koṭara-kṣapālenābhihitam-bho bhoḥ kim ayaṃ kolāhalo nagara-madhye ? tad gamyatām |
children.translated_text: Then, having ushered them inside the house, having secretly shut the door, he struck them on the head with club-blows. Some of those who were struck died; others, with split skulls, began to cry out in pain. In the meanwhile, hearing that uproar, the city governor said: 'Ho, ho! What is this commotion in the midst of the city? Let it be investigated.'

children.text: te sa sarve tadādeśakāriṇas tat-sahitā vegāt tad-gṛhaṃ gatā yāvat paśyanti tāvad rudhira-plāvita-dehāḥ palāyamānā nagnakā dṛṣṭāḥ pṛṣṭāś ca-bhoḥ kim etat ? te procur yathāvasthitaṃ nāpita-vṛttam |
children.translated_text: And all those who were carrying out his orders went swiftly with him to that house. As they looked, they saw naked monks with bodies drenched in blood, fleeing. And when asked: 'Sirs! What is this?' — they reported the barber's actions as they had occurred.

children.text: tair api sa nāpito baddho hata-śeṣaiḥ saha dharmādhiṣṭhānaṃ nītaḥ | tair nāpitaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ-bhoḥ ! kim etat bhavatā kukṛtyam anuṣṭhitam ?
children.translated_text: And he, the barber, was bound by them and, together with those who survived the beating, was taken to the court of justice. The barber was asked by them: 'Sir! What is this evil deed you have committed?'

children.text: sa āha-kiṃ karomi ? mayā śreṣṭhi-maṇibhadra-gṛhe dṛṣṭa evaṃvidho vyatikaraḥ | so 'pi sarvaṃ maṇiprabha-vṛttāntaṃ yathā-dṛṣṭam akathayat |
children.translated_text: He said: 'What can I do? I saw this very kind of result in the house of the merchant <s>Maṇibhadra</s>.' And he told the whole story of <s>Maṇiprabha</s> exactly as he had seen it.

children.text: tataḥ śreṣṭhinam āhūya te bhaṇitavantaḥ-bhoḥ śreṣṭhin ! kiṃ tvayā kaścit kṣapaṇako vyāpāditaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then, having summoned the merchant, they said: 'O merchant! Did you kill some <s>kṣapaṇaka</s>?'

children.text: tataḥ tenāpi sarvaḥ kṣapaṇaka-vṛttāntas teṣāṃ niveditaḥ | atha tair abhihitam-aho śūlam āropyatām asau duṣṭātmā kuparikṣitakārī nāpitaḥ | tathānuṣṭhite tair abhihitam-
children.translated_text: Then he too reported the entire account of the <s>kṣapaṇaka</s> to them. Then they declared: 'Let that evil-souled barber who acted without proper examination be impaled on a stake!' When this was done, they proclaimed —

children.text: kukkuṭaṃ kuparijñātaṃ kuśrutaṃ kuparīkṣitam |
children.translated_text: A cock poorly recognized, something poorly heard, something poorly examined —

children.text: tan nareṇa na kartavyaṃ nāpitenātra yat kṛtam ||Panc_5.16a||
children.translated_text: that should not be done by a man — [nor] what was done here by the barber. // Panc_5.16a //

children.text: athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: aparīkṣya na kartavyaṃ kartavyaṃ suparīkṣitam |
children.translated_text: What has not been examined should not be done; what should be done must be well examined;

children.text: paścād bhavati santāpo brāhmaṇī nakulaṃ yathā ||Panc_5.17||
children.translated_text: afterwards comes remorse — as the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> [regretted] the mongoose. // Panc_5.17 //

children.text: maṇibhadra āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇibhadra</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: te dharmādhikāriṇaḥ procuḥ-
children.translated_text: Those judges of justice said:

children.text:
kathā 1
brāhmaṇī-nakula-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 1
The Story of the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> and the Mongoose

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne devaśarmā nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati sma | tasya bhāryā prasūtā sutam ajanayat | tasminn eva dine nakulī nakulaṃ prasūya sṛtā | atha sā suta-vatsalā dārakavattam api nakulaṃ stanya-dānābhyaṅga-mardanādibhiḥ pupoṣa, paraṃ tasya na viśvasiti | apatya-snehasya sarva-snehātiriktatayā satatam evam āśaṅkate yat kadācid eṣa sva-jāti-doṣa-vaśād asya dārakasya viruddham ācariṣyati iti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Devaśarman</s>. His wife gave birth to a son. On that very day, a female mongoose gave birth to a young mongoose and died. Then that mother, full of love for her child, raised the mongoose too — like her own child — with breast-feeding, oil-massage, and the like. But she did not trust him. Because of the surpassing nature of maternal love, she always feared thus: 'Someday, by the fault of his own [animal] nature, he will act harmfully toward my boy.' And it is said —

children.text: kuputro 'pi bhavet puṃsāṃ hṛdayānanda-kārakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a bad son brings joy to the hearts of men —

children.text: durvinītaḥ kurūpo 'pi mūrkho 'pi vyasanī khalaḥ ||Panc_5.18||
children.translated_text: even if ill-mannered, ugly, foolish, addicted [to vice], or wicked. // Panc_5.18 //

children.text: evaṃ ca bhāṣate lokaś candanaṃ kila śītalam |
children.translated_text: And thus the world says: 'Sandalwood is indeed cool,

children.text: putra-gātrasya saṃsparśaś candanād atiricyate ||Panc_5.19||
children.translated_text: but the touch of a son's body surpasses even sandalwood.' // Panc_5.19 //

children.text: sauhṛdasya na vāñchanti janakasya hitasya ca |
children.translated_text: Of affection, of a father, of a benefactor,

children.text: lokāḥ prapālakasyāpi yathā putrasya bandhanam ||Panc_5.20||
children.translated_text: and of a protector — people do not desire the bonds as they desire those of a son. // Panc_5.20 //

children.text: atha sā kadācic chayyāyāṃ putraṃ śāyayitvā jala-kumbham ādāya patim uvāca-brāhmaṇa, jalārtham ahaṃ taḍāge yāsyāmi | tvayā putro 'yaṃ nakulād rakṣaṇīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now one day, having laid her son to sleep on the bed, she took a water-pot and said to her husband: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall go to the pond for water. This son of ours must be protected by you from the mongoose.'

children.text: atha tasyāṃ gatāyāṃ, pṛṣṭhe brāhmaṇo 'pi śūnyaṃ gṛhaṃ muktvā bhikṣārthaṃ kvacin nirgataḥ | mātāpi taṃ rudhira-klinna-mukham ālokya śaṅkita-cittā nūnam anena durātmanā dārako bhakṣitaḥ iti niścintya kopāt tasyopari taṃ jala-kumbhaṃ cikṣepa |
children.translated_text: Then, when she had gone, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too left the empty house and went out somewhere for alms. The mother, seeing his [the mongoose's] mouth smeared with blood, became suspicious in mind — 'Surely this wicked one has eaten the child' — and, resolving thus, in anger hurled the water-pot upon him.

children.text: evaṃ sā nakulaṃ vyāpādya yāvat pralapantī gṛhe āgacchati, tāvat sutas tathaiva suptas tiṣṭhati | samīpe kṛṣṇa-sarpaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtam avalokya putra-vadha-śokenātma-śiro vakṣaḥ-sthalaṃ ca tāḍitum ārabdhā |
children.translated_text: Having thus killed the mongoose, as she entered the house lamenting, the son was still sleeping just as before. Seeing a black serpent cut to pieces nearby, she began striking her own head and chest with grief for having killed her [innocent] son [i.e., her foster-son, the mongoose].

children.text: atrāntare brāhmaṇo gṛhīta-nirvāpaḥ samāyāto yāvat paśyati tāvat putra-śoko 'bhitaptā brāhmaṇī pralapati-bho bho lobhātman ! lobhābhibhūtena tvayā na kṛtaṃ mad-vacaḥ | tad anubhava sāmprataṃ putra-mṛtyu-duḥkha-vṛkṣa-phalam | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: In the meanwhile, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who had obtained alms, arrived. As he looked, the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, tormented by grief for [killing] her son [the mongoose], was lamenting: 'O you, greedy-souled one! Overcome by greed, you did not heed my words. So now taste the fruit of the tree of grief for a son's death!' Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: atilobho na kartavyaḥ kartavyas tu pramāṇataḥ |
children.translated_text: Excessive greed should not be indulged in; one should act with due measure;

children.text: atilobhaja-doṣeṇa jambuko nidhanaṃ gataḥ ||Panc_5.21||
children.translated_text: by the fault born of excessive greed, a jackal met his death. // Panc_5.21 //

children.text: brāhmaṇa āha-kim etat ?
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: sā prāha-
children.translated_text: She said —

children.text:
kathā 2
lobhāviṣṭa-cakra-dhara-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 2
The Story of the Greedy Discus-Bearer

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne catvāro brāhmaṇa-putrāḥ parasparaṃ mitratāṃ gatā vasanti sma | te cāpi dāridryopahatāḥ parasparaṃ mantraṃ cakruḥ-aho dhig iyaṃ daridratā ! uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: In a certain town, four <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> youths, having become friends with one another, lived together. And they, stricken by poverty, consulted with each other: 'Ah, cursed is this poverty!' And it is said —

children.text: varaṃ vanaṃ vyāghra-gajādi-sevitaṃ
children.translated_text: Better a forest inhabited by tigers and elephants,

children.text: janena hīnaṃ bahu-kaṇṭakāvṛtam |
children.translated_text: devoid of people, covered with many thorns,

children.text: tṛṇāni śayyā paridhāna-valkalaḥ
children.translated_text: with grass for a bed and bark for clothing,

children.text: na bandhu-madhye dhana-hīna-jīvitam ||Panc_5.22||
children.translated_text: than life without wealth in the midst of kinsmen. // Panc_5.22 //

children.text: tathā ca-
svāmī dveṣṭi susevito 'pi sahasā projjhanti sad-bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: The master despises [him] even when well served; worthy kinsmen suddenly cast [him] off;

children.text: rājante na guṇās tyajanti tanujāḥ sphārībhavanty āpadaḥ |
children.translated_text: virtues do not shine; children abandon [him]; calamities expand;

children.text: bhāryā sādhu suvaṃśajāpi bhajate no yānti mitrāṇi ca
children.translated_text: even a good wife, well-born, does not attend [him]; friends do not come;

children.text: nyāyāropita-vikramāṇy api nṛṇāṃ yeṣāṃ na hi syād dhanam ||Panc_5.23||
children.translated_text: and even lawfully acquired valor [avails not] — for men who have no wealth. // Panc_5.23 //
And likewise —

children.text: śūraḥ surūpaḥ subhagaś ca vāgmī
children.translated_text: Heroic, handsome, fortunate, and eloquent,

children.text: śastrāṇi śāstrāṇi vidāṃkarotu |
children.translated_text: let him master weapons and scriptures —

children.text: arthaṃ vinā naiva yaśaś ca mānaṃ
children.translated_text: without wealth, a mortal obtains neither fame nor honor

children.text: prāpnoti martyo 'tra manuṣya-loke ||Panc_5.24||
children.translated_text: here in this human world. // Panc_5.24 //

children.text: tānīndriyāṇy avikalāni tad eva nāma
children.translated_text: Those senses are unimpaired; the name is the same;

children.text: sā buddhir apratihatā vacanaṃ tad eva |
children.translated_text: the intellect is unobstructed; the speech is the same —

children.text: arthoṣmaṇā virahitaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eva
children.translated_text: yet that very man, bereft of the warmth of wealth,

children.text: bāhyaḥ kṣaṇena bhavatīti vicitram etat ||Panc_5.25||
children.translated_text: becomes an outsider in an instant — how strange this is! // Panc_5.25 //

children.text: tad gacchāmaḥ kutracid arthāya iti sammantrya sva-deśaṃ puraṃ ca sva-suhṛt-sahitaṃ gṛhaṃ ca parityajya prasthitāḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: 'So let us go somewhere in pursuit of wealth.' Having thus resolved, they abandoned their own country, city, homes, and friends and set out. Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: satyaṃ parityajati muñcati bandhu-vargaṃ
children.translated_text: He abandons truth, he relinquishes his circle of kinsmen,

children.text: śīghraṃ vihāya jananīm api janma-bhūmim |
children.translated_text: he quickly leaves even his mother and his native land;

children.text: santyajya gacchati videśam abhīṣṭa-lokaṃ
children.translated_text: he departs for a foreign country, [seeking] the desired people —

children.text: cintākulīkṛta-matiḥ puruṣo 'tra loke ||Panc_5.26||
children.translated_text: a man in this world, his mind agitated by anxiety. // Panc_5.26 //

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa gacchanto 'vantīṃ prāptāḥ | tatra siprājale kṛta-snānāḥ mahā-kālaṃ praṇamya yāvan nirgacchanti tāvat bhairavānando nāma yogī saṃmukho babhūva | tatas taṃ brāhmaṇocita-vidhinā sambhāvya tenaiva saha tasya maṭhaṃ jagmuḥ | atha tena pṛṣṭāḥ-kuto bhavantaḥ samāyātāḥ ? kva yāsyatha ? kiṃ prayojanam ?
children.translated_text: Traveling thus by stages, they reached <s>Avantī</s>. There, having bathed in the waters of the <s>Siprā</s> and bowed to <s>Mahākāla</s> (Lord <s>Śiva</s>), just as they were leaving, a <s>yogī</s> named <s>Bhairavānanda</s> appeared before them. Then, having honored him in the manner proper for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, they went with him to his monastery. Then he asked them: 'From where have you come? Where will you go? What is your purpose?'

children.text: tatas tair abhihitam-vayaṃ siddhi-yātrikāḥ | tatra yāsyāmo yatra dhanāptir mṛtyur vā bhaviṣyatīty eṣa niścayaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then they said: 'We are seekers of magical attainment. We shall go wherever either the acquisition of wealth or death shall be — this is our resolve.' And it is said —

children.text: duṣprāpyāṇi bahūni ca labhyante vāñchitāni draviṇāni |
children.translated_text: Many things hard to obtain, [including] desired riches, are obtained

children.text: avasara-tulitābhir alaṃ tanubhiḥ sāhasika-puruṣāṇām ||Panc_5.27||
children.translated_text: by those daring men whose bodies are weighed against opportunity. // Panc_5.27 //

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: patati kadācin nabhasaḥ khāte pātālato 'pi jalam eti |
children.translated_text: Water sometimes falls from the sky into a ditch, and sometimes rises from the netherworld;

children.text: daivam acintyaṃ balavad balavān nanu puruṣakāro 'pi ||Panc_5.28||
children.translated_text: fate is unfathomable and powerful — but human effort too is surely powerful. // Panc_5.28 //

children.text: abhimata-siddhir aśeṣā bhavati hi puruṣasya puruṣakāreṇa |
children.translated_text: The fulfillment of all desires comes to a man through human effort;

children.text: daivam iti yadapi kathayasi puruṣa-guṇaḥ so 'py adṛṣṭākhyaḥ ||Panc_5.29||
children.translated_text: even what you call 'fate' is itself a human quality known as 'the unseen.' // Panc_5.29 //

children.text: bhayam atulaṃ guru-lokāt tṛṇam iva tulayanti sādhu sāhasikāḥ |
children.translated_text: The daring ones weigh tremendous fear from the assembly of elders as if it were a blade of grass;

children.text: prāṇān adbhutam etac cārtiṃ caritaṃ hy udārāṇām ||Panc_5.30||
children.translated_text: [they weigh] even their own lives — wondrous indeed is the conduct of the noble! // Panc_5.30 //

children.text: kleśasyāṅgam adattvā sukham eva sukhāni neha labhyante |
children.translated_text: Without giving the body to toil, pleasures are certainly not obtained here in comfort;

children.text: madhubhin mathanāyas tair āśliṣyati bāhubhir lakṣmīm ||Panc_5.31||
children.translated_text: those who embrace <s>Lakṣmī</s> with their arms must first churn [like the churning of nectar]. // Panc_5.31 //

children.text: tasya kathaṃ na calā syāt patnī viṣṇor nṛsiṃhakasyāpi
māsāṃś caturo nidrāṃ yaḥ sevati jala-gataḥ satatam ||Panc_5.32||
children.translated_text: when he sleeps for four months, always dwelling in the water? // Panc_5.32 //
How would the wife of even <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> not become fickle,

children.text: duradhigamaḥ para-bhāgo yāvat puruṣeṇa sāhasaṃ na kṛtam |
children.translated_text: The portion belonging to another is hard to attain so long as a man has not undertaken daring action;

children.text: jayati tulām adhirūḍho bhāsvān iha jalada-paṭalāni ||Panc_5.33||
children.translated_text: the sun, having ascended the scale, conquers the masses of clouds here. // Panc_5.33 //

children.text: tat kathyatām asmākaṃ kaścit dhanopāyo vivara-praveśa-śākinī-sādhana-śmaśāna-sevana-mahā-māṃsa-vikraya-sādhaka-varjita-prabhṛtīnām ekatama iti | adbhuta-śaktir bhavān śrūyate | vayam apy atisāhasikāḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'So tell us some means of [acquiring] wealth — whether by entering caves, invoking <s>Śākinī</s> spirits, frequenting cremation grounds, selling human flesh, or any other such practice. You are said to have wondrous powers. And we too are exceedingly daring.' And it is said —

children.text: mahānta eva mahatām arthaṃ sādhayituṃ kṣamāḥ |
children.translated_text: Only the great are capable of accomplishing the aims of the great;

children.text: ṛte samudrād anyaḥ ko bibharti baḍavānalam ||Panc_5.34||
children.translated_text: apart from the ocean, who else could bear the <s>Baḍavānala</s> (submarine fire)? [Panc 5.34]

children.text: bhairavānando 'pi teṣāṃ siddhy-arthaṃ bahūpāyaṃ siddha-varti-catuṣṭayaṃ kṛtvārpayat | āha ca-gamyatāṃ himālaya-diśi | tatra samprāptānāṃ yatra vartiḥ patiṣyati, tatra nidhānam asandigdhaṃ prāpyasva | tatra sthānaṃ khanitvā nidhiṃ gṛhītvā vyāghuṭyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhairavānanda</s> too, for their success, prepared and gave them four <s>siddha-vartis</s> (magical wicks). And he said: 'Go in the direction of the <s>Himālayas</s>. Wherever a wick falls from the hand of one who has arrived there, there is a treasure beyond doubt. Dig at that spot, take the treasure, and return.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite teṣāṃ gacchatām ekatamasya hastād varitr nipapāta | athāsau yāvat taṃ praveśaṃ khanati tāvat tāmramayī bhūmiḥ | tatas tenābhihitam-aho, gṛhyatāṃ svecchayā tāmram |
children.translated_text: When this was done, as they were traveling, a wick fell from the hand of one of them. As he dug at that spot, [he found] a copper-yielding earth. Then he said: 'Ah, take copper as you wish!'

children.text: anye procuḥ-bho mūḍha ! kim anena kriyate yat prabhūtam api dāridryaṃ na nāśayati | tad uttiṣṭha agrato gacchāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The others said: 'You fool! What use is this, when even an abundance of it cannot destroy poverty? So get up — let us proceed forward.'

children.text: so 'bravīt-yāntu bhavantaḥ | nāham agra yāsyāmi | evam abhidhāya tāmraṃ yathecchayā gṛhītvā prathamo nivṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'You all may go. I shall not go further.' Having said this, he took as much copper as he wished and was the first to return.

children.text: te trayo 'pi agre prasthitāḥ | atha kiñcin-mātraṃ gatasyāgresarasya vartir nipapāta | so 'pi yāvat khanitum ārabdhas tāvad rūpya-mayī kṣitiḥ | tataḥ praharṣitaḥ prāha, yat-bho bho, gṛhyatāṃ yathecchayā rūpyam | nāgre gantavyam |
children.translated_text: The remaining three proceeded forward. When the foremost had gone a short distance, his wick fell. As he began to dig, he found a silver-yielding earth. Then, delighted, he said: 'Friends! Take silver as you wish. There is no need to go further.'

children.text: tāv ūcatuḥ-bhoḥ pṛṣṭhatas tāmramayī bhūmiḥ | agrato rūpya-mayī | tan nūnam agre suvarṇa-mayī bhaviṣyati | kiṃ cānena prabhūtenāpi dāridrya-nāśo na bhavati | tad āvām agre yāsyāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: The [remaining] two said: 'Friend! Behind was copper earth; ahead is silver earth. So surely ahead there will be gold earth. And even much [silver] does not destroy poverty. So we two shall go further.'

children.text:
evam uktvā dvāv apy agre prasthitau | so 'pi sva-śaktyā rūpyam ādāya nivṛttaḥ | atha tayor api gacchator ekasyāgre vartiḥ papāta | so 'pi prahṛṣṭo yāvat khanati, tāvat suvarṇa-bhūmiṃ dṛṣṭvā dvitīyaṃ prāha-bho, gṛhyatāṃ svecchayā suvarṇam | suvarṇād anyan na kiñcid uttamaṃ bhaviṣyati |
sa prāha-mūḍha ! na kiñcid vetsi | prāk tāmraṃ, tato rūpyaṃ, tataḥ suvarṇam | tan nūnam ataḥ paraṃ ratnāni bhaviṣyanti | yeṣām ekatamenāpi dāridrya-nāśo bhavati | tad uttiṣṭha, agre gacchāvaḥ | kim anena bhāra-bhūtenāpi prabhūtena ?
children.translated_text:
Having said this, both proceeded forward. He too took silver according to his capacity and returned. Then, as those two were traveling, the wick of one fell ahead. He too, delighted, began to dig, and seeing a gold-yielding earth, he said to the second: 'Friend! Take gold as you wish. Nothing better than gold will come.'
He said: 'Fool! You understand nothing. First copper, then silver, then gold. So surely beyond this there will be gems. By even a single one of them, poverty is destroyed. So get up, let us go further. What use is even much [gold] that is a burden?'

children.text: sa āha-gacchatu bhavān | aham atra sthitas tvāṃ pratipālayiṣyāmi | tathānuṣṭhite so 'pi gacchann ekākī, grīṣmārka-pratāpa-santapta-tanuḥ pipāsākulitaḥ siddhi-mārga-cyuta itaś cetaś ca babhrāma |
children.translated_text: He said: 'You may go. I shall stay here and wait for you.' When this was done, that one too, going alone, his body scorched by the blazing summer sun, tormented by thirst, having lost the path to success, wandered here and there.

children.text: atha bhrāmyan, sthalopari puruṣam ekaṃ rudhira-plāvita-gātraṃ bhramac-cakra-mastakam apaśyat | tato drutataraṃ gatvā tam avocat-bhoḥ ! ko bhavān ? kim evaṃ cakreṇa śirasi tiṣṭhasi ? tat kathaya me yadi kutracij jalam asti |
children.translated_text: Then, while wandering, he saw on the open ground a man whose body was drenched in blood, with a revolving wheel on his head. He quickly went to him and said: 'Sir! Who are you? Why do you stand thus with a wheel on your head? Tell me — is there water anywhere?'

children.text: evaṃ tasya pravadatas tac cakraṃ tat-kṣaṇāt tasya śiraso brāhmaṇa-mastake caṭitam |
children.translated_text: Even as he was speaking thus, that wheel instantly transferred from that man's head to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s head.

children.text: sa āha-bhadra, kim etat ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'Good sir, what is this?'

children.text: sa āha-mamāpy evam etac chirasi caṭitam ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'In the same way it attached itself to my head too.'

children.text: sa āha-tat kathaya, kadaitad uttariṣyati ? mahatī me vedanā vartate |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Then tell me — when will this come off? I am in great pain.'

children.text: sa āha-yadā tvam iva kaścid adhṛta-siddha-vartir evam āgatya, tvām ālāpayiṣyati tadā tasya mastakaṃ caṭiṣyati |
children.translated_text: He said: 'When someone like you, holding a <s>siddha-varti</s> that has not worked, comes thus and speaks to you — then it will attach to his head.'

children.text: sa āha-kiyān kālas tavaivaṃ sthitasya ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'How long have you been standing thus?'

children.text: sa āha-sāmprataṃ ko rājā dharaṇī-tale ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'Who is king on the earth at present?'

children.text: sa āha-vīṇā-vādana-paṭuḥ vatsa-rājaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: '<s>Vatsa-rāja</s>, skilled in <s>vīṇā</s>-playing.'

children.text: sa āha-ahaṃ tāvat-kāla-saṅkhyāṃ na jānāmi | paraṃ yadā rāmo rājāsīt tavāhaṃ dāridryopahataḥ siddha-vartim ādāyānena pathā samāyātaḥ | tato mayānyo naro mastaka-śruta-cakro dṛṣṭaḥ, pṛṣṭaś ca | tataś caitaj jātam |
children.translated_text: He said: 'I do not know the count of time. But when <s>Rāma</s> was king, I, afflicted by poverty, took a <s>siddha-varti</s> and came by this path. Then I saw another man with a wheel on his head, and I asked him. And then this happened.'

children.text: sa āha-bhadra ! kathaṃ tadaivaṃ sthitasya bhojana-jala-prāptir āsīt ?
children.translated_text: He said: 'Good sir! How then, standing thus [all this time], did you obtain food and water?'

children.text: sa āha-bhadra ! dhanadena nidhāna-haraṇa-bhayāt siddhānām etac-cakra-patana-rūpaṃ bhayaṃ darśitam | tena kaścid api nāgacchati | yadi kaścid āyāti, sa kṣut-pipāsā-nidrā-rahito jarā-maraṇa-varjitaḥ kevalam evaṃ vedanām anubhavati iti | tad ājñāpaya māṃ sva-gṛhāya | ity uktvā gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Good sir! <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>, lord of wealth), out of fear that treasures would be taken, has devised this wheel-falling punishment for <s>siddhas</s> (treasure-seekers). Therefore no one comes here. And if someone does come, he becomes free from hunger, thirst, sleep, old age, and death — but only experiences this pain.' 'So command me toward my home.' Having said this, he departed.

children.text: tasmiṃś cirayati sa suvarṇa-siddhis tasyānveṣaṇa-paras tat-pada-paṅktyā yāvat kiñcid vanāntaram āgacchati tāvad rudhira-plāvita-śarīras tīkṣṇa-cakreṇa mastake bhramatā sa-vedanaḥ kvaṇann upaviṣṭhas tiṣṭhatīti dadarśa | tataḥ samīpavartinā bhūvā sarvārthaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ-bhadra ! kim etat ?
children.translated_text: As he was delayed, the one who had found gold, intent on searching for him, following his footprints, arrived in a certain forest clearing and saw him — body drenched in blood, a sharp wheel revolving on his head, moaning in pain, seated there. Then, being near him, he asked the full story: 'Good sir! What is this?'

children.text: sa āha-vidhi-niyogaḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'The decree of fate.'

children.text: sa āha-kathaṃ tat ? kathaya kāraṇam etasya |
children.translated_text: He said: 'How so? Tell me the cause of this.'

children.text: so 'pi tena pṛṣṭaḥ | sarvaṃ cakra-vṛttāntam akathayat |
children.translated_text: And he, being asked by him, related the entire account of the wheel.

children.text: tac chrutvāsau taṃ vigarhayann idam āha-bhoḥ ! niṣiddhas tvaṃ mayānekaśo na śṛṇoṣi me vākyam | tat kiṃ kriyate ? vidyāvān api kulīno 'pi vastuto buddhi-rahito 'si | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the other censured him and said: 'Friend! I forbade you many times — you did not listen to my words! So what can be done? Though learned and of good family, in truth you are devoid of intelligence. Or rather, this is well said —'

children.text: varaṃ buddhir na sā vidyā vidyāyā buddhir uttamā |
children.translated_text: Better is intelligence than that learning; intelligence is superior to learning.

children.text: buddhi-hīno vinaśyanti yathā te siṃha-kārakāḥ ||Panc_5.35||
children.translated_text: Those lacking intelligence perish — like those who created a lion. [Panc 5.35]
