children.text: cakradhara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The wheel-bearer said: 'How is that?'

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-
children.translated_text: The gold-finder said:

children.text:
kathā 3
siṃha-kāraka-mūrkha-brāhmaṇa-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 3
The Story of the Foolish <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> Who Created a Lion

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne catvāro brāhmaṇa-putrāh paraṃ mitra-bhāvam upagatā vasanti sma | teṣāṃ trayaḥ śāstra-pāraṅgatāḥ parantu buddhi-rahitāḥ | ekas tu buddhimān kevalaṃ śāstra-parāṅmukhaḥ | atha taiḥ kadācin mitrair mantritam-ko guṇo vidyāyāḥ, yena deśāntaraṃ gatvā, bhūpatīn paritoṣyārthopārjanaṃ na kriyate | tat pūrva-deśaṃ gacchāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain town, four <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sons who had attained the closest friendship lived together. Three of them had mastered all the scriptures but were devoid of practical intelligence. The one, however, was intelligent but entirely averse to book-learning. Once, those friends consulted together: 'What is the use of knowledge if one does not go to foreign lands, please kings, and earn wealth? So let us go to the eastern country.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite kiñcin mārgaṃ gatvā teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhataraḥ prāha-aho ! asmākam ekaś caturtho mūḍhaḥ | kevalaṃ buddhimān | na ca rāja-pratigraho buddhyā labhyate, vidyāṃ vinā | tan nāsmai svopārjitaṃ dāsyāmaḥ | tad gacchatu gṛham |
children.translated_text: When this was done and they had traveled some distance, the eldest of them said: 'Ah! One of us four is a fool — merely intelligent. And a king's patronage is not obtained by intelligence alone, without learning. So we shall not give him a share of what we earn. Let him go home.'

children.text: tato dvitīyenābhihitam-bhoḥ subuddhe ! gaccha tvaṃ sva-gṛhaṃ, yatas te vidyā nāsti |
children.translated_text: Then the second said: 'Ho, <s>Subuddhi</s> (Good-mind)! You go home, since you have no learning.'

children.text: tatas tṛtīyenābhihitam-aho, na yujyate evaṃ kartum | yato vayaṃ bālyāt prabhṛty ekatra krīḍitāḥ | tad āgacchatu mahānubhāvo 'smad-upārjita-vittasya sama-bhāgī bhaviṣyatīti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Then the third said: 'Ah, it is not proper to act thus. For we have played together since childhood. So let this noble one come — he shall be an equal sharer in our earnings.' And it is said —

children.text: kiṃ tayā kriyate lakṣmyā yā vadhūr iva kevalā |
children.translated_text: What use is that wealth which, like a [secluded] bride, is solely [one's own]?

children.text: yā na veśyeva sāmānyā pathikair upabhujyate ||Panc_5.36||
children.translated_text: That which, like a courtesan, is commonly enjoyed by wayfarers [is better]. [Panc 5.36]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also —

children.text: ayaṃ nijaḥ paro veti gaṇanā laghu-cetasām |
children.translated_text: 'This one is mine, that one is another's' — such is the reckoning of the small-minded;

children.text: udāra-caritānāṃ tu vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam ||Panc_5.37||
children.translated_text: for the noble-hearted, the entire world is one family. [Panc 5.37]

children.text: tad āgacchatv eṣo 'pīti |
children.translated_text: 'So let this one come too.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite tair mārgāśritair aṭavyāṃ mṛta-siṃhasyāsthīni dṛṣṭāni | tataś caikenābhihitaṃ-aho ! adya vidyā-pratyayaḥ kriyate | kiñcid etat sattvaṃ mṛtaṃ tiṣṭhati | tad vidyā-prabhāveṇa jīvana-sahitaṃ kurmaḥ | aham asthi-sañcayaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: When this was done, while on the road in a forest, they saw the bones of a dead lion. Then one of them said: 'Ah! Today let the proof of our learning be made! Some creature lies dead here. So let us bring it to life by the power of our learning. I shall assemble the bones.'

children.text: tataś ca tenautsukyād asthi-sañcayaḥ kṛtaḥ | dvitīyena carma-māṃsa-rudhiraṃ saṃyojitam | tṛtīyo 'pi yāvaj jīvanaṃ sañcārayati, tāvat subuddhinā niṣiddhaḥ-bhoḥ tiṣṭhatu bhavān | eṣa siṃho niṣpādyate | yady enaṃ sajīvaṃ kariṣyasi tataḥ sarvān api vyāpādayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: Then, with eagerness, he assembled the bones. The second joined the skin, flesh, and blood. Just as the third was about to infuse life, <s>Subuddhi</s> stopped him: 'Sir! Stop! This is a lion being created. If you bring it to life, it will kill us all.'

children.text: iti tenābhihitaḥ sa āha-dhiṅ mūrkha ! nāhaṃ vidyāyā viphalatāṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: Having been thus told, he said: 'Shame, fool! I shall not render my learning fruitless.'

children.text: tatas tenābhihitaṃ-tarhi pratīkṣasva kṣaṇaṃ yāvad ahaṃ vṛkṣam ārohāmi |
children.translated_text: Then he [<s>Subuddhi</s>] said: 'Then wait a moment while I climb a tree.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite, yāvat sajīvaḥ kṛtas tāvat te trayo 'pi siṃhenotthāya vyāpāditāḥ | sa ca punar vṛkṣād avatīrya gṛhaṃ gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-varaṃ buddhir na sā vidyā iti |
children.translated_text: When this was done, the moment [the lion] was brought to life, those three were killed by the lion as it rose. And he then descended from the tree and went home. Therefore I say: 'Better is intelligence than learning...' and so on.

children.text: ataḥ param uktaṃ sa suvarṇasiddhinā-
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the gold-finder said:

children.text: api śāstreṣu kuśalā lokācāra-vivarjitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even those skilled in scriptures, if devoid of worldly conduct,

children.text: sarve te hāsyatāṃ yānti yathā te mūrkha-paṇḍitāḥ ||Panc_5.38||
children.translated_text: all of them become objects of ridicule — like those foolish scholars. [Panc 5.38]

children.text: cakradhara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The wheel-bearer said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 4
mūrkha-paṇḍita-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 4
The Story of the Foolish Scholars

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne catvāro brāhmaṇāḥ parasparaṃ mitratvam āpannā vasanti sma | bāla-bhāve teṣāṃ matir ajāyata-bhoḥ veśāntaraṃ gatvā vidyāyā upārjanaṃ kriyate |
children.translated_text: In a certain town, four <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had become friends with each other lived together. In their youth, the thought arose in them: 'Let us go to another country and acquire learning.'

children.text: ath:anyasmin divase te brāhmaṇāḥ parasparaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā vidyopārjanārthaṃ kānyakubje gatāḥ | tatra ca vidyā-maṭhe gatvā paṭhanti | evaṃ dvādaśābdāni yāvad ekacittatayā paṭhitvā, vidyā-kuśalās te sarve sañjātāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then one day, those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having made a mutual resolve, went to <s>Kānyakubja</s> (Kanauj) for the acquisition of learning. Going to a school of learning there, they studied. Thus, having studied with single-minded concentration for twelve years, they all became accomplished in learning.

children.text: tatas taiś caturbhir militvoktam-vayaṃ sarva-vidyā-pāraṅgatāḥ | tad-upādhyāyam utkalāpayitvā sva-deśaṃ gacchāmaḥ | tathaivānuṣṭhīyatām ity uktvā brāhmaṇāḥ upādhyāyam ukalāpayitvā anujñāṃ labdhvā pustakāni nītvā pracalitāḥ | yāvat kiñcin-mārgaṃ yānti, tāvad dvau panthānau samāyātau upaviṣṭāḥ sarve |
children.translated_text: Then, the four of them meeting together, said: 'We have mastered all branches of learning. So let us take leave of our teacher and go to our own country.' Having said 'Let it be done so,' the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> took leave of their teacher, obtained permission, took their books, and set out. When they had gone a certain distance on the road, two paths appeared. They sat down, all of them.

children.text: tatraikaḥ provāca-kena mārgeṇa gacchāmaḥ ?
children.translated_text: One of them said: 'By which road shall we go?'

children.text: etasmin samaye tasmin pattane kaścit vaṇik-putro mṛtaḥ | tasya dāhāya mahājano gato 'bhūt | tataś catūrṇāṃ madhyād ekena pustakam avalokitam-mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthaḥ iti | tan mahā-jana-mārgeṇa gacchāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: At that very time, in that town, a certain merchant's son had died. A great crowd of people had gone for his cremation. Then one of the four, consulting his book, [read:] 'The road by which the multitude has gone — that is the path.' 'So let us go by the route of the multitude.'

children.text: atha te paṇḍitā yāvan mahājanam elāpakena saha yānti, tāvad rāsabhaḥ kaścit tatra śmaśāne dṛṣṭaḥ | atha dvitīyena pustakam udghāṭyāvalokitam |
children.translated_text: Then those scholars, going with the multitude along with the funeral bier, saw a certain donkey in that cremation ground. Then the second, opening his book, looked.

children.text: utsave vyasane prāpte durbhikṣe śatru-saṅkaṭe |
children.translated_text: In a festival, in calamity, in famine, in danger from an enemy,

children.text: rāja-dvāre śmaśāne ca yas tiṣṭhati sa bāndhavaḥ ||Panc_5.39||
children.translated_text: at the king's gate, and in the cremation ground — he who stands [by one] is a kinsman. [Panc 5.39]

children.text: tad aho ! ayam asmadīyo bāndhavaḥ | tataḥ kaścit tasya grīvāyāṃ lagati | kaścit pādau prakṣālayati | atha yāvat te paṇḍitāh diśām avalokanaṃ kurvanti tāvat kaścid duṣṭo dṛṣṭaḥ | taiś coktam-etat kim ?
children.translated_text: 'So ah! This is our kinsman.' Then one embraced his neck; another washed his feet. Then, as those scholars were looking around in all directions, they saw a certain camel. And they said: 'What is this?'

children.text: tāvat tṛtīyena pustakam udghāṭyoktam-dharmasya tvaritā gatiḥ | tan nūnam eṣa dharmas tāvat |
children.translated_text: Then the third, opening his book, said: '<s>Dharma</s> moves swiftly.' 'So surely this is <s>Dharma</s> itself.'

children.text: caturthenoktam-iṣṭaṃ dharmeṇa yojayet |
children.translated_text: The fourth said: 'One should yoke the dear with <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: atha taiś ca rāsabha uṣṭra-grīvāyāṃ baddhaḥ | tat tu kenacit tat-svāmino rajakasyāgre kathitam | yāvad rajakas teṣāṃ mūrkha-paṇḍitānāṃ prahāra-karaṇāya samāyātas tāvat te praṇaṣṭāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then they tied the donkey to the camel's neck. But this was reported to the donkey's owner, a washerman. When the washerman came to beat those foolish scholars, they fled.

children.text: tato tāvad agre kiñcit stokaṃ mārgaṃ yānti tāvat kācin nadī samāsāditā | tasya jala-madhye palāśa-patram āyātaṃ dṛṣṭvā paṇḍitenaikenoktam-āgamiṣyati yat patraṃ tas asmāṃs tārayiṣyati | etat kathayitvā tat-patrasyopari patito yāvan nadyā nīyate tāvat taṃ nīyamānam alokyānyena paṇḍitena keśāntaṃ gṛhītvoktam-
children.translated_text: Then, as they go a short way ahead on the path, a certain river was encountered. Seeing a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) leaf floating in its water, one of the scholars said: 'The leaf that was to come — it will carry us across.' Having said this, he fell upon that leaf, and as he was being carried away by the river, another scholar — seeing him being carried off — seized him by the hair and said:

children.text: sarva-nāśe samutpanne ardhaṃ tyajati paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: When total loss has arisen, the wise man gives up half;

children.text: ardhena kurute kāryaṃ sarva-nāśo hi duḥsahaḥ ||Panc_5.40||
children.translated_text: with the [remaining] half he accomplishes his purpose — for total loss is unbearable. ||Panc_5.40||

children.text: atha taiś ca paścāt gatvā kaścit grāma āsāditaḥ | te'pi grāmīṇair nimantritaḥ pṛthag gṛheṣu nītāḥ | tata ekasya sūtrikā ghṛtamaṇḍa-saṃyutā bhojane dattā | tato vicintya paṇḍitenoktaṃ yat-dīrgha-sūtrī vinaśyati iti | evam uktvā bhojanaṃ parityajya gataḥ | tathā dvitīyasya bhaṇḍakā dattāh | tenāyuktaṃ-ativistāra-vistīrṇaṃ tad bhaven na cirāyuṣam | sa bhojanaṃ tyaktvā gataḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, going further, they reached a certain village. They too were invited by the villagers and taken to separate houses. Then one was given vermicelli mixed with ghee for his meal. Then the scholar, having reflected, said: 'That which is long-threaded perishes.' Having said this, he abandoned the food and left. Likewise, the second was given <s>bhaṇḍakā</s> (flat-cakes). He reasoned: 'What is excessively broad and wide-spread does not last long.' He abandoned the food and left.

children.text: atha tṛtīyasya vāṭikā bhojane dattā | tatrāpi tena paṇḍitenoktam-chidreṣv anarthā bahulībhavanti | evaṃ te trayo 'pi paṇḍitāḥ kṣutkṣāma-kaṇṭhāloke hāsyamānās tataḥ sthānāt sva-deśaṃ gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the third was given a <s>vāṭikā</s> (round cake with holes) for his meal. That scholar too said: 'In holes, misfortunes multiply.' Thus all three scholars, with throats parched from hunger and being laughed at, departed from that place to their own country.

children.text: atha suvarṇa-siddhir āha-yat tvaṃ loka-vyavahāram ajānan mayā vāryamāṇo 'pi na sthitaḥ tata īdṛśīm avasthātum upagataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-api śāstreṣu kuśalāḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'Because you, not knowing the ways of the world and ignoring my warning, did not stay [home], you have come to such a state. Therefore I say: "Even those skilled in the <s>śāstras</s>..." (verse above).'

children.text: tac chrutvā cakradhara āha-aho akāraṇam etat | yato hi-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'Ah, this is without cause. Because:

children.text: subuddhayo vinaśyanti duṣṭa-daivena nāśitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those of good intellect are destroyed, ruined by evil fate;

children.text: svalpa-dhīr api tasmiṃs tu kule nandati santatam ||Panc_5.41||
children.translated_text: but even one of small intelligence in that [fortunate] family always prospers. ||Panc_5.41||

children.text: uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati daiva-rakṣitaṃ surakṣitaṃ daiva-hataṃ vinaśyati |
children.translated_text: What is unprotected stands protected by fate; what is well-protected, struck by fate, perishes;

children.text: jīvaty anātho 'pi vane visarjitaḥ kṛta-prayatno 'pi gṛhe na jīvati ||Panc_5.42||
children.translated_text: even an orphan abandoned in the forest lives; even one for whom great effort is made does not survive at home. ||Panc_5.42||

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: śatabuddhiḥ śirastho 'yaṃ lambate ca sahasra-dhīḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śatabuddhi</s> (Hundred-Wit) here hangs upon [the fisherman's] head, and <s>Sahasradhī</s> (Thousand-Wit) hangs [below];

children.text: eka-buddhir ahaṃ bhadre krīḍāmi vimale jale ||Panc_5.43||
children.translated_text: I, <s>Ekabuddhi</s> (Single-Wit), dear one, sport in the clear water.' ||Panc_5.43||

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
sa āha-
kathā 5
matsya-maṇḍūka-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 5
The story of the fish and the frog

children.text: kasmiṃścij jalāśaye śatabuddhiḥ sahasrabuddhiś ca dvau matsyau nivasataḥ sma | atha tayor ekabuddhir nāma maṇḍūko mitratāṃ gataḥ | evaṃ te trayo 'pi jala-tīre velāyāṃ subhāṣita-goṣṭhī-sukham anubhūya, bhūyo 'pi salilaṃ praviśanti |
children.translated_text: In a certain lake there lived two fish named <s>Śatabuddhi</s> (Hundred-Wit) and <s>Sahasrabuddhi</s> (Thousand-Wit). And a frog named <s>Ekabuddhi</s> (Single-Wit) had become their friend. Thus the three, on the lake-shore at evening-time, having enjoyed the pleasure of conversation full of wise sayings, would enter the water again.

children.text: atha kadācit teṣāṃ goṣṭhī-gatānāṃ tasmin jalāśaye samāyātāḥ | tataḥ salilāśayaṃ dṛṣṭvā mithaḥ procuḥ-aho bahu-matsyo 'yaṃ hrado dṛśyate, svalpa-salilaś ca| tat prabhāte'trāgamiṣyāmaḥ | evam uktvā sva-gṛhaṃ gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then once, while they were gathered in conversation, [fishermen] arrived at that lake. Then, seeing the water-body, they said to each other: 'Ah, this lake appears to have many fish and little water. So we shall come here tomorrow morning.' Having said this, they went to their own homes.

children.text: matsyāś ca viṣaṇṇa-vadanā mitho mantraṃ cakruḥ | tato maṇḍūka āha-bhoḥ śatabuddhe ! śrutaṃ dhīvaroktaṃ bhavatā ? tat kim atra yujyate kartum ? palāyanam avaṣṭambho vā ? yat kartuṃ yuktaṃ bhavati tad ādiśyatām adya |
children.translated_text: And the fish, with dejected faces, took counsel with one another. Then the frog said: 'O <s>Śatabuddhi</s>! Have you heard what the fishermen said? So what is proper to be done here — flight or firm resistance? Let what is proper to do be directed, today.'

children.text: tac chrutvā sahasra-buddhiḥ prahasya āha-bhoḥ mitra ! mā bhaiṣīḥ | tayoḥ vacana-śravaṇa-mātrād eva bhayaṃ na kāryam | na bhetavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Sahasrabuddhi</s> said with a laugh: 'O friend! Do not be afraid. Fear should not be entertained merely from hearing their words. One need not be afraid.' And it is said:

children.text: sarpāṇāṃ ca khalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ duṣṭa-cetasām |
children.translated_text: The designs of serpents and of wicked people and of all those of evil mind

children.text: abhiprāyā na sidhyanti tenedaṃ vartate jagat ||Panc_5.44||
children.translated_text: do not succeed — that is why this world continues. ||Panc_5.44||

children.text: tāvat teṣām āgamanam api na sampatsyate | bhaviṣyati tarhi tvāṃ buddhi-prabhāveṇātma-sahitaṃ rakṣayiṣyāmi | yato 'nekāṃsalila-caryām ahaṃ jānāmi |
children.translated_text: 'Their coming may not even take place. But if it does, then I shall protect you along with myself by the power of my intellect. For I know many water-maneuvers.'

children.text: tad ākarṇya śatabuddhir āha-bhoḥ yuktam uktaṃ bhavatā | sahasrabuddhir eva bhavān | athavā sādhv idam ucyate |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Śatabuddhi</s> said: 'Friend! What you have said is proper. <s>Sahasrabuddhi</s> himself is you.' Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: buddher buddhimatāṃ loke nāsty agamyaṃ hi kiñcana |
children.translated_text: For the intelligent, there is nothing in the world that is inaccessible to intellect;

children.text: buddhyā yato hatā nandāś cāṇakyenāsi-pāṇayaḥ ||Panc_5.45||
children.translated_text: for by intellect, the <s>Nandas</s>, sword-wielding [warriors], were destroyed by <s>Cāṇakya</s>. ||Panc_5.45||

children.text: tathā-
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: na yatrāsti gatir vāyo raśmīnāṃ ca vivasvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Where neither the wind nor the rays of the sun can go,

children.text: tatrāpi praviśaty āśu buddhir buddhimatāṃ sadā ||Panc_5.46||
children.translated_text: even there the intelligence of the intelligent always enters quickly. ||Panc_5.46||

children.text: tato vacana-śravaṇa-mātrād api pitṛ-paryāyāgataṃ janma-sthānaṃ tyaktuṃ na śakyate | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, merely from hearing their words, one cannot abandon a birthplace inherited through generations of forefathers.' And it is said:

children.text: na yat svarge'pi saukhyaṃ syād divya-sparśena śobhane |
children.translated_text: Not even in heaven would there be such happiness — touched by divine [blessings] — O beautiful one,

children.text: kusthāne'pi bhavet puṃsāṃ janmano yatra sambhavaḥ ||Panc_5.47||
children.translated_text: as men may have even in a poor place, if it is where their birth occurred. ||Panc_5.47||

children.text: tan na kadācid api gantavyam | ahaṃ tvāṃ buddhi-prabhāveṇa rakṣayiṣyāmi | maṇḍūka āha-bhadrau ! mama tāvad ekaiva buddhiḥ palāyana-parā | tad aham anya-jalāśayam adyaiva sabhāryo yāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: 'So one should never go [away]. I shall protect you by the power of my intellect.' The frog said: 'Dear friends! I have only one wit — [and that is] devoted to flight. So today itself I shall go with my wife to another lake.'

children.text: evam uktvā sa maṇḍūko rātrāv evānya-jalāśayaṃ gataḥ | dhīvarair api prabhāte āgatya, jaghanya-madhyamottama-jalacarāḥ matsya-kūrma-maṇḍūka-karkaṭādayo gṛhītāḥ | tāv api śatabuddhi-sahasrabuddhī sabhāryau palāyamānau ciram ātmānaṃ gati-viśeṣa-vijñānaiḥ kuṭila-cāreṇa rakṣantau jāle nipatitau, vyāpāditau ca |
children.translated_text: Having said this, that frog went to another lake that very night. And the fishermen, having come at dawn, caught all the aquatic creatures — the best, middling, and lowest — fish, turtles, frogs, crabs, and others. Those two as well — <s>Śatabuddhi</s> and <s>Sahasrabuddhi</s> — along with their wives, fleeing and protecting themselves for a long time through knowledge of special maneuvers and crooked movements, fell into the net and were killed.

children.text: athāparāhna-samaye prahṛṣṭās te dhīvarāḥ sva-gṛhaṃ prati prasthitāḥ | gurutvāc caikena śatabuddhiḥ skandhe kṛtaḥ sahasrabuddhiḥ pralambamāno nīyate | tataś ca vāpīkaṇṭhopagatena maṇḍūkena tau tathā nīyamānau dṛṣṭvā abhihitā svapatnī-priye ! paśya paśya-
children.translated_text: Then, in the afternoon, the delighted fishermen set out toward their own home. Because of his weight, one [fisherman] placed <s>Śatabuddhi</s> on his shoulder; <s>Sahasrabuddhi</s> was being carried dangling [from a pole]. Then the frog, who had come to the edge of the tank, seeing those two being carried thus, said to his wife: 'Dear one! Look, look!'

children.text: śatabuddhiḥ śiraḥstho 'yaṃ lambate ca sahasradhīḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śatabuddhi</s> here rests upon [the fisherman's] head, and <s>Sahasradhī</s> (Thousand-Wit) hangs [below];

children.text: ekabuddhir ahaṃ bhadre krīḍāmi vimale jale ||Panc_5.48||
children.translated_text: I, <s>Ekabuddhi</s> (Single-Wit), dear one, sport in the clear water.' ||Panc_5.48||

children.text: ataś ca varaṃ buddhir na sā vidyā yad bhavatoktaṃ tatreyaṃ me matir yat na ekāntena buddhir api pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, better is [practical] wisdom than that book-learning you spoke of. Here is my opinion: that intellect alone is not absolutely authoritative.'

children.text: suvarṇasiddhiḥ prāha-yadyapy etad asti, tathāpi mitra-vacanaṃ na laṅghanīyam | paraṃ kiṃ kriyate ? nivārito 'pi mayā na sthito 'si, atilaulyāt vidyāhaṅkārāc ca | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'Even though this is so, still a friend's words should not be transgressed. But what can be done? Even when restrained by me, you did not stay, out of excessive greed and pride of learning.' Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: sādhu mātula gītena mayā prokto 'pi na sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Well done, uncle, with the singing! — though told by me, he did not stay;

children.text: apūrvo 'yaṃ maṇir baddhaḥ samprāptaṃ gīta-lakṣaṇam ||Panc_5.49||
children.translated_text: a novel jewel has been tied on [him] — [he has] attained the mark of singing.' ||Panc_5.49||

children.text: cakradhara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 6
rāsabha-śṛgāla-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 6
The story of the donkey and the jackal

children.text: kasmiṃścd adhiṣṭhāne uddhato nāma gardabhaḥ prativasati sma | sa sadaiva rajaka-gṛhe bhārodvahanaṃ kṛtvā rātrau svecchayā paryaṭati | tataḥ pratyūṣe bandhana-bhayāt svayam eva rajaka-gṛham āyāti | rajako 'pi tatas taṃ bandhanena niyunakti |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a donkey named <s>Uddhata</s> (Arrogant). He would always carry burdens at the washerman's house, and at night roam about at will. Then at dawn, from fear of being tied up, he would come by himself to the washerman's house. And the washerman would then bind him for work.

children.text: atha tasya rātrau kṣetrāṇi paryaṭataḥ kadācic chṛgālena saha maitrī sañjātā sa ca pīvaratvād vṛtti-bhaṅgaṃ kṛtvā karkaṭikā-kṣetre śṛgāla-sahitaḥ praviśati | evaṃ tau yadṛcchayā cirbhaṭikā-bhakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā, pratyahaṃ pratyūṣe sva-sthānaṃ vrajataḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, as he roamed the fields at night, a friendship once arose with a jackal. And he, being fat and having broken through the enclosure, would enter a gourd-field together with the jackal. Thus the two, eating gourds at will, would return to their own places each day at dawn.

children.text: atha kadācit tena madoddhatena rāsabhena kṣetra-madhya-sthitena śṛgāo 'bhihitaḥ-bhoḥ bhaginī-sūta ! paśya paśya | atīva nirmalā rajanī | tad ahaṃ gītaṃ kariṣyāmi | tat kathaya katamena rāgeṇa karomi |
children.translated_text: Then once, that donkey — arrogant with excitement — standing in the middle of the field, said to the jackal: 'Ho, nephew! Look, look! The night is exceedingly clear. So I shall sing! Tell me, in which <s>rāga</s> (musical mode) shall I do it?'

children.text: sa āha-māma ! kim anena vṛthānartha-pracālanena ? yataś caurakarma-pravṛttāv āvām | nibhṛtaiś ca caura-jārair atra sthātavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Uncle! What is the use of this vain invitation to ruin? For we are engaged in the business of thieves. And thieves and paramours should remain here in silence.' And it is said:

children.text: kāṃsī vivarjayec cauryaṃ nidrāluś cet sa puṃścalīm |
children.translated_text: He who is a thief should avoid bell-metal [vessels]; a sleepy one [should avoid] an adulteress;

children.text: jihvā-laulyaṃ ca rujākrānto jīvitaṃ yo 'tra vāñchati ||Panc_5.50||
children.translated_text: one afflicted by illness [should avoid] indulgence of the tongue — whoever here desires to live. ||Panc_5.50||

children.text: aparaṃ tvadīyaṃ gītaṃ na madhura-svaraṃ, śaṅkha-śabdānukāraṃ dūrād api śrūyate | tad atra kṣetre rakṣā-puruṣāḥ susuptāḥ santi | te utthāya vadhaṃ bandhanaṃ vā kariṣyanti | tad bhakṣaya tāvad amṛtamayīś carbhaṭīḥ | mā tvam atra gīta-vyāpāra-paro bhava |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, your singing is not sweet-voiced — it is like the sound of a conch, audible from afar. And here in this field, the watchmen are fast asleep. They will rise and inflict beating or binding upon you. So eat your fill of these nectar-like gourds! Do not be absorbed in the business of singing.'

children.text: tac chrutvā rābhasa āha-bhoḥ vanāśrayatvāt tvaṃ gīta-rasaṃ na vetsi, tenaitad bravīṣi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the donkey said: 'Ha! Because you are a forest-dweller, you do not know the essence of song — that is why you speak thus.' And it is said:

children.text: śaraj-jyotsnāhate dūraṃ tamasi priya-sannidhau |
children.translated_text: In [a night] cleansed by autumn moonlight far into the darkness, in the presence of the beloved —

children.text: dhanyānāṃ viśati śrotre gīta-jhaṅkāra-jā sudhā ||Panc_5.51||
children.translated_text: into the ears of the fortunate enters the nectar born from the humming of song. ||Panc_5.51||

children.text: śṛgāla āha-māma, asty etat | paraṃ na vetsi tvaṃ gītam | kevalam unnadasi | tat kiṃ tena svārtha-bhraṃśakena ?
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Uncle, that may be so. But you do not know singing. You merely bray. So what use is that which causes the loss of one's own interest?'

children.text: rāsabha āha-dhig dhiṅ mūrkha ! kim ahaṃ na jānāsi gītam ? tad yathā tasya bhedān śṛṇu-
children.translated_text: The donkey said: 'Shame, shame, fool! Do I not know song? Then hear its divisions as follows:'

children.text: sapta svarās trayo grāmā mūrcchatāś caikatriṃśatiḥ |
children.translated_text: Seven notes, three scales, thirty-one <s>mūrcchanās</s> (melodic progressions),

children.text: tānās tv ekonapaūcāśat tisro mātrā layās trayaḥ ||Panc_5.52||
children.translated_text: forty-nine <s>tānas</s> (melodies), three <s>mātrās</s> (measures), three <s>layas</s> (tempos), ||Panc_5.52||

children.text: sthāna-trayaṃ yatīnāṃ ca ṣaḍ-asyāni rasā nava |
children.translated_text: three registers, six <s>asyānis</s> (ornaments), nine <s>rasas</s> (sentiments),

children.text: rāgā ṣaṭ-triṃśatir bhāvāś catvāriṃśat tataḥ smṛtāḥ ||Panc_5.53||
children.translated_text: thirty-six <s>rāgas</s>, and then forty <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) are mentioned. ||Panc_5.53||

children.text: pañcāśīty-adhikaṃ hy etad gītāṅgānāṃ śataṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: One hundred and eighty-five are mentioned as the elements of song —

children.text: svayam eva purā proktaṃ bharatena śruteḥ param ||Panc_5.54||
children.translated_text: proclaimed of old by <s>Bharata</s> himself, beyond [mere] hearing. ||Panc_5.54||

children.text: nānyad gītāt priyaṃ loke devānām api dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: Nothing dearer than song is seen in the world, even among the gods;

children.text: śuṣka-snāyu-svarāhlādāt try-akṣaṃ jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ ||Panc_5.55||
children.translated_text: from the delight of [song's] notes on dried sinews, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> grasped the Three-Eyed One [<s>Śiva</s>]. ||Panc_5.55||

children.text: tat kathaṃ bhaginī-suta mām anabhijñaṃ vadan nivārayati ?
children.translated_text: 'So how, nephew, do you restrain me while saying I am ignorant?'

children.text: śṛgāla āha-māma ! yady evaṃ yāvad vṛtter dvāra-sthitaḥ kṣetrapālam avalokayāmi, tvaṃ punaḥ svecchayā gītaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: The jackal said: 'Uncle! If so, then let me station myself at the entrance to the field and watch for the field-guard while you sing at your pleasure.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite rāsabha-raṭanam ākarṇya kṣetrapaḥ krodhāt dantān dharṣayan pradhāvitaḥ | yāvad rāsabho dṛṣṭas tāval laguḍa-prahārais tathā hato, yathā pratāḍito bhū-pṛṣṭhe patitaḥ | tataś ca sac-chidram ulūkhalaṃ tasya gale baddhvā kṣetrapālaḥ prasuptaḥ | rāsabho 'pi svajāti-svabhāvād gata-vedanaḥ kṣaṇenābhyutthitaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
sārameyasya cāśvasya rāsabhasya viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: For a dog, a horse, and especially a donkey,

children.text: muhūrtāt paratau na syāt prahāra-janitā vyathā ||Panc_5.56||
children.translated_text: the pain caused by a blow does not last beyond a moment. ||Panc_5.56||

When this was arranged, the field-guard, hearing the donkey's braying, grinding his teeth with anger, rushed out. As soon as the donkey was seen, he beat him so with cudgel-blows that [the donkey], struck down, fell to the ground. Then he tied a mortar with a hole to his neck and fell asleep. The donkey too, by the nature of his species, having recovered from the pain in an instant, rose up. And it is said:

children.text: tata tam evolūkhalam ādāya vṛttiṃ cūrṇayitvā palāyitum ārabdhaḥ | atrāntare śṛgālo 'pi dūrād eva dṛṣṭvā sa-smitam āha-
children.translated_text: Then, taking that very mortar and crushing the field-fence, he began to flee. In the meanwhile, the jackal too, seeing [him] from afar, said with a smile:

children.text: sādhu mātula gītena mayā prokto 'pi na sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Well done, uncle, with the singing! — though told by me, he did not stay;

children.text: apūrvo 'pi maṇir baddhaḥ sāmprataṃ gīta-lakṣaṇam ||Panc_5.57||
children.translated_text: a novel jewel has been tied on — now [he has] attained the mark of singing.' ||Panc_5.57||

children.text: tad bhavān api mayā vāryamāṇo 'pi na sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'So you too — though restrained by me — did not stay.'

children.text: tac chrutvā cakradhara āha-bho mitra ! satyam etat | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'O friend! This is true.' Or rather, well is this said:

children.text: yasya nāsti svayaṃ prajñā mitroktaṃ na karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who does not have wisdom of his own and does not follow a friend's advice —

children.text: sa eva nidhanaṃ yāti yathā manthara-kolikaḥ ||Panc_5.58||
children.translated_text: he goes to destruction, like <s>Manthara</s> the weaver. ||Panc_5.58||

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 7
manthara-kaulika-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 7
The story of <s>Manthara</s> the weaver

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne mantharako nāma kaulikaḥ prativasati sma | tasya kadācit paṭa-karmāṇi kurvataḥ sarva-paṭa-karma-kāṣṭhāni bhagnāni | tataḥ sa kuṭhāram ādāya vane kāṣṭhārthaṃ gataḥ | sa ca samudra-taṭe yāvad bhraman prayātaḥ tāvat tatra śiṃśapā-pādapas tena dṛṣṭaḥ | tataś cintitavān-mahān ayaṃ vṛkṣo dṛśyate | tad anenaiva kartitena prabhūtāni paṭa-karmopakaraṇāni bhaviṣyanti | ity avadhārya tasyopari kuṭhāram utkṣiptavān |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a weaver named <s>Mantharaka</s>. Once, while he was working on cloth, all his loom-frame timbers broke. Then, taking an axe, he went to the forest in search of wood. While he was roaming along the seashore, he saw a <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) tree. He thought: 'This appears to be a great tree. If I cut it down, it will yield abundant materials for my loom.' Having resolved thus, he raised his axe upon it.

children.text: atha tatra vṛkṣe kaścit vyantaraḥ samāśritya āsīt | atha tenābhihitam-bhoḥ ! mad-āśrayo 'yaṃ pādapaḥ sarvathā rakṣaṇīyaḥ | yato 'ham atra mahā-saukhyena tiṣṭhāmi | samudra-kallola-sparśanāc chīta-vāyunāpyāyitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, a certain <s>Vyantara</s> (nature-spirit) had taken refuge in that tree. He said: 'Ho! This tree is my dwelling — it must be protected at all costs. For I live here in great comfort, refreshed by the cool breeze from the touch of the ocean waves.'

children.text: kaulika āha-bhoḥ ! kim ahaṃ karomi ? dāru-sāmagrīṃ vinā me kuṭumbaṃ bubhukṣayā pīḍyate | tasmād anyatra śīghraṃ gamyatām | aham enaṃ kartayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'Ho! What can I do? Without timber for my loom, my family is tormented by hunger. So go elsewhere quickly — I shall cut it down.'

children.text: vyantara āha-bhoḥ ! tuṣṭas tavāham | tat prārthyatām abhīṣṭaṃ kiñcit | rakṣaimaṃ pādapam iti |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vyantara</s> said: 'Ho! I am pleased with you. So ask for any desired boon — [only] spare this tree.'

children.text: kaulika āha-yady eva tad ahaṃ sva-gṛhaṃ gatvā sva-mitraṃ sva-bhāryāṃ ca pṛṣṭvā āgamiṣyāmi | tatas tvayā deyam |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'If so, then let me go home, consult my friend and my wife, and I shall return. Then you shall give [the boon].'

children.text: atha tatheti vyantareṇa pratijñāte sa kaulikaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sva-gṛhaṃ prati nivṛtto yāvad agre gacchati, tāvad grāma-praveśe nija-suhṛdaṃ nāpitam apaśyat | tataḥ tasya vyantara-vākyaṃ nivedayāmāsa, yat-aho mitra ! mama kaścit vyantaraḥ siddhaḥ | tat kathaya, kiṃ prārthaye ? ahaṃ tvāṃ praṣṭum āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: When the <s>Vyantara</s> agreed with 'so be it,' the weaver, delighted, turned back toward his home. As he was going forward, at the entrance of the village he saw his own friend, a barber. Then he informed him of the <s>Vyantara</s>'s words: 'Ah, friend! A certain <s>Vyantara</s> has become favorable to me. He will grant any wish. So tell me — what should I ask for? I have come to consult you.'

children.text: nāpita āha-bhadra ! yady evaṃ tad rājyaṃ prārthayasva, yena tvaṃ rājā bhavasi ahaṃ tvan-mantrī | dvāv apīha sukham anubhūya para-loka-sukham anubhavāvaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: The barber said: 'Friend! If so, then ask for a kingdom, so that you become king and I your minister. We two shall enjoy happiness here and then experience the happiness of the next world. And it is said:'

children.text: rājā dāna-paro nityam iha kīrtim avāpya ca |
children.translated_text: A king who is ever devoted to giving, having obtained fame in this world,

children.text: tat prabhāvāt punaḥ svargaṃ spardhate tridaśaiḥ saha ||Panc_5.59||
children.translated_text: by the power of that [fame] again [attains] heaven, rivaling the gods. // Panc_5.59 //

children.text: kaulika āha-asty etat tathāpi gṛhiṇīṃ pṛcchāmi |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'That is true; still, let me consult the wife.'

children.text: sa āha-bhadra ! śāstra-viruddham etat yat striyā saha mantraḥ | yatas tāḥ svalpa-matayo bhavanti | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: He said: 'Friend! It is contrary to the <s>śāstras</s> to deliberate with a woman. For they are of limited intelligence. And it is said:'

children.text: bhojanācchādane dadyād ṛtu-kāle ca saṅgamam |
children.translated_text: One should give women food, clothing, and union at the proper season,

children.text: bhūṣaṇādyaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ na tābhir mantrayet sudhīḥ ||Panc_5.60||
children.translated_text: and ornaments and the like — but a wise man should not deliberate with them. // Panc_5.60 //

children.text: yatra strī yatra kitavo bālo yatra praśāsitā |
children.translated_text: Where there is a woman, where there is a gambler, where a child is the ruler —

children.text: tad gṛhaṃ kṣayam āyāti bhārgavo hīdam abravīt ||Panc_5.61||
children.translated_text: that household goes to ruin; so has <s>Bhārgava</s> (Śukra) declared. // Panc_5.61 //

children.text: tāvat syāt suprasannāsyas tāvad guru-jane rataḥ |
children.translated_text: A man's face remains serene, he remains devoted to his elders,

children.text: puruṣo yoṣitāṃ yāvan na śṛṇoti vaco rahaḥ ||Panc_5.62||
children.translated_text: only so long as he does not listen to a woman's words in private. // Panc_5.62 //

children.text: etāḥ svārtha-parā nāryaḥ kevalaṃ sva-sukhe ratāḥ |
children.translated_text: These women are self-serving, devoted solely to their own pleasure;

children.text: na tāsāṃ vallabhaḥ ko 'pi suto 'pi sva-sukhaṃ vinā ||Panc_5.63||
children.translated_text: no beloved, not even a son, [matters to them] apart from their own comfort. // Panc_5.63 //

children.text: kaulika āha-tathāpi praṣṭavyā sā mayā | yataḥ pativratā sā | aparaṃ tām apṛṣṭvāhaṃ na kiñcit karomi |
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'Even so, I must consult her. For she is a devoted wife. Moreover, without consulting her, I do nothing.'

children.text: evaṃ tam abhidhāya satvaraṃ gatvā tām uvāca-priye ! adyāsmākaṃ kaścid vyantaraḥ siddhaḥ | sa vāñchitaṃ prayacchati | tad ahaṃ tvāṃ praṣṭum āgataḥ | tat kathaya kiṃ prārthaye ? eṣa tāvan mama mitraṃ nāpito vatady evaṃ yat-rājyaṃ prārthayasva |
children.translated_text: Having said this to him, he went quickly and said to her: 'Darling! Today a certain <s>Vyantara</s> has become favorable to us. He will grant our wish. So I have come to consult you. Tell me — what should I ask for? My friend the barber advises: "Ask for a kingdom."'

children.text: sāha-āryaputra ! kā matir nāpitānām ? tan na kāryaṃ tad vacaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: She said: 'Noble husband! What wisdom do barbers have? So his advice should not be followed. And it is said:'

children.text: cāraṇair vandibhir nīcair nāpitair bālakair api |
children.translated_text: With bards, panegyrists, low persons, barbers, children,

children.text: na mantraṃ maitmān kuryāt sārdhaṃ bhikṣubhir eva ca ||Panc_5.64||
children.translated_text: and mendicants — a wise man should never deliberate. // Panc_5.64 //

children.text: aparaṃ mahatī kleśa-paramparaiṣā rājya-sthitiḥ sandhi-vigraha-yānāsana-saṃśraya-dvaidhībhāvādibhiḥ kadācit puruṣasya sukhaṃ na prayacchatīti | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, the maintenance of a kingdom is an unending chain of troubles — alliance, war, marching, staying firm, taking refuge, double-dealing, and the like — it never gives a man happiness. For:'

children.text: yadaiva rājye kriyate'bhiṣekas tadaiva yāti vyasaneṣu buddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The very moment one is consecrated to kingship, that very moment the mind turns to calamities;

children.text: ghaṭā nṛpāṇām abhiṣeka-kāle sahāmbhasaivāpadam udgiranti ||Panc_5.65||
children.translated_text: the pitchers of kings at the time of consecration spew forth disaster along with the water. // Panc_5.65 //

children.text: tathā ca-
rāmasya vrajanaṃ vane nivasanaṃ pāṇḍoḥ sutānāṃ vane
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>'s exile to the forest, the dwelling of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s sons in the forest,

children.text: vṛṣṇīnāṃ nidhanaṃ nalasya nṛpate rājyāt paribhraṃśanam |
children.translated_text: the destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, King <s>Nala</s>'s fall from his kingdom,

children.text: saudāsaṃ tad-avastham arjuna-vadhaṃ sañcintya laṅkeśvaraṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Saudāsa</s> and his [wretched] condition, the slaying of <s>Arjuna</s> [Kārtavīrya], seeing the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>

children.text: dṛṣṭvā rājya-kṛte viḍambana-gataṃ tasmān na tad vāñchayet ||Panc_5.66||
children.translated_text: brought to disgrace for the sake of kingship — therefore one should not desire it. // Panc_5.66 //
And also:

children.text: yad-arthaṃ bhrātaraḥ putrā api vāñchanti ye nijāḥ |
children.translated_text: That for whose sake brothers and even one's own sons desire

children.text: vadhaḥ rājya-kṛtāṃ rājñāṃ tad rājyaṃ dūratas tyajet ||Panc_5.67||
children.translated_text: the death of kings — that kingdom one should abandon from afar. // Panc_5.67 //

children.text: kaulika āha-satyam uktaṃ bhavatyā | tat kathaya kiṃ prārthaye ?
children.translated_text: The weaver said: 'You have spoken truly. Then tell me — what should I ask for?'

children.text: sāha-tvaṃ tāvad ekaṃ paṭaṃ nityam eva niṣpādayasi | tena sarvā vyaya-śuddhiḥ sampadyate | idānīṃ tvam ātmano 'nyad bāhu-yugalaṃ dvitīyaṃ śiraś ca yācasva, yena paṭa-dvayaṃ sampādayasi purataḥ pṛṣṭhataś ca | ekasya mūlyena gṛḥe yathā-pūrvaṃ vyayaṃ sampādayiṣyasi, dvitīyasya mūlyena viśeṣa-kṛtyāni kariṣyasi | evaṃ saukhyena svajāti-madhye ślāghyamānasya kālo yāsyati, loka-dvayasyopārjanā ca bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: She said: 'You currently produce just one piece of cloth daily. From that, all the household expenses are met. Now ask for another pair of arms and a second head, so that you can produce two pieces of cloth — from the front and from the back. With the price of one, you will manage the household expenses as before; with the price of the second, you will accomplish special purposes. Thus, enjoying happiness and being praised among your own people, time will pass, and merit for both worlds will also be earned.'

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇya prahṛṣṭaḥ prāha-sādhu pativrate ! sādhu ! yuktam uktaṃ bhavatyā | tad evaṃ kariṣyāmi | eṣa me niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: He too, hearing that, said joyfully: 'Well done, devoted wife! Well done! What you have said is fitting. I shall do exactly that. This is my resolve.'

children.text: tato 'sau gatvā vyantaraṃ prārthayāṃcakre-bho, yadi mamepsitaṃ prayacchasi tat dehi me dvitīyaṃ bāhu-yugalaṃ śiraś ca |
children.translated_text: Then he went and made his request to the <s>Vyantara</s>: 'Ho, if you will grant my desire, then give me a second pair of arms and a [second] head.'

children.text: evam abhihite tat-kṣaṇād eva sa dviśirāś caturbāhuś ca sañjātaḥ | tato hṛṣṭa-manā yāvad gṛham āgacchati tāval-lokaiḥ rākṣaso 'yam iti mānyamānair laguḍa-pāṣāṇa-prahārais tāḍito mṛtaś ca |
children.translated_text: The moment he said this, he became two-headed and four-armed. Then, as he was coming home with a delighted heart, the townspeople, thinking 'This is a <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon)!', struck him with blows from staffs and stones, and he died.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-yasya nāsti svayaṃ prajñā iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'He who has no wisdom of his own...' [and so on].

children.text: cakradhara āha-bhoḥ ! satyam etat | sarvo 'pi jano 'śraddeyām āśāpiśācikāṃ prāpya hāsya-padavīṃ yāti | athavā sādhv idam ucyate kenāpi-
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'Ho! This is true. Everyone who obtains the possession-demon of incredible hope arrives at a laughing-stock. Or rather, well is this said by someone:'

children.text: anāgatavatīṃ cintām asambhāvyāṃ karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who worries about the future that has not yet come, about what is impossible —

children.text: sa eva pāṇḍuraḥ śete soma-śarma-pitā yathā ||Panc_5.68||
children.translated_text: he himself lies pale [with grief], like the father of <s>Somaśarman</s>. // Panc_5.68 //

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 8
soma-śarma-pitṛ-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said:
Story 8
The story of the father of <s>Somaśarman</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścin nagare kaścit svabhāva-kṛpaṇo nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati sma | tasya bhikṣārjitaiḥ saktubhir bhukta-śeṣaiḥ kalaśaḥ sampūritaḥ | taṃ ca ghaṭaṃ nāgadante'valambya tasyādhastāt khaṭvāṃ nidhāya satatam eka-dṛṣṭyā tam avalokayati |
children.translated_text: In a certain city there lived a Brahmin who was a miser by nature. A pot had been filled with the leftover barley-flour obtained from his begging. He hung that pot on a wall-peg and, placing his cot beneath it, constantly gazed at it with fixed eyes.

children.text: atha kadācid rātrau suptaś cintayāmāsa-yat paripūrṇo 'yaṃ ghaṭas tāvat saktubhir vartate | tad yadi durbhikṣaṃ bhavati, tad anena rūpyakāṇāṃ śatam utpatsyate | tatas tena mayājād vayaṃ grahītavyam | tataḥ ṣāṇ-māsikam āprasava-vaśāt tābhyāṃ yūthaṃ bhaviṣyati | tato 'jābhiḥ prabhūtā gā grahīṣyāmi | gobhir mahiṣīḥ | mahiṣīr baḍavāḥ | baḍavā-prasavataḥ prabhūtā aśvā bhaviṣyanti | teṣāṃ vikrayāt prabhūtaṃ suvarṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | suvarṇena catuḥśālaṃ gṛhaṃ sampatsyate |
children.translated_text: Now one night, lying in bed, he thought: 'This pot is filled with barley-flour. If there is a famine, a hundred silver coins will be obtained from it. With those I shall acquire a pair of goats. Then, within six months, due to the [goats'] breeding, a herd will come from them. Then from goats I shall obtain many cows; from cows, she-buffaloes; from she-buffaloes, mares. From the mares' offspring, many horses will come. From their sale, abundant gold will come. With the gold, a four-courted house will be obtained.'

children.text: tataḥ kaścid brāhmaṇo mama gṛham āgatya prāpta-vayaskāṃ rūpāḍhyāṃ kanyāṃ mahyaṃ dāsyati | tat-sakāśāṭ putro me bhaviṣyati | tasyāḥaṃ somaśarmā iti nāma kariṣyāmi | tatas tasmin jānu-calana-yogye sañjāte'haṃ pustakaṃ gṛhītvāśva-śālāyāḥ pṛṣṭha-deśe upaviṣṭas tad-avadhārayiṣyāmi | atrāntare somaśarmā māṃ dṛṣṭvā janany-utsaṅgāj jānu-calana-paro 'śva-khurāsanna-vartī mat-samīpam āgamiṣyati | tato 'haṃ brāhmaṇīṃ kopāviṣṭo 'bhidhāsyāmi-gṛhāṇa tāvad bālakam | sāpi gṛha-karma-vyagratayāsmad-vacanaṃ na śroṣyati | tato 'haṃ samutthāya tāṃ pāda-prahāreṇa tāḍayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: 'Then some Brahmin will come to my house and give me a beautiful daughter of marriageable age. From her a son will be born to me. I shall name him <s>Somaśarman</s>. Then, when he has reached the age of crawling on his knees, I, taking a book, shall sit behind the horse-stable and study it. In the meanwhile, <s>Somaśarman</s>, seeing me, crawling on his knees from his mother's lap, will come near me, close to the horses' hooves. Then I, filled with anger, shall say to the Brahmin woman: "Take hold of the child!" But she, busy with household work, will not heed my words. Then I, rising up, shall kick her.'

children.text: evaṃ tena dhyāna-sthitena tathaiva pāda-prahāro datto yathā sa ghaṭo bhagnaḥ, svayaṃ ca saktubhiḥ pāṇḍuratāṃ gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-anāgatavatīṃ cintām iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, while he was absorbed in thought, he kicked in exactly that manner — and the pot broke, and he himself became white [covered] with barley-flour. Therefore I say: 'He who worries about what has not yet come...' [and so on].

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-evam etat | kas te doṣaḥ, yataḥ sarvo 'pi lobhena viḍambito bādhyate ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'So it is. What fault is yours? — since everyone is tormented and harmed by greed. And it is said:'

children.text: yo laulyāt kurute naivodarkam avekṣate |
children.translated_text: He who does [something] out of greed and does not consider the consequences —

children.text: viḍambanām avāpnoti sa yathā candra-bhūpatiḥ ||Panc_5.69||
children.translated_text: he meets with disgrace, just like King <s>Candra</s>. // Panc_5.69 //

children.text: cakradhara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: sa āha-
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text:
kathā 9
candra-bhūpati-kathā
children.translated_text:
Story 9
The story of King <s>Candra</s>

children.text: kasmiṃścin nagare candro nāma bhūpatiḥ prativasati sma | tasya putrā vānara-krīḍā-ratā vānara-yūthaṃ nityam evāneka-bhojana-bhakṣyādibhiḥ puṣṭiṃ nayanti sma | atha vānarādhipo yaḥ sa auśanasa-bārhaspatya-cāṇakya-mata-vit tad-anuṣṭhātā ca tat-sarvān apy adhyāpayati sma |
children.translated_text: In a certain city there lived a king named <s>Candra</s>. His sons, delighting in playing with monkeys, always nourished a troop of monkeys with abundant food and delicacies. And the chief of the monkeys, who knew the doctrines of <s>Uśanas</s> (Śukra), <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and <s>Cāṇakya</s> and practiced them, used to instruct all of them.

children.text: atha tasmin rāja-gṛhe laghu-kumāra-vāhana-yogyaṃ meṣa-yūtham asti | tan-madhyād eko jihvā-laulyād ahar-niśaṃ niḥśaṅkaṃ mahānase praviśya yat paśyati tat sarvaṃ bhakṣayati | te ca sūpakar yat kiñcit kāṣṭhaṃ mṛṇ-mayaṃ bhājanaṃ kāṃsya-pātraṃ tāmra-pātraṃ vā paśyanti tenāśu tāḍayanti |
children.translated_text: Now, in that royal household there was a flock of rams suitable for carrying the young princes. Among them, one [ram], out of the greed of his tongue, would shamelessly enter the kitchen day and night and eat whatever he saw. And the cooks, [seeing him], would strike him with whatever piece of wood, earthen vessel, bronze pot, or copper pot they could see.

children.text: so 'pi vānara-yūthapas tad dṛṣṭvā vyacintayat-aho meṣa-sūpakāra-kalaho 'yaṃ vānarāṇāṃ kṣayāya bhaviṣyati | yato 'nna-rasāsvāda-lampaṭo 'yaṃ meṣo, mahā-kopāś ca sūpakārā yathāsanna-vastunā praharanti | tad yadi vastuno 'bhāvāt kadācid ulmukena tāḍayiṣyanti, tadorṇā-pracuro 'yaṃ meṣaḥ svalpenāpi vahninā prajvalayiṣyati | tad dahyamānaḥ punar aśva-kuṭyāṃ samīpa-vartinyāṃ pravekṣyati | sāpi tṛṇa-prācuryāj jvaliṣyati | tato 'śvā vahni-dāham avāpsyanti |
children.translated_text: The monkey-chief, seeing this, thought: 'Ah, this quarrel between the ram and the cooks will bring destruction upon the monkeys. For this ram is greedy for the taste of food, and the cooks are quick-tempered — they strike with whatever is near at hand. If someday, lacking [other] objects, they strike him with a firebrand, then this ram, being thick with wool, will be set ablaze by even a small fire. While burning, he will then enter the nearby horse-stable. That too, being full of straw, will catch fire. Then the horses will suffer burns from fire.'

children.text: śālihotreṇa punar etad uktaṃ yat-vānara-vasayāśvānāṃ vahni-dāha-doṣaḥ praśāmyati | tan nūnam etena bhāvyam atra niścayaḥ | evaṃ niścitya sarvān vānarān āhūya rahasi provāca, yat-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Śālihotra</s> has stated that the burn-injury of horses caused by monkey-fat is healed. So surely this [slaughter of monkeys for their fat] is bound to happen — of this I am certain.' Having thus resolved, he summoned all the monkeys and said to them in private:

children.text: meṣeṇa sūpakārāṇāṃ kalaho yatra jāyate |
children.translated_text: Where a quarrel arises between the ram and the cooks,

children.text: sa bhaviṣyaty asandigdhaṃ vānarāṇāṃ kṣayāvahaḥ ||Panc_5.70||
children.translated_text: that will undoubtedly bring destruction upon the monkeys. // Panc_5.70 //

children.text: tasmāt syāt kalaho yatra gṛhe nityam akāraṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, a house in which constant causeless quarrel arises —

children.text: tad-gṛhaṃ jīvitaṃ vāñchan dūrataḥ parivarjayet ||Panc_5.71||
children.translated_text: that house should be avoided from afar by one who desires to live. // Panc_5.71 //

children.text: kalahāntāni harmyāṇi kuvākyāntaṃ ca sauhṛdam |
children.translated_text: Palaces end in quarrel; friendship ends in harsh words;

children.text: kurājāntāni rāṣṭrāṇi kukarmāntaṃ yaśo nṛṇām ||Panc_5.72||
children.translated_text: kingdoms end in bad kings; the fame of men ends in evil deeds. // Panc_5.72 //

children.text: tan na yāvat sarveṣāṃ saṅkṣayo bhavati, tāvad evaitad rāja-gṛhaṃ santyajya vanaṃ gacchāmaḥ | atha tat tasya vacanam aśraddheyaṃ śrutvā madoddhatā vānarāḥ prahasya procuḥ-bho bhavato vṛddha-bhāvād buddhi-vaikalyaṃ sañjātaṃ, yenaitad bravīṣi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: So before there is destruction of all, let us abandon this royal palace and go to the forest. Then, hearing those unbelievable words of his, the monkeys, puffed up with pride, laughed and said: O you! A mental derangement has come upon you due to old age, that you say this. And it is said —

children.text: vadanaṃ daśanair hīnaṃ lālā sravati nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The face is bereft of teeth, saliva constantly drools,

children.text: na matiḥ sphurati kvāpi bāle vṛddhe viśeṣataḥ ||Panc_5.73||
children.translated_text: the mind does not stir anywhere — in the young and especially in the old. ||Panc_5.73||

children.text: na vayaṃ svarga-samānopabhogān nānā-vidhān bhakṣya-viśeṣān rāja-putraiḥ sva-dattān amṛta-kalpān parityajya tatrāṭavyāṃ kaṣāya-kaṭu-tikta-kṣāra-rūkṣa-phalāni bhakṣayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: We shall not abandon the various heavenly food-delicacies, like ambrosia, given by the princes, and eat bitter, pungent, acrid, salty, and rough fruits in that wilderness.

children.text: tac chrutvāśru-kaluṣāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ kṛtvā sa provāca-re re mūrkhāḥ ! yūyam etasya sukhasya pariṇāmaṃ na jānītha | kiṃ pāka-rasāsvādana-prāyam etat sukhaṃ pariṇāme viṣavad bhaviṣyati | tad ahaṃ kula-kṣayaṃ svayaṃ nāvalokayiṣyāmi | sāmprataṃ vanaṃ yāsyāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, making his gaze clouded with tears, he said: O fools! You do not know the consequence of this pleasure. Like the tasting of ripening [poison], this pleasure will become like poison in its outcome. So I shall not witness the destruction of my clan with my own eyes. I shall now go to the forest. And it is said —

children.text: mitraṃ vyasana-samprāptaṃ sva-sthānaṃ para-pīḍanam |
children.translated_text: A friend who has met with calamity, one's own place being oppressed by another —

children.text: dhanyās te ye na paśyanti deśa-bhaṅgaṃ kula-kṣayam ||Panc_5.74||
children.translated_text: blessed are those who do not witness the ruin of their country and the destruction of their clan. ||Panc_5.74||

children.text: evam abhidhāya sarvāṃs tān parityajya sa yūthādhipo 'ṭavyāṃ gataḥ | atha tasmin gate'nyasmin ahani sa meṣo mahānase praviṣṭo, yāvat sūpakāreṇa nānyat kiñcit samāsāditaṃ tāvad ardha-jvalita-kāṣṭhena tāḍyamāno jājvalyamana-śarīraḥ śabdāyamāno 'śva-kuṭyāṃ pratyāsanna-vartinyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having said this, abandoning all of them, that herd-leader went to the wilderness. Then, on the next day after he had gone, that ram entered the kitchen. When the cook could not find anything else [to drive it away], he struck it with a half-burning log, and it, its body blazing, making noise, entered the horse-stable which was close by.

children.text: tatra tṛṇa-prācurya-yuktāyāṃ kṣitau tasya praluṭhataḥ sarvatrāpi vahni-jvālās tathā samutthitā yathā kecid aśvāḥ sphuṭita-locanāḥ pañcatvaṃ gatāḥ | kecid bandhanāni troṭayitvā ardha-dagdha-śarīrā itaś cetaś ca hreṣāyamāṇā dhāvamānā sarvam api jana-samūham ākulīcakruḥ |
children.translated_text: There, on the ground full of straw, as it rolled about, flames of fire arose everywhere in such a way that some horses, their eyes bursting, died. Some, having broken their bonds, their bodies half-burnt, neighing and running here and there, threw the entire crowd of people into confusion.

children.text: atrāntare rājā saviṣādaḥ śālihotrajñān vaidyān āhūya provāca-bhoḥ ! procyatām eṣām aśvānāṃ kaścid dāhopaśamanopāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, the king, distressed, summoned physicians learned in <s>Śālihotra</s> (veterinary science) and said: Sirs! Prescribe some remedy for the burns of these horses.

children.text: te'pi śāstrāṇi vilokya procuḥ-deva ! proktam atra viṣaye bhagavatā śālihotreṇa, yat-
children.translated_text: They too, consulting the treatises, said: Lord! In this matter it has been declared by the venerable <s>Śālihotra</s> that —

children.text: kapīnāṃ medasā doṣo vahni-dāha-samudbhavā |
children.translated_text: The affliction born of fire-burns in horses

children.text: aśvānāṃ nāśam abhyeti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ||Panc_5.75||
children.translated_text: is destroyed by the fat of monkeys, as darkness [is destroyed] at sunrise. ||Panc_5.75||

children.text: tat kriyatām etac cikitsitāṃ drāk, yāvad ete na dāha-doṣeṇa vinaśyanti |
children.translated_text: So let this treatment be quickly carried out, before they perish from the affliction of burning.

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇya samasta-vānara-vadham ādiṣṭavān | kiṃ bahunā, sarve'pi te vānarā vividhāyudha-laguḍa-pāṣāṇādibhir vyāpāditāḥ iti |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing that, ordered the slaughter of all the monkeys. In short, all those monkeys were killed with various weapons — staves, stones, and the like.

children.text: atha so 'pi vānara-yūthapas taṃ putra-pautra-bhrātṛ-suta-bhāgineyādi-saṅkṣayaṃ jñātvā viṣādam upagataḥ | santyaktāhāra-kriyo vanād vanaṃ paryaṭati | acintayac ca-katham ahaṃ tasya nṛpāpasadayānṛṇatā-kṛtyenāpakṛtyaṃ kariṣyāmi | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Now that monkey herd-leader too, knowing of the destruction of his sons, grandsons, brother's sons, and nephews, became grief-stricken. Having abandoned food and activities, he wandered from forest to forest. And he thought: How shall I take revenge upon that wretched king and discharge my debt? And it is said —

children.text: marṣayed dharṣaṇāṃ yo 'tra vaṃśajāṃ para-nirmitām |
children.translated_text: He who tolerates an outrage against his lineage wrought by another,

children.text: bhayād vā yadi vā kāmāt sa jñeyaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ ||Panc_5.76||
children.translated_text: whether from fear or from desire — he should be known as the lowest of men. ||Panc_5.76||

children.text: atha tena vṛddha-vānareṇa kutracit pipāsākulena bhramatā padminī-khaṇḍa-maṇḍitaṃ saraḥ samāsāditam | tad yāvat sūkṣmekṣikayāvalokayati tāvad vanacara-manuṣyāṇāṃ pada-paṅkti-pradeśo 'sti na niṣkramaṇam | tataś cintitam-nūnam atra ākrānte duṣṭa-grāheṇa bhāvyam | tat-padminī-nālam ādāya dūrastho 'pi jalaṃ pibāmi |
children.translated_text: Then that old monkey, wandering about somewhere tortured by thirst, came upon a lake adorned with lotus-beds. Looking at it with careful observation, he [noticed] there were footprints of forest-dwelling humans [going] in, but none coming out. Then he thought: Surely there must be a wicked crocodile lurking here. So I shall drink water from a distance using a lotus-stalk.

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite tan-madhyād rākṣaso niṣkramya ratna-mālā-vibhūṣita-kaṇṭhas tam uvāca-bhoḥ ! atra yaḥ salile praveśaṃ karoti sa me bhakṣyaḥ iti | tan nāsti dhūrtataras tvat-samo 'nyo yaḥ pānīyam anena vidhinā pibati | tatas tuṣṭo 'haṃ, prārthayasva hṛdaya-vāñchitam |
children.translated_text: When this was carried out, a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) emerged from its midst, his neck adorned with a garland of jewels, and said to him: Ho! Whoever enters this water becomes my food. So there is no one more clever than you, who drinks water in this manner. Therefore I am pleased — ask for whatever your heart desires!

children.text: kapir āha-bhoḥ ! kiyatī me bhakṣaṇa-śaktiḥ ?
children.translated_text: The monkey said: Ho! How great is your devouring power?

children.text: sa āha-śata-sahasrāyuta-lakṣāṇy api jala-praviṣṭāni bhakṣayāmi | bāhyataḥ śṛgālo 'pi māṃ dharṣayati |
children.translated_text: He said: I devour hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, and hundred-thousands that enter the water. Outside [the water], even a jackal can overpower me.

children.text: vānara āha-asti me kenacid bhūpatinā sahātyantaṃ vairam | yady enāṃ ratna-mālāṃ me prayacchasi, tat parivāram api taṃ bhūpatiṃ vākya-prapañcena lobhayitvātra sarasi praveśayāmi |
children.translated_text: The monkey said: I have an extreme enmity with a certain king. If you give me this jewel-garland, then I shall entice his retinue and even that king himself with a web of words and make them enter this lake.

children.text: so 'pi śraddheyaṃ vacas tasya śrutvā ratna-mālāṃ dattvā prāha-bho mitra ! yat samucitaṃ bhavati tat kartavyam iti |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing those trustworthy words, gave the jewel-garland and said: O friend! Whatever is appropriate should be done.

children.text: vānaro 'pi ratna-mālā-vibhūṣita-kaṇṭho vṛkṣa-prāsādeṣu paribhraman janair dṛṣṭaḥ | pṛṣṭaś ca-bho yūthapa ! bhavān iyantaṃ kālaṃ kutra sthitaḥ ? bhavatā īdṛg ratna-mālā kutra labdhā ? dīptyā sūryam api tiraskaroti |
children.translated_text: The monkey too, his neck adorned with the jewel-garland, was seen by people while wandering about in the tree-palaces. And he was asked: O herd-leader! Where have you been for so long? Where did you obtain such a jewel-garland? It outshines even the sun with its brilliance!

children.text: vānaraḥ prāha-asti kutracid araṇye guptataraṃ mahat saro dhanada-nirmitam | tatra sūrye'rdhodite ravi-vāre yaḥ kaścin nimajjati, sa dhanada-prasādād īdṛg-ratna-mālā-vibhūṣita-kaṇṭho niḥsarati |
children.translated_text: The monkey said: There is in a certain forest a very hidden great lake, made by <s>Kubera</s> (lord of wealth). There, when the sun is half-risen on a Sunday, whoever dives in emerges with his neck adorned with such a jewel-garland by <s>Kubera</s>'s grace.

children.text: atha bhūbhujā tad ākarṇya, sa vānaraḥ samāhūtaḥ | pṛṣṭaś ca-bho yūthādhipa ! kiṃ satyam etat ? ratna-mālā-sanāthaṃ saro 'sti kvāpi ?
children.translated_text: Then the king, hearing that, summoned that monkey. And he asked: O herd-leader! Is this true? Is there somewhere a lake endowed with jewel-garlands?

children.text: kapir āha-svāmin ! eṣa pratyakṣatayā mat-kaṇṭha-sthitayā ratna-mālayā pratyayas te | tad yadi ratna-mālayā prayojanaṃ tan mayā saha kam api preṣaya, yena darśayāmi |
children.translated_text: The monkey said: Master! The proof is this jewel-garland placed visibly on my neck. So if there is a use for jewel-garlands, send someone with me, and I shall show [the lake].

children.text: tac chrutvā nṛpatir āha-yady evaṃ tad ahaṃ sa-parijanaḥ svayam eṣyāmi, yena prabhūtā ratna-mālā utpadyate |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king said: If so, then I myself shall come with my retinue, so that abundant jewel-garlands may be produced.

children.text: vānara āha-evaṃ kriyatām |
children.translated_text: The monkey said: Let it be done so.

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite bhūpatinā saha ratna-mālā-lobhena sarve kalatra-bhṛtyāḥ prasthitāḥ | vānaro 'pi rājñā dolādhirūḍhena svotsaṅge āropitaḥ sukhena prīti-pūrvam ānīyate | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
tṛṣṇe devi namas tubhyaṃ yayā vittānvitā api |
children.translated_text: O Goddess <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (Greed)! Salutations to you, by whom even the wealthy

children.text: akṛtyeṣu niyojyante bhrāmante durgameṣv api ||Panc_5.77||
children.translated_text: are engaged in improper deeds and are made to wander in impassable places! ||Panc_5.77||

When this was carried out, the king's wives and servants all set out with him, lured by greed for jewel-garlands. The monkey too, placed by the king — who was riding in a palanquin — upon his own lap, was carried along comfortably and with affection. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: icchati śatī sahasraṃ sahasrī lakṣam īhate |
children.translated_text: He who has a hundred desires a thousand; he who has a thousand craves a hundred-thousand;

children.text: lakṣādhipas tathā rājyaṃ rājyasthaḥ svargam īhate ||Panc_5.78||
children.translated_text: the lord of a hundred-thousand craves a kingdom; the king craves heaven. ||Panc_5.78||

children.text: jīryante jīryataḥ keśāḥ dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ |
children.translated_text: The hair grows old as one ages; the teeth grow old as one ages;

children.text: jīryataś cakṣuṣī śrotre tṛṣṇaikā taruṇāyate ||Panc_5.79||
children.translated_text: the eyes and ears grow old as one ages — desire alone remains youthful. ||Panc_5.79||

children.text: atha tat-saraḥ samāsādya vānaraḥ pratyūṣa-samaye rājānam uvāca-deva ! atrārdhodite sūrye'ntaḥ-praviṣṭānāṃ siddhir bhavati tat sarvo 'pi jana ekadaiva praviśatu | tvayā punar mayā saha praveṣṭavyaṃ, yena pūrva-dṛṣṭa-sthānam āsādya, prabhūtās te ratna-mālā darśayāmi |
children.translated_text: Then, having reached that lake, the monkey said to the king at dawn: Lord! Here, when the sun is half-risen, success comes to those who enter. So let all the people enter at once. But you must enter with me, so that, reaching the previously seen place, I may show you abundant jewel-garlands.

children.text: atha praviṣṭās te lokāḥ sarve bhakṣitā rākṣasena | atha teṣu ciramāṇeṣu rājā vānaram āha-bho yūthādhipa kim iti cirāyate me parijanaḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then those people entered and were all devoured by the <s>Rākṣasa</s>. Then, as they delayed, the king said to the monkey: O herd-leader! Why is my retinue taking so long?

children.text: tac chrutvā vānaraḥ satvaraṃ vṛkṣam āruhya rājānam uvāca-bho duṣṭa-narapate ! rākṣasenāntaḥ-salila-sthitena bhakṣitās te parijanaḥ | sādhitaṃ mayā kula-kṣayajaṃ vairam, tad gamyatām | tvaṃ svāmīti matvā nātra praveśitaḥ | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the monkey quickly climbed a tree and said to the king: O wicked king! Your retinue has been devoured by the <s>Rākṣasa</s> dwelling within the water. I have accomplished my vengeance born from the destruction of my clan. So go! Thinking 'you are the master,' you were not made to enter [the water]. And it is said —

children.text: kṛte pratikṛtaṃ kuryād dhiṃsite pratihiṃsitam |
children.translated_text: One should do in return what was done; one should retaliate against one who has harmed;

children.text: na tatra doṣaṃ paśyāmi yo duṣṭe duṣṭam ācaret ||Panc_5.80||
children.translated_text: I see no fault in one who acts wickedly toward the wicked. ||Panc_5.80||

children.text: tat tvayā mama kula-kṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ mayā punas tava iti |
children.translated_text: So — by you the destruction of my clan was wrought; by me, the destruction of yours.

children.text: athaitad ākarṇya rājā kopāviṣṭaḥ padātir ekākī yathāyāta-mārgeṇa niṣkrāntaḥ | atha tasmin bhūpatau gate rākṣasa-spṛṣṭo jalān niṣkramya sānandam idam āha-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that, the king, filled with rage, departed alone on foot by the path he had come. Now when that king had gone, the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, having been touched [by the experience], emerged from the water and said with joy —

children.text: hataḥ śatruḥ kṛtaṃ mitraṃ ratna-mālā na hāritā |
children.translated_text: The enemy is slain, a friend has been made, the jewel-garland was not lost —

children.text: nālena pibatā toyaṃ bhavatā sādhu vānara ||Panc_5.81||
children.translated_text: by drinking water through a stalk, you have done well, O monkey! ||Panc_5.81||

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-yo laulyāt kurute karma iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'He who out of greed does a deed...'

children.text: evam uktvā bhūyo 'pi sa cakradharam āha-bho mitra ! preṣaya māṃ, yena sva-gṛhaṃ gacchāmi |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he said again to <s>Cakradhara</s>: O friend! Send me off, so that I may go to my own home.

children.text: cakradhara āha-bhadra ! āpad-arthe dhana-mitra-saṅgrahaḥ kriyate | tan mām evaṃvidhaṃ tyaktvā kva yāsyasi ? uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: Good friend! Wealth and friends are accumulated for times of calamity. So, abandoning me in such a state, where will you go? And it is said —

children.text: yas tyaktvā sāpadaṃ mitraṃ yāti niṣṭhuratāṃ vahan |
children.translated_text: He who, abandoning a friend in distress, goes bearing cruelty —

children.text: kṛtaghnas tena pāpena narake yāty asaṃśayam ||Panc_5.82||
children.translated_text: that ungrateful one, by that sin, goes to hell without doubt. ||Panc_5.82||

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-bhoḥ, satyam etad yadi gamya-sthāne śaktir bhavati | etat punar manuṣyāṇām agamya-sthānam | nāsti kasyāpi tvām unmocayituṃ śaktiḥ aparaṃ yathā yathā cakra-bhrama-vedanayā tava mukha-vikāraṃ paśyāmi tathā tathāham etaj jānāmi yat drāg gacchāmi mā kaścin mamāpy anartho bhaved iti | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: Friend, this is true if one has the power to [go to] an accessible place. But this is an inaccessible place for humans. No one has the power to free you. Moreover, as I see the distortion of your face from the pain of the wheel's spinning, I know this much — that I should leave quickly lest some harm befall me too. For —

children.text: yādṛśī vadana-cchāyā dṛśyate tava vānara |
children.translated_text: Such as is the complexion of your face that is seen, O monkey —

children.text: vikālena gṛhīto 'si yaḥ paraiti sa jīvati ||Panc_5.83||
children.translated_text: you have been seized by <s>Vikāla</s> (the demon); he who departs [from here] lives. ||Panc_5.83||

children.text: cakradhara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: How is that?

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 10
vikāla-vānara-kathā
children.translated_text:
He said —
Tale 10
The Story of the <s>Vikāla</s> Monkey

children.text: kasmiṃścin nagare bhadraseno nāma rājā prativasati sma | tasya sarva-lakṣaṇa-sampannā ratnavatī nāma kanyāsti | tāṃ kaścid rākṣaso jihīrṣati | rātrāv āgatyopabhuṅkte, paraṃ kṛta-rakṣopadhānāṃ tāṃ hartuṃ na śaknoti | sāpi tat-samaye rakṣaḥ-sānnidhyajām avasthām anubhavati kampādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain city there dwelt a king named <s>Bhadrasena</s>. He had a daughter named <s>Ratnavatī</s>, endowed with all auspicious marks. A certain <s>Rākṣasa</s> wished to abduct her. Coming at night, he would enjoy her, but was unable to abduct her who had been provided with protective charms. And she would experience the condition born from the demon's proximity through trembling and such [symptoms].

children.text: ekam atikrāmati kāle kadācit sa rākṣaso madhya-niśāyāṃ gṛha-koṇe sthitaḥ | sāpi rāja-kanyā sva-sakhīm uvāca-sakhi ! paśyaiṣa vikālaḥ samaye nityam eva māṃ kadarthayati | asti tasya durātmanaḥ pratiṣedhopāyaḥ kaścit ?
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, that <s>Rākṣasa</s> was standing in a corner of the room at midnight. And that princess said to her companion: Friend! Look — this <s>Vikāla</s> torments me always at this time. Is there any means of warding off that evil-souled one?

children.text: tac chrutvā rākṣaso 'pi vyacintayat-nūnaṃ yathāhaṃ tathānyo 'pi kaścid vikāla-nāmāsyā haraṇāya nityam evāgacchati | paraṃ so 'py enāṃ hartuṃ na śaknoti | tat tāvad aśva-rūpaṃ kṛtvāśva-madhya-gato nirīkṣayāmi | kiṃ-rūpaḥ sa kiṃ-prabhāvaś ceti ? evaṃ rākṣaso 'śva-rūpaṃ kṛtvāśvānāṃ madhye tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> too thought: Surely, just as I [come], some other one also named <s>Vikāla</s> always comes to abduct her. But he too is unable to abduct her. So let me take the form of a horse and, stationed among the horses, observe: What does he look like? What is his power? Thus the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, having taken the form of a horse, stood among the horses.

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite niśītha-samaye rāja-gṛhe kaścid aśva-cauraḥ praviṣṭaḥ | sa ca sarvān aśvān avalokya taṃ rākṣasam aśvatamaṃ vijñāyādhirūḍhaḥ |
children.translated_text: When this was done, at midnight a certain horse-thief entered the royal palace. And he, looking at all the horses, recognizing that <s>Rākṣasa</s> as the finest horse, mounted it.

children.text: atrāntare rākṣasaś cintayāmāsa-nūnam eṣa vikāla-nāmā māṃ cauraṃ matvā kopān nihantum āgataḥ | tat kiṃ karomi ? evaṃ cintayan so 'pi tena khalīnaṃ mukhe nidhāya kaśāghātena tāḍitaḥ | athāsau bhaya-trasta-manāḥ pradhāvitum ārabdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> thought: Surely this one named <s>Vikāla</s> has come, and thinking me a thief, has mounted me in anger to kill me. So what shall I do? Thinking thus, he too, having had a bit placed in his mouth by that one, was struck with whip-blows. Then, his mind terrified with fear, he began to gallop away.

children.text: cauro 'pi dūraṃ gatvā khalīnākarṣaṇena taṃ sthiraṃ kartum ārabdhavān | sa tu vegād vegataraṃ gacchati | atha taṃ tathāgaṇita-khalīnākarṣaṇaṃ matvā cauraś cintayāmāsa-aho naivaṃ-vidhā vājino bhavanty agaṇita-khalīnāḥ | tan nūnam anenāśva-rūpeṇa rākṣasena bhavitavyam | yadyapi kañcit pāṃsulaṃ bhūmi-deśam avalokayāmi tad ātmānaṃ tatra pātayāmi | nānyathā me jīvitavyam asti |
children.translated_text: The thief too, having gone far, began trying to steady him by pulling the bridle. But the [horse] went faster and faster. Then, observing that it completely disregarded the bridle's pull, the thief thought: 'Ah! Horses of this kind, that disregard the bridle, do not exist. So this must surely be a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) in the form of a horse. If I see some dusty patch of ground, I shall throw myself down there. Otherwise there is no way for me to survive.'

children.text: evaṃ cintayata iṣṭa-devatāṃ smaratas tasya so 'śvo baṭa-vṛkṣasya tale niṣkrāntaḥ | cauro 'pi baṭa-praroham āsādya tatraiva vilagnaḥ | tato dvāv api tau pṛthag-bhūtau paramānanda-bhājau jīvita-viṣaye labdha-pratyāśau sampannau |
children.translated_text: While he was thus thinking and remembering his chosen deity, that horse emerged beneath a banyan tree. The thief too, reaching a hanging root of the banyan, clung to it there. And so the two, having separated, both became supremely joyful, having regained hope for life.

children.text: atha tatra baṭe kaścid rākṣasa-suhṛd vānaraḥ sthita āsīt | tena rākṣasaṃ trastam ālokya vyāhṛtam-bho mitra ! kim eva alāyyate'līka-bhayena ? tad bhakṣyo 'yaṃ mānuṣaḥ bhakṣyatām |
children.translated_text: Now on that banyan there was a certain monkey, a friend of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>. He, seeing the <s>Rākṣasa</s> frightened, said: 'O friend! Why are you terrified by a false fear? This human is your food — eat him!'

children.text: so 'pi vānara-vaco niśamya, svarūpam ādhāya śaṅkita-manāḥ skhalita-gatir nivṛttaḥ | cauro 'pi taṃ vānarāhūtaṃ jñātvā kopāt tasya lāṅgulaṃ lambamānaṃ mukhe nidhāya carvitavān |
children.translated_text: And he, hearing the monkey's words, assumed his true form and, his mind apprehensive, came back with faltering steps. The thief too, knowing him to have been summoned by the monkey, in anger seized the monkey's dangling tail and crunched it in his mouth.

children.text: vānaro 'pi taṃ rākṣasābhyadhikaṃ manyamāno bhayān na kiñcid uktavān | kevalaṃ vyathārto nimīlita-nayanas tiṣṭhati | rākṣaso 'pi taṃ tathā-bhūtam avalokya ślokam enam apaṭhat-
children.translated_text: The monkey too, thinking him to be even more powerful than the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, said nothing out of fear. He merely stood there, closing his eyes, suffering. The <s>Rākṣasa</s> too, seeing him in that state, recited this verse —

children.text: yādṛśī vacana-cchāyā dṛśyate tava vānara |
children.translated_text: 'From the expression on your face that I see, O monkey,

children.text: vikālena gṛhīto 'si yaḥ paraiti sa jīvati ||Panc_5.84||
children.translated_text: you have been seized by an evil spirit — whoever gets away from here lives.' [Panc 5.84]

children.text: ity uktvā praṇaṣṭaś ca | tat preṣaya māṃ yena gṛhaṃ gacchāmi | tvaṃ punar anubhuṅkṣvātra sthita eva lobha-vṛkṣa-phalam |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he vanished. 'So send me away so that I may go home. And you, remain here and enjoy the fruit of the tree of greed.'

children.text: cakradhara āha-bhoḥ akāraṇam etat | daiva-vaśāt sampadyate nṛṇāṃ śubhāśubham | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'Friend! This is without reason. By the power of fate, good and evil befall men.' And it is said —

children.text: durgas trikūṭaḥ parikhā samudro
children.translated_text: His fortress was <s>Trikūṭa</s>, his moat the ocean,

children.text: rakṣāṃsi yodhā dhanadāc ca vittam |
children.translated_text: <s>Rākṣasas</s> were his warriors, and wealth came from <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera),

children.text: śāstraṃ ca yasyośanasā praṇītaṃ
children.translated_text: and his treatise was composed by <s>Uśanas</s> (Śukra) —

children.text: sa rāvaṇo daiva-vaśād vipannaḥ ||Panc_5.85||
children.translated_text: yet that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> perished by the power of fate. [Panc 5.85]

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: andhakaḥ kubjakaś caiva tristanī rāja-kanyakā |
children.translated_text: A blind man, a hunchback, and a three-breasted princess —

children.text: trayo 'py anyāyataḥ siddhāḥ saṃmukhe karmaṇi sthite ||Panc_5.86||
children.translated_text: all three were made whole by circumstances unforeseen, when <s>karma</s> stood before them. [Panc 5.86]

children.text: suvarṇa-siddhiḥ prāha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text:
so 'bravīt-
kathā 11
andhaka-kubjaka-tristanī-kathā
children.translated_text: He narrated — Story 11: The tale of the blind man, the hunchback, and the three-breasted woman.

children.text: asty atra dharā-tala uttarā-pathe madhu-puraṃ nāma nagaram | tatra madhusenā nāma rājā babhūva | tasya kadācid viṣaya-sukham anubhavatas tristanī kanyā babhūva | atha tāṃ trastanīṃ jātāṃ śrutvā sa rājā kañcukinaḥ provāca, yad-bhos tyajyatām iyaṃ trastanī gatvā dūre'raṇye yathā kaścin na jānāti |
children.translated_text: There is upon this earth, in the northern region, a city called <s>Madhupura</s>. There once ruled a king named <s>Madhusenā</s>. To him, while he was enjoying the pleasures of his realm, a three-breasted daughter was born. Then, hearing that a three-breasted girl had been born, the king said to the chamberlains: 'Ho! Take this three-breasted one far away to a distant forest and abandon her, so that no one may know.'

children.text: tac chrutvā kañcukinaḥ procuḥ-mahārāja jñāyate yad aniṣṭa-kāriṇī tristanī kanyā bhavati | tathāpi brāhmaṇam āhūya praṣṭavyāḥ, yena loka-dvayaṃ na virudhyate, yataḥ-
yaḥ satataṃ paripṛcchati śṛṇoti sandhārayaty aniśam |
children.translated_text: He who constantly inquires, listens, and retains [knowledge] ceaselessly —

children.text: tasya divākara-kiraṇair nalinīva vivardhate buddhiḥ ||Panc_5.87||
children.translated_text: his intellect flourishes, like a lotus by the rays of the sun. [Panc 5.87]

Hearing that, the chamberlains said: 'Great king! It is known that a three-breasted daughter brings misfortune. Nevertheless, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> should be summoned and consulted, so that neither this world nor the next is violated, for —

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise —

children.text: pṛcchakena sadā bhāvyaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā |
children.translated_text: A man of discernment should always be an inquirer;

children.text: rākṣasendra-gṛhīto 'pi praśnān mukto dvijaḥ purā ||Panc_5.88||
children.translated_text: a twice-born one, seized by the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, was freed long ago through asking questions. [Panc 5.88]

children.text: rājā āha--katham etat ?
children.translated_text: The king said: 'How is that?'

children.text: te procuḥ-
children.translated_text: They narrated —

children.text:
kathā 12
caṇḍakarma-nāma-rākṣasa-kathā
children.translated_text: Story 12: The tale of the <s>Rākṣasa</s> named <s>Caṇḍakarman</s> (Fierce-deeds).

children.text: deva ! kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe caṇḍakarmā nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati sma | ekadā tena bhramatāṭavyāṃ kaścid brāhmaṇaḥ samāsāditaḥ | tatas tasya skandham āruhya provāca-bho agresaro gamyatām |
