children.translated_text: Lord! In a certain forest region there lived a <s>Rākṣasa</s> named <s>Caṇḍakarman</s>. One day, while wandering in the forest, he came upon a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Then, mounting upon his shoulders, he said: 'Ho! Walk forward!'

children.text: brāhmaṇo 'pi bhaya-trasta-manās tam ādāya prasthitaḥ | atha tasya kamalodara-komalau pādau dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇo rākṣasam apṛcchat-bhoḥ ! kim evaṃ-vidhau te pādāv atikomalau ?
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too, his mind stricken with fear, set out carrying him. Then, seeing his feet as soft as the interior of a lotus, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> asked the <s>Rākṣasa</s>: 'Sir! Why are your feet so exceedingly soft?'

children.text: rākṣasa āha-bhoḥ ! vratam asti, nāham ārdra-pādo bhūmiṃ spṛśāmi |
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> said: 'Sir! I have a vow — I never touch the ground with wet feet.'

children.text: tatas tac chrutvātmano mokṣopāyaṃ cintayaṃs tat-saraḥ prāptaḥ | tato rākṣasenābhihitaṃ-bhoḥ ! yāvad ahaṃ snānaṃ kṛtvā devatārcana-vidhiṃ vidhāyāgacchāmi tāvat tvayātaḥ sthānād anyatra na gantavyam |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that, thinking of a means of escape for himself, he reached a certain lake. Then the <s>Rākṣasa</s> said: 'Sir! While I bathe and perform the prescribed worship of the deity and return, you must not go anywhere from this place.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite divjaś cintayāmāsa-nūnaṃ devatārcana-vidher ūrdhvaṃ mām eṣa bhakṣayiṣyati | tad drutataraṃ gacchāmi, yenaiṣa ārdra-pādo na mama pṛṣṭham eṣyati |
children.translated_text: When this had been done, the twice-born one thought: 'Surely after the worship ritual, this one will devour me. So I must flee quickly, so that this wet-footed one will not pursue me.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite rākṣaso vrata-bhaṅga-bhayāt tasya pṛṣṭhaṃ na gataḥ | ato 'haṃ bravīmi-pṛcchakena sadā bhāvyam iti |
children.translated_text: When this had been done, the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, fearing the breach of his vow, did not pursue him. Therefore I say: 'One should always be an inquirer...' and so on.

children.text: atha tebhyas tac chrutvā-rājā dvijān āhūya provāca-bho brāhmaṇāḥ ! tristanī me kanyā samutpannā, tat kiṃ tasyāḥ pratividhānam asti, na vā ?
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that from them, the king summoned the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and said: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>! A three-breasted daughter has been born to me. Is there a remedy for her, or not?'

children.text: hīnāṅgī vādhikāṅgī vā yā bhavet kanyakā nṛṇām |
children.translated_text: A maiden who is deficient in limbs or excessive in limbs —

children.text: bhartuḥ syāt sā vināśāya sva-śīla-nidhanāya ca ||Panc_5.89||
children.translated_text: she would bring destruction to her husband and ruin to her own character. [Panc 5.89]

children.text: yā punas tristanī kanyā yāti locana-gocaram |
children.translated_text: And a three-breasted daughter who comes within one's sight —

children.text: pitaraṃ nāśaty eva sā drutaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||Panc_5.90||
children.translated_text: she destroys her father swiftly — there is no doubt of this. [Panc 5.90]

children.text: tasmād asyā darśanaṃ pariharatu devaḥ | tathā yadi kaścid udvāhayati, tad enāṃ tasmai dattvā, deśa-tyāgena sa niyojayitavyaḥ iti | evaṃ-kṛte loka-dvayāviruddhatā bhavati |
children.translated_text: Therefore let His Majesty avoid seeing her. And if someone wishes to marry her, then having given her to him, he should be made to leave the country.' Thus done, there will be no violation of either world.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ tad-vacanam ākarṇya sa rājā paṭaha-śabdena sarvatra ghoṣaṇām ājñāpayāmāsa-aho ! tristanīṃ rājakanyāṃ yaḥ kaścid udvāhayati sa suvarṇa-lakṣam āpnoti deśa-tyāgaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing their words, the king ordered a proclamation everywhere by the beat of a drum: 'Hear all! Whoever marries the three-breasted princess shall receive a hundred thousand gold pieces and [must accept] exile from the country.'

children.text: evaṃ tasyām āghoṣaṇāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ mahān kālo vyatītaḥ | na kaścit tāṃ pratigṛhṇāti | sāpi yauvanonmukhī sañjātā sugupta-sthāna-sthitā yatnena rakṣyamāṇā tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: Thus, while that proclamation was being made, a long time passed. No one accepted her. And she, now reaching the threshold of youth, kept in a well-guarded place and carefully watched over, remained there.

children.text: atra tatraiva nagare kaścid andhas tiṣṭhati | tasya ca mantharaka-nāmā kubjo 'gresaro yaṣṭi-grāhī | tābhyāṃ taṃ paṭaha-śabdam ākarṇya, mitho mantritaṃ-spṛśyate'yaṃ paṭahaḥ | yadi katham api daivāt kanyā labhyate | suvarṇa-prāptiś ca bhavati, tathā sukhena suvarṇa-prāptyā kālo vrajati | atha yadi tasya doṣato mṛtyur bhavati | tadā dāridryopāttasyāsya kleśasya paryanto bhavati | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Now in that very city there lived a certain blind man. And his guide, a hunchback named <s>Mantharaka</s>, held the staff for him. Those two, hearing the beat of the drum, conferred with each other: 'Let us beat this drum. If somehow, by fate, the princess is obtained, and gold is received, then we live in comfort with the gold. And if death comes from her defect, then there will be an end to this suffering brought by poverty.' And it is said —

children.text: lajjā snehaḥ svara-madhuratā buddhayo yauvana-śrīḥ
children.translated_text: Modesty, affection, sweetness of voice, intelligence, the beauty of youth,

children.text: kāntāsaṅgaḥ svajana-mamatā duḥkha-hānir vilāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: the company of a beloved, attachment to one's own people, relief from sorrow, grace,

children.text: dharmaḥ śāstraṃ sura-guru-matiḥ śaucam ācāra-cintā
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, learning, the wisdom of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, purity, right conduct —

children.text: pūrṇe sarve jaṭhara-piṭhare prāṇināṃ sambhavanti ||Panc_5.91||
children.translated_text: all these arise in creatures only when the belly-pot is full. [Panc 5.91]

children.text: evam uktvāndhena gatvā, sa paṭahaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ | uktaṃ ca-bhoḥ ! ahaṃ tāṃ kanyām udvāhayāmi, yadi rājā me prayacchati |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the blind man went and beat the drum. And he said: 'Sir! I shall marry that princess, if the king gives her to me.'

children.text: tatas tai rāja-puruṣair gatvā rājñe niveditam-deva ! andhena kenacit paṭahaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ | tad atra viṣaye devaḥ pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: Then those royal servants went and reported to the king: 'Lord! Some blind man has beaten the drum. In this matter, His Majesty is the authority.'

children.text: rājā prāha-
children.translated_text: The king said —

children.text: andho vā vadhiro vātha kuṣṭī vāpy antyajo 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: Whether blind, or deaf, or leprous, or even an outcaste —

children.text: parigṛhṇātu tāṃ kanyāṃ sa-lakṣāṃ syād videśagaḥ ||Panc_5.92||
children.translated_text: let him take that princess with the hundred thousand [gold pieces]; he shall be a foreign-dweller. [Panc 5.92]

children.text: atha rājādeśāt tai rāja-puruṣais taṃ nadī-tīre nītvā suvarṇa-lakṣeṇa samaṃ vivāha-vidhinā tristanīṃ tasmai dattvā, jala-yāne nidhāya kaivartāḥ proktāḥ-bho ! deśāntaraṃ nītvā kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne'ndhaḥ sapatnīkaḥ | kubjakena saha mocanīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, by the king's command, those royal servants took him to the riverbank, gave him the three-breasted woman together with the hundred thousand gold pieces in a wedding ceremony, placed them on a boat, and told the boatmen: 'Ho! Take them to another country and at some settlement, release the blind man with his wife and the hunchback.'

children.text: tathānuṣṭhite videśam āsādya kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne kaivarta-darśite trayo 'pi mūlyena gṛhaṃ prāptāḥ sukhena kālaṃ nayanti sma | kevalam andhaḥ paryaṅke suptas tiṣṭhati, gṛha-vyāpāraṃ mantharakaḥ karoti | evaṃ gacchatā kālena tristanyā kubjakena saha vikṛtiḥ samapadyata | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text: When this had been done, having reached a foreign land, in a certain settlement shown by the boatmen, the three of them obtained a house for money and lived in comfort. The blind man simply lay sleeping on the bed while <s>Mantharaka</s> managed the household affairs. As time passed in this manner, the three-breasted woman developed an illicit attachment to the hunchback. Or rather, this is well said —

children.text: yadi syāc chrī-talo vahniś candramā dahanātmakaḥ |
children.translated_text: If the ocean were sweet, if the moon were of the nature of fire,

children.text: susvādaḥ sāgaraḥ strīṇāṃ tat-satīs tvaṃ prajāyate ||Panc_5.93||
children.translated_text: if the ocean floor had fire — then women would be chaste. [Panc 5.93]

children.text: athānyedyus tristanyā mantharako 'bhihitaḥ-bhoḥ subhaga ! yady eṣo 'ndhaḥ kathañcit vyāpādyate, tad āvayoḥ sukhena kālo yāti | tad anviṣyatāṃ kutracid viṣam, yenāsmai tat pradāya sukhinī bhavāmi |
children.translated_text: Then one day the three-breasted woman said to <s>Mantharaka</s>: 'O handsome one! If this blind man is somehow killed, then we two shall pass our time in comfort. So find some poison somewhere, so that by giving it to him I may be happy.'

children.text: anyadā kubjakena paribhramatā mṛtaḥ kṛṣṇasarpaḥ prāptaḥ | taṃ gṛhītvā prahṛṣṭa-manā gṛham abhyetya tām āha-subhage ! labdho 'yaṃ kṛṣṇa-sarpaḥ | tad enaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtvā prabhūta-śuṇṭhy-ādibhiḥ saṃskāryāsmai vikala-netrāya matsyāmiṣaṃ bhaṇitvā prayaccha yena drāg vinaśyati | yato 'sya matsyāmiṣaṃ sadā priyam | evam uktvā mantharako bahir gataḥ |
children.translated_text: On another day, while wandering about, the hunchback found a dead black serpent. Taking it and delighted in mind, having come home, he said to her: 'Beautiful one! This black serpent has been found. So cut it into pieces, prepare it with plenty of dried ginger and other seasonings, and give it to this sightless one, telling him it is fish curry, so that he quickly perishes. For fish curry is always his favorite.' Having said this, <s>Mantharaka</s> went outside.

children.text: sāpi pradīpte vahnau kṛṣṇa-sarpaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtvā takra-sthālyām ādhāya gṛha-vyāpārākulā taṃ vikalākṣaṃ sa-praśrayam uvāca-ārya-putra ! tavābhīṣṭaṃ matsya-māṃsaṃ samānītam | yatas tvaṃ sadaiva tat pṛcchasi | te ca matsyā vahnau pāvanāya tiṣṭhanti | tad yāvad ahaṃ gṛha-kṛtyaṃ karomi, tāvat tvaṃ darvīm ādāya kṣaṇam ekaṃ tān pracālaya |
children.translated_text: And she, having lit a fire, having cut the black serpent into pieces, placing them in a pot of buttermilk, busy with household chores, said respectfully to the sightless man: 'Noble husband! Your favorite fish curry has been brought. Since you always ask for it. Those fish are on the fire for cooking. So while I attend to the household work, take a ladle and stir them for a moment.'

children.text: so 'pi tad ākarṇya hṛṣṭa-manāḥ sṛkkaṇī parilihan drutam utthāya darvīm ādāya pramathitum ārabdhaḥ | atha tasya matsyān mathnato viṣa-garbha-bāṣpeṇa saṃspṛṣṭaṃ nīla-paṭalaṃ cakṣurbhyām agalat | asāv apy andhas taṃ bahu-guṇaṃ manyamāno viśeṣān netrābhyāṃ bāṣpa-grahaṇam akarot |
children.translated_text: He too, hearing that, joyful in mind, licking his lips, quickly stood up, took the ladle and began to stir. Now, as he stirred the 'fish,' a blue film oozed from both his eyes, touched by the poisonous vapor from the pot. And he, blind as he was, thinking this was highly auspicious, especially drew in the vapor with his eyes.

children.text: tato labdha-dṛṣṭir jāto yāvat paśyati, tāvat takra-madhye kṛṣṇa-sarpa-khaṇḍāni kevalāny evāvalokayati | tato vyacintayat-aho, kim etat ? mama matsyāmiṣaṃ kathitam āsīd anayā | etāni tu kṛṣṇa-sarpa-khaṇḍāni | tat tāvad vijānāmi samyak tristanyāś ceṣṭitam | kiṃ mama vadhopāya-kramaḥ kubjasya vā ? utāho anyasya vā kasyacit ? evaṃ vicintya svākāraṃ gūhayann andhavat karma karoti yathā purā |
children.translated_text: Then, having gained his sight, as he looked, he saw in the buttermilk only pieces of black serpent. Then he thought: 'Ah! What is this? She told me it was fish curry. But these are pieces of black serpent. So now I fully understand the three-breasted woman's designs. Is this a scheme to murder me, or the hunchback's, or someone else's?' Having thus reflected, concealing his expression, he acted as a blind man, just as before.

children.text: atrāntare kubjaḥ samāgatya niḥśaṅkatayāliṅgana-cumbanādibhis tristanīṃ sevitum upacakrame | so 'py andhas tam avalokayann api yāvan na kiñcic chastraṃ paśyati, tāvat kopa-vyākula-manāḥ pūrvavac chayanaṃ gatvā kubjaṃ caraṇābhyāṃ saṅgṛhya sāmarthyāt sva-mastakopari bhrāmayitvā tristanīṃ hṛdaye vyatāḍayat |
children.translated_text: In the meantime, the hunchback arrived and, without suspicion, began to embrace and kiss the three-breasted woman. And he, though seeing it all, as long as he did not find a weapon, with his mind agitated by anger, went to the bed as before, seized the hunchback by the feet, and by his strength, whirling him above his own head, struck the three-breasted woman upon her chest.

children.text: atha kubja-prahāreṇa tasyās tṛtīyaḥ stana urasi praviṣṭaḥ | tathā balān mastakopari bhramaṇena kubjaḥ prāñjalatāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: By the blow of the hunchback, her third breast was driven into her chest. And similarly, by the forceful whirling above his head, the hunchback became straight-bodied.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-andhakaḥ kubjakaś caiva (84) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'The blind man, the hunchback...' (verse 84) and so on.

children.text: suvarṇasiddhir āha-bhoḥ satyam etat | daivānukūlatayā sarvaṃ kalyāṇaṃ sampadyate | tathāpi puruṣeṇa satāṃ vacanaṃ kāryam | punar evam eva vartitavyam | atha evam eva yo vartate, sa tvam iva vinaśyati | tathā ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'Sir, this is true. By the favor of fate, everything turns out auspiciously. Yet still, a man should heed the words of the virtuous. One should always conduct oneself in just this way. But he who conducts himself thus [heedlessly] perishes like you.' And likewise —

children.text: ekodarāḥ pṛthag grīvā anyānya-phala-bhakṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Sharing one belly but with separate necks, eating different fruits —

children.text: asaṃhatā vinaśyanti bhāruṇḍā iva pakṣiṇaḥ ||Panc_5.94||
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s> birds perish when they are not united. // Panc_5.94 //

children.text: cakradhara āha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text:
kathā 13
bhāruṇḍa-pakṣi-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 13
The Story of the <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s> Bird

children.text: kasmiṃścit sarovare bhāruṇḍa-nāmā pakṣī ekodaraḥ pṛthag-grīvaḥ prativasati sma | tena ca samudra-tīre paribhramatā kañcit phalam amṛta-kalpaṃ taraṅga-kṣiptaṃ samprāptam | so 'pi bhakṣayann idam āha-aho ! bahūni mayāmṛta-prāyāṇi samudra-kallolāhṛtāni phalāni bhakṣitāni | param apūrvo 'syāsvādaḥ | tat kiṃ pārijāta-haricandana-taru-sambhavam ? kiṃ vā, kiñcid amṛta-maya-phalam idam avyaktenāpi vidhināpātitam |
children.translated_text: In a certain lake there lived a bird named <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s>, with one belly but separate necks. While wandering on the seashore, it obtained a certain fruit, like ambrosia, cast up by the waves. And while eating it, one [head] said: 'Ah! I have eaten many fruits brought by the ocean waves that were like ambrosia. But the taste of this one is extraordinary. Is it perhaps born of a <s>Pārijāta</s> or <s>Haricandana</s> tree? Or is it some ambrosia-filled fruit cast down even by the inscrutable Providence?'

children.text: evaṃ tasya bruvato dvitīya-mukhenābhihitam-bho, yady evaṃ tan mamāpi stokaṃ prayaccha, yenāham api jihvā-saukhyam anubhavāmi |
children.translated_text: While it was speaking thus, the second mouth said: 'Ho, if so, then give a little to me too, so that I too may experience the pleasure of the tongue.'

children.text: tato vihasya prathama-vaktreṇābhihitam-āvayos tāvad ekam udaram | ekā tṛptiś ca bhavati | tataḥ kiṃ pṛthag bhakṣitena ? varam anena śeṣeṇa priyā toṣyate |
children.translated_text: Then the first mouth said with a laugh: 'We two share one belly. And there is one [common] satisfaction. So what is the point of eating separately? It is better if the remainder is used to please our beloved.'

children.text: evam abhidhāya tena śeṣaṃ bhāruṇḍyāḥ pradattam | sāpi tad āsvādya prahṛṣṭatamāliṅgana-cumbana-sambhāvanādy-aneka-cāṭu-parā ca babhūva | dvitīyaṃ mukhaṃ tad-dinād eva prabhṛti sodvegaṃ sa-viṣādaṃ ca tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: Having said this, it gave the remainder to the female <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s>. And she, having tasted it, being most delighted, lavished many caresses — embracing, kissing, and the like. The second mouth, from that very day onward, remained agitated and despondent.

children.text: athānyedyur dvitīya-mukhena viṣa-phalaṃ prāptam | tad dṛṣṭvāparam āha-bho nistriṃśa ! puruṣādhama ! nirapekṣa ! mayā viṣa-phalam āsāditam | tat tavāpamānād bhakṣayāmi |
children.translated_text: Then on another day, a poisonous fruit was obtained by the second mouth. Seeing it, it said to the other: 'O heartless one! Lowest of beings! Uncaring one! I have obtained a poisonous fruit. Out of spite toward you, I shall eat it.'

children.text: apareṇābhihitam-mūrkha ! mā maivaṃ kuru | evaṃ kṛte dvayor api vināśo bhaviṣyati | athaivaṃ vadatā tenāpamānena tat phalaṃ bhakṣitam | kiṃ bahunā, dvāv api vinaṣṭau |
children.translated_text: The other said: 'Fool! Do not do so. If you do this, both of us will perish.' But while it was thus speaking, that one, out of spite, ate the fruit. What more need be said — both perished.

children.text: ato 'haṃ bravīmi-ekodarāḥ pṛthag-grīvāḥ (92) iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: 'Sharing one belly but with separate necks...' (verse 92).

children.text: cakradhara āha-satyam etat | tad gaccha gṛham | param ekākinā na gantavyam | uktaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Cakradhara</s> said: 'This is true. So go home. But one should not go alone.' And it is said —

children.text: ekaḥ svādu na bhuñjīta ekaś cārthān na cintayet |
children.translated_text: One should not enjoy delicacies alone; one should not ponder affairs alone;

children.text: eko na gacched adhvānaṃ naikaḥ supteṣu jāgṛyāt ||Panc_5.95||
children.translated_text: one should not travel a road alone; one should not stay awake alone when others sleep. // Panc_5.95 //

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: api kāpuruṣo mārge dvitīyaḥ kṣema-kārakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even a coward as a second companion on the road brings safety;

children.text: karkaṭena dvitīyena jīvitaṃ parirakṣitam ||Panc_5.96||
children.translated_text: by a crab as a second companion, a life was saved. // Panc_5.96 //

children.text: suvarṇa-siddhiḥ prāha-katham etat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s> said: 'How is that?'

children.text: so 'bravīt-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text:
kathā 14
brāhmaṇa-karkaṭaka-kathā
children.translated_text:
Tale 14
The Story of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the Crab

children.text: kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne brahmadatta-nāmā brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati sma | sa ca prayojana-vaśād grāmaṃ prasthitaḥ sva-mātrābhihitaḥ, yad-vatsa ! katham ekākī vrajasi ? tad anviṣyatāṃ kaścid dvitīyaḥ sahāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain town there lived a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Brahmadatta</s>. And he, having set out for a village on account of some business, was addressed by his own mother: 'Child! How do you go alone? Find some second companion.'

children.text: sa āha-amba ! mā bhaiṣīḥ | nirupadravo 'yaṃ mārgaḥ | kārya-vaśād ekākī gamiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Mother! Do not fear. This road is free of dangers. On account of my business, I shall go alone.'

children.text: atha tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā samīpastha-vāpyāḥ sakāśāt karkaṭam ādāya mātrābhihitaṃ-vatsa, avaśyaṃ yadi gantavyam | tad eṣa karkaṭo 'pi sahāyo bhavatu | tad enaṃ gṛhītvā gaccha |
children.translated_text: Then she, learning of his resolve, fetched a crab from a nearby pond and said to him: 'Child, if you must go, then let this crab too be your companion. So take it and go.'

children.text: so 'pi mātur vacanād ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ na saṅgṛhya karpūra-puṭikā-madhye nidhāya, pātra-madhye saṃsthāpya śīghraṃ prasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: And he, at his mother's word, grasping it with both hands, placed it inside a camphor pouch, set it in a vessel, and departed swiftly.

children.text:
atha gacchan grīṣmoṣmaṇā santaptaḥ kañcin mārgasthaṃ vṛkṣam āsādya, tatraiva prasuptaḥ | atrāntare vṛkṣa-koṭarān nirgatya sarpas tat-samīpam āgataḥ |
sa cābhyantara-gatāṃ karpūra-puṭikām atilaulyād abhakṣayat | so 'pi karkaṭas tatraiva sthitaḥ san sarpa-prāṇān apāharata | brāhmaṇe'pi yāvat prabuddhaḥ paśyati, tāvat samīpe mṛta-kṛṣṇa-sarpo nija-pārśve karpūra-puṭikopari sthitas tiṣṭhati | taṃ dṛṣṭvā vyacintayat-karkaṭenāyaṃ hataḥ iti | prasanno bhūtvābravīc ca-bhoḥ ! satyam abhihitaṃ mama mātrā yat puruṣeṇa ko 'pi sahāyaḥ kāryaḥ | naikākinā gantavyam | yato mayā śraddhā-pūrita-cetasā tad-vacanam anuṣṭhitaṃ tenāhaṃ karkaṭena sarva-vyāpādanād rakṣitaḥ | athavā sādhv idam ucyate-
children.translated_text:
Now, as he was walking, scorched by the summer heat, he came upon a certain tree by the roadside and fell asleep right there. In the meanwhile, a serpent emerged from the tree's hollow and came near him.
It ate the camphor pouch that was inside [the vessel], out of excessive greed. And that crab, remaining right there, took the serpent's life. When the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> awoke and looked, he saw a dead black serpent lying beside him, on top of the camphor pouch. Seeing it, he thought: 'This one was killed by the crab.' Becoming grateful, he said: 'Ah! Truly spoken was my mother's word — that a man should have some companion; one should not go alone. Because I carried out her words with a heart filled with faith, I was saved by the crab from complete destruction.' Indeed, well is this said —

children.text: kṣīṇaḥ śrayati śaśī ravim ṛddho vardhayati payasāṃ nātham |
children.translated_text: The moon, when waning, seeks refuge with the sun; when waxing, it augments the lord of waters;

children.text: anye vipadi sahāyā dhanināṃ śriyam anubhavanty anye ||Panc_5.97||
children.translated_text: some are companions in adversity; others enjoy the prosperity of the wealthy. // Panc_5.97 //

children.text: mantre tīrthe dvije deve daivajñe bheṣaje gurau |
children.translated_text: In a mantra, a pilgrimage site, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a deity, an astrologer, medicine, and a teacher —

children.text: yādṛśī bhāvanā yasya siddhir bhavati tādṛśī ||Panc_5.98||
children.translated_text: as is one's faith, so is one's attainment. // Panc_5.98 //

children.text: evam śrutvā suvarṇasiddhis tam anujñāpya svagṛhaṃ prati nivṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Suvarṇasiddhi</s>, taking leave of him, returned toward his own home.

children.text:
iti śrī-viṣṇu-śarma-viracite pañcatantre aparīkṣita-kārakaṃ nāma
pañcamaṃ tantraṃ samāptam
||5||
children.translated_text:
Thus ends, in the <s>Pañcatantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Viṣṇuśarman</s>,
the fifth <s>tantra</s> named <s>Aparīkṣitakāraka</s> (Hasty Action).
||5||

children.text:
yady apy evaṃ tathāpi tvaṃ darśaya taṃ caurasiṃhaṃ yathā vyāpādayāmi |
 (alt.) yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
 (alt.) rāja-puruṣaiḥ
 (alt.) devaśakti-kathā
children.translated_text:
'Even so, show me that thief-lion so that I may destroy him.'
(alt.) 'He who sees, truly sees.'
(alt.) 'by the king's men'
(alt.) 'The story of <s>Devaśakti</s>'
